review_text: Summit Chile was recommended by our Hostal host as one of the 3 reputable companies to do the volcano trek in Pucon. we checked out Summitt Chile first and we were immediately impressed with the professional attitude, enthusiasm and equipment, that we booked there and then for a vulcano trek later in the week. Summitt Chile is operated by Husband and wife team, Claudio and Suzie, a ChiLean mountain climber and A Canadian hiker, and they are very much involved in improving safety on the vulcano as there are many rogue operators. We were not disappointed as we had a party of 4 and Claudio had another competent guide coming with us as well. He operates on a 3 to 1 guide basis with a maximum of 12 customers. We had a great day as Claudio was funny and constantly interacting whilst keeping a close eye on our group, with regular stops. At the Summitt, he checked out all the areas first before he allowed us to proceed near the crater, which had started to rumble again after 4 years of being dormant. Claudio stayed with all the time as opposed to some parties of which the hikers were roaming around close to the crater without supervision. When it was time to descend, Claudio guided us off the steeper part of the vulcano before he allowed us to slide down on the plastic pads, after having given us the proper instructions. He does not believe in exposing his customers to unnecessary danger, unlike some of the other operators who, I noticed, push their charges down from the very top. Summit Chile's office is located at Urrutia 585, which is adjacent to the main street of Pucon. I definitely recommend Summitt Chile to anyone who wants to do the vulcano trek.

review_text: Went with the public bus, which leaves from La Serena at the corner between Francisco de Aguirre and Matta to Punta Chorros at 8:30 am (9,000 CLP round trip). There we payed 10,000 CLP for the bus ride and I think it was around 1,000 - 2,000 CLP for Conaf which makes the trip much cheaper than going on one of the tours offered around La Serena (~35,000 CLP). We left the mainland snd already shortly after we saw a group of at least 20-30 dolphins swimming close to our boat and jumping out of the water. They were putting on a show just like in sea world but in their natural environment and completely voluntarily... It was a magical experience!! After landing on Isla Damas we got a short introduction by someone from Conaf who told us that 80% of all Humboldt penguins live in the three islands that comprise the Reserva Nacional Pingüinos de Humboldt. We walked around the island for about one hour and took some pictures of the cactae and the rest of the flora (no wildlife though) before we went back into the boat again. Passing by Isla Chorros we saw hundreds of birds nesting and many penguins along with some seals and sea lions. We were told that people can only get off the boat at Isla Damas because they don't want to disturb the animals on the other islands, what I can fully understand since Isla Damas was already pretty crowded with tourists. I don't want that to happen to the other islands as well. Back on the mainland we had another hour left before our bus picked us up at 3:30pm towards La Serena. We had lunch there at one of the food stalls which was mediocre... better bring your own food

review_text: Taken here as part of a vineyard tour. The vineyard is in a smart imposing building accessed from the main Santiago to Valparaiso road. There are pretty gardens, alpacas, chickens etc as well as the vineyard and wines. Our tour was three English speakers plus some 9 Spanish speakers. Our guide managed to inform us all by giving the information in both languages. We were taken round the vines where the whole process was described. This included explanations of the chickens, there to help with pest control, the alpacas, there to provide fertiliser etc. As the vineyard is both organic and uses bio dynamic principles it was interesting to hear and understand how they dealt with these issues. Add to this the vegetable garden and other aspects designed to reward and involve the workers and it seems good to the staff. Then came the wine tasting, two whites followed by two reds. The whites were a Chardonnay and a Viognier. They were very different but both tasty and easy to drink. The two reds a Carmenere and blend of several grapes. Both had very soft tannins, were clean and tasty and like the whites easy to drink on their own. The last was the complex in its flavours but was still easy to drink. We were also treated to a sample of their expensive red. This was approximately ten times the cost of the others but had the potential to age whilst still being drinkable now. This was a complex wine with more pronounced tannins as well as more complex flavours. Overall an informative, educational visit with good wines to taste.

review_text: We booked 4 tours with Whipala and communicated via email. The communication was sometimes in Spanish but they were always very responsive. Upon arrival in Atacama, we went to the office and paid in Chilean Pesos for a 20% discount. We did the Valley of the Moon, Tatio Geysers, Cejar and Red Stones tour. They were all lead by Whipala. If they don't have enough people (I think it is 8), they will have you join another tour company. Some tours picked up at the hotel and some we left from the office. We had Christopher for 2 tours and Cristian for 2 tours. Christopher was a much better and more patient guide. He always used a microphone and was easy to understand. Valley of the Moon - spent 45 minutes trekking and parts of it walking through a cave. Bring a flashlight. Spent 1.5 - 2 hours climbing the Big Daddy dune. Bring WATER and wear trekking shoes. It gets hot. Bring a hat. Left office at 4 pm and returned at around 8 pm after sunset. Tatio Geysers - it is VERY cold. Bring warm clothing. It is high altitude as well. We had Christopher as a guide and he made us a good breakfast with cooked eggs, hot tea and coffee. It was 5:15 am - noon. Picked up at hotel. Cejar - spent about an hour here. There are showers and people swam in the lake. We spent about 45 minutes for the sunset at Laguna. There were cocktails with pisco sour. Left office at 4 pm and returned around 8:45 pm. Red Stones - this is an all day tour with pick up at your hotel around 8 am. The roads are bumpy and there isn't much walking. Breakfast is included. Lunch was also included in a restaurant in a small town. We returned at around 5:30 pm. This was a very enjoyable day tour. However, you might get altitude sickness since it is at high altitude. For all these tours, entrance is NOT included and you must bring cash.

review_text: To start let me point out I am Chilean and I know my people how they behave and treat tourists... so let me also say I am so so sorry. The place is gorgeous, the view is amazing provided that pollution is not fading the away you $ 10000CLP The personnel is bilingual (English-Spanish) so if you need to ask any triviality you'll find the answer, but... I felt annoyed when while passing through security my partner who does not speak Spanish had to go back because no one told him what thing or things should be put into the baskets to go through the scanner. The person in charge of checking the content of the baskets was rude and I was really glad my friends didn't understand Spanish. I think for a touristic place in which tours are given in both English and Spanish the most reasonable thing to do is, start the bilingual instructions from the very beginning, from the moment you payed, specially if we talk about security. If they have personnel giving tours in English how come the security personnel does not give bilingual instructions. My personal opinion is, if you have bilingual staff that provides entertainment, you clearly know your target audience will be international, so please invest a little in security personnel that gives instructions in both English and Spanish at all times, no matter if the visitor speaks either or.

review_text: My wife and I took a one-day sea kayaking trip to the Reloncavi fjord on December 13. Juanfe was very responsive to emails in the weeks and days before the trip and on time to pick us up at our hotel in Puerto Varas. He was even very flexible when we told him our luggage had been delayed and agreed to push the trip back by one day. We were the only participants that day and so received totally personalized attention. He put us at ease with his charming and friendly manner on the ride to the fjord and briefed us thoroughly on technique and safety (in very good English) since we had never kayaked before. He was fully prepared with gear and a nice packed lunch including hot soup and tea because it was an overcast day. We spent about 1.5 hours kayaking, stopped for lunch on a beach, and then about the same back. Along the way, we were able to enjoy the views of the fjord and the coastal vegetation. Although Juanfe would have been happy to go longer, it was our decision to return since our arms were quite tired from paddling and the wind was picking up. Instead of heading straight back to Puerto Varas, he then took us a little further along the fjord in his van to see the village of Cochamó with its little church and the salmon/mussel farms along the way. He has a very broad knowledge of the area and many interesting stories to tell, and we had some great conversation on the way back to Puerto Varas. In short, we had a wonderful day that has given us a beautiful experience of this area and a positive, fun introduction to sea kayaking. I would absolutely recommend Juanfe and Yak Expediciones!

review_text: “The average hike length is 8 hours but I’ve had many trips that have been over 11” ; the somewhat ‘menacing’, certainly ‘sobering’ words of my Guide Valentina, as we prepared for the ‘off’. Looking up, I could feel the acute angle of my neck ! I’d been told - warned - that this officially categorised ‘challenging’ activity had within it 3 phases, the first being an ascent taking circa 90 minutes. An aerobic workout that definitely tested. And replenishing water bottles from the gushing rivers/falls was as necessary as it was a relief. Phase 2 - through the forest - was easier, albeit each ‘down’ was met with the next ‘up’. The occasional returning hiker’s telling grin - in sync with a recurring ‘keep going’ salutation - was commensurate with a presumed sense of descending joy ! The 3rd and final ‘stretch’ was arguably the hardest. You’re 10Km ‘in’ at this stage and ahead of you is a last 1Km that takes a good 50 minutes to complete. You’re clambering over uneven rocks & small boulders, all the time ascending. You sweat. You ache. You occasionally entertain the odd expletive. This is arguably as much a mental resilience issue as it is physical. Then…there ‘they’ reveal themselves ! South, Central & North, alongside Condors Nest. Magnificent ! Dramatic. Imposing. ‘Mighty’ ! Beautiful too. And all of this with the tranquility of a shimmering lake in the foreground. Any hint of negativity dissipates, all doubts are forgotten. Because no doubt - it’s worth it ! ‘That’ sight before you impacts…and with it, there’s a powerful sense of achievement. Memorable. And being one of the first to reach the destination brought privilege, in that there was a discernible peace about the environment, that later - after eating our lunch - had been replaced with lots of busyness and queuing for the best photo opportunity. Don’t be lulled into a false belief that the return to base is straightforward. Occasionally slipping & sliding on the rocks in the first phase, equates to a need for a more minded purpose of footing. Hiking protocol dictates that you give way to Ascenders. For each ‘down’ there continues to be an ‘up’…right to the end. But Vally telling me ‘You’re the real deal Hiker JP’ at the end of 7 hours, 20 minutes was a moment of magical affirmation. Review of: Full-Day Hiking Tour to the Base of Paine Towers at Torres del Paine National Park

review_text: The view from Cerro San Cristobal is great, but key parts of the experience include the pleasant ride up the traditional old funicular (uphill train) and the various vendors and hub-bub and both the top and the bottom. I think this is a great way to start a visit to Santiago. I went with my daughter and we had a great time, including buying candied peanuts at the top and enjoying the music and general festive atmosphere on the weekend. Notably, the hill itself is only thinly populated or built-up and the walk up or down the hill is reputed to include a substantial risk of theft, so I would advise sticking to the funicular ride in both directions unless you are with a group of people, and then only during full daytime.

I enjoyed the walk due to the really spectacular landscape you pass through, however it does need better signage and the path needs some maintainence so take care! We have provided feedback to CONAF.

review_text: It's a steep hike to the top of Manquehue, the track is unstable in many places, you need good shoes and walking poles for the way down. There is no shade whatsoever so better do this in cooler weather. The views are great as you are above the Santiago smog, you can see the 6,000m-peaks of the Andes. Also condors are flying around the mountain. It's a great day out of the big city, the track itself is 3-4 hours in total. We started the walk from the Los Trapenses end. You can take buses to the Lo Barnechea neighbourhood (for example C14) and get off at the junction Los Trapenses with Golf de Manquehue. The track starts at the very end of Gold de Manquehue, 2km from the bus stop. Or take a cab from the closest metro station, we came from Las Condes area and the cab was less than 10,000 pesos.

review_text: The mountains are simply stunning. You may be happy just watching them from the miradors by the road, but the even better views and different nature along the trails are worth taking a day hike or a longer trek. However, this is not the easiest, nor the cheapest destination for trekking. We read many blogs, a guide book, and the official web site. There was a lot of misinformation and some essential details are not said anywhere. Here are some things you may want to consider while planning your trip. Most importantly, if you plan on doing any multi-day treks, you need to book all camp sites several months in advance. We traveled there from the other side of the world, as we read that the camp sites should be reserved from the visitor center, just to hear that all the camp sites are full. There were a couple of campgrounds by the road that don't have to be reserved in advance, so we could still do day hikes. These campgrounds had amazing views to the mountains. I don't know how you are supposed to reserve the camp sites if you're doing a longer trek. There are contact forms to some campgrounds on the web site. It might be difficult to know the exact dates and your route several months in advance. If you have a car or take a bus from El Calafate to Torres del Paine, you need to get cash in advance. There is no ATM at the border. There is a guy exchanging dollars, euros, and Argentinean pesos to Chilean pesos in the restaurant / souvenir shop at the border. Also, there's no gas station, and the grocery stores at the border and in Torres del Paine are really small, so it might be easiest to spend one day in Puerto Natales anyway. Everything in Torres del Paine is very expensive. Most places, including the entrance, accept credit cards, but they may require cash at certain times of day. US dollars are commonly accepted at a bad rate. Remember that you cannot bring meat, vegetables, etc. across the border, though canned food and trekking food should be OK. Another thing is transportation inside the park. There is supposed to be some kind of bus or mini van transportation from Hotel Las Torres to the pier where you need to get to start the W trek. We rented a car just to be sure we get there, but the trek ends in a different place so you still have the problem of how to get back to your car We saw some buses, but I think they were for organized tours. I don't know if the park offers any transportation; based on the number of hitchhikers we saw, not anything frequent at least. In February, the weather was not that big problem, but the wind was even more extreme than I thought. The weather in Patagonia was generally nice and the days were warm because of the sun. The mountains are almost always cloudy, and if you trek closer to the peaks, you'll get rain showers quite often. The nights get pretty cold, so you need warm clothes and sleeping bag.

review_text: Beautiful, unique place to visit. I read a lot of forums on this area and recommend that if you do not mind driving over rough terrain, and can navigate basic maps--suggest you rent a car so you can decide which day to hike, and where to hike. The weather is very unpredictable. We rented an all wheel drive car in Punta Arena and it took about 5 hours to arrive at our hotel. The last 1.5 hours was on a rough gravel road--as other travelers noted, fill up the tank in Puerto Natales I am not a backpacker--tried it a few times and decided that hotels are my best travel option. Still had a wonderful experience, and was able to hike a portion of the W--could have done more of the trail, but the wind was high enough to close the French Valley. If you want more of hiking experience, you could stay a few nights at one of the hotels not on the W circuit, then stay 1-2 nights at the Lodge on the West Side of the W trail. We took the catamaran ride over and hiked to the italian camp--great 5 hour hike on a very windy day. While we were waiting for the catamaran to return, we had some wine/beer in the lodge--looked like a nice place to stay. Definitely take the catamaran across and hike a portion--very well marked trails and you do not need a guide--just the right day hiking equipment. The other hikes we did included Sandy Point and Lago Sarmiento--all great. Highly recommend this if you are traveling either to Argentina or Chile. Met another couple who had rented a car from Bariloche and was doing a circuit

review_text: Not a very big one but a "nice-sized" one (especially for its length) with also plenty of big trees for shade and where there's like no shortages of benches alongside the walkways, this park is one where I had a pretty good walk-around in the afternoon unlike at Parque Bicentenario (to the further north) where the walk was just one under the sun with pretty much no shade whatsoever (due to a lack of big trees in that park). And apart from a nice walk here, my suggestion is not to miss this fairly-sizeable sculpture featuring some people on a boat with also a big bird on one end of the boat and water coming down the rocks under the boat to the circular pool below (just "interesting to look at" located on like the small roundabout at the end of a walkway to the east side of the Park), and actually there's also (in my opinion "somewhat surprisingly") a bust of American President Abraham Lincoln to be found in this park. And despite being an "urban park" pretty much right in the heart of the city (just a bit less than a half-hour walk east from Plaza de Armas), this park located at Barrio Lastarria (a "somewhat quaint" neighborhood with outdoor art vendors & such) is kind of set apart I would say from the hustle & bustle of the city, and yes also located in the same neighborhood at just about a 10-minute walk from this park is Cerro Santa Lucia (a "beautiful hill" very pleasant to walk around with a tower on the very top for a nice 360-degree view) which you'll actually pass by on your way to this park if coming from Plaza de Armas (I visited that hill before coming over here); and also directly across the street on the north side of this park is Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes (worthwhile stopping by with two floors of sculptures & paintings although not too many for a museum of that size I would say).

review_text: Located in the Casablanca Valley, a major wine-producing region of Chile, Puro Caballo (Just Horses) highlights the beauty and nobility of the Chilean Horse, historic equestrian traditions and fine local gastronomy. La Vega Ranch, home of Puro Caballo, is near Lagunillas (Little-Lakes), an ancient town of about 700 people which seems to have remained stuck in the past, particularly after a new highway linking the city of Casablanca with the Port of San Antonio by-passed the already sleepy town. The owners of the ranch have been breeding purebred Chilean Horses for about 80 years and at one point decided to showcase their activity to the public by displaying the fine animals, showing their particular characteristics and demonstrating their abilities in the Chilean Rodeo, a traditional competitive sport that originated around the 16th Century and in 1962 was declared by law, the national sport. Besides the activities associated to the breeding of horses and rodeo training, Puro Caballo is also a place where locals and visitors from other countries, particularly from cruise ships visiting the port of Valparaíso, can see an exhibition of the national sport, the Chilean Rodeo, have a country style meal at the Puro Caballo restaurant, and acquire horse related souvenirs and handicrafts.

review_text: The valle de la luna is nearby San Pedro, and therefor a magnet for people who come to see the sunset. We found the canyon and caves interesting to explore, and did only a quick tour of the other viewpoints, in order to be in time to see the sunset from the dune. Although less spectacular color changes than promised it's still nice to set quiet and enjoy. We were a bit surprised that the park guards started to tell people to leave just after the sun gone down, because the variations in colours of the rocks and the air were probably at best around that time. When by car, be carefull, many cyclists on the exit road have no light on the bike, no reflective clothing and wear no helmet. Maybe a suggestion for the many bike rental places in town!

review_text: For anyone with an interest in the history and politics of modern Chile, particularly the overthrow of Allende and the years of dictatorship under Pinochet, this museum is an absolute must see. The displays of film, documents and artifacts are comprehensive and very moving, especially the stories of torture and the "disappeared". Very good English language audio guides are available, with over 60 specific sites to link to as you tour the museum (the guide is accompanied by a map of the 3 levels of the museum, outlining the route to follow and the places at which to use the audio guide). There is a memorial room and wall with photos of thousands of victims of the dictatorship which is beautifully simple and very emotional, even for someone with no link to Chile. The space itself is beautifully designed. The fact there is no admission charge is almost embarrassing given the quality of this museum ( donations are welcome). Highly recommended.

review_text: We had a bad experience with this agency in San Pedro de Atacama on November 03, 2016, in a tour to the Valley of the Moon. Although the group in bus had around 10 people over 60 years old, the guide summarily ignored us. At the first stop he rushed into the cave with the group of young ladies and left us behind. My husband, who is a tall man, felt a great discomfort crawling through the narrow and low cracks of the caves, and complained to him (when we finally met him again at the exit of the cave) and asked to be informed about the level of difficulty of the next visits. He treated us with disdain and did not give us any further information. Because of that, we stayed in the bus during the next stop, which was just a walk with no real difficulty (as we were informed at the end). Finally, when we stopped at the Valley of Mars he informed that a glass of sparkling wine would be served to toast the sunset. Not for us… He carefully filled generously the glasses of the young ladies so at our turn (the four people sitting at the back of the bus) there was noting left! At the end of the tour we returned to the office, told them about our experience and cancelled of our next booked tour. There are many agencies in San Pedro specialized in adventure tours for the youngest. That is not the business of Touristour according to their website. They just don’t care for older tourists. Estimada: Entendemos su malestar sobre la situación, revisaremos en conjunto con la persona encargada de la zona, para mejorar nuestros procesos. Saludos.

review_text: We arrived to the national park by taking bus tour 35,000 and hiking base tour 40,000 booked through hostel Patagonia adventure (middle person) exclusive of Park cost 21,000 clp for 3 consecutive days visitation. Make sure you get the park to stamp your next day return at registrations. This is also where all the bus parked. If you are planning to hike the base, booking a tour is not necessary at all. If you are not hiking at all then bus tour is recommended otherwise xan skip it. The base trail is pretty obvious everyone is going the same directions and there are trail sticks through out the whole park. Last bus appears to be 615PM there's a huge board showing bus (300 clp est with bus sur etc) time in the information cafe area (1-2 miles from registration; 15 mins walk from hotel las torres). Myself and another lady with ankle issue started at 930AM and finish the hike at 7PM. the guide follow us with walkie talkies in case of issues. As for the other 5 hikers in our group they did not need our guide at all and finished at 6PM, which is average time if no leg issues. Base trail is 10 km long but you have to take same trail back so 20 total. after 3 km from entrance of dirt elevated trail there is rest area with toilet ( 500 clp). Next trails you will go through windy pass, forest, more elevated dirt trail...and finally 45 mins of climbing large rocks to get to the base. Way back is very slippery!! (My reason for slow hike compared to tour group). Make sure you have hiking shoes with good soles, hiking socks,pants that is not dragging on the floor). Only benefit of guide is their walkie talkie as there are no reception, hotel pickup, do not need to walk between information center and registration area if necessary, flexibility of finish time if you are slow. If you are not hiking the base or trail, then bus tour is a good alternative to visit the park. Otherwise, this tour can be skipped as the view can be seen outside the windows of the bus on way to hiking trail. Only difference is with bus tour there are 4 different stops for you to take pictures from a distance. See icebergs of lago grey which is hit or miss pending on when you arrive. And midlon cave , which is only ok... We been to a lot of other caves in past and they are bigger and more impressive. Not to mention 5,000 clp admission fee.

review_text: Francisco met me right at the entrance of their stunning property surrounded by native Arucaria trees. The renovations and development that his family are investing in on the property is incredibly thoughtful . The design and overall space where you can gather and enjoy the micro climate is warmly inviting and actually incredibly natural. They operate a certified organic produce garden that sits in front of the entrance to the (also certified organic) vines. The vines are in a micro terroir that offers a distinct classification of each of their wines. While invitingly walking through the vines you can visually notice the difference of authentic terror. In addition to a beautiful lineup of terroir-driven wines to taste , you can relax at the asado to taste classic and stunningly prepared meats and small plates. The hospitality is so warm from all the staff and you can tell the family truly cares about wine tourism in Chile and the promotion of an organic lifestyle. I highly recommend a visit , and don’t rush- enjoy and soak it all in.

review_text: We were in Punta Arenas for two full days at two different times and worked with Cecilia at Far South to arrange two of their birding tours. One was the Patagonian Steppes, which was wonderful scenery, and we saw guanaco, condor, rheas, and other steppes birds. The other was the Magellan Straits which offered an entirely different environment with forests, owls, woodpeckers, ruddy geese, and other small birds. The packed lunch is lovely and has plenty of snacks in it for the day, too...though we might recommend bringing some extra water. Our guide, Sebastian, was excellent, an avid birder himself, he could spot the birds and helped us see even rare birds in the area! Ramon, our driver, was also excellent, we felt safe and the ride was smooth. These were our first birding tours that we've taken, it was a lot of driving, and we brought our own binoculars, which you will want to do. The guide has binoculars and a spotting scope (which we got to see some birds really close with!) but having your own makes a huge difference. We would definitely recommend Far South and use them again in the PA area, their longer tours would be lovely, we just didn't have the time....

review_text: A friend and I just returned from the 6 day, Pumalin Park trip that Yak offers. The whole experience was beyond anything I could have ever imagined. Beautiful scenery: think lush green mountains, snow capped volcanos, waterfall every where you turn, hot springs with vistas straight out of a National Geographic Magazine. Authentic Experience: we were lucky enough to dine with local fisherman families on several occasions throughout the trip. Honestly, some of the best meals I enjoyed while in Chile, along with a chance to here the stories from very interesting people. Juanfe also provided rich, colorful stories and facts as we paddled about the culture, history and landscape of Pumalin Park. Great Guide: Juanfe was an OUTSTANDING guide. He has the ability to seamlessly combine fun with structure, keeping the group aware, alert and educated on the paddling conditions and potential dangers. Letting us know the appropriate times to paddle slowly and enjoy the scenery vs. times to be focused on the conditions and the task at hand. On the last day of the trip, we encountered a extreme rainstorm. The days leading up to this, Juanfe was incredible at keeping an eye on the radar and forecast, keeping us informed and adjusting the paddling schedule to avoid dangerous conditions and wind. The storm was so bad, we actually have to leave a day early from our last campsite. (The first time this has happened on a YAK trip) Juanfe has such amazing relationships with the local families that folks went out of their way to help us out as we travelled by boat, ferry, and car to get to a safe, dry location. I felt incredibly safe and fortunate to be in this situation with such a knowledge guide. As Juanfe clearly states on the YAK website, this trip is not for everyone. If you are not into camping, living out of a garbage bag for a few days, this trip is not for you. Flexibility, a positive attitude, willingness to work hard and a sense of adventure are required!!

review_text: We totally hit the jackpot---in terms of the weather, the scenery and the company we chose to take our trip with. We booked our one day trip, last minute with Juanfe--the owner of Yak Expediciones. From the get-go he was personable AND professional. Juanfe knows the area, clearly loves what he does and is a seasoned professional who makes safety his top most priority. The "safety" talk at the beginning of the trip, admittedly had me a little nervous about venturing out into this huge mountain lake where the wind and the waves could appear out of nowhere. But, Juanfe takes the safety part of his job very seriously----which is EXACTLY what you want on these kinds of trips. He is incredibly knowledgeable too--about the history and the birds and wildlife. Very interesting and entertaining. Lucky for us, the weather was perfect. There was almost no wind and we had Lago Todos Los Santos completely to ourselves. Volcanoes all around. Birds. Blue sky and silence. It was incredible. And, he even extended the trip a bit so we could get a view of Tronador----which required us to kayak an additional 1-2 hours. He was totally flexible! My only regret? That we do not have enough time to book a 3-4 day trip with him. For me was like holidays travelling with you...thanks for your possitive inputs during the trip.

review_text: This stargazing evening (9pm-1am in our case) was a really nice experience. Super enthusiastic guide (Jorge) who gave us a great lecture about the universe, it’s star constellations and planets. His facilities are rustic but comfortable and very well planned. It wasn’t too cold and his blankets and outdoor heaters made us comfortable as he first presented the sky and it’s stars with an amazing laser pointer. We then watched certain pre-planned stars and planets using his 6-8 different telescopes. He also took some pictures of us individually and in group with the stars as background - which was pretty neat although it is difficult to get any sharpness with long shutter speeds of people. I wouldn’t recommend this for kids under 10 but overall this was a memorable evening and Jorge was an ideal instructor who shared his immense knowledge and enthusiasm. The snacks and drinks he served were also delicious.

review_text: We hiked up from the Bellavista area and down the other side on paved road. There is tons of info available on various options for getting up and down the hill on trip advisor and elsewhere. We preferred walking but cycling would be a good option if you have that option available. Monday is really quiet since cable cars and funiculars are closed on Mondays. Weekends are apparently very busy, so we avoided the area then. Lots of bicycles and runners, walkers especially on a weekday evening (not Monday). We actually felt more safe in the evening on (Thursday) than mid-day on Monday when it almost felt deserted...felt safer to have some company. Only because there are many crime warnings in the area. Our hotel advised not to take any of the mountain bike paths (we were not planning on it) but apparently tourists who take those paths as a "short cut" are targeted by robbers. Anyway, we felt safe the two times we went up but didn't take any valuable belongings anyway. There are bathrooms and some shops at the top but hours are variable... Summer is smoggy/more difficult to see but seemed to vary depending on time of day and still a good view of the city regardless...

review_text: We recently visited Salar de Tara organised by Cosmo Andino. We were picked up promptly in a small bus and only 8 of us on the tour. Unfortunately we were the only visitors with English as a first language so the others tended to group together and we felt a little excluded, in particular as the guide was rather partial to the two Brazilian women in the group. Although Pablo, our guide, was very good at doing English translations throughout the day, it was disappointing that in such a small group, he obviously had no clue what our names were. The tour takes an immediate ascent from San Pedro up to around 4500m within the first hour. The landscape is utterly amazing and we saw vicunas and llamas enroute. The tour continues onwards and upwards with regular stops for photos at different points of interest. At around 1pm, the group arrives at Salar de Tara and the group is invited to walk down the hill enjoying the view of the lake and surrounds (also another toilet opportunity behind rocks) while the driver goes on to set up lunch. There were several other tour groups doing the same trip so this is no longer a trip that is just done by Cosmo Andino. Lunch was a very disappointing affair for the cost. There was rice, chopped avocado and tomatoes and a cold vegetable lasagne. Wine was also supplied along with other cold drinks. There was no where to sit and it was very exposed in the sun. Some camp chairs to sit on and some shelter would be a nice addition. By this time, my 11 year old daughter was very sick with the altitude but the guide was not that interested. She slept most of the trip home and it was a good 24 hours before she felt well again having vomited once we reached the hotel. Respect the altitude - you reach 4800m in very quick time. Drink plenty of water for the 24 hours prior and during the trip (at least 3L), get plenty of sleep, eat lightly and don't do any sudden movements or over-exert when you at altitude. Do everything slowly. I followed these rules and escaped with a mild headache only. There are NO TOILETS during this trip so the only place to do it is out in the open. There are very few opportunities to find a rock big enough to hide behind, so do it when you get a chance. Unfortunately, it is fairly obvious that thousands of other people have preceded you due to the masses of toilet paper left behind in these various spots. Drip dry if you can to avoid this travesty to the landscape! The landscapes are utterly amazing and very varied to see as you traverse the Andes. Be aware of the altitude and toilet situation. Take snacks and water as there is none provided other than lunch. This is an 8 hour trip of which about 6 hours is spent driving so be warned.

review_text: We had an excellent day on the volcano 6k (which is basically the same as the snow hike, once winter hits). The 6:30 am pickup time is early, but trust them. They are avoiding rush hour, allowing for travel/weather variables, and contributing to the local community. They care about community, conservation & ecology. We felt very safe with our driver, Diego, and guides, Sebastian & Gabriel. They are energetic, respectful & knowledgeable. We also enjoyed meeting the 3 other tour-takers from Ireland & Brazil. We were surprised that the entire trail was covered in snow and enjoyed hiking in snowshoes surrounded by the beautiful Andes mountains. In winter, be sure to bring warm clothes/layers and wear or rent waterproof hiking boots. We got back to our hotel around 5:30 pm, just in time to view sunset in Santiago after a amazing day! review_text: We (my son and I) wanted some more adventure. To be specific, beside hiking on the Grey Glacier, we also wanted to do some climbings (for beginners!). Since this isn't popular and therefore do imply more safety regulations, it was difficult to find a company that was willing to deviate from their standards to organize that apart for us, until we came across "Patagonia Adventure Natales". We are very glad with the prompt service, the persistance character and formal threatment we had from this company, especially, from miss Amandine, who managed to make this "custom made" excursion possible for us. The hiking was fascinating. Luckily the weather was good, with a clear sky. We could enter inside the glacier, following a deep and long fissure. There, everything around you become blue, because of the color of the ice. The climbing was sufficiently adventureous. Above all, safety precaution was notable and seriously complied with. Our effort was worth it: we reached our goal; the top! So, we could not have asked for more. We are very happy that we had the opportunity to make this one in a lifetime glacier experience come true, thanks to Patagonia Adventure Natales. We are so happy that both of you enjoyed this experience, patagonia is the perfect spot for adventurers as you. We hope all the best for you and your family. Thanks Jorge.

review_text: If you make it to Rio Tranquillo, it's worth the price to see these. You can't see this from a road, you have to book it. They are serious about safety, tour guides are licensed & they require 2 on each boat - which seemed a bit silly since it was only the 2 of us passengers. I guess if one of us fell overboard, two people might be needed to pull us in. January & February are high season, you won't be alone. Lago General Carrera is beautiful! Best time to go is in the morning, there is usually less wind. We paid about $75 US for 1 1/2 - 2 hours (includes time to get to the caves & back). The price was for two of us & includes the tip. Weather fluctuates rapidly in this area, you'll want rain jackets which keep you warm in the wind, too. The day we went it was rainy at 8am & beautiful at 9, when we left. Trust your tour guide for the best time of day.

review_text: Being in Santa Cruz we were obviously going to visit a few vineyards and sample some great Chilean wine but hadn't planned on horse riding. I have never ridden a horse before in my life, but after a quick chat and a little reassurance from Ian all four of our group were booked on! My girlfriend's mum is a keen horse rider and we arranged this as a surprise for her. She was really pleased. Ian picked us up in the morning and drove us to his family stables where we met the horse trainer (Daniel) and the horses. With me being the least experienced, I jumped on a horse first and Ian gave me the basic information I would need to successfully ride the horse. Then, one by one, the other three mounted their horses and received the same instructions from Ian. Ian made sure that we were all at ease before we set off. The horses are really responsive and have obviously been highly trained by Daniel. Great for me as a first time rider and for the more experienced in our group. Ian and Daniel safely took us up through some great countryside to a wooden mirador (panoramic lookout) that has fantastic views of the Colchagua Valley and to the Andes mountains. Here, we enjoyed a couple of bottles of red wine from the family vineyard alongside cheese and cured meat. Why go on foot for a glass of wine when you can go on horseback! Ian is a great guy and we all chatted throughout the trip. We then returned down to the stables. What a great start to the day! Everyone had a great time and it's certainly one of the highlights from our trip! Thanks Ian! Review of: Horseback rides Santa Cruz, Chile

review_text: Hi there , me and my wife just got back from that great trek! Because from 2016 the park managment dicide the you must have resevation. You should know what are the options.. ( because you gonna need around a month before the trek for getting the free reservations..) Beside a medium- hard level day that you walk to the top of the torres , the other days are pretty easy for everyone.. So: 1) 3 nights- from west to east- A: refugio paine grande- leave your staff at refugio paine grande and walk along the gray glacier and back.- need to pay 5000 if i remember.. B: camping italiano- leave your staff there and go to the french vally view point, and the torres from the back- free reservation uncaf website C: las torres- long day, but the most beautiful, leave your staff in camp and go to the torres - free camp uncaf website. 2) 3 nights -east yo west- same instractions but from the other side.. Good: you can start your trek early ( dont depend on boat time..) after day 1 the trek is very calm.. Bad: hard start, and you finish with the torres at the begining.. 3) 4 nights- just put another night in camp francise or another in italiano ( on diffrent name) You can change the day in paine grande to camp gray, and have more time next to the glacier and the bridge.. It will give you resting time for the pepole who afraid from long days/ first treks in patagonia/ just chill pepole:) To sum up: you have to pay for only one camp no matter what. Beside los cuernos that is super expensive, the others is around 5000 clp for camp per person.. Good luck!

review_text: Firstly, we were to meet at the agency for 0845am to get prepared and our guide was almost 20 minutes late due to "problems" (no real apology given, it just seemed like it was more of a problem for our guide rather than for the paying customers). When we were finally given equipment, we were rushed to the van to take us to the dunes where we were given the most rushed "tutorial" if you could call it that. Most of us were not entirely sure as to how to proceed, and we was slated as "the slowest group that has taken part" (bearing in mind that our unapologetic guide was roughly 15 minutes late that morning). Our guide proceeded to rush us down the dune, to which we pretty much had to figure it out by ourselves as our guide proceeded to slide to the bottom and smoke for the remainder of the session. Most of us taking part could have benefited from a few more pointers, but our guide was more interested in not being in view for half of the time and smoking for the other half. We were also told that there would be an edited video of our session, but it was overlooked (both the day's before and the evening session were present, followed by the next day's sessions). All in all, I feel as though there was no pressure from competition to give a good service, and as such many liberties were taken after the fact that we had paid upfront. I will visit San Pedro again, but i will not be going to this agency again. This was the ONLY bad part of our visit, the rest was fantastic.

review_text: My husband and I disembarked on the 21st January 2017 in Valparaiso, we had been on a South American cruise with NCL. Juan and his Mother who was our driver was waiting for us at the port. We did a wonderful day tour with them to Valparaiso so colourful ,gritty not to be missed. Juan was infact the owner of Perro Tours who was a very knowledgeable guide who was very passionate about his country and the area who gave us such a detailed and comprehensive tour. We then went onto Vina del Mar an upmarket resort to see the Flower Clock, walk around the beach area to see an authentic Moai from Easter Island. They then drove us to Santiago where we enjoyed a city highlights tour seeing the historic quarter and other well known landmarks. They then dropped us off at our Hotel in Santiago. review_text: We did the Los Lagos route today, approx 10km not 8.8. Gorgeous walk, lots of monkey puzzle trees and beautiful lakes. A lot of up hill, 3-4km approx, we’re pretty fit and with a lunch stop for 30mins and several photo stops we did it in just over 4 hours. We saw gorgeous woodpeckers, dancing around us over our picnic. **Please note!!** Small 2wd rental cars WILL NOT make it down the road to the park, despite what people might tell you. The road is awful, 14km unpaved, stoney, gravel potholey track, some mud patches and lots of switch backs up the hill. The bus from Pucon is just as quick and will not void your insurance, worth getting the bus for sure.

review_text: An AMAZING Tour! This trip gives you a real and unforgettable experience, totally different from the usual tourist routes. We started with a van ride around the city, stopping at places with awesome views. Next, we took a lovely walk through the charming streets of Valparaíso. We explored cool spots that aren't usually on the tourist map, letting us dive deep into the local culture. Daniel, our guide, showed us around to typical hangouts where we chatted with locals, met artists, and even made friends with the friendly street dogs. The tour with Daniel is more than just regular sightseeing. He introduced us to people, stories, and places that truly capture the heart of Valparaíso. We picked out where to eat and had plenty of time to chill and enjoy each stop. The experience wrapped up with a boat ride giving us a fresh view of the city, and finally, a visit to a super charming winery. Plus, Daniel took some fantastic photos along the way with his keen eye. I HIGHLY recommend this tour. The spots we visited were perfect, and Daniel's company made the trip even better. He shared so much about the history, geography, politics, culture, and traditions of the area, making the tour both fun and educational. This tour is a one-of-a-kind experience, perfect for anyone who wants to see Valparaíso beyond the usual tourist attractions. Every second is worth it, offering a genuine dive into the soul of the city. Review of: Street Art in Valparaiso and Wines in Casablanca from Santiago

review_text: The total W trail is about 55 miles (including a hike up to the second suspension bridge to see the Grey Glacier (or about 88 km). We booked all our refugios three weeks before the trip. We also booked breakfast and dinner at the refugios so we didn't have to carry food with us. The hot dinners are definitely worth the money! The breakfast not so much. We carried our clothes and a sleeping bag. Even then, the hike was tough. Lots of steep climbs, steep descents, rocky trails, and changing weather. We did the 5 day hike at the end of October and felt really lucky to be blessed with great weather. We didn't get rained on at all! We recommend bringing trekking poles, which can be rented in Puerto Natales at any of the hostels, as they are really helpful in navigating the many rocky paths. The hourly estimates are accurate for hikers who don't stop too much along the way. We took a lot of pictures and a lot of rests so we ended up taking longer than the park estimates. Go at your own pace and be aware of what your body tells you! Drink lots of water and don't forget the sunscreen! Make sure your lip balm has SPF coverage. The sun is fierce and the air is dry. You'll burn and not even realize it. Highly recommend this to anyone looking for a challenging getaway from civilization. The views are totally worth it!

review_text: We booked several tours though this company, the first we did was the Condor tour. Although we booked and paid online, and had confirmations for the tours, in the morning of the condor tour, we decided to pass by to go over all the tours. We go vouchers and some information on all the tours, and people were friendly, if a bit slow. The new offices (rough guide has the location wrong) is near the regional museum, in a very nicely converted old factory hangar. Something you expect to see in Europe and norther America, but was surprised to see in Chile. The condor tour leaves in the early evening, and they come to pick you up. Even though we passed by in the morning, they managed to forget us. After calling 3 times, a driver finally showed up, and drove us to the site where the condor viewing occurs. Best to speak some Spanish, as they do not speak English, and be insistent. This is on private land, and the group size was small, about 7 visitors in total. There are plenty of condors to see up on the rock formation. Hardly visible by naked eye, unless they fly, one can see them through the zoom of a camera, or through the bird telescope the guide had with him. That was a high quality telescope through which you saw the condors in all their details. He was also able to take pictures with cell phones and compact cameras through the telescope. The guide showed us male, female and young condors, was very knowledgeable and spoke good English. The condors here stop here only for a few days, but in good weather are very active. Many Thanks Katrien, All our staff try thier best to give the best experience to our travellers. Have a great trip back home!!

review_text: Overall, this trip was fantastic. The views were breathtaking, our guide Nicolás was incredibly helpful, nice, and informative, and the packed lunches were very solid. However, a few of us had issues with our snowshoes (mine in particular was broken and kept coming of my foot, causing me to face plant into the snow repeatedly). Also, be warned, this is a pretty difficult trek, so if you're not mentally and physically prepared for hours of hiking up the side of a mountain (60-70° angles at times) in meter deep snow, I wouldn't recommend it. If you are, it's worth the effort. Personally, it's crossed off my bucket list and I'll never do it again. Thanks for your review Nicole, We are glad you have had a great experience. We apologize about the issue with the snow shoe. We are improving our maintenance system over our gear, in order this will not happen again. About the difficulty, we label the trips with people of different shape and experience. So we make an average. How every person feels the difficulty will vary, as some people feels warm when others feels cold. Also on the mountains there are a lot of conditions which could change the difficulty as: wind, snow, mud, fog, temperature and so on. Other people think the trip is too easy. The mountain is always changing and the conditions change a lot when you have 40 centimeters of fresh powder. We think that's part of the adventure. There's no any place with steeps of 60° or 70 ° degrees. For that kind of steepness you will need ropes and bolts. This trip has been performed by children of 14 years on summer, and the path is almost flat on the 80% of the length without any slope of more than 20 degrees. Thanks again A.E Team

Apparently this is a national Chilean drink. It was ok but not that impressive. We also stopped at a office supply store where my wife bought a tablet for sketching and a note book for recording her thoughts about our travels. This was an interesting place and was jammed with people. It was fun and interesting to see.

review_text: These 4 tours were an excellent way to get an overview of some fabulous sites around the Atacama Desert. Our guide to Valle de la Luna and Cejar Lagoon was Giulia. She was excellent at explaining the surrounding landscapes in both Spanish and Italian. Her manner was welcoming and she was most informative. Our guide to the Geysers of Tateo was Nicole. She was passionate about the special places of the high Andes and was brilliant at describing everything. The only issue with these tours is everybody is doing them and you are just another white bus and at some locations it seems like everyone is there which deflates the experience. Nicole did take us to the white Geyser and this was a personal and much appreciated experience. There also seems to be this thing about providing cocktail and snacks or breakfast on a little table by the bus. All the buses do it and I wonder why? Sometimes it is unnecessary and you actually would shorten the excursion time if this wasn’t included and that would be preferable especially on the Geyser day when we had to get the bus at 4am! The other issue I had was being collected from our hotel and then dumped in town at the conclusion of the excursion . This is probably fine if your hotel is in St Pedro but a bit of a rude awakening if you have a 20 minute night walk in darkness back to your hotel because you assumed you’d be taken home. So some tweaking about what is important to people taking the tours would be helpful Review of: 3 Days and 4 Tours in San Pedro de Atacama

review_text: My friends & I were desperate to do a stargazing trip whilst in San Pedro de Atacama. My boyfriend researched the different trips available and found excellent reviews for this trip on trip-advisor. We emailed Jorge directly and booked our night. We were collected at 12.30am by Jorge from our hostel, we were a group of 6 and there was only one other person to join us, so it was an intimate affair. When we arrived at the site we had seats, jackets & blankets provided - which is needed as you must wrap up warm, it can get really cold! Jorge was so passionate about Astronomy, the stars, planets, galaxies, planets, moons, asteroids, comets. He taught us so much, as we were all beginners. After the first session, hot drinks & snacks were provided. Then in the second half Jorge showed us stars/planets through his telescopes, it was really amazing to see everything close up! We finished up at 4.00am and had some pictures taken with the stars/milkyway which look incredible. This is more expensive than the other trips, but worth every penny as Jorge is really nice, interesting & enthusiastic.

review_text: My husband and I had an amazing time with Tom. We have been on many wine tours around the world and this was one of the most fun and educational wine tours we've been on. We learned many new things about the wine making process such as the type of conditions to grow the vines in in order to produce fruits, the process for harvesting the grapes, the history of the Casablanca valley, the way to smell the wine to get its fruits, body, and alcohol, etc. Tom was very friendly and personable. We had a wonderful time visiting the three different vineyards with him. The booking process was very easy and Tom was very communicative throughout the entire process. There are many wine tour companies on tripadvisor. We picked this one because it was the most reasonably priced tour. You still get to visit 3 vineyards and have lunch (however lunch is not included in the price). Our lunch was a total of $80 USD for wine, appetizers, and entrees. If you do the math, that's an additional $40 per person, which was still more affordable than some of the wine tours that do include lunch in their pricing. I could go on about how wonderful the tour is and I'm pretty sure a lot of the reviews for Bodega Wine Tours will mention a lot of similar positive reviews. I highly recommend this tour if you love wine, are only dedicating one day to wine tasting and want a good overview of chilean wines, and like learning new and interesting things about wine.

The descent path, although long, is worth doing on foot due to the beautiful landscapes (the view of the snowy mountains in the background is much better in this part than at the top of the sanctuary) and because it has a good structure.

review_text: My wife and I visited Chile and Argentina for wine and culinary trip in February 2016 and Kingston Family Vineyard was one of the favorites. We did a total of 8 days tasting wines and 2-3 locations a day, so in total we probably visited 18-20 wineries. Kingston was the best total tasting... what do i mean by total tasting? Well, to start, we drink a lot of wine and have visited many wineries in our 15 or so years wine tasting and at almost every place we visit we might taste 4 or 5 wine and it is normal for us to like half or less of the wines we try. A good winery we like 4 of the 5 but it is pretty rare for us to like everything we try. Kingston was one of those rare exceptions. We tastes Sauv Blanc, Chard, two pinot's and a syrah and they were all very good. It may not be the style everyone likes and it is definitely not traditional California style that I think many American have become accustom to but I think that's why we liked it. Clean, fresh, low alcohol, high acids, minimal oak wines are really our thing so this fit the bill. The facility is small and truly boutique (we noticed in SA that the definition of boutique was loosely used.... there were some pretty monster operations claiming to be boutique). The tour is simple but informative but our guide Judith made the visit great. We loved it so much we joined their wine club and have a case arriving this week. Cheers! Thank you so much for your visit and extremely kind review. We're so happy to know that you enjoyed our wines so much, of the many that you tried on your trip, that you joined our wine club in the U.S. We hope you'll continue to enjoy our wines and that you'll come back and see us in Chile again soon!

review_text: This is an unexpected experience for both tourists and locals. Most people know little to nothing about the Bahai faith (I certainly didn't). This temple is set up for the curious, with helpful information and volunteers and an inviting atmosphere. The temple itself has remarkable architecture, I've never seen anything like it. The grounds have been nicely landscaped and make for a beautiful stroll. The temple is situated on the very eastern extremity of Santiago, edging up the Andes foothills. As all the reviews attest, it is hard to find a better vantage point from which to view the city, short of hiking up into the mountains. It is possible to get here by bus, though it is not a short trip. However, any tourist with more than 3 days in Santiago should put this on their itinerary.

review_text: We went to have lunch at Valle Hermoso, the page said they had thousands of activities but only the restaurant and the pools are working. At the entrance they told us that if we did not pay there we could not enter the complex. We paid $20,000 each to have lunch at the restaurant, telling us that there were many menu options. Once upstairs we were disappointed with the place, super basic, the service was friendly but not professional and the menus were really pitiful. We feel cheated for paying that price that anywhere else in Valle Las Trancas would have been a gourmet dish (we have been visiting several restaurants these days). Here, on the other hand, we went with the expectation of going to a very good place, understanding that it is part of the Nevados de Chillan company, however, the fibrous and greasy meat, the hard and undercooked fries, undressed lettuce (only one basic flask with fake lemon) and the menu only included a glass of machine drink. It's really a shame, it was like any roadside snack menu that would charge half the price for that dish. When asking if we could order separate beers, they told us that it could be a shield or glass. No comment. The environment is beautiful and has a lot of potential, but they should not promote that restaurant as something luxury, and charge as a luxury restaurant, when its standard of food, service, atmosphere, bathrooms, etc. is nothing more than a roadside shelter. Needless to say, for the price of admission they give you a bracelet and tell you that you can stay for a maximum of 1.5 hours.

review_text: This is a very nice tourist attraction near Santiago as long as you don’t expect a detailed explanation about wine production and processing. The guided tour presents some trivia about of Concha y Toro Winery’s history, and allows one to taste either three or seven different types of wines depending on how much you pay for the visit (I payed 12000 CLP for tasting three wines plus the visit). We are also given the chance to visit the places were they stock the barrels, including the original place the famous legend of Casillero del Diablo was born. The local restaurant is very good, although a bit on the expensive side. I had a delicious salmon and an exquisite tiramisu as dessert. To reach the place you can take metro line 4 at Tobalaba station until last stop at Plaza del Puente Alto. Then you can take a metrobus (paying about 600 CLP for the trip) or a taxi (paying about 3000 CLP). I took the bus and everything was fine. Total trip from Tobalaba takes about 1 hour and 15 minutes.

review_text: WOW! WOW! WOW! My husband found Vina San Pedro through Conde Nast Traveler and thought it would be a nice diversion on the road from Santa Cruz to Santiago. BEST DIVERSION EVER! On the approach to Vina San Pedro, you traverse through a small farming town at the base of the Andes. You need a reservation ~ made at least 3 days in advance - to gain admission to the vineyard. Plan for an even greater lead time during high season since the number of guests daily is capped. There is a checkpoint verifying reservations before admission is granted. Upon passing through the checkpoint, we were awestruck by the vistas and scenery on a gorgeous fall day. The winery / hospitality center is thoughtfully designed to blend into the environment in an unobtrusive way. Slightly down the hill, the open air restaurant Bodega Chachapoal Andes invites guests to savor the flavors and setting as if in a friend's beautiful home. Francisca, the Hospitality Manager, was an absolutely lovely host and sommelier for our visit. Her demeanor and company were delightful and gracious. We learned what distinguishes San Pedro's icon wines as the second largest wine producer in Chile and were treated to a tasting that was thoughtful and enjoyable. Our lunch experience at the Bodega was one of the finest we have experienced anywhere in the world. The portion sizes were beautiful. The ingredients fresh, exquisite, and innovative without being overly complicated in their combinations. And, the pairings with the San Pedro wines impeccable. We felt like royalty in the way were were treated and would go out of our way to experience Vina San Pedro / Bodega Cacapoal Andes again. It was hard to leave because the setting was so casual, comfortable, peaceful, and welcoming. If you want to feel special and experience something truly special, visit Vina San Pedro / Bodega Cachapoal Andes. We'll meet you there, as we plan on doing the bike tour next time we visit.

review_text: We recently completed an amazing trip to South America and one of our favorite places was San Pedro de Atacama. While all of San Pedro de Atacama is breathtaking, stargazing in Northern Chile was on my bucket list. I can check this one off the list because we had such an amazing experience with Jorge. Based on the reviews in Tripadvisor we decided to book with Atacam Desert Stargazing (i.e., Jorge Corante). When we booked the evening we were informed that there were 2 other couples for that evening. We were excited for a small group. However, that afternoon Jorge informed us that the other 2 couples canceled and he came to our B&B to give us the option of joining the group for the following evening as it would be cheaper. We appreciated his honesty, but decided to pay the extra cost for a private evening. It was absolutely magical. As all of the other reviews indicated, Jorge gives you a detailed lesson of astronomy, specifically related to the southern hemisphere. This is followed by a large spread of food and drinks, including hot chocolate, coffee, tea and soft drinks. The food is all prepared by his wife and was delicious. After the break we were treated to some of the most amazing heavenly sights. Jupiter with its moons, two galaxies and numerous other stars and clusters. Jorge taught us about the Southern Cross and how ancient mariners used the stars to plot their courses. Jorge is knowledgeable, friendly with a great sense of humor. If you are planning on stargazing while in Atacama, you MUST book with Jorge. You will not be disappointed!

Take some handkerchiefs with you, cause it is all heartbreaking, specially the drawings and stories of the children. Not recomendable for little kids, too difficult, a lot to read and sometimes too heavy for little ones.

review_text: I had been emailing with Jose for several weeks prior to our arrival in Santiago and he was very helpful and accommodating in planning our wine tour. Andrea gave us all sorts of historical and cultural information, and shared a lot of insight on the Casablanca Valley and the wineries we went to. California but we all learned some new interesting information at both the wineries. The lunch was at House of Mondreve and was excellent! The best wines plus really good food pairings with each course. The only down side was that the tour was a little expensive. While I was still in the US I got quotes from 2 vendors, and they were basically the same so I booked with Uncorked based on how great Jose was to communicate with. However, when I got to Santiago I found a few tours that looked similar for much less money. I would imagine/hope that the quality of the tour guide, information and vehicle was not as nice as what we got with Uncorked, but it's worth noting for those who want to shop around for the best price. It would have gotten a four or five star from us standing alone, but Stamps treated us so inconsiderately in the process we can’t unlink that from this tour. review_text: I had the pleasure of having both Felipe and Claire as guides and I had such an incredible trip as a result. One of my first excursions was the hike up to the French Valley. The weather had turned that morning, so all the other hikers had decided to switch to less demanding/shorter trails. After checking that I still wanted to proceed and providing a breakdown of what to expect, Felipe guided me through the hike and it was the best! Great pace, with amazing details of the terrain/geography throughout, and fun conversation. The weather didn’t even end up being much of an issue. To top it off, on the way back to camp we saw a whole family of pumas! With Claire I got to go hiking to this beautiful isolated farm, such a serene location with bird spotting along the way, and at the end we got to warm up around a spectacular fire to have a Chilean bbq and drink amazing wine. It was snowing lightly at the same time, which the trio of us visitors (from Aus & Brazil) were very excited about - It was such an idyllic moment for me. And the cherry on top has to be the trip to the Grey glacier, which is an awe-inspiring view, and as we were sipping some Pisco sours on the boat back, with clear blue skies above, it started hailing out of nowhere...so we tried to catch the small bits of ice in our glasses and had a great laugh with the (surprised) boat’s captain. I had so many fun and unique moments like that one on my trip because of them, that I would go back for another visit in a heart beat! Hi Sofia! It was so nice to meet you! Hiking the French Valley with you was so much fun! And then Claire took care of you the following days and she had the time of her life, specially when her pisco sour glass got filled with ice from the sky! Hope to see you again when you visit Patagonia! Best, Felipe y Claire.

review_text: This is the fourth year that I have used Uncorked in Chile. I keep coming back in November of each year for more and this time I brought a friend. Jose Miguel, Connie, and Andrea are terrific. They always make the wine trips pleasurable. I've been to some wineries previously and also some new ones. Every time I learn something more about the grapes and the wine process. There is so much to absorb. The lunches at the various vineyards are outstanding (too much food but very delicious). I've also had the opportunity to attend their cooking class on four occasions and the fantastic visit to the Central Mercado -- truly an experience you won't forget. review_text: This is a very somber museum, and definitely worth a visit if you want to learn more about the recent history of Chile, and other world human rights issues. The museum is free, and is literally connected to a Metro stop, so it's a very easy trip from the city center (also, there is a fantastic park across the street). Everything is in Spanish, so non-Spanish speakers should get the guide. Knowing some things about the desaparecidos in Argentina and some other South American countries (where no one admits to, or talks about anything), it was refreshing to see how Chile recounts their past (albeit appalling) and learns from it.

review_text: So, my Friend, I have just saved you a lot of time. There are very few things in life that I can recommend unconditionally, but our time spent with Mauricio earned that honor. My wife and I had a few days in Santiago before traveling to Portillo to ski. I did the exact thing that you are doing now -Yes, You!!! I hit the Internet to do some research. I saw some good reviews and made contact. Mauricio was very friendly and attentive by e-mail and offered several tour options of the wineries and asked about our preferences. He ultimately recommended one of the options to us, and guess what! It was not the most expensive!! He genuinely listened to us and also gave us a few tips regarding do's and don't' about our stay in Santiago before we even met him. On the day of our tour, he was very friendly and personable. Speaks fluent English! He brought us to a restaurant that serves authentic delicious empañadas out of adobe ovens and paired a wine for the occasion. He was very into wine pairings. So much so that at our third winery, we ate a five course sampling with different paired wines, and every food course was invented by him. What that means is that no one else in the restaurant was eating what we were eating, and every course paired about three or four flavors (ie. abalone, cous cous, tomatoes, and lemon) that were meant to be swallowed with the wine as well. This was our first trip to Chilè. I did not know what to expect. I have been on tours where tour guides have brought you to places and pushed you to buy the owners' wares. That didn't happen even once! I have so much more to say about our experience, but I just promised you that I had saved you time. So what are you waiting for? Go ahead and book! I promise you that you won't be disappointed, or you can hassle me and give me crap.

review_text: Last year I started planning a major six-week expedition through the southern half of South America, in Chile and Argentina. A friend of a friend told me about Carrie and Venture Patagonia. Working with them was the best decision I made on this whole adventure. When you travel to a remote place with a different language you need a partner. Venture is the perfect partner. My plan was to meet some college buddies in Santiago, rent a truck and drive to the southern end of South America - and back. The complexity of this trip cannot be exaggerated. There were multiple border crossings, vehicles picked up and dropped off in various cities, air flights to be coordinated, and a total of 18 stay overs. Carrie and Daniella found the coolest places to stay, the absolutely best guides and activities. In the middle of the expedition there was a major snafu that could not have been expected, and they jumped in to resolve it immediately, getting alternative accommodations, changing vehicles, booking new flights, etc. They were amazing. Carrie also has access to one of the best things we did on our whole trip - visiting and staying on the Estancia La Peninsula on the Fjord of Last Hope near Puerto Natales. It was amazing. It should be noted that Venture, not only knows Patagonia, but the entire countries of Chile and Argentina, which was essential because only half our trip was in Patagonia. Wow! Thank you for the extensive and great review! I know it takes time and we appreciate you making the extra effort. Your trip was fun for us to plan as well, and we so enjoyed getting to meet you. We travel extensively throughout Chile, Argentina and to Easter Island, always looking for partners, exemplary accommodations and unique experiences, in addition to making sure to cover the main attractions. It does help to be flexible and always be ready for unpredictable events, like the major 3 day ferry cancellation. We were happy to figure out an alternative and rework everything for that portion of your expedition. Best of luck in your adventures to come. If ever you return to Patagonia, we would love to welcome you back.

review_text: I didn't expect to have an experience so different from a typical tour. Instead of showing you some buildings and tell you things that you could find by yourself in Google, this was a passionate journey through the most important and tragic events in recent Chilean History. As an American, I was deeply (and sadly) unaware of how my country intervened and helped destroy the Chilean economy from 1970 to 1973. The impact of the US propped dictatorship is still felt everywhere you look in Santiago, and Chile in general. Apart from this, the guide was very warm and patient regarding my many questions. Walking tours aren't usually my cup of tea, but this time I wanted to try one and I was not disappointed at all.

review_text: Seeing a wild puma (aka cougar and/or mountain lion if you’re from the U.S.) in nature has been a lifetime dream, top on my bucket list, but I wanted to do it responsibly. No treeing the cats with tracker dogs. No radio collar tracking. Just an honest, respectful, naturally occurring and socially responsible sighting. I decided to go on a Patagonian puma safari only to be overwhelmed by all options when it comes to selecting lodging, a tracker and guide services in/near Torres del Paine, Chile. Ultimately I elected to stay at Refugio Laguna Amarga (see separate Trip Advisor review) in the heart of puma county and was fortunate enough to get a referral to a tracker named Jorge Cardenas, owner/operator of Wildcat Expeditions, and based on our experience the best puma tracker ever! Here’s some of what we think sets Jorge and Wildcat Expeditions apart from others - Jorge personally knows the owners of Refugio Laguna Amarga. He seems to know every square inch of the vast estancia (ranch) and where the cats are most likely to be seen. Most importantly, he is committed to sustainable puma eco-tourism as a win/win business model for the ranchers around Torres del Paine National Park. He is working with some of the most respected land owners and puma trackers in the area to catalog the resident pumas, learned their territories, patterns and habits. He is also supporting development of industry guidelines for the protection of the cats and to promote safe, responsible, wild puma viewing opportunities. Because of his knowledge and experience we saw puma everyday! So many I could never have imagined it. All they weren’t all distant sightings. Many were within 25-50’. Some even closer. One cat hiked along side us (or rather let us hike alongside her) for like 20 minutes. We got incredibly lucky and I don’t think it happens every time but we witnessed everything from lone cats, and cats with cubs, to rarely witnessed assertions for territorial dominance and prey take down. Any one element of our experience would have been enough to give Jorge 5 stars out of 5. We found him to be professional, knowledgeable and accommodating. Unlike other tour operators who only offer fixed tour dates/packages Jorge arranged a private 5 day tour for me and my husband on the dates that worked best for us. He offered us several lodging alternatives and hired a great guide (Cristian Asun) for us to supplement our experience. They went above and beyond to ensure we saw puma but also got to truly experience Patagonia - everything from meeting the locals, to learning the history, geology, flora and other fauna of the area including Chilean condors and flamingos and foxes. Our tour included hotel pick-up and delivery from Punta Arenas. Jorge even took us shopping on our way back to Punta Arenas the last day so we could pick up souvenirs and a much needed duffle bag! And when I told him one of his on-line photos had captured my heart he sent me a copy! What a nice man. Very special trip. Far exceeded our expectations and reasonably priced. Patagonia is not easy or inexpensive to get to. If you invest in going all the way down there and want to experience wild puma viewing at it’s best, do yourself a favor and hire Jorge Cardenas, Wildcat Expeditions. Thank you very much Kerry!!! It was truly a pleasure and honor to have taken you to see pumas.
