He is working with some of the most respected land owners and puma trackers in the area to catalog the resident pumas, learned their territories, patterns and habits. He is also supporting development of industry guidelines for the protection of the cats and to promote safe, responsible, wild puma viewing opportunities. Because of his knowledge and experience we saw puma everyday! So many I could never have imagined it. All they weren’t all distant sightings. Many were within 25-50’. Some even closer. One cat hiked along side us (or rather let us hike alongside her) for like 20 minutes. We got incredibly lucky and I don’t think it happens every time but we witnessed everything from lone cats, and cats with cubs, to rarely witnessed assertions for territorial dominance and prey take down. Any one element of our experience would have been enough to give Jorge 5 stars out of 5. We found him to be professional, knowledgeable and accommodating. Unlike other tour operators who only offer fixed tour dates/packages Jorge arranged a private 5 day tour for me and my husband on the dates that worked best for us. He offered us several lodging alternatives and hired a great guide (Cristian Asun) for us to supplement our experience. They went above and beyond to ensure we saw puma but also got to truly experience Patagonia - everything from meeting the locals, to learning the history, geology, flora and other fauna of the area including Chilean condors and flamingos and foxes. Our tour included hotel pick-up and delivery from Punta Arenas. Jorge even took us shopping on our way back to Punta Arenas the last day so we could pick up souvenirs and a much needed duffle bag! And when I told him one of his on-line photos had captured my heart he sent me a copy! What a nice man. Very special trip. Far exceeded our expectations and reasonably priced. Patagonia is not easy or inexpensive to get to. If you invest in going all the way down there and want to experience wild puma viewing at it’s best, do yourself a favor and hire Jorge Cardenas, Wildcat Expeditions. Thank you very much Kerry!!! It was truly a pleasure and honor to have taken you to see pumas.

review_text: Well, what can I say? I absolutely LOVED Jorges stargazing tour! I had been looking forward to it since before I even arrived in chile because I had read so many great reviews about his tour! However, I was persuaded to go on one of the generic stargazing tours with a company that was highly recommended to me by a few fellow travellers. Even though I enjoyed that tour, it didn't feel personal at all - the guys speech throughout the tour felt a bit rehearsed and it's quite crowded - all in all I did not get the experience I was after. So I was lucky enough to be able to go stargazing for a second time and was able to book in with Jorge! And I am so so glad that I did! The whole tour feels so personal from the moment he picks you up at your hostel until the moment he drops you off again! There were three other girls on my tour which was a perfect number to have a great personalised experience - he provides chairs and warm blankets whilst he teaches you about the night sky - Jorge also asked what our existing knowledge of astronomy was (which was zero for all of us!) and so he catered the lesson to our level of knowledge. He is also passionate when he is teaching you about the sky, I thought this was great as it shows that he loves what he does and wants you to love it too! The snacks and hot drinks he provided were perfectly timed and much needed in the cold dessert at night! He has a great selection of telescopes and has a good way of explaining what you are looking at, and being such a small group of people we had plenty of time to peer through the telescopes. And then there is the photography! He helps you with your camera settings to enable you to capture amazing images of the night sky - he also lent me a tripod :-) I think we all got carried away taking photos of the Milky Way for ages, but Jorge seemed very patient and was happy to help us anyways :) I would absolutely recommend spending the little extra and going for this amazing stargazing experience

review_text: My wife and I were looking for a way to see the Cochamó Valley on horseback and I can’t imagine having done such an amazing trip with anyone other than Southern Trips. Our gaucho, Fabian, was very inch the horse whisperer and mountain guide that we could’ve hoped for. Fabian was English speaking, kind, friendly and incredibly knowledgable. He also had the patience of a saint when it came to us riding our horses, since we were complete beginners. Regardless of our utter lack of experience the whole trip was made to feel natural and easy from the very start and thanks to the horses being so well-trained and good-natured, we didn’t have any problems whatsoever. Every day Fabian made us a nice, fresh lunch on the trail (salad and fruit etc) and in the evenings - a delicious dinner with Chilean wine, either in the log cabin (no electricity, but hot water and everything else you could ever need) where we slept in for two nights or at the Refugio (campsite) at the top of the pass in El Arco. Obviously, riding horses up a mountain might not be the cheapest option for trekking, but these guys were excellent value for money and worth every single penny. Not to mention the fact that after four days of riding we didn’t have a single blister or achy bone to speak of, which is always a bonus in this part of the world. If we’re ever back, we’ll be doing it again.

review_text: On a recent holiday to Chile we booked a small, private day trip to the winelands and coast through Servitour. Our very pleasant, friendly guide, Guillermo, arrived on time and immediately proceeded to point out places of interest and gave us a most informative overview of the city of Santiago and it’s people, while exiting the city. He was also more than willing to answer our many questions. Our first stop was Veramonte, a wine farm in the Casablanca valley. After tasting some very good Chilean wines it was time for an informative, interesting, educational ‘history lesson’ on how Chile as a country came into being. Guillermo’s extensive knowledge and story telling was highly appreciated by all. From there it was on to Vino Del Mar for a delicious seafood lunch followed by a visit to the unique Valparaíso. We thoroughly enjoyed our ride up and down the hills and photographing the many quaint houses, lovely wall art and beautiful views over the harbour. All to soon it was time to head back to the city with a welcomed coffee stop on the way. A memorable trip thanks to Guillermo! Cindy, Thank you very much for your more than positive feedback. We are glad you had a good time enjoying chilean wine and our dear city of Valparaíso. Hope to see you again. Best Regards.

review_text: We joined Spicy Chile's Patrimonial Route through the Brasil and Yungay neighborhoods because we hadn't explored these yet, and were so glad that we got to know them with Spicy Chile! Our tour guide Franco was super knowledgeable, enthusiastic and charming and it was great to learn more about these neighborhoods from him. He also stopped at a hole-in-the-wall empanada shop for a snack and we all loved the empanadas we tried there - and none of us in the group would have found this place without him. The stop at the historic Pelu­quería Francesa (an old-fashioned barber shop) and the adjacent French restaurant Boule­vard Lavaud were highlights of the tour - both well worth a visit and neither of them were in any of our guide books. We definitely felt that we got to know a part of Santiago that we would have missed without this tour and that goes beyond the 'beaten track'. Even though we have seen all the sights that are covered in the other two tours offered by Spicy Chile we are tempted to go on another tour with them, just because we know we would learn a lot more about Chilean culture, history and the city.

review_text: We were met at the San Antonio cruise port terminal by Fabian, an employee of HecTours. He was terrific! He was there waiting for us when we got off the ship! He brought a Mercedes van around to us, loaded our bags, and off we went! He was a great driver, spoke perfect English, and was full of information about the area as we drove toward Valparaiso. And he was "only" the driver! We picked up Felipe, the primary tour guide, as we approached Valparaiso. Felipe was born and raised in the area, and knew it like the back of his hand. Felipe told us all about Valparaiso and Vina del Mar while Fabian expertly navigated the car through narrow hilly streets. We checked out all the tourist sites, but then went through the back roads of the neighborhoods to get a real feel for the place and the people. He led us to a small local restaurant near the funicular where we enjoyed a delicious crab pie and corn pie for lunch and some local beer. Then we walked around the picturesque area and got some GREAT pictures! He even took us by a local candy shop known for its handmade lollipops! DELICIOUS! By the time Fabian dropped us off at the Marriott Courtyard in Santiago ( an absolutely fabulous hotel!) we were tired but excited after a great day. The next day HecTours picked us up at the hotel in a spacious, comfortable Mercedes van to tour the beautiful city of Santiago. Again, we had a very knowledgeable guide who knew all there was to know about the city. We weren't able to walk long distances, so he adapted his tour to a combination of driving and walking in areas that had plenty of shade and places to sit when needed. It was perfect! On the 3rd day, we ventured out in the comfort of our Merceded to Portillo, a ski resort in the Andes Mountains. Our driver had to negotiate narrow roads with over 30 hair-pin curves, stopping along the way to get pictures of the beautiful scenic drive. After enjoying the beauty of the mountainous area we enjoyed a great lunch at La Ruca, a favorite place for the local residents in the Aconcagua Valley area. For dessert, we headed to a winery! We were treated to a personal tour of the small, family owned Vina Peumayen Winery in Panquehue, Chile. Francisco, the owner's son, took us out to the fields to see where the grapes grow. He then took us back to the winery and showed us each step involved in harvesting grapes and making the wine. As our dessert, we sampled two of their best wines! We were even allowed to put the labels on the bottles of wine we purchased! Again, we were brought back to the Marriott Courtyard after a long but enjoyable day! If we get back to Chile, HecTours will be our guide again. They were right on time, every day. They were very personable and attentive. They adapted to our limited physical mobility with a very comfortable van and modified the tours to accommodate our needs. And best of all, their love of their city and country showed through every comment they made over the 3 days. You will NOT find a better tour company than HecTours to show you Santiago and the surrounding areas/

review_text: Laguna Verde is a saltwater lake located in Bolivia at the base of the Licancabur volcano, just past its remote border with Chile. For many people, myself included it is the first (or last depending on which way you are travelling) of half a dozen lakes in the 3 day 2 night San Pedro De Atacama to Uyuni salt flats tour. It's known as the green lake due to it's suspension of arsenic and other minerals which result in a turquiose appearance. When we visited I struggled to appreciate this colour. It was extremely windy and very cold. On the northern side is a hot spring which the tour normally stops at to allow people to have a dip. The temperature (heated by Licancabur) is lovely but unfortunately the outside wind is brutally cold meaning you never want to get out! Bring a towel!

review_text: We so looked forward to this trip from Puerto Montt to Puerto Natales and were not let down in the least, that despite appalling weather for the entirety of the voyage. The crew could not have been more kind and helpful, at all times they genuinely wanted to ensure you had a brilliant experience. One strange part of the trip was being required to board a day earlier (slightly annoying as it meant cutting short our horse trek) although in the end it was such a relaxing and comfortable experience that we didn’t mind at all. The first 24 hours was spent in the port whilst they loaded cargo and finally we set off around 8.00 pm after supper. The ship is so quiet it was hard to imagine we were even moving so sleep was not impeded at all, our four berth cabin was very capacious but I’m not sure I would’ve liked to share the space with two more people, it was perfect for the two of us, maybe we’re just too spoilt! Each day the bathroom was cleaned and bins emptied so we took care of keeping our beds tidy which was no big deal. There were only 45 passengers on board, I gather they can take up to 250, so also this could have been a defining factor as to why it was so special, by the end of the trip we were like a family. The food is served by the endlessly fabulous and friendly Anna (Anita) who we all fell a little bit in love with. Christian and Jose were always on hand to look after us, along with the purser who I’m ashamed to admit I can’t recall his name. And as for our Captain, he’s marvellously full of wit, fun, good information and clearly dedicated to his ship and crew. We were all invited up to the bridge which was fascinating. Throughout the journey we were treated to films regarding the area, some lectures describing what we would see along the way and talks about the geography and wildlife. There was a yoga/Pilates class offered free each day, games to play and you can never tire looking out at the changing landscape. Even in mist, rain and at times hail we ventured outside to take advantage of spectacular sights. One night was less soothing for sleep when we spent 12 hours out in the Pacific. Everyone on board was offered a sea sickness pill and as far as we’re aware no one was sick (we certainly didn’t even feel ill) despite being buffeted through the night with high seas and winds (I did mention we had adverse weather conditions). Apparently the passengers who’d done the trip in reverse had perfect conditions throughout and saw whales which was disappointing (not for them but for us). This said we would not have changed a thing, we just relaxed into it and enjoyed. Even when we arrived at Puerto Natales the wind was so high and we had to spend another night on board we laughed about how were being kept prisoner on the Esperanza; the 3 day cruise had now taken 5 full days. As our captain rightly told us at the first address, we are not travelling on a highway, this is the sea with all it’s complications. At no point did we ever feel unsafe or concerned, we knew we were in very safe hands. Thank you crew, you are all wonderful.

review_text: The bus tour from San Pedro de Atacama usually leaves at 4pm in order to catch the sunset. The area is only a few kilometres from the town and some companies will offer bike tours and walking tours. The first point of interest is the area of the 'Great Dune' which from an elevated viewpoint provides a magnificent impression of the entire area and truly conveys the enormity of the region. This part involves a short but steep climb but is well worth the effort. The next stop is to a number of rock formations known as 'The Three Marias' which are the result of differential erosion. The final stop here provides an opportunity to wander through the varied rock structures including a cave-like formation. Prior to sunset the tour groups converge on an overhanging area with a huge drop to the canyon below for photo ops and a chance to see the effect of the sunset on the changing colours of the rocks. There is a quick visit afterwards to the Valle de la Muerte ( Death Valley) before returning to San Pedro around 8pm. A good tour and not expensive at approximately US$20.

Next time I’m in Chile I’ll be back to see what is new there . One of the wines Velado was made by mistake via the 2011 earthquake. review_text: Beautiful place, with great potential for growth, however, it left something to be desired in terms of respect for Brazilians, highlighting that the country receives the most Brazilians. There are more than 500 thousand per year. We hope when we arrive at a place like this to have fun, play, forget our problems and not have bad memories. Example of treatment, the SKY school is terrible, teachers know a lot but they know, if you fall you turn around to get up, if they are Brazilians they forget that we understand Spanish and that they are swearing in another language. In other words, Brazilians are boring, rude, not quarrelsome. The people I saw stressed about receiving us were the ones who were being paid to teach us. I had an accident that could have been serious if I hadn't pushed my teacher and told him to get away from me. The steel cable grabbed and pulled along the back and I couldn't let go, I couldn't get up, it was 5 hellish minutes in which I could have seriously injured my back and never walk again. Where I only managed to free myself because I broke the cable hook and felt it from the clothes that grabbed it, there were 3 attempts and the 4th was the accident. I pushed him and broke with all my strength what was holding me back. Without air, married, and with a lot of equipment that in a few hours doubles the weight. Other than that, he leaves class immediately. I went away from them, and had fun alone on the mountain, because I felt safer away from them than with them. So here's the tip. It's a new sport, people have never done it, it's their first time, so go through a refresher course in human and technical treatment and then deal with human beings. I felt the lack of a helipad or an upa or an ambulance for emergency care. People get sick and may die due to a sheer lack of logistics and commitment. Maybe I wouldn't go back to Valle Nevado. But I sincerely hope that they improve their treatment and respect us. Because we are Brazilians. But Brazilians talk about their problems in their homeland and we do not accept anyone else calling us thieves or using xenophobic arguments when we are invested in leisure, respecting their space and culture. I loved Chile and hated the lack of respect for me and my family in Valle Nevado. Goodnight

review_text: We had a spectacular few days travelling to Uyuni from San Pedro. First of all - we booked through Lithium Aventura in San Pedro as they consistently received good reviews in the book in the tourist office, and no bad reviews at all. So when people say all the company's are much of a muchness I would protest strongly - choose wisely - there are good ones and bad ones - as you'd expect. The other company that had great reviews was Estrella Del Sur who were a bit more expensive. We paid 95,000 and Estrella was 105,000. We found when we got to Bolivia that Lithium often work with drivers from Estrella - which I'd heard before. Our driver Gendry/Henry (correct spelling?) was excellent. Super safe driver. As everyone says they only speak Spanish (what do you expect?! You've got a Bolivian driver!), but he gave us some explanations of the places we visited, and was friendly, and we shared some conversation with him. He was very kind in sharing loads of his coca leaves with us. The scenery is of course spectacular - loads of flamencos, stunning lagunas of different colours, amazing mountains and volcanos, desert, rock formations, and of course the salt flats! Which I actually thought beforehand might've been over-hyped - they're not! Great fun taking photos! The accommodation was pretty good - all seemingly booked ahead. Shared accommodation first night - I was expecting worse. It was clean, warm and tidy. Bathrooms were passable. We were expecting something closer to the refugios in Argentina - but it was better than that. At the end of the day, it's only a place to sleep and the bed was fine. Second night's accommodation in the Salt Hotel was fine too. Warm enough, and again passable bathrooms. Had showers, but I didn't use them - you have to pay a small amount - like 3 bol. Food the whole time was excellent - some of the best food we've had in south america! Breakfast and dinner we had a large buffet spread and in the evenings, a bowl of veggie soup with either pasta or chicken. Def bring a large 5L bottle of water with you though as they don't give enough water. Don't bother bringing snacks - they're not needed. There's too much food as it is! Honestly - don't let the stories about accommodation put you off, they're more than adequate. It was a great adventure shared with a great group of people. Don't worry about it - do it! Just don't try to save money by going with the really cheap ones - there's a reason they get bad reviews!! We went with one of the more 'expensive' ones and even then it works out very cheap.

review_text: The agency was good and responds fast to any questions. However, our guide Valentina was no so good. We were taken to a tourist trap in Viña Del Mar, we were taken to Chinqui restaurant a super expensive restaurant where we felt obligated/forced to eat there, she did not tell anybody that it was our last stop and to go explore the town after lunch (I did) but a lot of people didn’t because they were under the impression that we were going to continue with the tour. We should have the options or given the options to eat anywhere we want and not to be taken to that expensive place and pretty much be forced to eat there. The picture of the meal im leaving here was $36 dollars which it was ridiculous. The food is not great the salad was whole leaves of lettuce, no dressing or lime even when I asked for it. Valentina created a WhatsApp group and told everybody she was going to send us a link to leave a review but she removes the people she think were not satisfied with the tour so we don’t leave reviews. She really needs to communicate and be clear with the itinerary. Again the agency was good and if you do this tour make sure you find your own place to eat. Definitely avoid Chinqui restaurant…or avoid any restaurant your guide takes you to, find your own you will find better and cheaper food… Review of: Full Day Tour in Valparaiso and Vina del Mar it's unfair for you to reduce our tour to one star just based on your self-chosen food. It's not true what you're saying about being forced to eat where we left off. We understand your dissatisfaction with the food in the country, but all tourists know that eating in Chile is expensive. This is not under our control, there are other options for you to choose next to the restaurant. You are on a shared tour, there is a lunch stop. We cannot be letting everyone eat to their own personal taste as it is a shared tour. Imagine if we were going to take each one to lunch in different places.

review_text: We went kayaking with Kayak Chile for a 1/2 day trip on the Lower Liucura. They were very organized and asked a lot of questions about our ability before we went, so I felt they were a safe company. The first part of the river was Class I but beautiful and I hadn't been in my boat for a few years, so I didn't mind. We took a very short hike to some beautiful falls, and shortly thereafter stopped for a lunch of sandwiches, fruit, chips and cookies (yum). For the second part of the trip, the rapids stepped up quickly - wave trains and one rapid with a rock garden that you are supposed to avoid, which I went through. Our guide Marshall explained each rapid before we went down, which I really appreciated. We also went through Kayak Chile to do the Volcan Villarica, but we ended up not being able to do it due to weather conditions on the mountain. I would highly recommend this company! Happy we were able to get you guys on the Liucura! Its still one of my favorite rivers around here. Hopefully next time the weather will cooperate and you guys can get on the Volcano. review_text: Beware of Tourist Offices advertising that anyone can reach the summit with no previous experience. They just care about your money, not your safety.They don´t tell you that during the winter the climb is way more difficult. Halfway, you find yourself being exposed to life-threatening hazards with limited safety equipment that you cannot use because the guide still didn´t teach you how. Sometimes you face some huge, very slippery, nearly 45-degree slope glaciers to climb. If you fall, the only chance is stick your Axe into the ice, or you´ll be plummeting to your death. The weather can be unstable even on sunny days. Strong winds and snowstorms add extra burden to walk on snow up to our knees carrying a 40-pound bag over your shoulders. I am not a professional climber, but I am a runner, in good fitness. This is not an ordinary hiking, it´s a beautiful but very dangerous and exhausting adventure. We hired Patagonia Experience Agency in July 2014. Our guide was both professional and sarcastic. Maybe he was not interested in summiting the volcano, so he kept trying to discourage us with ominous comments. Because I could not keep the pace, he told my wife that I was climbing "another" mountain. Then I realized that this guy was treating me like an idiot, so I decided to quit. This was definitely not a delightful adventure. Expensive and risky. Not recommended.

review_text: We did a five day horseback riding tour with Horseback Riding Patagonia by Vicki Mattison in February 2018. We rode for 6-7ish hours a day and stayed at amazing estancias, all well organized by Vicki. We can't say enough about the trip. We rode out from different estancias, on different horses, out to Torres Del Paine park and saw so much. It's hard to capture. She organized it all and we had a guide the whole time who worked with us and the ranches to ensure a great adventure. The gauchos spoke a Spanish variation, often no English, and our guide was invaluable. We rode out to a glacier, up on a mesa, up and around the park. We saw so much more of the park on horseback than you can see on foot in the same time allotment, in part because the terrain is rough and the horses can navigate it quicker than we could ever on foot. The guide ensured our breakfast, picnic lunch, and great dinners at the estancias. Vicki provides great direction on what to bring and what to be prepared for and managed all concerns. We had a very last minute change due to one section of our planned trip being flooded out from the glacier melts and we ended up at an amazing estancia with what was close to a 4 star accommodation and Michelin restaurant - in the middle of nowhere! It was a pricey adventure but so completely worth it. Breathtaking views, great horses, long gallops across pampas, agile climbs, long rides with great refreshments and meals. Not for a beginner rider for sure. One of us was a near beginner but very athletic and confident and the other is an experienced trail rider. You should have some experience in cantering/galloping before going because you start that almost from the beginning as you need to get from ranch to ranch over the course of the day. The weather is variable - from strong sun to high winds to horizontal rain pelting you - all in one day. We rode up slippery rock to a mesa and the horses never flinched or lost footing. The ranch horses varied in comfort but the saddles were very comfortable and we experienced minimal discomfort at the day's end. But then you return to a place with a bed, hot water, great food, staying with locals who were very willing to talk with you about the area, the culture, the changes due to climate changes, the challenges of living out so far from amenities. Do not expect bars, dancing, clubs, nightlife. You are in people's homes or cabins and you have long days of riding ahead of you. Not for children. Not for people who aren't flexible and prepared for rapid weather shifts. Vicki is a wonderful hostess and organizer. Our guide was well versed in the area, the flora and fauna, the terrain, and helpful with getting adjusting to the gaucho riding style. We crossed rivers, climbed mountains, saw burial sites, lots of animals. It's incredible to be out where for miles there is nothing but wild land, free of civilization, guarded by watchful guanacos on crests who call to the herd below of your approach with high pitched bleeting calls. An amazing trip. An amazing adventure. Travel there was long from the US but relatively easy. You take a bus from Punta Arenas to Puerto Natales and Vicki meets you there. We stayed a couple of days first in Punta Arenas and did the penguin tour which is also very cool. The buses are easy to find and navigate. We stayed a few days in the lodge by the park entrance after our tour, did more local riding and the hotel shuttled us to the airport, which was several hours back to Punta Arenas. Take all meds, batteries, sun screen, and personal needs stuff - no markets or drug stores or stores at all for that matter once you leave Puerto Natales. Highly recommend the tour and Vicki.

review_text: Cerro Concepcion and Cerro Alegre, above the port, are to be seen together and represent the epitome of easy living by the Europeans in the 19th century. Take a look at the Anglican and Lutheran churches, which are among the best preserved buildings in the town. But mainly admire the lovely mansions which house all kinds of art galleries, bars, restaurants and boutiques. The best of those are in Calle Lautaro Rosas, up on Cerro Alegre. Browse the books in Casa E; look at the etchings of the brilliant Chilean artist, Jorge Martinez-Garcia, and his talented wife Herna, in the Taller de los Alquimistas; wander round the boutiques and tea shop across the road at no. 377. Go by foot, take your time, adjust to the pace of life. Then go and see the Palacio Baburizza and enjoy the art.

The most obvious comparison is to the archaeological museum in Mexico City, which is bigger, of course, and has the famous show-stopper pieces that everyone wants to take photos in front of. This may be heresy, but I prefer this museum in Santiago. I was just as awestruck by the beauty but found it more manageable.

review_text: Whether you're stargazing enthusiasts or a novice, I think you'll get a great experience out of Jorge's tour. We are novices taking the TAT tour and saw some really amazing stars (and even some planets!). Don't go with just any tour (or think you can just drive anywhere in the desert for the same views). Jorge has his own piece of land, ideally situated with clean skies (and impossible to find in the dark by anyone but Jorge). His set-up is really cool -- he has many types of telescopes, but also blankets for the chilly night air, and puts out a nice spread of food/drinks too (there are also porta-potties on property). Jorge also has a camera set-up that allows him to take high-res photos of your group against the starry skies, it's a great keepsake especially since your regular phone cameras won't really be able to capture the magic. Jorge is not only knowledgeable, warm and organized, but his passion & enthusiasm for stargazing is so infectious, you'll come away with a new appreciation (maybe even obsession) for it!

review_text: We had read hilarious good & bad reviews about the Navimag trip from Puerto Natales to Puerto Montt so had low expectations. We sailed on Eden and found it comfortable and a very old fashioned kind of slow travel: no wifi, no real coffee, no entertainment and no alcohol (so smuggle some on board if you need a drink). The staff were cheerful and the food was plain but fresh. We read books, played cards, chatted to other travellers (who all had good stories and/or were doing interesting trips), and watched the sea for hours (saw almost nothing other than 2 dolphins briefly on the last day and seals in Puertto Montt harbour). The weather was grey and wet and visibility pretty poor for all three days. And, contrary to reports of delays, we arrived in Puerto Montt 10 hours early. We enjoyed it - one of the most relaxing things we've ever done.

review_text: La Moneda is located on Constitution Plaza. My wife and I tried to get into the palace but we were told by the policeman outside the palace that we were not permitted to enter because it was an operating government building with the office of the President of Chile. One of the guidebooks told us that we could get in if we showed our passports but, since we did not have them with us, we were unable to go inside. The architecture of the palace is beautiful and could compare with the White House in the United States. The palace was bombed by Chilean jets and was gutted by fire on the first day of the Pinochet coup of September 11, 1973. Obviously the palace has been completed restored. The Museum of Memory has videos of the bombing of the palace and pictures showing the results of the fire that gutted the building.

review_text: If we hadn’t had a guide in ‘Valpo” we would have completely missed the essence of the city. We might have thought to ourselves, “actually some of that graffiti was pretty good” and left with memories of the absence of greenery and prevalence of dog poops. But when you have a guide like Jorge Rodriguez of Perro Tours who can show you the symbolism, and bring home the emotion and struggle of hundreds of years under various foreign rulers to help you appreciate the mural art as an urban storybook to emotionally access your appreciation of the history of the city. Also the community caretaking of a very obvious and healthy appearing feral dog population was heartwarming. Feeding bowls were everywhere and no hostility noted among the pooches. We were fortunate enough to have Jorge as our guide,whose understanding of the art and the local artists was firsthand to the point of his actually having helped a well known muralist with one of his works and himself placed a bathtub in the center of a pedestrian street. Valpo is a work of art and deserves more tour guides like Jorge. Highly recommended.

review_text: I hate to give my first cat-skiing experience a poor review but I feel it's important to be honest. I booked a trip with Santiago Aventures to have a variety of snowboarding in Chile since I probably won't be able to go back. I was most excited about Arpa and I was the most let-down by my experience. Pros: The views are beautiful and unlike another review about the guides, our guides were really great. They were upbeat and funny to chat with. Cons: It hasn't snowed much and this does not stop them from taking your money. There was definitely not enough snow, it was icy and slippery and the conditions were so irritating to ride that I couldn't wait for the day to be over. If you have the luxury of booking a trip on a whim, PLEASE check conditions first. I had done Machu Picchu before my snowboarding week and since that was booked 6 months in advance, we had the whole trip previously planned-not based on weather. They also try to make it seem like it's the greatest experience but its not. We did 4 runs, on east coast conditions and they don't provide any food - they actually charge for 2 inch sausages they cook on the grill afterwards! I had done Harris's heli-skiing in NZ and it was double the price but it was also double the runs and they provided an awesome lunch in the valley. I cannot recommend Arpa unless it has snowed because as a business, they will sell you that it's great but it was not if it hasn't snowed. I'm an East Coast snowboarder in Vermont and I'd equate the conditions as worse yet they still take your money to take you out.

review_text: In spite of last minute scheduling, Tom arranged a fantastic day for my first introduction to Chilean wine tasting. Placed in the very capable care of Leo (careful driver, translator, tour guide, historian, and great guy), thoroughly enjoyed several micro wineries, the history, approach to wine making, and the exceptional wines produced in Aconcagua Valley. Vina Sanchez de Loria provided an in-depth tour of their facilities and a lovely tasting with a spectacular view! El Escorial provided a fantastic tour and thoroughly delightful tasting in the underground storage cellar. Next was an informative tour at Flaherty micro winery for a fantastic premium wine tasting with cheese and charcuterie board in the cozy comfort of lovely garden. Lastly, a quick stop at Vina Almendral to sample traditional sweet Chilean wines (not my usual preference, but pleasantly enlightened by the clean, fresh flavors of the numerous flavor options). A thoroughly enjoyable day and the excellent wines Chile has to offer!

review_text: It sure was cool to be able to go kayaking in the Strait of Magellan. The area is stunningly beautiful. We were picked up from the pier where our Norwegian Cruise Lines ship pulled in. Unfortunately, our ship arrived at a different place than anticipated. Had we not had a cell phone, we would have missed the whole tour. It seems that NCL didn't update its information so it wasn't necessarily the tour company's fault. But, we were a bit frustrated. We elected to go for the 1/2 kayak trip. The gear was top quality. The over-clothes were comfortable and warm. It was very windy when we went. There were five guide kayaks for the three guest kayaks. We couldn't go very far or fast because we had to stay in convoy with two other boats with people who had never been kayaking before. So, while we'd hoped for a bit of adventure, we did a lot of waiting. That was frustrating considering how much we'd paid for the trip. We were quite capable and yet were never trusted. The after-paddle snack was pretty tasty though not substantial. But, we had a lot of fun with the people that we met - once the kayaking part was over.

review_text: It was an absolutely amazing experience – everything about it was wonderful. The team that you have in Punta Arenas were friendly and helpful, the crew onboard (those that we came into contact with at least) were friendly, the food was great, the guides onboard were knowledgeable, fun and informative, and the vessel itself… where do I start… The whole experience was quite exceptional and far exceeded my expectations. Of course, it was a great shame that there was a Covid case on the voyage which zapped a couple day from our excursions, and then it was even more of a shame that due to the high winds in the Drake we had to return to Frei a day early – but we completely understand why and everything was communicated to us very openly, effectively and efficiently. In our own case we were able to make very good use of the ‘extra’ time, and went up into Torres del Paine to look for (and find) pumas – so there was no time wasted. I thought the ship was absolutely superb and can say that without question it is the best expedition ship I have ever been on – it is also the only purpose-built expedition ship I’ve been on. I liked the size of it (even if it had been full), the comfort level, the thought that had been put into the ‘public’ spaces (lounge, library, lab etc), and the way that embarkation and disembarkation occurred on the zodiac deck – it was brilliant. In fact, if there was any criticism it was that it was almost too luxurious and that because of the huge floor to ceiling windows in the cabins there was no real need to be out on deck. That is ridiculous of course, and Nicky and I were on deck as much as possible (I suspect far more than any of the other passengers actually), and the layout of the bow and stern viewing areas was also excellent for photography which is a big part of any trip that we offer. If there was any ‘regret’ about the trip it was that we were unable to spend time on the bridge, and that ‘mingling’ with other passengers and the guides etc at dinner and in the bar (which can be a most enjoyable part of any expedition voyage) wasn’t really possible – but that is a product of travelling in the Covid era rather than anything else. And, we were obviously very lucky to be able to travel when we did, especially as I understand that the following voyage was cancelled due to the high winds preventing the DAP flights from going across the Drake. Dear Chris, Thank you for your positive feedback regarding your trip with Antarctica21. We are glad to hear you had an exceptional experience on board on Magellan Explorer and that you are understanding of the current situation due to the pandemic and the unpredictable weather in Antarctica that can result in changes to the itinerary. It is great to hear that you enjoyed the cruise experience on our custom-built ship designed for Antarctic expedition travel. Our polar guides are passionate and knowledgeable about Antarctica and enjoy sharing this with our guests on board and on land. Thank you again for taking the time to share your experience with us. Best regards, Crystal Manafi Marketing Manager at Antarctica21

review_text: Javiara our tour guide and Manuel our driver were terrific. Javiara was waiting just outside the port - as described - and easy to find. We waited for about 15 minutes for other passengers to get off the ship. The morning was perfect with both volcanos out as we drove to the Petrohue falls. Javiara provided much information. We crossed our fingers that Osorno would still be out when we arrived to the falls but she was already behind clouds by the time we reached the falls. An opportunity to take a picture of Osorno by the lake was lost because so many of the ship's tour buses stopped at the pull off, so our bus didn't get any good pictures of Osorno. I would recommend to Javiara that anytime the Volcano is out - STOP THE BUS - so the tourists can take a picture. I am very disappointed by missing this opportunity. That aside, we had a short time in Puerto Varas - although there was a lot to see. We hurried to Fruttillar where we had more time to walk around a smaller town - than Puerto Varas. I would rather have had more time in Puerto Varas. .Frutillar has few shops but it does have an amazing bakery with German-inspired kuchen. All in all it was a fabulous full day trip. Review of: Frutillar, Puerto Varas, and Petrohué Waterfalls Excursion from Puerto Montt

review_text: We did three tours with Atacama Magic: Valley of the Moon with Gustavo, Rainbow Valley with Denny, and Salt Flats Route with Felipe. We enjoyed all three tours. Communication is through What’s app and is very good. Pickup for the tours all went well and the drop off point was in front of our hotel. The Valley of the Moon tour involves driving a few minutes to the park, doing an easy hike in the park to see beautiful scenery, a quick stop at one other portion of the park, and then driving to an overlook nearby to watch the sunset with snacks. Rainbow Valley is about an hour drive each way and then a walk through the park to see the scenery. We also saw llamas and donkeys on this tour. Breakfast is provided. Both these tours are easy 1/2 day tours. The Salt Flats Route is an all day tour with lots of driving stopping at various points to take photos. Both breakfast and lunch are provided. We got up to about 16,000 feet on this tour. One caution - there are no public bathrooms on this tour. All three guides were very knowledgeable. We had a very positive experience with this tour company.
title: Good tours of the Desert!

review_text: I was in Puerto Varas, Chile for a business event and had the opportunity to get out in the Patagonian wild for a few fantastic paddling days before all the work started. We were given nearly 50 choices of activities, but I chose Yak Expediciones' seakayaking offer because of the great location and the mixture of both nature- and culture-based elements. The trip was great because there was definitely plenty of paddling (10 km / 6 mi the first day and approx. 30 km / 18 mi the second day) but also other unique pieces to make it feel like a well-rounded experience! We visited a small, local hot springs resort on Llancahué Island for a relaxing break, saw lots of wildlife (like sea lions, birds, pelicans), and camped on the land of a local family, taking dinners in the house together with the matriarch. Technically speaking, the paddling was easy for me, although some heavy winds on the first day added some excitement in the form of hard paddling through high waves! (By the way, I love to go kayaking but I'm not a total river-rat, so this experience was suitable for a wide range of experience levels.) The weather for us was very comfortable - overcast, although I still got a lot of sun on my face. It was calling for rain, though, so an open mind, ready-for-anything attitude, and good waterproof gear is highly recommended :) For me, the natural look of the Pumalín Park and Lakes Region was the biggest draw, but it was the cultural elements - eating home-cooked food and hearing about personal life stories (in Spanish) from the host - which were absolutely the most memorable! Come paddle with Yak Expediciones if you want both an exciting sea kayaking experience and a taste of the local culture at the gateway to Patagonia!
title: Fantastic Paddling Days in Pumalín Park!

title: Stars Travel, 100% Recommended

review_text: Just thank Leonidas and Jordan for their magnificent tour, both very kind and friendly. Thanks guys!!!
title: Magnificent Astronomical Tour

review_text: A wonderful morning on the river with Guillermo and Lorenzo. Every detail was taken care of - excellent communication, enthusiastic knowledgeable and safety conscious guides, quality equipment and most importantly a beautiful river to paddle on. Highly recommended if you want a refreshing natural experience rather than an adrenaline hit. review_text: We have been using Sol y Nieve for years. They are extremely professional and focused on making your experience spectacular. Wether it's river rafting, volcano climbing, fishing, horseback, canyoning or just going to The 'Quincho' for a asado it is always a satisfying time.

review_text: Our taxi driver recommended this stop and we are glad we did, we spent about 45 mins walking the gardens and grounds, and going to the top of the mirador. Beautiful views. The Castillo hildago wasnot open for visiting, but it was a nice experience anyway.
title: Stunning gardens in springtime.

review_text: After visiting the deserts in Peru and Bolivia I was thinking of skipping this one but I was glad I did not. It was the most spectacular and divers one. We booked a tour via our hotel, there are a lot of tour operators in town. Highlights were the salt caverns and the dunes at sunset.
title: Unique landscapes

review_text: It was very good, entertaining and knowing a little about its history and culture thanks to the Guide and the driver who transported us and who played good music.
title: Excellent and I recommend it

review_text: An absolutely incredible Farmers type vegetable market. They also have Meat and Fish it's really a pretty authentic experience. I paid about dollar a pound for cherries and strawberries and had a thoroughly enjoyable time looking at everything else
title: Amazing veggies

review_text: We had to leave at 4.30 am for a very windy drive to the geysers, arriving about an hour before sunrise. I was told that the fumeroles stopped after sunrise, but this was not the case, so we could have left a bit later. The geysers were not large like others I had seen. We did not swim in the hot pool. This is high, at least 13.000 feet so walking fast became rather an exertion.
title: fumeroles on the high plain

review_text: There was a cheery atmosphere with drinks and a fire. We sat on hay bales and were given blankets. However, the astronomy viewing was very basic. We didn't view anything more than I can see in my home backyard with my basic telescope(the moon, Saturn and the moons of Jupiter). Since we had the clear skies of the Atacama, I thought we would get to see more but that didn't happen. The picture taken of us against the backdrop of the stars was a nice touch. We also got impressive moon shots that were taken through the telescope with our phones.
title: Basic astronomy visit to the Atacama

review_text: The truth is we ended up here because the line for the funicular at Cerro San Cristobal was over an hour so we left (so note -- go to San Cristobal early if you want to ride up). But this stop was great too! A nice walk up the hill to see beautiful mountain views and it was all free. Nice fountains, old remains of forts and towers on the site. Definitely worth a stop for 45 min. to an hour especially on a nice day. We walked from Cerro San Cristobal and it was about a 15-20 min. walk.
title: Nice walk up and nice views

review_text: This is one of my favourite places in Santiago. A small neighbourhood, ideal to shop and good coffee or some cocktails and dinner. Very near to Santa Isabel station (Subway Green Line).
title: Great idea for a city weekend

review_text: German emigration required their own brewery and the owners built this house which has many rooms furnished as in the mid C19. Enjoyed it!
title: A little piece of Germany in Chile

review_text: We arranged for Michael to transport us from our hotel in Santiago to our hotel in Valparaiso based on Tripadvisor reviews. Thank you Tripadvisor! We started with tours of two vinyards in the Casablanca Valley and then the beautiful little fishing village of Quintay for a delightful lunch. Like others we went with Michael to visit his elderly friend and see his private museum in Quintay. There is no way to describe what that visit is like, but don't miss it if get the chance. We needed to call home because a dear friend had died the day before and Michael took us to his lovely apartment for the call. It was a day we will never forget.
title: Wonderful day with "The Pirate"

review_text: some very interesting period artifcats from the days before Europeans - you don't need more than 45 min to work through this museum but worth a vists for sure - close to Plaza das Armas
title: interesting if a bit small

review_text: The best way to see them is taking a boat trip from Zapallar. Very important to have binoculars. But from land and good birding equipment (Binoculars and a scope).
title: Good place for Humboldt Penguins observation.

review_text: Catherine was our guide, very entertaining and organized, with Alex in driving we had a great day!! The cocktail before sunset was really exquisite!!! My son is happy with everything he learned. Highly recommended Review of: Half Day Tour to Valle de la Luna

review_text: Be sure to stop by to enjoy some of the fresh seafood available. I especially like the smoked salmon and the smoked cholgas. The small restaurants along the road are generally good and reasonably priced. The markets are good for souvenir shopping. There are boats to cross to the island (for a small fee) where you can walk up to the cross on the hill to see the Puerto Montt shoreline. If you want a cheaper, more authentic seafood market the one in Calbuco (about an hour south) is nice, quiet, and has good, cheap seafood. Most everyone in the area is friendly and welcoming.
title: Shopping, seafood restaurants, and fish market

review_text: Note 10. Perfect service! They follow every step of the journey. They don't leave you in the hand. Needing is just call you are always ready. Vanessa who took care of me is amazing! I will return to travel with them🙏 Nossa equipe fica extremamente feliz sabendo que sua viagem se concretizou e que pudemos gerar a melhor experiência que o Chile pode proporcionar ❤️🇨🇱

review_text: 6 of us spent a special 3 nights with the family in this amazing location. Got away from it all with no internet and power only 5 hours a day. The warmth of the welcome from the family was amazing and genuine especially the hosts birthday celebration. There is a double room and another with 4 bunks so it’s all a bit cozy. Spotted seals and dolphins from the front garden. Did the one hour horse ride and a full day trek. Difficult to wander off and do your own walking through the thick scrub so you need the guide or just sit bank and drink in the atmosphere Thank you very much for your comment, it's good to know that you were happy during your stay, we hope to see you again soon, a hug from all our Mercedes family.

review_text: I wanted to thank the Experience area enormously. Due to the rains, we could not make our walk to the hill, (as a youth church group) and the workers Camila Orrego, Antonella Valenzuela and Tomás Binder, contacted us via wasap from the previous day, answered kindly all our questions, keeping us informed about the process. We appreciate knowing that there are people behind a wasap, and that these people are willing to help. Excellent service! review_text: I could almost swear the masseuse had three or four hands. She was a godsend to my poor aching back. Highly recommend!
title: Magic hands

review_text: We are travelling through Chile specifically to see the wildlife. The first time we arrived here there were no boat trips running as the sea was thought too rough. There is no harbour so people just have to walk into the sea to get into the boats. This means it has to be really calm to run the boat trips. The lady looking after the toilets (300 pesos a go) told us it would be a few days before the boats would be running. So we went elsewhere and returned a week later. We did enjoy excellent views of Skimmers on the beach though. On our second visit the boats were running. We put our name down on the list, 6000 pesos each, and waited for the next boat. Each boat takes 15 people and a loudhailer calls you when a boat is ready to depart. We waded into the sea about 8 inches deep and were helped on to the boat. Life jackets provided. Then we had a trip to the island but did not see any large concentrations of birds. Just a few Humboldt penguins and Peruvian pelicans and some sealions. The small boat was full, so photography was difficult. We think the Humboldt Pinguinos Islands are better- at least for us!
title: Not many birds!

review_text: This is a great way to see Santiago. Andre is a great guide and has an inspiring passion for his city, Santiago. Not only do you get to visit the main parts of the city, but also the back-streets where you get to see fantastic architecture, beautiful parks and learn a lot about the history of the city. The bike's are great, and the cycling is very easy and enjoyable. Definitely do this tour when you are in Santiago.
title: A must do in Santiago

review_text: I loved visiting the Concha y Toro vineyard. The guide Germán Guajardo was great and the driver Gabriel also deserves compliments. All the professionals of the vineyard served us super well, it was muuuuito good! The tasting was delicious and the gardens were beautiful. Review of: From Santiago: Viña Concha y Toro Traditional Half-Day Tour Muito obrigada por compartilhar sua experiência tão positiva! 😊 Que bom saber que você amou a visita à vinícola Concha y Toro e que Germán Guajardo e o motorista Gabriel contribuíram para tornar o passeio ainda mais especial. É maravilhoso saber que o atendimento foi excelente, a degustação deliciosa e os jardins encantadores. Esperamos te receber novamente em futuras aventuras pelo Chile! 🍷🌿✨

review_text: I spent two days touring the beautiful city of Valparaiso on foot (and funicular) with Juan. He was one of the best guides I have had when touring a new city/country. Juan was insightful and talked a great deal about the country, the city, socialism, food, Chilean pesos, culture, etc. all of the things I love learning about when I visit a new country. I cannot say enough good things about the tours I enjoyed. Thank you Michelle for sharing your experience with Perro Tour with other travelers! It was a real pleasure to me to show you my loved Valparaíso for two days and I am, of course, sincerely happy that your time with me was super and enjoyable. Thank you!
title: Two Super Days Touring with Juan

review_text: Before my vacation I kept reading how Enotour was Chile's wine experts. With that comes an expectation that all aspects of a tour would be exceptional...especially when I paid US $380 for a full day private excursion. The vineyards I visited were Vina de Martino and Vina Perez Cruz and they were both awesome. The guides representing these places were informative and they were proud to show off their grapes (!) What I was disappointed in were the following. If Enotour calls themselves tour experts, and charges premium rates, they should also include the aspects of their organization too. 1. Communicate with the wineries - going forward, it would be helpful if Enotour communicated with the wineries in advance so there won't be duplicate information. Enotour should have checked to see what information would be highlighted and discussed. As a result, I found the information repetitive but was respectful when I heard the same discussion from the vineyard staff. 2. Be prepared - my Enotour guide should have researched lunch options in advance instead of the driver trying to find a possible place to eat. Did the guide ever touch base with the driver before the tour to make sure there were options? If this "Maipo Valley Full Day" tour is offered in their brochure, you would think Enotour has a list of places that worked for others. I understand about limited options in the wine region but I don't understand why we had to stop and ask a local person and turn the car around to go in the right direction. When we finally found a place 1 1/2 hours later, the local whole in the wall restaurant was certainly not as identified in the brochure "after enjoying a leisurely gourmet place". They didn't event have bottled water available. The "pear" drink that was available was sickening sweet and not thirst quenching. The food was passable as I was really hungry but felt it was not up to Enotour standards, 3. Know your audience - This might be picky but as part of my tour bottled water was offered. Most Americans (like myself) don't drink carbonated water and I consciously didn't bring any water with me from the hotel (the carbonation affects my stomach, just like soda and i can't drink it) and you would think there were have been water "sin gas" but there wasn't. When I brought this issue to my guide, there was no attempt to make it better. I am a seasoned traveler who has participated in other private tours overseas and the option is always given to you. A small ice chest would have also been nice to have the water cold too as other local companies would want to enhance their customer's experience. Instead of creating flashy brochures, Enotour might want to take a look at what they offer to tourists or change their pricing structure. Overall, my tour was not worth the money. I could have taken a local taxi and worked directly with the vineyards to get the same vino experience.
title: Great vineyards but I'm whining about Enotour

review_text: Pablo was a great tour guide. He was very friendly, funny and knowledgeable. We had a lovely tour of the cities and then had some free time for lunch. Nice air conditioned transport from our hotel. Review of: Valparaiso Port and Vina del Mar Full-Day Tour from Santiago It's the details that make the diference. Like the guide, the vehicle etc.. We're glad you had a great time. Thank you for your review.
title: Great tour

review_text: We went with my son on this tour, spots, comfortable van, guide Mauro knew a lot about flora and fauna of the place. We did 3 trails plus a stop next door chapo, very nice, a little exhausting but totally worth it 100% recommended tour
title: Tour park Andean larch

review_text: The tour was great. I did the morning tour and it was a small group with two great guides. I have found that chileans are very passionate about their country and the more questions you ask, the more info they have to give. My only complaint was that my first choices in tours were the night and the wine tour and they have a two person minimum. I could book neither since I was traveling alone and there were no other bookings on these days. We are glad you enjoyed the tour with us and feel really sorry for not being able to get to show you Santiago by Night, as you wished.
title: Wish I could have done more.

review_text: We booked all of our tours through Desert Adventure after recommendation from our hotel. We booked our tours the day before and there was no problem getting a seat. Price was reasonable, 3 tours for around $100 per person which included transportation. Ossie, our guide for 2 of the 3 tours was amazing. He has such a love and passion for what he does and it truly shines through his explanations and sharing of history in each tour. He was by far our favorite tour guide in San Pedro. Would definitly recommend doing the morning Geyser tour as it was stunning to watch the sunrise and Geysers become active. Highly recommended!
title: Beautiful Experience

review_text: When I was planning my trip to Atacama, I found that most problems would happen when the agency you hired would pass you to other agencies. When we hired 123 Andes, we asked explicitily if this could happen. Elias guarantted us that all of our tours would be directed by 123 Andes. The first tour, "Lagunas Escondidas", went great. Gabriel, the guide, was great. We also did "Rotas dos Salares", with the guide Marcel, that also went really well. The best guide was Victor. We did "Valle de la luna", "Lagunas Altiplanicas" and "Geysers del Tatio" with him. The problem was in the "Laguna Cejar" tour. We waited almost 1 hour for the van to pick us up. As we got on the van, It was really crowded and didn't even have a guide! We shared the van with people from a lot of other agencies, who had agreed with a crowded van and no guide, because they'd paid less than half of the amout we had. This agency will promisse you everything to make the sell, but will not see it through. For the price they charge, I would expect a better job. Would not recommend.
title: They will pass you to other agencies

review_text: Jacqueline Fuhrer Mihoevic and Sebastian (our driver) have provided wonderful, personalized friendly service all week, from a tour of Santiago to a day in Valparaíso y Viña Del Mar and an overnight visit to the Colchagua valley and Santa Cruz. Lovely people, great job! Highly recommended. Review of: Valparaíso and Viña del Mar Full Colors Delighted to read your comment wgclements and know that you enjoyed the experience lived with us at all times. We hope you share your memorable memories with family and friends who are about to visit Chile. Do not hesitate to return soon, we will be waiting for you with new experiences. Regards!
title: Excellent guide!

review_text: My parents just arrived in Chile to visit my partner and me, so one of the first things to do was to visit a winery close to Santiago. We all were very happy with the choice we made. We did only the normal tour, but I guess one could easily stay the whole day at this nice place since there is the museum, a restaurant and the park as well. That already shows some diversity that others don't offer, but also the actual tour had some nice little details in my opinion. And I guess most important is the tour guide, and our guide Pablo was very knowledgeable, lively, spoke very clear and well English, and explained things very nicely. So all in all, I can only recommend to visit this winery.
title: Beautiful place, diverse visit and tour

review_text: What a great evening. Yes, it is a bit more expensive than some of the other tours you can do in the Santiago region, but so worth it. Damaso and his colleague Franco describe themselves as "romantic astronomers". You spend the evening in their garden on the outskirts of Santiago. The garden is a quiet paradise full of telescopes of all shapes and sizes. You start of watching sunspots and solar flares on the setting sun, then move to the planets in the evening light and finally to the stars/satellites after dark. Throughout you will be plied with charcuterie board, snacks, ceviche and endless wine while entertained by the hosts. Francisca at Chile Off Track was super helpful getting all the logistics sorted for this evening. Review of: Observatory Stargazing Tour from Santiago Thanks so much for your feedback! We'll pass it on to Damaso, as he also loves to hear back from travellers. This tour is really a special experience and I'm very happy you enjoyed yourselves!
title: Great evening out under the stars on the outskirts of Santiago.

review_text: Awesome experience with Miguel, spotted several puma's over a day. With his eye sight, tracking skills and patience you are very likely to find them. He was also very friendly, and shared some of the personal foto's he took while we were with him. His lessons in the behavior of several Animals was very insightful Hola Morty, Nos alegra saber que este viaje resultó mejor de lo esperado, se logró el objetivo principal y superamos los avistamientos de pumas en un día, eso fue increíble. Esperamos que se encuentren bien, muchas gracias por escribirnos. Hasta pronto!
title: Puma spotting

review_text: We had a great stay in Pucón thanks to Aguaventura agency and highly recommend it to everyone. The activities they offer (volcano excursions, watersports ...) are great, the guides are really nice and everything is done to ensure safety. Besides, they gave us many advices and tips to organise our stay so we could have the best experience! Thanks again for everything
title: Best agency in Pucón

review_text: We did a full day trip from Santiago to Aconcagua with Gabriel. I did not find it easy to find someone who does this tour! Gabriel is knowledgeable, fun, and articulate. It was an amazing day which more than filled our expectations, we had a private tour (not deliberate). The day was well planned, we had a opportunity to meet the local restaurant owner, all border crossing matters were handled efficiently, and he is a good photographer! There were a number of interesting stops ( Inca Lake, statue on border at top of very high, insane road) on the way there and back, which broke up a long day. We had a blast, thank-you! We will recommend Gabriel to friends and will definitely contact him next time in Santiago.
title: Superb Guide and Great Guy - Day Trip to Aconcagua

review_text: You must allow a few hours to wander slowly around Cerro Santa Lucia. The views are impressive and it is such a quiet and peaceful place to be. Its a must see while in Santiago
title: Great views and so peaceful

review_text: Beautiful kayaking experience with Jorge. Very well organized activity including: Car transfer, great equipment, tasty brunch. We kayaked in the fjord with Jorge and small trekking with 360° views. We were the only ones in the fjord and Jorge was very helpful in guiding us and telling us about the peculiarities of the place. Super recommended!
title: Kayaking in the fjord

review_text: My first experience with la Bicicleta Verde was last year when I went with my parents to the Bike and Wine tour. We had a great time, enjoyed excellent wines and a great lunch. The guides were really nice and informed and the views of the Andes mountains were unforgettable! This time, we decided to do another tour with my boyfriends parents, the evening tour. We were concerned about the traffic and the physical effort but everything was under control, the guides were always concerned about us and the ride went smooth trough parks and bike lanes. We could enjoy and learn other views of Santiago, not the typical downtown area, and pedal downhill along the Mapocho river. The last stop was a restaurant in Bellavista, a great way of finishing our evening with cocktails and nice food!
title: Fun for everyone!

review_text: Our tour to Portillo was cancelled the previous afternoon, with the argument of unavailability, but we had bought in May 2024. Review of: Small-Group Tour of Portillo Ski Center and Inca Lagoon from Santiago Obrigado por compartilhar sua experiência! Lamentamos muito os inconvenientes ocorridos e investigaremos seu caso para que isso não volte a acontecer. MTO Tour Team

review_text: Leo has the gift of introducing you to the scientific charm of bird watching, with all his wisdom and learning he is very generous to share with you on his walks that are very short and playful. Rubén is always erudite, providing interesting and new data. Great value both. A hug with love. Ma. Angelica. See you soon.
title: Group bird watching with the best duo Rubén and Leo

review_text: We really enjoyed exploring this urban oasis. The fountains are beautiful and our family enjoyed the meandering stairways and paths. Stop at the yellow information desk to the left of the fountain. We were given great maps of the city that we wish we had the whole visit.
title: Great getaway in the middle of the city

review_text: I went with a tour company and it was a cool ride and the scenario was really beautiful... The weather also helped because it was a beautiful and sunny day!
title: Very nice tour...

review_text: Very smooth transfer from Calama Airport to our hostel in San Pedro de Atacama. Easy to find & pay at Calama airport, a short wait, into a comfortable minivan which took us all the way. No problems!
title: Easy and smooth transfer!

review_text: We are really glad that we took time to tour this museum which is housed in the Palazzo Barbarizza. Admission (for two seniors) cost only $1.50 - a good deal for sure. The rooms of the palazzo have been turned into galleries for the city's fine art collection. While I don't see much evidence that the Met or the Louvre are at risk, the collection is charming in its own way. Also engaging is the architecture of the building. It once was a real home, well "real" but hardly ordinary. The master bedroom has spectacular views of the bay. The master bathroom is an exhibit in itself. Check out the shower. Evidently all you had to do was stand in it and the water jets did the rest, sort of like an automatic carwash. Ah, the pleasures of money. The staff were very friendly and helpful too.
title: Well Worth a Visit

review_text: This winery is really fresh and lovely, and their restaurant is really good too - a cut above the usual level in Chile. The wine is excellent - as is their modern historical cultural museum.
title: Lovely winery

review_text: My wife and I spent a great day with Angela and her driver. Jose, the owner of the company, arranged the itinerary for us and it included a 5 hour visit to Valparaiso and then a stop at a vineyard for wine tasting on our way back to Santiago. When we left Santiago early in the morning it was cool, cloudy and drizzling rain. An hour and a half later we arrived in Valparaiso and there was bright sunshine, warm temperatures and blue skies. Angela took us on a fantastic locals tour of this amazing city and shared her wealth of knowledge about the city with us. From shops filled with art a crafts by local artisans, to historical sights and the beach we saw it all. She recommended lunch at the Portofino restaurant which over looks the city and the bay. The typical Chilean food and the views were both excellent. On the way back to Santiago we stopped at a nice vineyard and enjoyed a great tour and several glasses of excellent wine. Really a perfect day planned and executed by Uncorked Wine Tours. Review of: Best Wine Tasting in Santiago
title: Great Private Tour To Valparaiso and Wine Country

review_text: We came to Santiago looking for a city tour, we met turisk where we went on a tour of the main tourist attractions Great service from Giselle Review of: Cable Car, Funicular and Sightseeing Bus in Santiago two days Prezado viajante, ficamos felizes em saber que teve uma boa experiência com nossa equipe, muito obrigado por compartilhar sua experiência. Estamos ansiosos para sua próxima visita!
title: Wonderful

review_text: We visited in mid April before the funicular was repaired. Caught the free bus both up and down. the trip up goes up fairly directly, but the bus ride back down seemed to curve around and take a very long route with some other views along the way. the views from the top are great and you can take great photos of the city with the Andes in the background. Interesting to see the cute little church and the statue of the Virgin Mary too.
title: City and Andes Views

review_text: Excellent tour of the vineyard in shell and bull the marquez experience is worth it. For half a day in santiago is great.... Review of: From Santiago: Viña Concha y Toro Traditional Half-Day Tour Muchas gracias por compartir su experiencia junto a nosotros.

We visited as part of a tour. Felipe was our guide and was very friendly and knowledgeable, providing us with lots of information about the grapes, their unique processes, their fine wines and other specialty lines. This winery aims to produce wine blends and products that are a little outside the box. They clay pots that they ferment the grapes in, is quite unique in itself. After our tour we enjoyed a delicious alfresco luncheon in the courtyard and also enjoyed some generous servings of 3 of their unusual blends. The service was impeccable as well. Thanks guys for a fabulous afternoon. We all rolled merrily back onto the bus, but I think most of us dozed all the way back to Santiago.
title: A perfect place to enjoy wine, lunch and a tour.

review_text: Lovely trip, the barge is very comfortable and the crossing is worth doing, the only thing is that in summer time it costs to get tickets
title: Nice experience

review_text: Grateful to the agency and the guys who work at it! It was really amazing! The tours and services 100% recommended! The guides provided excellent service and it is appreciated that they know everything about the tourist attractions! Furthermore, the people who work at the agency are always willing to help and that is greatly appreciated! I will return home happy, since everything was really incredible :) I recommend them one hundred! I'm sure you'll enjoy it as much as I do! Review of: Full Day Tour Piedras Rojas Altiplanic Lagoons Chaxa Lagoon
title: Excellent tourist agency!

review_text: I read a few reviews and my day did not go as terrible (thankfully) as others. Felipe was awesome, really nice and just a normal day-to-day guy, not some snooty or idiot tour guide, so that was the first plus. I was promised to be picked up at 915, but did not get picked up until 945, no big deal. Spent 1.5 or so hours to Valparaiso, where Felipe did a great explaining about the history of the towns, places on the way there, etc. We spent about an Valparaiso, did the tour, walked down some streets, went to the top with a great with some merchants. We were taken to a very expensive, albeit good, restuarant (Ode del Mar? something like that) - I don't mind this part, but I know a few folks would have preferred a more authentic, less expensive cuisine. We spent very little time in Vina Del Mar, thankfully, because as the others says, it's just a tourist beach town (but might be awesome in the summer, it was cold yesterday). After that we sped off to the winery to round the day, which was fun with the tasting. For $39,000 I would not complain. It was a good value with good company. Felipe even told us about some local secrets and places to shop etc. I recommend, but would not have high hopes of having a spectacular, over the top type tour. As others mentioned, even taking the bus to Valparaiso would be cool, and then you can take the Free Tour tour that they offer (which costs about $5000 pesos in tips). Gracias Toan D, siempre tratamos de mejorar nuestros servicios, su opinión es de gran ayuda. Saludos Juan Pablo Abarca, Jefe de Marketing
title: Decent tour, decent price

review_text: There are two miradores (overlooks) at this site, which is in the Reserva Nacional de Flamencos and has a modest admission fee. From the mirador you look down on geologic formations that appear to be mini-mountains arising from the desert floor. There are other interesting formations and one area where one can see four geologic strata—dips, strikes, sinclines, and anticlines—all exposed in one section.
title: Among the most unusual geological formations anywhere

review_text: I joined the 4-day tour from San Pedro de Atacama to the Uyuni Salt Flats, and it was nothing short of incredible! The journey itself felt like an otherworldly adventure. From the surreal landscapes of the high-altitude deserts, steaming geysers, and vibrant lagoons filled with flamingos to the endless white expanse of the salt flats, every moment was breathtaking. Our guide Vladimir was a great driver and gave us great insights along the way, sharing stories about the region’s history and geology. The accommodations, while basic, were comfortable and added to the charm of the adventure. Watching the sunrise over the salt flats and taking those iconic reflective photos were definitely highlights of the trip! If you’re looking for a unique and unforgettable travel experience, I can’t recommend this journey enough. Just be prepared for the altitude and pack layers!
