review_text: This is mostly a review to help with logistics. But simply put, this place needs to be on your bucket list! Despite the difficulty of the W trek, the remoteness and uniqueness of this place adds to its raw beauty. I strongly recommend you visit! Few things to note for this review: 1. This is the W trek West-to-East, which we did by ourselves (no tour company involved). I strongly recommend doing it this way if you are with someone; you can go at your own pace, and it is a LOT cheaper (we did it at less than half the price of what most tour companies charge!) 2. We booked the campsites using a helpful website called “torres hike”. You can book direct with the companies (Vertice and Fantastico Sur) that own the campsites to avoid torres hike’s booking fee, but I found the company websites slow and clunky. 3. We did this in early October. Timings may change in high season! And it will probably be busier. 4. I will review the refugios/campsites (Grey, Paine Grande, Frances, Chileno) separately here on TripAdvisor, although the first time I mention each one I will say how many stars they get. 5. The Refugios are in the same place as the Camps. A Refugio has dorms & bunk beds, and is where you eat if you bought meals in advance. The camp part is usually next to the refugio. 6. Between the 2 of us we carried our clothes, a tent, 2 sleeping bags, 2 sleeping mats (all of which we managed to rent the day before in Puerto Natales from Yagan House & Lili’s Patagonicos), plus a first aid kit, toiletries, and other bits & pieces. Day 1: Puerto Natales > Camp Paine Grande (5*) > Camp Grey (5*). We caught the 07.00 bus to Torres del Paine National Park with Bus-Sur. It stopped at Laguna Amarga first at about 08.30; everyone gets off here to have their national park ticket checked. Those who are doing day trips, the W trek east-to-west, or starting the O trek from here catch a shuttle to the beginning of the trails at Hotel Las Torres & Central Camp. We got back on the bus to go to Pudeto, the catamaran stop; this should only take about 40mins but we had to go slow for the ultra-runners. We still made it in plenty of time; the catamaran leaves at 10.30 and costs CHP 25000 or US$ 30, cash only! By 11.15 we were at Camp Paine Grande. After a quick toilet break and bag adjustment we headed off at 11.30. Signs state the walk to Camp Grey is 3.5 hours - this was roughly correct for us, but if you are not carrying your own tent, etc you will probably do it quicker. The walk itself is beautiful, although burnt trees are still scarred from a fire 10 years ago (partly why open fires are no longer allowed). The first 2 hours were difficult as we faced REALLY strong winds, to the point we sometimes had to stop, because lifting one foot may have meant falling over. The final 90mins were easier simply because there was less wind, though there are some uphill sections throughout. Once we reached Camp Grey we had a quick late lunch, put up our tent, then continued along the trail for another 45mins to see the “hanging bridge” (a wood, rope and metal suspension bridge) where you can get a good view of Lago Grey & the glacier. Once back, we had dinner, moved our tent into better shelter from the wind, then quickly fell asleep. Day 2: Camp Grey > Camp Paine Grande. We were supposed to fill our morning with a kayak session near the glacier (you can book this through the company direct, Big Foot Patagonia, online or at their office in Puerto Natales, and they also do an ice hike on the glacier) - unfortunately, it was cancelled as the winds were still too strong. So we trekked back the way we came on Day 1, meaning we ended up at Camp Paine Grande at 13.00. We completed it in just over 3 hours this time, as the wind wasn’t as strong as Day 1. Day 3: Camp Paine Grande > Camp Frances (4*) > Mirador Britanico (via Valle del Frances) > Camp Frances. This was our favourite day! We left Paine Grande at 09.30 and had a nice, although slightly wet, 2.5 hour hike to Camp Frances, where we could thankfully check in early to set up our tent. Once we had done that, packed our day bag and had lunch, we set off at 13.00 to hike the Valle del Frances. (Note that you can leave your big bag at the park ranger station at Camp Italiano, which is 1km before Camp Frances and also the start point for the hike into Valle del Frances. We decided to go to Camp Frances first to pitch our tent in case the weather got worse - thankfully it didn’t). From Camp Italiano, the hike is mostly uphill for the first 90 mins to Mirador Frances; you go through a lot of wooded areas so most of the time you are sheltered from any wind or rain. Once at Mirador Frances, you can turn back or continue to Mirador Britanico; this is about another 60mins, although we didn’t do the last 10mins because we got to a point where the forest opened up to an amazing view anyway. The hike to Mirador Britanico is still uphill but not as steep as to Mirador Frances. We then hiked back to Camp Frances, returning at 18.00. Day 4: Camp Frances > Camp Chileno (3*). This was our hardest day, both physically and mentally. By this point you begin to really feel the aches and strains from the previous days hikes, and it’s not made any easier by the fact that you have to walk approx 16km with all the weight in your bag. Most blogs I’ve read have put the timing of this walk at about 6-7 hours; we did it in 6.5 hours, including about 40mins of rest breaks. The first 3km of the walk, to Refugio Los Cuernos, is mostly downhill. It then alternates between uphill and downhill, but steadily increasing in elevation overall. The last 4km (roughly) were the hardest for us; after taking the left path at the fork for Camp Chileno or Hotel Las Torres, you cross some boggy ground before heading uphill for a good hour or so, and this is where the wind picks up again! At the top you reach Windy Pass (forget about using rain covers here - ours were ripped off), and then you’re less than 30mins from Camp Chileno. Watch out for horses for these last 30mins too - riders pass by delivering supplies to the camp. Day 5: Camp Chileno > Mirador Base Torres > Puerto Natales. And this was our second hardest day! Up at 5am, a quick breakfast at the Camp Chileno lodge (make sure you arrange this with lodge staff the night before), then off to Mirador Base Torres at 05.45. With our day packs, this took the recommended 2 hours - we might have been quicker had it not been for the fact we had to trudge slowly through amazing SNOWY landscapes! It was like that scene when they enter Narnia, except better! Anyway moving onto the logistics, the first hour was fairly easy with little uphills and downhills. The second hour, after you pass the turnoff for the park ranger station, was where it got hard with the constant uphill, and maybe even a little dangerous with all the snow covering the rocky trail. We knew we’d be a bit disappointed at the top, which we were (the Torres del Paine were shrouded in cloud and mist) but the scenery was just so breathtaking that the disappointment didn’t last. We had to be careful on the way back down - there were definitely a few slips and slides - but we made it back to Camp Chileno in about 1hr 45mins. After packing our tent and gear away, and a quick pick-me-up hot chocolate, we left Camp Chileno at 10.30 and descended all the way to Refugio Central, arriving at about 12.30, in plenty of time for the 14.00 shuttle bus (CHP 3000, cash only!) to Laguna Amarga. Then it was a short wait for our 15.00 bus back to Puerto Natales (we had pre-booked this, but at least one couple were able to get on without a ticket, with the bus driver saying they could pay back at Puerto Natales - doubt you could do this in high season though). I hope some of this helps with your planning 🙂
title: Should definitely be on your bucket list! Plus a detailed logistical review of the W trek.

review_text: We did the Parks and Politics tour and really enjoyed it. Cruising around on bikes is a great way to see the city and get around. The guides were really informative and you could tell for one of the tour guides that the more recent history of the city/country has a lasting impact on her. It was touching to see (without going into to much detail) the personal side of what so many of us could only learn about in the news. Hola hola hola urnmalone! Thanks for not giving away the personal secret of your guide :) Santiago, and the rest of Chile, have lived a rough past, which is part of the reason Chileans are such interesting people to talk to. We are happy you enjoyed the tour, the guide, the city. Thanks for choosing our small, but crazy fanatical, team of Santiago-lovers... We know you have thousands of options, from bus tours to helicopters, so gracias for choosing us! Sincerely, Peter

review_text: Franco was a great tour guide, he is well spoken, funny and very intellegent. I believe he does the morning tour on week days only. The four hour tour provided lots of information about what we were seeing, as well as a good historical, and political prospective on Chile. He is quite willing to answer any questions about Chile: food, politics ,culture, wine, resturaunts, musems, music(he has a band), nothing is out of bounds.. The pace was really great and I enjoyed our stop for ice cream mid-way through the tour. It was also a great opportunity to chat with others in our group. I would highly recommend this to anyone visiting Santiago. We have been to Santiago about 6 times and I wish we had taken the tour sooner. The tour operates on tips only, Franco recommeded no more than $10 per person. But that is up to the individul.
title: Great Tour

review_text: We had a great tour led by Miguel. We got the train from Santiago & walked to the meeting point (a 15-20 minute brisk walk but straight forward). We had a group of about 10 so it wasn't too crowded or difficult to hear everything. Miguel guided us expertly through all the tiny alley's, showed us amazing street art & more importantly, the stories behind them. The empanade stop was delicious, just go for it!! I couldn't not mention a large part of our tour: the dogs! From early on, we were joined by 2 strays that Miguel knew very well, then this increased by another 2 Miguel was also familiar with. Luckily the group was very fond of dogs so they were a great addition, with plenty of cuddles all round! (If you're not a big fan of dogs, Valpo might not be the place for you!)
title: Fantastic tour of Valpo!!

review_text: ……..A real fascinating big well laid-out and immaculate-lii maintained wide open space on the edge of the Mapocho river and almost in the centre of the business district of Santiago de Chile, Entrance is free of charge and you can just wonder in at leisure and enjoy a safe and quiet ”walk in the park”, it’s very clean and there are benches strewn all over at well placed distances so you can walk look at all the fascinated modern sculptures take a break read a book and then continue. Some of the pieces on show are open for you to make up your own mind as to what the artist is trying to convey as someone once said “the artist learns to communicate and the public learns to make a connection” this is so true when you are wondering around here. There are even parakeets frolicking around on the green-lawns and chirping merrily in the trees. There is a nice sized exhibition centre where companies or businesses can display there good in this love-lii natural environment. Very interesting to see when you take time to read the little plaques in the flower-beds you will come to see that many of the plant species and trees are from different counties in the world. If you just want to take a break bring a picnic basket and do what many Chileans do during the day, they come to the park and relax and have a good time. This is a must visit park when in the area its rejuvenating and fun-filled……………
title: A Walk In The Park!!!

review_text: We hire a 6 night program with excursions and accommodation. The first day the problems left, we had to wait 2 hours at the airport to be picked up. When we arrived at the hotel in Puerto Chacabuco they did not want to deliver lunch because they said it had been delivered in a transfer, which was not real. Then we realized that the hotel has no pool or spa. WiFi internet does not work, we asked more than once to fix it but we were not taken into account. The food included in the package is buffet, but neither breakfast, lunch, nor dinner is of good quality, the menu is repetitive and little varied. When I ordered a bean coffee at breakfast, not a machine like they offer, they wanted to charge me as an extra (a small thing). In general you see few people with experience in reception and restaurant. Receptionists have no power or criteria to make decisions and solve problems. For some reason that I do not know the electric power tends to fail on bad weather days, apparently they do not have backup equipment or voltage stabilizer. The rooms do not have air conditioning, which is already a basic standard, considering that the rooms on the north side are very hot on sunny days. Maid service needs to improve, sometimes they don’t remove all the trash and they don’t change or leave the towels, not to mention that the towels are small and worn. TVs are old, none are smart TVs. They have a very basic cable TV system. The rooms also have no fridge, so it is not feasible to buy drinks and leave them there. They never gave us slippers even though they had to give to guests. On the other hand, the excursions are very good, so it is clear that the service is focused on that and not on the rest, less on the hotel, which is promoted as 4 stars in booking, but I consider that it does not give you for more than 2 stars (rooms and restaurant). It is also listed as being in the top 10% of hotels in the world according to TripAdvisor, which is misleading for the passenger, as it tends to be thought to be in the top 10, which is not effective. With regard to meals, I was left with the feeling that we overpaid for a service that is not properly used. The last day we were supposed to be taken to the airport at 12 noon because our flight was leaving at 15:40, that's what they offered. However, we were forced to leave the room before 10hrs, with no alternatives, that is, in addition to the non-compliance, we had to wait about 1 hour at reception because the transfer had changed schedule and did not warn, plus 3 hours at the airport for arriving early. A disaster of service. When I presented my claims to the hotel manager, he simply told me "it's his opinion", with high-handedness, intransigence, zero empathy, zero self-criticism and zero willingness to solve the problems of the passengers, while, he unraveled in attentions for people of the TV who were apparently invited to promote the place (it seems that he does not understand that the best or worst advertising is that of the paying passengers). I think it is better to have a hotel like Dreams de Coyhaique as your accommodation and from there hire excursion services. You would have much better hotel service and maybe even cheaper. I’m left with the feeling that we overpay for a service whose added value isn’t in the entire service value chain – we receive much less than we expected and what we pay for. Consequently, I recommend excursions, but for no reason recommend the hotel, it is a place I would never return to again.
title: The Hotel, a mess of service

review_text: What can I say?... I've spent 6 weeks traveling alone across Chile and this was definitely the highlight of the whole trip. To my person, I am 31 years old, have only minimal spanish knowlegde, have experiences in seakayak trips and of course like to spend time camping in the wilderness. So it seemed to be the perfect plan to do this trip. But in the end it exceeded my expectations. And this not only because of the stunning landscape and animals. But mainly because of the whole combination of wilderness, a perfect tour guide Juan who is experienced, knows the area by heart and is a reaaally warmhearted person who tries anything make this a perfect trip for you and of course the other locals who hosted us/me so openminded and cordially (even though my spanish was too bad to talk a lot besides the patient translations by Juan). The (pre)organisation was already really good and easy. Because I was traveling alone and it was already a bit off-season (april), I had the opportunity to do this trip as the only participant. Everything, concerning finding a date, gear, hostel in Puerto Varas, payment and what I should expect was so well organized and I never had doubts it could be a bad decision to do this trip. I could talk of course a lot about the trip itself, the waterfalls, hotsprings, the animals, the campsites, but as there are so many pictures on facebook for example - just take a look there. What you see is what you get! (at least a feeling of it - paddeling in those fjords is breathtaking). What you cannot see on the pictures is how warm you are welcomed by the locals and which makes this trip exceptional compared to trips that you do on your own just in the nature. Thanks a lot Juan for this wonderful opportunity you gave me. Next time I will stay at the car ;) Muchas gracias y saludos atentos! Hola, sorry for taking so long to express my surprise to your comments, mainly after what you write: " this was definitely the highlight of the whole trip." To my person, I am 31 years old, have only minimal spanish knowlegde, have experiences in seakayak trips and of course like to spend time camping in the wilderness. A friend recommended Valparaiso was a must-see so after a Trip Advisor search, we joined a Stamp's Tour less than 24hrs out. The well organised info & notification system made it all very easy. The collection & drop off from our hotel was on time & saved the hassle of getting lost. The trip did not disappoint, and the gem was our English speaking guide Franco whose extensive knowledge & passion for this region was palpable. The way he shared what he knew, sometimes using pop quiz style to get group participation, was very engaging & unified our group of 11. A great way to immerse & learn some history & culture. review_text: This winery is worth a visit simply for the building and the location. Beautiful attention to detail in all aspects, including the wine.
title: Architectual wonder

review_text: The hill is easily accessible and is a large green area, you can enjoy the day in the hill doing trekking, cycling, walking or cable car. It is recommended for friends, family, athletes or alone, and go early by the morning. The other attraction that San Cristóbal hill has is the Japanese garden, even if it is a small garden, it gives you the possibility of having a beautiful view of Santiago and taking pictures.
title: Nature

review_text: Its not hard to understand why Neruda had his house in Isla Negra. The place is beautifully located there at the ocean front of the roaring pacific ocean and with the washed rolling in over the rocks. The museum is interesting and offers a lot of insight to Neruda and his life, and offers a nice window in to his tastes and decorations. Its a bit of drive from Santiago, but I my mind, worth the trip, especially in combination with lunch at the restaurant with the ocean view. The showing are in time slots, so just be aware, that you might have to wait for some time to get your turn (we waited an hour and had lunch in the meantime).
title: Museum with an ocean view

review_text: My choice for Flávia Bia's Company was based on information on the internet. I was very satisfied with the service provided. professionalism, personalized service, accurate information regarding tours and clothing, competent and attentive guides. The service was impeccable!
title: Experience in Atacama with FlaviaBia

review_text: The park is very nice, and the trail is easy to walk although it is fairly far up to the top. At the top the view of town is blocked with trees and underbrush. The limited view is not worth the effort and time. If this review is helpful then please indicate so below.
title: Fairly Long Walk to the Top with Viewpoint Obscured by Trees

review_text: Atacama is driest and highest dessert on the earth with extraordinary beautiful scenery ,rock formations, salt flats, lagoons, flamingoes, volcanoes,sand dunes, geysers, hot and cold weather in same day, unique colors... Truly amazing, breathtaking nature, above our expectations.
title: One of the most beautiful landscapes and driest place on the earth

review_text: Interesting walk through the salt flats and watching Andean and Chilean Flamingos strut their stuff. The interpretive centre is also interesting as is the lifecycle of the waterborne shrimps which inhabit the lake.
title: Flamingos

review_text: You can visit the vineyard and learn about the wine´s production since the foundation. The house´s family is mantained but unfortunely is not open for visitation but the yard with plantation and the lagoon are nice. You can taste the most wines sold and get the glass as a gift. Then you can choose to bye some botlles in the market. Review of: Half Day Maipo Valley with Full Wine Tour plus Family Farm with 2 tastings
title: Family history and wine production

review_text: Very good and explanatory. I have been touring the area but when I passed by the museum I got a semi-complete movie of the entire territory. I'm missing a deeper indigenous topic. Should include the topic of killings
title: Good idea to visit

review_text: My sister and I bought the bus tour directly from the Costanera Mall customer service. We explained that we would have to finish the tour by 4pm, which the attendant said was possible and, according to him, with time to spare. However, during the tour we discovered, after waiting for over 1 hour and 30 minutes at stop 3, on the Cable Car, that the buses were running at longer intervals, possibly due to one of them being inoperable due to mechanical problems. Because of this, we had to end the tour halfway through, meaning we didn't enjoy the tour we paid for. We requested by email, on 01/31/2024, a refund of the amount paid for the 2 tickets, however, to date, there has been no response from the company regarding the request. That's why I don't recommend this tour. Review of: Tourist bus around Santiago for a day Prezado viajante, lamentamos sinceramente que sua experiência tenha sido afetada por essa situação. Muito obrigado por nos informar para que possamos trabalhar para melhorar nossos serviços. I recommend and would recruit this company.

It is worth noting that, at the agency Pukarumi, there was no guide, but some agencies offered guide and wardrobe for greater comfort, which would be a good option for those seeking more convenience. Still, the experience was wonderful and very well worth it. Review of: Puritama Hot Springs

review_text: Our guide was Franco. Spoke impeccable English, and had a good knowledge of both historical facts of chile and interesting cultural information. Friendly, informative, funny. All good. Probably the best walking tour I have taken in 3 months. I reccomend!

review_text: We had an amazing day out with Gonzalo in a small group with only two others! We got picked up from our accomodation at 9.30, and in little over an hour we were at a ranch up in the mountains. Not many cities you could say that about! The horses were very well trained, 3/4 of us had never been on a horse before and there were no problems. We got 3-4 hours going up and down and through various landscapes and terrains , the scenery was out of this world! The trip ended with a nice packed lunch provided by Gonzalo, water was also included in the cost. This trip was worth every peso, if you're thinking of doing it just go for it, you definitely won't regret it! Thanks a lot for your review, but we are more happy to know you really enjoyed your day with Andoandes!

review_text: We thoroughly enjoyed the entire tour to the Santa Rita Winery with Daniel. We were picked up at our hotel, then taken to a meeting point to board the van that took us to the vineyard. Daniel provided a lot of information about the wine industry in Chile and Santa Rita Winery. When we arrived at the winery part of us went on the walking winery tour and part went on the bicycle tour of the winery. Our Santa Rita Winery guide was very informative and the tasting of three wines at the end was very pleasant. At the end of the tour we were delivered back to our hotel. Review of: Santa Rita Vineyard Tour with Lunch An unforgettable experience! We appreciate your comment dear traveler, it is very important for us to know about your experience.
title: Great Tour

review_text: Joaquin is super friendly, and a great and knowledgeable guide. Hey Dylan thank for the comments! I hope you continue with your climbing trips, welcome again if you want to come here or maybe we can climb in the states soon! Cheers and say hi to Veronica too!

review_text: Impresiv long and old human history "This is a well designed modern museum set in an oasis-like park. It covers the prehistory of northern Chile with special exhibits of the Chinchorro culture (8,000-6,000 BC). The dryness of the desert has preserved organic artifacts such as cloth, baskets, wood tools etc. and examples are displayed. All text is in Spanish. Worth the time if you are at all interested in prehistory. Caution-exhibits include human remains."
title: Impresiv long and old history

review_text: We are a family of 6 so prefer the private tours. I had booked the excursion not realizing that they did not cater to the port. Felix was very accommodating and honored the booking. review_text: This place is stunning first of all due to the nature and forests that transform the entire destination into a trekking and hiking place and second of all, waterfalls are breathtaking and beatiful place in the southern part of Chile that is worth visiting. It's quite known among the tourists in that visit Chile but it's not crowded at all.

review_text: Excursions at Antilco Ranch cater to horse riders of all levels. You're assigned a horse depending in your experience and can choose to gallop, canter or trot depending on your level of comfort in horseriding. A demonstration is given before you set off so even if youre a complete beginner, it shouldnt be too challenging. The three-hours long trek winds its way through quiet country roads, open meadows crops of trees and along the Rio Tacura, making for an extremely scenic ride, particularly on a clear day when you can see Volcano Villarica in the distance. You can choose to go direct to Antilco Ranch or through one of the many agencies that offer horseriding expeditions in Pucon. The prices are roughly the same.
title: Pretty Countryside Excursion

review_text: This tour was an amazing experience with such a professional and educational approach to it by Francisco. We got to learn about the history of the desert, its unique geology and patrimony, but also enjoy the guide’s hospitality with his tasty snacks for all of the crew during this sweet expedition! Can’t recommend the Francisco and agency enough! Review of: Tour to Vallecito and Magic Bus
title: Impeccable

review_text: We had an absolutely incredible time - highly, highly recommended! Lucas did such a phenomenal job of explaining the mission of the refugio, and the ways in which humans can help reduce our impact on the natural world. He shared fascinating facts about local plants, and it was wonderful seeing the animals up close. You get some time to explore the forest, but it's not too much walking for young children.
title: A must-see excursion for nature and animal lovers

review_text: In total it was just a very good experience. Jorge enthusiasm and knowledge of the sky makes you want to learn more. We took the Traditional Astronomical Tour (TAT) tour. We covered the following: brief History, coordinates and orientation, general learning sky, Andean astronomy and cosmology, observation and Astrophotography. We had enough time to get a good general knowledge of the subjects, to ask questions and to observe the sky with the telescopes. Absolutely worth it! Dear Visitor, Thank you very much for your comments about our stargazing tour. In ADStargazing feel ourselves so happy when visitors like you enjoyed and learnt the sky night knowledges. While the time has been passed our tours are longer because we want to give you the most complete stargazing tour in information and observation giving two section per night. Very soon coming more great surprises and we´ll keep you informed. Warmest regards Jorge and Johanna
title: A must do!

review_text: Lovely views but is not that high, only 62 levels for lookout. Compared to other towers around the world is actually quite low. I went at 5:30pm and the sunset view was amazing on the snow capped mountains. Also no queues. It cost 5000 pesos for weekday and 8000 weekend.
title: Nice views of santiago

review_text: Truth is that I’m not a painting specialist, so I will not speak about the paintings that there are in the museum. The reason of my visit it’s the building itself. Don’t miss it if you visit the city. It’s located on the hill with perfect view, just next to the cable car station. Entrance fee for foreigners is 4000 pesos that’s mean apprx. 8 USD
title: Incredible house

review_text: Gui Alejandro Garcia was a very good person and attentive to all passengers, it was a fun and safe trip. I recommend
title: Tour to Vina del Mar and Valparaiso

review_text: I took a Viator excursion from my Santiago hotel to the port. The Casablanca Valley was a very beautiful area with the vineyards and rolling hills The group stopped in a small restaurant for coffee and pastries. Llama's were fenced in in the back garden area for the visitors to see. A nice change of scenery from the huge Santiago area.
title: On the way to the port from Chile.

review_text: I would like to leave a few comments about the tours we did. Overall, everything went well and we had good support from Oasis, especially from the girl who served us, always calm and friendly, unlike the boy. The collaborating agencies that conducted the tours with us were also good. The Suenos Seller team was always attentive and close to solve doubts and help us with the refund of one of the tours that we were unable to make due to adverse weather conditions, always open and transparent communication. All guides were great, knew a lot about what they were talking about and knew how to organize the tours satisfactorily. Positive highlights for the guides Jonathan (I do not remember the name of his agency) and Carolina (Andes Travel), for the moristas Daniel (Andes Travel) and Gregory (the same agency Jonathan). As points to improve note that the driver Marcelo (Andes Travel) was extremely imprudent and did not seem to have experience with the route of the Salares, which led us to have to stand still for about 30 minutes waiting for a car with new brakes during the route. In addition, the Astronomical Tour was very disorganized, we tried to make the tour the day before and we were not warned if it would occur by 2:30, they appeared at our door at 23:00 by surprise, when we were already sleeping, that is, there was no communication. When we managed to make the tour there were too many people, about 28 people and this left everything more complex, the photo was not professional (the positioning angle of the photos was bad and there was no direction for who was photographed), only took 1 photo of us when we paid for 2, during the whole experience there were lights around. Music around and high, breaking the mood of the moment. The agency was Atacama Borealis. I am very grateful to all those involved who helped us realize the dream of meeting Atacama with as much support as possible.
title: 5 Days in Atacama

review_text: My visit was in late March and the travel agency didn't tell us that the majority of the penguins were long gone. We expected to see thousands instead there were only a few hundred. However a few of them were curious and and made their way over to us and this made for some good pics. Be sure to ask before you go if there are any penguins.
title: The penguins were gone

review_text: Alyan Family Wines, a special winery. I've been to many. In Argentina, Chile and Brazil. This was, without a doubt, the best of all! In every corner you can see and breathe the soul of a family history that respects the land and wine production with care! Andres, Alicia and their children created a perfect and welcoming environment, in addition to serving guests the best house wines. Intense aromas and colors that remain forever in your memory! The house, what a house! There are no words to describe the details of the beautiful decoration that tells the story of humanity that the family brings along its journey! The big surprise was the meeting with the founder himself, who gave a speech relating life and wine in a wise way! The quails represent Alyan! It’s a must to visit and discover why! Excellent wines, sold only in the bodega and exported only to Asia. Small and careful production, meaning of excellence! Thanks!
title: Excellence in wine

review_text: I was a bit underwhelmed by this site. Am not sure it was worth the trek to several of the caves. Admittedly, I was expecting more of a Las Caux cave experience or something resembling Mesa Verde. The trail to the lesser caves is uneven and rocky, though the views of the dandelion fields and purple sage or calafate flowers was very pretty. For the experienced hiker, this is not a difficult walk but for someone unsteady on their feet, it can be a challenge. A walking stick may be helpful. A sculpture of the milodon gives scale to the cave.
title: Caving to the Milodon

review_text: This church was a highlight spot in Castro. Bright yellow and purple on the outside after Pope John Paul II's visit, the inside is traditional with vaulted wood ceilings.
title: Gaudy on the outside and epic on the inside

review_text: I've not done the winery tour, but I could see how beautiful is the winery. I've had lunch experience (4 dishes and wine matching) and although the food was good, the service was slow and terrible because the restaurant was crowded.
title: Beautful winery, poor service

review_text: A nice view of the Neff and Baker rivers meeting. Great photo op of beautiful waters and lots of energy. Its a ten minute walk from the road through a nice park. A good break after a long drive.
title: Confluencia Rio Baker

review_text: Went to do the 'Patrimonial Tour' on a Thursday and turned up with plenty of time to spare. Others were waiting and waited for another half hour after alloted time, unfortunately no one showed up. We were very disappointed as we were looking forward to tour and walked it ourself but of course had no idea what we were looking at. I understand things happen, but my problem with this group is that I emailed afterwards and have never got a reply which is why I would not recommend them.
title: Didn't show up

review_text: It probably takes about 20 minutes to hike up the hill, unless you take a more scenic route and make stops along the way. Great views of the skyline from the lookout at the top of the hill. The hill is easily accessible via the Santiago subway system.
title: Great Views of Santiago

review_text: Indescribable experience! Super recommend, the super attentive ballooner! Wonderful sunrise view!!! It exceeded all my expectations!
title: Sensational

review_text: Cristian was happily awaiting us at the port. He is an enthusiastic ambassador for his home city of Valparaiso and really took the time to give us the local flavor of this interesting and historic city. Our day also included a tour of Vina del Mar and Santiago with a stop at the Macerado Restaurant in the Casablanca Valley for a delicious Chilean meal with equally tasty wine. He is more than willing to tailor a tour to your personal taste and is very flexible if you want to veer off the beaten path. I cannot say enough good things about him. It was notable that everywhere we went in Valparaiso, he greeted and was greeted by many locals--this guy could run for President. He also took photos along the way and when we arrived home,he emailed us a link with the photos! An absolutely wonderful ending to a spectacular vacation. Wow, I´m speechless.... Thank you so much for expressing your feeling towards our day together! It was a beautiful day and we saw and did so many things in the time frame that we had available (including coffee.. haha)!! Your joyfulness and interest (both of you) made it hard for me not to enjoy myself during the whole day. I had a great time!! I love the fact that you were also flexible which made it possible to take the most advantage of our day together! You are very sweet people and I hope everything stays well with you back home and you continue to have a great time!! I hope a piece of Chile will stay with you always!! All the best, Cristián
title: Best Tour Ever!

review_text: Unless you have a big interest in Neruda, this place is really an interesting old house with great views of the town
title: worth it for views

review_text: Our guide, Daniel, was very knowledgeable and did his tour even though only my friend and myself showed up. He taylored the tour to whatever we were more interested in, and spent two more hours than the tour actually is meant to last, just feeding us with information. He knows the local history very well, and illustrates it with the buildings and places along the route. Great tour, great guide! Small groups just make it better.
title: Great tour of central Santiago

review_text: Amazing experience with Desertour – highly recommended! I made four tours with Desertour – the astronomical tour, the Vale de la Luna, the Geysers and the Uyuni Salar – and they were all absolutely amazing! Since Portugal, the whole process of organization went impeccably. The communication with the team was always clear and fast, with all the indications well explained before each ride, which gave me a lot of confidence. The tours themselves were very well conducted, with friendly, knowledgeable guides and always available to help. Each experience was unique, especially the Salar do Uyuni, which exceeded all expectations. The logistics always went well, the schedules were respected and I always felt safe and well accompanied. I highly recommend Desertour to anyone planning to explore the Atacama Desert or Bolivia. A professional and attentive organization that made this trip even more memorable!
title: Amazing experience with Desertour – highly recommended!

review_text: Pros: Ski slopes for different skiing skill levels. Great views. One of the nicest mountains to ski in the south of Chile. Tracks are wide and long. Very good place for learning as it has a very big area with easy tracks. There's great staff available for hired one-on-one classes (expensive though; about US$80 for 1 hour). Cons: Very slow lifts (and long waits if it's too crowded) Bad weather warning: when there's strong wind, most of the lifts will be closed, be sure to ask before paying. Lift tickets fee differ: high season US$45; low season US$30; special promotions US$18.
title: Great skiing provided there's good weather

review_text: Well laid out museum, with a well presented collection. English translation provided for displays. Central Santiago location -easy to get to. Classy gift shop .
title: small but informative

review_text: We did the tour with 10 Grados at sunset. The changing colors of the landscape are spectacular and the cocktail with pisco sour was very nice.
title: Go at sunset

review_text: Nice place and very nice views. It has a historical burden, not much leveraged. Security maintenance and control is not very suitable for this type of place
title: Historic place

review_text: Did an airport pickup, a 5 hr walking city tour of Santiago and a transfer and 3 hr walking tour in Valparaiso with Ignacio! He was wonderful! Very Passionate about his city! Was enthusiastic about everything! Could not have chosen a better guide!! Suggested some wonderful restaurants. He was always early and very organized. We forgot a small shoulder bag in his car when we got dropped off at the cruise terminal. Nothing serious in it except raincoats and car keys. He took photos of all contents and whatsapt it to me and then proceeded to courier it back to Canada!! What a great person! Love you Ignacio! You cannot go wrong when you choose him! Dear Charleen and Hubertus, Thank you for being so nice Tourist!! I'm so glad to have met you. Being with you for two days gave me the chance to know more about you and learn a lot from you too. I'm happy that you liked the tour that we have prepared through Santiago and Valparaíso for you. Cristian the guide in Valparaíso was really happy with you too.!! Thank you again for having chosen me as your guide and have trusted me. I'm happy that you bag got back to Canada safe!! Come back soon to Chile we have many landscape that you should also see!! Love you too and do not forget your friend Ignacio =)!!
title: Ignacio was wonderful!

review_text: We only found out about the Valparaiso street art tour late the evening before our last day. Unfortunately the 10.30am one was booked out but we couldn't the guy and ended up arranging a private tour for the afternoon. Jake, our guide was awesome - friendly, smiling, accommodating and informative. Jake took us through the streets and explained all the street art, who made it, what inspired them, the history and importance behind street art for Valparaiso, the different stages of graffiti for artists. Being an art lover it was fascinating and informative! After the 2 hour tour we also included a graffiti art workshop meeting two of Chile's most famous street artists, where they we're painting one of the world's largest graffiti works on the back of a skyscraper / apartment block. The artists then showed us techniques on how to paint, showed us how to write a 'tag' for our names and let us play around with colour and spraying techniques. It was heaps of fun. Jake also gave us recommendations on where to eat, drink and things to do. His English is perfect. Valparsio is all about the street art, to go here without doing this tour would be missing out on seeing the real Valparaiso. For $80 US for two people it's a must do (includes workshop and private tour). Review of: Valparaiso City History & Graffiti Tour
title: Fantastic tour & great workshop!!

review_text: We visited beautiful places and at the agency two lovely girls assisted us, Jose and Fernanda organized a program for us with the must-see places in San Pedro de Atacama and promptly resolved any questions or concerns.
title: Our stay was incredible, for example visiting the Tatio Geyser, the Cejar lagoon, the valley of the moon and the rainbow

review_text: had some time to kill in the sleepy town, and we found the hot spot. the Sky Bar on the roof of the casino has incredible views from very large windows on two sides (facing the town and the water). Food was good, drinks were great and the atmosphere was excellent. Would stop here again, and the prices compared to the USD are very reasonable. Spent about 5-6 hours here, and the time flew by. thankfully our wallets didn't feel a huge dent like it would have spending that much time in a local bar in the USA.
title: Loved the Sky Bar on the roof

review_text: Booked a private day tour to check out Valparaiso and Vina del Mar. Anneliese picked us up in Santiago in the morning and we had a wonderful day with her out on the coast of Chile. The tour was well organized and highly personalized! - Take the scenic route to stop at a picture spot? Yes - Stop at a winery and taste some wine? Ok - Lunch with a view? Sure - Go behave like children at a kids play ground? Definitely - Any questions about Chile + lifestyle? Lots! - Food and activity recommendations for the remainder of our trip? Where to start... Anneliese was a fun local who had lots of stories to share and knows the ins and outs of the areas we visited (not to mention an extremely talented wood carver). We saw the highlights of what we wanted to see, and had a blast doing it! Highly recommended :)
title: <3 Valparaiso

review_text: Great service, cool and brainy people in charge, the place is a gifted location away from light pollution from San Pedro, near to Moon Valley, greeted with some Chilean Wine, hot cocoa for the cold, very cool telescopes, the guy in charge really knows his stuff and you get to learn some cool features of our wonderful night sky. :)
title: Amazing!

review_text: The landscapes are amazing. Nature in this place is lush, explodes life despite the aridity. An experience that should be experienced by all the peoples of the earth. Review of: "Astronomical Adventure in San Pedro de Atacama"
title: An experience for life!

review_text: Constanza Valdivieso When we got into the bus early, we were delayed in delivering the devices, which caused us to miss the information on the first stops. The girl explained them to us and treated us very well. When we went back up everything very well Review of: Tourist bus around Santiago for a day ¡Muchas gracias por sus comentarios!
title: March Trip

review_text: Excellent experience. Very educational and interesting. Don Pedro was super friendly and nice during our visit. We're leaving very happy.
title: Tasting and learning.

review_text: I just have to thank you. Mari gave me all the assistance I needed. All the tours were wonderful. I recommend it with my eyes closed.
title: Mari Mundi- everything perfect

review_text: This replica of the real Esmaralda is perfectly made. Lots of details and looks very authentic. The guided tour gives a good understanding of the battle between the Peruvian and Chilean forces. The guide gave a lot of information on the ship, but also on the people working on the ship. There a few videos that explain details of some of rhe parts and there is sounds played all over the ship to make it fell like the ship is sailing etc.
title: Best museum we have visited for a loooooong time.

review_text: We had a beautiful day, the scenery was spectacular, the guide named Germán was a boy from this area where we went, super informed about both landscapes and fauna, super friendly and friendly. Available at any time for any doubt or to solve any situation. I highly recommend it! Review of: Cajon del Maipo: El Yeso & Spa reservoir in El Morado Muchas gracias por sus comentarios, nos alegra saber de que disfrutó junto a nosotros su recorrido.
title: Getting to know Cajon del Maipo

review_text: My wife and I had a great fishing day with Ben in late Jan. 2017. He picked us up in his 4x4 at our hotel. We drove in the direction of Torres Del Paine park until cutting off on a gravel road to a large estancia in sight of the Torres. We fished a small river (creek) about 10-15 meters wide that ran through a pasture area. Most of the time we were on the bank and not wading. Fishing was slow due to very low water conditions. The fish finally woke up and we each got some quality brown trout. Ben brought a good lunch and set up table and chairs for a nice rest at noon. The wind came up in the afternoon which made it quite a challenge to cast across the river (where the fish were hiding). I'm sure that and my poor casting ability cost me several more fish as I was unable to accurately cast to the proper spots. All in all a good day. Just wish I could get back there soon.
title: Great Day with Ben!

review_text: Javiera & Vicente are great guides, I´ve been in a couple of tours and they are just responsable, being with whole group during the journey, they just care about my experience at mountain, since you apply they make sure you are capable for that tour meanwhile just you need to be follow their leads, Javiera & Vicente are both certified to be at mountains, I´ve been trekking here at Chile since 2018 and Puma Adventures I would say is the best group, they care about safety, if you do not wanna go with group they offers private tour with is dope, that´s why I am giving them 5 stars review, if you want to choose a group, Puma Adventures is best option. Thank you Ennio for your kind words! We are glad that you liked the experience of going out with us! And for us, it is always a pleasure to share with you. See you on the mountain!
title: BEST TREKKING GROUP

review_text: The ride was great. Mathias, Leo and Rafa very professional, attentive and fun. Excellent! I really liked it. Review of: From Santiago: Valparaíso, Viña del Mar and Neruda Museum Muchas gracias por sus comentarios, nos alegra saber de que disfrutó junto a nosotros su recorrido.
title: Very professional

review_text: Julio was a great guide for our day trip. We also used this excursion instead of spending the day at the airport and were really glad we did. We loved the visit to the fish market, got to see red-footed boobies, had a fabulous lunch, and learned a lot. Julio was always mindful of our comfort and provided a ton of information about Chile, our drive, and our city tours. He was also very easy to communicate with Review of: A full Private Tour of Valparaiso from Santiago
title: Great way to visit Valparaiso!

review_text: Our group spent 2 days with Hector and really enjoyed it. He is very knowledgeable could answer every question we had. Also made great suggestions on where to go and tailored the tour for us. When I go back I will definitely use Hector again
title: Very knowledgeable really enjoyed tours

review_text: Uncorked made our trip to Santiago. We took three tours, with Andrea and Barbara as our guides, through the Casablanca, Aconcagua, and Colchagua valleys. All three tours were quite different, but equally great. If we had to pick our favorite, we would probably pick Aconcagua, although I believe that Casablanca is their most popular tour. We have taken several extensive wine tours both in the U.S. wine regions and abroad (Bordeaux, Tuscany, Rioja), and my husband and I both remarked that the Uncorked tours were among the best we have taken anywhere. The wines are also high quality, which stands in stark contrast to many of the other wine tours available in Chile, which only go to the cheap, mass production wineries. Uncorked is world-class experience that is absolutely worth the price. Review of: Best Wine Tasting in Santiago
title: World-class wine tour

review_text: Great view of the city! There are different ways to get up, walking/biking or by the fulicular. If you want to get there fast and is not willing to do much exercise, take the funicular up ..but I advise at least to get down walking, it's really worth the view and the walk! But the best way I still gues it's by bike!
title: Great view of the city

review_text: A quirky museum with several life sized replicas of ships (inc Magellan’s Nao Victoria and Darwin’s Beagle) that you can walk on/ in etc. It is, however, quite a way out of town- you will need a taxi to get there (5000 pesos). There is no easy way to return as no taxis wait here- your best bet is to walk back to the main road and flag down a taxi (there are an awful lot of taxis in Punta Arenas so it shouldn’t be too difficult).
title: Long way out- well worth a visit.

review_text: Desert of the Atacama is a unique and impa place in the world, it was simple sensational the days I was there, the We Love Chile a company would be and provided us with an excellent service, very punctual in their schedules, wonderful guides, I want to let you know that the Celeste guide very attentive and very polite, I want to manifest my satisfaction with the total, and say worth apena to do all the TUR with the We Love Chile!!! Ficamos muito felizes em saber que sua experiência no Deserto do Atacama foi incrível! 😊 Agradecemos imensamente pelas palavras sobre a nossa equipe, nossos guias sempre se dedicam a fazer os passeios ainda mais especiais. Agradecemos a confiança e ficamos à disposição para futuras aventuras!❤️
title: Wonderful all the TUR

review_text: We did the morning your with Chris and the night tour with Liz. Both guides were amazing and knowledgable about their country/city. Chris took us through the markets and to the cemetery and educated us about the traditional Chilean food as well as the history and politics. Chris brings along these trinkets to show you pictures and audio recordings of historical moments. Liz also showed us around to different places like the plaza de armas where she recommended their amazing completos/Italianos! She also took us to the presidential palace to show us some of the Chilean history and politics. Both guides were nothing short of amazing.
title: Love the tour and guides

review_text: Fantastic experience the instructors super professional and friendly. Great equipment and felt very safe the entire time Review of: Medio Día de Kayak en el Lago Llanquihue Thanks for your comment, always welcome!
title: Fantastic experience

review_text: Fantasilandia is by far the better park in Chile (if not the only one). Good roller costers, fair price... I recomend to go by taxi, also in Metro.
title: Fun and in the middle of a huge park!

review_text: We did the Villarrica Volcano ascent with Politur after being recommended through our hotel. We were able to drop by the day before to fit hiking gear which I would totally recommend to avoid some stress in the early morning. There was a small hiccup with our hotel pickup arriving 30 minutes late but everything else went smoothly. The ascent was a tough climb but not as hard as we expected from reading other reviews. It took around 3 hours to reach the summit after taking the chair lift. The climb itself is not that interesting since it’s just over snow. But the mountaineering equipment make it feel like a real expedition. The views climbing up are stunning, the country is laid out before your eyes like a map, you can see over a 100 kilometres in the distance. Reaching the summit is very satisfying, the idea that’s it’s an active volcano makes it all the more exciting. Finally sliding down is a lot of fun. Totally worth doing. The guides were patient, encouraging and spoke good English.
title: Villarrica Volcano ascent, great experience & good guides

review_text: We went on the 3 day/2 night tour of the Uyuni Salt Flats leaving from San Pedro de Atacama in Chile. Cruz Andina organised the tour, and when we crossed the border into Bolivia the company who took us on the tour was White and Green Bolivia, who transported us in their jeep. It was all well-organised and seamless. Alfio was our guide. The tour was in Spanish, and even though we only spoke basic Spanish we got by, particularly with the help of a bilingual tour mate! The accomodation was basic but very comfortable, and the food provided was great, my food allergy was easily accommodated for. Alfio was a wealth of knowledge, friendly and easy-going. He took lots of fun photos of us throughout the tour, particularly on the Salt Flats, which were an incredible and otherworldly site. Other particularly memorable moments were visiting Laguna Colorada with its many flamingos, soaking in the Termas de Polques and climbing the Italian Perdidas. The tour was also a convenient way to transit from San Pedro to Uyuni, and then depart from Uyuni to La Paz or somewhere else in Bolivia. We highly recommend this tour.
title: Excellent San Pedro to Uyuni tour

review_text: The tours are excellent, sites with wonderful views providing amazing photos. The agency has also always been on top and the guides are attentive.
title: Perfect journey

review_text: Wonderful experience! I recommend going with a tour since the path is difficult if you don't know it and they can explain more details about the place to you. It is an amazing landscape!
title: AMAZING

review_text: Colin gave us a day to remember with prompt pickup, a knowledgeable and colourful market tour, then an unforgettable lunch experience. Four courses delivered with the freshest possible ingredients, and hands-on preparation in a delightful home venue, we loved every flavour and the chance to learn about Chilean life in a very special way. Fantastic food, wine and company. If you have the opportunity to do this, just grab it with both hands! A unique and very lovely day, for foodies and people who relish something different totally and individual. Review of: Small-Group Santiago Food and Market Tour Including Mercado Central
title: Great experience, delicious lunch - memorable day

review_text: Great experience with tours to Farellones, Valparaiso and Viña del Mar, Valle Nevado and Black Island ⁇ by Simone and Marcelo. Special thanks to the drivers Guide Chris Simonette and Cristian Castro and the guide Lilian for cultural information, attention, care and professionalism.
title: Aggregated experience

review_text: Claudio was a great tour guide - very knowledgeable and made the tour really fun! I had a great day and highly recommend doing this tour if you only have limited time in Santiago - you get to see loads of amazing sights and taste some good wine and food! Claudio also kept in touch and gave me some further tips for my trip down to Patagonia which was much appreciated - he is an excellent tour guide! :) Review of: Valparaiso Port and Vina del Mar Full-Day Tour from Santiago
title: Great tour guide!

review_text: My experience at Escuela de Surf Arica was fantastic. Great location, great gear, great atmosphere, great people. Marcelo and Victoria are awesome people and the training lesson was a blast. I learned a lot in a short period of time and am hooked. Can't wait till the next time I can surf and thanks for the Marcelo and Victoria I had a perfect first experience. I went with two friends, one of which was pretty good and didn't do the lesson so the rental experience for him was great and really easy. Highly recommended for anyone: experienced just needing gear, beginner needing some more instruction, or a first timer like me. If you're in Arica, DO THIS! :) thanks for your review, i look forward to hearing from you and your family soon
title: Perfect!

review_text: Sean (our tour director) is an amazing and knowledgeable historian of Chilean culture. I will never imagine such a great experience along with all my family, we were 11 in the group. The time learning about the Alpacas and listening to the processes, the feeding, breeding, the fashion, etc is certianly unique. After our stylish and fashion Alpaca's tour Sean took us to one of Chile's marvels....there was the whole Pacific with astonishing views, wind and nature all over the place...this was completed with a view of the penguins from the shore. always will remember this day in my life Review of: Private Full-Day Chilean Treasures Nature Tour: Alpacas and Penguins Thanks, Angel. I really appreciate the time you took to write such a nice and detailed review. It was a pleasure meeting you and your sweet family. I am so glad you enjoyed yourselves and had fun with the alpacas and spotting penguins in their natural habitat! All the best, Sean
title: Unique Best in class Chilean Turism

review_text: How am I supposed to describe the park in this tiny little TripAdvisor box? I cannot, so I will not. Beautiful experience in a beautiful place at the end of the world. Worth it if you are able to get down here. We hiked the W, a 5 day 4 night adventure. Again, well worth the time, money and energy.
title: Impossible to Summarize

review_text: We enjoyed our tour at the winery and off course the tasting. The tour started with a carriage ride in the wineyard. Then our guide Cesar showed us the rest of the winery and we ended up with tasting four different wines. Cesar explained everything very good and in a pleasant way. The winery is not so big so you're not visiting a "wine factory".
title: Visiting Laura Hartwig Winery

review_text: Unlike skiing in north america, you will be above the tree line and have large open spaces to ski. It is a wonderful setting. Try all three of the local hills (la Parva, Valle Nevado and El Colorado). I would do one day at each though, as the multi-pass is really not worth the extra price.
title: Beautiful andes!

review_text: It's amazing everything we visited in such a short time! Pancho is a great guide super attentive to all questions and with very good energy Review of: Santiago: Viña del Mar, Valparaiso & Casablanca Valley Tour
title: A day to get to know a lot

review_text: Lots of bad reviews here but we found the service to be very reasonable. The snow has come very late this year which gave us the chance to go and speak to Ski total before the big snow came and before the rush began. Arranged our contract for ski and snowboard equipment and clothing rental on Friday afternoon when the shop was empty; the employee spoke English and was very helpful. It is quite a lengthy process so I can see how people can get frustrated if they try and do it on the day they go skiing when the shop is very busy and everyone is rushed off their feet. Having made the rental contract we came back early on Monday morning once the snow had arrived and there was a certain level of organised chaos on account of the number of people who are there wanting fitted for boots, skis jackets etc. Once we had our kit there was a sign in table for transport to the mountain. Transport was very reasonably priced and we were given a bus number and taken to the transport area. There was somebody here checking tickets and helping people get in the right vehicle- all went very smoothly. The ride to the slopes took just over two hours as the road up to the mountains is treacherous and icy; our driver was great but you are limited by other trucks and cars struggling to make it up there ahead of you on the narrow track. Once up there we got 5 and a half hours of skiing before we got back in the van to descend. The way back only took an hour and a half as the track had been fully cleared of ice by the end of the day. Overall the experience could be more streamlined as if it was any busier it may have taken an age to get rental stuff sorted, contracts made etc before we got to the transport vehicles- avoid this by making the contract and exchanging details the day before you go when the shop is quiet. Expect a long ride to the slopes but this can't be helped. For us it was exactly what we required and we loved every minute of it. I normally ski in Kitzbuhel which is the benchmark for great service and seamless rental experience but the Santiago equivalent day trip including rental, transport and lift pass only cost us £110 each which wouldn't buy you lunch in Kitzbuhel so I guess you get what you pay for! I would recommend this company for the competitive price and reasonable service.
title: A great day on the slopes of El Colorado

review_text: The MTO agency rather disorganized, we were cancelled without reason the day before and then told that the tour was done. Then they complied with everything stipulated. The tour itself is very good, all the stops indicated were made and the times were very well set. We highlight the work of driver and guide Pablo who did his job very well and the most enjoyable walk. Review of: Small-Group Tour of Portillo Ski Center and Inca Lagoon from Santiago Gracias por compartir tu experiencia! Lamentamos el pequeño inconveniente pero nos alegra que la experiencia junto a nosotros haya sido buena. No dudes en contactarnos la próxima vez que vengas, estaremos encantados de recibirte, MTO Tour Team
title: Tour to Portillo and Laguna del Inca.

review_text: It's a stunning location surrounded by the Andes. We hired a car and stayed in a local hotel. We were up early and there well before the Santiago trippers, quiet and peaceful. The road isn't too difficult, all sorts of cars were making the journey. When you get to the quarry you will doubt you are on the right road. Keep going, you are and all becomes clear. The changing rooms are primative but the final touches to new showers were being made when we were there. Go it alone and have an experience, you won't regret it.
title: Go under your own steam.

review_text: We had a wonderful time seeing the highlights of Torres del Paine National Park and the Milodon Cave. We were worried because the weather forecasted rain and clouds, but our guide, Daniel, and driver, Roberto, made sure we saw the towers! Daniel is enthusiastic and engaging when sharing his love for these beautiful natural treasures! His enthusiasm was infectious, and his positivity kept the group engaged. He mixed nature and history and took some great photos too! I really cannot compliment him enough. I wanted to share some praise for Roberto as well. While it seemed his English was more limited, he was still able to exude friendliness. I have been on many tours all over the world, but hands down, he was the best driver I have ever had on a tour! He had an eagle eye and spotted condors, rheas, and guanaca for us. While nearly all the group were sleeping, I was awake to witness how carefully he avoided potholes while not excessively swerving for everyone's comfort - he did this for over an hour and I know it was probably exhausting. Truly, he's awesome. In any case, Torres del Paine is an unmissable place, but Roberto and Daniel made this an unforgettable experience! Gracias por tomar el tour junto a nosotros! esperamos haber entregado una experiencia inolvidable en el Parque junto a nuestro guía y conductor.. Te esperamos para la próxima.
title: Beautiful sights made better with a wonderful guide and driver!

review_text: Weloved the lagunas and the drive up there. Just make sure you have enough water, food and petrol - there is no place to get food or petrol easily. If you are wiling to eat out in one of the tiniy restaurants - as we did - you might get good, basic food of the region, but that`might not be everyone`s cup of tea. We drove up there in the afternoon - just counterclockwise to all the groups, as they go in the mornings. Could not have done it any better! It was sooo quiet!
title: Amazing!

review_text: A must-see place in Punta Arenas and it is also free for Chileans. Excellent experience that tells part of the history of Punta Arenas through those who were key pieces in its past.
title: Safety pin

review_text: Highlight of my trip to San Pedro. The drive alone was worth it. Beautiful mountain valleys and mostly just me, my truck, the road and the mountains. Pictures don't do justice to the color once you get to the lake and mountains either. Great place to go.
title: Amazing

review_text: A very different and interesting place. In the morning it is best to see the “phenomenon” of the reaction of hot water with cold and it is certainly worth knowing.
title: Incredible

review_text: We were first time visitors to Chile and booked this tour via MTA, and we are so glad we did. As others have mentioned, the Cajon is still closed to tour groups because of a bad accident with some tourists, so they substitute Ski Portillo now. Our small group fit well in the Sprinter van with plenty of space and comfort (much nicer than the big coaches/groups we saw). The best was Gonzalo - everything you could ask for in a guide. He gave a fully narrated tour in two languages while the driver took us to the various stops. Gonzalo was fun, funny, very knowledgeable, and genuinely cared that we had a good time. His passion was contagious. We loved the stops and explanations he gave, he took time to make sure we enjoyed the experience. He gave lots of pointers on other things to do/see in Santiago too. I dreaded the meal stops, fearing they were “tourist traps”, but the food and wine was reasonable and good. It’s a full day and we highly recommend Gonzalo and MTO tours! Review of: Small-Group Cajón del Maipo Full-Day Tour and Picnic Dear Jerry, Thank you for your comment! We are very happy to know that you enjoyed the tour with us. We will pass on the message to Gonzalo who will be proud to read your review. It is very important for us and our guides to know that you had a good experience. We will be happy to welcome you to another of our tours in the near future, when the circumstances are right. Best regards, Maria from MTOtour
title: Great experience - well worth the trip

The day of the excursion everything was perfect, I felt safe with them and me and my brother had an incredible time. The scenery is stunning. Please note, this experience is NOT for people with heart, respiratory or musculoskeletal conditions, and if you are sedentary, you may not feel well. Otherwise... you must do it! Review of: Andes Day Volcano 8k Private Tour
title: Great experience

review_text: The Expedition to Laguna San Rafael See with pictures @ http://run.kobish-il.com/LSR/LSR.htm The story starts 6 months ago when I decided to make a trip to Chile, the trip planning process included some discussions with friends and very shortly the important goals where defined, since I love Kayaking and heard about Laguna San Rafael and the San Rafael majestic glacier such an expedition was set as a corner stone... After consultation with Yosale Dror from my Kayak club (Optimist Sdot-Yam) I have made a decision to paddle in the unknown waters where tide range is 5 meters, currents are strong and weather is unpredictable with a professional guide. I have started looking for a guide and found Rolando Toledo from AguaHielo. Quitralco 411, Puerto Aisén, Chile Tel: +56 9 7605 3580 Mail: aguahieloexpediciones@gmail.com Besides the everlasting smile on Rolando’s face in the gorgeous pictures and videos, Rolando answered me in perfect English which for me is very useful, making the communication easy and fluent, we have set a date for the expedition on February 20th and I was waiting for it impatiently :). On January 21st My partner Giora and me were on a flight to Chile and after trekking in Torres del paine Jeinimini and more we arrived at Coyhaique and rented a nice pickup, first thing we did was driving to Puerto Aysen to meet Rolando and get acquainted We have met Rolando and indeed our good internet impression became an understanding we have made the right choice, we have made a short kayak paddling trip down the Rio Simpson made sure the equipment fits us and asked Rolando for a tip where to camp, to make a long story short our pickup (not 4x4) required some help, it was 21:00 (PM) and Rolando came in 15 minutes from call and towed us out.... what a man We agreed to meet on February 20th in Puerto Tranquilo where the expedition will start We made our way down the Caratera Austral had great time visiting Capillas de Marmul, Rio Baker (rafting in Puerto Bertrand) Cochrane (Festival), Villa O’Higgins (El Musco glacier), Chilechico red rocks (Rolando’s recommendation) and more... On the 19th we were in Puerto Rio Tranquilo and on the 20th afternoon Rolando arrived as agreed with his famous Bongo loaded with Kayaks, food and equipment Roland opened with a short plan review using a map The planned route was the following We packed quickly and headed Los Tres where we plan to get into the water tomorrow In Los Tres we met with Don Jaime and Sra Vera, we got a splandid Salmon based dinner (Lazanga, and on the plancha) And heard the stories on Salmon fishing, Jaime's Balsa (Raft), How the way to Puerto Grosse was opened using fire and water... vey very warm and homelike feeling Morning the Los Tres point is the merge of 3 rivers and due to the rain in the last few days water level is high and the current is fast (8 knots) looks chalanging but fun as well, we pack the Mexicano (Marco) is saying last goodbye to Vera and we go in, the feeling can not be described, the current the mountains the waterfalls so the best way will be to look at Edgardo singing down the river Rolando is leading making sure the path is clear from wood and eddies and soon we are getting into the pacific waters We continue to paddle and the wind is coming up, Rolando takes a decision to call it a day and we are heading a small lagoon very protected and nice, We lift the Kayaks 4 meters since tide is low and in minutes Edgardo and Rolando are setting the camp and start cooking Dinner is a great so a great day is behind us Second day weather looks nice and we start paddling we pass a Salmon farm and watch the jumping fish, the farms are nice but bring a lot of pollution... while paddling one can see the seagulls tonina dolphines and sea lions We pass the the strait of Golfo Elfantes, paddling down current avoiding the eddies and having grreeat fum, Patagonian weather is surprising so after a very good weather at day start we suddenly get strong head wind waves start rising and rain is striking our faces, Rolando is signing to get closer to the shore and is tieing one of the boats to his Kayak we are back in safety soon enough :), wind goes down we continue paddling and get to a very nice beach for the second night, good food, good wine, full moon light, huge campfire what more can we ask for Third day, we will start late because we want the incoming tide water current to take us into Laguna San Rafael, paddling against the current will not be a good idea :), since we are lucky not only tide current is at our back but also the wind, Rolando has a small sail but all us fly with the current and back wind into the laguna and get to see the floating glaciers Camping at Laguna San Rafael is convinient, meal is good as always and in the next morning we are hiking by foot to the San Rafael glacier mirador (lookout) a little rest from the long ~110 KM we covered in the last 3 days Afternoon short Kayak trip to the glacier during which we pickup some ice from the water for a special use Last day in the laguna consists of paddeling through the ice to the far side of the glacier and walking to its blue icy face, the expirience is so wonderful words will not be good enough and also the pictures only hint how great this is For dinner Rolando says he will fish, I must confese I wasn't optimistic but in an hour I witnessed the miracle Rolando got 4 large Robalo fish which Edgardo prepared in the oven.... how come we have an oven during an expadition? well Rolando being a very generous expedition manger got hard rain forecast and decided to rent the guarderia building for us and eventhough the rain was not that hard we got the luxurious building along with wine and very nice jokes Marko was telling we had great evening In the morning we took all the gear packed and loaded a small boat that took us back Great great expirience, many thanks to the profesionalism of Rolando and Edgardo and the nice team, Giora, Roberto, Francisco, Marko, Mauricio and me Kobi the writer of the above Bottom line very recommended expedition and if you decide to do it only with Rolando and Aguahielo
title: Laguna San Rafael expedition

review_text: The best tours we have ever been. We did El Tatio Geysers, Rainbow Valley and Puritama Hot Springs. Pato was extremely knowledgeable on almost everything from botanic to history. Professional pictures was a great plus. Definitely recommended
title: Best tours, great pictures

review_text: I was crammed for the whole day (12 hours) in the very back row of a minibus, a seat that felt more like a “little ease”, with 0.70 sq. ft., no room to stretch legs under the seat in front because of the back wheel. No switching around (some seats were more comfortable I think)! The Porvenir museum was an interesting stop. Penguins are visible only from a distance and as the guide insisted so much on not taking any food on the premises, I left my bag (with food but also with my binoculars) in the bus. I suppose the excursion would have seemed nicer if the material and physical conditions had not been so terrible. To top it all, the driver would either switch cold ventilation to very high or stop all ventilation, causing windows to fog up. To cut a long story short, certainly not worth 90 USD, + lunch and entrance fee to the park.
title: Pinguino Rey: not worth 90 USD ++

review_text: Tremendous experience the buses were clean and the operational team. Attendees Monica and Mauricio explained the whole process and we had no stumbling block. I recommend them Review of: Cable Car, Funicular and Sightseeing Bus in Santiago one day Estimado viajero, nos alegra saber que disfruto de su recorrido y junto a nuestro equipo de trabajo, muchas gracias por compartir su experiencia con nosotros. ¡Esperamos su pronta visita!
