review_text: The most magical 10 days in Torres del Paine with Miguel and JP. We were absolutely blown away by the depth of their passion for the natural world. The 10 days we had with Miguel and JP were life changing. Their knowledge of the park's flora and fauna blew us away. Their [Miguel and JP's] tracking skills were phenomenal. We learnt so much from them. On top of all of this, they are incredibly ethical. The animals come first, always. The vegan snacks from Puerto Natales kept us fuelled and warm in the snow! We left already planning a future trip. If you're going to the park and want to see wildlife, leaving nothing but footprints, don't hesitate going with Miguel and JP! Review of: Torres del Paine fotográfico; amanecer/atardecer/paisajes/fauna (día completo)
title: Incredible experience

review_text: Excellent!! The guy who quoted us the tour, very kind, made us an itinerary accordingly, so that we could take advantage of the few days we were there. We missed knowing and without a doubt, we would take the service here again. All the schedules were met, the guides too, all very good vibes!! Especially Isaac, who accompanied us in Valle de la luna, took tremendous photos of us, was very kind and charismatic. Thank you all!! We had very nice experiences and memories :D
title: 100% recommended

review_text: We went to Lauca National Park last year, in august. It was a wonderful experience. No better place to leave behind your troubles. Open plains, vulcanos, more than 500 alpacas and vicunas. We organised the tour through a little tour agency in Arica: Orange Travel. You can e-mail them at orangetravel@terra.cl. We went for the 3 day tour (Lauca National Park + Las Vicunas National Reserve). I strongly recommend the full tour through Las Vicunas (with Salar de Surire), because it is the road less traveled. We were alone in the park for the complete day, only alpacas and vicunas held us company. And our wonderful tour guide Oreol, who gave us the absolute best tour experience ever. He lives in Putre, not far from the parks. He knows the region, drove us around in his little bus and took his little dog with hem. He invited us to meet his friends on a barbeque while we watched the football game Chile-Argentina. That is when we fell in love with Chile. It was wonderful. If you go to Chile, don't miss out on this northern region. This was absolutely better than San Pedro de Atacama, where we saw more people than wildlife and nature. Take the less traveled road and head to Arica!
title: Undiscovered: great experience!

review_text: A very good introduction to Valparaíso-its history and explanation of the art. Also very knowledgeable about Chilean history and current affairs. Geans is obviously very passionate about his city. Able to answer questions very confidently and also suggest places to eat and drink. Review of: Walking Tour Valparaiso, History & Art - Private Optional
title: A great introduction to the city! Well worth it!

review_text: Very good! Beautiful place!! The Viajar Chile agency fulfilled everything it promised, including punctuality (which is rare for this type of service). At 9pm the day before the tour, they send a message setting the time they will pick you up at your hotel/airbnb. On the day of the tour, they arrive punctually. Another advantage, the Rodrigo guide is not a "robot" that decorates a text and gives standardized information to the client. He really understands a lot about Chile's history, culture, etc.
title: Portillo is beautiful!

review_text: It was a stunning visit, the vineyard, the facilities, the atmosphere in the dining room with its excellent food, all fantastic!
title: Lunch and tasting at the Haras de Pirque Vineyard.

review_text: This is a very strange, personal museum, full of items that Pablo Neruda collected and lived with. The audio guide is quite comprehensive and will take about 45 minutes as long as you follow the 14 numbered rooms in the correct order. Fantastic for anyone interested in the sea and sailors as th house has a strong nautical theme. Some good photo spots outside. The views of the sea from each room in the house are fantastic. A bit far out from Santiago for anyone without a car.
title: Great museum

review_text: Like a rugby scrum. You will be pushed and shoves. Overcrowding is an understatement. Saying that it's clean efficient and cheap
title: Don't travel at peak times

review_text: I think the vibe for the ferry got started before the Chileans realized they could overcharge non-Chileans and get away with it. This is for old boats that need a fair amount of work. Furnishings are worn, but, hey, it is a ferry and you're not sleeping on the deck. Don't pay up for the AAA rooms -- they need a lot of fixing and are no better than the lower-cost ones. Keep in mind, too, that if the captain can go by open ocean (in good weather), he will -- and there goes your viewing of the fjords. Pray for crummy, violent weather.
title: Only a good deal if you're a Chilean

review_text: Enormous shopping, with all the shops, but absurdly crowded. But beyond what you can imagine. So, entering the most popular shops, you need to be willing to want to garimpar. Most shops with clothes stacked, turned, people experimenting in the middle of the store and putting the pieces in qq place, finally, a chaos. The jumbo is inside the shopping, and tb eh bemm crowded, no matter the time of day and week, eh always extremely crowded. The wine and chocolate part is crazy. But it's worth it. For tour, in high season, choose other options.
title: A real chaos in high season.

review_text: Zita was an incredible hostess and was passionate about educating people on marine life. She is very knowledgable about the marine mammals of the area and shared her enthusiasm about preserving the natural habitat around the caleta. I would recommend this excursion to anybody. We were able to spot on land guanacos, Chilean foxes, and wild donkeys. In the ocean we saw blue whales, fin whales, penguins, an albatross, sea lions, and marine otters. An amazing day that my family will not soon forget. Dear Troy, Thank you so much for joining our tour and for your feedback! It is great to hear that you, Tammy and the boys had a great time! Very memorable tour for us too with the first blue whales of the season, in great company...! We hope to see you again one day, maybe Gary´s enthusiasm (and expertise) for whales would lead him and your family back to us one day. Have a Happy New Year! Greetings from us and the whales: Zita
title: Wildlife advocate

review_text: This is an excellent museum with an extra-nice cafe and shop with indigenous handicrafts and fine permanent exhibit of pre-columbian artifacts. We were blown away, however, by a special exhibit which is no longer on display -- Paracus culture funeral bundles with brilliantly colored and elaborately embroidered cloths. Don't know what's next. The museum is an easy walk from the city center.
title: Special exhibit

review_text: I had the opportunity to take the "Santiago 1973" tour with Sebastian. The tour is perfect if you want to know the recent history of Chile - which is sadly interesting. What I liked the most of this tour is its structure (4/5 stops very closed to each other and loaded with tons of historical content) and its originality (one-of-a-kind). I will recommend this tour to friends and family in a heartbeat
title: Santiago 1973 - Unique tour - Totally recommendable

review_text: Parque Pumalin is great if the weather is nice. The top is the new trail to Volcan Chaiten which erupted in 2008. The pleasant Camping el Volcan is 7 km away. Then at El Amarillo, the camping Ventisquero is one of the best in Chile, it lies 10 km from the highway and from there an easy trail brings you to the glacier. Those campsites are free offseason. The ferry(and the daily bus that boards the ferry) from/to Hornopiren is also great. Beware that the bus Puerto Montt Chaiten can be fully booked 2 days in advance.
title: Volcan Chaiten trail and Ventisquero Amarilllo campground

review_text: Spent there 3 days. Wonderful experience.Very impressive nature. Good tracks, very windy. Must have reservation for tracks in the park.
title: Wow

review_text: Tour guides extremely rude and do not treat the customer with respect! When we asked about respective things that were not on the tour, for example: picnic missing items of food, as the other companies made the question of putting more appetizing foods and more polite guides, at the times of questions, they were just bullshit! They don't leave the guests in the hotel on the back of the tours. They leave in the corners, super dangerous of Santiago. I do not recommend this company in any way! Olá renata! Lamentamos muito que sua experiência não tenha sido positiva. O respeito e a qualidade no atendimento são essenciais, e seu relato nos alerta para pontos que precisam ser melhorados, especialmente na postura dos guias e na logística dos retornos. Desde janeiro de 2025, realizamos ajustes para aprimorar o atendimento e garantir uma experiência mais confortável e segura aos nossos clientes. Seu feedback é fundamental para continuarmos evoluindo. Esperamos poder oferecer uma experiência positiva no futuro.
title: Bad guides, disrespectful and poorly explained services

review_text: Araya was a recommendation from a friend, and it was the best decision of our trip. I went with my mother (a lady of 71), and they were always very attentive to her. All the guides and drivers were very careful with her on all the tours we did. The vans are very good, the food too. The agency sends a message before the tour with the schedules, the names of the guides, what clothes to wear and what you need to bring on each tour. They were never late. We loved Atacama too much and the choice for Araya was definitely fundamental for us to have this differentiated experience. We love a lot, and I intend to come back, this time with my husband. Sure, we will close with them again! Thank you for taking so good care of us!
title: Attentive Agency

review_text: We had originally signed up for the 8K hike but were asked if we wanted switch to a shorter hike which then included a trip to the hot springs. The tour guide picked us up exactly on time at our hotel. He spoke perfect English and was very informative on the trip to the mountains. We were ready at this point to get out of the large city of Santiago and see more of the countryside. I would definitely recommend having a driver who knows this area over renting a car, especially when we got off the main roads. The 4K hike was strenuous (it is the mountains) but not too much for our group though we were glad we went for the shorter hike. The views were gorgeous and I got to mark hiking in the Andes and seeing a live volcano off my bucket list. It was then a short drive to the volcanic hot springs. Soaking in the springs on a cool fall day was nothing short of amazing. I am so glad we took this option especially since I also got to take soaking in a natural hot springs off my bucket list. Review of: Andes Day Volcano 8K - Cajón del Maipo
title: Marked several things off my bucket list!

review_text: I thought the organisation and tour guide was great . Super punctual and organised so clearly and easily- our guide was also lovely . She was bubby and friendly BUT this was essentially a tour where you sat on a bus all day as you were driven to a few locations specific for tourists where you are loaded off the bus to buy goods. Eg 9am after a 7 am pickup we were left off at a warehouse with clothes and tourist gifts to purchase and were told it was also a “wine tasting”. Most people didn’t even have breakfast so a wine tasting didn’t go down very well. Didn’t make sense at all and a giant waste of time to encourage us buy goods we didn’t want. There was some good information given by the tour guide on the bus she was very friendly however it was very scripted and there was a section where we got off of the bus to view street art and she only spoke about one piece of art - the rest of the walk was essentially to take photos which you could do on your own or with a local walking tour . I think in retrospect, I would get the public bus from Santiago and maybe a walking tour in Valpairiso as this was just a bit of a waste of a day on a bus . It was very expensive as it didn’t include any food or water. We were left off at a restaurant for lunch which was quite pricey too so a bit of a gut punch when you’ve just paid a decent amount for the tour itself. If your looking to be chauffeured around to view these areas from the window of a bus and like the stereotypical tourist trap chat and destinations - this is the tour for you. If you want to explore these 2 destinations and have more intimate information on the area and street art and history - I would probably recommend a different tour . Great organisation, friendly staff , just not great value and we didn’t do much ! Sorry :( Maybe I booked the wrong tour but from talking to some other people in the group they had similar feelings. Sorry to be so harsh but I think the itinerary might benefit from a bit of a review to inject some life into this day tour Review of: Full Day Group Tour - Viña Del Mar-Valparaiso -Casablanca -Reñaca Thank you for sharing your experience with us! MTO Tour Team
title: Not for me but it might suit someone else !

review_text: My partner and I arrived here full of anticipation of an interesting tour and tasting. Instead we were greeted by uninterested and indifferent staff who seemed totally bored.
title: Indifference

review_text: We did the 3D / 2N tour from Uyuni to San Pedro and it was awesome. Our guide, Ron, was brilliant and kept us entertained the whole trip. There’s a fair amount of driving but it felt like we were barely in the car and every stop was really informative. 10/10 - definitely recommend.
title: Awesome trip

review_text: The landscapes are amazing, but going there is perrengue! It is a ski resort that the one-day tourist is not welcome. It has no structure. The bathroom, even paid, has huge queues. There's nothing to eat or drink except for a food truck. You don't get close to the pond and you have to turn around in the middle of so many people to take a decent photo. Review of: Portillo and Laguna del Inca Tour Lamento muito saber de sua experiência. Parece que a estação de esqui tem algumas deficiências importantes em termos de serviços e comodidades para os visitantes. É importante que os destinos turísticos possam oferecer uma experiência mais completa e acolhedora para todos os visitantes. Espero que você tenha experiências melhores em seus próximos passeios!
title: Perrengue nothing chic

review_text: Our tour was wonderful. Nicole and Maurício were very helpful and friendly. We recommend the experience to everyone. Review of: Cable Car, Funicular and Sightseeing Bus in Santiago two days Ficamos felizes em saber que teve uma boa experiência com nossa equipe e esperamos sua próxima visita!

review_text: Amanda, I would like to express our sincere thanks for all the attention and support we received during our stay in Chile. His dedication and professionalism were fundamental to making our experience exceptional. From planning to the final details, you were always present, ensuring everything went perfectly. We are very pleased with the service provided by MineironoChile and, especially, with your service. Certainly, this trip will remain in our memories for a long time. Once again, our very thank you.

review_text: Five star experience from beginning to end. Joaquin and team provided me all the information I needed to a day prior to my scheduled excursion. He arrived on time with a very welcoming and pleasant attitude. What I loved most is he gave me information and history about the city that I didn’t know. We booked THE PRIVATE TOUR which gave us private pickup and more time to talk. Once there things moved quickly but was provided all the information we needed to ensure a safe horseback ride. He wanted to be sure we spent most time riding through the Andes. During the experience he constantly gave us tips to ensure safety and enjoyment. This I clearly something that he loves to do and comes natural. After the experience be ready for the best wine you’ve ever experienced! Review of: Authentic Andes Adventure: Private Horse Riding and Cheese & Wine Thanks a lot for recommending us! It was a pleasure meeting you Ashley! Kindest regards,
title: United States

review_text: We really loved the tours! My son, despite being small, enjoyed it a lot. Rodrigo's service was excellent!

review_text: Excellent alternative to take clients or visitors from abroad. Valentina, our guide, with a wonderful command of English, knowledge of wines (and history), added to her charm, made a fabulous visit that was a perfect match with high quality wines. Review of: Premium Wine Tour in Viña Cousiño Macul Spanish official

review_text: We went to Valparaiso and Viña del Mar with the guide Tomás who gave us a lesson about the local culture, the driver Juan also collaborated so that we had an excellent experience!

review_text: I took the Vina del Mar and Valparaiso tour - guide was nice enough english was above average but we were taken a place to eat at lunch that was completely over rated - food was average and overpriced for what it was.
title: Average

review_text: This was such an unforgettable and amazing experience. Carla was so helpful with planning and booking and answering all the questions I had. JP was constantly making sure I was comfortable and happy. Miguel was professional, passionate, experienced, and relentlessly talented. The team worked so hard to make sure I not only saw a puma, but had enough time to capture a photo I was happy with. They are also clearly respectful of the park and its conservation efforts. The puma and its space are honoured at all times. Can’t recommend this enough!

review_text: Beautiful landscapes, worth the long drive to get up there. It's very cold and windy, so make sure to dress appropriately, as that was my only regret. You can also see local fauna at that altitude, like vicuñas and vizcachas.

review_text: La Plaza has with well kept gardens, palm trees and fountains. It has a replica of Big Ben Clock and its chimes. It is a great place to rest from your walking. During siesta time, most shops are closed, if you fancy an ice cream you will need to get one, couple of streets away from the Plaza. And it is true, there are no coffee shops around the Plaza at all😩😩

review_text: Amazing structure with a 360 view of Santiago. Engineering wonder as well. Very uncrowded at the top with tons of window space for viewing.
title: Breathtaking View of Santiago

review_text: TOP 5 things to do in Chile! Hiked to the top twice this year (March & November). Both times were spectacular! If you are in Pucon and the weather is good, this is a must do! (Warning: Both times I had great weather... i definitely see how this could be miserable is the weather is not good.) Both times I went with Aguaventura Tour Company and they were great, honest and legit!

review_text: I am glad that I took the Urban Adventure / Urban Bites tour! This was how we found this! It is a great way to see a sky view of Santiago literally. Wear comfortable shoes and be prepared to climb stairs. There is plenty of seating along the way. But the view at the top is breathtaking! There are souvenir shops and food/drinks available too while you’re resting. Dear Visitor, thank you very much for your comment, a hug.
title: Worth the View!!!

review_text: They are experts in MTB, the equipment is first-class, the technique and guidance are dry, they fully adapt to your physical conditions during the operation. You are being guided at all times, they look for you wherever they agree and leave you later. Gracias por compartir con nosotros, fue un gran día el poder mostrarles los mejores senderos de Los Andes mountains, los esperamos para una próxima aventura. No dejes de pedalear.
title: The best in Santiago

review_text: We went with my team recently. Unfortunately the last track of Los Mineros was bad; When our time was up, the manager came and told us the answer to the last riddle, but we explained to him that we would never have been able to leave because the clues were bad. The manager told us that the previous group must have changed certain clues. In the end they didn't give us any compensation and we were very sad so we had to go to a place to endure the bitter pill... Currently, even as a team we remember this situation; Sometimes I dream of being trapped in the mine, without air, without food and without water. I still don't understand why the chemical elements written on the walls were not used. From that day on, the team was never the same. Let's hope that the next time we go they don't break our hearts like that fateful September afternoon.
title: We were disappointed.

review_text: We visited Portillo on one day and Viña del Mar and Valparaiso on another. Guides know a lot about the history of Chile and the regions we visited and speak well Portuguese. I highly recommend.
title: Wonderful tours

review_text: We hiked Villarrica Volcano with Zenit in mid September 2022. The guides are fantastic - knowledgeable, personable and great at encouraging you to keep moving when it gets a bit tough! We felt safe whilst out on the volcano with these guys. I'd recommend doing the hike with Zenit - thank you to all the team there for making the day so great!
title: Great guides and experience

review_text: I'm not a fan of artisan markets at all, but I really liked the building and this is the main reason I recommend visiting. It's colonial charm got me. We've had lunch upstairs and I really enjoyed it so I can recommend eating there as well. It's some kind of special because of the view and the ambiance even though it's a little pricy. And yeah I enjoyed buying some overpriced papaya sweets - I simply couldn't resist. :) As halfblooded Chilean I prefer buying pricy over stolen cheap stuff. Ok maybe it's more the Swiss in me. ;)
title: Not a fan of artisan markets

review_text: Even if you already know a lot about the military dictatorship this museum is still worth visiting for its architecture and some interesting installations. While there check out the grafitti in Barrio Yungay.
title: A ncessary museum. Interesting architecture.

review_text: Very nice small place you can walk everything quietly in less than 1 hour, anyone can do the tour there are no climbs. The only bad thing is that there are no toilets being so touristic. There is a small craft fair, and they also sell little things to eat. Only parking is paid.
title: Cute cute but no bathrooms

review_text: We're glad we dropped by to see this impressive building and see the changing of the royal guards (together with a massive Chilean flag on the main road!). We didn't go in and I am not sure if you can, we just admired the buidling from outside. The Catherdral is not too far away
title: Heart of the city

review_text: It was an amazing day, full of laughs with the best Guide (Cris) besides Guide is the best photographer also kkkk thank you very much
title: Travel Embalse del yeso/ thermas

review_text: This review is for the penguin and Magdalena Island tour. Overall a good tour with some great guides, but organization and communication needs to be improved. We waited at the bus-sur station from 640am~830am for what was supposed to be a 7-730am pickup. No communication from the organizers and it was unclear it the tour was going to happen or was canceled. Eventually the staff arrived, and it turned out a cruise ship caused problems that morning. We needed to check in at both the bus and the boat. The dock was so close it would have been nice it we had the option to walk rather than ride the bus just a few blocks. We eventually set sail ~1 hour late, maybe more, and had a smooth sail across to the island. On the way guides answered questions in both spanish and english, showing maps and talking about this area. We saw a whale, dolphins, seals, and sea lions. The island itself was fantastic! You have about an hour to walk a 1mile loop. The guides were great, taking photos and answering questions along the way! My issue with this tour lies with the "main" guide and the feeling of the morning's delay constantly being pushed onto the patrons. The entire walk we were hounded with reminders of the 1 hour limit (despite moving more than fast enough) and at the end as we were loading the boat, constant mentions of how late we were returning to punta arenas. The other passengers we sat with, along with my group, didn't appreciate that when it wasn't our fault we left port late that morning. If I had to do it over, I may check out Solo Expediciones where some friends of ours had a better experience.
title: Penguins are cute but tour organization and communication needs work

review_text: An easy 4 k ride from town with sign posts every k to make sure you get there. These are ruins from a pre Incan civilsation of people from Atacama. It is interesting to contrast with some of the various Incan strucutres we had seen in Peru and Bolivia. The fort was very strategically located with the possibilty of a sneak attack here nearly impossible. This is also the site of some fierce batttles with the Spanish invaders. Also great views from here.
title: Take a bike ride

review_text: Ray was a knowledgeable and friendly guide and I really wanted to give the tour a 5 as a result, but the content covered (I assume scripted by Tour4tips) was a bit too political for me, my adult son and his fiancée. I took another one on my adult children on the same tour 6 years ago and the spoken content was noticeably different especially during the General Cemetery walk. Six years ago, the tour felt much more “offbeat” with discussions of colorful characters buried at the cemetery (one had his tombstone covered in beers bottles!) and a walk through the Italian mausoleum (quite the structure!), versus this tour’s concentration on one political figure. That said, the walk through Market Central and La Vega was as wonderful as last time. The colors (and size!) of the produce, smells of the meats and fish, sounds of vendors trying to lure you to their stall to buy, and crowds of people going about their shopping all make for an energizing and vibrant experience not to be missed!
title: Santiago Offbeat - Wonderful Guide but Content too Political

review_text: Surprising place, tremendous, I never imagined that it has such beautiful places, when entering the mountain.. cliffs, native tree forests... Martina and Ramon excellent and professional guides.. If you doubt more than recommend, a must in the basin of Lake Llanquihue!!!

review_text: This is what it sounds like, a touristic experience. They pick you up in a small minibus and then drop you off close to Fallabella Parque Arauco where you switch to a larger bus. First you must wait for all the other 100 minibuses to arrive. If you stay close to the interchange point, ask if you can go there directly and skip the first minibus. Once you have received your sticker and arrived at the vineyard, you will be guided in a group to look at threes, a church, the factory (stay within the yellow lines) and finaly you will taste three different wines. Afterwards, you are taken to the shop where you can buy wine. The wine tasting itself is around 30 minutes, rest is minibus, bus, the 1h guided walk in the park and factory, then bus and minibus back. Half day in my case was pickup at 8am, and drop off (not at starting point but in Patio Bellavista) at 2pm. Review of: Santa Rita Vineyard Tour with Lunch An unforgettable experience! Estimada(o) Karl B. Lamentamos profundamente que le haya faltado tiempo durante su experiencia junto a nosotros. Respetamos su punto de vista y por eso nos gustaría conocer si posee alguna crítica directa que nos permita mejorarla ya que en lo que leímos, no existe ningún comentario de algún error o crítica que podríamos mejorar. Por otro lado, queremos resaltar que el retorno de nuestros viajeros es en el lugar que ellos prefieren. Bien sea en su hotel o cualquier otro punto cercano a las diferentes opciones que brindamos para el beneficio y la comodidad de todos. Nos encantaría conocer de su parte mayores detalles para continuar mejorando día a día y seguir brindándole un servicio de calidad a todos nuestros queridos viajeros. ¡Escríbanos por privado! Feliz retorno a casa. Un abrazo.

Because of the forest fires in Valparaiso, we had to reshuffle our itinerary and arrive in Santa Cruz five days earlier than expected. Everyone we encountered was friendly, welcoming, and knowledgeable. The wines and properties were fantastic. We are so grateful to Connie for being so flexible, accommodating, thorough, prompt, and kind while we rearranged our plans. Highly recommend Colchagua Wine Tours! 🍷🍷🍷🍷🍷

review_text: Quebrada del Diablo (or Garganta del Diablo) is an awesome, AWESOME bike ride. From the entrance to the quebrada, it's about a 2 hour ride, twisting through rock walls and dirt hills. It's probably not for beginners, but with a bit of athleticism, you'll be fine. The views are gorgeous, but be careful, THERE ARE NO SIGNS! There are karns in some places, and footprints and horse hoof-prints to follow in others, but we eventually got lost. We found two other couples who were also lost, so we know it wasn't just us. We eventually found the river and followed it downstream over hills of sand until we found a way out onto the road. We definitely weren't on the trail, though. If you like to mountain bike, don't miss this! But be prepared and ASK about the path before you go! (I bet Juan Carlos, who is in charge of bike rentals at Apacheta in the plaza, knows!)
title: Awesome bike ride, but be careful! There are no signs!

We didn't feel like coming back.

review_text: We hiked the park over 5 nights and 6 days (why rush through the park when we had spent so much effort to get there). We were blessed with perfect weather and clear skies. Every day had a wow factor and this is a glorious place on earth to hike. Only negative was the huge queue to get into the park (have to be processed through the national park office) which took ages and seemed very inefficient.
title: Just wonderful - day after day

review_text: Costanero Centro is the largest shopping mall in South America filled with many shops located in the tallest building in South America. It can be very chaotic to be there regardless of the time. Each floor is dedicated to a specific theme. I was with friends who had to stop at the Zara store. There is a huge food court on the 6th floor as well as a cinema in the complex. The Hard Rock Cafe is on the ground floor along with Jumbo, a supermarket. It is close to the metro station Tobalaba and has access to Sky Costanero, a 360 degree outlook with great views on a clear day. The entrance fee here, however is pricey-15,000 pesos. Pay attention when you are there since petty thievery occurs if you are not alert.
title: Interesting visit!

review_text: I really wanted to come here but my husband didn’t. He admitted it wasn’t as boring as he thought it would be. They’ve done a great job with the audio tour. You get a real sense of his life and are done and dusted in about 30mins. The house is charming and full of delightful quirks.

review_text: I went with my mom as a pit stop during a day of exploring and I'm so glad we went! We went to the Costanera center at about 12pm on Friday and there was no line at all, the entire platform was empty so we were able to relax, take our time, and get lots of pictures! They have free wifi and the workers are really helpful, but stay out of your way and let you look around. It's very nice and good for families and children or anyone looking for a great view of the city. Some days the smog can be pretty thick and it obstructed the view of the mountains while I was there, but I'd go again!
title: Awesome View

review_text: La Vega is the market where the locals go. You’ll find numerous stalls of fresh vegetables and fruits here. The second floor is the best kept secret for dining in Santiago. There are rows and rows of restaurants serving authentic Chilean cuisine. If you ate all your meals in Santiago at La Vega you would be doing better than 99% of the other tourists. Be sure to visit the flower market located in a separate smaller building just outside the main building at La Vega.

review_text: In chile we dont have many of this sort of activities, the planetary of stgo is a must if your a local or a foreigner. review_text: While visiting Santiago we were lucky enough to get to watch a soccer (aka, futbol) game (Chile versus Burkina Faso). We had a large group of Americans and when our friend was buying the tickets he was told we would not need our passports. Upon arrival, however, they would not let us in saying we had to have it. We did finally get in when we gave them our passport numbers which our leader had by email for the trip. So make sure you have identification when you attend a game. You will need to bring pesos to use the bathroom while there. While walking to the game the military police had obviously sprayed some teargas and all of our group members were suffering from burning eyes, sneezing, and/or burning throat. That was surprising. I realized afterwards that many Chileans had handkerchiefs over their faces. Now I know why. For Chile having such a great team I was surprised they did not have a nicer stadium. We did enjoy the game however. The patriotism was catching and we had soon learned and were chanting their cheers with them. It was a great game and of course, Chile won! If you take the subway/metro to the game, remember the gates close at 11 and leave yourself plenty of time to make the long hike to get back in time. Our group squeezed in just as the police were closing the gates. Close call!
title: Great Experience But There Are Some Pointers

review_text: I booked a airport shuttle (2 days before my flight out of Calama Airport) from my airbnb location in San Pedro de Atacama with Francisco for 15,000 Chilean pesos ($25USD). They were to pick me up at least 3 hours before my flight out of Calama airport, and said the drive takes about one hour to the airport. My flight was at noon. Francisco said they would pick me up at the airbnb house in town between 8:30-9:00am. He gave me a Whatsapp phone number to call or message with any questions. On the morning of my flight, I texted and called starting at 9:14am when there was still no one to pick me up. I even called the number listed on the website. Multiple messages and calls but no response. I was getting very worried I would miss my flight! Finally I frantically ran to the bus station at 9:45. The bus station employees said that there was no bus that would get me to the Calama airport now on time, that I would need a taxi right now in order to make my flight. The bus station employee was nice enough to get me a taxi and I was able to make it to the airport for a 50,000 Chilean pesos ($85USD)! I made it in time just as the flight was boarding! Two days later I saw that there was a missed phone call from Lithium's number on my Whatsapp. I called back and spoke with Eva. I was very upset and explained that I nearly missed my flight and emergently had to pay $85USD for a private taxi. I was very stressed out and teary-eyed that I nearly missed my flight. Eva apologized and said she would look into what happened and get back to me. I said I wanted $108USD refunded to me because they needed to pay back the original shuttle van cost and the cost of my last minute private taxi (this was the conversion rate at the time, as it changes every day). Ten days of messaging me and making excuses, like "it's raining in San Pedro" she never sent me the money. I made it easy by creating a custom link to Pay Pal for her to send me the money. Every day, she said she needed more time, and more excuses. Be VERY hesitant of all of these 5 star, perfect reviews. None of these were here when this happened to me January 3, 2018. Multiple perfect reviews are often written by false accounts, be very suspicious!
title: Thieves and Liars!

review_text: I travelled to this winery from Santiago. With traffic, it took me about 45 minutes to get there. Once at the winery, I was assigned a guide who was fluent in Spanish and English and ran a joint language tour. Although the guide was friendly and knowledgeable, I wasn't over impressed with the tour, which dragged on a bit by virtue of being in Spanish and English. The composition of the group (primarily Spanish speakers) meant that the guide put more focus on the Spanish speaking group. He spoke in Spanish for minutes at a time, and then provided an abbreviated version of what he had just said to the English speakers. The net result was that the tour felt a bit long in the tooth and left me with the sense that I was only getting a fraction of the experience that Spanish speakers got. Additionally, I had anticipated more discussion of wine and more tasting opportunities, and instead got a tour of the wine making facilities and lots of stats on how much the winery produces each year. We only tasted three wines. Also a little disappointing was the fact that the grapes are harvested in March and the vines were empty. If you're the kind of person who'd like to see the grapes in full bloom, take this into account when planning your trip. The winery was still quite scenic, though. Overall, the tour was good, but not great.

review_text: Preparation: We rented a car in Copiapo for 2 days, it has to be a powerfull 4x4, with atleast 2.5 liter engine. (We bought 2 plastic tanks of 20 liters filled with gas, very important because there are no gas stations in the park area. You are going to sleep in very high altitude, prepare yourself, drink 2 liters of water a day and consider to take pills for prevention of altitude sickness (Acetazolamide). Day 1: Copiapo to Laguna Santa Rosa ( 2 hours drive with lunch stop) the altitude is 3,700m. We payed $5,000 entrance fee in the Conaf (per car). You can sleep in your tent or car, or sleep in the refugio, it is private and costs $10,000 per person, it has 6 beds, kitchen with gas and water, and inside toilet. The woman that works there is very nice and came few times to check that everything is fine. The Laguna is beautiful and has many flamingos . It is freezing after the sun down, take a warm sleeping bag and worm clothes. Day 2 : from Laguna Santa Rosa (2:30 hours drive) to Negro Francisco the altitude is 4,200, we got lost a little bit, there are no signs , just follow the electrical posts, the Laguna is amazing, breathtaking view if the water, mountains behind it and lots of flamingos. keep driving until the free big refugio there. If you keep going 5 more kilometers after the refugio you will see a nice view (the Conaf suggested us) . Then we continued to Laguna Verde (2.5 hr) 4,300 altitude. Don't take the shorter way that GPS suggets you, take the highway. We barely got out the huge holes in the dirt road (without 4x4 you're stuck) we came to the Laguna Verde at 19:00 and it was really windy but the amazing view made you forget about the cold. Then we continued with the road until Termas, the refugio there was overcrowded (max 10) and the water wasn't hot enough to get into the termas considering the strong wind. We headed back to the refugio at Volcano ojos, (small sign on the road) it is a free refugio, on the first level one private small room with 2 matresses , kitchen, (no gas and no water) big spacious room with bunk beds, enough room to put 10 mattresses on the floor, one more private room with one matress, second floor has 4 beds. The toilet is outside without a door and in a bad shape. It looks abondened, has no light, quiet scary to be there at night in the middle of nowhere. During the night we got altitude sicknes, terrible headaches, hard to breathe so we couldn't sleep, also it was freezing cold in there. We waited for the first light to get out of there. My suggestion is to sleep in Laguna Santa Rosa where the altitude is weeker. On the way back to Copiapo we drove to the salar de Maricunga.

review_text: While in Santiago, Chile we wanted to visit a winery and the Santa Rita got the most nods. It was a four hour tour that took us from the grape vines through the whole process of fermentation, storage, bottling and finally tasting. Our guide was a young man named Mattias that explained the whole process with knowledge and information that I had never experienced before. The winery itself is in a beautiful old building that once was the estate of a woman that saved 120 soldiers during the war of independence with Spain. They now have a wine named 120 for these brave soldiers. Information like this just made the whole place come alive and the four hours passed incredibly fast. Too fast. Soon it was time to get back on the bus and back to the city. We did come away with a lot more knowledge of the whole process and appreciation of effort the winery puts into ensuring a wonderful tour.

review_text: This was one of the highlights of my life. I skied Portillo in August in the 1990's After my boyfriend who I was with on and off for 16 years broke up our relationship. At the time, I was heartbroken. But I had the most amazing 7 day vacation. Portillo is 22,838 ft above sea level. World Class Skiing. 100 percent above the tree line. Condors in the sky. It's located 160 km By vehicle from Santiago Chile. Opened in 1949, it hosted Alpine World Ski Championships in August 1966. It marked The emergence of Jean Claude Kelly. I got lucky. I skied beautifully, And the men there were gorgeous. Only the Finest from Chile and Argentina. Everybody there was divorced and many Had attended Columbia University in New York City. I was the only pretty blonde American Woman that was there from New York City. Enough said. I felt beautiful being so popular. The owner of the resort was American and I was always invited for dinner to eat at the Owners private table with him and his wife, who was Chilean. My boyfriend in New York asked me to go back with him the week after I returned to New York. I felt so beautiful from Skiing Portillo I was glowing for weeks. I spent 16 years of my life with my boyfriend in New York. We did not live together. We keep separate apartments but we had lunch with each other every day,and spent evenings together 3 times a week. He was a Magnificent man, but he Didn't want to get married because his parents had had such a terrible marriage And that was quite painful for him. I was told at a the age of 11, that I could not have children. We were a great pair until he got Horribly Sick. He married a nurse that he Had know as a friend for over 30 years. She takes care of him and his finances. He is now in a wheelchair. He was a Tribal Art Dealer, internationally And he had 3 other businesses, so he could never travel with me in August. He Was busy with the accountants. But we did travel together, often on business in London or in Paris. I met him when I was 29 years old and fell madly in love. He took me To 11 Cadogan Gardens for my 30th birthday. You will love Portillo, Chile. There is nothing in the world like it.
title: The Most Exciting Mountains I have Ever Skied

review_text: I went in June a couple days after rainfall in Santiago. There's a small area to park at the bottom of the trail, but nothing official. I can imagine this fills up in the middle of summer. It gets COLD and up there during the winter. Make sure to bundle up well, especially something for your hands and face. i had some thin gloves on and kept my hands in my pockets the whole time, and my hands were still freezing. But, it's well worth it during the winter still. As others have said, the first half an hour going up is a little bit harder than the rest of the trail. There's a beautiful lake half way up to the glacier, which was mostly frozen over. Up towards the glacier there was actual snow! Exciting stuff when you're coming from Santiago, hahah. There's a river following much of the trail. I'll definitely be heading back in the spring/fall!!! At the bottom of the trail there's the little guard-house where you pay the entrance fee and some bathrooms. There's also places to buy snacks, have lunch/dinner, and buy knick-knacks at the bottom, but I didn't really check anything out. The Baños/hotsprings were closed despite the sign saying it was open on those days and those times... but maybe it's closed for the season?

review_text: Valparaiso was already a very important city globally, especially before the operation of the Panama Canal, as it functioned as a commercial warehouse. It currently has one of the highest unemployment rates in Chile. Home to frequent earthquakes and some tsunamis, it still has several buildings (such as one of its churches) damaged and unavailable for visit, even after 14 years of the last major earthquake. It has one of the biggest camelodroms I've ever seen in my life, which works as an informal market. The city is distributed by hills, with huge population density, reminiscent of the Brazilian favelas, but without (so much) garbage on the streets or sewage at open sky. Ja Vina del Mar is a younger, more beautiful and more elegant city. The beach, however, is of more yellow sand, darker, and the water (of the Pacific) is frozen. Complete the landscape many stones on the beach and a more violent sea, which requires a lot of caution. Review of: Valparaiso Port and Vina del Mar Full-Day Tour from Santiago Thank you for your review.
title: City with high unemployment, beach ok

review_text: Beautiful. Weather is inconsistent when we visited in 2nd week of Nov. In the same day we went from short sleeves to high winds, to rain to snow with limited visibility. winds reached gale force 71 km/hr. This held true for the entire 4 days. The trek is strenuous due to long days. from refugio to refugio they are full day hikes. The legs to the various view points are moderately steep not particularly difficult however they are long days. The weather was bad consistently except for the Gray Glacier portion.
title: An interesting trek.

review_text: The museum brought back fond memories of our visit to Easter Island a number of years ago. Other reviewers have stated that this moai is the only one (or one of 3, or one of 6, etc) of the Moai statues removed from Easter Island and currently on display outside the island. It is difficult for me to ascertain for certain from my brief Internet search, but there seems to be at least 8-10 other ones on public display outside the island. But it is stiil a very rare item and definitely worth seeing in person, especailly if you are not able to take the trek to Rapa Nui. It is one of the "smaller-sized" ones, but still worth seeing. The museum is inexpensive to enter (equivalent to a couple of US dollars) and small emough to go through is less than a half hour - or even quicker if you just want to skim through some of the less interesting rooms. If you have your own car, parking around the area may be difficult, but there are the parking "guides" who will help you try to find a place to park on the adjacent street - which is posted as parking only for museum visitors.
title: Small local museum with an "original" moai outside

review_text: Besides having the bad luck of entering the station with way less snow than expected (reason why the only track open was the Ski Lessons/Basic Track), I didn't have a positive experience overall, due to the main reasons below: - Crowd: Absolutely awful. Went up on a monday (29/07), already after the oficial winter holidays in Chile and off from the weekend and even so there was way more people I expected. Lines to get to the belts that take you to the highest point on the only open track as I said before could get up to 15 minutes. Basically you stay 15 minutes in the line, 2 more to reach the "top" and then 30 seconds to go down. All other rides had lines worse than that (Canopy, Tubing, etc.). - Infrastructure (Food and Drinks/Stores/Bathrooms, etc): Ok for the bathrooms (haven't seen if there was toilet paper available), but cleaningness was "OK". Stores. Food options are extremely limited and very expensive. You can definately have a healthier option paying much less if you bring food from home. One thing that bothered me quite a lot was the disorganization to get rental equipment (snowboard/skis, boots and accessories overall). Employees haven't been quite helpful and they behave to rush everyone out of the rental tent, which is very small to the amount of people they receive (specially if the site is in its first hour). Good to bear in mind that they do not provide clothing rental, equipment ONLY. Instructors: Had some basic classes and they went well. The instructors were fine and attentive. If you are focused on skiing/learning to ski, this is not the best option for you.
title: Bad infrastructure/organization

review_text: My visit here was one of the best mornings of my entire life - and I'm 53. We arrived around 9:30 AM and it was literally empty. You descend into a narrow valley, practically a fissure in the earth, surrounded by beautifully rugged red clay walls and mesas. And there awaits a bubbling river nestled into giant ornamental beach grass and tumbling down from level to level, connected by small, therapeutic waterfalls. And the water is deliciously warm - maybe 85 degrees! It's a magical experience floating on your back down the stream, and then letting a natural jacuzzi massage your trek-weary muscles. Be sure to find the falls where you can sit, cross-legged, behind the waterfall. It's magical. NOTE: The best price we could get for this excursion from San Pedro was 40K pesos each, plus 15K entry fee. So we hired a cab, which drove us there, waited two hours, and drove us back for a total of 40K pesos . . . one third the price. No guide is needed! Don't miss it . . . and enjoy!
title: An Oasis in Paradise

Hidden gem, we found "REZ" restaurant means beef in spanish, and had grass fed argentina beef served a diiferent way than us "Foco de Chao" in that they served for 2, 4, 6. We had for 2 in an iron grill with beef, pork, chicken, sausages to die for, and came with over the top salad bar. Best part for me is that draft beer is rare in most places, and they had my favorite Chile beer Christal, and Heineken in draft ice cold in 32 oz glass mug. Over 3 days went went back every night and tried more of the menu. Casino is very nice, non smoking, friendly tables.

review_text: I had a really great day out on this tour lead by Alvaro. It was unexpected as originally I had booked to go to Portillo but that tour wasn’t able to go so the tour company offered me this one instead. I had a really lovely day as the tour was filled with expected and unexpected stops. On our way to cajon del maipo, we stopped at a few photo moments, along with a cafe in the morning to get coffee. At the reservoir there is about a 30 min walk to the main sight. The walk was not hard but the elevation and altitude made the air feel thinner so I was a bit out of breath. Once there the views are breathtaking. On our way back we stopped at a quick bathroom stop where there were some alpacas and farm animals. From above we were able to see condors which was very exciting. We then stopped at a unique chocolate shop, and then a wine and cheese tasting. After this we got delicious empanadas - you get to choose what you want inside which is ideal for a picky eater like me. That really concludes the tour. It’s then back to Santiago. We got back around 4.45pm. Highly worth the day trip. It was beautiful to see all the mountains, and the stops along the way were fun. Thanks Alvaro!! review_text: We did a little excursion on a boat with Orgines Tours, starting in Quellon to explore the nearby islands in a small group. Altogether there were five of us in the tour (two others from the US and US/Ukraine and we bumped into them at dinner). This is the third guided tour we've taken (Prague, Mexico City) and it is essential for travelers who don't know a lot about a city and are visiting for only a short time. review_text: After a lot of research on trip advisor, I picked Cruz Andina for a round trip tour to Salar de Uyuni from San Pedro Atacama. I was very impressed by the tour and have nothing negative to point out. 1. Booking: I booked with them over email. Responses were prompt (albeit in Spanish). All details were clearly provided particularly regarding the requirements and documents needed to procure a visa at the border 2. Confirmation at SPA: I reconfirmed with them the day I arrived in SPA and paid the outstanding balance. They provided clear detailed instructions for the tour and guided me through getting Bolivian currency and necessary photocopies of documents for the visa 3. Pickup and travel to border: Pick-up was promptly at the scheduled time. They took us by shuttle to the Bolivian border. They even reviewed the customs and immigration forms we filled out - question by question. I speak very limited Spanish and they were helpful in talking to the Bolivian immigration officers on my behalf at the border. After clearing immigration, we transferred to 4x4s for the rest of the tour 4. Driver/Guide: Our driver and guide was Jose Luis. A genuinely great chap, he was a calm and patient driver - we always felt safe with him. He arranged for our food and explained all the sights to us. Though he spoke almost no English, he spoke slowly and patiently and I had little trouble understanding what he was saying. 5. Accommodation and Food: I spent a little bit extra to get private rooms instead of shared rooms. While the hotels were fairly basic, I had no complains - I had a private room with clean private baths, hot water showers available and towels etc. provided. Through the trip the food was great - homemade style simple food - soups, pasta, stews etc. Simple but hearty and satisfying 6. Sights: The sights you see are to die for. They are unreal and it feels like you are in the middle of a Planet Earth or Nat Geo documentary All in all, I would recommend Cruz Andina to anyone considering a trip to the Salar.

review_text: My daughter and I decided to visit the park but weren't sure where to start. We walked to the Pio Nono entrance to go up on the funicular. It was about 1 pm. We encountered a 90-minute wait. So instead we took a five-minute taxi ride for $5 up to the Plaza Tupahue. From there, we could walk 30-40 minutes up a steady, slight incline to the Cerro San Cristobal (a giant statue of the Virgin Mary is at the top) or take the teleferico to the top (where the Virgin Mary is). We didn't have time to walk. So I paid $5 per round-trip ticket. We waited 10 minutes in line to ride one stop to the top. It was a scenic ride. The line to board the teleferico to ride down looked long. But they separate the line into two - the line for three or more was about 45 minutes. The line for the two of us was about five minutes. We rode down to the bottom station, Pedro de Valdivia. The park was filled with Chilean families. If we had more time, we would have explored the various nooks and crannies within the park. Alternatively, if you are a jogger, you can start at the entrance near the Pedro de Valdivia teleferico stop and make your way up the slight uphill incline to the Virgin Mary. It takes me about 45 minutes. The park's gates open at 7 am.

review_text: As scientists, veterinarians, wildlife enthusiasts and passionate photographers of nature, me and my wife went to Patagonia to explore its wildlife. We were very worried if we would see those amazing animals like in a NatGeo documentary. We spent three days in self-guided trails, but just spotter some guanacos... Then, we decided to spend 2 (amazing) days with Miguel Fuentealba (ISO100 owner and field guide) with our guide. Approximately 40 minutes after he picked up us at the very first day, he suddenly stopped the car and said "Look, a cougar will jump from that rock!!!" Unbelievably, suddenly a cougar jump from behind the rock and also cross the road in front of our car!!! At the same day he tracked some footprints and was able to find two young brother cougars... Amazing!!! He do all the cougar track with a huge respect for the animals and for their habitat... We have seen some guides in Paine with have no real respect for the wildlife. Miguel is a real example of guide with a great sense of respect and love to nature. Besides that, he is a lovely person, has a great knowledge of the region and all its major attractions. Also, he has another major skill, he is wildlife photographer!!! So, we got several advices for the best shots and videos of the local animals!!! Two amazing days in the company of this awsome guide and human being. We have seen 8 different pumas (cougars) in Torres del Paine in the company of Miguel Fuentealba. We do not have words to thank him!!! For sure, we want to come back to Patagonia and Torres del Paine, and of course, enjoy the company of Miguel (ISO100). We have met guides all over the world, and we can assure that Miguel is an outstanding one! Thanks, "Chê"... We hopw to see you again soon... Hola José, Como equipo agradecemos cada palabra y por supuesto la confianza depositada en nosotros. Fueron días interesantes, logramos el objetivo principal sin pasar a llevar la fragilidad de este hermoso y saludable ecosistema, es la idea de todas nuestras salidas, y estamos felices de seguir recibiendo viajeros como ustedes, con la paciencia y sus intereses muy claros. Esperamos que aún tengan los recuerdos muy frescos y bien atesorados. Hoy estamos en pausa, pero seguimos positivos y a la espera de poder regresar a terreno. Saludos a Fernanda, que estén muy bien. HASTA PRONTO!!
title: A lifetime puma (cougar) experience!!!

review_text: I am giving this a mixed review for a few reasons. First I want to say that the guides were absolutely wonderful. None of my issues have to do with them, as they were really accommodating, informative, friendly and flexible when we hit the bad weather. So context: my partner and I were in Puerto Varas only because we had come over the Cruce Andino from Argentina. We had a day to kill, and when I did several google searches for what to do in Puerto Varas - this is what came up (and that was reinforced when this was the main thing being sold at the tourist desk in our hotel). However, the day we did this it was pouring rain. That was not a problem when seeing the waterfalls - absolutely beautiful. But it was so foggy that when we got to the top of the volcano, you could see nothing. The tour even just stopped there, we took a funny pic with the whiteout, then got back in the van. So my take on this tour? If it is bad weather then don't do it - not worth it. But I'd also add: I didn't look into the cost of renting a car and doing this ourselves. That may have been a better idea, as it turns out there are other walks in the national park we could have done if we had the time/opportunity. So mixed review: good tour guides, worthwhile if there is nice weather, but if you have the opportunity to rent a car and do it yourself, that's probably a better option. Review of: Osorno Volcano and Petrohué Waterfalls

review_text: This is a must see when visiting Santiago. The art is startling in its richness and complexity. The Museum presents it well. There are good English descriptions giving great context. The complexity and color in this very old cloth is astounding. The special presentation on funeral wraps from Peru was also excellent. The curation at this museum is first-class. The physical environment enhanced the collection.
title: Excellent pre-Colombian art, very well presented. Special exhibit on weaving was phenomenal

review_text: We did a fair bit of research before choosing Chilean Wine Lovers as our guides for 3 full days in the Santiago area. Corresponding via email several months prior to our trip, Mauricio took the time to understand the type of experiences and sights we wanted do & see. From this he crafted 2 custom itineraries for each of the 3 days, that included wineries, sightseeing, gain some understanding of the culture, and architecture. He is also super flexible with the itineraries, when a road wash-out occurred that prevented us from going into the mountains, he easily created a day for us in Maipo Valley that was outstanding. For wineries he selected different types of experiences, One a small boutique winery just outside Santiago, where in true boutique fashion, all labels are made on site and applied by hand, The second was organic winery The House of Morande, a full vineyard tour, followed by private session on the learning the essentials and of wine tasting, This was followed by the best (and I mean the best) ever custom tasting menu paired with spectacular wines in the most incredible setting... If you only have time for one Winery this would be it... Finally we toured Underraga Winery, which was the largest of all the wineries and here we also toured the vineyards, the fermentation area and another wonderful .wine tasting... Underraga gives you the glass to take home...Each of the wineries were all beautiful settings, which added to the experience. We also had an impromptu picnic one day, several bottles of wine, traditional meat pies, the top of a mountain, overlooking Casablanca Valley - magical. We spent a few hours in Valparaiso and Vina Del Mar... and after seeing Valparaiso a Unesco world heritage, sight, I am both very glad that we had the opportunity and that we had a private guide...get so much more understanding of the people and the area with a guide...(plus where to go and where not to go...important in Valparaiso) We spent time in a small town that specializes in making pottery and had a wonderful traditional local meal there also.....also accompanied by outstanding wines, that Maurico brought with them. We also wanted to see Santiago, yes the traditional great places to see such as the Mercardo, but also the architecture, both old and new, as well as learning a little more about how the people of Santiago live... Mauricio accommodated all of this for us, including getting to see the "burbs" Mauricio, readily shares his tremendous knowledge and insight of the area, in such an personable way, and he loves what he does.. Before this trip we had never used the services of a private guide. I am now totally convinced this is the way to go, when you have a short time in an area, want some unique/memorable experiences, an understanding of the culture and people and do not speak the language. When I return, I would absolutely call Mauricio, it would be visiting an old friend.

review_text: We really enjoyed our 3D/2N tour from San Pedro to Uyuni. Booking was easy and clear as Raül in the office spoke very good English to us. We were explained the route carefully and given an itinerary. If you pay in USD make sure they’re in good condition or mint, as they won’t accept any worn notes. We were picked up promptly when Cruz said, and the van was a spacious new van with 12 people in total. As the border near San Pedro was closed due to snow, we had to take a detour 3 hours north to the Ollagüe border. The border crossing at Chile was slow due to several tour groups, but easy. The driver remained with us for this and made sure we all got stamped ok. Passing through Bolivian border was super fast, our passports stamped in no time, and we were transferred to the 4x4’s and set off. It’s worth agreeing with your fellow passengers to rotate in the 4x4s as the back seats are a little cramped. The food provided was good quality, and we were catered for well being vegetarians. Breakfast was usually bread, cheese, spreads, cake, biscuits, tea, coffee. Lunches were pasta, rice, vegetables, potato bakes, salads, etc. Dinner the second night was excellent and we got some Bolivian wine too. Maybe take some snacks with you and plenty of water in case you get peckish along the way as there aren’t any stops for supplies. The sights we saw were incredible, some of the best in 9 months of backpacking. We saw mountains, valleys, flamingos, llamas, lagoons, canyons, which was all in addition to the salt plains on the last day. Our driver Andreas was very careful, professional and told us little snippets about places along the way. He spoke basic English but we had a Spanish speaking passenger translating for us in the car. He was always asking us to play music, and stopping regularly for photos. He was super chilled, wanted us to see a range of things and a genuinely nice guy. The accommodation on the first night was basic but fine. We asked for sleeping bags when booking which helped massively as it was absolutely freezing. Plenty of blankets on the bed as well. The bathrooms weren’t the cleanest, and some showers were not warm but we got on with it, knowing the second night would be better. The Salt hotel on night 2 was super cute, well insulated en suite rooms with hot water (one person showering at a time!) There were only a couple of small matters which were a little disappointing. Firstly communication wasn’t the best as once we paid for the tour, that was when we were told the border near San Pedro had been closed due to the snow so there may be an alternative route. It would have been better to inform us of the potential new route in advance of paying. We wouldn’t have changed our minds as any other tour group would be in the same situation, but as it remained closed, we went the alternative route which meant we missed out the red lake and the geysers (the geysers were actually closed due to the weather). Apparently the red lake was frozen over too so consider this if you’re going in winter. Secondly, dinner the first night was extremely disappointing as we were served pasta with a very small dish of sauce to share, and the non-vegetarians got a very small piece of meat too. We were all starving as we had lunch early, and dinner was served after 8pm. As all the other meals were substantial, I can only hope this was a one off. Some of the stops listed on the itinerary we didn’t not go to, but there were some stops we visited which weren’t on the itinerary. This was not much of an issue as everything we saw was absolutely incredible. If you’re specific about what you want to see then maybe speak to the driver to make sure you don’t miss out. Overall this tour was excellent, we loved it. We would definitely recommend Cruz Andina and Andreas our driver. We just would have liked clarification on the border situation before booking.

review_text: My wife and I stayed at Chepu Adventures during the third week in December. Southern Chile is in the middle of one of the rainiest 10 day periods in recent history. All of the locals were shaking their heads at the unusual weather. At any other resort this type of weather could have cast a real dark spell on the scene. Not at Chepu Adventures. The owners Amory and Fernando were wonderful with making sure that ALL of their guests needs were attended to.We managed to get a couple of kayak trips up the river in during our stay, but a lot of our time was spent socializing with other " Eco" guests at the lodge. The rooms are very comfortable and clean and the dinners that Amory prepared were very good. The owners take care to make all of their guests feel at home and understand the history and the reality of living in a remote and fragile environment. Even with the wet weather we had a great time ; I can only imagine how great it would have been in warm weather.
title: Amazing in any weather

What more, it's organized according to type of store, so all the bookstores are near each other. There are also nice clean bathrooms and proximity to the metro (Tobalaba). The only thing that's missing is cheap food; all of the restaurants are pretty pricey. If you want a cheap churrasco, go down Providencia to Av Suecia or Lyon. review_text: Where to start? Juane arranged two adventure-filled and wine-packed days for us while we were in town. To begin, an amazing and informative driver picked us up from the airport and transported us to our accommodation. He toured us around town a bit, pointing out the major attractions as we passed them by. The next morning Juane arrived to take us on our day hike in the hills of the Andes. It was so much fun, the scenery was amazing and Juane knew the route like the back of his hand. We crossed the rapids, drank from a stream, and had an incredible spread at the end of the hike that included avocado, tomato, meats and cheese, and the most amazing bread (and a bit of wine, because we were obviously dehydrated,ha!) The next day Juane picked us up once more and this time took us to the Casablanca wine region where he'd set up two amazing bodega tours as well as brunch. The tours were informative and the tastings were incredible. Great scenery and even better company. Juane also arranged our transport from Vina del Mar to the airport. Honestly, we had the most fun and I'm so glad I stumbled upon this tour group. I can't imagine having anyone else plan and accompany us on our trip. When we make it back to Chile, I'm certain I'll use their services again and I recommend them highly, completely to take care of any tour needs you'd have while in the area. Simply, the best! Hi Holly, Thank you for booking with us! We are so happy to hear you and your friends had such a good time! Juane also had a blast with you girls! See you on your next trip to Chile!

review_text: We arrived in Santiago on Tuesday, almost midnight. We had the entire itinerary planned and Wednesday was free, however, the agency sent a message that the tour on Thursday (Portillo) would be closed and moved us to Wednesday, we approved the change because they have greater knowledge of things. Okay, tired and almost sleepless because at 5 something in the morning the van came to pick us up, we went, it had already been reported that the road would be closed on Wednesday/Thursday and even so the agency sent the entire van there to waste time, we arrived in Santiago again, almost 13 hours and as if that wasn't enough, the driver who had a non-defensive driving style committed traffic violations, being stopped by the police and making us lose another 1 hour! He even told us to walk back to the apartment! Yes…you hire a well-rated agency because you want security/peace of mind and need to go through such embarrassment. The next day, we went for the “Andes Panoramic” tour, but halfway through we discovered that it was the “Sky Day” tour, we had no intention of going sky, I sent a message to the saleswoman who responded hours later informing me that the tour Panoramic, it wouldn't happen that day, however, I was already in the new van on the way to this same tour and it would happen! (I really didn't understand her stance). Thank you, guide Vitor, for responding promptly and solving the problem for us! I just didn't give it one star because my evaluation is based on reliable experience and the guides Vitor, Sol and Alexandro and also the driver Emerson provided me with a great service! Thanks! As for the 2 incidents, the agency showed no intention of compensating me, apologizing, etc. Obviously when you travel the last thing you want is for a situation like the one described above to occur in order to obtain advantages or discounts, but they acted as if this was normal, so I was very scared! And there is no money that can pay for 1 lost day of a trip planned for a long time, anyone who plans knows…. Imagine being a person with an anxiety attack, being in another country and being in a van with 5 police officers interrogating the driver and you there without knowing anything or anyone on your first day! Total horror! EVERYTHING could have been avoided if the agency hadn't sent the van on the day the tour was closed! But in the end it must have been a relief not to have climbed 29 mountain bends with a reckless driver!
title: Experience

review_text: When we decided to visit the Chilean Patagonia we carried out a detailed search for guides to make our trip a safe and unforgettable one. In that search we identified Gerardo from Amigos de Patagonia. Gerardo not only organized our visit to Patagonia but he also became a friend of those that life presents to you along the way. Knowledgeable of history, detail oriented and personable. We couldn't have made a better choice. If you ever visit Chilean Patagonia, he is the one. And Torres del Paine is simply a magical place. Review of: Private Torres del Paine & Milodon, departing from Punta Arenas
title: A simply unforgettable experience

review_text: Our guide Thomas was our guide on a day trip to Cajon del Maipo. We were picked up at our downtown hotel promptly as promised. There were a total of 4 passengers on our tour. We stopped for hot chocolate and blueberry cake on the drive up. The river, reservoir, and snowcapped mountains were beautiful, and a lunch of snacks and wine was provided at a scenic spot by the reservoir. We had plenty of time to walk around a bit and take photos. On the return to Santiago, we stopped for empanadas and a beer. You won't return to Santiago hungry! The weather on our tour was cool but otherwise perfect. The guide was knowledgeable and shared information on the natural history of the river and reservoir. Our only recommendation would be for the tour company to clean the van windows more thoroughly in the morning.
title: Great day out of Santiago

review_text: I took 4 tours with Bora to Chile and they were all wonderful! Super prepared team, comfortable vans and everything very well organized. The places are beautiful and the guides tell you a little about the history of Chile, which makes the tour even better. In addition to the tours, they gave me great tips on what to do in Santiago and places to eat. I recommend it with my eyes closed! A special thank you to the guides Nana, Débora and Gabriel with whom I had the pleasure of taking the tours. Thank you also to the drivers Jorge and the birds who were very careful on the roads.
title: Best agency in Santiago, you can go there without fear!

review_text: I went to Valle Nevado, the experience was perfect! The guide was super attentive! Staff very professional and removed all doubts before the tour.
title: Best Day of Ski

review_text: Thanks Jonathan and Gregorio are a great duo, fun, helped us with the photos, Jonathan was always attentive asking if we were okay!!! Rich cocktel at the end, it was a nice experience.

review_text: We booked this tour as it was rated no.1 on Trip Advisor, and probably is, as we have no other comparison, and it was fun and interesting. Jorge is super enthusiastic and it's just unbelievable to see all the stars and milky way, and he explains everything with a lot of passion - the location is priceless. However, it was pricey and to be honest, I think we'd have enjoyed it more, if it had been half as long (we were there for three hours) and half the cost. Also, having more basic instructions on how to spot the constellations etc would have been nice, rather than the more advanced info and history lesson that was given. There was lots of gazing (naturally) through telescopes, but unless you really know your stuff, it is a little too much for someone who just likes looking up and wants to know roughly which star you're looking at. We found the 3 hours a long time - especially when you're tired from having done other activities in the day - I guess Jorge is just so passionate, that it was hard to gauge the tiredness of the group, and as a few there were really into it, it went on for a bit too long. However, that said, we did enjoy it and appreciated his passion, and the photos and his help in getting the settings right, and the hot chocolate is as lovely as everyone says! Dear Sona, Thank you very much for your review. Perhaps the tour you needed take it was TAT because SAT 1 is for advanced watcher and if you wanted to watch more time the night sky without a long astronomy class TAT is shorter and more time to observe the classic objets and price looks high compare with other similar companies but everyone that take the tour pay the knowledges that I know and give them. Anyway we felt very happy that you took the tour with us. Best Regards Jorge Corante F.
title: Great, but you have to be a real enthusiast to really get the most out of it.

review_text: The Chilean poet laureate Pablo Neruda was an eccentric and extraordinary man. This home reflects his personality. He was a collector of people and things, and guests visiting the home will get a glimpse into the whimsical mind of one of the world's most beloved and most translated poets. Don't forget to visit the artisans who set up tables outside the home and in the surrounding areas. You'll be sure to find unique hand-made jewelry and souvenirs. If you get lucky, you may even get a music lesson from a little old man selling ocarinas. The artisans are usually around on the weekends. We went in the middle of March and there were no crowds on a Friday afternoon.
title: Beautiful home overlooking the Pacific Ocean

review_text: Santiago is not prepared for bicycles on public streets. They are more dangerous then motorcycles for the lack of visability of car drivers. One crept up on me when waiting for a stop light. I put on my blinker to turn left, did not check my right rearview mirror, being unaccustomed to bikes in the area and to my horror ran into him! Neither car drivers nor roads in Santiago are prepared for this invasion of bikes. It is more dangerous than motorcycles. The city is beginning to make stretches of bike paths but it has a century to go to get up to Holland's standards. Biking in parks is another story. The Bicentennial Park, over 53 hectares, has a bike rental stand at the beginning of the south end. It has lovely bike paths weaving through the park in safety and with plenty of room for bikers to enjoy. Paul McCarthy rents a bike there when he comes to Santiago to not only for the exercise but also to enjoy the view, a lovely contrast with the Andes to the north and a cosmopolitan city to the south with its sky scrapers. The park also has paths for joggers. The park is a stone throw away from the Airbnb B&B rental called "Magical Views". The park as a children's area with jungle gyms etc apart so that children don't bother those using the park for other reasons. It is a visit for all types, couples, families with little children, growing children, friends, perhaps for business reasons? but as per the other options its a great place for those who want to be alone. One can spend an hour or a day. Its a great place not only for working out, picnics are discretely held around the thousands of Chilean trees dispersed throughout the park.
