review_text: We spent 3 days rafting this wild river in this unbelievably beautiful location. At the very start of the season, Bochinche was the only operator that offered us a multi-day rafting adventure, covering pretty much every main rapid the Futaleufu has to offer: Terminator section, Puente a Puente section, El Macal section. Our local guide, Daniel, knew the river like the back of his hand and has 10+ years of experience guiding trips all over the world. The river is powerful and the high class rapids are technical, he takes the time to explain each section before we start and really draws you in the adventure. We had some rainy days and the water levels were high, but the team did everything to adapt our trip to the conditions in a safe way, i.e. reshuffling some of the sections, changing the start time, bringing along extra safety kayaks, etc. I'm confident no other operator would have given us the same experience. As for safety, every trip had at least one safety kayak and cataraft accompanying our raft. At the end of the third day, Daniel and Giorgia invited us to their home for a great asado with the other guides. After a couple of days on the river, we definitely felt connected, and truly welcomed. An unforgettable experience, thanks a lot! Hi Maarten and thanks a lot for your comment. It was great meeting and getting to know you guys and a pleasure showing you the amazing Futaleufu river. We hope to see you soon for another extraordinary adventure!!!
title: Amazing multi-day rafting adventure

This is the winery that put Chilean wines on the map by doing blind taste tests with very established wines - and winning. State of the art facilities for making Icon wines. review_text: I recently returned back from my South American Adventure which included my trip to Chile, Argentina, Uruguay and Brazil. Prior to my departure from the US for the start of my trip I did some research on certain things and places I wanted to see. I have been overseas before and had done bike tours in other countries and felt that this was a great way to orient myself to the city as well a see some sites from the perspective of a local so I tried to find something similar in Santiago, Chile and came across, Paseos en Bicicleta. Now this wasn't any ordinary bike tour, it was led by a really nice man named, Andres Garrido, who is well versed in the sights, popular as well as local, the architecture of the city (after all, he is an architect himself) and other advice regarding Santiago. For me the bike tour was particularly unique because it was one on one, this isn't always the case but he does keep the size of the tours small. I learned about the history of Santiago as well as I was able to see the sights associated with this city's history. We even made a few stops while we were riding to go into a few historical buildings and parks. We did a lot of bike riding which I welcomed since I feel it is the best way to see a big city. Most was on flat ground but this particular tour I chose allows you time to bike up Cerro San Cristobal to see the sunset over the city...which I may add is spectactular. This was a little tiring but well worth it. To top things off, the tour included a wine and cheese dinner after the sunset which was a great way to end the evening. I thoroughly enjoyed my day with Andres and also was glad to be able to meet his wife and friends after the tour at our dinner location that overlooked the sparkling city lights of Santiago. I felt like I was in the company of long time friends instead of on a tour. After dinner we were able to ride our bikes down the hill which was also breathtaking and a great experience. I felt this was a great way to start my South American journey and would recommend this tour to everyone. Now, Andres, only does these tours on Friday, Saturday, Sunday because he works during the week but it tells you something when someone is willing to give up their weekend and free time to show you around THEIR city. He has day and sunset tours. I took the sunset/wine and cheese dinner tour. He would be able to answer any specific questions you have and is very prompt with responding to emails. He is a great person to get to know in Santiago and feel I have made a new friend from my experience. Thanks Andres... I really enjoyed my time and Santiago! Feel free to email me through tripadvisor or Andres at Paseos en Bicicletat at paseosenbicicleta@gmail.com As the owner of Paseos en Bicicleta, I would like to thank all our 2008 customers for the warm and sincere opinions they have written in this forum and for the comments they have privately sent us. Paseos en Bicicleta is a small company created 2 years ago with the only objective of sharing an experience. And this is the joy we experiment when we discover and share with our passengers the treasures and gems of this amazing city. We are a luxury bike tours company because we believe in taking care of the small details, because we believe in simplicity and because we believe that making our best effort will never be enough: there will always be a way to make things better. We are commited to keep our project as a rare gem, as a unique and unforgettable experience: we want to keep biking off the beaten tracks exclusively. To all who have experienced Santiago with us this year, we send our best wishes! Andrés Garrido General Manager Paseos en Bicicleta

Afterward we went to Valparaiso. We only spent about a half an hour there walking down a path through the colourfully painted houses. I feel that we missed much of what this UNESCO site had to offer. We were very disappointed in our guide, an older gentleman, who appeared to only want to do the minimum necessary and spent a lot of time telling bad jokes that centered on women’s incompetence. review_text: The museum displays the rise and fall of the military regime led by Pinochet. The exposition zooms in on different topics and also various personal cases. Like cases of a the disappearance of a specific group of people, the effect of this time the children, a close look to how the newspapers had a role to play, etc. I think that all these points of view create a good image on that time. A must see! Entrance is free, audio guide is 2000 pesos.
title: Impressing museum about a time no Chilean wants to be remembered of.

review_text: I arrived in Pucon around 8:15 after an overnight bus from Santiago and checked into my hostel. Since it was too late to do the Volcano trek (6:30) and I had missed the earlier bus to Huerquehue National Park, this was an ideal alternative as there are very regular buses to and from the Santuario and I didn't want to waste a day hanging around the hostel and town (not that either were bad). I took a bus around 10:15, which arrived about half an hour later (its the bus station opposite the JAC terminal around the corner from Pullman). I just mentioned El Cani and jumped on the right bus, the driver should shout when you get to the spot. A brief walk and you need to pop into the hut they have and pay entrance (3,000 pesos I think / 6 dollars) and you get a basic map that one of the guys write on (there is a check point further up where you may or may not have to show this (I didn't...un-manned). In all honesty, the first part of the hike up to the refugio is very dull and not particularly fun (dirt tracks). The map indicates about 2 hours to get there albeit I did it in almost half the time as I was on a bit of a mission that day and ran a little. After the refugio the hike got a reasonable amount easier as you start heading to the lakes. The lakes were a big disappointment for me being perfectly honest. The first was almost completely dried up and the second was quite small and also part dried. From the second lake however, you start a tough 30 minute ascent to the mirador (viewing point), and believe me, that was worth it. The views from the top are pretty spectacular, with three volcanoes in the distance (including Villarica of course). Its pretty clear up there and there are plenty of rocks to perch yourself and rest your tired feet whilst munching a few snacks. I actually got to the top in two and half hours so it can be done a lot quicker than indicated. Whilst parts of the above sound quite negative, the view really is fantastic and I imagine the rest of the park would be much better out of peak summer time when the lakes have more water, or when the trees are covered in snow. The other additional bonus is that most people go to Huerquehue and so you practically have it to yourself (I was the first person in the park even at 10:45). Well worth a visit, especially for the more budget conscious seeking a panoramic view.
title: Challenging hike with a beautiful reward despite poor lakes in summer...

review_text: The geysers were phenomenal! This is definitely a must see place in San Pedro (probably my number one recommendation here) because there's nothing like it! It was really cool to see and I enjoyed getting in the hot springs after (though they weren't as warm as I was expecting except in some areas). The hot springs def warmed me up and didn't feel as cold after. The only hard part is getting out of the springs to change back into normal clothes in the cold weather. But, the geysers were completely worth it!! Desert Adventures has a great tour there, so I highly recommend using them for the tour! The guide was really knowledgeable and fantastic!
title: Definitely worth the early start and cold!

review_text: Beautiful park with great views of the city and the Andes mountains. You can hike, bike, or take the Teleferico or Funicular to the top. Only reason I didn't give it 5 stars is because the wait to buy the funicular tickets is too long, they need to organize it better.

review_text: Beautiful Lagunas, both Miscanti and Miniques. They are quite a long drive from SP de Atacama, but are easily accessible on your own vehicle. You have to pay an entrance fee, but not too expensive. I strongly suggest that if you drive up to here, continue on Chile 23 to visit salar de Talar, Piedras Rojas, and Laguna Tuyajto. They are all wonderful and with no entrance fee.
title: Beautiful Lagunas! Combine with other sites in the area

review_text: We visited Antilco back in February, but it was such an amazing experience I needed time to ensure the review did Mathias and Karin justice. My husband and I spent a week staying in their beautiful wooden cabin, with 4 days of riding (2 half days and a 2 day trek) alongside 5 mornings of studying Spanish with Karin. We couldn’t have had a better introduction to Chile. It was such a perfect combination as Mathias organised the horse riding on his ranch whilst his wife runs a language school in Pucón. We barely knew any Spanish before leaving England and after a week of studying at Antilco we left with a good foundation of Spanish for the rest of our month exploring Patagonia. We hired a car for 10 days and had great fun picking up hitch hikers to ensure we kept practising! The horse riding was absolutely incredible and the ultimate highlight was the 2 day trek into the mountains. It was such a dream come true to go camping under the most amazing stars, travelling by horse. The food provided on the camping trip was delicious and we will never forget cooking the steaks over the fire under the stars. We would highly recommend Antilco and Lingua Plus for horse riding and/or learnings spanish. We really hope to return in the future for a 4 day horse trek as this really was our highlight from a month exploring Chile. A huge thanks to Mathias, Karin, our 2 guides and of course the horses who looked after us over the 4 days of riding Polka, Moro, Sombra and Bonita.
title: A week of riding and learning Spanish

review_text: I enjoyed a really nice small-group tour with Central Tours to the Elqui Valley, the highlights being the Puclaro Dam & reservoir, the Gabriela Mistral museum in Vicuna, a pisco distillery, and a nice lunch in Pisco Elqui. There were other short stops for scenic lookouts and small towns, and we did some walking but nothing too strenuous. Some were just quick stops that allowed us to get out and stretch our legs and snap a few photos, without hanging around too long. I felt it was very well paced overall. Our guide was Sebastian, who was very knowledgeable about the area. It is certainly a scenic ride, but he really made it come alive with information about the local history, natural resources, and social aspects. The rest of the group was Spanish-speaking, but Sebastian is completely bi-lingual, and immediately offered to give the tour in both languages. I told him it wouldn’t be necessary, and I was able to follow most of his commentary, but nevertheless he kept checking in with me in English throughout the day to be sure I understood. And if he would point out something quickly as we drove by it, he made sure to get my attention, as well. That is a real sign of a quality guide, in my opinion. One note – their web site is only in Spanish (maybe they’ll have English translations soon?), and my first call to them wasn’t a very good cell connection. But they got back in touch with me quickly on WhatsApp in English (which I prefer when making arrangements), and were able to accommodate me on short notice. I would recommend Central Tours without hesitation.
title: Excellent tour with friendly, informative guide

review_text: I loved the city, we walked through the Costanera and went to the multiple handicraft markets. There are also a lot of restaurant to eat. The teatro del Lago is also a stunning place to visit.
title: nice walk

review_text: All the rave reviews of this tour are all true, and Daniel is a gem of a guide!! Daniel is not your typical guide. He genuinely loves art and culture and he is passionate in what he does and we believe he wants the best for his clients (sounds weird since I don't think he views us as his clients -- we are more like his friends!!). His tour truly stands out from other Valparaiso tours. I compared most of the Valparaiso tours on TripAdvisor, and his is the only one that allows flexibility and focuses on the art and culture aspects of what Valparaiso offers. Our tour took place on NYD (today)!!! This is what Daniel described as a "hard holiday" meaning things are closed and his employees are not available (he worked as our driver and our guide) so the question is should he still offer the tour while running the risk of disappointing his "clients?" We were very lucky because he did!! And he was very transparent and honest with us about the limitations of touring on NYD and what he could or could not do!! We did not do the wine tasting part of the tour since the vineyard was closed (which was just fine). Instead we did an in-depth tour of Valparaiso, and it was truly memorable. Daniel is clearly so well loved by many in the neighborhood. We had our luggage with us (Daniel's team is the only one that offers airport pickup and drop off, too!!!!) he was so responsible that he went out of his way to store our luggage with a street vendor (can you believe that???). He also knows local artists!! We ran into the great and amazing Varas Mackenzie (!!!) who is Daniel's friend and Varas invited us to visit his studio on NYD when his studio was closed!! WOW!! Daniel himself is truly interesting and knowledgeable. He has a grad degree in philosophy and he's an excellent photographer and he has the best taste in music (he played cool local musicians and singers' music and MV during the drives)!! All of his knowledge and interests in art make him the perfect guide you would want for an art and culture tour like this one. He also took excellent (!!!) photos of us without us asking!! We feel like we were accompanied by the best possible personal photographer and guide!! Hands down the best guide and tour, and absolutely the perfect way to start off the new year with!! Review of: Street Art in Valparaiso and Wines in Casablanca from Santiago

review_text: We originally booked the Maipo tour but was emailed 1 day prior to advise that the route had been closed to tourists due to an accident. They then offered us the Portillo tour instead, claiming that it was twice the cost and we would still see lots of mountains. The first stop was to the snow clothing hire shop. We were convinced it was going to be a lot colder and the tour guide recommended that we dress accordingly. Our hire came to a total of $86aud for pants, gloves and snow boots for 2 people. Only to find out when we arrived to the mountain that they were not necessary. We then were taken to a snow area on the side of the highway to play in the snow. We were told that the ski resort would be too crowded and this would be a good time to get photos etc. As most of the bus was from Brazil, our tour guide spoke mostly in Portuguese, translating to English every now and then. However when we arrived to the ski resort at midday, our understanding was that we were to spend and hour and a half at the resort and have lunch at the restaurant. The guide took a list of names who were wanting to go to the restaurant as we were told that the hotel only wanted paying customers at the resort. The food was terrible and overpriced. We paid $70aud for 2 meals and the meat was so over cooked, it could be cut or chewed. This was quite disappointing considering how much we paid and even though we bought lunch, we were not allowed to use the bathrooms. We were told that these were for hotel guests only. The resort is a bit of let down also, there’s not much to do, other than take photos in one designated area for tourists. When we arrived back to the bus, we were told that we would drive for another hour and half to take back the snow gear and then have lunch! We approached the driver and told him we thought he asked us to have lunch here. There was another English speaking person on the bus and she too had lunch at the resort from the guides instructions. Clearly something was lost in translation. The food at the lunch spot was half the price too and looked much more appetising. We were very disappointed. Overall I would not recommend this tour to anyone. It was boring and we ended up paying more on the day then we did the tour cost. review_text: My wife Judy and I met FredaTopolosky in Holland America's Zaandam laundry, we were very lucky. Why? Because Freda had trolled the Internet and found out about the Nao Victoria Museum and with her husband Bruce, invited Judy and I to join them on a visit. We disembarked from the Zaandam at Punta Arenas, using tenders, and then went through Chilean immigration and customs. The four of us then muscled into an impossibly small taxi for the four mile journey to the musem, easily located on the right hand side of the main road in the eastern part of the city. What did we find? First of all we met a delightful father and son who, between themselves, had built a beautifulful full size replica of Magellan's Nao Victoria, one of five ships that left Spain in September 1519 to sail around the world. We were able to climb into Nao Victoria and marvel at the skill of Magellan's navigation and seamanship, and the toughness of the crew. Of the 42 crewmembers that set sail from Sanlucar (near today's Gibraltar),19 survived to return to Spain almost exactly three years later. Under construction is a replica of the famous British ship, HMS Beagle which, on its second voyage around the world, took scientist Charles Darwin to the Falkland Islands, Punta Arenas and then onwards through the Magellan Strait and up along the Chilean coast to the Galapogos. This replica construction will be completed by the end of 2015. Also worth viewing is a replica of the sloop that enabled explorer Ernest Shackleton and some of his crew to escape Antartica in appalling weather. Sadly, none of the Punta Arenas promotional material mentions this museum, it is well worth a visit, children and adults will be fascinated to climb into a 500 year old ship and to view things like the amazing steering system which was also used on the Mayflower.
title: Come and look at a replica of Magellan's Nao Victoria in Puerto Arenas

review_text: Neruda is both poet and social conscious of Chile. His architectural tastes and aesthetic are interesting, but not all of his houses are created equal. He has three you can tour: downtown Santiago, in the Bellavista neighborhood; Valparaiso; and Isla Negra, south of Valparaiso and accessible by cab or bus. The house at Valparaiso is the least interesting of the three. The Neruda house in Santiago is an excellent introduction as is the house just south of Valparaiso, at Isla Negra. The Santiago house has the most interesting furnishings and architectural styling (Neruda was fascinated by the sea, and the rooms in Santiago are very reflective of that). The furnishings and artifacts at the Valparaiso house are less interesting and less typical of his style. The Valparaiso house is currently under renovation, so the third floor is closed. At the very least, until the entire Valparaiso house is open, I'd give it a pass, unless you are a serious Neruda fan.It's a bit out of the way, and ti's not particularly cheap, and likely to disappoint. Visit the houses as Isla Negra or Santiago instead.

review_text: I had this dream of going to Torres del Paine for over 25 years. I've always thought this place was sort of a mythical place, one of those natural wonders you find only in movies. To my surprise everything that I've seen there was real, and beautiful, and perfect. Raw nature, unique landscape, a great deal of mixed scenarios all around - a beautiful glacier, huge towering rocky behemoths, snow-capped mountains, dangerous cliffs, green valleys, emerald lakes, multicoloured granite monoliths and assorted wild animals all around, from foxes to condors. The place is filled with civilized outposts and trekkers, so you won't find it hard to cross with people either to get directions or any kind of support or stimulation. In general all people I've met were generous, life-lovers and well-intentioned fellows. I felt like I was meeting elves! ;) Regardless, I believe this is one of those incredible places we believe that doesn't exist in real life. Amazing trip, in a place that made me feel like Yosemite was falling behind in both regards of natural beauty and turistic infrastructure. Unbelievable.

review_text: Let me start with a heart full Thanks to Juan! Perron Tour went beyond what anyone could imagine! Juan showed us the beauty of his city and why he loves it! The tour encompassed the history not just of Valparaiso but of Chile. I learned who the ancestors of people from Valparaiso originated from centuries ago that shape this city we walked through today. The art was incredible! And I should know because living in Europe for a number of years, I have been to so many art exhibitions, museums etc I have lost count! The architecture of this city may not be impressive to some people but combine it with the history and other factors you can understand and appreciate the city in a completely different way. If you want a unique experience while visiting Valparaiso contact Juan and book his tour! I am not someone to recommend something as I have very high standards but I have to give Juan my highest recommendation! Thank you so much for sharing your experience with Perro Tour with other travelers on TripAdvisor, Sarah! review_text: The experience with Araya was good. Good service and organization of the team. The meals on the tours are excellent. Special greetings to guides: Cristian, Selena, Kevin, Favio, Isaky, Adalid (the latter is the guide of the Bolivian partner company that makes the Uyuni crossing). They are all very well prepared and attentive, it is noticeable that they like what they do and are concerned that people’s experience is good. In addition, excellent photographers, worrying about this issue as well. Congratulations also to the drivers of the tours that we did with them (I do not remember the names of all). Despite the positive items described above, TWO IMPORTANT QUESTIONS HAVE MAKED US NOT GIVE A MAXIMUM POINT TO ARAYA. I will quote below. The Kristhel guide completely excludes the guides mentioned above. On the walk we did with her (Altiplanicas lakes and red stones), she walked without worrying if everyone was listening. Inside the van she did not get the job of turning back to give the warnings (everyone else did this), many things were not possible to be heard, even asking for her to speak louder. I took pictures anyway, while all the others I cited were dedicated to taking good photos. On the day of the tour, we were waiting in front of the hotel, she passed and parked a few meters in front and did not call us. As all other guides would call, we thought it was another van, only after a few minutes she called and saw a telegram (did not leave the van). Another point was the astronomical experience tour. There is a part of the tour where we sit in specific chairs to observe the sky in the outside area (seats that lie to allow better visualization of the explanations). My wife's chair was broken and we requested the exchange, but a different, uncomfortable chair was provided, which did not allow you to lie down to view the explanations. There was no reservation chair of these specifics.

review_text: Arriving early in the morning before the crowds, me and my sister bought coffee from a local man selling espresso out of a small cart and sat down by the pier and watched the waves ripple across Lake Llanquihue. Frutillar doesn't have much to do, but that's kind of the beauty of it. After we finished our drinks, we wandered around town admiring the unique architecture in the town. Homes in Frutillar and the Lake District in general fuse Germanic elements with characteristically Latin color combinations on what would otherwise be run-of-the-mill buildings. Keep your eye out for the music school which has forest green corrugated metal siding with ornate wooden window frames. It is definitely worth spending some time exploring this small German colony! To get here, take the mini busses going down Av San Francisco in Puerto Varas. Hop on any one that says "Frutillar Bajo." It costs CLP$1000 and takes about an hour each way.
title: Get that Postcard Shot!!

review_text: 81 years ago, Guillermo Pohl, a visionary, bought 38 hectares in Palguin, 30 km from Pucon, Chile. Amid forests of coligues and beside the sound Palguin River, he founded the HOTEL TERMAS DE PALGUIN. There he built individual wells with the best hot springs in the area and pool. Waters of sulphur, potash, lithium and great healing properties. In 1998 the fire consumed these facilities. Rolling her son, she allowed herself to be defeated, but not her granddaughter Romina, with her husband Angel. Today, they have great rooms, dressed and equipped with taste and comfort. There are no televisions, which invites quiet reading listening to the river. Owners collaborate with state institutions and universities in volcanological studies and preserve the ecosystem. A piece of paradise on earth... Hopefully we can come back!!!!
title: A piece of paradise in Palguin.

review_text: I had a fabulous "trip of a life time" with Southern Trips. Favi is an outstanding guide - a pro. Tati, his sister set up the trip logistics - all went perfectly. Favi led me on a 10 day horse pack trip from Cochamo, Chile to Argentina and back. I stayed at Campo Aventura's lovely rustic Riverside lodge and also their La Junta mountain lodge. A great part of the trip. We had splendid days going through deep river valleys, up steep passes, into gorgeous old growth forests, and beside pristine lakes. We had campfires for lunch and dinner, fished, tented, stayed in refugios and with local families. Be prepared for a rigorous ride! One of the best experiences of my life!

review_text: This pier has been significantly updated since the last review was posted here on Trip Advisor. It now hosts a wide variety of water sport activities for people of all ages. Here you can rent kayaks, stand-up paddle boards, and small sailboats. You can receive instruction in all these activities, and I also saw people doing scuba diving (not sure if there is instruction for that). It is also accessible for people in wheelchairs, and we saw a gentleman in a wheelchair on a paddle board out by himself out on the water! We have twice rented small sailboats here (about 4 meters long). I have zero experience sailing so if I can do this, anyone can. They have captains who go out with you and explain how to sail the boat while they take you around Valparaíso Bay. If you want, you can try your hand at the rudder and help with the sails. As I understand it, the wind comes up in the afternoon so it's best to do this at 1:00 pm or later. Of course they give you life jackets and they even had sunscreen if you forgot your own. The sailing lasts about 2 hours, you have fantastic views of the city and the huge cargo ships, not to mention sea lions and lots of birds. For the 2 hour trip with captain, they charge CLP $35.000 - you can fit up to four people on the boat and the captain makes 5 total. The pier also has several restaurants and an enormous sign that says "VALPARAISO" that is a must-have photo opp for any tourist coming to the city. Access to the pier is a bit tricky due to a lot of construction in the area, but you enter near the "Barón" metro station and follow the signs. I would call this a must-stop for anyone who likes the water and wants to do something a little out-of-the-ordinary
title: Sailboat/kayak/paddle board rentals and the VALPARAISO sign!

review_text: An excellent day out made even better by Luis, an awesome guide who explains everything in both English and Spanish. You will need a good camera to take photos otherwise just enjoy the time with these amazing animals. Review of: King Penguin & Tierra del Fuego Tour

The wine tasting was fabulous as you have a small cheese/chocolate pairing and do the tasting outside overlooking the incredible views. We loved the wine so much that we became wine club members! Don't miss visiting Kingston if you are in the Casablanca Valley! Thank you so much Caroline for coming to our vineyard! You and your husband were great fun to host, and you both taught me a lot about wine during our tasting on the upper terrace. I hope you are enjoying your club shipments back home. If you are ever back in Chile, be sure to stop by to say hello! Cheers, Aubree

We also stopped at Vina del Mar, the fish market (which was a real treat), saw a Mo'ai and did wine tasting at Emilianas in the Casablanca Valley before heading back to Santiago. Rodrigo did an amazing job keeping us safe navigating the Chile traffic. A really great day. Thanks for making it so special, Nacho (and sharing your birthday with us)! We're glad you had a great time in Valparaíso with Nacho and his knowledge, thank you for your review.

review_text: This tour is a must for anyone visiting Santiago. I was born there (but left years ago) and it was still very interesting and enjoyable. The guide was knowledgeable and provided a good introduction to the basics of the history of Chile, including a very balanced and rational description of the turbulent 70's. The tour does not go into the buildings, but shows you the outside and talks about them, so that you can come back and visit. The four hours pass very fast, and you get a coffee/beer stop in the middle. The tour is free, but you are expected to tip the guide, I would recommend at least US$10.
title: Great orientation to the city and introduction to its history and culture

review_text: After a very early start to get to the Geyser del Tatio at sunrise, it was very impressive. There were plenty of geysers to see, and understanding the different ages of them was quite good. It was very cold in the morning though, about minus 10 Celsius, so be prepared for that depending on the time of year you go. We did a tour to get there with Cosmo Andino and were very happy with their service (we later did the Valle de Luna tour as well). There is a thermal pool there as well which was quite pleasant, if crowded, as well, though getting changed was a rather chilly experience. There are change rooms there though which makes life easy. I'd recommend a trip to the geysers, particularly if you haven't previously seen any.
title: Impressive

review_text: The Fonck Museum, located in Cuatro Norte Street, housed in a spectacular palace. This museum exhibits an impressive collection of fossils and pre-Columbian artifacts including a Easter Island Moai (one of the only six Moai sculptures found outside the island). Founded in 1937, the museum itself is quite small. The Moai brought from Easter Island in 1950 stands majestically in the garden by the museum's entrance.
title: Moai from Easter Island

title: Excellent��

review_text: I was a part of a larger group of students from a US based school. We enjoyed couple of different tours with this company - walking city tour, biking city tour, Valparaiso walking tour and Vineyard biking tour. Needless to say, both Peter (the owner) and his entire team of tour guides are some of the most passionate people you'll ever meet. They love what they do and it shows in their work. Their knowledge, passion and love for Santiago and Chile is insurmountable. They pride themselves in having some of the best tour guides in the city that make their tours worth every dime spent on them. They love being asked loads of questions regarding the city's history, culture, food, and people so ask away. They are nice, friendly to speak to. My favorite experience was the biking tour in the vineyard with Rodrigo. It was his first time doing the vineyard tour and he was impeccable for his first time. He did a great job answering all the my questions at length regarding the winery. Their team is funny, passionate and love having fun with what they do. There will never be a dull moment in their presence, they love life and are high energy people so be prepared to enjoy a thrilling ride with them. Also, Peter (owner) has excellent recommendations for great local food and alcohol in the city. Feel free to pick his brain regarding some restaurant recommendations. He has known the city and country for a good while and is an excellent resource to learn about various Chilean topics in general. You cannot go wrong with any tour you choose with this company. :) Make sure to enjoy your time while in Santiago and you'll be compelled to write your own reviews here. ;) Wow Cherryace! I think this is the longest review we have ever received, but almost coming from someone who took 4 tours with us... extra special. Happy that our passion and knowledge stood out for you. You made our day. We check reviews daily to make sure we are living up to your standard and our own, so we are thrilled we landed this one just right. Come again and thanks for the support and online love, Peter
title: Excellent resource for exploring Santiago for a first timer!

review_text: They are all tied in to the Putana volcano. As you cross the bridge, there is a wetland on both sides of the road. Ducks were present as were Andean geese. In the distance was the imposing presence of the volcano. After a long day that started early with a visit to El Tatio, the wetland was a bit of a respite, a chance to see another side of Mother Nature.
title: A BRIDGE, A WETLAND AND A VOLCANO

review_text: If you go with children, bring sunscreen and exercise, the walk is approximately 2 km or a little more to reach a “dock” that is not even close to what you can see in the photos, it is a small platform and they charge 3000 per person in addition 3000 for parking, and the truth is it is not a very well made trail. and there was a wait in line of approximately 1 hour and a half just for the photo
title: It was not what I expected

review_text: Our guide (Franco) was a storyteller. He told the history so well, i felt more like i was listening to a tale from a book, rather than a boring point by point history. I enjoyed learning about the Mapuche people and the cultural diversity that Chile has to offer. It was also very good exercise, we walked throughout the city and he pointed out the different museums. Although the tour is free they do work on donations, they suggest $10USD, which is not bad at all considering the time we spent and the history we learned.
title: Guide (Franco) was very knowledgeable and entertaining.

review_text: Great all the services, in particular the arrangement of clothes and sporting goods. They should do more events in the year
title: I loved everything

review_text: Laposrolle winery, Montes winery and Viu Manet and we have the best driver we've ever had traveling around the world. Francisco with Colchaugua wine tours. He's American who started his own company and after years working in the tech industry and his love of Chilean wine he moved to Chile. If you are ever traveling in Chilean wine region and you need a driver please check out Francisco with his company Colchauga wine tours. He's really amazing and in his own time he takes care local stray dogs. Just amazing person and he helps support local businesses too.

review_text: Barring the obligatory American tourist desecrating a grave after being told not to (not the tour's fault), this was everything you could need when visiting San Pedro for the first time. I left with a better knowledge of the local area and indigenous people, and really got to grips with the town's layout too. Very good, great staff, nice job.

review_text: Excellent view created by lagoons in forefront and number of volcanoes in backdrop. Visit after noon as the sun is behind you and lagoons appear blue in color. Better photographs. In morning the sun is in front and pictures are not as clear or beautiful. Very serene and peaceful environment as well. Must do tour in Atacama.
title: Lagoons surrounded by Volcanoes

review_text: Great experience and awesome people! The views were amazing! Food was great! And the tour guide Christian was the best!! Review of: Valparaiso Port and Vina del Mar Full-Day Tour from Santiago We're glad you enjoyed the views, food and company. Thank you for your review.

review_text: I was only able to visit a small portion of this sprawling metropolitan park so I can only speak to this experience. The views from atop are great and there are a plethora of amenities (food vendors, cafes and restaurants along the top). The venue is family friendly and overrun with tourists, locals and cyclists who are either labouring up the winding roads or zooming down the pathways and designated trails. To get to the top you can either walk or bike (5-6km) up the various roads and trails or take the busy funicular up. The funicular round trip for an adult is $2,600 CLP. Be prepared to wait 30 minutes to an hour to get to the top and then again to get back down. Once at the top you can walk along to the Japanese botanical garden or take the scenic gondola across to the next peak for an extra fee. Budget at least 2-3 hours for the visit but you can easily spend there the whole day exploring.
title: A sprawling park with nice views of the city but very crowded

review_text: My wife and I recently visited Chile. Family found a website for Hec Tour Service who advertised tours suitable for disabled persons. My wife who owns a Travel Agency in Taradale, New Zealand, is wheelchair bound so we decided to contact Hec Tour Service to ascertain if they could provide us with a suitable tour that would also cater for my wife’s needs. I mailed Hec Tour Service through their trip advisor link late on the Thursday evening and received a very prompt reply. After further communications Hec Tour Service confirmed a private tour on the Friday at 1100 am. They collected us from our accommodation promptly on time at 1100 am with an English-speaking tour guide. The guide was wonderful – very polite and beautifully spoken. We were transported in an excellent modern car and taken on a wonderful tour through several of Valparaiso’s delightful and charming cerro’s (hills). We stopped for lunch at a very Chilean restaurant which our guide had told us had the best empanadas in Valpo. We were not disappointed – they were excellent, washed down by a pleasant cold Chilean cerveza. We were then taken through Vina del Mar and onto Concón. In summary we saw 3 greatly different locations during the tour – the eclectic beauty of Valparaiso, the modern of Vina del Mar, and the sandhills and awesome scenery of Concón. We were then returned to our hotel at the end of a wonderful day’s touring. The following day Hec Tour Services provided us with transportation within Valparaiso, again with the wonderful prompt and attentive service of the English-speaking guide. Hec Tour Service provided us with an experience way above our expectations and we will be delighted to recommend this company to any of my wife’s clients, or our friends, visiting Chile. Muchas gracias Hec Tour Service – a 5-star plus operation!
title: A top class experience in Valparaiso

He ensured a safe and well-organized tour while creating a relaxed and fun atmosphere.Tristan's passion for nature and the history of the volcano made the hike a fascinating learning moment. His narrations about the geological formations and the local flora and fauna enriched the experience enormously.In addition, Tristan was extremely accommodating and helpful as a guide. He took time to answer our questions and encourage us to overcome our personal limits. His positive attitude and enthusiasm were infectious and helped make the hike an unforgettable experience.The view from the top of Osorno Volcano was absolutely breathtaking and richly rewarded our efforts. I can fully recommend Tristan as a guide for the Osorno climb. With him by your side, you will not only reach the summit, but also experience an unforgettable time full of adventures and memories. review_text: On December 19, 2016, I had the full day to see this attractive city and had pre-arranged a private tour with Perro Tour. My guide, Pedro, met me at my hotel at 9:00 a.m. and we began a wonderful walking tour of his city of which he is very proud. He was extremely knowledgeable and answered every question I asked and many I hadn't thought of to ask. He wanted to know if there were sights that were of special interest. I said, "show me everything you think is interesting in your city." I liked that we used the funiculars and city bus just to Vina del Mar rather than taking a bus tour of the whole area. We stopped for lunch in a quaint restaurant and visited a market where Pedro was very patient as I tried many sweaters. As I am an older lady, he made sure our pace was comfortable for me and we were able to include all the highlights before we parted at 5 p.m.. I could not have had a better guide or a more pleasurable experience in Valparaiso and Vina del Mar. I highly recommend Perro Tour. Thank you Frances for sharing your trip experience with Perro Tour with other travelers on TripAdvisor. We love to read that your guide (Pedro) was on time, that he was knowledgeable and answered every question you asked him, that he took care of you and walked at a comfortable pace, and that you had such a pleasurable experience in Valparaíso and Viña del Mar. review_text: While visiting Santiago on business, I pondered what to do with my free time on the weekend. After looking through the options, I choose to take a tour of the Sewell Mining Town about 2.5 hours drive from Santiago. I went with a tour (TuristTour) and I think that is probably the only way to really get something from the experience. I choose this activity over the other options for two reasons: 1) to learn a little more about the economically vital copper mining industry in Chile and 2) to get out of the city and get up into the Andes mountains. This accomplished both. Our guide, Javiera, was very knowledgeable about the history of this town built into the mountain and even was able to explain a little bit about copper processing. We were able to stroll the town (it is not often I get to tromp through snow in July), walk through a couple of buildings and eat lunch with the mine employees in the cafeteria. This World Heritage site gives a good look at the mining industry and the life of the miners. The museum treated the subject of copper with a bit of a light overview but this is probably the best approach for the average tourist. On the other hand, it does a good job of showing the importance of copper to our everyday lives. The city is pretty amazing because it is like very few places you will see anywhere else. I also found out in talking with Javiera that the mine used to be private (as some of the displays in the museum suggested) but is now part of the state-run mining operation. She indicated that the mine was nationalized in the Allende era and this is a subject that I find deeply interesting. I had a very worthwhile off-line discussion with her concerning this subject. This is a matter about which many Chileans still display quite an uncomfortable reticence. Even if copper mining is a subject that holds little interest for you, this still represents a very important aspect of both Chilean history and its current economic vitality (Javiera indicated 40%+ of Chilean GDP is related to the mining industry). Being there and walking the town is a worthwhile experience. And the scenery to which you are exposed along the way is a major bonus.

English tour group had only 5 people so we got lots of time on the telescope. The view of Jupitor was amazing through the scope. The guide was very knowledgeable and I came away awe struck at the beauty and vastness of the universe. JUST AWESOME!
title: Highlight of our trip

review_text: A great experience. As most reviewed indicate - you need to take into account this is a ferry (read: cargo ship) not a cruise liner. Therefore all things being considered it was clean, had great service and was overall good value. I enjoyed the yoga classes (could have been more!) and the fact they cater for all diets. I am coeliac - and they handled it well, including me asking interrogating questions of the food. A great chance to switch off for three days with excellent views. We are glad that the trip was to your liking and that we could help with your special diet. Thank you
title: Great value for money and experience

review_text: Waling or driving to downtown you will pass it, step down and look around. Not much more to do here.
title: You will pass it

review_text: We really enjoyed our tour of Santiago today. Franco was an excellent guide, with a perfect blend of historical/cultural understanding and humour. We've done a few free walking tours (Europe and Middle East) in the last few months with our 2 teenagers and we all agree this was one of our favourites. Franco brought us close to the political demonstrations, but we felt safe and secure with his expert knowledge and awareness of our surroundings. The whole tour took about 3.5 hours with a nice half hour stop at a restaurant (with no pressure to buy), but moved at a good pace and we didn't get the sense that any of the group of about 20 (aged from teens to seniors) were getting tired. Franco has so many good recommendations for restaurants, etc. that we'd suggest taking the tour early in your stay to take advantage of some spots in the following days.
title: Free Walking Tour of Santiago

review_text: Terrible, very delayed entry, then very bad organization, starting with wanting to buy a drink, a cashier with a cash machine, endless line 🤦🏻‍♂️ The music is terrible, the DJs are very bad, they don't expect to start a song when after “20 seconds” they already change it… I've never seen DJs change music so quickly, it doesn't make any sense… anyway, very bad! Very bad, impossible to be a Tripadvisor recommendation!
title: Appalling!

review_text: I listened to the reviews on here and rented the audio guide (which I never do in a museum) and I'm glad I did since almost nothing was in English. The museum is free, but audio guide is CHP$2000. It's extremely convenient to the train station (Quinta Normal) and you don't even have to go outside. The museum is very detailed and powerful. To be honest, after visiting concentration camps in Germany and Poland, this one is much more mild, but nonetheless sheds light on a tumultuous time in Chilean History. I think it's a tribute to the people of Chile that this was built so relatively soon after the dictatorship. The strongest message is at the end - they tell the story so humans don't ever treat other humans that way. If only the rest of the world we live in felt that way.
title: Worth seeing in Santiago

review_text: We took the 4 tips tour with Felipe and it was very interesting, with lots of information not only on history, but also on recent events in Chile. We recommend!
title: Great tour of Santiago!

review_text: 100% recommended An intimate, very instructive tour by Rodrigo, a passionate about the night sky. 100% recommended experience. Ideal for new moon days and super warm. We set off with a direct view of the sky with an interesting delivery of astronomical data. Then seen by telescope and finally a pleasant campfire accompanied by coffee, wine and something to eat. Of course, photos with the starry sky in the background.
title: 100% recommended

review_text: A group of friends and I, ten of us in total cake here on 02/05/19. A very professional and safety focused company. Very efficient and streamlined. Great safety briefing and very to the point, no time wasting. Great range of equipment supplied, wet suits, wind jacket, wet boots, helmet and life vest. Took us from office location in town by minibus to the river, about 10 minute drive. Again, safety briefing and straight into a fantastic fun day. Our instructor Daniel and Nico absolutely superb, fun and informative and helped us all every step of the way. A truly great day out for most ages from teens to more mature. Providing you can swim you’ll be fine. Cannot day enough just how much fun the group and I had. I’ll definitely be back with these guys again. Great day out..the best of fun..superb experience. Thank you guys a million Hi!, ​ We are glad to know that you get a good memory of Cajón del Maipo and the our company Please, don't hesitate to return in a next opportunity! Regards!
title: Excellent day rafting

review_text: Our guide Mauricio was amazing and had a great sense of humour. He gave a rrally good English and Spanish description throughout. The food was fantastic, the driver was very professional and competent. The bus was modern, clean and comfortable. We wanted to leave a generous tip, but we hadn't been informed that we needed to pay the park entrance fees in cash, leaving us with no money. Review of: Red Stones, Altiplanic Lagoons and the Atacama Salt Flat Thanks for sharing your experience! We are glad to know that you enjoyed your experience with La Yana Travel. San Pedro de Atacama is an incredible place and we love being able to share its beauty with travelers like you. We hope to see you soon on another adventure. Best regards Layana Travel. 🌵
title: Fantastic Guide

review_text: What an amazing tour, they arrived on time, so much is done is one day without being rushed, and of course the tour guides Frank and Jimmy were just the best, friendly, funny, informative and just overall sweethearts
title: Amazing

review_text: Angelo & Hector were fantastic. Hector is very knowledgeable and passionate & provided a lot of helpful commentary on the areas we visited as well as those we just drove passed (including pointing out some of the wildlife). The path to the lagoon was closed because of the ice but the view from the hotel was still beautiful. Had a brilliant time and would highly recommend it. Review of: Inca Lagoon in Andes Mountain Range - Visit Local Vineyard with Tasting included
title: Brilliant 👏

review_text: Full eyes, breathtaking scenery, at the gates of the desert! Simply Beautiful!!! to see without hesitation!!!!
title: To do!!! exceptional landscapes

review_text: You should not miss this. Absolutely fascinating. This was one of our "must-do" trips. We were on a cruise and the bus met us and took us a couple of miles down the coast where an ancient car ferry was ready to take us across. It was more than an hour and a half. Coming back it got rough. Not horrendously rough, but enough for the waves to be breaking of the bows. Being a flat ferry, almost like a landing craft, it was very bouncy in spite of the route back being modified to miss the worst. It took 2 and a quarter hours to get back. Nobody was sick, but some were quite green Wrap up warm.
title: Absolutely brilliant, but getting there...

review_text: We enjoyed visiting this place. If you are in the area it is a must. It's a very impressive structure that towers over Coquimbo with amazing views.
title: Great views of the city

review_text: Don Pedro an excellent guide!!! Friendly, explains perfectly and is also fun. Very pleasant experience, everything very nice.
title: Marvelous !

review_text: Excellent professional,responsible and punctual Note 10!!! Super recommend. Knowledge and dedication in your guidance they made all the difference Ready, patient, sensational!!!
title: Excellent Professional....

review_text: We cycled there from San Pedro. I think most people can make it, even with minimal hiking experience. If you are out of shape you may need to walk your bike up a couple hills. Make sure you have sunscreen and water. We spent about 5 hours round trip.
title: Cycle there!

review_text: We did a wonderful tour guided by Vivi, our friendly English speaking guide, who was also very knowledgeable about the wines. We visited two very different smaller wineries where we learned all about the winemaking and the specifics of the region. And off course also a great tasting. A traditional four course lunch with paired wines made the experience complete. Review of: Best Wine Tasting in Santiago
title: Delightful tour of Casablanca Valey

review_text: RAI was an excellent operator. Very organized and prepared with what people lacked in equipment/gear. Provided snow shoes and poles and gloves to those that didn't have any or jacket if he had a spare one. Although it is recommended to bring your own as he won't always have this. Was picked up on time at our hotel and made our way over mid way for gas station and washroom break before we continued our long journey to the base of the volcano. Takes about 2.5hrs. While 8k is the stated distance, felt shorter than actual, or maybe because we enjoyed it so much that we wanted to go further. Enjoyed the nice views from the base of mountain. Would have liked to go up more but this tour isn't that. Rai made some personally made sandwiches for our lunch, which was delicious! Stopped and ate a the middle of field/snow field to have lunch and look over the mountain ranges. 1hr lunch ish break. Then made our way back down to the car to enjoy a glass or two of wine and cheese/crakers/olives. Overall great trip/excursion! Review of: Andes Day Volcano 8K - Cajón del Maipo
title: Snow hike to Volcan San Jose

review_text: I had a fantastic time on the Sunday night I did the cooking class with Connie (and another lady who I can't remember her name but she was lovely!) There was just one other person in the class so it was small and intimate and I felt really comfortable like i was at a friends home cooking in the kitchen with a glass of wine in hand We made a large suite of tasty Chilean foods with accompanying wine - Connie is extremely knowledgeable with her wines which made the cooking class also feel like a wine tour I only wish I had time to join one of their wine tours they had on offer! Highly recommend for anyone who just wants to do something a little different - money well spent!
title: Fantastic Sunday night!

review_text: My wife and I chose this tour based on the fact it looked the most authentic. A great decision!! The whole thing is run by Alex, his father Wilson, mother Clara and dog Angelito. From the moment we were collected at our hostel the whole family’s sole aim was for us to have an amazing, informative and memorable night. The excitement and passion that Alex has for Astronomy and photography is simply inspiring, the amount we saw and learnt about space as well as the indigenous Atacamenean constellations was awesome. A fantastic spread of hot drinks, snacks and homemade empanadas made by his mum was a nice touch. He even printed photos straight away for us as well as sending a heap through later on. A real bonus was Alex taking the time to give us a tutorial with our own camera around how to take high quality photos of the night sky. From start to finish this was one of the best experiences we have had in South America, genuine, authentic and enlightening. I would highly recommend Alex over a mainstream alternative anyday. You will definitely enjoy this tour! Review of: Astronomy Tour in San Pedro de Atacama Mark & Leena, we highly appreciate you took the time to come up with such wonderful words and by all honesty the honor was ours to have given you the best night experience possible! our fulfillment goes in hand with your excitement from that night ;) We wish you all the best!
title: Outstanding Authentic Local Experience

review_text: Maria José was exceptional! Impeccable service as a guide, photographer and mediator! He explained every square meter of the trip, from the fauna, flora and color of the water in the Inca lagoon in Portillo. We even managed to take a photo with the Llamas with Maria José’s tips! Thank you for everything, dear. My wife and I were amazed with your service!
title: Portillo - Amazing Tour

review_text: I took the tour today (19/06/2024) to Farellones with the excellent guide Juan, punctual, with a great explanation of the route. Congratulations Juan, for being such a helpful guide!
title: Guide Juan

review_text: This is a nice park just down the street from the Santa Lucia Metro station or 5 minutes walk from Plaza de Armes. You have to sign a guest register to enter; no admission fee or ID required. The park is clean and has many flower gardens and a few historic structures. The top of the park is an easy walk, and depending on the weather, provides good views of the city. This is good for a few hours of relaxation.
title: Nice Park with Decent Views

review_text: It was a really amazing experience we had been on a tour in mamalluca years ago, but today far exceeds this very well thought out and designed music the rapporteur, the view of the stars and the spectacular moon, the hot chocolate and photos, I recommend it was a very pleasant experience thank you very much
title: Something different and very well thought out

review_text: Excellent Service ! Very knowledgeable and Ricardelle Pascal and team really helped us with the tour as my husband was working and told us when to get on and come off and best places to work. One of the best and we travel all over ! Review of: Cable Car, Funicular and Sightseeing Bus in Santiago one day Dear traveler, we are glad to hear that you had a pleasant experience with our staff. We hope to see you soon!
title: Excellent Service and Team

review_text: Valley of the moon is a cheap tour but definitely worth it. The landscape of this valley is unlike anything you've seen, comparable to the surface of the moon, so much so that Nasa has done testing there. The sunset at the end of the tour is magical. Don't miss this while in San Pedro!
title: Don't miss Valley of the Moon!

review_text: I travel quite a bit and book a lot of tours/day trips online. I have to say the Cajón del Maipo and Volcán San José Hike 8K was one of my favorite day trips so far. This tour was amazing if you want a nice hike with amazing views. Our guide Francisco was great. He was on time picking us up from the hotel. He was very knowledgable and passionate about the area and culture. They provide a lunch and large water bottle for you. They also ask ahead of time if you have any food allergies which I thought was nice. I also brought my own water bottle and a few small snacks. It started out kind of chilly in the morning but then got much warmer as the hike went on. I wore layers that I could take off as I went and that worked out well for me. It was a lot dustier than I expected. That did not take away from enjoying the hike, but if you have allergies you might want to pack some meds/kleenex for that. We had a great group where everyone walked about the same pace and had beautiful weather. I know both of those things could maybe change your experience but we really lucked out and had a fun time. (For reference my friend and I are in our 30s from the United States) Review of: Andes Day Volcano 8K - Cajón del Maipo
title: 10/10 Hike

review_text: Best experience!! Very attentive and punctual, always responding quickly and withdrawing doubts. The Guide Coqueiro was out of series, Wonderful!!
title: Sunset House Zeroing

review_text: We loved going on this adventurous experience! San Pedro de Atacama has a way of bringing out the adventurous side of people and this is a great way to create an amazing memory. We did the afternoon trip and the staff was very forward and helpful. We recommend staying hydrated prior to the trip and take plenty of water! The sandboarding itself was really fun and the staff was helpful or they will let you go off and do your own thing. The sunset views were incredible and worth the trip in itself. Check out our blog for more information about the trip and about San Pedro!
title: Adrenaline rush with amazing views!

review_text: Like the Blue Lagoon near Reykjavik, the Laguna Cejar is one of those experiences you can’t miss. High salt level, very warm but with a soft mellow feel. Very relaxing. Dropped one point because getting out was a bit tricky and sharp on the feet and hands, more so when losing grip and falling back onto fagged surfaces. No lasting injuries but either we could have been warned or advised to wear precautionary footwear or they could have build or contrived a simple easier route out. But don’t be put off, it’s not enough to miss swimming here. Review of: Laguna Cejar
title: Good time in the lagoon.

review_text: I have done bike tours in many other big, busy cities and this was one of the best. Maurizio and Adrian clearly love their job and love showing a side of Santiago that most visitors don't see. They made sure everyone was safe through some thick traffic and gave great information. Bikes and helmets were good. We were a family of four and two more joined in late, don't know how a large group would be. Booking is easy and they send restaurant and hotel tips before your visit. Hola Bokbok4 Than you for your kind words, Adian and Maurizio do seem to like it here a lot, and they know the city by bike like the back of their hands, it's rare you'd spot them without a bike! I love hearing that Santiago is your favourite city to bike in, its great here and you can discover the hidden gems cars can't get to! I hope you used some of our tips and discovered more of Santiago solo! I expect if and when you come back someday you'll see much more people on their bikes! Safe travels Bokbok4! Muchas Gracias Peter.
title: Local life and markets, great tour

review_text: You can walk up the hill, bike up the hill, drive up the hill or take the funicular. It is very peaceful at the top with spectacular views. It was very hazy when I was there and they tried to tell me it was all caused by forest fires in the area. I think it was smog myself:))) If you wish to go to the small chapel at the top, you will have to climb a couple of flights of stairs. However, you can rest and the stairs don't cause too much of a challenge.

title: Nice

review_text: My guide Jorge took me around Orlando, monja, mariposa, Florida, bellevista, plan, in a great afternoon tour. I felt safe the whole time and from very little prior knowledge I learnt about the history and culture of the city. It is an amazing city and Jorge seemed to know every painter. The city is on of the most beautiful I have visited, the most culturally interesting I have seen in south America, it is an eclectic city with beautiful street art. I was in a small group and it seemed very flexible to different routes. With great restaurant an ba recommendations this is a Must for when you start your time in valpo. Anyway, end of my rambling, highly recommend you fork out for it when you come to th most amazing city in Chile, or maybe south America!

review_text: This feels like at times you've stepped in to Aladdin. It is breath taking and stunning. On our tour we did do an hour hike up to the tip of a sand dune so bring lots of water in case that happens to you and sun cream as there is scarcely any shade. This is just a once in a lifetime experience not to be missed. The Atacama desert!!

review_text: Nice to hear about the city from a local. He took us to places and told us stories only known by locals. We even went to a tiny coffee shop with the best coffee and a great owner. It’s across the street from the music school. Since we visited during summer break, we didn’t see any students nor staff. Review of: Famous Valparaíso! Premium Walking Tour with a Native Guide

review_text: My best friend and I did a tour onto a 5900m active vulcan with Licancabur Expediciones last year. The enterprise is led by Amapola and JP, a wonderful couple with a lot of mountain experience. We have never been on a mountain that high and we are no hikers at all but we felt good and cared by the two of them. They know how to make you feel safe and thus made our hiking experience perfect! In addition they invited us to their house for Christmas and we had a lovely night with them and their friends. Without Amapola and JP we probbably would have spent our night alone somewhere in Chile. Amapola is by the way super talented and showed us her self made shoes, art and calenders, she is just amazing!! Thank you so much guys, we enjoyed the summit and the time after that with you so much!! I can only recommend this wonderful couple and their hiking experiences! I hope to see you guys soon in Austria, Cari and I wish you all the best :)
title: Lovely couple with a big heart

review_text: I do not have enough words to describe how awesome this excursion was! My husband and I booked the day long Sea kayaking tour and would highly recommend. Perfect for beginner kayakers! Our guide, Juan, was great! He spoke wonderful English and had a wealth of knowledge.

review_text: Best with a guide or guidebook to fully appreciate the rich history. Different from Buenos Aires as it has a bit more of a “community” feel and the grounds/trees are very well maintained (hence 4 stars). About a 20 minute walk from central square, straight down the boulevard.
title: Well worth a visit, architecture and history combined

review_text: This review is both for Kayak en Patagonia and its sister company, Fortaleza Expediciones . We did a 7 day hiking/kayaking trip that covered Torres del Paine National Park and Bernardo O'Higgins National Park in Patagonia. These places are indescribably beautiful, wild, thrilling and enthralling, and Fortaleza/Kayak en Patagonia provided the guide, gear, logistical support and food to make the trip seamless, stress-free, an information hound's dream, and a total blast. We did 3 days of hiking in Torres del Paine, and I highly recommend going in the low season - the weather was great and there were relatively few people on the trail. We stayed in the refugios on the hiking part of the trip, and they are all very nice and well-maintained. Absolutely gorgeous scenery. We had a very smooth transition to the 4-day kayaking part of the trip, with all the different gear miraculously appearing at our campsite just as we needed it, including our tents and dry suits. About the dry suits. They are really a stroke of genius on the owner's part. While we were kayaking the Grey and Serrano rivers, the weather changed constantly, from beautiful sunshine, to snow, to slanting rain, and back again - but it mattered not to us. With our dry suits and pogies we were able to paddle serenely along enjoying the scenery in all its glory without suffering from the wet or cold. Fantastic. Our guide Jose Luis was terrific. Knowledgeable, accomplished, capable and a great cook. On our final day he took us on an ice-breaking kayaking trip in the lake below Serrano glacier - a definite highlight of the trip. Along the way on the Serrano River we also camped on the land of a local rancher, and this proved another highlight of the trip. So if you're going all the way to Chile, I definitely recommend going both the hiking and kayaking in Patagonia with Cristian (owner) and his crew. It just doesn't get better than this.
title: Outstanding in Every way

review_text: We did two tours: astronomical and another in the flowered desert We were delighted with the landscapes but especially with the careful attention of Top-rated guides Monserrat and Rodrigo I recommend them in closed eyes

title: Excellent tour!

review_text: I liked the tour with Francisca, the instructions before the tour were clear and tour covered a lot of places with incredible places for making photos and be amazed by Chile’s nature, with great breakfast and lunch included. I can only recommend the tour as it was well managed and everything went well Review of: Full Day Tour to Piedras Rojas, Altiplanic Lagoons and Chaxa

review_text: We did the Chilean cooking course and enjoyed every moment of it! It's a great way to emerge yourself in the Chilean culture. We loved select ing our own menu and personally shopping for the ingredients at the market. Our chef, Boris was great and we had a great afternoon chopping, cooking and chatting!! The food turned out to be delicious, especially coupled with the red wine and pisco sours provided!! We learned to make salsa, ceviche, chilean corn pie and pisco sours!! All this finished off with a cappucino and desert and it was the perfect meal and way to spend an afternoon. After months of backpacking, we so enjoyed spending time in this beautiful kitchen overlooking Valparaiso, listening to local music, it felt like we were 'home' for an afternoon!!
title: The perfect afternoon...

review_text: We started our visit to Cile in Valparaiso. Vinizio was our preferred place for the dinner. Good wines served during our meal. Absolutely necessary to try the plat of a mix of cheeses and cold cuts; nice atmosphere. Alway open even at late evening, and even when all the others were closed.
title: Our first stop in Chile

review_text: The park is a quite a distance from the centre. Local came here for walking, jogging and cycling. At the far end of the park there are ponds with pink Flamingos and also White Swans with black neck and head ( Unusual) . there are machines to buy food to feed them for 100 peso each. At the far end there is a restaurant . Free and clean toilets are avialable.Walking shoes and camera are essential. Suggest 1-2 hours here.
title: A bit far from but a beautiful park.

review_text: A few weeks in Chile, and our family recognizes that even public facilities can turn into "tourist trap" destinations. This is a spot that is worth the annoyance of paying for parking, then going through gift store to then pay for entry. Yup, worth it! Park along the road, and if it is extremely crowded, don't go in. Previous reviews have warned that if it is too busy, it isn't enjoyable. The narrow walkways leave people angling for the perfect photo. And what a photo! Really stunning, and noisy, Class VI rapids with Volcan Osorna directly behind, are the visual highlight. The boardwalks are well built, and crowded. Elbow in to take the perfect picture, then head for the less crowded lower trails. We did the one that goes downstream, and it wasn't crowded at all. A lovely side waterfall and private pool that at one time must have been the perfect (but cold) blue lagoon swimming spot, and shaded streamside trail. Two trails totaled 1 kilometer of easy, but not handicap accessible, trail. We skipped the third trail. There are facilities to buy food within the park, and (free) restroom.
title: Avoid crowds, and save time to enjoy variety of scenery of the entire area.

review_text: On our last day on San Pedro we walked to the ruins, which only took us half an hour from the center. The ruins are pretty good but the Mirador is even better. You walk up a serpentine trail for about half an hour and you will be rewarded with a breathtaking view of the valley. Really something if you have some time!
title: Great and easy to access

review_text: Great salt lake with solid salt, blue and turquoise waters in an endless plan with wildlife, ancient bacteria colonies at the shore and view on the surrounding mountains in the distance. Do this in the evening, enjoy sun set and with Atacama Connection get Pisco sour.

review_text: Prior to a recent cruise of South America and Antarctica, we spent four days in Santiago, Chile, where we planned on touring highlights of Santiago and several Chilean wineries. Before our trip, I looked to Trip Advisor for recommendations on top Chilean Tour guides. I was attracted to the excellent reports on “Chilean Wine Lovers” both for wine tours and Santiago City highlights. I contacted the CEO of Chilean Wine Lovers, Maurico Rodriguez and, after a friendly exchange of emails, we planned a tour for each of the four days. My wife and I have done extensive international travel and used some of the highest rated tour agencies in the world. Our experience with Mauricio far exceeded other experiences. Mauricio’s attention to detail and professionalism went far beyond our highest expectations. He arranged for us to be met at the airport, followed by a very informative tour of central Santiago including lunch. On day 2, Mauricio picked us up at the hotel, and 2.5 hours later we arrived at the Aconcagua Valley and visited the Vina San Esteban and Vina Errazuriz Wineries. Both make exceptional wine and Mauricio was a great teacher of the history, soils, climate and production facilities of all wineries visited. Mauricio is truly a wine expert and enjoys sharing his knowledge with his clients. On day 3, Maurico took us to visit the High Maipo Valley, which included stops at the Peres Cruz, Santa Rita Mojaito and Huelqen Wineries. Every day we experienced a fantastic tour, excellent wines, and an enjoyable, fun tour. We ate a great lunch at a restaurant in a rural location only visited by local citizens. The food, ambience and service by the owner were impeccable not to mention the great value. During our stay, Mauricio shared his incredible knowledge of the Chilean Wine Industry with stories, histories, and anecdotes that made each day an adventure as well as a learning experience. Day 4 arrived, and there was Mauricio - waiting to take us to another winery on the way to the port city of Valparaiso. That last wine tour was to the Casablanca Region at Bodega Wines, where they use clay pots for making wine! Each day with Mauricio, we were accompanied by one of his young daughters and on the last day by his two youngest daughters. The girls were truly an added delight to our tours and at the conclusion of our visit, we felt as though we were family! On the way to dropping us at the port in Valparaiso where our cruise ship waited, Mauricio stopped at a convenience store to make a small purchase for us. I joined him in the store and in doing so accidentally dropped my passport on the street while getting out of Mauricio’s van. We proceeded to the port and discovered that my passport was missing. The ship was scheduled to depart in about two hours. Mauricio returned us to the convenience store and talked to the manager. No passport had been turned in to the manager. Mauricio assured us that if the passport had been found by a local resident, it likely would be turned in to the police as local residents know that foreign visitors cannot get out of the country without going to their embassy which would result in their missing the cruise departure. Mauricio then called the police and learned that indeed the passport had been turned in to the police department. Mauricio went to the Police Headquarters, retrieved my passport and took us to the ship in time for departure. All of this was done in the span of 90 minutes in a large port city. We could not have asked for more from Mauricio – he is a wonderful, honest, knowledgeable and well-connected host with a tremendous sense of humor! We feel that we have made a good friend. If you plan to visit Santiago’s wine regions, become knowledgeable of the Chilean Wine Industry, have several great tours, and meet a superb host who will handle all of the details including ensuring your personal safety, contact Mauricio at Chilean Wine Lovers. We will return to Chile in the future -- our first call will be to Mauricio. - JK, Visited December 2015
