review_text: It was an incredible experience. The landscape, the stops and the whole route made the tour excellent. The Rosita guide alongside the driver Francisco made the ride even better. Note Mil
title: Sunset Cordilheira

review_text: A pleasant surprise for me the compulsive buyer. 4 floors full of all the great brands for all tastes. Super sophisticated the sports floor with exclusive shops of Helly Hansen, Under Armour, Mammut, Merrell and Doite. Great food court with many options for every visitor.
title: Best mall in town

review_text: Quinta Normal has a number of Museums in the Park, so drop into this Museum if you are in the area. Terrible things happened during the Pinochet regime and the people affected should be commemorated. The space has been used in a very interesting way and the material on display is important in Chile's modern history. However having read a lot on the subject, it did not tell me anything I did not know. If you want to learn about this period then the Museum if well worth a visit, especially for young Chileans who probably know little of what happened.
title: Worth a visit if you know nothing about the Pinochet era

review_text: Gradosur was able to accomodate my very last minute request for an active day tour out of Santiago! While all other companies came back with either ridiculous prices or wine and bike tours in which I was not interested, Gradosur was really helping me out and listened to my wishes. We did an active & challenging one-day MTB trip in the Andes on the El condor route and Igor was my guide. Due to my trip schedule I only had one free day in Santiago and it was the best day I could have wished for. Magnificient route, good bike, nice food & great guide! Not only made Igor feel me very safe and secure, he also was great company with a lot of nice stories about the country and surroundings. Thank you for this wonderful trip and the flexibility in setting it up!
title: Active MTB day tour out of Santiago - El Condor route

review_text: The script was amazing. Driver and guide very attentive and polite. The tasting at the wineries was excellent. We had lunch at Casa Del Bosque and it was a great experience. Review of: Exclusive wineries in Casablanca Valley & Tanino Restaurant
title: Incredible tour!

review_text: All Trips with the Lucio do bora Pro Chile were fantastic, I recommend him as a travel consultant. Amazing Landscapes
title: Travel set/24

review_text: Our afternoon at the Chilean Cuisine Cooking school was a surprise for us and what a wonderful experience it was. My 16 year old son and I had been traveling through Chile together and were lucky enough to be treated to this culinary experience. The classes are held in a unique old building in a vibrant, exciting neighborhood. Our instructor led us through all of the ingredients and prep with gentle ease and excellent insight about how each dish fit into the Chilean culture. We used the freshest of ingredients, purchased that afternoon at the market, and prepared fragrant, interesting dishes that all complimented each other and were delicious. We ended our evening by sitting down to a lovely dinner that we enjoyed immensely.
title: What an amazing culinary experience!

review_text: Worth to go a have a stroll thru the streets, enjoy the tranquility and the bohemian spirit. Have a coffee in one of the cafes! and feel the spirit of Santiago!
title: Nice Walk

review_text: We tried attending the 9:30 Blue Tour while in Santiago. Arriving early, we confirmed with the guide it would be in English. The tour didn't start at the advertised time, as the guide kept waiting to see if more people would join. By the time we were ready to go, about 25 minutes after the supposed start time, the guide informed us it would only be in Spanish as some of the visitors that had arrived did not speak English, but that we could "ask as many questions as we wanted". Not speaking fluent Spanish, our wait was pointless. We instead joined Tour4Tips (highly recommended!) which was starting at 10:00 nearby and had, as advertised, tours in English. We were very disappointed with Spicy Chile.
title: Disappointing... save your time and go with another company.

review_text: I actually discovered the metro a bit late in my visit to Santiago, but it did work for me a few times. Largest underground system I've ever seen. I'm from Vancouver, Canada and our system is a toy compared to this. Huge stations, inexpensive and fast.
title: good fast and looks pretty safe

review_text: This is a plaza you will stop by and walk through. It is not a solo destination. It is a nice place to walk a bit and get some exercise. We walk by it to get to a small mercado to buy gifts. Many shops and street vendors selling their goods.
title: Nothing special

review_text: Four of us walked to San Cristobal Hill and took the funicular up to the top of the ride. Off and walked up many steps to the statue of Mary. We had hoped that we would get a good view of the city and the Andes. Not to be - at this time of year there is a fog/mist that sits in the valley obscuring parts of the city and only leaving an outline of the Andes. Would be superb on a clear day.
title: Hopeful View

review_text: Fantastic experience. One full day in the river, in the fjord and visiting a Chilean family. Impressive landscape and good organization. One of my third best adventures in Chile.
title: Sea Kayak in North Patagonia

review_text: Very very nice tour! I went alone and met some very nice people who kept me company. Antonio was our guide, a person eager to tell you everything he knows about Chile, which made the tour very interesting. Valparaíso with its art really surprises, and the cups at the end make the closure spectacular:) Review of: Santiago: Viña del Mar, Valparaiso & Casablanca Valley Tour
title: Excellent tour! Even if you travel alone

review_text: Awesome trip, cool temple, great wine! Alejandro, Franscico, and Valentina freaking crushed it! I would do this trip again Review of: From Santiago: Bahai Temple and Cousiño Macul Vineyard Thank you very much for your comment Viajero Turistik, we are glad that you enjoyed your stay with us.
title: Awesome, yummy, and much love

review_text: This museum is a gem. The house itself is interesting, and the art is varied and tasteful, including European and Chilean artists. I especially liked the landscapes. Better paintings here than in any of the Santiago museums. Takes about an hour to go through. Highly recommended.
title: Pleasant surprise - interesting house, loved the art

review_text: Incredible architecture, the country's history is impressive, easy access for tourists, many mobility options around the city Review of: Cable Car, Funicular and Sightseeing Bus in Santiago one day Prezado viajante, ficamos felizes em saber que teve uma boa experiência durante sua viagem e que gostou da arquitetura de nossa cidade de Santiago. Esperamos ansiosamente por sua próxima visita!
title: Very good tour, passes by all the tourist attractions

review_text: We took the trip to Valle Nevado, with the intention of skiing. The place is beautiful, the day was incredible. However, we were extremely uncomfortable with the guide Cecília and the driver (who now I don't remember his name). She showed impatience during the trip. He didn't give us time for coffee, he rushed us too much to rent clothes and accessories. He incessantly demanded compliance with schedules with the justification that "if they stuck to the schedule, we had to do it too" (now look at that!). On the way back we didn't even have time to take off our ski boots, I had to change while the car was moving. This is all combined with the fact that she is very unfriendly and uninformative about the tour itself. Anyway, I hope you don't run into any professionals like that on your next trips. The following week I rented a car (since the road was free of ice) and we went skiing all day without any discomfort.
title: Valle Nevado - Ski day

review_text: We have been doing all our tours in Atacama with Araya. The entire team that served us, drivers (Georgia, Luis, Robinson and Cláudio) and guides (Anita, Valentina, Marcelo Max and Francisco) were prepared and kind, knowledgeable about the region in detail. Excellent breakfast, lunch and picnics included. We definitely recommend Araya for a premium experience in Atacama.
title: Top Team

review_text: The wind blew, I got soaked on the transfer to the main boat (50-seater), the captain reserved the right to turn round as the waves rose above the windows... and then the sun came out, the wind died, my trousers dried in the breeze and we had a great time! Dramatic scenery as you visit different types glacial flow at three points in the same glacier. Leave a half-day for the whole trip to the boat, the boat trip (ca. 1 hr?), sight-seeing, return, disembarking, and trip back to our hotel. But well worth it.
title: Worth the visit

review_text: Another most enjoyable and humbling tour of Santiago.A must for any visitor.everything was well organised and reasonably priced.The Lady herself was an amazing sight from the city,to be at her feet was awesome.
title: San Cristobal Hill

review_text: This part of the city is good if you are looking for food or bars. The place has people till late at night and is generally safe
title: Good part of the city to check out bars and food

review_text: We loved our tour! We got a really great feel for the city and Natalia's insights made it extra special and personal. Would highly recommend to get a sense of the city, see the key sights and learn about the history of Santiago and Chile. Hi Mattie W, Natalia is an absolute artist in her craft. She is so full of energy and positivity, but at the same time so insightful and knowledgeable. I'm glad you felt the tour was so personal. It's never fun to just have someone spit facts at you, and that's why we try to make our tours more engaging. Thanks so much for taking the time to leave a review, and I really appreciate the incredible vibes. Safe travels, Peter
title: A wonderful tour that introduces you to the history and culture of Santiago

review_text: Tours with vans and animated guides and with great knowledge. We participated with Lolo, João and Rodolfo, the Pablo also that although the driver to the thermas showed the differential of the agency, the roupão of the agency to go to the thermas and lagoons cease, was essential. Review of: Half Day Tour to Geysers del Tatio
title: Lively and knowledgeable tours

review_text: You need to be there early to get the effect of the steam rising at sunrise. Spectacular. Plus the colors are diverse and amazing. We choose to skip the dip in the pool as it was quite chilly. The drive was nice too. The countryside has wildlife and lovely vistas
title: Worth getting up early

review_text: We visited at opening time on a Sunday, and the house was quite and pleasant to still around. It is not easy to find, although just a short walk from the funicular there are limited sings and the building itself is not obvious. Google maps helps.
title: Go early

review_text: We took a boat trip up the Chepu river with Fernando to try to see the southern river otter. We were lucky enough to get a view of one. He was very friendly and stayed close to the boat for a while. You are very lucky to get to see one of them. After we ate at their restaurant. It was very good and Fernando's wife was very friendly
title: Saw the southern river otter with Fernando

review_text: A fabulous day out with Francesco and Andreas! My only issue was my altitude issues I developed. The guides, particularly Andreas, split and made a seperate part of the day to accommodate myself and my companion. I felt much better when we stopped ascending. Definitely be aware of the altitude! Review of: Andes Day Volcano 8K - Cajón del Maipo

review_text: View of the valley is superb. Just stoped for a tasting ... Chardonnay of honey and cab full of fruit
title: Worth the view and the vine

review_text: the changing colors on the rocks and mountains in the back when the sun is setting is amazing! It is an easy trip; close to San Pedro de Atacama. You can also go by bike (but some steep hills) or by horse.
title: stunning

review_text: If you want to appreciate democracy and the resilience of the Chilean people, this museum depicts the 1973 Coup, it's aftermath, the eventual resistance that led to Pinochet's downfall and a return to democracy. I gave 4 stars instead of 5 because the English recording device that guides you through the museum is hard to follow...but you really don't need to follow the audio tour exactly in order to understand the events....so go and experience!

review_text: Close to the city (inside), you can reach by underground and a short inexpensive taxi ride. This high volume producer of wine, which I believe any wine aficionado has tasted. It is the disneyland of wines. Buy your tickets folk's type. If you like that, you will enjoy. I prefered to go directly to the restaurant and make a tasting of Don Melchor 1990 and Don Melchor 2012. Was a great experience. Their top Schyraz "Grava" is also a must drink. A lot of people love Almaviva, made jointly with Rothschild , still I preferred the already mentioned ones. They do have vines of every varietal walking distance from the main house and in season you can taste and compare the grape tastes of all types.

review_text: this is a very small vineyard that produces a premium syrah. the owner, maria luisa, is charming as well as an excellent hostess, who gave us a tour of the installations. this is a must stop in the valle del elqui
title: an exquisite boutique vineyard

review_text: We were very well received by the Turistik staff. Everyone was well educated and very attentive, especially Jenifer, Manuel and Jorge, who accompanied us. Notal thousand! Not to mention the tour itself, which is wonderful. We also had a tasty lunch. I highly recommend it!!! Review of: Portillo and Laguna del Inca Tour Agradecemos seu tempo para nos deixar seu comentário, ficamos felizes que tenha gostado de seu passeio com nossa equipe, esperamos tê-lo de volta em breve, um abraço a Turistik.

review_text: An amazing experience, full of learning and beautiful scenery. Bethlehem made sure it was unforgettable, along with Juan Carlos. Everything excellent!! Mirmar&Ignacio <3 Review of: Red Stones and Altiplanic Lagoons

review_text: The tour of the vineyards is amazing. Alex and Pablo guaranteed the fun and were super friendly! In addition, we were very well received by the teams of La Quirinca, Sta Ema and Undurraga. Review of: Maipo Valley Wine Tour with 4 vineyards from Santiago. title: Wine Tour - Isla de Maipo

review_text: Benjamin de guide was great, he was enthusiastic, knowledgable and very informative. The tour was nice, driver was very skillful and kind. The group size was perfect, I love everything. Thanks Benjamin! Review of: Inca Lagoon in Andes Mountain Range - Visit Local Vineyard with Tasting included
title: Benjamin de guide 🫡

review_text: The Moneda is the presidential palace in Santiago. It is an imposing, well-maintained building, definitely worth a visit among the key historical sites downtown. Mostly, you can just walk around the building, but there also are interesting exhibits in a subterranean gallery on the Southeast corner of the building. This is the building that was shelled and bombed during the military coup against President Allende in 1973, and from which Allende and his staff fired at tanks from balconies before he committed suicide rather than be taken alive.
title: Presidential Palace worth a brief visit for its history

review_text: The history of the churches in the Castro area is fascinating and it is wonderful that they have been rebuilt as needed yet preserving colors and materials like the originals. The Ruta of the Chuches offers several of the UNESCO preserved buildings and we thought the church on the Rilan Peninsula the most beautiful and the trip on the Rilan Peninsula one of the prettiest drives in the area.
title: FASCINATING ROUTE OF THE CHURCHES.

review_text: We made the Day Trip to Maipo Valley & El Yeso Reservoir. I can only say the best. The tour guides were flexible and nice and it was a lot of fun and a great day. We could go out of town in the Andes, see the scenery, walk a little,had a lovely picnic. Hi Jutta and Heinz! Thank you so much for taking the time to review us here! It was great to have you on our Day Trip to Maipo Valley and El Yeso Reservoir! Looking forward to seeing you again in Chile or Austria! Best wishes! Jenni & Pato

review_text: The favourite part of my experience was the passion Jorge has for astronomy and how he shared that with us. Anyone could point us towards the sky and show us the stars, but Jorge provided an experience I will remember for the rest of my life. On top of that, his home observatory is literally out of this world. He had so many high-powered telescopes that we used to look deep into the universe, at least 7 or 8 different ones. He spent lots of time educating us so we knew what we were looking at. And during our break, he provided us with a very thoughtfully put-together drink and snack selection. An amazing experience. Definitely one of the highlights of my journey to Chile.
title: Atacama Desert Stargazing

review_text: I visited for the first time this austral winter. I was looking to rent bikes to go across the park and even outside, for instance to the San Cristobal hill which is just besides and along the park. I could not find any place to rent it. I think in some more years when the trees will be bigger this park will get more "charm" ; for the moment its looks too new
title: Nice area helpful to contrast with the army of buildings in this part of santiago

review_text: Excellent crossing. Easy and simple trekking, but the best the Richard Guide, very friendly, friendly and very concerned about the group. Review of: Trekking trhough Lagos Andinos Trail Muchas gracias por tu comentario, Lagos Andinos es un trekking familiar y que se disfruta mucho debido a su dificultad fácil, saludos.

review_text: I highly recommend a professional team, quality equipment in good condition, my personal experience is very good, I really enjoyed not giving up the climb to the volcano, one of the things I had to do. Thank you Tal! We're so happy you didn't give up!

My sister and I had a 2-day pass that included a one-hour city walk with Eduardo - there were only 3 of us on the walking tour so we had lots of time to ask him questions and learn lots about the history of the buildings in old part of the city, as well as the social and political history over the centuries and more especially in the past 50 years. If you can, taking a 2-day pass is best as allows more time to stop off and visit the Sculpture Park, one of the big shopping centres as well as do the cable car ride and other areas of the city at a leisurely pace. Review of: Tourist bus around Santiago for a day Delighted to read you Gwen H and discover that you have enjoyed incredibly with your sister and our partner Eduardo, the walking tour we offer through the Hop On Hop Off Premium service. Thank you for taking the time to comment and comment on your memorable memories with us. We hope to have you back very soon. Regards!

review_text: What a perfect tour! It was definitely a highlight. The boat ride on Lake Todos Los Santos was spectacular, as were the Petrohue Rapids....and everything in Vicente Perez Rosales National Park. You see the Osorno Volcano from many different vantage points. Loved every part of this tour. Review of: Cruise Passenger: Tour Petrohue Falls, Todos los Santos Lake and Osorno Volcano Thanks! Glad you enjoyed the tour with us. It was a short time, but a wonderful one! Nice to meet you!

review_text: Santiago is full of high-end malls like Alto Las Condes, Parque Arauco, Costanera Center and some others, Buenaventura Premium Outlet is definitely a different option. Is far from the city, around 30 mins by car and worth the visit only if you spend a decent amount of money, otherwise buy in the regular malls that have also good prices... I go to Buenaventura every time I get a Car in Santiago. This time we spent the whole day!. We will probably return before we leave Santiago!.

The team has an amazing knowledge about the area mixed with a great passion to tell the stories and is ready to answer any questions on top of providing all the information without hesitation. review_text: Wonderful afternoon and evening. The sunset was spectacular over the Andes and the experience of the drive with the hairpin bends to reach Valle Nevada was quite something. Review of: Tour Panoramico Farellones & Valle Nevado

review_text: Super interesting visit, with a good level of detail and good description of the wines. Excellent harmonization and lots of learning. Highlight for the guides - Éric and Daniela are always helpful and have a lot of knowledge to share

review_text: Very easy to navigate yourself around and colour coded to make it even easier. You need to buy a prepaid card/ticket which you load with a certain amount of money. The same card can be used by more than one person. Prices are ridiculously cheap by European standards. Each time you use it, the entrance gate screen tells you your remaining balance. Like any city in the world take care of your valuables when busy.

review_text: The Sophi guide was very good and friendly. Apart from that the rest is not recommended at all, in Valparaiso there is nothing to do, just see empty streets, with low lighting, murals with worn paintings and dirty streets. In the middle of the tour two policemen approached to tell us to be careful on the streets. 10 hours tour is too excessive to go to Valparaiso as there is really NOTHING TO DO or see, just old and unpainted buildings. You walk, you walk and you walk and you don't see anything interesting. I DO NOT RECOMMEND THE TOUR. If you plan to go, first check the weather as it clouds very easily. review_text: The best experience The relaxation was the best and we came with the recharged batteries will always be our intention to return

review_text: Went with my 2 years old and my parents. We booked by e-mail and it's easy to get there by any transport means and it's in the heart of Santiago. The garden was beautiful and the wine tasting refreshing. Andrea, the guide, was lovely, knows a lot about the wine history and answered all our questions. Definitely, a place to visit when you're in Santiago!

review_text: I had a great experience with Sousas tour on a tour of the Undurraga winery. Easy communication via WhatsApp and punctual service.

review_text: The metro is clean, fast, and frequent. The best way to get around Santiago, as street traffic is often snarled.

review_text: Very beautiful winery, set in the Maipu valley. Worth the short hour long tour. You learn about how the wines are made and what separates a premium wine from a common wine. The tasting was well too but it could have been a tad more descriptive about the history of wine, about the legs the wine leaves in the glass (they mention/reference it but expect you to already know about it), and the importance of a cork (like why it is handed to you when you get a bottle). Only setback of the whole place is that they will not ship a case of wine for you as most wineries in SouthAmerica will do. Normally you can have a case or two shipped internationally for a very small fee as the wineries already distribute their product. Overall a great experience.

The tour guide was Vanessa and she was excellent. It starts by the subway station in the Catholic University of Chile and ends in Plaza de Armas. It usually takes 3-4h, depending on questions. We walk about 4 km, nice and slowly, with lots of places to sit while she explains the sites. Very recommended! Hello! Thank you so much for taking the time to leave a review, we appreciate your feedback and love to hear from you. We are happy to hear you enjoyed the tour of Santiago with Vanesa and we will be waiting for you to come join us for more amazing Strawberry Tours!

review_text: Well, I am a volcano apassionata - I find ways within my budget (and often on the sidelines of a work trip) to get to volcanoes and climb them - the more active, the better. So I have been to volcanoes in Java, Costa Rica, Tanzania, Montserrat, Greece and Italy and loved every one of them. But Villarrica is a thrilling volcano because it's normally covered with snow. That makes it easier to climb (ironically, since you can contour-zigzag) and quicker to get down (since you can toboggan!). Sol y Nieve is a wonderful adventure-sports company in Pucon with seasoned in-house and freelance guides, and a lovely, extremely helpful and bilingual front-desk lady in Bernardita Reyes. At first, one might think that they are a little casual about safety and equipment, but I realized that they are extremely wise, friendly, and sensitive to the mountain, and they don't baby their clients. I loved every moment of this thrilling adventure. Watch it on You Tube or Vimeo (not my videos - Google "climbing volcan Villarrica" or similar) and contact Sol y Nieve. They may not be the cheapest in town, but they have solid credentials and history behind them, and they are far easier for non-Spanish-speaking international clients like me to use. Gracias! Thank you SO much for your wonderful review! We really appreciate the time you have taken to post this write up and are super happy to hear that you had a great and memorable experience with Sol y Nieve! We do hope one day you will return to Pucón to summit Villarrica again and we wish you the best for your next volcano adventure, wherever that may be!
title: Best volcano adventure ever!

review_text: Not a great summer destination - though a great place to stop off for a meal if you're on your way to Argentina or Chile through the border. The restaurant serves very good food, despite how modest the restaurant area looks and feels. The view of the lake is beautiful, but the surroundings are barren in the summer and there is nothing else to do there, no lifts are running, and no hiking that we saw. Dear Genevieve K.: Thank you for your review! We would very much love to welcoming you for the winter season...a totally different experience! review_text: Leonardo was an excellent tour guide and Renato was a great driver for this early morning trip to Cajon de Maipo. review_text: I think it is a recommended place for those who are interested in history. It's great that he was able to make the day both interesting and fun for you. We appreciate your kind words and hope to welcome you again for more memorable experiences! Patricio
title: Great tour with Mauricio

review_text: for less than $.50 you can chill in one of these old school trolley buses. I love the romance of just sitting in them. Also gets you from one side to the other of this lovely city-- the non hilly part, that is.
title: old world ecological transportation

review_text: We had a great night finding out about the stars, looking at the sky with the naked eye and finally looking through telescopes. A highlight was definitely seeing Saturn! Rodrigo was really nice and knew absolutely everything about the night sky! Lovely drinks and snacks too. Just a note that we didn’t get back to our hostel until nearly 2am, so best to avoid an early trip the next morning.
title: Great experience!

review_text: We just turned up on the day and a very nice lady gave us a selection of their wines to taste. We chose 4 including their own grape Cab Franco. Very generous measures at a fine price. Walked in from Santa Cruz.
title: Wine tasting

review_text: Enjoyed this all day tour to the seaside. The hotel pickups were a bit of a process as a small bus picks you up as well as other guests and then drops you at the main building where you wait while people go in to pay. After that you get on the coach bus which was comfortable. The tour guide tried very hard to ensure that everyone was well informed and happy. The first stop was a picturesque winery where you could do tastings. The lunch stop was very good with delicious seafood and a lovely view of the ocean. Enjoyed the harbour boat tour, and the walking tour of the murals. Hotel drop offs went quickly. Good value for the money. Review of: Viña del Mar and Valparaíso Thanks a lot for spread the word... The Turistour team works hard to provide a unique experience in the beautiful cities of Viña del Mar and Valparaíso, and we really appreciate your comments Hasta la vista! Turistour team !
title: Great Tour

review_text: Lovely place, interesting to meet, enjoy a coffee! For shopping the values are slightly higher, as it has a more artisanal character. Super easy to get from Metro, which is the last stop of the red line.
title: Meeting the Fair Los Dominicos

review_text: Everything excellent!!! It was our first massage experience and we were fascinated✨ thank you very much! We hope to return
title: Marvelous

review_text: The trip was more than we expected, we loved everything from the scenery to the staff who took us everywhere, special thanks to Andrea who went out of her way and made everything great for our family, we want to come back!!! Review of: Uyuni Salt flat fron San Pedro de Atacama, (In Hostels)
title: Beautiful trip for a family

review_text: Glad we fitted in this feature but the views were less impressive than we expected because of the ubiquitous haze across the city
title: OK but views were obscured by haze

review_text: The tour takes about 40 minutes. They have a very good gift shop. It is pricy compared to other museum in Santiago who are either free of very cheap.
title: A bit Pricy but worth it if you are a fan of Neruda

review_text: After a large lunch in the Mercado Central ( Seafood market), we walked through town ( Paseo Ahumada) to La Alameda and then town to Cerro Santa Lucia. We entered through the main entrance of fountains and terraces before hiking up the eastern side of the cobbled road. We then found pathways that acted as switchbacks of sorts so we can get to the original fort walls and the top of the hill. Along the way, we had the first of many healthy street dogs follow us up. Also viewed the chapel and the Japanese gardens before descending along the western side of the hill and reaching the Cerro Santa Lucia metro station .
title: Serene Hike up Fortress Hill in Heart of Santiago

review_text: Even when greatly damaged by the big earthquake of 2010, it has been partially repaired and recovered today as a living museum for public visits. Original belongings (fortunately not damaged by the earthquake) from President Federico Errázuriz's family are intact and can be seen during the guided visit. A beatiful church is also part of the estate. To visit El Huique is like travelling to the past. Highly recommended!
title: Old farmhouse from the end of nineteenth century, originally belonging to the Errázuriz family.

review_text: Responsible company, punctual, polite, friendly drivers, answered all my questions, I highly recommend them.
title: Travel to Chile

review_text: This is a great attraction for a city. Its free, not a long walk up and youre surrounded by beauty. Take your time walking up. Great views of the city when you reach the top.
title: Beautiful!

review_text: Very nice Guide Isidora, explained everything we asked, told stories of local culture and gave tips. It was very clear in the instructions. The driver was great, he drove well, stable. Very good.
title: Cool tour and great guides!

review_text: We go up in this cable cabins really cool, and with great view during the hole time, up is an amazing space to walk around, see the city, all the Holy Mary sanctuary is beautiful and very interesting seeing all the letters and promises people have left there. My recommendation is to check up the weather before you go up, as the city has so much contamination if is a bad day you won't be see any far. But with a clear day the view is amazing.
title: Amazing view

review_text: The driver offered factual knowledge and shared cultural legends. He was considerate while driving and did not speed. The road leading to the lagoon was a surprise, and the views at the destination were unparalleled. It was a true adventure. Emanuel gave us a day we will never forget.
title: Excellent Tour to Cajon del Maipo

review_text: We had a brilliant time on this tour - we took the 3 day expedition from San Pedro de Atacama to the Bolivian salt flats. Our tour guide, Marcello, was amazing - he explained everything in detail in both Spanish and English, and encouraged questions at all times. He took good care of us, always offered to take photos and always checked we were having a good time! He also taught us about some key Inca facts and about Bolivian culture. The sites we saw en route in a 4x4 to the salt flats were spectacular - there were many amazing landscapes and animals (e.g. llama, alpaca etc) to see along the way - the photos do not do justice to the pure beauty of Bolivia & its lands, rich with natural resources. We would highly recommend this company as the memories we have taken away are unforgettable! Thank you!
title: Excellent tour, highly recommended

review_text: The tour was ok, but I was expecting a longer cycling time. Right at the beggining of the tour we already stopped for almost 30min to have ice cream... and all the stops took too long. The tour took 3 hours but could easily be made in less than 2 hours. Additionally, I was very unsatisfied to see that I paid a higher price for the service at the site, when compared to the balcony price (CLP 24.000 against CLP 18.000). All in all, the guide was friendly and gave us a good overview on the visited parks and neighboring buildings. Dear Tiagodorn, on behalf of the green team, we apologize for the lack luster and long tour experience you had with us. We agree that 30 minutes is too long for ice cream no matter how yummy it is. We have already addressed this issue and if you give us another chance, I am sure you will think it is faster. All the tours we do should be great and you should expect no less, so send me an email peter@labicicletaverde.com and I will make sure you are given a discount based on what you think is fair and reasonable. Sincerely, Peter
title: It was ok... I expected more riding!

review_text: Beautiful beach, very quiet. Family, to sleep and rest. Very clean. There is a parking space, but it fills up. It is better to walk or leave the vehicle on streets, in front. The entire city is very quiet and clean. We felt very safe and we walked a lot.
title: Excellent experience in Iquique

review_text: Terrible service at Café La Panadería, Museo Andino and Villa Santa Rita. There is no doubt that they prefer to serve foreigners, I waited a long time and then they answered me in a terrible tone, what do you want? bad experience. I am an art appraiser and I came for work. In addition, they left me locked in the museum and the guard responded that they always left people locked in if they didn't listen... incredible. The museum exhibit is excellent and the place is great. But next time, I will speak in French so they can serve me better. Estimada Carolina, Lamentamos que su visita no haya cumplido sus expectativas, revisaremos en detalle sus comentarios para poder mejorar la experiencia. Esperamos poder recibirlo nuevamente! nos podría comentar el día que realizo sus actividades para ver la forma de que esto no vuelva a pasar.
title: Staff poorly trained for all care

review_text: Give yourself plenty of time to see as much as you can of this park, which has a variety of things to see. It's also good exercise.
title: Wonderful city park

review_text: Guide francisca toppp💖💖💖 was a very pleasant informative and quality tour, we loved the experience would return. Review of: Cable Car, Funicular and Sightseeing Bus in Santiago one day Muchas gracias por sus comentarios.
title: Tour Santiago

review_text: It's just few blocks, a good ice cream shop, I bought a cool ring from an artesano at a fair price, had a Turkish desert shop with a yummy baklava. There re some cafe and restaurants but we didn't find a cool place to sit and have some coffee
title: It's small

review_text: It's a huge park! Inside it many museums and attractions. A good budget option to tour and walk in Santiago.
title: Park with many attractions

review_text: We already experienced free tours in 3 cities: Prague, Buenos aires and Santiago. Franco, our English speaking guide was perfect. he was very knowledgeable and open to all kinds of questions and requests for help about Santiago. He is very experienced in using the time very efficiently; he balances information and entertainment very well. He puts all his energy to his work. we have seen 3 barrios of Santiago in about 4 hours and we learnt about history of Chile, history of Santiago and Chilian culture. Thanks Franco.
title: Perfect experience

review_text: Easy minivan ride from santiago with a guide who spoke perfect English and was a great host. Great way to start our trip in Chile The 3 wineries were varied and all amazing. The lunch was absolutely spectacular. Treat yourself, your taste buds and do this tour.
title: Incredible casablanca wine tour

review_text: When in the CasaBlanca region this is THE MUST visit winery. The range breath and depth of wines are nothing short of stunning. The fact it is organic is a fully added bonus. If you are unfamiliar with organic wine practices, take the tour as it is fully explained. Do the winetasting. Add the chocolate that go along. Add the 5th cup. Add a designated driver so everyone can fully enjoy the wines.
title: Take the tour and the tasting and add the chocolate with the tasting

review_text: Very good tour. The guide Mr. Daniel Guerrero is very attentive and explained well about the historical points we passed. .
title: Tour to Val Paraíso and Vinã del Mar.

review_text: A very nice area to walk around in and just breathe the atmosphere of Santiago. After you have strolled around for a while the perfect stop is lunch at the Bocanariz
title: A perfect (late) morning

review_text: We went without booking which was no problem. Decided to have the 6 course tasting menu. We don’t eat meat and were easily accommodated. Our waiter Ignacio was amazing as was the sommelier. The food was brilliant and the wine excellent I’m not a red wine drinker but the Pinot noir was lovely. We had got a Uber to the restaurant but they don’t collect. We had no cash for a taxi but Ignacio sorted it all out beautifully we we very grateful to him. It’s a great experience a lovely environment if you are near give it a shot.
title: Amazing wine tasting menu and staff

review_text: We spent out first day in Chile here, what a treat! The grounds are absolutely stunning. We took the wine tour and did the wine tasting. The guides were all knowledgable and made the experience fun for everyone. We had lunch on the patio and were very please with our meals. Highly recommend a trip out to this winery!
title: Beautiful atmosphere, great wine!

review_text: The historic building of "La Moneda" the Chilean presidential palace is a nice place to visit, but not much to see except the nice surroundings. Below this building there is an underground museum and convention center which sometimes has interesting exhibitions. There also is a cafeteria and a handcraft shop, worth visiting,
title: Not much to see

review_text: We met 2Govan, through our blog Nos in Chile, and what made us choose for sure was their service. From the time of the budgets, Pamella our consultant, responded promptly and removing all doubts. With our arrival in Chile, it was no different, besides all the instructions well passed, Pamella still gave us tour tips that were fundamental to our trip. During the tours, what stood out was the punctuality and education of everyone. The super friendly and attentive guides, and polite and very prudent drivers. On all the tours, we were one of the first to arrive which helped us a lot on high season travel, it was perfect! Surely, I highly indicate the agency and at a next opportunity, we will be back!
title: Unique experience!

review_text: We did the climb in January 2020, Diego and Juan (and the girl whose we unfortunatly don't remember the name, sorry!) were great, really friendly and answered all our questions. It was small groups (about 1 guide for 2 people) which is very nice. The descent was amazing ! Gracias por todo :)
title: Great experience

review_text: I went on the red stones and highland lagoons tour. A super complete tour, with an excellent driver and guide! With a good disposition, kind, happy and with a lot of knowledge. The previous treatment at the agency was just as good. They explain very well what the tour consists of.
title: Excellent tour, very complete. You see variety of landscapes and biodiversity

review_text: It is a place of a lot of peace and good energy, even not practicing a religion, we greatly ⁇ the visit. There are guides and directions on site, everything well explained, all very kind. Seeing Santiago from above is very beautiful and the building of the tb temple is wonderful.
title: Peace and meditation

review_text: I had a great time wandering the markets and cooking with Ines! I happened to be the only person on the tour which can sometimes be awkward, but this was not an issue with Ines; she was an incredible guide/instructor! We toured the markets to purchase a random assortment of local products, then spent quality time in the kitchen creating (and devouring) tasty Chilean dishes. Great experience!
title: Super Personalized Experience (Cooking w/Ines)

review_text: We have been here some 4 or more years in a row and were never able to enter, being closed. Today we were lucky and entered from the side door, crossing the courtyard we noticed repairs on the yard. The exterior of the Church shows it’s signs of ageing but the interior revealed a space of beauty and tranquility.. all in such a touristic area of Chile. The cathedral ceilings and icons are gorgeous. We felt privileged to share this space.
title: At Last we could Enter ... a Beautiful Must See in PElqui.

review_text: Maria served us very well. Thanks. Long live Chile We really liked the bus, excellent tour, we will be back soon. We love the city of Santiago, very hospitable. Review of: Cable Car, Funicular and Sightseeing Bus in Santiago two days Prezado viajante, ficamos felizes em saber que você teve uma boa experiência durante sua viagem, muito obrigado por compartilhar sua opinião conosco. Esperamos ansiosamente por sua próxima visita!
title: Very good

review_text: We went scuba diving here back in April for this year. It was great experience, we did the ship wreck in Quintay Bay. The only downfall we had was the water was EXTREMELY cold, no fault of anyone as we were told it was going to be cold. After the ship wreck we went to the kelp forest and that was pretty good as well. Got me over my fear of seaweeds. It all followed by a much needed hot shower at the facility and lunch at the near by restaurant. We had hotel pick up and drop off and it was great customer service. We are very happy you enjoyed your dives, thank you very much for your review... :D
title: Great Dive

review_text: Nacho was absolutely a delight to guide this tour. He is very knowledgeable, spoke fluent English (bonus) and very interactive with his group. He is polite, patient & witty. Thank you Nacho & Sebastian the driver who drove us safely. Review of: Valparaiso Port and Vina del Mar Full-Day Tour from Santiago We're glad you had an overall great time with our guide and driver. Thank you for your review.
title: Valparaiso Port and Vina del Mar Full-Day Tour from Santiago

review_text: Excellent service and unforgettable tour. We went with Souza to get to know the wines of the Colchagua Valley (vinicula Montes and Viu Manent) wonderful for example. Our driver Denis was sensational, extremely comfortable vehicles with 7 seats with individual Basques, who did not even notice the distance. Super punctual ride, very comfortable and safe. Unforgettable
title: A lot of comfort and safety to visit Top Vineyards!

review_text: Delayed and incomplete Lynn Tour guide Johnny was very patient and kind to show me the places contemplated in the itinerary, but there was no travel kit as promised by the program I paid for. In addition, the operator did not receive communication of my reservation from Viator or did so in time, so the tour was postponed for three days. If I couldn't have stayed in the city I visited, I would have had to cancel the contracted service.
title: Delayed and incomplete

review_text: When viewed in the morning light, Lago Pehoe is so turquoise blue you would not believe it. It's easy to combine a trip to Lago Pehoe with a visit to Salto Grande. Turquoise blue in the morning, it is a darker shade of blue in the afternoon when viewed from the western end with the Torres as a backdrop
title: A turquoise blue delight

review_text: We loved the tour and the Guide Alexis is amazing, sympathetic, attentive and speaks a great Portuguese!! Super recommend !! I think this walk is the most beautiful.
title: Beautiful walk

review_text: We booked several tours with Patgonia Shore. The guides were all very good except one. At every port, the guides mebs at the port at the correct t ime. Jaime Liebrecht was always quick to resond to all message. Review of: Full-Day Tour to Petrohue Falls Through the Lake District , Chile thanks for your preference, it was a pleasure
title: Shore Excursionsin Chile and Argentina

review_text: This memorial park is a great opportunity to see some of Chile's history firsthand. The audio guide is available in English and is very good. It is a little bit outside of the city but we took a taxi there and back for about 6000 pesos from las condes. Entrance to the park and the audio guides are both free.
title: Great site to learn chile's histriy

review_text: The landscape is sensational, as is the Guide Yuri!!!! He has a wonderful astral! You know a lot about the history of Chile! We learned much with him! And we also made several laughs, besides being an excellent photographer! Yuri vc is 10!!!
title: Laguna del Inca with Yuri (Zerando Chile)

review_text: We enjoyed our tour to Valparaiso! Our tour guide, Antonio was amazing and had great knowledge of the region. Our group had both english and spanish speaking tourists and Antonio spoke in both languages. Review of: Santiago: Viña del Mar, Valparaiso & Casablanca Valley Tour
title: Amazing day trip

review_text: What a great hike - one of the toughest ones I've ever done (the gradient of the climb to the nature reserve is almost as steep as some of the hikes in our drakensberg mountains) - the gradient was hectic, but what made it so tough was the length of the climb... but once you were in the nature reserve and hiking through the restored forests, it was an incredible nature experience and even more so once I got to the Auracaria trees, and then the lakes. and the final cherry on the cake, was the final climb to the Mirador viewpoint - what a great view of the nature reserve and broader landscape from the top...
title: A tough hike, but what an amazing experience...

review_text: Deyd took care of our entire itinerary in Atacama. We stayed for 5 days and it was incredible. In addition to taking care of the itinerary, she gave several tips on where to eat, transfers and what to do. She helped us a lot, in addition to, of course, all the support she provides for Brazilians. I highly recommend it.
title: Atacama an incredible place

review_text: This is a must-see in Valparaiso. Photography is not allowed, but I think it helps you take in more of the poet's life that way. The views of the harbor from the poet's bedroom are stunning! If you're a student, bring your student ID and get a substantial discount on the price of admission.
title: Excellent look into the life of an amazing poet

review_text: Juan Victor was recommended and all of the arrangements were completed prior to our arrival in the AM in Santiago. Juan Victor picked us up at the airport and took us to our hotel for a quick shower and a nap, before covering Santiago. The following day we drove to Valparaiso, with a pre-arranged stop at an organic vineyard. Once in Valparaiso, again, a quick shower and the best empanas ever. Dinner that evening with Juan Victor and his mother at one of the local seafood restaurants. A wonderful couple of days with the best tour guide in Chile. Dear MDiamant, Thank you for having chosen Perro Tour to be part of your South American experience! Personally, it was a real pleasure to explore Santiago and Valparaíso with both of you. I'm happy to be sure that you tried the best fish and seafood in Valparaíso, all with one of the nicest views of the city. Regards from Valparaíso
title: Juan Victor/Perro Tour is the best way to see Santiago and Valparaiso

review_text: After Christmas shopping we went to the Mall, it is huge, clean, modern, with a great feeling of security inside and around, we sat in a little cafe on the boulevard and we were happy, a 7 all around.
title: High level

review_text: Very nice and interesting tour. Daniela was very attentive to my family. When I return to Santiago, I will definitely take the tour again. Review of: Cable Car, Funicular and Sightseeing Bus in Santiago one day Agradecemos o tempo que dedicou para nos contar sobre sua experiência.
title: Great family experience

review_text: I found this trip to be poor value. A stop after 30 minutes at a restaurant and then onto Valparaiso. The countryside is nothing to get excited about. Valparaiso's has some charm with its hilly outlook and uniquely coloured houses. There was smog/fog hanging over the city which didn't help. Our stop at the Noble Laureates house was short and we didn't go inside. Other than a short uninteresting street walk that was it. I paid $50usd for lunch something I don't normally do and I wasn't happy with the choices nor the service. My advice would be pay as you go as it probably won't come to 50 bucks. We drove through the seaside city which is a modern city you would find anywhere by the sea. The trip was advertised to finish at 1900 but I was happily dropped off at 1730. This tour reminded me why I travel individually and don't use tours. Not worth it at all!
title: Day Trip to Valparaiso

review_text: Excellent tour! We loved our tour to Valpariso and Vin del Mar with Alexis (the great) tour guide and Jimmy (Hendrix) our driver. We appreciated Alexis’ enthusiasm & knowledge of this area and he did a superb job of entertaining us the entire trip. The walking tour through Valpariso was excellent, we loved the history of this area. A “MUST DO” trip! Review of: Valparaiso Port and Vina del Mar Full-Day Tour from Santiago
title: A “MUST DO” trip!

review_text: We went to Portillo (Salvador guide is great) and to the Aylan winery. It was an incredible experience with beautiful landscapes.
title: Sensational tour

review_text: Concluded!!!! 3 hours of walking, 2:30 to climb and 30 minutes to descend. 50 minutes enjoying the view of Bolivia 🇧🇴 and Salar de Atacama 🏜️. And you can see Argentina 🇦🇷 too. Sensational!!! Have patience and a little physical preparation. Don't challenge your limits. Every photo was worth the effort of this trek. I highly recommend it!!! A good guide is essential for driving. Review of: Ascent Cerro Toco
title: Climb and spectacular view!!!

review_text: An unmissable opportunity to discover a stunning natural treasure, with dedicated and conscientious hosts. I recommend it as top of the list for anyone with an interest in nature, bird-watching or looking for natural beauty.
title: A natural treasure with unforgettable people

review_text: The restaurants and food that you find at Patio Bellavista are overpriced. You can find a wide selection of restaurants, but the place is just for tourists, and so are their prices! Walk away a couple of blocks and you will find a wider variety and better prices.
title: Extremely tourist and overpriced

review_text: In the middle of the desertic landscape you can appreciate a green area covered with many different kinds of plantations! Its is just beautiful!!! My husband and I did a whole day tour, where we visited a Papaya plantation, a Pisco small factory, the small towns of Pisco Elqui and Montegrande, the house of the famous Gabriela Mistral and we also had a delicious lunch in a Solar restaurant! They have solar ovens and cook everything outside! The views are amazing and it is definitely worth a visit!!! You ca go with a tour or rent a car to spend the day visiting the region!
title: Beautiful views of the rural area!

review_text: it took us 9 hours round trip. we had all 4 seasons in 1 afternoon. hot and sunny, cold and rainy, always windy.....not easy, especially at the top, but a great time and very difficult....
title: Best and Hardest hike we have done.

review_text: Very beautiful views from the top of the volcano. It is well worth the hike. There is an option to take a ski lift to the top, but I would recommend hiking up. There is a restaurant/ski resort on one side of the mountain. Nice place to grab a drink or some food.
title: Worth the drive from Puerto Varas or Puerto Montt

review_text: To understand Chile, I believe it is important to come to this museum. It was very easy to get to via the great metro, and adjacent to a very lovely park. The woman at the reception desk so kind, and told me that while a lot of this was in Spanish, there were audio guides available. The events are presented in a very moving way, and the tribute wall to those missing is moving and emotional whether you understand Spanish or not. It is a lovely place, historically, spiritually, and architecturally. Everyone who visits lovely Santiago, should visit this museum.
title: Important to see

review_text: We met the chef, Francisco at the central market. We walked the entire market including the seafood market, flower market, meat market, fruit/vegetable market. Francisco was incredibly informative and accommodating. Off to the kitchen, a short 10-min ride away, and it was the most dreamy kitchen I have cooked in. Beautiful buildout, accompanied by an incredible assistant Christina. On to the cooking, and it was the best cooking class food we have ever experienced. Also, helpful were the detailed take-home instructions to re-create at home. If you are in Santiago and interested in a cooking class, look no further!!! You will love this group, location, and experience!!!
title: Best travel cooking class I have ever attended

review_text: This place is just incredibly amazing! The colors are unbelievable, especially before the sunset. We rented a car (a pick up) to go there, among many other things we could squeeze in one day and it was a really good decision. When you have to turn from the main road is not clear, but you can ask at the archaeological site on the way. Basically, when you reach a bridge, you have to take the small dirt road right before the bridge. A 4x4 is definitely required to reach the site, since you will have to cross a shallow river a few times.
title: SO AMAZING!

review_text: I loved the tour!! Excellent van, responsible, friendly and efficient driver! The guide Roxana is friendly, attentive, careful, and does an excellent job.
title: A magical place

review_text: It was sensational!! I recommend the best of all!!! Fuck! Sensational !! I highly recommend Zeroando Chile and Casa Zeroando! It's very worth it!
title: Sooooooooooooooooooooooooooooo cute

review_text: I loved the tours I made from the Trip Chile. Many lovely places!! Guides prepared and friendly, especially Joana and Danny!!
title: Divine Nature

review_text: We booked our tour that morning and it was one of our best days to date. We caught the metro out to Pirque where we were promptly collected in a mini bus and brought out to collect our bicycles. Our day was quite different from the usual wine tour and it was so much fun. Riding a bike on a very sunny day in February lead by the fabulous Ivonne and supported by Lucas brought us to vineyards and walnut trees as we toured the beautiful Maipo valley. Ivonne who clearly loves her job and is passionate in recounting the stories and history of Chilean wines made this experience so very personable and enjoyable. We thoroughly enjoyed our visit to the smaller winery where we saw in great detail the complete production process from vine to bottle and also tasted the grapes which were deliciously sweet . A really informative fun day and one of the best we have enjoyed to date! Review of: Bike and Wine Tour Half Day Maipo Valley Hi Roisin C, It's awesome that you guys had such a great experience during your Bike & Wine tour. You're right Ivonne is a great guide who loves sharing her passion for Chile and of course wine! Thank you so much for taking the time to write such a nice review. If you guys ever come back to Santiago, don't hesitate to stop by the office for recommendations or even for a chat. All the best, Peter
title: Fabulous experience .

review_text: We enjoyed the sanctuary as well as the people watching. There was a spwcial feeling here which we did mot expect.
title: Great feeling here.

review_text: A wonderful place. You breathe nature, peace and tranquility. The trails are prices. The views are beautiful. We take many pictures. The atmosphere is relaxed and family friendly. We loved it! We will return when we can.
title: A treasure in Puerto Varas

review_text: I went here in a tour and we drive up to the lake. We were able to get out and go for a walk to take some photos. However, you should be warned that Chile's highway 11 passes right next to the lake and has huge numbers of trucks that are crossing the border into Bolivia. This seriously detracted from the area and really lessened what would've been an amazing place.
title: Nice Lake but LOTS of Trucks

review_text: Wonderful experience. First time in Chile and we took this tour on the first day. Simply spectacular. As for the agency, I really liked it and recommend it. The dynamics of picking up passengers were the best I've ever seen. Our Guide Koke was very competent and attentive. Review of: Small-Group Cajón del Maipo Full-Day Tour and Picnic Obrigado por compartilhar sua experiência! Ficamos muito felizes em saber que vocês aproveitaram tanto o tour com a nossa equipe, e muito obrigado pelas lindas palavras, elas sempre são bem-vindas. Transmitiremos suas palavras ao Koke. Não hesite em nos contatar na próxima vez que vier, estaremos encantados em recebê-lo. MTO Tour Team
title: Super recommended!!

review_text: Nothing was missing. We Love (Giovanna, Laíse), the guide (Javiera) and the drivers were very helpful and met all expectations. They made the whole experience special! Muito obrigada! A gente espera vocês aqui pra uma próxima aventura. Um abraço enorme de toda a equipe WLC.
title: Very good all the service

review_text: The sign is there both in one direction and the other, it is the classic photo spot. There is good that so few cars pass by that you can stop quietly.
title: Photo spot

review_text: We were very disappointed with our day. The mini van was full of people and it was very uncomfortable. Especially on the bumpy windy roads. To drink, there were two bottles of rich Carmenère wine alongside a pitcher of pisco sour for us to share. Upon arrival, we were also greeted with several tasty cheeses, fresh bread, and dips to munch on as we prepared the rest of the food. It was easily the best meal I had during my time in the country. Second, the hosts—Patricia and her husband Enrique—were some of the most fun and warm people my girlfriend and I met have met in a long time. The two of them welcomed us into their home as if we were family. The conversation was top-tier; we shared travel stories, recipes, and more. They were engaging, friendly, and open, and it was such a treasure to hear about their life stories as we shared dinner together. Patricia has organized these traditional Chilean cooking classes for over seven years now, and her experience, as well as her passion for cooking, truly shows. I cannot recommend them highly enough. Thank you for everything! Review of: Traditional Chilean Cooking Class with a Local in Her Santiago Countryside Home

review_text: There is much history with this mountain, looking it up online Charles Darwin climbed it and found new fossils. We hiked Jan 24, 2016. Trail starts near kilometer 70 on route 9. The road was closed at 65km on route 9 with new bridge construction that is closed on weekends. This adds 5 km beach walk to the hike (doubles the distance of hike). We asked a local and heard during the week when the crews are working that the bridge and road are open past this point, but don't count on it. The condition of the new road is very poor past the new bridge and when the crews do allow cars to pass a 4x4 vehicle would be needed if you were allowed to drive all the way to the trailhead. The Tarn trail is overall very visible and easy to follow on a clear day. We found on the way up many orange flags on trees. The trail is cut right through the peatland, and then through the forest, repeating this pattern several times. Once above treeline *about 500m) the trail gets tougher to follow, and was much windier but there are still many flags. There are many trails through muddy pools and even a ravine that was full of snow we had to cross. If you don't have waterproof footwear you will be very wet from this part of the hike. Sometimes I sank in peat and mud up to my knees. There are white poles to follow and more flags on trees in the shrub and peat zone above treeline. To get to the summit peaks and above the shrub-line we needed to climb up about 30-40 meter tall snow slope. Even in January this snow persisted, but was easy to climb up and slide down. Above vegetation line (>650m) there are no markers, and no cairns marking the trail. The slope is loose scree and you need to have sight of the peaks where you are going, or in our case in the middle of an ice storm with low visibility a GPS with the route mapped. You need to be careful near the summits as it is not very clear when you are up there which of them are the real summit. There are a few places with steep crevasse between the hills and on the eastern slopes drops are >100m. After walking over the first large hill or summit, there is the 2nd peak with a trail visibly cut through the scree around the back. This trail leads to the 3rd peak which is the true summit. There is a Chilean flag on the actual summit (photo) that can be visible once you get around the second peak. Do not walk past the Chilean flag, as the drop is vertical and would be deadly. On the way back down it is much easier to get lost, as the flags are somewhat less visible. Most of the way you can follow others tracks. Once back to the beach we needed to hike the 5km back out to the cars again. All together the hike from car to summit to car was about 7 hours.

review_text: Lascar - or Laskar - is 5.600 m above sea level and, even though it's not the hardest climb around San Pedro, the effort you put into it makes reaching the crater a very special experience. My boyfriend and I booked the tour with an agency named Ivero, on Caracoles street, and loved it. We were with a group of 7 people and there were 2 guides. One of them spoke reasonable English and they were both very professional. They took our pulse and didn't let us eat much for breakfast, cause digestion takes a lot of oxygen. The price of the tour was 85.0000 pesos per person. It's not cheap, but totally worth it! The agency provides walking poles and boots if you need them. You don't have to be fit to do it, just pay attention if you are feeling headaches or too much dizziness. We had no problem and recommend it! The view from the top and the crater is incredible!

review_text: The funicular Santiago is situated in the Parque Metropolitano. It provides a steep ride from the end of Pio Nono street to the zoo and/or the top of Cerro San Cristobal. It is a very popular attraction, which results in long queues on weekends. Prices also differ depending on the day you visit: they are more expensive on weekends & holidays Adults pay 800 pesos (week) or 1000 pesos (weekend) for a single ride to the zoo; 1500 pesos (week) or 1950 pesos (weekend) for a single ride to or from the top, and 2000 pesos (week) or 2600 pesos (weekend) for a return ride to the top of the hill. My husband is 65+, so he payed 1950 pesos instead of 2600 pesos for a return ride to the top on a Saturday. We had to ask for it in Spanish though, as the price for pensioners wasn't advertised. Winter opening hours are Monday :13- 18 pm., Tuesday-Sunday and holidays : 10 am -19pm Summer opening hours are Monday : 13-20 pm., Tuesday-Sunday and holidays : 10 am-19.45 pm.(last car down) If you want to stop at the zoo you have to do so going up, because the tracks split into two at the zoo station and the car going down doesn't stop there. You can also walk up the (steep) hill to the entrance of the zoo. Be aware that the entire zoo is built on the flanks of the hilll and you have to be fit to climb from one level to the next. There are several benches to rest on along the way, though. ¡Thanks for your opinion! Take Care.

review_text: Magical Day horseback riding and kayaking in Punta Arenas, Chile with Kayak Agua Fresca What a magical day! Claudia was waiting with a sign for us in the parking lot of the port after we cleared security. She was very friendly and spoke good English. She led us to a very nice small bus that we shared with one other family. We drove about 20 minutes to a family farm, where we changed into our kayaking gear, which included pants and a jacket that goes over your clothes. They also gave us water shoes and life jackets. We then drove about 5 minutes to the beach (Strait of Magellan). Johan was our guide and he trained us on the operation of the 2 person kayaks. We kayaked for over an hour down the coast and saw dolphins jumping. Claudia was also kayaking and took family pictures for us (our two children, ages 10 and 13, were with us). After kayaking, we returned to the family farm where we ate a hearty lunch (there was also a vegetarian option). Our kids enjoyed the farm animals, including a lamb, cats and several dogs. Following lunch, the horses were waiting for us just a few steps away and we started the best trail riding experience we have ever had. The horses were calm and well mannered, though my wife said that I got the horse that I deserved (like me, he preferred snacking to walking!). They had 2 guides with the 8 of us, and we didn't just ride around a flat field. Instead, we rode for over two hours and the views were spectacular. Not only did we get to ride through meadows filled with wildflowers, we forded several streams and rivers, traversed a forest and ended up on a mountainside overlooking the Strait. The final trek took us through a stream and then onto the beach for the trip home. One of the horses on the ride had recently foaled and the baby horse (2 months old) followed alongside us on the ride. She was feisty and frisky and so much fun to watch. Every so often, she would kick her back feet in the air and gallop away, then come back close with a toss of her mane. Three of the owner's dogs came along for the walk too and we enjoyed watching them living a dog's best life, free and happy with their paws muddy and their tongues hanging to the ground. We don't know how this day could have been any better. Kudos to Claudia and Kayak Agua Fresca for the experience of a lifetime!
title: Magical Day horseback riding and kayaking in Punta Arenas, Chile with Kayak Agua Fresca

review_text: This winery was included in a tour from Santiago through Chilean Tourist Service. I had not heard of it before (I hadn't done my homework on the wineries of Chile) and I got a real surprise. My tour guide, Javier, had only been at the winery for 4 months but he was very knowledgeable and enthusiastic, and humorous as well! The winery is medium-sized and has been recognised internationally for its consistency and innovative single terroir wine styles. The short tour of the vineyard was very instructive - a plot of labelled vines of different types and a small underground viewing area so you can see the layers of the soil in which the vines are growing, including how far down the roots go. The tasting consisted of 4 wines - "Pomerape" 2012, a very nice sauvignon blanc only available at the winery, "Sibaris" 2012 carmenere, a red grape variety now only found in Chile (it died out in the Medoc in the late 19th century phylloxera outbreak) with a very nice nose and flavour, "Founder's Collection" 2009 cabernet sauvignon, which was sensational, and a late-harvest Semillon/chardonnay, which was very pleasant. You get to keep the wine tasting glass. Another aspect of the visit, which I did not expect at all, was the "museum quality" of a display of ancient and historic artefacts relating to the Mapuche indigenous people. I say museum quality not only for the actual items on display but for the way they are displayed. One of the owners has a special interest in supporting these people through the educational aspects of the displays, in and around the buildings - the landscaped gardens are small but beautiful and include wooden totem sculptures - but especially through donating money to the community from the sale of wine with their "Aliwen" label. The American wine magazine "Wine & Spirit" just voted Underraga "Winery of the Year", and I can see why. Don't miss it if you're visiting Santiago.

Couple people on our tour couldn't enjoy the hot sprint because they are not feeling well due to the high altitude. There are many geysers (>80) so it's a pleasure to walk around in the field and enjoy the scenery. After that, we can go to the hot spring in the geyser field for about an hour. He hot spring has only one section that is hot so most people are hanging out there. After the hot spring, the tour takes us to the wet land where we can see many desert animals (flamingos, birds, vicuña , llama ... Etc). Very nice and beautiful. In the village we also tried the llama skillet and that is very tasty. (A lot better than the llama we tried in the restaurant). Recommend to take a small size tour so you don't have to wake up at 4am to wait for the pick up. Our tour pick up time is 5 to 5:30am.

review_text: On my first ever visit to Santiago de Chile, I contacted Kylie to ask if she would be able to do a relaxed gourmet wine visit and lunch near Santiago. I had been traveling for 6 weeks on long distance buses from Buenos Aires to Patagonia and then back up to Santiago. I wanted a low-key lunch that would out of, but within an hour, of the city. Most importantly, I wanted to treat myself to some great Chileno food and wine! Kylie had a small lunch tour going to a gorgeous winery called Casas del Bosque about 1 hour west of Santiago de Chile (on the road to Valparaiso). Kylie took us there for a bit of wine tasting and a scrumptious 5-course lunch. Immediately the waiter arrived at our table with a lovely freshly cooked bread and the ubiquitous Chilena salsa of pebre, along with a lovely glass of Sauvignon Blanc. Many of the courses were served with some of the top wines that this bodega produces, including a delicious Sauvignon Blanc and Pinot. The wine and food pairings were fantastic. I thoroughly enjoyed every lip-smacking course... and every wine that went with it. At the end of the meal, I for one didn't really want to go on the scheduled wine tour, opting instead to sit on the lovely couches in the tranquil garden at the winery and have another class of their Gran Reserva Pinot. Kylie quickly reorganised with the winery and I had another leisurely hour in the garden before we headed back to Santiago. Kylie did a fabulous job organising a perfect day out - easy travel distance, delicious food and wine in a very low key and tranquil setting, away from the hustle-bustle of the city. I give Kylie 5 stars for great personalised service. She delivered a tour that had everything that I wanted... and more. I will definitely do another tour with Kylie when I am next back in Santiago! Thanks for your review. I know your tour was a while ago, and I'm so glad that it was still fresh in your mind by the time we were listed here on TripAdvisor. And with great photos too! I hope to see you if you're back in Chile sometime soon. Best wishes!
title: Perfect day out!

The only thing not explained is the reasons why so many voted pro Pinochet in the referendum...
title: Harrowing

We had a morning tour of city, then we're on our own to do as we please. We caught the red line train to Los Dominicos as we were advised of the Artisan Market. It was a great afternoon walking around a quaint little area full of Chilean handicrafts. It varied from jewelry, to wood, iron, paintings, to a gentleman who made beautiful guitars and other instruments. I would highly recommend the area, especially if your time is limited. A full morning or afternoon is the perfect amount of time.

This was really beautiful, had facilities, and staff were kind...it was disappointing in the same way that most things in the Atacama are - you just can't get close to it and there are tons of people. I completely understand protecting the environment and also other people wanting to do the same thing I'm doing, it just wasn't what all my research had led me to believe it would be. I pictured more or less secluded lakes I could sit next to and enjoy, but instead it's like you're being herded past a painting behind rope in a museum. Just manage your expectations accordingly, and you'll really enjoy your trip to the Atacama.

The Mountains were amazing and when we reached the top it was just unbelievable, the views were spectacular. We were in agony the next day though! Thanks so much Oli, we had such a great time. Glad you guys enjoyed your hike, the pain the next day is what tells you that you put effort in the day before. It's always a pleasure to share the mountains I know and love with others. review_text: My husband surprised me with this destination! I found out about it literally 10 minutes before our orientation meeting! I am not an agile person anymore, but they took very good care of each one of us, there was never a problem!! What an experience!! From us getting sized for our ugly gray boots (sure glad we had them!!) to the surprise BBQ on the deck (a good one, too!!) while we watched as we floated by icebergs on either side!!! Excellent!! Never a bad meal; all were excellent! Fine wines and a full bar with great views. I was also impressed by the bridge being open to all passengers for observation purposes. Very relaxed, but very able crew. Our guides were some of the best in their fields and passionate about the the wildlife we found -- literally hundreds of thousands of penguins, whales up close and personal, seals basking on icebergs just feet away!! Thank you very much for all your hard work, and for promoting the conservation of Antarctica and the rest of the world!
title: Excellent Experience of a Lifetime!

review_text: I loved the rambling layout of Neruda's home in Santiago and seeing how he and Matilde lived. The home is decorated in simple, artsy and quirky style and very much a reflection of a creative mind. The tour covers both the home and grounds and the audio guide is helpful in pointing out details and features. It's too bad photography isn't allowed as I would love to have had some graphic reminders to have at home. Not sure why it's such a taboo - there really isn't anything there that's that unusual or priceless. Heck, the Louvre lets you take photos! I was, however, a little dismayed to see all the ivy covering one of the outside walls of the home. That is not beneficial to a historic home in any regard and looks as if that ivy's been growing there a while. And since the foundation charges a rather high entry fee in benefit to the home, I hope they would use part of that for the home's upkeep. Overall, it's a short tour, pleasant and not mentally taxing. We enjoyed spending Saturday morning there.

review_text: This is Chile’s Yad Vashem, to preserve the memories of the loss of democracy in Chile from the military coup which overthrew the government of Salvador Allende, the atrocities committed by the regime of Augusto Pinochet, the desaparecidos and desaparecidas, and the hard road back to freedom. The museum is very well done, with both good English translations and a good English audio guide. There are lessons here for everyone who needs a reminder of how fragile democracy can be — and we all need that reminder.

review_text: This trip was something i havent done before in my life so it was exciting to me. People said if you did something similar before, you wouldnt find this amusing. Anyway, the tour bus came slightly later than they said they would but it was alright. The tour guide, Jorge, a thin man with curly hair, was very friendly and funny. He managed to explain everything very well switching between English and Spanish. He also let us know when you should use the toilets as there will not be any toilets from which point to which point. Before the island was a journey across the deserts, we managed to see some wildlife, cactus, deers and foxes. It was a fun thing to see. The tour towards the island with animals was great! Especially the part where the boat was moving and chasing the dolphins! It was very entertaining and eventhough it was cold, the excitement warmed all of us up! We also got to see sea lions laying lazily on the rocks, different types of birds and what they do or how to distinguish them (thanks to our knowledgeable tour guide) and penguins too! However, the penguins were a disappointment because there were only a few of them >< the tour guide said theres a season where the penguins will bring their hatchlings down and swim. Sadly the end of October wasnt the season =( anyway, we got compensated with the sightings of sea otters! The tour guide said it was a rare scene, dont know how true is that but it was fun to look at =) After the animals, we disembarked at another island where we were given an hour to explore the island. 1 hour wasnt enough to explore the entire island if you are walking around slowly and taking pictures along the way. I decided to hike up the hill to get a view of the entire island and the sea, it took me 40mins to go up, snap lots of pictures, and come back down. After that, we headed back for lunch at about 3.30pm, lunch arrived about 4pm. The portion was small, not enough for a big eater like me but the food was good. Overall a good experience! Would definitely recommend it! But i would recommend it on seasons where the penguins are with their hatchlings at the bottom of the hills, definitely not end of october.
