review_text: Going to a cemetery on vacation sounds kind of odd, but its really amazing. Take the subway to the cemetery stop and wander down to the oldest crypts. The architectural styles vary from gothic revival to neoclassical to art deco and are all unique and interesting. Several presidents are buried here as well as other cultural leaders of Chile. The cemetery remains active and you may see a funeral. Near the main gate (which is on the opposite side of the cemetery from where you enter if you come off the subway) and in the square outside it were large displays about the different groups that settled Chile. It was quiet, restful, and interesting. I think I took more pictures here than anywhere else on our trip.
title: A very neat way to spend a few hours!

review_text: The trip through the fjords is fantastic with magical landscapes all the way up until the end. Snowy, rocky, forested and steamy mountains, waterfalls, volcanoes, narrow passes… in all sorts of lightning (sunrise, sunset, at night, misty, etc.). Do not forget to look at the stars, as if the night is clear you may get to see the Milky Way, the Southern Cross and the Magellan Clouds, among others. Besides, the staff at the ship were very friendly and willing to help. Food was also good. Catching up with fellow travelers from around the world and with truck drivers from Chile was also a highlight. We were two wheelchair users, but we could not stay at the wheelchair accessible room because there was only one low bed. We stayed at a regular cabin and occupied the two lower bunk beds and NaviMag left free the accessible cabin, so that we could use the bathroom and shower. Even though, boarding and disembarking was a bit difficult with the wheelchairs (the ramp to get to the ship is steep and has anti-slipping metal bands for cars and trucks not to slip in bad weather), we could move quite freely between decks 5 and 6 (passenger decks). Some of the doors to the decks had a lower step (about 2 inches) that was easier to overcome (others were about 6 inches) and there was always someone to help if doors were shut (they are all very heavy, including cabin doors). Thus, if you can get over 2 inch steps, you should be alright. The only inconvenience was our ferry leaving a couple of days later than scheduled, so do not plan anything important the days after the expected arrival and have some flexibility of schedule if you plan on taking the ship. That we would depart one day later we knew 15 days in advance, but the extra delayed day was adjourned on the same night that we had to board due to bad weather, so we had to find accessible accommodation in a rush, which was not easy, as our previous hotel was full for the night. All in all, we feel that communication could have been clearer, but that is the only downside of the whole experience. We would also like to give special thanks to Gaspar, Camila, Alexia and all the crew for helping us throughout the whole trip. During meals, they helped us carry the trays and they were always attentive to our needs. They also arranged that the van that picked us up could enter the port and come near the ship. So all in all great service from the NaviMag team. If you are not tight on schedule and want to wind down a bit and do some slow tourism, this is your trip.
title: Magical landscapes, fantastic staff and some accessibility in place

review_text: A well traveled friend once told me one should never have favourites when travelling, after visiting Torres Del Paine National Park I find it extremely hard not to... We visited the Mirador Torres, Valle de Frances, Los Cuernos, Lago Pehoé Paine Grande and Lago Skóttsberg (sort of a revised take on the popular "W" hike). All were stunning but if I were pushed for time I'd recommend the Torres and the boat trip across the Lago Pehoé. There's plenty more to see and you probably wouldn't run out of new sights if you spent 10 days or more here. We unfortunately only had 4 days so we might just have to do a return journey sometime in the future. Liked Most: Incredible awe inspiring scenery. Liked Least: Quite an undertaking just to get to the park (that could of course be a positive in many a travelers book though).

review_text: This Museum (which is free) has some excellent pottery collections from various civilisations. review_text: We started in San Pedro de Atacama. We purchased the tour 2 days before. The office hours are not exactly the same as shown here on tripadvisor... Seems they take a siesta during the day. We purchased the private room also on the first day for extra. The transfer from Chilean minivan to Bolivian 4x4 went smoothly, although there were no toilets at either border. When we signed up, they told us they already have filled up one car and in the second car there was only one couple and us if we signed up. When we were transfered to the 4x4, we were put in a car with 6 people total, not 4. We tried to figure out why it was done like this, due to private accomadation, etc, but couldn't come up with logical answer. So if they tell you at the office that there are only 4 people in car so far fpr second group, doesn't mean you will be in this car. It is little cramped with 6 people in one car, but it is doable. You switch the seating each day, but we found to be the furthest back seat for two most comfortable. If you are less then 180cm tall, then you should be fine, don't expect lot of leg room but you have lot of room on the side which is nice for backpack etc. All other seats, you had to have the backpack on your lap or between legs. The accomadations were actually quite better, then we expected, especially the first day, we even had our private shower. They have solar heating so need to take quick showers, which is fine. It was quite simple accomadation. The food was actually good, but be sure to ask if they serve lama if you don't want to eat it. In Bolivia, the time changes so make sure you have correct time so you do not wait for dinner one hour thinking they are late or wake up one hour too early for breakfast... The locals gave us looks, as to why are they awake already. The high elevation is felt, but if you stay few days at San Pedro and do some day trips, you should be fine. Coca leaves helped as well. Andreas, our tour guide, was very good amd funny. Even though they promised us that guide will speak about 30% english, he spoke about 5-10% english. The other guide spoke better english. But he explained to us things as well, and we tried to understand with our basic spanish and his basic english, in the end it was fine. His driving was quite good and safe. He even took us on a top of a rock, where we had to do little climbing, which other tours seems did not do. The view was nice. At the salt flats, his proximity picture taking skills were not as good as other drivers had, when we saw pictures of some other groups. It took a while for our group to get a hang of it, it is not as easy as it seems. The food Andreas prepared was excellent. The car had trouble only once, due to engine overheating, but Andreas fixed it after while. I am not surprised that the car overheated, due to high altitude and terrain, and they only put water in the radiator, and not a mixture of anti-freeze, which has much higher boiling temp. Maybe it would be time to change the refrigerant in the A/C as the air was not that cold. Otherwise our tour was overall very nice experience.

review_text: This was an incredible experience all around. If you're looking to learn a lot about astronomy and see some incredible constellations and celestial bodies look no further. First Jorge picks you up at your hotel and takes you to his private stargazing property far away from any light pollution. You are given a warm poncho/blanket and seat and then start the experience with a lecture from Jorge about various topics such as how a telescope works, history of astronomy and he points out various constellations and celestial bodies that you can see with the naked eye. Afterwards you take a break where food and drinks will be provided and you all sit around a warm fire (which is very nice on a cold desert night). Honestly we were impressed with the spread of food (light bites, pastries and snacks) and drinks (both alcoholic and non-alcoholic) that were provided. Finally, you start viewing various celestial bodies through the telescopes. Because of the wide range of telescopes Jorge has, you get to see various objects at various distances which all look incredible. Jorge is an incredibly knowledgeable astronomer and was able to answer any question we had whether it be about the history of an object or the science behind it. We really can't recommend this experience enough, if you're interested in a stargazing tour look no further than Atacama Desert Stargazing!

review_text: Staying at Hotel Las Torres this park was the experience of a lifetime. It was declared a world biosphere reserve in 1978. I arrived late in the afternoon to see hundreds of guacanos running down the hill to cross the road in front of us and head up the other side. It's puma country and apparently they can come close to the hotel around March. I went on a 6km hike and at the summit (it's not that hard) a condor flew overhead as if to check us out. My guide said 'This is the real Patagonia' but I was choked up and couldn't answer. The tours and walks are extensive and varied to suit anyone's level of fitness and the guides are smart, patient, knowledgeable and all pretty easy to converse with. I went at the beginning of the season which can see 250,000 visitors, as I'd rather a cold day than hordes of people, but then it's only the lucky few in the world who see this park in their lifetime. The rest of my trip included the Pantanal (Pantanal Jaguar Safaris, contact Leen) and the Stella Australis which makes the next holiday hard to top.

review_text: In May of this year my daughter and I visited Patagonia. We stayed in Puerto Natales. We went with Angelo and Niko to Lago Grey to kayak. I have to say this was one of the best days I have ever had. We got an early start and saw the countryside of Patagonia at sunrise. It was absolutely beautiful. We stopped numerous times on the way to the park to take pictures of the various sights along the way. Angelo seemed as excited about this as we were, taking pictures of his own. We got to Lago Grey. Angelo had everything we needed to go kayaking: the boats, the gear, the protective clothing, everything. We had a brief tutorial about kayaking safety and off we went. What we saw then was like nothing I have ever seen in person. Shortly we were up upon some of the most beautiful icebergs that have come off Glacier Grey at the other end of the lake. We felt like little kids. The wonder of the place is hard to describe. I felt like I was in a National Geographic photo shoot. You could tell that Angelo and Niko also appreciated the experience also. They were the guides, of course, but they seemed more like our good friends who took us to their favorite place. We had lunch on a rock cliff. Angelo brought plenty of everything for some hungry kayakers. They took our cameras at the beginning of the trip and shot great pictures and videos throughout the trip. The pace was our own and totally unhurried. It is a an experience my daughter and I will never forget. I wish everyone could have a day like this. It was largely the location and the sights but also due to the great way Angelo took care of all the details and just let us immerse ourselves in the experience. I can highly recommend this for a once in a lifetime experience. Thanks again Angelo and Espiritu Patagon. Tom and Hali
title: Lago Grey Kayaking Among the Icebergs - Indescribable

review_text: I just completed the roundtrip Puerto Montt-Puerto Natales-Puerto Montt on the Eden at the end of June 2015. The observations of other travelers remain relevant, but some things are new. Although the ferry had only a handful of passengers (except for the Puerto Eden- Puerto Natales stretch where it provides local transportation) there was no interaction with the deck officers and the bridge remained off-limits at all times. Panoramic views of the waterworld were available only from the open decks on a ferry steaming through snow and ice. Summer side trips to a glacier and a visit if Puerto Eden are no longer offered. There is television on board, but only soccer games and hype were on. Smoking is allowed and done only outside. A fixed course meal is served at set hours in the cafeteria. The food is tasty and ample enough. Between meals fruit juice is available, but no soft drinks or snacks can be bought. Alcohol is no longer allowed on board (supposedly some drunk truckers were barbequeing in their cabin and set the ship on fire, although they just may have tried to stay warm). The local passengers provide for themselves and carry on what they need. Of special importance is the fact that the frerry schedule is only approximate. For example, the schedule of my northbound leg had a listed Tuesday departure and Thursday morning arrival. The ferry arrived late in Puerto Natales, so the return trip left on Saturday and arrived on Tuesday afternoon. Reasons for delays are loading problems, high winds and the need to pass tricky passages in daylight with the proper stage of the tide.The ferry can only be late, but never be early, and it generally cannot make up delays. Navimag appears to offer full refunds if a trip must be called off because of delays, but travellers with non-refundable air tickets better have cancellation insurance in case of late arrival (make sure that high winds and contrary tides are not considered excludable acts of God). Added attractions are a possibly very choppy 18 hour stretch of open ocean and, on a northbound leg, the opportunity to share the boat with truck trailers full of cattle on their way to slaughter. And always, the bunks come with bedding, but towels are not provided. For a rare but extreme Navimag adventure google the "wreck of the Navimag Amadeo". Enjoy the trip! I did - both ways (cattle or not)! The fact that Chile won the Copa Americana 2015 helped.
title: Don't expect a cruise.

review_text: My partner and I went on this tour and it included 5 others in our direct group. It was a really fun day!I have a few recommendations for those booking this tour: (1) wear closed toe, comfortable sneakers as you will be walking the grounds of wineries and there may be some mud, (2) the tour companies communicate via WhatsApp and it works really well in case you want to download this app before arriving in Santiago (3) eat breakfast and hydrate before the tour, lunch was around 2 for us. It is a long day and there are excellent wines to indulge in on this tour. We booked our tour about a month in advance and received a confirmation pretty quickly afterward. Our scheduled tour was on a Monday and received a WhatsApp message for hotel pick up time about 12 hours before the start of tour, Sunday at around 8 PM local time in Santiago. This practice seems normal for the tours here, so do not fret if you haven't received a pick up notification until the night before your tour. Our pick up was right on time. Benjamin was our guide and he made the day very enjoyable, and our driver was Ricardo who delivered us safely throughout the day. Our first stop was a modern winery with a beautiful building and well manicured landscape, Vinedos Veramonte. The wine tasting featured 4 wines. None of these wines really spoke to us. We spent some time walking the grounds here and they were very beautiful. Also, got to see some alpacas. Then, we went to Casa Villa Vinamar that included all sparkling wines that were delicious. We enjoyed the grounds here which looked like a palace with a large fountain in the front. Next, we went to Bodegas RE winery, our favorite of the day. The wines here were all very special. They utilize Carignon in some of their blends and have a stand alone with that grape, which is rare. This was our favorite wine in all of the tastings in Chile. Lastly, we got lunch at the Vina Casas del Bosque winery that featured dishes paired with their wine. All food and wine here was delicious. This tour was such a fun way to experience the Chilean countryside, and drink delicious wines. Review of: Exclusive wineries in Casablanca Valley & Tanino Restaurant

review_text: I usually jump on a red bus the first day I’m visiting a new city so I can then choose what to do next with more time. This bus departed on time and it had friendly staff, WiFi and the sound with headphone worked perfect. The next 2 buses I caught didn’t have WiFi, the poor quality headphones they gave only worked on one side, when they worked. The recordings were at extremely low volume and if you changed the language, when on the WiFi option (last bus) sometimes they overlapped or broke down. So frustrating. The stops were not on time - at all. The stops are not well defined in the map or their app. And even if you happen to be 20mts away waving your hands at them, they ignore your signals and leave you stranded. Oh, their app is badly designed. Can’t zoom well on it, does not tell you where YOU are, does not have accurate sense of how far the next bus is. Lastly, the staff from the first bus were friendly and knowledgeable; and they were young. The rest (4 more buses) behaved like your typical teenagers, did not provide good enough information on the system, the sites’ stops and how to jump back on, or any other support. I stoped at the second last stop and walked directly to the hotel instead of jumping back on. I’ve had the best experiences on these types of city bus tours. It is the first time I am so dissatisfied. It looked to me that there were plenty of public transport buses doing the exact same routes. Review of: Cable Car, Funicular and Sightseeing Bus in Santiago one day Dear traveler, we sincerely regret that your experience has been affected by what you tell us, thank you very much for sharing your experience with us, so that we can continue to improve our services. review_text: We thought that the amount of art was rather sparse. We toured about a dozen sizable galleries, each with only about a dozen pieces of art. We did try, but were unsuccessful, at deciphering the connections between the art located within a gallery. The admission was free.
title: Sparse

review_text: Honestly, I went into the adventure not knowing much about formal wine production or tasting but I can tell you, Mick is the best! His welcoming California-style attitude and enthusiasm for wine makes for an outstanding day in the picturesque Maipo Valley. We went out on a Monday when most wineries were closed but Nick used his connects to open up 5 outstanding locations for us. Here are my thoughts on 3 of them. Our first stop was at the Viña Antiyal where we learned all about Biodynamic Garagiste wine production. Don’t know much about Biodynamic Garagiste? You will when you leave! The rooftop patio we did our tasting on overlooked acres of grapevines and the Andes mountains in the background. It was then off to the Perez Cruz vineyard for a look at a larger production boutique winery. Their main facility was designed by renowned architect José Cruz Ovalle and it’s enchanting! The wine isn’t so bad either ;) Each tasting is paired with a local cheese, nut or chocolate. And make sure they pour you a glass of their rosé. Our day wrapped up with a quick trip to the William Fèvre winery. Here is where got to try Victor Pino Torche‘a award winning Espino Reserva Especial Chardonnay. I wanted to buy a case and bring it back with me! Needless to say, when we were dropped back off at our hotel we were happy, filled with knowledge and more than a little tipsy. Enjoy the trip! Review of: Full-Day Wine Tour from Santiago with Sommelier Guide
title: Gorgeous, Educational & Boozy Day in the Maipo Valley

review_text: One of the best walking tours we have done and Antonio made it this way. He was informative, funny, and engaging.. exactly what you want from a tour guide!

review_text: A new agency that are really friendly and help you to get the right tour. We had three tours through them and they have all been brilliant. We are waiting you for the next adventure.

review_text: We originally booked the trip to Cajon del Maipo, but were reassigned to the Portillo tour. review_text: We had the pleasure of meeting Felipe Sunkel when we traveled to Patogonia while my daughter was studying abroad in Chile. He was one of the guides working in the hotel we booked for our stay. How lucky we were to meet him on the day we arrived!! From our first hike to our last, Felipe ensured that we had one of the most amazing experiences of our lives. We wouldn’t venture out with anyone else!! Not only does he know EVERYTHING about the country, the trails, geology, the food, the wildlife, etc., but he also knows how to form relationships and make people feel comfortable and welcome-no matter their hiking ability. By the end of our adventure, Felipe felt more like a member of our family than a guide. We have kept in touch with him through Facebook since our trip, and hope to experience another adventure with his new company sometime in the near future. I would recommend Filipe’s guide services to anyone seeking an exhilarating, informative trip of a lifetime!! BOOK YOUR TRIP- you won’t be disappointed!! Hi Patty! review_text: Eugenio was the perfect tour guide. Has great communication and makes sure you get the experience you want. His knowledge of the area helped him reveal to delights of the tour in a way you could never get with a large group. Each sight he revealed uncovered more interesting sights and the place he picked for lunch was one of the best restaurants with amazing food and drink -- I don't think I've ever had such a wonderful lunch with an ocean view anywhere in the world. And Eugenio continually checks in to make sure you're comfortable and enjoying the day. If you begin in Santiago, don't let the travel deter you, the transportation was timely, comfortable and safe. If you pick this tour up when visiting the port, it will beat any tour from a larger company or cruise hands down. The personalization and ability to share the points of interest just could not be matched with a large bus full of a tour group. I would readily turn to Eugenio for any other sign seeing in the area. He's a gem. Review of: Valparaiso historical Unesco city and Viña del Mar tour - FD

My advice if you are day hiking, go to the main entrance (dirt roads, be ready), and do the full hike to the second laguna (can't remember the name)- it's beauty is comparable to something you'd see in Yosemite or better! The hike roundtrip is about 12 miles and pretty difficult (read, lots of mud and roots) - but fun if you like a challenge. Go early so you can spend lunch there and have time to enjoy and hike back. They close the gates at 6ish, so make sure you are back in time to get your car.
title: Unexpected beauty - hike to the second Laguna!

The lady explained to us that this is very common, i.e., different companies share their passengers in order to fill the cars with 6 tourist each. The experience with Hodaka was luckily very good!

review_text: We traveled here as a family of 4 adults. We hiked only 1 portion, the west leg of the W from Refugio Grey to Refugio Paine Grande. On the map, it shows 11km and estimated 3 hours. However, we took 5 hours to complete the hike. The first half is mostly uphill, and the second half is mostly downhill. We hiked on a very windy day; our kayaking excursion earlier in the day was cancelled due to the wind. We visited in late December, and the temperature was around 50 degrees F but with variable, strong winds and rain. Waterproof jacket and pants are recommended. The trail is well-maintained and clearly marked. We originally intended to hike more on the following days, however we are around 60yrs old and not regularly active, so we decided this was all we could handle for now. Our adult children did hike from Refugio Paine Grande towards Camp Italiano on the second day. This is a beautiful trail to hike, however you have to come prepared. Be aware that it is harder to hike with packs, and hiking sticks were a huge plus for us.
title: Beautiful but challenging trek

review_text: Go early if you want to avoid being at the viewing platform with dozens of other tourists. Park opens at 8:30 afaik. Entrance fee is 5000 per person. The walk through the forest is awesome, but can be more exhausting than the distance of 3300m might make you think. We loved it, although is was warm and very humid. The Glacier itself might not be the largest, bluest of Patagonia, but certainly one of the most unique. View from the Laguna is almost better, but being closer, at the top on the platform should not be left out. You can take a boat from the Laguna or even go by kayak (guided). We would highly recommend checking out this Glacier if you are in Puyuhuapi or have a few hours to spare when you drive by. We stayed about 4,5h in total.
title: Lots of tourist, but worth the visit

review_text: Fantastic place to eat great food, get together with friends and have a drink or two. Great on weekends as you can enjoy some antiques or old books and magazines at the open fair. Close enough to Cerro Santa Lucía and the city center. What I love the most is the happy feeling of this neighborhood.

I would highly recommend her services to anyone with a serious interest in exploring the great vineyards around Santiago. Thanks Kylie! Thanks for the great review, and thanks for coming along on the tour with me. It was great to have the "three" of you along and I'm glad you enjoyed your afternoon. I hope to see you again next time you're passing through this part of the world. All the best!

review_text: I made three trips with the Bora pro Chile and I am very satisfied! We did Sunset Cordillera, Portillo and Viña del Mar and Valparaíso. review_text: We hiked Cani today and loved it. We took a bus at 12 from Pucon. The first 2 hours are very steep, then there is 1 hour ok steep and last 30 minutes are quite steep again. However, it is the last point, the mirador, that is trully rewarding. You will get views of volcanoes, lakes, araucaria trees and mire. The trees themselves can be observed from the second lake already, but you should finish the hike, to really appreciate the place. Watch out: we were told the last bus runs at 20.10 but it never arrived so we had to hitchhike. The last one was actually at 19.45 and we just missed it. Confirm with the bus station before going.
title: Steep climb, great views as a reward

review_text: I am studying abroad in Chile, and my mom and aunt came to visit me. I wanted to show them Cajon del Maipo, and this hike was the perfect difficulty for them, and the views were incredible. Also, Gonzalo is a terrific guide! He was very knowledgeable about the area, fauna and geology. Would recommend! Thanks a lot for your review!! Its an incredible experience..we are glad!!

review_text: Our family went to this facility prompted by the good reviews. We arrived around midday and were told that zip lining was not available for our younger children, nor was horseback riding. We were only allowed to sign up for a guided walk at 3pm. review_text: Much of the Atacama is just the poor man's version of Bolivia—except at 10 times the price! Laguna Chaxa is the perfect example of what I'm talking about: the flamingo lagoons and salt flats here utterly pale in comparison to their counterparts in Bolivia, which are just a few hours away by car. Yes, Bolivia is higher altitude and requires more acclimatizing, but it's so worth the effort. If you're coming all the way to the Atacama to see flamingos and salt flats, please do yourself a favor and add Bolivia's Salar de Uyuni and Eduardo Avaroa National Reserve to your itinerary. They're much cheaper, less crowded, and far more spectacular than what this place offers.
title: Skip this and go to the Bolivian side instead

The French Valley was closed when we walked due to snow, but the 3 towers peeked out from the clouds on our day there - the hightlight of the trip. The Refugios along the way are very good accommodation options - nice to have the option of a cold beer at the end of long day's walk!

review_text: After trying to book via the website which kept skin wierd things (maybe due the dodgy internet in our hotel) we ended up booking via Hotel Martin Gusinde in Natales which was quite pain free process. Ww were warned that leave at least 2.5 hours to drive to Lago Grey from Natales and this was good advice due to the many road works along the way. There is a 2km walk along a pebble beach once you have ‘checked in’ and you need to allow time for this too. The trip itself was superb; we got very lucky with the weather which cleared up just before we got to the glacier and the viewing was spectacular ... the boat has plenty of space for all to get the views and photos they want and spends about 45 minutes cruising past three faces of the glacier. There’s a pisco drink included in the fair and it’s pretty good. The on board bar also sells beer, wine and spirits and is busy for the whole trip! Crew are great and do their best to share their enthusiasm for the whole experience. The trip is worth every dollar - if you’ ve come all the way to Patagonia you would be crazy to miss it.

review_text: The attention given to tourists is terrible! On 06/9 it was raining and most of the trips were outside and they did not offer umbrellas. What could have been an unpleasant but excusable mistake became worse when at the beginning of the tour I complained to the guide Marta, who was wearing an umbrella and didn't even offer her umbrella or apologize, but kept trying to explain why we should accept getting wet! When I told him that if there was no solution, he just had to apologize, he said he wouldn't apologize! Rude! Who is the manager that allows such a person to serve customers? When the Tasting began, the first three wines were presented in an external area with people standing in front of a counter. The wines were reasonable. The second part presented by sommelier Teo was adequate, in a comfortable room and accompanied by cheese, but it did not have the main wine: Don Merchor Cabernet Sauvignon. Opposite the exit from the Tasting room was the Restaurant but to gain access, despite having a closed door, we were forced to walk all the way around the outside area in the rain, the same route to go to the bathroom. We went for lunch: we ordered a salad to share and two pastas. The salad didn't come first but with the pasta which was cold and I had to ask for it to be warmed up. I asked for a glass of Terráyuno wine to go with it, and to my surprise they didn't present the bottle, the label, much less the taste: it came with a glass served with less than a portion in my opinion. The seafood pasta had a hospital taste: no taste of anything, just pepper that we asked for and added. I thought it was better not to risk even the coffee, I paid the bill without the services and I will never go back! The wifi requires a password from the bracelet and drops out all the time and needs to be restarted, meaning they don't even offer this quality. For a long time now, this winery has lived more on tradition than on its products. Casilero is a bad wine, but cheap. The best are more expensive than they deserve, made on an industrial scale and do not have a good cost-benefit ratio. We came from Mendoza where we were wonderfully treated in all the wineries, from the biggest like Monteviejo to the small ones like Masi Tupungato, any of them infinitely better and more attentive. At no point, whether the guide or Somelier asked for our assessment, it doesn't seem to matter. Who knows, I'll read it here, but I doubt it will have any effect. I do not recommend! review_text: This is quite a unique spot, located at 4'200 meters altitude, where you can explore the geysirs and hot ponds on your own. Very little people, as a matter of fact, we were only the two of us ... :-) Easy to find: Set your navi to Mauque, coming either from Colchane or Huara, driving on the A-15. Then turn on to the A-487, heading for Mauque. From there, you will see sign-posts and the location is really easy to find. Google Maps lists it as "Campo geotérmico de Puchuldiza". The A-487 is a dirt road, but a very soft one. No bumps, no holes. Only two very tiny creek crossings, one 50cm wide and the other 2 meters wide; both approx. 20cm deep. No problem even for a 2WD car; maybe a little more height, e.g. with a cross-over can help, but not mandatory. The Geysirs spout continuously, since some years ago a geothermal company explored the area, and plugged some pipes into the ground. Before, the geysirs were spouting every so often, like the ones in Iceland, but now there is a continous flow of hot water being shot in thte air by several Geysirs; we had three "running" at the same time. Plus many water and mud pools. On top of this, there is - of course - the beautifully coloured valley with all the sulfur minerals giving great many colours. Finally, there is also a hot water pool - with changing rooms male/female ! All of the area is very clea, and the car tracks are marked with red stones, so that the thermal features are preserved. If everyone sticks to being careful with these hot springs, they will remain super-beautiful for many years ahead, and provide tavellers with a superb one-of-its-kind experience !

review_text: This is one of the more rougher treks I've done. Both in terms of adressing my routefinding skills many times (while there is a collection of signposting as well as the much more frequent markerstones, I did manage to wander off track quite a few times) as in the actual difficulty of the terrain (boulder hopping, steep descents, muddy marshes, negotiating tree roots & branches) your progress will be slow each of the 3 or more days you're trekking the 32km/20mi long Dientes. I solo-hiked it in 4. But they say: the rougher the trek, the more beautiful it gets. That counts here also. It's a little more wilderness than the one in Torres del Paine. While you're on the most southerly inhabited island of the world in Puerto Williams, a Chilean Armada town slowly growing into a tourist destination, enjoy the view of Cerro Bandera while you start your climb. On top there's a beautiful view of the Beagle Channel and Argentina's Tierra del Fuego mountains across. Continue along the edges of the ridge to a steep drop to Laguna del Salto, one of the many tundra lakes in the area. I stayed here for the night on a terribly wet and uneven floor, but with fresh water. My second day started with a climb up to Paso Australia and over loose boulders up Paso los Dientes (I wandered off track here which did cost me half an hour) to eventually descent to Laguna los Dientes and Laguna Escondida again with plenty big boulders to hop. Campsites and water were no problem finding here and were in better condition. There's a beautiful view of the jagged peaks of the actual Dientes ('teeth' in spanish), for which the area is named. On a clear day the more southerly Lago Windhond is visible as are the Cabo de Hornos islands. My third day ended up being the easiest one. Only two easier uphill sections and drops to arrive at the beaver affected area of big Laguna Martillo, where I took a wrong direction again costing me about 45 minutes. After the big lake there's a beautiful valley to cross where I saw signs of a big animal nearby, possibly a puma. I eventually camped at the foot of the biggest climb of the whole trek, Paso Virginia. The fourth day started with a muddy ascent of the lower section of the climb and ended at a fantastic overview of a very steep and possibly dangerous descent to Laguna Guanacos. Take care here in bad weather. After this lake there is a long mixed section of marshes, woods and farmland to get you down to the end of the trail at an old fishery at the road which will lead you to Puerto Williams again in 2 hours. I only saw people on the first night and was thus almost the whole time alone on the trail. Weather can be a problem here because of the southerly location of the Island, but most of the time I was hiking in clear sunny skies in late March 2017. Recommended.
title: Rough wilderness hike at the most southerly tip of the world

review_text: I can't say enough good things about my experience with Private Tours Santiago. I contacted Esteban to see about having the tour pick us up at the airport, sightsee for 3-4 days, then drive us to San Antonio to catch our cruise. Esteban worked closely with me to identify our areas of interest and activity level, and put together a wonderful itinerary for us. Esteban provided great recommendations for local crafts and restaurants. He was readily available to chat via what's app, texting and email. He was very patient with all my questions, and all of this resulted in a fabulous start to the trip. Esteban promised us great guides, and he delivered! We were very impressed with our guide, Benjamin, and driver Louis. By the time they dropped us off at our ship, we felt like good friends. Benjamin's English was great, and he was very knowledgeable about the history of Santiago and its sights, and he shared numerous stories with us. We felt very safe the entire time, especially since Benjamin is a martial arts specialist! We had such a marvelous time! From exploring a beautiful private park, a day trip to the Andes, a wonderful wine-tasting and meal at Barrica 98 (owned by a friend's son), seeing the city from the top of the Sky Costanera, to taking us to the Jumbo grocery store to look for local treats. We filled each day to the max, and had a fantastic time. Whenever we got out to explore, Louis stayed with the minivan, so our belongings were always safe, and I didn't have to carry my purse with me all the time. Louis is a superb driver---we put him to the test driving up/down the windy roads to the ski resort, and up/down the windy roads of Valparaiso. Even though I did not speak Spanish, we could still communicate, and he was very friendly. Louis and Benjamin were always very punctual--from meeting us at the airport, to meeting us at our hotel when promised. They were also willing to modify activities on the fly, if we wanted to be dropped off somewhere instead of our hotel, for example. For anyone planning a trip to Santiago or its neighboring cities, you can rest assured that Esteban, Benjamin and Louis will take exceptional care of you.

The Museo is at once poignant, historic, informative and moving. It is only with some more perspective that one can somewhat recuperate with the stories that the disappeared ones have to tell. (It is with some shame that my country had a hidden hand in making the coup possible...)

review_text: We booked a guided trip to summit volcan villarica with this company. The main reason for doing this was because We were arriving in late to pucon the night before summiting (only one good day weather was forecast for the next day) and we because of this we could not rent the required equipment to summit on time (crampons, ice axe, helmet etc). This is a really easy hike if you have some experience with mountains and you can definetly do this without a guide if you have time to organise renting equipment. However the company were really nice from the very start. They stayed open late (over an hour and a half late) to fit us with our gear on the night before summiting. The next morning picked us up from our hostel and brought us to the mountain in a pickup. We were in a small group of 6 which we then split into two groups along the way due to different fitness levels. Three of us went ahead with one guide at a faster pace to the others. I really appreciated this as up to that point I had been frustrated by the slow pace of the group. The guides were all really cool and full of good conversation (in english). We enjoyed a long break at the top and returned by sledding down the snowy part of the mountain before reaching the scree and walking the rest of the way. We then returned to pucon where we shared some beers on the roof of their shop. Overall this was a really good experience which I would 100% recommend if you have NO mountain experience. If you have some experience I would recommend renting equipment and doing it by yourself. wow we feel praised with such a wide comment, thanks for the time for sharing your experience. We are pleased to know that you had a good time and felt good company, just like us of you. Good recommendation the same for people who have knowledge in mountains, as you say they can do it on their own if they have their equipment and experience, and otherwise we are so you can do it Best regards from all Antü Rios and Mountains staff

review_text: If you are interested in going to Patagonia, I strongly recommend booking with Extremo Chile. My friend and I booked a 3 night, 4 day guided W trek experience of Torres Del Paine and it was incredible. Not only was the trek and the landscape picturesque but having a guided tour and everything organised for us made it even more worthwhile and enjoyable. A few call-outs that made our experience amazing and why you should book with Extremo Chile if you’re considering going to Torres Del Paine: 1. Communication prior to the trip was excellent. Carlos (the owner of Extremo Chile) replied quickly to all our questions and provided us with a packing list of things to take on our trip. 2. Carlos came to our hotel the day before the hike to confirm we had everything we needed and to answer any other questions we had. When we looked at other companies offering tours of the W trek - they included this as part of the first day to make it seem like a longer trek but you only need to do the W trek in 3 nights / 4 days. Carlos also picked us up from the hotel the morning of the first day. 3. The food was exceptional!!!!! And there was plenty of it, which you need especially walking so much. Carlos cooked for us each night and we had great fresh food. Carlos made sure to also cater for our dietary requirements. We also even had wine and beer some nights with our food! 4. The service was amazing. We booked the camping W trek, and each night when we arrived at the campsites, our tents were already set up for us and the tent, mats and sleeping bags were premium quality. We also didn’t have to carry any of these which was amazing, we only carried our snacks and personal items for the hike each day. Carlos also let us borrow hiking poles for the duration of the hike and lent us ice crampons for the first day as the Towers were quite icy. He also lent us water proof bags to put some of our clothes in when it rained one day. 5. The guide was incredible and so knowledgeable. He had 20+ years experience of Patagonia and we were able to appreciate the walk so much more. 6. It is such great value for money in comparison to other companies we were looking at. Even if you choose to not get a guide, I would still recommend the unguided tour at Extremo Chile as the food and the hire equipment at the Campsites each night (if available) are so expensive. I wish I could give more than 5 stars. I have recommended to all my friends and family! If you are going to Patagonia, you must book with Extremo Chile.
title: The perfect way to experience the W trek

review_text: The experience with Araya was sensational. I don't see how it could have been better. The guides are prepared and friendly, just like the drivers. review_text: We had heard that the Sky Constanera was expensive and just another observation deck. I’m so glad we decided to go and didn’t listen to that! Yes, it does cost money to go up but it is worth it. We went up on a Saturday afternoon around 1pm and had the place basically entirely to ourselves. There were probably 5-10 other people around. The views are stunning and there are plaques explaining what you are looking at as well as small speakers you can hear describing what you are viewing when you stand right under them. There are two levels that you get access to when you pay to go up. The highest level is literally the highest level. When you look up, it’s open air!! To me that was so cool because most observation decks don’t have that feature. You can read about the construction of the building and there is a chart showing how it compares to other tall buildings around the world. We really enjoyed our time here and spent about 45 minutes really enjoying it. When you enter you go through a meta detector and your bag is x-rayed. After that, you have a brief wait and while the elevator goes up the guide in the elevator explained in English and Spanish a bit about the building. When you’re ready to head down, there is an area to line up and the guide in the elevator heading down was very friendly and chatted with us about how we enjoyed the experience. We were shocked at how we didn’t have to wait more than a minute and there were no lines. He said we were there during lunch time and that helped reduce the amount of people who would normally be there. It is a little confusing when you enter the mall to figure out how to go to the look out. Go to one of the white electronic guides. It basically looks like a giant iPad or computer screen on a holder. You can change the language to English if need be and it will tell you exactly where to go from where you are to access the entry to the look out. All in all, totally worth it. Definitely a must do while in Santiago!
title: Totally worth it

review_text: I put below review here not to scare everyone, but I do want to hi light some facts about the hike. when the accident happened on the1st of March causing 2 death, several injuries, my boyfriend and I were just there. Although with another tour operator, we still find the whole tour needs add more security meaturement. Luckily with only 5 people in the team, the situation was a lot easier to control. we were still going up when the weather condition changed dramatically. certain points we couldn't see much, only wind and snow blowing to our face, and freezing. It was bad. I was so scared that I called it off when we literally 20 meters away from the top, I insisted to one of guide to go down. so 3 others continued with an older guide, me and my boyfriend turn back. Now i think about it, I was so happy that I made that choice. There is no meaning to risk your life just to see nothing! The only thing to use to hold yourself is a ice axe. If you have never used such thing before, don't expect you can stop yourself sliding by using the little tool. about 2300 meters when we add ice spikes to our shoes, the guides used 1 mins to explain what to do if you fall. To me this is ridiculous!! If nothing happens, great! BUT if something happens, just like the 2 death happened on that day, you can't expect yourself react so fast! From all the blogs, post and travel books we read, the only thing mentioned about the hike is Physically fit, honestly I think there are a lot more than that. these 2 death were 20 years old young boys, I bet yes they were! Accidents happen of course, maybe it was the terribly bad weather on that day, or maybe it was the careless, but overall I think the security of the operators all have issues. It's not a W-tour or a hike to the lake. I want to share my opinion sincerely with you, and I hope people read this review knowing what they expect from the hike.
title: Not only physically fit

We covered a lot of the city and loved every minute. Finally we were given a print painting of the city as a memento and Isaac gave us a lock to put on the iron fence overlooking the city to remind us of our love for Valapraiso which we did and do. We love Patatour!!

review_text: Being quite disorganised I hadn't planned ahead to be able to do the W or the O but I still made it to the Torres on a one-day hike. Buses leave early, and at the same times irrespective of the company, from the main bus station in Puerto Natales, and the ticket is a return one. Shop around - most are priced at 15,000 return, I got mine for 12,000. The bus journey takes about 90 minutes. When you arrive you need to queue for park entrance - be sure to get the back of your ticket stamped if you are there for the day but plan to return, as the ticket is valid for 3 days, but only if stamped. Then it's an extra 3000 pesos for the return coach to the start of the trail up to the Torres. Here you will also find a cafe and a Patagonia store. It took me 3h20 to reach the Mirador Las Torres. There is a path but it is rough in places and most importantly, it is very undulating, so don't expect to save any time on the way back. It is also a scramble over a very rocky part to reach the mirador - just when you think you're nearly there, you have to content within a very rocky stretch - a scramble and then a climb up. The views are rather stunning the whole way, and if you're lucky you'll get to see the helicopter ferrying goods in and litter out. There is a cafe and toilets about half way. It's an intense walk - I had planned to return to the park the day after but was too tired and aching. But it was completely worth it, and I can't wait to go back and do the O! Be sure to make it back to the cafe at the start of the trail for the last connecting bus to the park entrance! It's unlikely you'll want to walk the extra kms!
title: One day hike - tough but worth it!

Each end of the 500 metre long tunnel have become a shrine to Rojas Reyes where everything from football scarves to graves of dead dogs can be found. review_text: We were warned repeatedly that the early morning trips to the Geysers were very cold and to dress warm, but the long and freezing cold bus ride there was one of the most miserable travel experiences I've had. (Of course, that could be unique to our tour company.) In any case, the geysers were interesting, but not enough to justify the journey and discomfort. And I'm not a wimpy US snob tourist... I love backpacking and have slept in snow caves on various trips. The thing that killed us was that the thermal spring you can swim in was supposed to be a highlight, and instead it barely felt warmer than the air. Maybe it was an unusual day, but our guide said people claim it's 35 degrees (C) but is really more like 30. It cannot possibly have been more than 25 when we got it. As soon as I was in, I wanted to get out, I was no more comfortable inside than out. Fortunately, the amazing views of the beautiful mountains all around and the cool places we stopped on the way back to San Pedro after the frigid and disappointing morning made the whole ordeal worth it. But my advice is make sure your tour company has a comfortable and heated bus to get you there, and DO NOT get in to the spring unless you feel it with your hand first and are confident you will not regret it.

review_text: The lagoons were paired with our visit to the flamingo reserve and what a treat it was to have those two sites in the same tour. After seeing the wonders of the flamingoes, we really didn't anticipate doing more than enjoying the sight of the ultramarine blue water and scruffy terrain and flora, with volcanoes as backdrop. But the vicunas had something else in mind entirely, much to our delight. As we stood watching a lone flamingo feeding at the edge of the second lagoon, and our guide pointed out some nesting Chilean geese, two bands of vicuna (each male has a harem of about a dozen females plus their young) sauntered down the hill to a salt lick adjacent to the water and converged at the base of the hill. Because males are very competitive, there was some posturing from the two leading their respective families. As they did their thing, the females and young darted around, clearly happy to interact with newcomers. They pranced back and forth together along the edge of the lagoon. Young vicuna chased each other while one or two females kept an eye to make sure they didn't wander too far. It was like "a ballet being born out in the valley" (sorry Bruce!) right before our very eyes. And once the males had sorted out their differences, the vicunas formed a single file and walked along the laguna, sometimes into it, and then headed toward the other laguna. Our guide was as delighted as we were. He had never seen anything like it. The scene made for a most memorable visit!

review_text: The tour to Casablanca vineyard, Viña Del Mar and Valparaiso with Lucho from Travitur is amazing. Lucho knows a lot of historical, geographical, cultural and random facts that make the information really fun and memorable, so you visit a lot of places and learn in a very fond way. In Casablanca we had a wine tasting experience, the mansion and winery are very fancy and well kept. In the ride he explained a lot about Chile, the microclimate, the valleys and just how life is in the day to day here. In Viña Del Mar we went to a manor called mansion Rioja, we saw an original aboriginal sculpture from Rapa Nui, we also got to see a Rodin sculpture in a Park, the beautiful flower clock, the sea lions on the beach and had a delicious meal at a restaurant with an impressive view of the beach. In Valparaiso we saw the navy building, the docks, a statue for an admiral with an everlasting flame, the funicular (cable car), and many bars and alleys in the graffiti urban landscape of Valpo. On our way back we learnt more about history and compared the cities. Review of: Full Day Private Tour in Casablanca Valparaíso and Viña del Mar

review_text: 2 days in Pucon and rain will keep us off the volcano bith days. Decided to catch the local bus to the National Park and hike the Los Lagos trail to the three lakes. Despite the drizzle / light rain it was an enjoyabke walk, if a bit wet. In our group we had the very fit hikers in proper boots to the not-so-fit in sneakers. All made it to Lago Verde, the furtherest lake in a little over two hours. We only made a few stops as rain meant we couldn't get the cameras out. The hike back down was muddy and slippery. The walks to the waterfalls add less than 10 minutes each and we all made it back down after a short lunch stop (10 minutes) for the 2.20 pm bus back. If the rain is heavy I wouldn't bother as you won't be able to see anything at the very few view points and the track will be horrible. Wish we could have been here in warmer, drier weather.

review_text: This tour was disappointing, largely due to the tour guide, Maria. It did not feel like a guided tour, more like an organized itinerary and transportation. It paled in comparison to our free walking tour the day prior and honestly could not be classified as a guided tour. Beginning with the itinerary itself, the Viña Del Mar portion felt like an add on. The two stops were superficial, solely for the photo opp, and you don’t get the opportunity to walk around or explore at all. The Valparaiso portion did feel like a decent amount of time and the vineyard was a nice addition if you like wine tasting. Although, be aware that the tasting only covers two wine samples. From the beginning, Maria’s actions did not inspire confidence. The pickups did not go smoothly and took longer than necessary because she wasn’t sure where/who she was picking up. Additionally, she wasn’t organized on the tour itself. Once we got to Valparaiso for the walking tour, she didn’t seem like she knew where she was going or had a plan. She had to stop to withdraw money because she didn’t have cash for the funicular. She repeatedly asked us where we wanted to go in Valparaiso, i.e., which street we wanted to go down; this defeats the purpose of a tour. Additionally, her English abilities were not sufficient to lead a tour in English. She was able to communicate basic facts but nothing more complex. We asked specific questions about the history of the port and significance of the graffiti and street art, but she wasn’t able to elaborate any further than what we already knew in our very basic understanding of Valparaiso culture and history. When she did point things out it was just to say this is so and so’s house but with no further information about the context or significance. She seemed more interested in making small talk than sharing information. Rather than sharing interesting facts and tidbits about history and culture, she shared personal information instead, not limited to family, birthdays, and personal opinions questioning the validity of graffiti as street art. One of the reasons we decided to do a guided tour was because we had been cautioned about the safety of walking alone in Valparaiso. However, if you speak Spanish and are decently savvy and are able to get around on your own would recommend exploring the city without a tour as you’d likely be able to do/see more on your own. We felt no safer with Maria due to her disorganization and clear unfamiliarity with the city than if we had been on our own. She almost left someone behind and had to be reminded by another person on the tour. She didn’t seem to realize we would all want to stop for lunch because she had taken us to a subpar empanada place for a quick snack. For lunch she took us to a street that she herself was unfamiliar with and was unable to provide recommendations other than reading the menus to those who did not understand Spanish. For the price we paid we expected a knowledgeable tour guide. We booked the tour because we read all of the excellent reviews of tours guided by other people, but we did not share this experience. It felt like this was Maria’s first time guiding a tour in Valparaiso. Unfortunately, we think this could have been an excellent tour with the appropriate tour guide. The driver was excellent and we felt very safe. It was convenient to have transportation and not have to navigate the bus system from Santiago to Valparaiso and the metro from there to Viña Del Mar, however, if you are well travelled, speak Spanish, and are decently comfortable traveling on your own, would recommend proceeding without a tour. That’s what we would have done in retrospect. However, we may have felt differently with a different tour guide. Review of: Valparaiso Port and Vina del Mar Full-Day Tour from Santiago

review_text: My wife and I have been blessed with the opportunity to visit many wineries across Chile, some of them with a visitor's center infrastructure way more developed than De Martino. That said, this winery and the tour around it are by far one of our favorites. The private tour we opted for has a cost of CLP 17,800 (USD 26) for individuals doings a normal tasting (3 wines - 1 standard reserve and 2 premium) whereas individuals just doing the tour pay CLP 8,000 (USD 12). María Jesús is the woman who pretty much handles the visitor center at De Martino. She is indeed a very knowledgable person on wine but it is very much up to the visitors to ask questions. As with any tour María Jesús does have an interesting script of what to say while visiting the fields (including a trial pit), the warehouse, the cellar and the winemaking area. However, it is when you start interacting more with her that you get to realize much there is to know about winemaking and the wine business. We felt we learned a lot from her. After the 1.5 hour tour is pretty much over, you are headed to a tasting room. María Jesús allowed us to figure out the wines by ourselves without imposing her views and what each wine should be. She gave us time and space, which allowed us to enjoy the tasting as a learning experience and/or just as a fun moment enjoying some very good wine. 100% recommended. Dear Ignacio, We really appreciate your comments and we are very glad that you enjoyed your visit at De Martino!, that you and your wife learnt something with us after visiting several wineries and enjoyed our wines! review_text: Took the metro to Baquedano (this is the closest stop) then it's a 15 minute walk to the hill. When you get to the hill look for the castle-type building. This is the funicular entrance. Cost for a round-trip: adult 2000 pesos, child 1500 pesos. (More expensive on weekends/holidays: 2600 and 1950 pesos.). After buying your ticket join the line-up for the next funicular. We went straight to the top. If you are trying to avoid seeing zoo so your kids don't know it's there it's not a problem. Our funicular did not even stop at the zoo.....maybe it was closed. You cannot see it anyway. Opening hours for funicular everyday 10am - 7pm, Monday's it does not open until 2pm. Once at the top there are craft stalls, food etc and seating areas. There is another short walk up (5 minutes) to get to the statue. It was a lovely family trip out. We took lunch and ate it at the top. Everyone says to go on a clear day. Due to time restrictions we went on a cloudy day. We could not see any mountains (haha!) but it did not spoil the trip. It's still a spectacular view from the top.
title: Nice family trip out

review_text: To understand Chile today it is necessary to take the time to go through this museum and follow the history of the Pinochet coup and the slow return to democracy in Chile. The museum is set up so you follow the history sequentially over time and it takes at least 2-3 slow hours to make your way through. It becomes emotionally draining (e.g. listening to people describe being tortured) and you naturally want to hurry on to the presumed "happy ending". But the ending doesn't come all that easily - for example, you learn that Pinochet never really paid for his crimes. Follow the whole story through to the end, it's worth the time. Some notes: first, if you don't speak and read Spanish you have to get an Audioguide or you will miss a great deal. Second, don't go on Mondays - it's closed.
title: A Necessary Visit (but emotionally draining)

review_text: I'd highly recommend the Navimag ferry from Puerto Natales to Puerto Montt. I did the 4 night, 3 day trip in May 2012. I thoroughly enjoyed it, but, having read the reviews below and based on a few comments from fellow passengers, I think a lot depends on what your expectations are. To enjoy it, I think you have to be interested in a fairly slow, calm journey through the magnificent fjords simply enjoying the views when the weather is good. If you're looking for constant activity and excitement plus, you're going to be disappointed. It's RELAXING! I was actually surprised when one of my fellow passengers said to me, "The scenery is all the same!" with the clear impression that he was bored. I couldn't relate as I thought the scenery was magnificent, and I found it wonderful to sit on board the boat and watch the world/scenery pass by. Many of the passengers found the section through the Pacific and the Bay of Paynes (?) to be rougher than they would have liked and ran to their beds. I didn't think it was that bad, but very few folks were out and about - and it's lots worse on other crossings from what our guide said. There were presentations every afternoon - both in English and Spanish - on the wildlife and history of the fjords. One thing I would say was a problem with Navimag was their communication before the trip. My information said the boat left at 6 am so I planned on getting there one hour beforehand. Only by chance did I learn that we had to board the night before at 9 pm. I'd recommend contacting Navimag before your trip to find out any particular boarding instructions. I think the times change based on the tides and when they need to pass through certain channels at high tide.
title: Great, relaxing and scenic way through the fjords.

review_text: We (a group of 3) ordered a full day wine tour by Detour by placing a request on their web-page. Only minutes after i sent the form on their page, an operative from detour called me and we made a booking. However, this booking was cancelled at 18.06 the day before it was supposed to happen due to some problem with a winery. The company sent this in an email and that was that. (when a booking is made over the phone, it is customary to cancel over the phone as well) In the evening, most tourists are getting ready for dinner and checking emails are not a priority. We cut our night short, since the tour was to start at 8 am. At breakfast we noticed the cancellation email. So not only did we not get a tour, they affected our whole schedule for our vacation. When we called about a replacement tour of another district, they were defensive and non co-operative, talked lots to eachoter in spanish and hung up on us. NOT what you expect of a company in the tourism business. My advice to other travellers is STEER CLEAR OF DETOUR!

All it turned out to be was a drive up the mountain,, which was a little nerveracking courtesy of the first 32 hairpin, and I mean hairpin bends.The remaining 30 or so were not so tight. We stopped at Farrellones, looked over the wall and continued our journey upward. It was Chilean summer so there was not much going on at the top. The thing that annoyed me was that our guide, a bilingual American girl ,told us we could leave a tip if we wished - a little brazen I'd say

review_text: To set the stage: We had just arrived in Santiago from Valparaiso, via a wonderful guide service from Valparaiso, Mini Trole, who took us on a wonderful winery tour in the Casablanca Valley at Emiliana Winery before dropping us off at our hotel, the Vespucci Suites. After checking in to this very nice hotel we started looking at tour brochures in the lobby for tours of the Concha y Toro winery. We decided on Turistik's tours. We had the front desk call to make reservations for us for a tour the next afternoon. We wanted the front desk to call so there would be no confusion on details due to the language issue, we don't speak very good Spanish. First problem was the tour wan not available at the brochure price of $29,000 CHP! (about $44 US each). We were told the new price was $32,000 CHP (about $50 US ea.) We agreed to the new price and were charged immediately on our Visa card. We were told to be in the lobby promptly at 1:45 PM the next day for our tour pick up. We were very much looking forward to the tour so were in the lobby at 1:35 PM, 10 minutes early! By 2 PM when no one had arrived we asked the front desk to call for us and when they did they were assured we would be picked up momentarily. We were finally picked up at 2:45 PM with no excuses or apologies at all! We were shuttled a mile to a large bus depot where we were told to wait until we were called for the 2:30 PM Concha y Tora tour, and at that time it was 3:10 PM! We finally boarded a very full bus for the 45 minute ride to the winery. Upon arrival at 4:15 PM we were given our passes for our English tour and told to be back on the bus by NO LATER than 5:30 PM or the bus would leave without us! We had a nice tour of the winery, though rushed because of our late arrival. After the tour we barley had time to grab an additional glass of wine and a quick appetizer.We wanted to stop in the winery store to purchase some of the fine wines we had tasted but didn't have the time if we were to be on the bus by 5:30 PM as instructed. Upon getting on the bus at 5:25 PM we noticed that there were quite a few people missing that had arrived with us. By 5:45 PM when these people had not arrived on the bus we asked our guide what was happening. She said that 8 people had taken the Spanish only tour that included an additional wine tasting with the wine maker! She said we were not offered that additional tasting, which by the way was at no additional cost, because it was for Spanish speaking guests only! As if that wasn't enough, these last Spanish speaking guests didn't show up at the bus until 6:45 PM! To add insult to injury there were no apologies or offers of a credit to all those who were stuck on that bus for an hour waiting for those ill mannered guests! When we arrived at the bus depot for our transfer back to our hotel we again had to wait 30 minutes! We arrived at our hotel just before 8 PM! Please do yourself a huge favor, and tell all your traveling friends, DO NOT book any tours through Turistik Tours in Santiago, Chile! We appreciate your comment dear traveler, it is very important for us to know about your experience.
title: Poor service!

Julio is careful to adapt the tour to the needs and interests of his clients. He takes pride in honestly and openly sharing his country with the outside world. With Julio, I felt that I had a local friend to show me around. I highly recommend Chileprivatetours!

review_text: On a brisk morning in the spring month of October, we met our guides out of Kayak Sin Borders arranged by Tierra Patagonia. After a quick trip to Lago Grey and a quick bathroom stop at Hotel Grey, we were treated to an hour of how to out on a dry suit to go kayaking. A combination of pilates, yoga, and mechanical engineering resulted a sealed dry suit that would deter anyone from even mentioning the need for another restroom stop. The next 1.5 hours gliding along the mirror like waters of Lago Grey between and next to ice bergs was heaven on earth. We had the entire lake to ourselves and only the sounds of crackling ice bergs broke the tranquil silence. The subsequent journey down River Grey along class I rapids (maybe class .5 rapids) finishing at a wonderful picnic with panoramic views ended the amazing day. A rare and unique day without any wind in Patagonia, with photos that are unreal, was comparable to the Base of the Tower Hike as the highlight of our entire trip. What an amazing world!

review_text: Wow, wow, just WOW! This is a must see place in Santiago. It is free, but I would recommend paying the CP2000 for the audio guide in your native language. We were expertly assisted by Nico as our guide, Daniel on the safety raft and safety kayak (who was brilliant and whose name now escapes me- sorry!!!). The day was fantastic, finishing off with lunch including pisco sours! They even have lovely dry changing rooms and a hair dryer for post rafting. Their base is brilliant; they’re also about to get loos plumbed in. My husband has rafted before and was blown away- he’d never experienced such a well organised outfit before. When our ferry was cancelled the next day we almost drive the whole way back to do the whole thing again! If you are in any doubt, you MUST go with this company! review_text: Benjamin is very dynamic and allowed us to discover places that were not included in the initial tour. We had a great stay of 3 days, thank you for everything!

review_text: Flamingo teamed up with Sajama Expediciones based in Uyuni to offer our 3 night / 4 day Bolivian day flat tour! Peter our spanish driver was a steady and safe driver who was a lovely guy, making sure we were comfortable and enjoying the tour. He spoke little English, but lucky for us we had a Brazilian couple on the tour, who translated anything we didn’t understand. You can request a English tour guide for extra money but we chose not to and wing it. The sights we saw were an absolute highlight and made the long days totally worth it. Some meals were better than others but we took it all within our stride. We also paid a bit extra for private rooms and bathrooms which we thought was worth it but is totally down to your budget and preference as a traveller. We would recommend this trip to anyone wanting to do the same from atacama desert! Massive shout out to Peter who we felt lucky to be our driver and guide and made our experience a great one!
title: Valle de Luna and 4 day Salar de Uyuni Tours

review_text: We did the 10am walking tour with Franco on the day after we arrived. It was a great way to see the city and showed us areas we would have never otherwise visited. Our guide was excellent, extremely informative and more than happy to help at all times

Friendly and knowlegable, puntual, made our trip enjoy able. We would recommend them without hesitation.

review_text: The excursion was amazing. Our guide Alberto (graduated astronomer) knew so much and could explain everything very well and in an understandable manner. It was just the two of us and he picked us up at the hostel, which was not included. We drove outside of San Pedro to a small place of his. At the beginning we took a few pictures and then we could see through the telescopes and ask questions and have a drink. He is really kind and keen on giving his knowledge to other people - it was a pleasure. We can totally recommend this tour. Review of: Stargazing Tour in San Pedro de Atacama
title: Amazing experience

review_text: Great wine tasting and cultural experience! Danny was a truly wonderful host and considerate of our group. We had so much fun tasting the wines, learning about the vineyards and enjoyed conversation with our group and Danny. All 3 wineries were top tier and we were well taken care of throughout. Highly recommend booking this trip as its a bargain for the price! Thank you Danny and Juan our driver! Review of: Casablanca Valley Wine Tasting Including 3 to 4 Vineyards
title: Excellent experience - highly recommend

review_text: Our B&B host in Valparaiso found Ritoque Expeditions and arranged for a ride the following day for my husband, myself and our 2 teenage daughters. An easy 30 minute drive from Valparaiso, the location is spectacular - high on a hill with 180 degree views of the ocean and beautiful sunsets. We wanted to stay overnight in Concon but couldn't find a hotel or cabina to our liking or budget. Owners Maria Elena and Sabastian (who are refreshingly on the "hippy" side) offered their guest cabin for $60 US but warned it was rustic. Upon arriving at this wonderful destination, we were greeted by a few friendly dogs, cats & ducks. Maria Elena explained that one of the ducks had bonded with dogs and followed them everywhere. There was also a litter of piglets that entertained us with their games, a new hatch of chicks and then the horses, of course! We felt like extras in a Dr. Doolittle movie! We LOVED the guest cabin, which was built out of many recycled materials. If you are visiting Valpo - stay here instead. It has 2 bedrooms, a living room, kitchen, full bath, sleeps 7. It is not luxury accommodations, but is clean and very comfortable. The gardens are filled with flowering plants, shade trees and the patio is very inviting to sit and relax. You will not regret staying here! Sabastian & Maria Elena went out of their way to make us feel like family. The horseback ride through the dunes, forest & beach was a day we will not forget (and I didn't even get sore!) Thank you for your comments on Trip Advisor, taking the time for commenting your experience with us means a lot for us, it helps us doing things better! When ever you are around Valparaiso again...WELCOME!!
title: Highlight of our week in Chile! Great cabin and horsebackriding!

review_text: We took a tour with Guide Guilhermo to Cajon del Maipo and Thermas and it was simply wonderful, an attentive, polite, committed guide, with a lot of knowledge, he made our tour wonderful. Grateful!
title: Guide Guillermo

review_text: Very friendly Jorge Escobar and Daniela Jones. Super attentive. Very nice walk this day. Thank you very much Review of: Cable Car, Funicular and Sightseeing Bus in Santiago two days Muito obrigado por compartilhar sua experiência conosco.

review_text: There isn't much I can say really about the place. The sights are decent, but the main thing in my opinion is there are better places in the world with better sights. Wildlife is nothing special and the weather let's face it even in summer is not great. If you are in that area you should definitely go, but I would question why go to the area in the first place.
title: Decent sights, but nothing special

review_text: This spectacular building is a must see in Santiago. Impressively tall it holds the record for the highest skyscraper in South America. Lower five floors contain a shopping mall and restaurants . The highest floor is a spectacular viewing floor offering great panoramic views of the City of Santiago.
title: The tallest building of Santiago offers unforgettable views from the top floors.

review_text: What you see is what you get. It is a nice piece on the waterfront. It will also take you 30 seconds to see this location, then time to move onto the next.
title: Nice, takes 30 seconds
