review_text: One of the must-do trips in SP de Atacama. Give yourself time in SP to aclimatise to thenaltitude first if you came from seal level.
title: Great trip

review_text: Ciro and his wife are very friendly. His wife prepares a nice gourmant tea before and after the day ride. The view is amazing through the trip and Ciro is very experienced. However he did not offer safety helmets. Also he did not adjust our leg holders so we were all hurting throughout the trip.
title: Amazing trip - safety could be better

review_text: The best for sure, every tour we met a different guide, NICO, EDGAR AND GUILHERME, all attentive and fun. We took 3 tours with them and it was super worth it, but the best driver is Sebastian who made us feel safe and fun! Thank you for the experience
title: Best choice in Chile

review_text: My 16 year old daughter and I travelled to San Pedro de Atacama to experience the world-famous wonders of the Atacama Desert. I chose to work with Jorge of Cota6000 based on other travelers' reviews, and he definitely lived up to his excellent reputation. He is a wonderful guide and a very kind man, extremely knowledgeable about the geology, wildlife, history, and culture of the Andean Altiplano. We learned a tremendous amount! He is patient and very attentive, a great driver off-road and on, careful of his clients' well-being, and a fun and stimulating conversationalist. He customized our itinerary to suit our interests and was always adaptable to variations in plans. I want to contextualize this extremely positive review by adding that I have traveled widely in very rough terrains around the world, and I have hired many guides. Without hesitation I feel that Jorge is the best guide I have ever worked with! I hope to have an opportunity to work with him again. Thank you Kenneth, I hope to meet you again as well, and discovered this wonderful hidden places in the Altiplano. I am happy you enjoyed this trip! Best regards, Jorge
title: Amazing and Unforgettable Experiences

review_text: This turquoise/white river is a hidden gem in the otherwise pictureque landscape of small fields, meadows with sheep, cattle and horses, dramatic snowcapped peaks all around. Literally speaking the river is all around you and yet mostly invisible except for a couple crossings. The way to experience the Futaleufú river is to go on a rafting trip and there are several, excellent operators out of Futaleufú village, most of which very reasonably priced. Outdoor Patagonia is one of these.
title: Excellent rafting

review_text: Lastarria has been renovated during the last 5 years. During daytime there are lovely places to drink coffee with something sweet as the Chileans love their cakes. Nice restaurants and shops to visit. Lovely atmosphere. University area with students living here. Night time this area are vibrant. Barrio Lastarria is a MUST to visit when you are in Santisgo.
title: Vibrant at night

review_text: Really amazing experience ...Cost was 100 dollars per person but it was worth it for a day out...Very good both guide(Sebastian) and the driver-entertaining stories.Fully recommend as visiting Santiago and not seeing the mountains is akin to visiting London and not seeing Big Ben...If you are Ukrainian/Russian and used to cold climate-water in the lake is quite warm and suitable for swimming(+3 degrees) Anton Dear Anton, thanks a lot for your review! They are really useful for a company like ours. We appreciate you took time to write and we really hope you had the best experience in Santiago!
title: Visiting the mountains and the lake near Santiago

review_text: My trip to Colchagua Valley was 100% fantastic all because of Francisco and Connie of Colchagua Wine Tours. We could not have asked for anything better, everything was PERFECT. Every single detail was taken care of so we could enjoy ourselves completely from beginning to end. A native of Chile, Francisco speaks fluent english and knows everyone! The tours include high end lesser-known niche vineyards and the bigger more commercial ones as well. They picked us up and dropped us off at our location in Santiago, rather than requiring us to meet at a hotel, as others do, a BIG plus! Their van was clean and new with a friendly driver. Vineyards tours and tastings, a gourmet lunch at Viu Manent and a museum tour made for an incredible day (do not miss the Colchagua Museum, an INCREDIBLE and comprehensive collection of Chilean antiquities). I will recommend Francisco & Connie to everyone without hesitation. I have never met a friendlier couple. They are fantastic at what they do and it shows!
title: Extremely knowledgeable, friendly, flexible, professional, the BEST in the valley!

review_text: This museum is situated 12 kilometres from Arica. You can either rent a bike and go there yourselve (1,5 hours) or take a taxi (4 euros). The museum has two buildings, and you will get a leaflet with a lot of information about the artifacts in the museum. Worth a visit if you are interested in these older cultures. Apart from the textiles and usual shards, they also have several mummies on display, which is very interesting.
title: Interesting museum

review_text: I bought wines in 3 different stores in Santiago. Here is where there are more promotions and greater variety but the care leaves to be desired, not only in cordiality but in care, pack the bottles anyway. It is also worth looking at El Mundo del Vino, as they sometimes cover prices.
title: Good variety and great promotions, cold service.

review_text: We had a very nice guide, the snacks provided were great! (Small tip: let us know about allergies etc. beforehand, they won't ask about them). The Valle de la Luna is definitely worth a trip. You end the tour with a relaxing view of the valley at the sunset. The short hikes were also really cool, for me there could have been more. Review of: Half Day Tour to Valle de la Luna
title: Worth a trip! Good travel agency

review_text: The beer garden is great, but the service when we went was a little disappointing. It took a long time to order drinks and when I did, they were out of beer mugs, so I had to wait until they quickly washed some out in order to get my drinks. Also, they closed their kitchen for an hour and I couldn't order food. Could have just been a busy day and they were overwhelmed, but we made the trip all the way there and didn't feel like it was worth it. Good beer though!
title: Nice beer garden, but disorganized service

review_text: We had a lovely day, from buying all the food and ingredients at the market from Valparaiso, cooking in the studio in Viña del Mar, eating the good food, drinking the pisco sour and wines, and having lovely talks with our teacher Ines.
title: Unforgettable experience

review_text: Nice wide walkways with plenty of areas to rest and just enjoy the views of the water. The whole area around the waterway is well maintained and clean. Makes for a nice place to stroll especially after and big meal.
title: Great Views and Plenty of Seating

review_text: Our tour guide, Alvaro, was great. He provided us with a great deal of information about the areas we visited and Chilean history and culture. Our driver, Angelo, was wonderful as well. We didn’t have a chance to visit the winery due to the holiday but we had some tasty snacks with two great wines where we stopped to see llamas. The Inca Lagoon and Portillo were beautiful. The scenery on the drive is spectacular. Review of: Inca Lagoon in Andes Mountain Range - Visit Local Vineyard with Tasting included
title: Wonderful day trip

review_text: Excellent tour!!! Millanti, Alejandro and Patricio geniuses. Tremendous visit to the winery and dinner... 100% recommended! Review of: Viña Concha y Toro Nocturno: Dinner Show Agradecemos de que haya compartido su experiencia junto a nosotros.

review_text: In the same days that there was the Festival there is a lot of animation and good atmosphere. Typical and pleasant place to take a picture of the beautiful square in the city of vineyard of sea
title: Very nice and well kept square

review_text: When we stopped in Curacautin, we had the chance to stay at Epu Pewen. We remember it as such a great experience as it s now our favorite hostel in Chile. Epu Pewen is simply an outstanding hostel, the owners Suyaï & Jose Miguel, and theirs employees make a huge difference thanks to their kindness & hospitality. Ideally located in Curacautin, few miles away from national parks Conguillio, Tolhuaca and the national reserve Malalcahuello, it is the best option to discover the area. The hotels inside the national parks are really expensive. If you would like to go for a trekking or rafting in the parks you can ask for information at the travel agency in the hostel. Epen Pewen is a sustainable hostel where recycling is a rule which is really unusual in Latin America. Rooms are spacious and really pleasant. The very-high quality bedding has nothing to envy to five-starred hotels. The kitchen is fully equipped and decorated with a vintage/Mapuche style which is a favorable feature. Regarding cleanliness, Epu Pewen is the most cleaned hostel we have stayed in. Common areas and rooms are meticulously cleaned every day. Suyaï & Jose Miguel will do their best to make the most of your stay and even in the worst case scenario. We can tell as we had a car accident on our first day. They supported us so much that we were sad to leave at the end of our stay.
title: The best option to visit the Araucania

title: Can’t miss it

Then to Viña del Mar and finally a walking tour of Joy Valley culminating with lunch (not included) at Casa Verde. Then we went wine tasting in a heavenly place. Everything very organized in time; without rushing but with the time necessary to make all the stops. Our guide, Pablo, gave us the walking tour with music and all the way on the bus he also played very beautiful Chilean music. Oscar is a great driver and at the end Pablo gave us a beautiful song as we left the vineyard. I recommend it 100% Review of: Valparaiso Port and Vina del Mar Full-Day Tour from Santiago
title: Your Valparaíso Avila Del Mar

They should warn about the weather, that in Val Paraíso and Vina Del Mar and colder than Santiago. We passed by the Casa Blanca Vinicula which has a Brechó, and we bought blouses for the cold! We didn't want and I didn't like making this investment in clothes that weren't good and weren't appropriate! They smelled mold and a lot of dirt! Very good restaurant! title: Chungará Lake Tour

review_text: We did the tour booked through the hotel desk and went in the afternoon. The tour was well conducted and arranged and interesting but when compared to winery tours around the world (or in the Colchagua Valley or Casablanca Valley in Chile), it is average. Mind you, if you have time it is a lovely way to spend an afternoon albeit that the wine is, well, we have had better. Great history and interesting for those not familiar with vineyards in Chile. Thank you for your comments; we are very pleased to hear that you had a good time visiting #SantaRita. Kindly, Tourism team.
title: Lovely But Not Essential

review_text: Beautiful, easy to get to. Extensive, but no too big. Very pleasant to wander around and was able to see the whole thing without being too exhausted to appreciate it. I especially loved the textile collections. Would highly recommend!
title: Incredible Museum!

review_text: I done this tour with my friend last week and really enjoyed it. Our tour guide, Felipe was very friendly and interactive with the group. He had a great knowledge of the city/country and his delivery of this was really good (he made reference to some personal experiences which I felt really added to the tour). I would highly recommend this tour
title: Great tour!

review_text: Booked through Viatour. Great opportunity to get up close and personal with Magellan penguins. Boat was a workboat like covered vessel that carried around 40 passengers. Buses leaves downtown Punta Arenas at 6:30 am to their loading area between PA and airport. Back in PA by 11 am. Went seamlessly.
title: Great Trip

review_text: We stayed a few minutes from San Francisco. Therefor, it became a landmark for us on our walking tours of Santiago. The church itself is rather ordinal lay, but it's location marks it as a special point of interest. An examination of the plaques along the inner wall of the church reads like a history of the barrio. While not the most elaborate church, San Francisco is an interest site to visit.
title: The church is a landmark

review_text: Sebastian and Jimenez were great. Patient and friendly and they made the tour even more enjoyable. It was great. I highly recommend it. Five stars for Turistik. Review of: Safari Park, Wild Experience Thank you so much for your wonderful feedback! 😊 We're thrilled to hear that Sebastian and Jimenez made your tour even more enjoyable with their patience and friendliness. We're honored by your five-star rating and recommendation! 🌟 We hope to welcome you again on another great adventure with Turistik. 🚍💙
title: Superb Safari Tour

review_text: Jean Claude picked me up from the hotel at 6am, and we headed to the trails. The bike was in top notch condition, and Jean Claude provided me also with a helmet, gloves, hydration pack and all other necessary equipment for a great day. We did the "Andes Secret Spot" tour, which was almost too much for my riding skills and stamina. Fortunately Jean Claude is able to adjust the route on the go, so we took a little shortcut in the end and got to the river safe and sound! This tour was actual _mountain_ biking, and Jean Claude was a great guide! I'm definitely doing this again if I ever have a chance to come back to Santiago again! Thank you very much, it was a pleasure, keep training hard for the next step.
title: Real mountain biking!

review_text: After running the Santiago marathon, we traveled to the Termas for some much needed relaxation. It was off-season for the most part, Chilan is pretty big ski town so there was lots of peace and quiet. The hot springs fill the pools and are quite amazing to lounge in, especially to relax some sore muscles. After a few days of rest and cervesas, we ventured into the Andes....on horseback. If you get the chance, definitely take the longest trip you can. We did a half day trip. The trails are challenging but the horses and guides are excellent and very little riding experience is necessary. There are spectacular views and vistas that you see in the movies and quite an adventure can be had.
title: Marathon Reward

review_text: I couldn't find a listing for the restaurant which is located in the distillery. We actually did not do the tour so I can't comment on that. We did however wander in for lunch and had very nice piscos as well as a good meal. Would recommend as good value for money.
title: Restaurant is very good

review_text: Whilst meant to be an easy way to get around Santiago it wasn’t as efficient as one hoped. Not all bus stopping places marked so you have to guess where the bus stopped . Told service finishes at 18.00hrs but when boarding bus at 17.10:told bus wouldn’t return to our stop so ended up paying for a taxi. Review of: Hop-On Hop-Off Bus Tour with Cable Car and Funicular Hello, how are you? everything is explained and developed in the flyers that are handed out everywhere. Finally, we have service until 18hs. but your stop ends before, so you must take the bus in advance. it is not very difficult to understand how it works!! greetings
title: Iffy service

review_text: Family owned. Personalized attention. Amazing disco, atmosphere, service. Feels like a throwback to a 1960's European lodge. Oh, and the skiing is world class as long as you don't spend too much time getting to know the pisco sours. Not enough stars. Dear GringoInChile: Thank you so much for this great review! We are delighted to hear that your stay at Ski Portillo was fantastic and that you loved all aspects of your experiencie! Hopefully we will have the pleasure of welcoming you back! Warm regards, Cecilia - Guest Service
title: Simply the most amazing ski experience

review_text: This was a great day trip out of Santiago and into the Andes. We had a small group, only three of us, and our guide. After being picked up, we started driving out of Santiago and stopped at a gas station for breakfast/bathrooms. During the drive we were told about the history of the area. Once we arrived, we hiked for about an hour and a half to a spot where we had lunch and relaxed for a bit, taking in the views. Then took the hour and a half hike back. There are a couple brief areas of elevation at the beginning, but most of the hike is relatively easy. There was a lot of walking over loose rocks. We wore tennis shoes and were fine. Part of the terrain was fine dirt, we got quite dusty. Be prepared to use a “natural bathroom” if you need to go. Overall we enjoyed this trip and would recommend for anyone looking to get out of the city and experience the mountains. Review of: Andes Day Volcano 8K - Cajón del Maipo
title: Easy hike, great views

review_text: Wonderful tour with Alvaro - amazing sights, sounds, smells ....... and of course tastes! Alvaro was very knowledgeable both about the markets and food and also gave us some history of Chile. Highly recommend. My only complaint is that I was so full of great food I didn't have any space left for dinner. Thanks for your review and glad to hear you enjoyed Alvaro's work. In Chile it is the norm to make sure a guest has been offered more food than maybe they need for lunch, and we would hate to disappoint. Now you see why restaurants start to fill up until after 9pm for dinner!
title: Great food and amazing experience in the markets.

review_text: Perfect tour!!!... The Branco guide is super attentive, he made everything even better, in addition to giving amazing tips and presenting the best empanadas, he took photos and gave all the support... it was incredible!!!
title: Wonderful experience

review_text: I was buying a bus ticket from Puerto Natales to Ushuaia, asked to pay with my Visa card, was told it was declined twice so I ended up paying cash (42000 CHP). Later that day two transactions had been made to my bank account, each of 42000 CHP each, went back to the bus company and was told that they had not charged my Visa card and that it was my bank who had made a mistake! 3 days later the charges was released back into my account, but 2 days after that Bus Sur charges 42000 CHP to my card again! This time the money is gone. Has been to their office in Punta Arenas to try and get my money back, staff is not very helpful, once again they mentioned that this is not their problem, but my banks mistake! Left them with my bank account details, hopefully I'll get my money back when they realizes it's their mistake. Also had problems with Bus Marga in Patagonia, who sold me and a bunch of other travelers 100 dollar bus tickets to a bus which was already full! Never got our money back but other transport was eventually organized, staff not very helpful here either.
title: Credit card fraud

review_text: We chose this company and did ignore at our own peril some poor reviews. We were to have a transfer for 3 couples who got together via Cruise Critic. We were the original organisers so paid a 1/3 deposit up front. Our correspondence with Fabiola at the company were answered quickly and professionally up to the date of the departure. We were waiting in the hotel lobby prior to the time we were to be picked up. Half an hour after the scheduled time for pick up, we contacted the other couple, whom we had not actually met, to see if they had been picked up. No. So we attempted to contact South Excursions and it was just going to voice mail. One hour later, we received a reply from Fabiola who said to us that there had been a flat tyre and they would be there in the next half hour. When we contacted the other couple they had been told there had been a traffic jam, so we agreed to text each other about further developments Finally 2 1/2 hours late we were picked up. On the way to pick us up the driver had apparently gone the wrong way down one way streets and even during a phone call to us refused to take directions from the hotel staff. We finally found out that the driver and guide were lost! They even had a satnav that they did not even connect. Fabiola spoke to us and said we wouldn't be charged for the tour of Valparaiso! Of course we couldn't fit it in as we were close to missing the ship embarkation time that we wanted. She met us at the port and still charged us the outstanding amount and gave each couple a bottle of cheap wine and chocolates. During the transfer the guide did not say one word apart from what she had to and they even had to ask us at the port which cruise ship we were sailing on as there were several in port that day. Upon our respective return we requested a refund and after some negotiations we did receive a refund several weeks after we returned home.

review_text: We (me and 2 daughters aged 19 and 23) actually booked through the website demonades.com and purchased the recommended tours for 3 days in San Pedro. It was only after booking that I realised that Layana was the service provider (and I did have some direct negotiations with them before booking on demonades). The main reason I booked on demonades is that it was easy to navigate and flexible. I was also keen to have things booked before I arrived in San Pedro. I didn't want to spend valuable holiday time evaluating and negotiating with the numerous tour companies in San Pedro who are all trying to spruik their wares. The Layana staff in the office were polite, friendly and english speaking. The tour guides, particularly Alex (Antiplanic lagunas) and Klaus (valle de la luna) were stand out excellent. The other guides we had were good. All the tours we did ran on time (or near enough). This is not Layana's fault, but with the benefit of hindsight, I would probably find an alternative to the Tatio geysers tour. I don't think the super early start (pick up from hotel around 4:30am) is worth it. I was very happy with Layana and don't have any problems recommending them.

review_text: Me and my friend had an incredible 6-day trekking through Laguna Piuquenes, Mt. Pintor, Cancha de Carreras, Mt. Leonera, and Piedra Numerada. We were accompanied by Vicho and Haima who were not only excellent guides but also fantastic companions throughout the journey. Even before the trekking started, Vicho went above and beyond by assisting us with gear preparation and choosing a route that perfectly suited our skills and preferences. Throughout the trek, he was very flexible, letting us decide on the route each day, making the experience feel truly personalized and tailored to our group. This was not an easy trek, partially due to its 6-day duration, however both on the trail and at camp, we always felt safe, cared for, and supported. The food was delicious and different every day, which was impressive given the remote setting! The breathtaking landscapes, and exceptional guidance made this an unforgettable adventure. We enjoyed every moment, from hiking through stunning terrain to playing Dobble and Uno at the camp :) If you are looking for a guide in the vicinity of Santiago than look no further, I cannot imagine a more memorable and better organized trekking experience! Wow, Roman! Thank you for such a detailed and kind review. It was truly a pleasure sharing this adventure with you both. We’re so happy you enjoyed the trek, the flexibility, the food, and of course, the camp games! It’s great to hear that the experience felt personalized—that’s exactly what we aim for. Hope to see you again for another journey in the mountains!
title: An Unforgettable 6-Day Trek Through the Andes

The views of the lake and port were amazing. There were stunning view of the volcano from the centre of the lake - this really is the best way to get clear views/photos. We were so pleased with the sailing tour, it was 90000 for four people for two hours and worth it.

review_text: Maria picked me up from my hotel at 9am and we had a wonderful conversation about the region's history and geography on our way to the horses. We arrived at a secluded river house and met Luis, another guide who accompanied us on the trek. Luis drove us across the river in his speedboat, to where the horses were tethered. I was introduced to mine, Cassamares (probable spelled incorrectly due to my poor Spanish) who was a gorgeous and well-tempered male. We began our trek through the forest, fields and up hillsides, crossed streams and ended up at a beautiful waterfall after around 2 hours. The trek was incredibly beautiful and Maria was an excellent guide, telling me all about the flora and fauna of the area in great detail. We took some photographs by the waterfall and continued up the hillside on horseback. We finished the 4 hour ride with a very fast canter, which was exhillarating to say the least (this was a request from myself as I have a history of horse riding, but is not mandatory for less confident riders! The trip is very tailored to your ability and Maria is very easy to confide in if you are feeling nervous at any point, and can provide excellent advice and guidance about riding if needed!). Maria and Luis then cooked a marvellous BBQ with wine and dessert, before I was dropped back at my hotel at around 6pm. I cannot recommend this trip enough, Maria speaks excellent English and was extremely friendly, not to mention informative about the area! The location was surreal, exceptionally beautiful and a top location for a horse ride, the horses were very well behaved and made me feel very safe (as did the guides!). The BBQ was delicious, and overall this tour is incredible value for money. Thank you Maria and Luis for an unforgettable trip in Puerto Varas - I look forward to many more in the future! Dear Holly. It has been a real pleasure to meet you and show you this amazing ranch. I hope to see you next year . Good luck! Maria.
title: Unbelievable Horse Trek in the Mountains - a MUST in Puerto Varas!

review_text: We had an amazing time on this tour. Thankfully, we were flexible and were able to do so. We also departed much later at night so that the moon would set while we were out. On the tour, we got to use his telescopes to see unique features on the moon and various unique stars and constellations. We then sat by a fire and had homemade snacks and warm drinks while we waited for the moon to set. Then we were able to see the Milky Way and more stars. Alex is very knowledgeable about astronomy, and he is also an amazing photographer!! We love the photos that he took for us! This was a long night out, but absolutely worth it. review_text: The Antarctica 21 experience was amazing all the way through !!! Everybody knows Antarctica has unpredictable weather due to the high winds so sometime it's a matter of luck and we were extra lucky as we had an extra day as plane that took us from Punta Arenas to Frei Station had to leave on Day 1 which is normally spent in Punta Arenas for briefings and sorting out boosts that they provide on loan for everyone (free). The staff was amazing ushering us and sorting out boots and everything on the go. Honestly having a 2 hour flight as opposed to 2 day journey through the Drake passage is a game changer. Allows you to enjoy the trip form start to finish with nothing but highlights. Basically 4 days compressed in 4 hours! Plus the 75 passenger planes are painted like penguins what's not to love ! We managed to go to lots of very different spectacular locations with the most epic views and amazing wildlife: dozens of humpback whales around the ship at times, orcas swam right next to the ship one afternoon, we saw 3 types of penguins (chinstrap, gentoo and adelie), leopard seals and many birds (skuas, sheathbills, cormorants, etc)! The crew was absolutely outstanding, I was utterly amazed by everyone and their life stories that they shared giving short presentations through out the journey (AJ went to the north and south pole skiing!, Nico climbed a mountain in Antarctica in crazy conditions, Steve made a wild polar bear sit and so many other crazy stories!). Since it was xmas the staff did a little dance and song show which was adorable! The cabins were very confortable and large with a really nice warm shower with great pressure (essential!). The food was very good and considering I'm vegetarian I had many great options for the buffet breakfast and lunch as well as really outstanding 3 course meals in the evenings. And finally the polar plunge (basically taking the shortest dip ever in the Antarctic) was a great way to end the journey with yet another great memory that I will cherish forever. What can I say I just loved every second of it :) Dear odi2k, Thank you very much for sharing your experience, we're very happy to read that you had such an incredible journey and that you enjoyed this beautiful continent! It seems like you had great luck as well with all the wildlife sightings! At Antarctica21, we're very happy to have such an exceptional team of expedition guides, we make sure to always have a variety of specialized backgrounds, who are also passionate about the region, and experts in guiding our travelers to the best sites. The polar plunge is definitely a great experience as well, I'm happy that you decided to join that adventure! Thank you again for sharing your experience with us!
title: Loved every second of the epic A21 experience! Highly recommend !

review_text: I'm a local expat and have taken all 3 tours (AM, PM, night). This is the best way to see Santiago. The AM tour shows you the real Santiago - markets and murals, Neruda and the main plaza. The PM tour hits to historical highlights - from the city's founding to the coup. The night tour reveals a side of Santiago that very few visitors see - local parks and hidden bars/restaurants. Skip the sterile bus tour, hop on a green bike, and get ready to enjoy yourself.

review_text: Any decent winery will explain and demonstrate the production process. Not Concha y Toro !! Then to a "tasting" of a white wine but no spittoons and no crackers or bread to clear the pallete. Then we were herded through a cellar, lights turned out and we had to endure some childish story of how the devil was kicked out of the cellar.... Really, please we are adults. Then to another table where 2 red wines were offered, again no real explanation, too much for a taste and no pallete cleanser between the two; however a couple of the party were observed topping up their glasses! We were then expected to go to the shop and pay much more than in downtown Santiago. So disappointed that I will probably avoid drinking this brand in future. A local resident later said we had opted for one of the worst winery tours around

review_text: 5-Star Review: Maipo Valley Wine Tour with Oscar & Rameses What an unforgettable day exploring the Maipo Valley with our fantastic driver, Oscar, and our incredibly knowledgeable and engaging guide, Rameses! From start to finish, this tour was perfectly curated, blending top-tier wines, stunning landscapes, and rich cultural insights. We began at Undurraga Winery, where we enjoyed a full vineyard and winery tour that was both informative and immersive. The ecological and Mapuche-inspired approach to the land, plants, and winemaking was truly inspiring. It was refreshing to see such authenticity and respect for nature woven into every aspect of the process. Next, we visited Santa Ema, where we indulged in a carefully selected wine tasting. The hospitality was exceptional, and the wines showcased the region’s depth and character beautifully. Lunch at Zinfandel restaurant in Isla de Maipo was a fantastic choice—self-pay but well worth it for the quality of food and the relaxing ambiance. It gave us a chance to sit back, reflect, and prepare for the final stop. The last winery was a new and exciting discovery, rounding out the experience perfectly. While the tour description mentioned four wineries, we actually visited three, which was just the right amount—any more would have been overwhelming. A personal note: this was my second time trying Pisco, and while it’s not quite my taste, I appreciate the opportunity to experience such an important local spirit. Overall, the guest treatment was top-tier, and this tour truly delivered an enriching and memorable experience. If you’re considering a Maipo Valley wine tour, look no further—this is the one! Review of: Maipo Valley Wine Tour with 4 vineyards from Santiago. The wineries that you describe in a detailed way are specially selected for that reason. An opportunity to enjoy wine culture on diferent levels of production. While having a great time With the guides and their knowledge. Thank you for your reveiw.
title: 5-Star Review: Maipo Valley Winery Tour and Tastings with Oscar & Rameses

review_text: The astronomical tour with Astrocoya was without a doubt one of the BEST experiences of my life! It was so wonderful that I want to go back to Atacama and do it again as soon as possible. Mario and Carolín are absurdly intelligent, attentive, careful, didactic and experts in astronomy. I researched a lot, a lot about which company to choose, and without a doubt it is impossible for there to be anyone better in the industry. I learned a lot from them who know A LOT, we had a super cool conversation and of course, I can't help but comment on the incredible photos that were taken. Mario is a professional photographer from “heaven”, he leaves you free to take the photo at your leisure and gives you directions on how to make it even better. It is important to highlight that they have several professional telescopes that give us a unique view of the stars and planets. Carolín, very careful, spent every minute checking whether the telescope was adjusted so that we could have the ideal experience when handling it. Mario, in turn, with all the patience in the world, explains to us how to identify stars even with the naked eye and ends with an incredible class, wine, pisco and snacks! I loved it, I loved it! I would like to express my gratitude and admiration for Astrocoya's work, I can't wait to return.
title: Best astronomical tour in Atacama!

Flaherty's is owned by Ed and Jen, two Californians and fronted by Craig, an utterly charming gent, also from CA. We turned up on a whim and completely un-announced to be greeted by Craig who was at the time washing the patio. Undeterred and with a fresh shirt on Craig set about a guided tour of this charming vineyard complete with wonderful stories and loads of history. So impressed were we with our visit that we decided to return for one of Jenn's inspired meals two days later. The meal was three courses with Flaherty wine to match and was wonderful. Thanks to Craig as front of house and to Jen for her wonderful cooking and presentation my wife and I had one of the most charming lunch time meals we have had since leaving the UK on a round the world trip. Don't miss Flaherty Wines out if you are visiting the area around San Filipe, it is a charming place with a great story and is run by truly inspired people

The only reason it wasn't 5 stars is because the actual amount of time on the water was much shorter than we were expecting; only about an hour. We were having a lot of fun so wanted to continue for longer! Hello Clare Thank you very much for your opinion about the trip on the Petrohue river. We depend on the water level on the river as we raft on a free flowing river. Levels depend on the rain and snowmelt we have. These months have been very wet and the river very high. This amount of water makes 1h40 trip much faster when you have twice more water. The flow pushes us faster and at the same time it is harder to get to eddies to stop. And last but not least, when temperatures are not that high we do spend much less time jumping in the water and swimming around with our guests than we do in summer time. Hope it helps. Thank you again. Richard Carrier

review_text: I used Huella Andina Expeditions (HAE) for a one-day attempt on Osorno volcano just outside of the small town of Ensenada. From the first moment of email contact, Jose Miguel was responsive and thorough relative to answering questions about logistics and time for an Osorno ascent. HAE was one of two mountian guide companies that CONAF has authorized to operate in Parque Nacional Vicente Pérez Rosales for Osorno climbs: http://www.conaf.cl/parques/ficha-parque_nacional_vicente_perez_rosales-28.html I chose Huella Andina over the other company because Jose was more flexible in accomodating my schedule and it appeared that HAE had more experience mountain climbing and guiding. Jose is friendly, safety concious, intelligent and passionate about mountain climbing/guiding. He is an experienced technical alpinist. He is very familiar with the park/area and is on very good terms with the park staff/administration and speaks very good English. The gear that Huella Andina supplied was top notch quality (Black Diamond, etc). I appreciate the fact that Huella guides only small groups on Osorno as well. Two thumbs up.

review_text: This review is for our all-day tour of the Lagunas Altiplanicas and Salt Flats. I want to first say that this review is in no way reflective of our driver, Miguel, who was very professional. However, our tour guide, Nicole, was awful and made the entire day miserable. I've detailed the experience below, but in short, Nicole has no business leading these tours and needs to take a basic course in politeness. Nicole arrived to pick us up at 7:15 AM (we were told pick up was between 6:30-7:00 AM). She did not apologize for the late arrival. We then rode around San Pedro for another 30 minutes, doubling back and forth for guests who apparently had overslept. During this whole time, there was no explanation for the driving back and forth, nor an apology. When a young woman from another hotel asked if there might be additional room in this van (there was an empty seat), Nicole curtly told her, “no!” and slammed the door. The entire time we were waiting, Nicole offered no explanation of why we were stopped. When I asked her in Spanish about why we were waiting and at what time we would return this evening, she told me to “calm down” and refused to give me an answer. I was left speechless - this was literally our first hour into the tour. She insulted my mother’s hearing later on by implying she couldn’t hear her explanations. She would frequently give a detailed explanation in Spanish, but incredibly short explanations in English. I’m bilingual and noted the significant difference in her commentary. There were also times while we were driving in which she would point out notable things in Spanish, but wouldn’t bother to translate for the 6 others on the tour who didn’t speak Spanish. Above everything else, we were originally told the tour would return around 4 PM. Instead, we were back in San Pedro at 6:15 PM. This was problematic because we had booked an evening tour that departed at 6:30 PM. Thankfully, we raced over and made it just in time. All in all, it was an unfortunate experience. I live in Chile and am used to things being a bit late, the Spanish and English translations being a bit different, etc. But this woman’s behavior was completely inappropriate and left a horrible impression on all of us, especially on my mother and sister who are visiting Chile for the first time. Dear leonor For us as an agency is really important the opinion of our clients, this claim it was presented to our ex tour guide and also it was delivered to the operation boss and we take the mesures of the case. so we spoke with nicole and she really sorry about the situation that you have to live in the tour. In the name of the agency we say sorry to you and I hope that this situation dont give you a bad look of the agency Grettings:
title: Awful Experience with Nicole

review_text: I decided to do something a little different for New Years this year and I looked into booking an adventure vacation somewhere I'd never visited before. I ended up picking a whitewater rafting vacation with H2O Patagonia on the "Futa" river and had one of the best vacations of my life. The scenery was beautiful and ever changing. We hiked in the Andes, got to raft some pretty powerful rapids on the Futa and even do some inflatable kayaking on a nearby river. Each day was a new experience and a new challenge, but each night it was really nice to return to the camp with its wood burning hot tub and truly amazing food and views of the snow capped andes and the sound of the river below. The best part of the trip, other than the amazing people I met at the lodge and the sights and adrenaline rush of whitewater rafting, was definetly the staff at H2O. They pampered us all at every chance and always made sure everyone was having a good time. The guides were especially exceptional, and made me feel very safe, even on class IV and V rapids! To anyone looking to travel in Patagonia I definetly recommend Futaleufu and H2O Patagonia.
title: Whitewater rafting on the Futaleufu River

review_text: Unfortunately I had a very bad experience, I booked tours 1 month in advance, 1 week into the trip I had to exchange Farellones for a snowy valley due to weather conditions, so far ok! Portillo tour scheduled for Sunday and the agency saleswoman informed me that I should go on Saturday as it would snow and close the road, ok so we went on Saturday but the preference was Sunday as we arrived on Friday and we were tired, but I stayed there for 5 days and not one day it snowed or the road was closed, so I felt stupid as this was an excuse to rearrange the day of the trip as they know the weather conditions very well, so Vale Nevado was scheduled for Sunday at 10:30pm on Saturday after almost 2 hours of sending a message to the seller without She answered me and paid attention, because I needed to know what time we would leave on Sunday, she sent me a message saying that the tour was canceled because the driver had an unforeseen event, we had a fully prepared itinerary, in conclusion we had to change everything, I was unable to go to the cable car because with changes in days what was left, the cable car didn't open, not to mention that the saleswoman is very lost, when I arrived at the snowy valley she sent me a message "how was the ride in Portillo"? Since I was in the snowy valley and had already been to Portillo, in short, lack of commitment, no customer support, disorganization, I don't recommend it!

review_text: For someone who usually does not like tours but have no choice with no own car and didn't want to bike to the site in the heat, I went with this company and had an enjoyable afternoon. Paula was our guide and she was attentive and enthusiastic. We covered the few key sites and the pace was good. For travelers who may not have stronger physique to go on the one hour hike, they can choose to opt out. Few of us walked a bit slow and we could have missed some info from the guide during the hike. Do get prepared with a big bottle of water, good covered shoes to hike, warm clothing after the sunset, and head flash light for the caves so that you can use your hands for climbing. Before the tour, I didn't receive any advanced notice of what to prepare and only did some homework through reading the TA reviews myself. Emailed the agency about shoes but only got reply the day of my arrival. Good that I brought my hiking shoes. Didn't bring any warm clothes but glad that we rushed to the van once sunset was done. Still try to bring it with you as you can leave stuff in the van. If one decides to stay in town for dinner after drop off, it will become useful. Overall, glad that I joined this tour.
title: An enjoyable Valle de la Luna tour

review_text: We came here as part of a cruise ship excursion from Puerto Chacabuco. The drive to get here is scenic and mountainous. This park may have an admission fee. We came here with a bus tour and had to pass through an entrance station. There is a visitor center with a little museum. All information is in Spanish only, but there are instructions on how to get English translation on your smartphone. Circling the visitor center is an easy loop trail through the woods which takes about 15 minutes, suitable for all ages. Scenery is mainly just woods with a view of the Simpson River. There are other longer trails available although we didn’t have time to explore those trails. It appears to be fairly new.
title: Easy loop trail

review_text: To the West of Torres del Paine, and still within the National Park, this is the largest glacier in the Park. It slopes down toward Lake Grey and is shrinking every year. Smaller icebergs float on the lake, the result of continued calving. Hiking around the lake, to get close to the glacier is a great wonder and good exercise to boot.
title: A humbling giant, and a reminder of climate change

review_text: Horrible! When booking our tickets to Torres Del Paine, the salesman at Puerto Natales pressured us into getting roundtrip tickets, which we were told were open-ended and could be used for any of their return trips. The catch- they don't run frequently, and they don't follow the schedule that they advertise. It is much easier to buy the tickets at your leisure from whichever bus company is available when you want to return. We had rushed back to the park entrance at 12:25 for Gus Gomez's 12:30 bus, which didn't exist (schedule printed on the ticket for proof). We ended up using Bus Sur and paying another 7,500 pesos (~$11 USD) per person.
title: Horrible. Use Bus Sur.

review_text: The church was colourful on the outside with a beautiful wooden interior. It was situated next to a nice town square. Easy to find as the yellow spires were clearly visible once you are near the centre of Castro.

review_text: What an incredible experience - I must say I had high expectations after reading the reviews on the overnight stargazing experience but Jorge exceeded them all. We spent the night in a remote location near the Valley of the Moon and were treated to a beautiful sunset (accompanied by cheese and wine) as we prepared for our astronomy lesson. Jorge took care of everything, from setting up our tents to preparing a campfire dinner in an old miner's bus. It was something you couldn't dream up. The meat and potatoes of course was the actual tour of the southern sky. He taught us the wonderful history of astronomy before we began and made sure we understood how fortunate we were to live in a time when this was considered common knowledge. It made the experience that much more humbling. If you're considering any sort of tourism and want the deluxe treatment in the Atacama, Jorge is your man. I hope to visit again some day - what a time!
title: Nostalgia for the light

review_text: We spent am amazing two days in December with Tom Taylor (the owner of Bodega Wine Tours) and his driver, Alberto. Tom is originally from the UK, but has lived in Chile for six years and forged excellent relationships with winery owners during this time. He does both group and private tours. He is fluent in English and Spanish. We arranged two days of private touring in advance. We appreciated his thorough and detailed planning and advance communication. His pricing is incredibly reasonable. Tom picks you up at your hotel (for us this was the Santiago Airport Holiday Inn) and delivers you back to your hotel at the end of the day. He picked us up at 8:00 each day and returned us around 4:30. Transportation is a very comfortable six seat van. The first day we toured three wineries in the Casablanca Valley and had a delightful lunch. (On private tours, the cost of the tastings and lunch are not included in the tour price. On group tours, the cost of the tastings is included. Not sure about cost of lunch on group tours.) Tom's tours are extremely reasonable in cost either way. In the Casablanca Valley he took us to two smaller boutique wineries first. We had amazing tastings with nuts, cheese and crackers. Got to explore the vineyards. Wine was amazing; huge pours. At the first winery we tasted both their pinot noir and chardonnay. At the second winery we tasted 7 different wines. We rounded out the tastings with a visit to a large producer (Quintay-a consortium formed by twenty different grape growers). Tasted eight wines there. The contrast between the small and larger producers was quite interesting. We finished up the afternoon with lunch at Casabotha restaurant. The next day we toured the Maipo Valley. Again we visited two boutique wineries and met their owners. We thoroughly enjoyed tasting their wines (Malbecs and two blends) and hearing about their operations. Very generous wine pours, delicious cheese, nuts and crackers to accompany the tastings. Both owners were so hospitable. The final winery visit was DiMartino (a large producer). Very nice tasting there as well with some unique wines. Lunch at Zinfandel Restaurant. We highly recommend Bodega Wine Tours. Tom and Alberto make the visit fun and educational. Tom caters to your every need or request. If you are visiting Santiago and want to do a wine tour, Bodega Wine Tours is the only way to go. ENJOY!
title: Outstanding Chilean Wine Experience

review_text: Most of the day is on the small bus (15 guests). Starts with driving around picking up other folks at their hotel. I was lucky because I was the last to board. After an hour you stop for coffee. Another hour driving you arrive. You spend an hour walking along a road around a beautiful lake. You then head back slowly. Stop at a waterfall and have a snack with wine. Stop and walk through an old train tunnel. Stop in a small town for 1 hour and either have lunch or shop. Your choice, you pay. All the while the guide explains, in spainish and english what you are seeing. This is an easy trip! You walk as little or as much as you want. Not high altitude. Only 1 mile of dirt road to drive on. Only negative...you are not alone. There will be other buses and cars doing the same thing. Because it is easy it is popular. Worth every penny. Personally, we were lucky to have a great guide and driver. And met great travelers from all over the world. Do not hesitate to contact us the next time you plan on visiting Chile, it will be a pleasure to welcome you once again. See you soon! Best regards, MTO Tour Team

review_text: If your dream is to see the Milk Way and nearby galaxies on naked eye, you will need more than Atacama super-clear skies and dim city lights: you will need as little moonlight as possible. Even a quarter moon can spoil the dream of perfect observation. The standard tour runs from 9:00pm to close midnight in any condition of moonlight except full moon. So the perfect night vision is not warranted. If you get disappointed with the moonlight during the tour hours, there is a hint that the guides do not always share: acquire an Astronomy app, search for the hours when the moon is below the horizon (maybe 3:00 or 4:00am...) and simply get out of your hotel room at that time and look above. It may give you a view closer to your expectation. If your interest is in information, in a brief naked eye observation, and in the opportunity to see a few deep sky objects through the telescope, all packed in a 2-3 hours experience, this tour is for you. Most interesting above all is the lecture about how different cultures (including Andean cultures) figured the sky objects.
title: Beware of the moonlight

We will look for Foto-Ruta wherever we go in the world in future and hope they will be there, as it is an excellent way to get to know a new city without just falling into the usual tourist routes. Sitting in the fish market in Santiago over a glass of wine with Cat as she offered great advice on the pics we had taken was a lot of fun and got us inspired for the remainder of our trip.

review_text: We went with a Show Travel tour (based in Iquique) and spent 12 hours in the park between driving and visits. It was amazing; geysers, thermal baths, mountains, volcanoes, pueblos and so much wildlife and unexpected vegetation in different parts of the park. We saw all 4 types of South American camelids! And flamingos! I recommend going with a tour guide who can explain the history of this region, the Inca presence, the significance of its wildlife and fauna, and the story of the indigenous people who cared for and respected this land and continue to do so today. You won't see many other tourists and you can truly get a slice of life in the desert. Unfortunately it's not a well protected park, which allows tourists to litter and get stupidly close to the historic and impressive petroglyphs. If you go, please respect this space and its beauty. Be sure to pack water and snacks as food is hard to come by. Highly recommended.
title: lovely park, so much natural beauty in the desert, go with a tour

review_text: I highly suggest seeing Glacier Grey when visiting Torres del Paine. It was the highlight of Patagonia. There is a hotel on Lago Grey that has a boat that goes out a couple of times a day. You have to hike down to the beach, walk a rickety bridge to a dingy that takes you out to a larger boat. The boat takes off and you see enormous blue and clear pieces of ice floating in the milky grey waters. The surrounding Andes mountains are breathtaking and weather changes constantly. As the clouds move, more mountains appear. It was probably a 4 hour excursion. The boat takes you through the icy, grey waters to the glacier. Then you all toast your Pisco Sours with the glacier ice in your glasses! I'll never forget this day.
title: Amazing!
