review_text: The agency Discover Chile m served super well. From the beginning of the contracting of service packages until the end of the tours. I want to leave a special thanks to the guide, Johana, who served us very well, very friendly and polite, in addition to an exceptional professionalism. I'm very pleased.
title: Very pleased with the whole team!

review_text: The Costnera Center is the tallest building in South America, and offers a 360 degree view of the city. It is very nice, but a bit pricy. Paid 15.000 CLP. Personally, I enjoyed the view from Cerro San Cristobal and Cerro Santa Lucia better, and both are for free. But if you are not on a tight budget, go for it! Nice way of getting an overview of the city.
title: Nice view

review_text: You gotta go to this beautiful and stylish park during sunset, you won't regret. The peaceful environment of kids playing, dogs walking and people just sitting around chilling is something to behold. Go ahead and appreciate the beautiful sculptures that make this place so special
title: Go during sunset

review_text: Excellent Geyser tour of the Tatio de Pukarumi, exquisite and hearty breakfast, prepare it right there. We were guided by Rudolph, very friendly and perhaps too energetic to be 4:30 am. Hahahaha, very well prepared, on the trip he took infography of the animals we were watching. The exquisite and hearty breakfast is prepared right there in a nice location. Review of: Half Day Tour to Geysers del Tatio
title: Nice experience

review_text: Had an amazing tour of the beautiful City of Santiago yesterday. He is so knowledgeable, funny, and helpful. We loved the tour and highly recommend it.
title: We love Franco!

review_text: It was an amazing experience - the beautiful setting and very well kept horses with a fine character made for an unforgettable morning ride. Not only was the riding very enjoyable, but I also learnt a lot about the premises and the process of making wine. Thank you again and I hope to be back soon. Charlotte: Thank you very much. Best regards Rodrigo
title: Morning ride through wineyards

review_text: Climbing the active volcano and making it all the way to the crater is a lifetime experience! Not only the challenging of the ascent is rewarding but also the view from the top as well as the fun from the way down sliding on ice and snow!
title: Amazing and thrilling experience!

review_text: The old historic cathedral did not survive the 1939 eartquake that hit the city. Instead this new church was built on the site. It dates from the 1940s and 50s, a period of scarce resources, which is reflected in the modesty of the structure. Consecrated in 1964 as not just holy, but most holy (Santísima) conception. Paid my respects to the red cross at the entrance in memory of Sebastian Acevedo who set himself on fire in front of the cathedral in 1983 to protest the arrest and torture of his children by the Pinochet regime.
title: New cathedral from the 1950s in central Concepcion

review_text: Beautiful wine estate and very interesting winery tour. Not only you learn about the estate, the grapes and terroir, but also there is an excellent Mapoche museum on the estate ( last part of tour). Very nice part of Chilean country side! Make a day trip out there, there is also a nice brewery Szot and restaurant Talacante 5 min from estate.
title: Beautiful winery, excellent Mapoche museum and superb wines

review_text: This was part of the tour we booked when docked in Puerto Montt. Good walking trails and not difficult. Lovely falls, rivers and foliage. The Petrohué Waterfalls inside the park are gorgeous and there are fabulous views to Osorno Volcano. This is a great stop for everyone of all ages. There are also some lovely shops near the entrance to the park.
title: Great National Park

review_text: Our guide Benjamin was great! He knew a lot of interesting facts and he also took some nice photos for me. The food I ordered at the beautiful hotel overlooking the lake was also amazing. I'm very happy with the tour overall. Review of: Inca Lagoon in Andes Mountain Range - Visit Local Vineyard with Tasting included
title: Very nice tour

review_text: I had one day to experience Santiago, and chose City Trekking to help introduce me to this city. The pre-trip communications with Sven couldn't have been better. He was always quick to reply to my questions, via whatsapp or email. Ignacio was a great guide, and showed me how Santiago, and Chile, has been affected by the recent protests. The visible damage caused by the protests served as evidence to their impact on daily life. Santiago, and the overall history of Chile, is worth exploring, and if you only have a day to experience it, I highly recommend the full or half day city tour. Review of: Authentic Walking Tour Santiago, Chile – Full Day Hi Jenifer, firstly, thank you for your reference. We appreciate you took the time to write this. Moreover we are very glad you were happy with our overall service. Please feel free to contact us again, Best regards from Chile
title: good overall intro to Santiago

review_text: I got the trip with an agency. However, they didn't have any added value. The guide knew few about the place. He spoke Spanish and a little English. Moreover, everything could be reached by bicycle. The view is very standard. You see dessert and salt stones. There is a small cave, so bring a flashlight with you. The sunset isn't enthusiastic. It is very banal. I would recommend to don't come this place. If you do so, do it yourself and not by an agency.
title: Wast of time - standart dessert view

review_text: We booked the astronomical tour with the agency and the experience was perfect from start to finish. For starters, the agency doesn't simply cancel the tour if visibility is bad. They postpone it every hour, greatly increasing the probability of seeing clear skies and, as a last resort, they also change the day. Arriving at the location, the entire experience is designed in an immersive way, the guide/speaker is very charismatic and explains everything clearly and captures your attention. Furthermore, it has the added bonus of a lual with a bonfire and live local music, completing the unique experience. I recommend it without a doubt, it’s unforgettable.
title: Astronomical tour with Rock and Tours

review_text: Amazing excursion and very passionate guide! We really enjoyed both the walk and all the facts on history and politics - helps to understand the country better!
title: Best tour

review_text: It was a great and perfect organized tour. The guide knows everything and was able to answer the question. Breakfast was top! Dear Christian Thank you very much for your nice comment and experience with us, for us it was a great pleasure to be at your service. Come back soon!!!
title: Great tour

review_text: Liked the well-organized paths to view the falls. However, it is a bit of a walk from the entrance to the falls, so if you have problems with walking, it may not be such a good place for you.
title: The Petrohue Falls was a pretty place to Visit.

review_text: The views were amazing! I took so many photos and videos. Juan was an excellent guide: very friendly, knowledgeable and organised Review of: Cajon del Maipo: El Yeso & Spa reservoir in El Morado Hello, thank you very much for your feedback. We are glad to hear that you enjoyed your experience. It is nice to know that our staff provided excellent service. Best regards!
title: Worth every penny! Shout out to the guide, Juan!

review_text: The climbing with Richard and Nicolas was an amazing experience! They both have a lot of experience and you can see that they know what they are doing. They offer a really good equipment and yet their tour might be the cheapest you can find to go to volcano Villarrica. Above all, Richard and Nicolas bring with them great spirits and brilliant sense of humor which make all the trip become a really great time! Review of: Terra Volcano Pucon - Climbing Volcano Villarrica Thank you very much to you! We always want to give our best so that you and the many who prefer us, always have the best experience. Terra Volcano Team.
title: A great volcano climbing experience with Richard & Nicolas

review_text: The safety and professionalism of the agency made the tours peaceful. I am very afraid to hire tours from Brazil, but I received the indication from a friend to look for Kátia. I thank him and Kátia for the incredible days we had in Santiago and excursions.
title: Tourism with safety

review_text: Our guides Esteban and Carlos were fun and energetic but we were a group of 12 and felt that 2 guides were not enough. Some people suffered from the altitude and the group got split immediately. Also they seemed to splinter off people into 2 groups (one to go for the summit and one that would not make it) but without little explanation of why they thought one group would make it or not. Bit odd. We did make it to the summit which was awesome but felt a little rushed “we need to go faster guys” and on the way down some of us did not feel well and the guides just motored on without checking on us too much “it is normal to feel sick”. We felt they wanted to get us down quick as the rest of the group who didn’t summit were waiting hours at the bottom. They needed more guides or another vehicle for a group that size. But did they get us to the top … yes so that was good and seemed to be good mountaineers. Review of: Ascent Cerro Toco
title: Good hike but felt rushed

review_text: Stumbled upon Bahia Utopica one afternoon and spent a good hour there look at the different collections of paintings, cards, posters and books. I was most impressed by the quality and contrast of the different artists on display. Contemporary. Hip. Whatever you want to call it it was just very cool.
title: What an art gallery should be!

review_text: Without a doubt, the best tourism company in Santiago. Super punctual and attentive. They deliver exactly the product they offer. We've been to Santiago again, we're back now and, certainly, thinking about tours means thinking about Turistik. I would like to thank, in particular, Viviane Araújo who helped us arrive on time for our last tour. She called us, made a video call, guided us to the best route and ensured we had fun! We were almost at the last minute because we received inaccurate information from a passerby. Thank you very much, Viviane! May the company value more employees like you. You are featured! Thank you, Turistik. You are fabulous! Thanks, Santiago! Always a pleasure to be back! Olá, muito obrigado pelo seu comentário. É um prazer ler comentários como este da nossa equipa, com especial destaque para a Viviana. Por outro lado, ficamos contentes por saber que gostou da experiência. Esperamos vê-los novamente quando quiserem visitar o Chile. Obrigado pelas vossas palavras positivas. Saudações!
title: Joy, fun, charm, good times, excellent bar food, fabulous drinks!

review_text: we couldn't get into the stargazing expedition recommended by our guide - so took this instead. It was amatuerish and shambolic. 21 people, 3 telescopes - just up a back road out of San pedro with lights from the road and the next door garage. The main guy knew his stuff - but spent all his time fiddling with telescopes. His English translator was hopeless (but nice). We mostly gave back and just looked at the stars .. which were wonderful we didn't even get our promised hot chocolate.... They would have made a lot of money from the two tours that night. Had we not been leaving early the next day we would have been on their doorstep demanding our money back.
title: Great stars, shame about the tour

review_text: You can definitely hire this company! They do several really cool packages around Chile, super punctual! It is worth it!
title: Great tours, punctuality and great team!

review_text: We were delighted with the agency from the moment they were cordial to us, the guides were very friendly and nothing to say about the meals being delicious. We would go back a thousand times to drink with this agency 🫶🏻
title: 100% recommended

review_text: In my previous review I complained about the service that we received as an employee was not flexible and helpful, but nothing of that took away the charm of the bike ride, which is super recommended. Yet, soon after I submit my review, the company's owner, Peter, contacted me apologizing and offering to reimburse 100% of the money. I found this a praiseworthy attitude. Satisfaction guaranteed.
title: The ride through the streets of Santiago are awesome!

review_text: I took both the morning and afternoon walks on April 8. Both guides were great (I had Berni in the afternoon - unfortunately the name of the man in the morning escapes me). Lots of great information about Santiago in general, and there were plenty of locations that were interesting to see. There was also some important and helpful discussion of the recent history in Chile before, during and after the dictatorship. Hola Rick D! So cool that you took both the morning and afternoon tours, doing both is definitely the best way to get to know this amazing city! I'll let Berni know you thought she was awesome and I'll check the schedule to see who did the morning tour and will let them know too. I'm so glad you liked the information we have in the tour, we want to teach all our lovely travellers all about Chile! Hopefully see you back in Santiago in the future, or take one of our tours in San Pedro de Atacama! Saludos, Peter
title: Good people and information, professionally run

review_text: The most incredible 4-hour long walking tour we’ve experienced! Our guide Esteban is a Valpo local - he was so knowledgeable not only about Valparaíso, but about its street artists as well (he could tell us about their stories, their craft - he even could tell us when certain artworks were painted!). He was able to answer all our questions, share historical facts and his own connections to certain places. We felt like we got a good grasp of Valpo in this tour alone as we explored through Cerro Alegre and Cerro Concepcion, weaving through the different districts. 100% recommend.
title: One of the best walking tours, run by locals

review_text: Okay to incorporate into a tour. A fair distance from down town (30 mins drive). One of the few significant sites to see in the area with mummies dating back 6,000 years. No flash photography was allowed but photos were permitted. All exhibition display information was in Spanish.
title: Interesting little museum at the university

review_text: Sergio is excellent. It offers a tour of Chilean history and makes you know not only the city, but also the historical context of each monument visited, the buildings, architectures, etc. It was simply amazing and I recommend too. Me and my husband ended the city tour with a taste of wanting more. It was a fun tour where we not only took pictures and saw sights, but also immerse ourselves in the history of Chile. Note 1000!! Review of: Santiago Center Walking Tour
title: Complete city tour by Santiago, simply amazing!

review_text: We enjoyed our day very much and our guide Sergio and driver Ricardo were very helpful and friendly and nothing was a problem. The tour took in some fantastic sights, including Aconcagua, the highest mountain in the Americas, the beautiful and stunning landscape in the surrounding Aconcagua Provincial Park, the Inca Bridge and Inca Lagoon/Portillo. We were also able to stop and get a wonderful view of the famous Los Caracoles and see some Alpacas at the beautiful restaurant where we had lunch. A highlight of our holiday and highly recommended! Review of: Full Day Trip to Aconcagua Park Argentina and Inca's Lagoon from Santiago
title: An amazing day in Aconcagua Park

review_text: Nice neighborhood with many good places to eat and bars. Better to visit at night, nothing special during the day.
title: Nice neighborhood

review_text: We brought a picnic lunch and after the trek in we enjoyed the thermal baths feeling like teenagers and enjoyed our healthy high altitude goodies before trekking out again!!!!!!!
title: Divino

review_text: The tour with Deyd was simply wonderful Everything well organized, snacks and gifts at the end of some tours, guides who are super knowledgeable about the subject, super fair prices Don't be afraid and complete your adventure with her, I highly recommend her!!!
title: Everything perfect

review_text: The tour had 4 stops. First one was a farm/small winery, second was a winery, third was a restaurant where we had lunch, fourth was a winery. Stops 2, 3, and 4 were good. Sort of standard places you’d go to on a wine tour. They had nice tastings. The first stop was terrible though. First problem was it was a combined tour with 36 people, well over the advertised cap. Second problem was it was bilingual; we always look for English only tours, and the tour took double the time being bilingual. Third problem was the length of the tour; we literally walked around the farm on this tour for 90 minutes before we had any wine. Fourth problem was the tour guide at the farm; her personality was annoying and she made it completely unenjoyable. And to be clear, this wasn’t just my opinion, everyone felt this way. About 10-15 of us were chatting the entire time about how poor the tour was and it was essentially unanimous that visit to the wine farm was terrible. Sadly I would not do this wine tour again because of the farm visit and that tour guide. Review of: Maipo Valley Wine Tour with 4 vineyards from Santiago. Usually, tours after Christmas tend to be bilingual in a Spanish speaking country. We are in high season at the moment, so we work hard to keep the high standards of the company. We are sad that you could not enjoy the first stop, which normally is the highlight of the tour. Regarding the guide, we understand she did not manage the tour well that day, and we have let the winery know. As a company we are always concerned of the opinion of our customers. Thank you for your review.
title: Proceed with caution

review_text: A simply incredible tour, Branco is an excellent guide!! Lots of information about Chile and smiles! I highly recommend it!!
title: Cajon Del Maipo Tour - Amazing

review_text: Very pleasant experience! Nacho creates a friendly atmosphere of confidence and positivity from the very first moment of the trip, the whole trip exudes positive energy and pleasant communication! Such a charge of energy remains for a long time after the trip! The tour bus is modern and convenient, the route is thought out and interesting, the whole day is full of excitement. Thanks! Review of: Valparaiso Port and Vina del Mar Full-Day Tour from Santiago A great way to enjoy your day near Santiago. We're glad you had a great time with Nacho. Thank you for your review.
title: Daily entertainment

review_text: We loved this cooking course, it was really great fun and one of our highlights of our South American trip. Ines the teacher met us at the top of the Acensor (recommend taking a cab if the Acensor not working as was the case when we were there) as planned and walked us the short way to the school. Ines in short was really excellent. She helped us to make empanadas with local salsa type dip (wow they were great), a vegetable and meat stew - very tasty, and a very simple dessert that we had never tried before and was a great fresh end to the meal. Along the way we also made an authentic Pisco Sour and the lunch we made and ate together was served with a nice Chilean Red wine. The food was great and knowing that we had helped make it was very satisfying. We were a small group which we enjoyed, and I think this helped Ines teach us so much more than cooking. We learned so much about Chile, the people, how they live, all about places, culture, food, education, way of life.... it was fantastic and more than we learned from any guide book. It was exactly what I had hoped we might also get and more- so it was great great fun. I'll definitely be making some of the dishes at home, we got the recipes afterwards and I can't wait to make the empanadas (my favourite). Martin the owner also swung by to say hello which was cool and again gave us another insight into chilean life esp for a foreigner. We loved it - you should book it and go you couldn't regret it.
title: Great Fun - give it a try

review_text: The hike to the laguna on Cerro Castillo was amazing- takes 5 hours total. Views of Lago Carrera are incredible on a clear day. It's a difficult hike (very steep) but well worth it! Can be cold at the top so bring layers.
title: Amazing views

review_text: Very pleasant excursion in the Chilean Andes. Thanks to Benjamin our guide and Alejandro our great driver. The atmosphere was extraordinary. Thanks to Benjamin for letting us taste white wine and red wine and a delicious empenada. Review of: Cajon Del Maipo Including Wine with Picnic and Empanada
title: Cajon del Maipo of madness

review_text: words cannot describe how amazing these lagoons are. wish i had not gone with a tour though, as i would have liked to spend more than 30 minutes exploring this magical landscape. crazy cold and windy, but a landscape this dramatic demands such!
title: insanely gorgeous

review_text: The beautiful view of the ocean and the waves splashed spectacularly against of the rocks by the shore.
title: Beautiful rocky shore line

review_text: Excellent Guide, super helpful and polite, knows how to direct the team. Besides being very patient with all customers
title: Otima

review_text: The tour was amazing, due to the ability of the guide Rosa to present with charm the cities of Valparaíso and Vina Del Mar. The staff was charming and made the tour excellent. About the cities, I loved to meet them and intend to return.
title: Tour in Valparaíso and Vina del Mar

review_text: Today's tours were very good, the guide Nacho and the driver were very helpful, it was an incredible experience taking the tour with them. I recommend it to everyone 👏🏻👏🏻👏🏻
title: Maipo Drawer

review_text: Our first fullday in San Pedro. All agencies we asked night before were full for trip to Piedras Rojo. Luckily we got a spot with this agency, alabalti . So happy we chose this agency. We had a Great experience. Got to see flamingos at laguna Chaxa, a few other beautiful lagunas, red rocks etc. the guide Philippe and driver Francisco were both friendly and informative throughout our trip. Next time back with family, definitely booking with this agency. Thanks for a wonderful experience :D
title: Best guide and driver

review_text: After four weeks travelling through South America and going to walking tours around Peru and Bolivia, I must say the one in Santiago was the best one! At first, I thought that the suggested 4 hours were too much, but it's amazing how time flies, especially after the quick stop for a pisco sour, or a coffee, if you prefer, in Lastaria. We were a group of nine and Felipe was an awesome guide, very enthusiastic and passionate about his town and Chile's history. His way of telling us more about the Santiago was also very engaging and it's impossible not to fall in love with it after the tour.
title: A must-do in Santiago!

review_text: We booked three tours with Turistik during our stay in Santiago. We booked the tours from the desk in our hotel. We did a private half day City Tour the first day and a private half day tour to Valle Nevado. Our guide was Marcelo and our driver was Jorge for both of tours. Marcelo is a wonderful guide. We learned so much from him. The City Tour includes a lot of walking, which was enjoyable after a long travel day to Santiago. Jorge is a great driver. Valle Nebado is a ski resort in the Andes Mountains. The drive to Valle Nevado is full of switchbacks and is also very narrow, but Jorge handled it well. We were lucky enough to see Condors while at the top of the mountain. There was time to walk around to go higher up on the mountain to get a better view of the glaciers. We wanted to get out of the city and into the Andes Mountains, so this tour for us was perfect. My third trip was a group tour to Isla Negra to see the Neruda house, and the Matetic Vineyard. The tour was very organized and very enjoyable and both destinations were worth the tour. The Neruda House sits on edge of the ocean with a beautiful view. The house is full of furniture, artwork and 1950s furniture. The Matetic Vineyard is very interesting because their winery practices biodynamic and organic agriculture, so there is a lot to learn. There was time to have a nice lunch outdoors and walk around the property. The only negative that I can say about this group tour was the time spent before the tour and after the tour for general transportation to the destination. I guess that is inherent in a group tour setting. Thank you for your comment. We are very pleased to have been able to deliver an excellent service. In Tursitik we want our passengers to return to their home with good memories and experiences of their visit to our country. See you soon. Turistik Team
title: Tours in Santiago and the Surrounding Area

review_text: They are very well-prepared, attentive, impeccable care, indicate with closed eyes to the agency, are all congratulated. Ficamos felizes demais em saber que curtiram o atendimento. Indicação de olhos fechados é um elogio que vale ouro e somos gratos demais!💛 Equipe Danny Travel Tourism.
title: Great service

review_text: This tour will forever hold a special place in our memories. Jorge's passion, knowledge and experience made for a wonderful and intimate night of observing the heavens. The sky in the Atacama desert is impressive enough but it was taken to a higher level with Jorge's explanations of how to properly appreciate the night sky followed by the use of some quality telescopes. Finally, it was the small details (blankets, hot beverages and personal gifts) that really sets this tour a part from the others. Please, do not leave San Pedro de Atacama without doing this tour. Dear Nelson, much appreciate your positive comments which do increase the interest for each night more and give better service to you. In recent years we have been looking for better methodologies to give great amount of information needed to understand the night sky allowing when the tour finish everybody comment that was easy to understand astronomy. Simple things like blankets, beverages and complimetary gift is a souvenir to remind the stargazing tour and if you return again it´ll be other and beautiful night sky experience. My Warmest Regards Jorge Corante
title: An "otherworldly" experience.

review_text: Following our bike tour in the morning we did this. We took the funicular up and the cable car to the Providencia end. Great views from the top and you now realize how extensive Santiago is. Pleasant way to fill in hour or two.
title: You don't realize how big Santiago is until here

review_text: We contacted this company because we wanted a custom tour of Valparaiso. It was a bit unusual for them to have someone just want to search for graffiti paintings in the area but they did the very best they could! We were very pleased with the results and had a delightful day there. Also asked them to reserve a lunch restaurant which again they did an excellent job. Thanks so much to Rocio and the driver for making this a great day. Review of: Private Full Day Guided Trip to Valparaíso, Viña del Mar & Reñaca from Santiago
title: Great custom tour of Valparaiso

review_text: We decided to take this tour of Valparaiso since our flight home was not til late that night. It was a fun day. Helen spoke perfect English (and Spanish as far as we could tell) and looked like she was from Sweden. We had a group of 10 so it was easy to make stops and get around. We had a break for lunch at a restaurant chosen by Helen and it was fun getting to know our fellow travelers. On the way back we stopped at a vineyard for wine tasting. The tour was very well organized. Review of: Valparaiso Port and Vina del Mar Full-Day Tour from Santiago
title: Day trip to Valparaiso

review_text: This was great fun to hike to the top and have the challenge of dong that, and some physical activity during our trip. However, it's rather disappointing to see at the top and large and very tall communications antenna was installed directly behind the statue. Also, the grounds were not very well kept in the area directly surrounding the statue - this was sad to see because it's supposed to be a respected religious site. We found the views and ambiance to be better at Cerro Santa Lucia. *Please note there is a cost to take the tram up to the top (and a long line sometimes). However, there is no fee to hike up to the top on foot!
title: Great for physical activity to hike to the top

review_text: We did both the El Tatio and the Valle de la Luna tours with Francisca yesterday. The tours were both outstanding- super well organised and the landscapes were absolutely breathtaking. Francisca was a fantastic guide- she gave us a treasure trove of information, was very knowledgeable and was friendly from the moment she picked us up in the very early hours of the day. Our driver Oscar was also great and his eggs in the morning were just perfect. Would absolutely recommend doing these two tours with Atacama Magic. Thank you Francisca and Oscar!
title: Great experience with Atacama Magic!

review_text: We had a great time on our tour, especially Valparaiso which is so interesting. Frank was a cool guide with a fluent English and it was nice he came from the area we visited. I've already recommended to friends!
title: Not to miss!

review_text: They are the newest hot springs in the area, where all the facilities are new. They have 3 big pools, one of them with roof. Also they have 6 hot tubs, for couples or a group of max 8. If you like this kind of things is very recomended. It located in the road towards termas del huife, but 6 kmts before.
title: New hot springs in the area

review_text: It's located in a geodesic dome lose to the football stadium and doesn't look much from the outside. Go in and you are met with friendly, enthusiastic and informative staff, with good English (including the guy who has only been learning for a month). There is an audio guide which explains all the exhibits around the edge in an accessible but in depth way. The staff will guide you through the star exhibits in the centre, which you can touch and on the way out you can have a go at identifying a meteorite. If you have any interest in science, this is a great place and far better than the outside appearance would suggest.
title: Great

review_text: Guillermo served us very well. There are several stops and we loved the bus ride and the kids had a lot of fun Review of: Cable Car, Funicular and Sightseeing Bus in Santiago one day Muito obrigado por seus comentários, caro viajante da Turistik. Ficamos felizes em saber que gostou do seu passeio conosco e com nossa equipe.
title: Passeio Santiago

review_text: Our tour guide Philippe was brilliant! I learn´t a lot about the city and the country. Can not recommend enough! The tour leaves from plaza de armas at 10am and 3pm every day. Look out for someone with a red t-shirt outside Cathedral de Santiago. It lasts for 4hours and include a stop at a cafe. The tour is free but there is a recommended tip of around CLP$7000 which is well worth it.
title: Fantastic way to see the city

review_text: Set in a secluded courtyard, this attraction offers a range of eateries, boutique shopping and quality art work. We enjoyed wonderful seafood in a relaxed outdoor setting.
title: Fine dining with arts and crafts

review_text: I was recommeded to take another walking tour by my hostel but decided to take this one because their walking tour in Santiago was excellent. I was not disappointed, their tour in Valparaíso was really good as well. Our guide was Felipe and he did a great job, particularly because this tour was bilingual (english+spanish both). The tour was very informative with our easygoing guide and I really enjoyed all the stories Felipe told us.
title: THE walking tour

review_text: This park is truly beautiful. There are stairs but their are also paths that will take you to the top. From each level, their is a beautiful view of the city. One level has a beautiful fountain and a small bridge. Everywhere, there seemed to be young lovers. It was worth the walk , cane and all.
title: Worth the climb

review_text: I know this might seem ridiculous - I mean how often do you get to be so close to a beautiful snow-capped volcano - but I found I was actually too close to it to fully enjoy it. Was certainly a thrill (once the cloud cleared) and glad I experienced this but I found being at the bottom and gazing at it over the lake was more enjoyable. Just saying!!!
title: It didn't wow me as much as being at the lakes

review_text: I went to lagunas cejar with Andes Travel and they did an amazing job, specially the guide Uriel! Being very well organized, providing great explanations of the nature and cool ideas for taking pictures he made us enjoy a lot.. and I saw us having more fun than the other groups, so there is no doubt that Uriel and Andes Travel is a right choice for tours in Atacama!
title: Great guide

review_text: The tour was amazing! Fernando, our Guide always attentive and gave us the best surprises: beautiful places. He made us the best photos and recommendations. I'd definitely repeat.
title: Un 10

review_text: currently no access to the falls- do NOT book a tour as you will end up being given the “alternative” which is a drive half way round the lake and back.
title: currently shut

review_text: The best way to explore the Atacama Desert and the Altiplano is with Raices Andinas. We did a 5-days tour in the North of Chile. Already our start in Arica with the first stop at the agricultural market of the city and later at the great museum of San Miguel de Azapa prepared us best for the things to come. We spend the following two days on the Altiplano 3500 – 4600 m above the sea level, discovering salt lakes and abounded villages. On the fourth day we made our way down to the Atacama Desert and stopped, for example, at the oasis of Pica or the Oficina Salitrera Humberstone. A ghost town in the middle of the desert, before heading to Iquique on our last day. Orlando, our tour guide, did a great job. He took us with him to this stunning nature and landscape on the Altiplano, surrounded by active volcanos and wildlife. Besides, the turned our focus on several topics like the history of this region, the ongoing conflict between Chile and Bolivia, but also to the harsh living conditions of the indigenous people living on the Altiplano. He gave us the opportunity to meet to local people living far beyond any streets or villages and talk with them about their way of live and their traditions. He also continued patiently stopping at any Vicuna we met to take a picture and adapted the tour to our interests. With him we had the chance to learn a lot about the unique ecological system, the (geological) history of this place and the struggle to find the balance between preserving the nature and utilizing mineral resources. If you want to visit this amazing area then I recommend you Raices Andinas.
title: Amzing experience

review_text: Patagonia is jam packed full of amazing hiking! Particularly, the Cerro Castillo day hike starting from the town of Villa Cerro Castillo is a great trail. The 3 pronged peaks of Cerro Castillo lends itself to comparison with its more well known 3 pronged counterpart. That would be Las Torres, which we were lucky enough to see on the W Trek. But with less people and hype, we hold this day hike in similarly high regard. There is a decent amount of information online about the multi-day Cerro Castillo circuit. But we are here to shed some light on the lesser known day hike option. Getting to Villa Cerro Castillo The day hike is easily walkable from the tiny town of Villa Cerro Castillo in Patagonia. If you are planning on travelling Patagonia south to north, hopefully you have visited Río Tranquilo for the incredible Marble Caves. From here, simply organise a transfer at the main bus station. In Patagonian summer as of February 2020, buses depart 8am daily heading to Coyhaquie via Villa Cerro Castillo for $10,000CLP ($12USD). Unfortunately, whether departing the bus earlier at Villa Cerro Castillo compared to the final destination of Coyhaique didn’t seem to change the price. But admittedly we should have questioned more before paying! The bus arrives into Villa Cerro Castillo around 10-11am. If you are not departing from Río Tranquilo, buses frequently head north from Cochrane to Villa Cerro Castillo on route to Coyhaquie. They should be easily booked with a day’s notice in town. Otherwise, if your trip is north to south, a bus should be easily organised from Coyhaquie to Villa Cerro Castillo. The Cerro Castillo day hike The Cerro Castillo circuit is often completed as a 4 day hiking trip. However, we had limited time in Patagonia. This day hike involves walking from the town of Villa Cerro Castillo to the laguna and back, measuring around 15km. It takes 5-6 hours. There is a steep elevation of 1.1km over 7.5km to reach the laguna There is varying consensus online as to where the Cerro Castillo day hike starts, and whether you have to pay or just jump the fence. As of February 2020, you must pay an entrance fee of $5,000CLP ($6USD) to landowners. This is because the beginning of the hike is on private farmland. You must also pay a separate $13,000CLP ($15USD) to the Reserva Nacional Cerro Castillo. The prices are extortionate for a day hike and may well put people off. However we assure you that the hike is worth it! In peak season, there are actually national park staff who will explain the trail to you before you set off. To be honest, having someone explain how to follow a trail was fairly unnecessary. It’s not rocket science! Nevertheless, the day hike itself is a very demanding uphill affair. There are phenomenal views back to Villa Cerro Castillo and the surrounding mountainous landscape on route to a stunning lagoon below the Castillo mountain.
title: Cerro Castillo Is A Hidden Gem Along The Carretera Austral In Patagonia

review_text: Claire and Felipe are two wonderful, honest and caring people with a wonderful sense of adventure. I had the pleasure of spending two trek days with Felipe, the most memorable being a hike up Cerro Paine. What is really great about Felipe is his desire to share new places, off the beaten track with visitors. The day we had planned to hike up Cerro Paine we woke up to a fresh coat of snow in late September. We assumed our hike would be rescheduled, but Felipe assured us that if we were up to it we could still go. We were so excited for the adventure. We were told we needed to have really good sunglasses, preferably polarized, to avoid getting snow blind. I did not bring my best pair and was worried that they might not be enough protection. Felipe helped ensure that I had the right gear and made it possible for me to still make the hike. While Felipe is an experienced hiker and could likely hike the mountain in record time, he is a patient guide and makes sure that we keep a pace that we all can keep up and would encourage us to ask for breaks when ever we needed. He is an amazing teacher and guide, proper hiking takes certain skills, and a certain amount of patience if non-experienced hikers are to make it up such a challenging trek. We made it up past the tree line and almost at our first summit when we stopped for a lunch break. Felipe told us that in his professional opinion we should turn back, but it was not a matter of life and death so if we wanted to keep going we could tell him so. He could see the state of the snow covered mountain and knew it was going to be tough. During lunch the wind started to pick up and we decided to listen to the professional advice of our guide. The trek down to the tree line was scary since the wind was dropping the temperature and there was no cover. But through it all we had Felipe's calm voice telling us we were fine and just keep moving, one step at a time. We made it back to tree line and immediately it got warmer and we were all joking again. Through it all I knew I could trust Felipe with my life and I loved every minute of the adventure, at least in hind-sight. That evening we had dinner together and shared some hilarious stories. These two are smart and care about the nature around them. You can feel it in the way they talk about Chile and the wilderness they bring you to. If you are looking for something different and spiritually cleansing, I highly recommend booking some adventure with Madre Roca Patagonia. Hi Fredella! Thank you so much for such an awesome review! I still remember the Cerro Paine hike day! It was cold from lunch on! "Slowly and steady is the way!". I am glad you folks had fun and enjoyed Cerro Paine, as it is one of my favorite hikes in Torres del Paine National Park. In Madre Roca, we think that there can´t be tourism without taking care for Nature. That is why we are commited to skip the most popular and over crowded hikes in Torres del Paine National Park, and we will take you to the off the beaten trails Thanks again Fredella! Big hug to Eddie! Best, Felipe.

review_text: Recently refurbished and reopened, this relatively small museum contains some of the best pre-Columbian artifacts I have seen anywhere in the Americas, carefully selected and beautifully and intelligently displayed (and with signs in both Spanish and English). Begin by going down stairs to the more ancient and archeological past. Then go up the stairs, but instead of going straight ahead, notice that left and right are galleries that open off balconies around two interior courtyards. First walk around the balconies above the two courtyards and read the excellent explanatory signs for the galleries. Then enter the inside galleries from the balconies. If you enter the inside galleries from the central hall first encountered, you will miss these excellent explanations, or only find them later. The relatively small size of this museum—selective instead of exhaustive—is a real plus. Each display has the room it needs and you have the time to enjoy it all. Among the galleries, I found the textile room, in particular, a real stunner. Also, if you go on Sunday (as I did), not only will it be free, but you will have the pleasure of mingling with local families enjoying this view of their country's heritage.
title: Exquisite and selective

I love to cook and feel very comfortable in the kitchen so I was happy to just take Ines's direction for each recipe and go with it. My husband doesn't cook as much and was extra excited to feel comfortable with some new recipes. The empanadas de pino were made vegetarian for me using eggplant instead of beef and were so incredibly good I could not stop thinking about them for the rest of our trip! Can't wait to make them this weekend. Thanks again, we loved this memory from our trip and recommend it to anyone going to Valparaiso - if you love to cook but are new to Chilean food or have never cooked before in your life you will enjoy this all the same!

review_text: We just returned from a three-weeks’ holiday in Chile; visiting Santiago, Atacama, Pucon, Puerto Veras, Eco Camp in Patagonia and Colchagua Valley. Despite beautiful scenery in Atacama and awesome experience in Torres del Paine, Pucon remains our favorite. Volcan Villarrica is spectacular and seemed to follow us wherever we went! Our congenial local guide, Agustin, is a committed environmentalist with a deep knowledge of flora&fauna as well as the culture of the indigenous Mapuche people. After a very pleasant first trek and a visit to Huife thermal springs, at short notice, we asked Agustin to organise another trek for us on the second day when he also suggested a boat trip to Isla Allaquilen on Lago Villarrica. It was a perfect end of our short stay as we were rewarded with blossoms scattered all over the island and a panoramic view at the top of the hill. Agustin is a perfect traveling companion, very attentive and went out of his way to make our trip a memorable one. Gracias por mostrarnos alguna cosa muy especial. We wish we could be back for the eclipse next year!

review_text: My husband and I booked a blind tasting and tour at the winery and were accepted even though we only booked it the night before. We were met at the entrance by our enthusiastic waving guide Marcello. First he took us out in the vineyard and showed us their grape vines and taught us to identify the different grapes by their leaves shape and color. Second we were brought into the cellars and were shown their tanks and barrels. Here we even got to drink wine out of the tanks. Lastly we were lead back up to their tasting area for a blind tasting of four wines that our guide Marcello even participated with us in. It was a really informative and fun way to try the wines without the labels and prices. We did end up guessing 2 of the 4 wines correctly. Along with the tasting we were served goat cheese and crackers and when we finished with the revealing of the wines we were told to take our time and to try more of any of the 4 wines. The wines are typical of the Colchagua region with Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Carmenere, and Syrah making up the wines that we tasted. They all had a nice fruitiness and the wines that were grown at a higher altitude were more defined in taste and had a bit more structure. Along with the tour, and tasting we were also given 30% off of our bottle purchases. The price for the tour and tasting was a bit high at 18000 pesos ($25) for bottles of wine that were between 5500 and 11000 pesos. Although, the tour and blind tasting were so great and personal that it was totally worth it for someone who is interested in learning more about the wine and region of Colchagua.
title: Very Fun and Educational Blind Tasting

review_text: Perhaps it is adequate to book their service from airport to any downtown hotels, but I tried their round trip service from San Cristóbal Hotel to Santa Cruz, the Colchagua Valley to visit Clos Apalta. I had agree to a price of US$270 to start with, as the receptionist was explicit that he offered me a “good deal” and therefore the discounted price. I settled all payment at their counter at once. To my surprise, their staff called me at San Cristóbal the night before I was about to go to Santa Cruz, and said there was a mistake in pricing and the total price for this round trip service would be US$400 in total, so I still owed them another US$130. Since I didn’t have much of a choice, I reluctantly agreed to top up the extra US$130. On the day of transfer, the driver again haggled with me about the price and said in fact the total should be US$560, so there was still a shortfall of US$160. I was very frustrated at that point, but not about the monies, rather the integrity and professionalism of this company. On my return trip, they insisted I pay US$560 or else they would not drive me back to Santiago, so I paid immediately, but what’s even worse was on my way back to Santiago Airport (as I was catching a flight to Atacama), the driver took a complete detour and we ended-up at somewhere in nether him nor me knew our whereabouts. What would originally took 2.5 hours from Santa Cruz to the airport eventually took 3.5 hours to get there, if I was not an Emerald member of the One World Alliance, I would have missed my flight because of this. So next time when you are dealing with this company Transvip, please be cautious.
title: A completely unreliable transfer service if One is going out of town

review_text: It starts with an easy boat trip. We were lucky we saw more than 10 toninas or Patagonian dolphins. A whole family with little dolphins included. Than we got to this really nice slayed spring water that is a hot spring in the sea shore. Absolutely amazing. Then they cooked some nice salmon and incredible sopaipillas. Celestino the owner , gave our kid all the stuff as he wanted to go fishing 🎣 , really nice person. Amazing easy day.
title: Excellent family activity!!

review_text: Embalse El Yeso is a must-see destination if you are visiting Santiago. The picturesque views of the vast water and mountains are breath taking. In the visit, I was first picked up from a hotel of my choice to where the Turistik bus leaves to start to excursion. I would say that there were about 15 people in the tour. They can do the tour in English and Spanish also. The bus driver was Mario and he got us everywhere on time. My tour guide was Valentina and she was great. She spoke in both languages and it helped me compare words, since I am still learning Spanish. We first stopped in a town to get snacks and go to the bathroom. Then we did some more driving and got out of the bus to start walking to Yeso. We had about an hour to explore and take pictures. I recommend walking to the very end first and then working your way back to the bus, because that is where you'll have the best mountain/reservoir photo shoot. Once you return to the bus there is juice, cheese, and crackers waiting. After that, we stop at a restaurant in the mountains. When I went there was a buffet of a lot of typical Chilean foods such a Pastel de Choclo. The late lunch wasn't included but it was worth it and the bathrooms at the restaurant are clean. On the way back Valentina helped show me where to go, so I would be able to get home quickly. She was very nice and I had a great experience. I would definitely recommend this to anyone (the hiking, well walking, was flat. don't worry) and you will for sure get amazing pictures. Review of: StgoPass: The best attractions of Santiago We appreciate the time taken in discussing your experience with us hannahupdegraff. Thank you for recognizing the quality of our service, especially the pleasant company of our guide Valentina. We are very happy to be part of your memorable memories of Chile. Come back soon! we will be waiting for you Greetings.
title: Must-See outside of Santiago

review_text: We made the family tour of the day to Lake Chungara from Arica, it was an excellent experience, Jorge, the guide, very prepared, gave us very clear information of each stop. At all times he ensured that passengers did not suffer inconveniences typical of high-altitude travel. Highly recommended to travel with Payachatas Tour!!!
title: Amazing experience

review_text: We had a wonderful bike tour led by JP who is the young entrepreneur behind this little business. His mother and father also support the business. His father makes some of the best sandwiches around and his mother does the scheduling. We took the tour out to Petrohue about 23 miles round trip. Stopped along the way to tour the national park. You can find longer trips but this was challenging enough for my wife and me. A little more uphill on the way out and easier on the way back but generally low intermediate overall. Bikes were in terrific condition. JP picked us up and drive us to the starting point about 30 minutes from Puerto Varas. He brought all the food, water, etc. for the picnic. On the way back he took us to a local brewery for a craft beer. The whole trip was enjoyable. The service was superb. JP’s English was excellent for those who don’t speak Spanish. A great way to see the area and get good exercise. Price included everything. Thank you very much for your opinion DPBconsulting, it was a pleasure having you with us, hope to see you again some day in Puerto Varas!!
title: Forget about the free bikes. Take a bike tour with these guys.

review_text: We were so excited for a unique experience to see Glaciar Jorge Montt. This is a once in a lifetime trip. We didn’t realize how hard it would be to find a reputable company to take us but Waeskar was willing. They just said they would look for more people to ride with us because we were only 4 and they wanted 6. Later that day, the day before our anticipated trip, they told us that we needed to find the other people or else pay for their spots. Not ideal and we even asked about getting a commission if we were to spend the rest of our evening hawking for this boat. Regardless, we did find 2 more people but there was no discount and we all rushed to depart by 9am the next morning. Unfortunately, our captain was 45 minutes late. We finally departed after that delay only to find out after nearly another hour that we didn’t have any gas. We had to turn around and go back, losing another hour. When we saw how much fuel they did have to load on the boat, it is baffling how they couldn’t have realized it was missing in the first place. We also had to stop 4-5 times during the journey to refuel. We did make it to close to the glacier, better late than never. There were some choppy waters which had everyone clutching the side of the boat and we had the aforementioned fuel stops, but we did dock near the glacier for a surprisingly good risotto, some soup and some cocktails. We did hike a bit but it wasn’t the hour we were expecting. We saw other boats getting closer to the glacier but ours did not get as close as theirs. On the way back, our guide, Tomas, kept coming to the back of the boat to drink pisco from the bottle the guests were supposed to enjoy. We made it back two hours later than expected and with the exchange rate, paid close to $900 USD for 6 people. The boat is nothing glamorous and the experience fell short of what we would expect for that amount of money. We did get close to the glacier but I think we would have been better off with a different tour company.
title: Better companies must exist

review_text: Family Walk, where I started the tour at Oasis Station ending at the Summit, I did the round trip. Nice, clean cabins, (there is a lack of more garbage cans on the outskirts). Also nice is the Funicular ride, up and down. I don't know if it applies to you, it's the Zoo, it's very bad, it's ugly, there's a lot of repairs, (they've been there for a long time), the few animals you see are very cramped, they don't look comfortable. Muchas gracias por compartir tu experiencia junto a nosotros y al resto de visitantes, nos alegra que hayas visitado nuestros servicios. Dando respuesta a tus comentarios, lamentablemente nosotros no administramos el servicio de Zoológico, pero de todas formas haremos llegar la información a Parquemet.

review_text: This place is definitely recommended, by tour or by rental car! Organised toures seem to arrive approx at the same time. With rental car you have the chance to be alone. We did it without 4WD vehicle. Approx the last 25km to reach the Piedras rojas are not paved and we just drove carefully. But we dont want to recommend to do it without 4x4, maybe it depends as well on the season (snow?). But the landscape with the red rocks and the white water are impressive! Do it!
title: Just GO!

review_text: 100% recommended, a free tour with tasting included. Staff are friendly and handy, the price are right cheap regards the quality

I think it's a must-see for anyone going to Santiago. Ah, it's super easy to go on your own and if you want to save money, it's an option...

review_text: Visiting for work in Santiago, we got a weekend in the middle so we visited Cerro San Cristobal. We went up with Teleférico and came down the Cable Car.. Great view of Santiago even with some smog.. must visit !!

review_text: I thought the agency was great, good guides, breakfast and lunches were good too. It was worth the experience and I highly recommend it. We enjoyed all the tours we took but the best for me was the Termas de Puritama and Piedras Rojas. Review of: 4-Day Tour in San Pedro de Atacama

review_text: I enjoyed staying in Dreams hotel in Punta Arenas: hotel staff was friendly and spoke good English, rooms were comfortable and Breakfast was good. it is close to many good restaurants as well

review_text: You can find anything you love to eat here. One restaurant next to the other...full of people, music, color

review_text: We took the tour to Casa Zerando with the guide Yuri and the driver Ravi and it was amazing! The guide was very helpful and fun throughout the day! Sunset at Casa Zerondo was incredible! We definitely recommend it!

review_text: If you would like to see the city centre from above have a soft drink and walk with your family and friends, this is great place. Specially recommended on a sunny day to have the amazing view.

review_text: We stopped in here on Easter Saturday, having wandered to the centre of Santiago. No queues, free entry, and a spectacular church once inside. Definitely worth a visit, and a great contrast to the hustle and bustle outside in the main square.

review_text: Coming from the deserts of the southwest US, I thought I'd seen it all, but this was truly special. The salt mountains and the singing rocks were quite unique. It had just enough walking and climbing without being too exhausting for older folks.

review_text: We found all three tours interesting and informative. Pablo, Fran and Francisco gave us a wonderful overview of the areas we visited, with history and personality!

review_text: This tour gives a nice blend of sight seeing with a good amount of wine tasting. The graffiti art was something I was not expecting to enjoy, but it was incredible. Review of: Valparaiso Port and Viña del Mar with wine tasting in Casablanca

review_text: If you're in Santa Cruz, you can't beat this excursion as a way to see the beautiful countryside and create memories of a lifetime. We had rented an apartment from Ian Garrett while in Santa Cruz, and this excursion was his suggestion. So glad we did it! I'm a little nervous around horses (even though I'm a veterinarian), and I didn't know anything about how to ride. But Ian was a great teacher and the horses are incredibly responsive and well-trained. I quickly lost my fear as I learned to navigate the horse and appreciate the gorgeous scenery. We truly enjoyed Ian's company, and he was a great tour guide in general for our time in Santa Cruz (he gave us so many helpful insider tips). Ian packed a delicious picnic snack for us to enjoy at the top of the hill overlooking the valley, with locally made wine, jerky, cheese, and nuts. What a great way to spend Thanksgiving! Be sure to wear jeans, long sleeves, and a hat to protect yourself along the ride. Also make sure the toes of your shoes aren't too thick - I had a little trouble squeezing my hiking shoes into the stirrups. Review of: Horseback rides Santa Cruz, Chile
title: Highlight of Trip to Chile!

review_text: I was excited to have this tour booked because it was a very hot day. Too hot to be walking all over Santiago. Spending a few hours in an air conditioned bus seemed like the perfect ticket. The bus was clean and new but the bounce is incredible. Add that to the 60 (yes, 60) hairpin tours up the mountain and it's enough to make anyone sick. Several did! I'm glad I took dramamine. The driver and guide were nice but not a lot of information was provided. There was a lot of downtime at places where there was nothing to do. The tour could have been reduced by an hour or more. We spent over an hour at a completely empty ski resort. I guess we were supposed to hike, but I didn't bring shoes for that as it was not mentioned in the description. No one did, so we just sat and waited . Then we moved to the sunset site. Cute little mountainside cafe with a perfect patio to see the sunset, but we had to wait about 90 minutes. The biggest disappointment was the tour was advertised as being in English, and while the guide did a great job of talking in English and Spanish, I was the only English one who spoke English. As a solo traveler, I took the tour hoping to meet other people, but there was no one else to talk to. It made the 7 hours even longer. Overall, it was just OK and a very long exhausting day. I think it would have been much nicer in spring when the mountains would still have snow but in the summer there really isn't much to see. Also, the empanadas are just cheese. You get 4 little ones. Since it was dinnertime, it would have been nice to just get 2 little beef ones instead. Review of: Sunset in the Andes Mountains Dear traveler thank you for sharing your experience and feedback, we are sorry that it was not entirely what you expected. We are glad that you enjoyed the air conditioning and comfort of the bus. We appreciate your suggestions regarding the length of the tour and the description of the itinerary, and we will take them into account to improve in the future. We are also sorry that the experience was not as social as you hoped, and we will make sure to improve communication so that all passengers feel included. Regarding the empanadas and the waiting time in some places, we took note of your comments in order to offer a more comfortable experience adapted to everyone's tastes in the future. Thank you again for your observations, we hope to offer you a better experience next time! 😄✨

review_text: It was, for sure, the best winery tour I’ve ever been. The same care Alice and Andres have with grapes and wines, they also have with their visitors. A special touch was our guide: Valentina. An amazing person with a great knowledge! She was very thoughtful and helped us having a personalized experience. No rush and no schedules, just good wine, good chat and good sight. I strongly recommend this tour! It’ll make your trip to Chile remarkable.

review_text: Walked by the office in Pucon today to inquire about the spa tour --first the door was closed and locked but when a young man let us in and we asked if they were closed, he rudely replied 'No'. We then asked about the spa tour and he pushed a brochure at us with no explanation about the tour or cost; when asked where the spas were located, again very rudely replied "I don't know". Really?? This is your tour and you don't know? Obviously they could care less about having any business. There are plenty of other tour companies in Pucon who appreciate your business.

review_text: We had a wonderful day visiting 3 wineries in the Casablanca valley with Kylie. It was such a relaxed experience - not having to think about anything because Kylie took care of it all (driving, bookings, choosing the wineries, selecting lunch etc.) We felt perfectly pampered! The three wineries - Veramonte, Casas del Bosque, and Viñamar - perfectly complemented each other. And of course Kylie herself is a treasure! Charming, entertaining and not getting tired of our constant questions about the wines, wineries, and Chile in general. She also gave us recommendations unrelated to the tour that were very welcome. So if you are looking to book a private tour of Chile’s wine country look no further. Just book Kylie! That you so much for taking the time to write such a great review. It was a pleasure to have you both along, and I'm glad I could show you three different wineries. I hope you enjoyed the other tips, and the rest of your time here in Chile. Thanks for choosing me for your tour!

If we compare both tours, we preferred Tracy's who had many more interesting details to share. Thank you Tracy!

review_text: Stayed at Las Torres Central, Los Cuernos, and Pain Grande all camping with their equipment. For Fantastico Sur (Central and Los Cuernos), I booked all my equipment online. At Cuernos I was told I only booked the site and not the tent which seemed a bit ridiculous so I had to pay extra there. Vertice's online site only allowed me to book the camping site so I went to their office in town to book the sleeping bag and mat. Central and Cuernos both had hot showers. The Cuernos camping sites were on elevated platforms with tents already set up. The Central site had tents already set up but on flat ground. I would recommend paying to stay at Refugio Pain Grande or heading to Refugio Grey. The camp site was crowded and the showers were cold. If you stayed in the refugio, they had a nice fire in the lounge where you could dry clothes if it rained and the showers were warm. The trails were a bit crowded so try to be the first up or hike later. For fast hikers, you could cut at least an hour off the recommended time.

review_text: We booked this tour at 9:20 the night before which allowed us to negotiate the price down to lower than we had seen anywhere else. Speaking to others on the tour who had organised other tours with them, similar discounts had been offered for multiple bookings. Apart from the price, the thing that really attracted us to the company was the fact that their breakfast seemed more generous than the others’ including scrambled eggs, bread, juice, chocolate milk, coffee, tea and biscuits. As we waited with all the other geyser-goers in the street in the early hours of the morning, we watched as everyone was picked up and wondered where our van was. The guy at the front desk of our hostel said that this company are always later than others. We were worried that they were not going to come but they were just a little late. At the time we were concerned that this would mean that we would miss sunrise at the geysers but it was not a problem at all. In fact in retrospect I wished that we had arrived a little later because we still seemed about half an hour to forty-five minutes too early for the start of the sunrise. Getting into the jeep at this very cold hour of the morning, we were each given a blanket- a very nice touch. The guide, although not speaking much English, was super friendly and enthusiastic and seemed to genuinely enjoy guiding the tour. He was a one man band, guiding, driving and cooking our breakfast but this certainly did not detract from the tour in any way. The breakfast was fantastic and as we were eating fresh scrambled eggs and drinking hot chocolate that had been warmed in the geyser I was certainly glad that we had chosen the company that we did. But what really set them apart from the others was that, when all the other groups left about 15 minutes after sunrise we remained as long as we wanted, lingering over coffee and sharing stories whilst enjoying the geysers, now in perfect morning light, all to ourselves. This flexibility to stay at locations as long as we liked, rather than being herded around to a tight time schedule as all other tour groups seemed to be, made the morning a lot more relaxed and enjoyable. As an aside, dress warmer than you think is necessary- it gets really cold!
title: Geyser fields tour above expectations

review_text: Fantastic experience, the best lagoons in the whole area. Impeccable organization with a rich final aperitif. Francisco was unique and made a difference compared to other excursions we have done. Ask him for guidance Review of: Tour to the Hidden Lagoons of Baltinache

review_text: The towers are an amazing site! If you go to Patagonia and are capable of hiking all day you basically have no choice but to go here. The hike isn’t too bad, I believe it’s probably 16-20km total when it’s all said and done. It’s a nice medium level hike for the most part, but the last hour towards the towers are no joke! It was still snowy and icy so very slippery. That being said, it’s worth it, so just prepare yourself and put on your big boy pants! We didn’t do the full W. I’m sure it’s amazing, but we don’t love being cold and wet.

review_text: The Sky Costanera is a symbol of Santiago and impresses with its size and shape. review_text: We went on a tour of laguna cejar with antonella- she was very knowledgeable, friendly and made everyone feel included. review_text: Hiking with Coigue has been one of the most amazing experiences I have had. I wanted to do something different than the regular excursions and they really made it come true. Nico, the guide, it is fantastic. He was a so kind, friendly and polite, with an outstanding knowledge about the Chilean coast and its complex ecosystems. I have done many hikes all over the world but never with such a professional as Nico. I do highly recommend the Pacific Coast Gardens excursion. It is surprising and rewarding the amount of new things that you could learn with only one excursion! We were very lucky to visit the park with huge waves, where we could personally witness the fantastic and unique “Puquen”. In addition, transportation is great, and food is fantastic. If you need an unforgettable experience, Coigue is your definitely your unique choice. Thanks guys for giving me the chance to experience such a fantastic excursion. You were lucky to see the Puquén in action! (when tidal waves strikes, a partially submerged cave ejects large sprays of sea water as waves retreat and allow rapid re-expansion of air compressed within). Pacific Coast Gardens excursion let as discover the truly untouched flora and fauna of the shoreline, just two hours from Santiago. Thanks for sharing your experience, we are truly happy that you've learned and enjoyed the hike. Hope to see you next time, Mauro

review_text: At Torres del Paine National Park, we enjoyed most spectacular views of irregularly shaped, rugged, snowy peaks diffusing into white puffy clouds. While we enjoyed temperatures in the 50•F – 60•F (10•C-15•C) range, days were misty, with constant drizzle, and gusty winds that forced us to straddle our legs while standing, so we would not get pushed by the wind. Patagonia branded wear was definitely inspired by this weather. On February 19, 2019, my husband and I hiked about 12 miles round trip to a glacial lake at the base of the Torres at about one kilometer of altitude. Our exhilarating expedition filled us with anticipation of spectacular views at every turn. We saw condors fly not much higher than us, and waters of many hues in distant lakes beneath us. Different accumulated minerals, we later learned, cause the different water colors.

review_text: We enjoyed very much the tour of Valparaiso and Santiago guided by Thomas Poussard on Dec. 18, 2014. We came off the cruise ship that morning in Valparaiso. Thomas picked us up and took us to see the interesting streets with the colorfully painted walls and the many "wall arts" in the old town of Valparaiso. If we had more time, I would definitely want to see more and take more photos. Then he took us to see a couple of places in the nearby city of Vina Del Mar - the various castles by the ocean near the Casino were nice looking. Then we visited the vineyard/winery in Casablanca (Casas del Bosque) where we had a tour, wine tasting, and lunch. The restaurant was very pleasant. After lunch, we continued towards Santiago. There Thomas took us to see the city square, the cathedral, etc. And we got a flavor of what life is like in Santiago. He then took us to see the museum of Pablo Neruda. The last stop before the airport was a shopping place where we could get some decent quality souvenirs. It was a short one day trip but Thomas helped us cover quite a bit of ground. He did exactly what we asked for and delivered with flying colors. We also found Thomas to be very pleasant and knowledgeable, so it was enjoyable to be around him. Wish we had more time to see more of the 2 cities. Maybe next time ....

review_text: On the whole, this was a well-organised trip from booking to embarkation through to the actual 3-day ferry journey itself (though the website needs improvement). For complete privacy, we chose an AAA cabin which, for a vehicle ferry, was well appointed and more spacious than we had expected. The briefings were thorough and the talks and films throughout the journey were good. The captain always announced things of interest to see. The staff were courteous and helpful. When we booked, what they failed to tell you on their website was that, for the eye-watering cost of choosing one of the few AAA cabins, you do actually get to eat in the separate AAA dining room with a better menu, tables with tablecloths and napkins, waitress service and free, good quality wines with all lunches and dinners – that’s a real bonus. The weather was mixed on our trip though fortunately the seas were largely calm. You take this trip to look at the scenery of the archipelago so the weather plays an important part of your enjoyment of it. In this region, you can’t predict the weather, so you have to take what comes. Tip: don’t book any onward travel too close to the expected arrival of the ship – if the weather’s bad, it can arrive many, many hours later than anticipated.
title: Pricey but worth the cost

review_text: I took a day tour from Santiago to Vina del Mar and Valparaiso with Turistik. I enjoyed the tour and would recommend it. Previous comments suggest that the tour company was not organized; on the contrary, my experience with Turistik was efficient and pleasant. Firstly, i could not pay with VISA online because of a technical glitch. I called the Turistik office and was able to book via the phone with payment to be made at the tour bus. I was picked up at the hotel on time and the transfer to the tour bus was efficient and straight forward. The tour guide, Felipe, was engaging and interesting. He flitted between Spanish, Portuguese and English with little effort. He was easy to understand, and standard tourist and tour jokes notwithstanding, was informative and pertinent. I have read some Tripadvisor reviews which mentioned that not information or facts were provided, but in this case Felipe provided the right mix of history, facts and anecdotal content (more factual info and we would then complain that it was exhaustive with facts). the tour minibus (of say 25 people) was clean and comfortable. The other nice thing about this tour was the pickup and drop off at the hotel plus they did not try and sell you a bunch of souvenirs and knick-knacks. The tour provided a good overview of the 2 cities so that one could then venture out on one's own and make a more detailed and personal exploration. Our tour was made up of around 15 persons, which i think is better than a whole busload. All in all - a good tour package, an efficient driver, an interesting tourguide and 2 picturesque but contrasting cities. i recommend this tour. Dear Customer, We are pleased to read you had an enjoyable time with us. We want to thank you for the positive review you made about our service and the compliments to our staff, who work with pleasure to make your trip an unforgettable experience. We are always available to deliver our passengers the best possible tourist service. As mentioned, Viña del Mar and Valparaíso are two completely different cities, even though they are one next to the other. So it is a must for those who are traveling to Santiago and want to know a little more about the history of Chile in two beautiful cities located just 1 hour and 30 minutes from the capital. We hope to see you again in the future and we thank you again for your positive comments.
title: Day tour to Vina & Valpo with Turistik

review_text: There are boat trips available that take you closer to the glacier. If you absolutely want to make this boat trip you should book in advance. When the boat arrived we saw why: boarding takes a lot of time, as they are shipping passengers to the bigger vessel in a small boat and the strong wind made the bigger vessel move quite slowly. If you are planning to see the Glacier Perito Moreno, skip the boat trip to Glacier Grey. review_text: We were in Australia with flights booked to Chile, how were we to get around? What was transport like? Hotels? Wine tasting and getting from one vineyard to the next (the reader may have guessed we’re into wine!)....... over to Google! Sent a simple email to Chile Private Tours and within hours Thomas replied. We told him when we were landing and when we were taking off and he put together a fantastic mix of wine and scenery and culture that although initially I thought a bit expensive - now it’s all over - I realise was great value for money. I won’t detail everywhere we went but all the places we went to were excellent. Our driver / host / wine expert / music lover Jorge, was fantastic, so helpful and professional giving a real insight into the country and culture. Again we did so much and all between boutique hotels and wineries that Thomas had planned. The penultimate day we were given a walking tour of Valparaiso by Thomas and then we met our chef for a cooking lesson - Pablo - bus to the market, buying tips for fresh fish and meat, veg - Chilean style - bus back to the cooking school all the Pisco sour, wine, ALL included. Brilliant afternoon and late into the evening. Last day to a final winery then Departures at Santiago aeropuerto! My advice - if you want to get a great taste of Chile, as the sportswear company says - just do it! You will really enjoy your experience. Feel free to ask any questions.

review_text: After reading quite a few reviews we decided to do our two night/three day tour with World White Tour and everything exceeded our expectations. AGENCY: The two ladies working at the office in San Pedro were super professional, kind and polite which made us feel very reassured from the beginning. Everything they promised did happen during the tour and even one of them was at the Bolivian border during our breakfast just before we jumped on the jeep. We thought the whole thing was very well organised and again helped us feel we were in the hands of people who cared. GUIDE: Casimiro was a very experienced and responsible driver, as well as a very knowledgeable guide. He literally tailored the trip for us so we could see things that weren't in the initial itinerary and worked around other groups doing the same trip which meant most of the time we were on our own and not with many other people at each stop. This is a big plus, especially when you want to see flamingos, which are very shy. Casimiro was super patient with us during the stops and didn't rush us once. He played great Bolivian music and let us play our own too. He also helped us take brilliant pictures and videos at the salt flat. I strongly recommend him as a guide. JEEP: It was a great jeep in good condition. We were a group of six (amazing people by the way, if you're lucky you will make friends through this experience!) and it felt comfortable and safe at all times. We constantly rotated seats so everyone got to be by the window and got good views during the drive. FOOD: Way better than expected. Generous portions and vegetarian options. Casimiro also gave our group a bottle of red wine on the 2nd night which was much appreciated. ACCOMMODATION: Basic but again better than expected and exactly as they advised when we booked the tour. We got our sleeping bags (which were good quality) included in the tour price. TOUR: The actual tour is just amazing. Impossibly beautiful landscapes that I never imagined could exist. It really is remote and untouched in some parts, which makes you feel deeply connected with nature and its wonders. I totally recommend this tour.
title: Amazing tour with World White Travel
