review_text: We loved our winery tour with Tom from Bodega Wine Tours. We've attended lots of wine tours in Australia and overseas, and this would have to be one of the best and most enjoyable. The tour is a bit different to what we are used to - normally rushing to 5 or 6 wineries in a day - but the Chileans like to do things a bit differently, and in this case I think it works! Firstly, Tom was very easy to deal with over email to make the booking and he even agreed to change his schedule so that we could visit Casablanca on a day normally reserved for Maipo. Tom reconfirmed the tour the day before and picked us up around 9:30am in a nice mini van with separate driver. The drive to the Casablanca valley took an hour or so while we chatted and before we knew it we were at the first winery - Veramonte - which as others have mentioned is a certified organic medium scale winery. Tom showed us the vines before we entered for our tasting. We sat down at a table and had our own dedicated host to describe the winery and each wine to us in detail. We tried 5 wines and each was a generous pour. All were very good quality - one of the nicest sauvignon blancs we have ever tried! Next we went to a microwinery called La Recova where you start the tour in the owner, David's, living room. This one is also organic, but not certified. Here we had a full tour of the winery wonderfully hosted and explained everything by David. We even got to try some of the not-quite-ready-yet wine from his tanks. After the tour David led us to a magnificent alfresco area where there were a range of delicious treats (cheeses, olives, oils etc) and three of his wines for tasting. An extremely generous pour of each was provided, with more offered if you wanted it. All three were delicious. Then David introduced us to a traditional Chilean sport (of which I cant remember the name!) but we all had a go and it was really fun and a unique touch which put this tour above any other. Then we went back to the house where we got to label a bottle of his wine ourselves (also a cool experience), which he then gifted to us. So lovely! The final winery was Vina Mar, a larger one with a lovely restaurant. The lunch is an additional cost, but even though its an upmarket restaurant the prices were extremely reasonable and the servings were a good size. We each just had a main and it was certainly sufficient. Tom also led us through a blind tasting to see what we had learnt - I think we all did pretty well! I booked this tour because of the good reviews and the price (it was one of the cheapest I could find) - and I'm really glad I did! even though US$105 per person might still seem a bit expensive to visit three wineries and pay for your own lunch, after having experienced the tour I now think its extremely good value. In this case quality definitely trumps quantity! If you like wine you must do this - it was a highlight of our month in South America!
title: A must do!!

review_text: Valparaiso is the oldest seaport in South America. You might be yawning now, but wait til you see this little city on the water! Some homes have actually been abandoned because their is no access as the elevators become a thing of the past. It is hard to describe, because it is so unusual. review_text: I very rarely (read never) can be bothered to write reviews on Tripadvisor, so this just goes to show how great Spicy Chile walking tours are!!!! I was somewhat sceptical when my friend insisted that we all did it, but I was definitely proved wrong. The format is as follows - Pick a route, meet a guide there at the listed time, walking tour round Santiago, tip what you think it´s worth at the end. Very simple, very effective. Our guide was called Rocio (Spelling, I don´t know, but she said we could call her Rose) was an incredibly friendly, knowledgeable bundle of fun, who instatly puts you at ease. Did I mention she´s the best guide? She speaks excellent English, and is a veritable fount of knowledge, on a variety of subjects ranging from culture, architecture, history, food, nightlife, wildlife, and everything in between. The tour we did was called Good Morning Santiago, taking in a real range of sights, sounds and smells, and includes a little cafe stop that serves excellent Empanadas. All of this is interspersed with humourous (Where appropriate) commentary, personal anecdotes and recommendations, and is crucially conducted at the general pace of the group, so you can stop and take pictures wherever you wish, ask for stops, or decline others, which is really nice! In fact, we liked this tour so much, that five of us came back and did Patrimonial tour today, which is pretty much the best proof of Spicy Chile being awesome I can offer! We visited all kinds of off the beaten track sights, which I would not have had a hope in hell of finding, even using a guide book and a map. It´s very interesting, as Rosio (again, same guide) really brought the history to life, and I can honestly say I was pretty much enthralled through out. Quirky, friendly, a great way to soak up the ambience of Santiago, and opens your eyes to all sorts of cool stuff to do for the rest of your stay! JUST MAKE SURE YOU LIKE WALKING! Both tours I did lasted for about 3 or 4 hours. It´s a fairly relaxed pace, but if you don´t do walking, it´s probably not for you. Although I don´t know why you would be looking at a walking tour if you don´t like walking. But I thought I´d better mention it anyway... What an awesome critic!!!! Thanks Harris!!! You made Rose super happy after your post!!! Hehehe!! Hope to see you back soon!!

review_text: Each time I looked up, which I tried to do as often as my footing would allow, I said "WOW!". The W is straight out of a movie with it's breathtaking landscape. We trekked east to west, doing to towers hike first. We were so tired by day 4 that we were thankful to have completed the most difficult hiking day first. TBH, if you have a reasonable baseline level of fitness (I am 52 and no longer a gym rat, but I am active) it's just not that strenuous. Super enjoyable with some huffing and puffing thrown in from time to time. :) Chile Nativo set us up with Nana as our guide, and she totally made the trip even more awesome for us. She was AMAZING! Our kids loved her, we loved her, she was super knowledgeable about the flora and fauna, she can spot a condor from 10 miles away, and she was a BEAST on the trail. She rocks! :) A few suggestions: I would say that hiking poles are a MUST for anyone over 50. We bought them in Puerto Natales (~$20 each) at our guide's suggestion and I am SO thankful that I had them. Some parts of the trail are pretty steep and my knees would never have forgiven me if I didn't have the poles to assist. You can drink the water straight out of the rivers and lakes, so skip the heavy filter bottles. We all had medium size Nalgenes, and they were perfect. Unless you are an epic sweat-er, plan to wear the same thing every day (except underwear), to keep your pack light. Lots of thin layers up top is key. The wind can take you from sweating to shivering to sweating on the same hike. We were there end of Dec and were very fortunate with no rain and good weather. I wore (all synthetic!) a short sleeve T, a thin long sleeve T, a thin running jacket, and a waterproof windbreaker. The top 2 layers went on and off as needed and I was super happy the whole time, even when the wind was howling at 40MPH. Hats MUST have a strap. A wool beanie or a buff is a better idea. Sunglasses at all times! SUNSCREEN people! And don't forget your hands. The backs of my hands are the only place that got sunburned, and it's not fun. Crocs for after hike were awesome cuz you can fit socks under them for warmth but it feels like you're barefoot. And they dry quickly after you wear them in the shower, which you will want to at the refugios. The refugios are cool! Not going to be your best night sleep ever, and keep in mind that they are on a very local septic system, but still a fun experience. The food is what the food is. Not a deal breaker. The smaller size quick drying towels from REI were perfection. Dry by morning, and they double as a "bedroom" curtain on your bunk in the refugio. Staying in the same room with other adults was not my new fav (but I would do it again for this hike!!) and the towel trick helped me sleep. Bring tip money. Each refugio has a tip jar, and they do work hard to make it a good experience for the guests. Plus, you'll want to tip your transport people, and of course, your awesome guide. BOOK IT!!! :)) Review of: W Trek Torres del Paine

review_text: We visited as part of a private tour to do stargazing and check out the countryside. The Elqui Valley does not disappoint - you have beautiful and progressively more rugged countryside as you drive in, lots of vineyards and lots of pisco distilleries (along with a very nice small winery in Cavas) and charming little mountain towns. At night, the stars are to-die-for - so clear and so dark, you can see things here that aren't visible much of anywhere else. The guided tour approach is a good one if you aren't fluent in Spanish, because in the valley few people speak any English. Be sure to check out the crafts in the village of Horcon (go no earlier than lunchtime), the Los Nichos pisco distillery, and the Restaurant Solar (all the cooking is via solar ovens!). If you can, stay in a dome at Elqui Domos (it calls itself a hotel, but it's really a collection of cabins) and pay for the personal astronomy tour they offer - way better than what you'll get at one of the public observatories, and the sky is darker there.

review_text: I hate to give my first low review from my trip but I have to. Portillo is catered for skiers. Don't bother going here, especially if you're a snowboarder. As far as what was good, they do an excellent job of grooming the trails with the minimal snow that they got. I cannot complain about the amount of snow because that's out of the resort's control. I will complain in regards to the fact that I read Portillo snow was going to be similar to that found in Colorado-I've been to CO and its no where near as good. It's more like East Coast conditions with frozen granular in the morning and slush by 12pm if the sun is out. Also, the food at Uncle Bob's was delicious although ridiculously expensive even for resort standards- $39 for 2 burgers, fries and 2 waters. As for the "resort" the trails are no better than a small mountain in upstate NY. Yes, the views are far more beautiful but this is not the place for an advanced/expert skier/rider. I suppose I could have worked on riding switch because I was bored within 2 hours of riding here. Not to mention the amount of skating and walking a rider has to do because of the pitch between trails. AND the steepness getting off the chairlift causing a snowboarder to really practice skating fast downwards. And I can't even begin to describe how the t-bars are the only access to the steep stuff. Visit here for the day to check out the oldest resort in South America. ONLY stay here for the week if you've for kids who are not very experienced-it's perfect for that. Just like a cruise ship with everything laid out for the week. It's best for families and should be avoided for serious skiers/riders. Choose Valle Nevado or La Parva instead.
title: It's called SKI Portillo for a reason- it's not good for snowboarders.

review_text: Vina Casas del Bosque is in the center of the Casablanca Valley, just about an hour west of Santiago. It is a modern, young winery that focuses on the production of mostly white wines, with Sauvignon Blanc, Riesling and Chardonnay being the main targets. The winery grows Syrah and Pinot Noir too, and it makes Carmenere and Cabernet Sauvignon-based wines grown in Maipo and Rapel, two other wine-producing areas of Chile.While the facility is modern and efficient, the production methods are somewhat unconventional. The resulting white wines are mostly young, fresh and pleasant, but not intended to age. They should be consumed within the first year or two. The basic wines are labeled "Reserva" as opposed to most other wineries around the world where this label means something special. Gran Reserve is the next level up and then there are a few wines produced in small quantities and greater care. These latter ones deserve attention and with time will likely grow into mature and enjoyable wines.

review_text: We self drove to the lakes from San Pedro, an easy drive. The entry fee is CLP10,000 per person. The salt lakes are home to local bird wild life. There are 3 lakes here and one is available for swimming - so sunblock to keep chemicals out of the water. Good modern bathroom facilities, outdoor showers to wash salt water off and change rooms are provided. All clean and well maintained. We couldn't resist the water. Although not as salty as the Dead Sea, the water has a similar effect of making it very easy to float. However, different to the Dead Sea, the water is thermal. Walking into the lake the floor is quite warm, then in shelves off into quite deep water which is cool on the surface and from the lower levels warm water rises in pockets. It was a lovely relaxing experience soaking in the lake with amazing views of the chain of volcanoes in front of us. A perfect desert setting. By the time we got out it was lunch time, so we took advantage of the shady areas provided. You have to bring your own food and drink with you. Recommend a visit.

review_text: We had an exceptional experience with World White Travel going to the salt flats! From pickup to drop-off, everything went smoothly and was one of our best tours of all times. The food was exceptional - well above standards - fresh fruit, vegetables, coffee/tea (needed as it was freezing), amazing meals cooked at the lodging by the people living there, and even a bottle of wine on our last night (unexpected)! Our guide, Johnny, was great - friendly and helpful, always on schedule and sharing information about each sight we passed as well as advising us what to wear and when to bring water. This was stand-out, as we heard many firsthand horror stories from other travelers and online of drunk drivers, drivers running out of gas and getting stuck in the cold, etc. It is worth it to go with a company that is safe, which World White was. We went to the standard stops as other tours, of course, but the tour company makes the difference. The car was warm, we felt safe, we had an awesome group - they did a great job pairing us with others. Our last day on the flats our guide went above and beyond to help with photos (they had props) and even made a video of us. He asked us what we preferred to do (are we cold, do we want to go back, do we want to get up for sunrise, did we have enough time, etc). The lodging was standard - first night is freezing in winter, there is no heat (small lamp for a few hours), but it is what we expected. Salt hotel is not actually a hotel, but had a fireplace which was nice. Highly recommend world white travel. Price was pretty standard, maybe slightly higher than other options but worth every penny - Thank you!

review_text: The Museo is conveniently located in central Santiago. Though it is a multi-story museum, it is not very imposing. Nor is it as large as, for example, the Native American museum in DC/EEUU. The Museo has a very wide-ranging collection of artifacts from many centuries, focusing on the pre-Columbus period. I came away from the attraction feeling like I had learned some aspects of Native American culture without feeling as totally overwhelmed (by the DC museum) . We were able to view the exhibits, with some detail, in a couple hours and had admiration for the textiles, tools, artwork and other display models. The naturally lighted basement area had several exhibits that were interesting. There is a delightful restaurant in the open air patio with good food, and good service.Admission prices were quite reasonable with discounts available for students/seniors/children. The Museum gift shop is relatively small, but has some unique gifts.
title: Refresher(& more) on Native Cultures

review_text: To "fully appreciate" the beauty of this city is to come up this tower with two levels of observatory on levels 61 & 62 with the upper one being "open sky" (although not a "wide-open" one where you can kind of feel the openness above unlike some of the observation floors I've been to like those of Marina Bay Sands in Singapore, Umeda Sky Building in Osaka & Palacio Municipal in Montevideo). In any case, I was actually somewhat amazed by "how green" this big metropolitan city down below was with its urban part of so-so-many buildings of 20-or-so-stories "nicely balanced" by its nature part of plenty of trees & tree-lined streets among those buildings (really a "greener view" than that of many other cities of the world I've seen from above); and at a "fair proximity" to the Andes Mountains (the east side of the city pretty much stretching to the foot of that mountain range), it was great to see a few "snow caps" on top of them although yes not as awesome as the big snow slopes I saw in some postcards of this tower (but which I guess was just a natural view in January which is summer in South America). And apart from enjoying the views, it was also great to learn from the info displays (on Level 61 the 1st level of the observatory) about the city's "premier sites" such as Plaza de Armas, La Moneda Palace & Cerro San Cristobal (actually a very good view of that hill from here and close enough to get a "tiny glimpse" of the big Virgin statue on the top if you look carefully). The only feature lacking on these two floors I would say as compared to the observation floors of other similar towers of the world is the "distances to other well-known cities" (which I'm kind of used to seeing them looking up above an observation floor). If coming by metro, Tobalaba Station (either Line 1 or Line 4) is where to get off at pretty much right beside this tower (with actually a big shopping mall directly below that you enter from like the overpass just a short walk from the street after coming out of the station), and yes it was "absolutely worthwhile" for me the admission of about 15,000 chilean pesos (which is a little less than 25 US$) not just for the phenomenal views of the city & beyond (as mentioned above) but also given the fact that this is the "tallest building" of the entire South American continent!

review_text: Torres Del Paine is a spectacular national park in Chile. You are at the bottom of the world in fantastic scenery and wildlife. I spent 10 days there and could have spent more. There is lots to do --- photography, hiking, camping, horseback riding, birding and more. The weather is wild -- beautiful days of blue skies and picnics and then winds that you fight to just stand upright, some so strong you can't even hike. The weather makes for some spectacular skies and clouds. It is fun to discover what is around the corner or over the hill -- mountains, waterfalls, wildlife or all of the above. It takes awhile to get there but it is worth it. You may even get stopped by a sheep traffic jam on the way.

review_text: The Atacama Desert plays host to some of the most stunning landscapes anywhere in the world. If you are into scenery on an epic scale you won’t be disappointed. I based myself in San Pedro which was ideal for getting to all of the major attractions, and with planning you can easily do two sites in a day. San Pedro is also a lovely little town ideally set up for tourists with good facilities, places to eat and loads of great little shops. I stayed at the Hostal Katari which at 195,000 pesos (about $220) for 5 nights was very good value (lovely room, clean and friendly staff). I chose to self-drive which was fine, Chilean drivers being respectful and accommodating. This gave me the chance to get out early to the sites and avoid the crowds. It also gave me a chance to drive some of the most spectacular roads in the world. The route east to the Argentine border is utterly otherworldly and south through the Atacama salt flats and up into the mountains was magical (go see the Salar de Agunas Calientes and Laguna Miscanti whilst you’re there) Most sites are ticket only admission but with a bit of patience you can arrange this yourself online. The major sites are also staffed (who were very helpful and patient as I don’t speak Spanish), and have toilets. Prices are reasonable around the $10-$15 mark and very good value. The El Tatio geyser fields are well worth a visit as long as you can tolerate the atrocious roads! And the ruins at Pukara de Quitor about 5km out of town should not be missed. I’d also recommend a swim in the Laguna Cejar which is also home to flamingoes and Valle de la Luna is a must see. San Pedro also offers a huge array of organised tours on minibuses. These range from a couple of hours to full days out. If you don’t want to drive or want the benefit of the knowledgeable guide these are well worth it. I did the Valle de la Luna tour with Whipala which was excellent. A truly incredible place!
title: Exploring the epic landscapes of the Atacama

review_text: This place is very busy in the summer. We arrived at 11, put our name down on the waiting list and were allowed to buy a ticket 40 minutes later. Then we waited in line for another hour. It's not that there are so many people. It's just that the house is small and crowd control is not good. I talked with another couple who tried to drive to Isla Negra on a weekend and gave up 1/2 way because the traffic was so horrible. I don't know about the rest of the year but, if you're going in the summer, go on a weekday and be prepared to wait. The house is worth the wait. Much bigger than La Sebastiana in Valparaiso. That man certainly loved his collections because he's got some of everything in the house. Lovely location. You can get a drink in the adjacent restaurant with a good view, while you wait to get your ticket or if you have a placeholder in line. We took the Pullman bus from Valpo. They let us off on a nondescript street corner. I asked the conductor where we caught it to go back and he vaguely gestured up the street. Later we went to the Pullman office, which was "up the street" but they had a sign saying another company operates to Valpo and you have to buy tickets on the bus. But you actually catch the bus farther up the street at a bus stop for local buses, rather than in front of the Pullman office. Fare is around $6 US each way. Admission for the house was $8 US.
title: Hard to get into but worth the wait

The guide comments that he can enter the hotel, but the hotel does not allow access There are some foodtruck carts with terrible snacks, bad empanadas, costing between 70 and 100 reais It has no structure Therefore, snow by snow, it is much better to go to Farellones which is closer to Santiago and has more attractions for children. review_text: My partner and I travelled with navimag during Mid May which is the low season so the ship was downgraded to a smaller sized one. From reading the reviews below we were aware of what was on offer. We thought the food was very good and there was a lot of it- you will never go hungry. Although it does cycle around the same theme of potato and some type of meat. The living quarters were very comfortable with not too many people and a tv that is constantly playing movies. There is a section of the trip that you sail on the open seas which can be rough and a few people were very ill during this time, however they do offer seasick pills. Fortunately I didn't get sick and had a great day on deck outside. Our arrival date was also delayed because of bad weather, this is a positive because the captain chose not to sail on the open sea when the waves were very large for the safety of his passengers and cargo. There was amazing scenery and wildlife to be seen along the trip including smoking volcanos, mountains, whales, sea lions and dolphins. It really was a great experience that everybody on board agreed was special. As for the animal cruelty... Chile is no different to the rest of the world. This is really an insight into how cows and animals that end up on our plate are treated worldwide. It is not specifically a Chilean thing, I think it is important to unveil how animals are actually treated around the world.
title: Amazing experience

review_text: We booked a transfer from the cruise terminal in Valparaiso to our local hotel with a 4 hour tour included. We booked early and I reconfirmed a couple of weeks before we left home to find out the best time to lead the ship. I got a prompt reply and all seemed good. Well we were let down and no one was there to pick us up. You can only imagine the mayhem at the terminal with 3 cruise ships arriving at the same time. We gave them plenty of time to arrive and kept walking around to see if they were in a different place. They didn't turn up and two hours later after trying to get a taxi we finally arrived at our hotel. It was a very stressful situation that we had planned to avoid. The response I had from Magic Chile was there was a fault in their booking system and it wasn't in it for that day. They offered to pay our taxi far but that will never correct the distress we suffered. Hopefully they have learnt from our misfortune. Dear Ms. Benson: We would like to apologize one more time for the inconvenience that the situation caused you. It was a human mistake and unfortunately your booking wasn’t made properly in our system. Of course we don't want to let down our customers, and this is the first time something like this happens to us and hopefully it will never happen again. We have learned from this experience, and we are going to use a new software for our booking system to prevent this situation in the future. Best regards Magic Chile Team
title: Double, Triple check your booking!!!

Ursula took care of us with a lot of patience and affection when we felt bad about the height. we fell in love with San Pedro, because of how beautiful it is, and because of how cute our experience was within the tour. 100% recommended! Hola chicas! Muchas gracias! Qué amables comentarios :) Me alegro mucho de que hayan pasado un tiempo tan maravilloso en Atacama con nosotros. Fue un verdadero placer! Fue un placer conocerlas a ambas y esperamos darles la bienvenida nuevamente la próxima vez. Un abrazo x
title: mace and almond :)

review_text: Our guide Crisitan and driver Osvaldo were engaging, organised and fun. We had great communication ahead of the day and the itinerary was well paced. Review of: Valparaiso Port and Vina del Mar Full-Day Tour from Santiago Comunicarion, organization and more are the details we ensure for a great experience. We're glad you had a great day. Thank you for your review.
title: Highly recommend

review_text: Excellent panorama! We went with a friend as a year-end disconnect and they treated us amazing. Really all the waterfall guides were very friendly, caring and you could tell the love they had for nature and place. Our guides were Hannibal and Ivan and made us feel safe at all times, constantly asked us how we felt and if we had any doubts, they also told us a little about the history of the place. The scenery, zip line and canopy all 10/10 full recommended, but really all experiences are completed by the team working on site. On Thursday 12/12 we made the hike to the waterfall to the animus and our guide was Patricio, also 1000/10 super good his interventions along the way, the history of the flora and fauna of the place very complete, he was worried at all times how we were going and if we needed to rest. The road really beautiful and quite quiet if you are not so used to trekking, in fact all the way the trees shade so it is not heavy either and that we went at 12:00 hrs. After 12/12 in the afternoon we did a massage in the SPA 🧖‍♀️ highly recommended also, I did the Ayurvedic massage with Eva and also the experience was 10/10, really all highly recommended and the guides and massage therapists really complete the experience to make it all amazing
title: Excellent place to relax and unwind

review_text: This is again a pretty large church, certainly considering the size of this village: a shipyard and a few houses. Again a slender central tower, with arches and a porch. However, the interior of this church reminds one of those in the altiplano. The interior is rather sober, but quite beautiful. Well worth the wait due to traffic works. The shipyard is interesting to have a quick look around.
title: church next to the shipyard of the island

review_text: Made me comfortable in contact Response quickly and clearly by removing questions and clarifying everything via whatsapp. I had no difficulties in contacting. Attention with attention
title: Made me comfortable in contact

review_text: It looks lovely from the outside but was locked up on Tuesday when we visited. There is nothing on it to say when it is open
title: Don’t know how to get in

review_text: The beach is beautiful and suitable for bathing, with the convenience of parking available for $5,000 a day. However, there are negative aspects that affect the experience. The massive presence of street vendors is quite invasive; some constantly scream, while others set up shop on the beachfront, blocking the ocean view, taking away the possibility of enjoying a relaxing atmosphere or connecting with nature. During high season, the situation worsens due to the large number of people, which generates discomfort to the point of feeling that they invade your personal space or even your awning. In general, it is not an ideal place for those seeking tranquility and disconnection.
title: Bad experience in high season

review_text: It's not so difficult to get there, really relaxing and easy to access walking through the park. A must!
title: A piece of heaven

review_text: This tour was one of the best we’ve ever taken. Jose was so knowledgeable and showed us some sites we would never have seen on our own or on a group tour. We were able to do the tour at our own pace and got to appreciate many facets of Santiago’s history through the varied sites featured. I highly recommend this as a ‘must do’ whilst in Santiago.
title: Behind Santiago’s facades

review_text: A long stroll with plenty of gift shops. Prices are fairly similar in all the stores as are the choices. A bit pricier in the main "square". Great seafood stands, try ceviches and a sea urchin sampler! Grab some locally made sweets, but don't overdo this: they don't taste as good as they look. Espresso drinks are in one specialized shop only, nowhere else. If you are driving, park elsewhere since it maybe hard to find a spot and taxis are cheap and plentiful.
title: The thing to do in Puerto Montt

review_text: I lived there when I was child. It was a great city in the mountains, but today don´t have nothing that what was. Any way for the people who never saw it before it is unbelievable how 11.000 people live there.
title: Sewell, a city in the mountains.

review_text: I have told to my wife. What a great place to spent some time as retired people. Just reading, writing, and listen to music and the great concert hall.
title: Very calm - Travel to rest

review_text: After quite a long research and going around the single companies in San Pedro we decided to do the tour with the Bolivian company Salar Andino. Edith - the seller explained everything and she had a lot of patience with all of our questions. We did the 3 day tour to Uyuni. Our driver Edy was driving very carefully and explained everything we asked about (speaking Spanish). The last day he spend lot of time with us in the Salar taking photos and he himself showed us some great tricks for the pictures. He was never rushing us when we were walking around or taking photos. The lunch and breakfast were always really good - the only let down were dinners provided by the hostels where we slept. In general the tour was worth the prize (95000 Chilean pesos/person + 250 bolivianos) and the company staff was very helpful and friendly. We would do the tour with Edy again! Thank you for an unforgettable experience!
title: Awesome tour, great and responsible driver

review_text: It was fantastic! Interesting program, not boring, great views...Julio showed us all beauties of Valparaiso and Vina del Mar. We recommend him. He is the best Thank you very much for your nice words. It was a real pleasure to show you Valparaíso. We, in Julio Turismo Chile, will be happy to see you here again, whenever you want to. Julio Aravena Bravo Co-Founder: Julio Turismo Chile
title: Wonderful trip!!!!

review_text: We climbed with Patagonia Experience - very professional! On a sunny day, you can see far into the distance. During our visit, the lava lake was reduced to dried up lava with a small hole, where you could see a bit of reddish glow from the lava. The tour companies hope the lava crust will collapse so you can see the actual lake again. Regardless, it's spectacular.
title: Must do

review_text: Rodrigo is a great acquaintance of the Atacama sky, and very didactic. He prepared a pleasant experience, and guided us through the sky first with the naked eye, and then by the telescopes Review of: Astronomical Tour "Under the Atacama Night"
title: Excellent

review_text: It took me a couple runs to do this right. It´s 2 to 2.5 hours round trip, so don´t leave at 5pm and chance it. Lessons learned: when in doubt, stick to the widest trail possible. Don´t go off on the single track if you plan to do the loop, and only the loop. At one point, when the trail narrows, you will be guided by arrows made of stones, or sticking out of the ground. Follow the arrows, and don´t expect it to be 100 percent clear. Also, I HIGHLY recommend RYM Expeditions (or RYM Adventures). It is a bike shop at about 160 or 170 Caracoles. I ride a lot at home, and was insistent on finding a shop where the bikes are maintained, and include the fixings - lights, helmets, repair kits, spare tubes, etc.) they include all the fixings, and the bikes are well-maintained, for the same prices as the other places. 3k per 6 hours. I have no skin in the game, as you can see from my reviews. But once I found this place, I ended up renting from them every day for a week. They also have photos on their computer, which will point out all the turns you need to make for whatever ride you want to do (not just the quebrada del diablo). No cost to enter the trail.
title: One of best MTB rides of my life - stick to widest trail

review_text: We got tickets as part of the hop on hop off package. Well recommended to speed up the queuing process. Only a 15 min or so wait and no queues to come down. Great experience. Get there early though. Lots of folk use it to get to the zoo and queues in afternoon were long. ¡Thanks for your opinion! Take Care.
title: Some kids were loving it, why not oldies too?

review_text: Very good tour, very clear and playful explanation, worth 100%, variety of products to try and know how to take them
title: Recommended! 100%

review_text: Alvaro and Gregorio were both lovely and very knowledgeable. They looked after us well and we had a great day with them. Thank you! Review of: Cajon Del Maipo Including Wine with Picnic and Empanada
title: Cajon del Maipo, chocolate, wine, empenada

review_text: Bernie showed us a great time in Santiago! She was passionate and enthusiastic, explaining a lot about the history in great detail and was considered in her opinions and views. This was our third Tours4Tips experience, each one great (in Valparaiso and Vina del Mar), but the 3pm Santiago highlights tour was really the best one! Thank you Bernie! Three tours with the Wallys, wow! Thank you ainamenneken for the great feedback. Bernie is a superstar and I'll be sure to let her know she was the highlight of your highlights. Cheers, Peter
title: Great tour of Santiago

review_text: Went to Petrohue Falls or Saltos del Petrohue with Puertomontt-Excursions. Had plenty of time to walk around the falls and rapids, visit rest rooms and snack shop. Great view of Osorno Volcano from this park.
title: Crowded but interesting and very good view of Osorno Volcano

review_text: We used the services of Hec Tour for our private tour of Santiago and it couldn't have been any better. We were picked up at our hotel. Our very professional and knowledgeable guide drove us all over town in his air conditioned vehicle. Half way through the day he took us to an open air market and took us to a little two table restaurant for home made empanadas that were delicious. All the highlights of town were covered. We found out on the tour that they also have 3 apartments that they rent out as well. Unfortunately we weren't aware of this beforehand or we would certainly have booked one of them. I wouldn't hesitate for a moment to use this fabulous company. They also offer transfers to or from the airport or the cruise port.
title: Santiago Private tour

review_text: Not sure why you would come to here and not see this either by bike or by tour. It is one of the main attractions, unlike all of the landscape I have been seeing on my travels in Chile
title: Must visit!

review_text: We visited this museum at 11am on a Sunday morning - it was pretty quiet at this time. It is free to get in - although you may wish to make a voluntary donation. The audio guide at $2000 are a must if you don't speak Spanish. A beautiful building and a powerful experience - highly recommend to get an in depth view of Chile's recent history.
title: Powerful and thought provoking

review_text: Just for the views is worth it, but expensive for the basic facilities. We got charged about US 15 a head. Beautiful turquoise waters, but with chalk type sediment at the bottom. The top pool is the hottest and they feed the ones down so they become cooler as they go down the mountain. I recommend an all wheel drive for the road, which is narrow in turns and a heavy traffic of trucks that feel they own it.
title: amazing location

review_text: An unbeatable way to climb the HILL. You can buy the ticket, visit Neruda's house and then go up without waiting in line. Short tour with views!! ¡Hola! Gracias por dejar tus recomendaciones, tal como mencionas al momento de comprar por internet te ahorras la fila de compra y solo debes realizar la fila de embarque. ¡Que tengas un excelente día!
title: RETRO FUNICULAR WITH VIEWS

review_text: There is not much to say, because it is a super famous tourist spot and in fact, in my opinion, it is worth visiting. The day I was a part of the floor was closed for an event, so the view was not as complete as it should be, but still, it was impressive! I went late in the afternoon and waited for the sun to come down and night. It's on the floor of the terrace, but I was pretty tired and I didn't think it would make much difference in terms of vision, so I didn't even go.
title: Famous tourist spot

review_text: Stunning scenery, great for kayaking and hiking! Easy enough to get the bus from Puerto Varas and enjoy a day there. One of my favourite spots!
title: A beautiful spot

review_text: Franco made this English tour of Santiago so interesting we did not want it to end! He took us to lots of places of historical interest and explained the complex history in an exciting way. He also explained the local food and drink, and social customs. His friendly relaxed manner meant that everyone on the tour enjoyed themselves and could ask lots of questions. Of course his side-kick Rollo (a fat stray dog that participates in the tour) was a bonus! Our stay in Santiago was enhanced by Franco's excellent knowledge and orientation.
title: Excellent guide - well done Franco!

review_text: A very nice beach to take a walk, ride a bike, surfing or just resting. Well lit during the night, and close to a number of restaurants and pubs.
title: Nice, well-maintained beach

review_text: I spent a week in Santiago Chile and each day uncorked led us to a new adventure in Chilean cuisine and wine. We had market and Vineyard tours that were lead by English speaking guides. On day we had a anthropological lesson in Chilean cuisine with courses that reflected the food of the time. Another day we participated in creating a 4 course meal. We explored the countryside and visited a goat cheese farm and a garden with a commitment to sustainable farming. The team was very organized and responded well to our questions and needs. I would recommend using them for as little or as much as you need for your trip Review of: Best Wine Tasting in Santiago
title: Learn about Chilean cuisine and wine with this tour group

review_text: The grounds surrounding the house are small but beautiful. The audio tour is well worth it, and highlights many of Neruda's intriguing eccentricities. The house is fascinating in its vertical layout. To be aware of: the tour is fairly short (perhaps 1-2 hours, depending on your level of engagement), there are many stairs, no photography inside the house.
title: relaxing way to spend an afternoon

review_text: The views are fascinating, one can take a lot of photos and there is a lot to see. The trip is also accompanied by adrenaline, this due to the small routes that one must pass to reach the caisson Review of: Cajon del Maipo
title: Amazing.

review_text: This place e was recommended to us by a good friend who grew up here during this time in history. You must get the audio wands if your Spanish is lacking , but recommend them even if it is good because they are very well done. The museum does a amazing job of getting to feel what it was like for Chileans during this time. You may even find yourself fighting back the tears, for it is that moving.
title: Have to go

review_text: We booked a day tour to the Petroue Falls and Osorno volcano while on a cruise in the region. Jaime Liebrecht of Patagonia Shorex replied to my enquiry promptly and the booking process was very simple. When we arrived in Puerto Montt our guide, Jerado, was waiting for us on the dockside and we began our day together before the ship tours and coaches left, which meant that when we arrived at Osorno we had the pace virtually to ourselves. Jerado was very knowledgeable and entertained us with details of the culture and history of the area during our time together. He seemed to know everybody and greeted them with a smile and a wave wherever we went; we thoroughly enjoyed his company and the freedom a private guide gives. Jerado was also very mindful of our needs – photos, coffee, rest stops etc. and we consider ourselves fortunate to have enjoyed the area with him as our guide Review of: Full-Day Tour to Petrohue Falls Through the Lake District , Chile thanks to you and was a pleasure
title: Great sights with a great guide

review_text: Simply amazing! The education, organization and animation of the Guide Coqueiro made all the difference. The sunset at Casa Zerando is an unforgettable experience that everyone should have at least once in their lives. The clothes are a differential on the deck and the care of the girls when returning from the tour is also excellent, always with a smile on the face and interacting with the prisoner. I'm already eager to go back home zeroing.
title: Unforgettable

review_text: Our trip to the Atacama desert was the best experience possible thanks to the service provided by Volcan Paniri (Pato Father and Son). Amazing landscapes, a lot of knowledge, delicious food prepared by Pato Pai (selected products, including bread from La Franchuteria). The route suggested by Duck allowed us to enjoy the best of the desert in our six days around the place. We thought we might not be able to take advantage of 100%, since we read a lot of reviews talking about the tours to be best suited to the younger. But we have to disagree with that, because the desert is quite democratic and everything was super quiet. Of course at this point, we have to give due credit to Duck, who gave the best tips. Plus, we got mega professional photos taken by Duck who is a great photographer. Review of: Private Atacama Photo tours
title: The Best of Atacama

review_text: being religious or not it is worth visiting the cathedral to see hints of Spanish architecture right in the middle of Andes mountain chain surrounded city of Santiago del Chile. they have renovated anything by the way, even the speaker sound system is by Bose, very cool care to local infrastructure!
title: beautiful building

review_text: Hector picked five of us up at the port in Valparaiso and spent several hours giving us a tour of the area. We had lunch and walked around parts of the city. He is very knowledgable since he grew up in this area. We then drove to Santiago where we had reservations for a two might stay. Hector agreed to be our guide the next day. We went up the Andes and toured the outskirts of the city. The next day he took us downtown for some shopping, lunch and then to the airport. We all agreed that Hector helped make these days a highlight in our vacation.
title: Great tour guide

review_text: I expected more . . . I don't know if the correct angle was missing. The thing is, the cars stop there and people drop on the asphalt and take the photos. It's got the plate and just... Nothing special. There are more interesting places along the way. If you can't go or don't stop, don't be disappointed.
title: Nothing special

review_text: The bike ride was a Wonderful experience! It followed a great course, and our guide (Lorena) led us through the extremely scenic pathway following the Petrohue River. She took us to points of interest and view points that were off the typical tourist beaten path. Mapu Activa provided new and very good equipment, too. Highly recommend! Review of: Petrohué Bike Tour
title: Awesome ride and scenery

review_text: The geisers themselves are pretty spectacular and our guide managed to cook us an egg for breakfast in one of the pools but what really impressed us was the wildlife in the surrounding area. The wildlife appears relatively use to humans and though not tame if you are careful, quiet and slow you can get pretty close to the birds and animals.
title: Like stepping into your own discovery channel documentary

review_text: Incredible service and Elias is very patient and an excellent driver, I highly recommend him! We booked a transfer and tour guide with him, it was incredible 👏🏻👏🏻 Review of: Private Transfer between Santiago and the Airport
title: Tour guide/transfer

review_text: Very nice and relaxing place with lots of nature around. The pools were good even tho only two of them where hot enough for a rainy day, the rest were cold or weren't available to use. Despite that it was great to come here. Thanks a lot.
title: Still a nice THING TO DO ON A RAINY DAY

review_text: They were in such small cages though but still very beautiful to see
title: White Tigers are wow very rare

review_text: We did both tours with Ecoturisme and both were great. Felipe was the guide for both tours. His English is very good, and he did it well by not switching English and Spanish every sentence but instead talking longer in each language. He also entertains the group well. Isla Damas: We had very good weather, but unfortunately saw no dolphins (but of course penguins etc.) Elqui Valley: Beautiful valley, lots of explanations, Pisco tasting etc. Felipe adapted to the group of we wanted to stay more at one place. Hi!! Good to know that you enjoyed the tours with us! It`s always a pleasure to help you to have a nice experience on your visit to La Serena area. Hope to have you here again someday Saludos!
title: Elqui Valley and Isla Damas

review_text: The best park in the heart of town with awesome statues and a view of the city once you get to the top which is super enjoyable Recommended: you'll find a green kiosk at top, stop by and enjoy a delicious and refreshing local "mote con huesillo"
title: Do not miss the view from the top

review_text: Like nearly all the ascensores, it is a little railway car that goes up en down, a bit shakily. This one is convenient for tourists, as it is quite centrally located, in contrast to Polanco or Artelleria. It furthermore takes one to some of the nicer streets in Valparaiso. Quite worth the experience.
title: funicular to popular streets on Cerro Concepcion

review_text: Super special care from Araya. All perfect. Atacama is wonderful, perfect nature.Desert, flora, fauna and humans in harmony.
title: Imperdível.

review_text: This Catholic Church is located in the center of Puerto Montt and is somewhat significant because of its architecture. It is made if wood and that is unusual. The other material is glass. wood withstands earthquakes because it moves. The only downside is fire. In addition to Mass, concerts are held in the church.
title: Architectural

review_text: Really incredible day of climbing this active volcano. After some search and shopping around, I chose the agency Vulcano Expediciones who have a shop on the main street of San Pedro with very friendly staff. My guide was Christian, very friendly, warm , experienced and professional guide with loads of knowledge about everything around San Pedro. We started at 5:30 and arrived to the Laguna Leíja right for a stunning sunrise during which we enjoyed a light breakfast. Then we climbed to the crater in a steady slow pace and enjoy fantastic view of the crater and fresh sulfur smell :) Then it was just a short while to the summit with incredible views. I really loved this trip, just be sure you acclimatize well before going so you can really enjoy it!
title: Incredible view!

review_text: The place is breathtakingly beautiful and the experience of floating in the salt water is unique. The driver David drives the van very well and is very friendly. Francisco, the guide, is very kind, cheerful and receptive, he has mastery of the topics presented during the tour, providing an even greater richness to the experience. Without a doubt, it was one of my favorite tours in San Pedro de Atacama. Review of: Tour to the Hidden Lagoons of Baltinache
title: One of my favorites!

review_text: The tour was very interesting, the bus that transported us was very comfortable and the explanation of the guide Jaqueline was complete. It's a good option if you want to get an idea of Chile in one day. Review of: From Santiago: Valparaíso, Viña del Mar and Neruda Museum Muchas gracias por compartir su experiencia vivida junto a nuestro equipo, nos alegra saber que todo salió bien.
title: Good option to take you in one day an idea of Chile

review_text: I had the best experience birding with Eduardo through Albatross Birding and Nature Tours. The booking process was very easy and Francisco was excellent to communicate with and sent me all the information I needed to know. Transportation was very comfortable and I had so much fun and learned so much birding with Eduardo.
title: Awesome Birding Outside of Santiago, Chile

review_text: Great experience hiking La Parva with Eduardo. Great guide, very prepared, adaptable with the group. Had a passion for hiking and was experienced. Highlight of our trip and would highly recommend. Thanks for your review! We are very glad you enjoyed this amazing trip. La Parva Mount and surroundings is like our backyard, a place where we ski in winter and hike and ride in MTB in summer just at one hour from our huge Santiago City. We hope to see you soon again with us, and we invite you to enjoy the snow in winter. Enjoy the journey!
title: Great hike of La Parva

review_text: We loved the selection of aircraft at the museum, they have a wide display of military and commercial aircraft used in Chile and some from other countries too. The only issue we had was that there was very little information in English (90% only in Spanish). One of the guides did walk us around a hangar explaining the planes but this was a kindness and not an organised tour. There is a kids play area and lots of space for a picnic but no food or drinks on site so take your own.
title: Lots of planes but not much information in English

review_text: We enjoyed the plaza, and got a chance to look around the statue. It's one of those over-stated historical things, but impressive.
title: Impressive statue

review_text: Absolutely incredible! This is our honeymoon trip and honestly it went above and beyond our expectations! The wine, the food, the scenery wow, definitely worth it. Jaime was our guide and he was amazing! We’ll be remembering this for the rest of our lives and hopefully repeat this tour next time we come back to Chile!
title: Above and beyond experience!

review_text: I went here on a tour with Touristours. This place is so great. The wines are devine and I learned quite a bit from the guides. We got to taste grapes off the vine and also 4 of the wines at the end. What an impressive operation! I loved it so much! The wine was also great!
title: Loved it!

review_text: Not your run of the mill cemetery that we know. Some huge edifaces, other smaller graves, surprising number of Croatian names. Worth a short visit.
title: Intruigoing

review_text: These two lagunas are not far from San Pedro and are outstanding places for making simple landscape photographic compositions, especially as the sun sets. In the middle of the day the light is too harsh and there will be busloads of tourists. I visited in winter and we were a group with our own minibus and driver who waited long after the tourist buses had gone.
title: Laguna Tebinquiche and Laguna Cejar

review_text: Just to be in the center of the square and take a look around to appreciate all the buildings close to you it's wonderful. So beautiful!
title: Beautiful

review_text: We did this tour as private tour with the guide Felipe Staig. This guys did a great job providing equipment and pace for elevation. Good English knowledge is also a bonus on a long drive from SPA :) It's really fantastic place. We've never been to active volcano, well frankly speaking ANY volcano and we did it going to the crater and to the nearest summit. The views, and whole impression is "OH MY GOD!" "I saw Orordruin!", "#%%#! It's still working!". I just can't express all that. The views from up there are amazing! IMPORTANT!!! FOR NON-PROFESSIONAL CLIMBERS!!! Attitude 5500 is not a joke! Prepare yourself for it before going there, go to a couple of tours above 4000 at least. We had the private tour. We - married couple and one guy from Germany, who didn't do the preparation. He felt really bad after getting to the crater and had to leave back almost immediately. Even that elevation itself is 500 meters only, it's from 5000 to 5500!!! Attitude sickness can destroy your journey!!
title: Get ready for the biggest active volcano in Chile!

review_text: We have the tour “Valley of the Moon” with the guide Alexis, tremendous experience, a lot of technical data, I learned quite, really a very pleasant experience. Without a doubt the next tours I will take with him, thank you very much atama zoom.
title: Very good experience

review_text: Excellent Walk and Excellent Guide!!! I definitely recommend it 💯. Very interesting? He provided much historical and valuable information. The restaurant booked very good. Review of: Valparaiso Port and Vina del Mar Full-Day Tour from Santiago Gracias por su review, nos alegra que disfrutará de su día todos los aspectos.
title: Unmissable excursion

review_text: Christian was really attentive, involved and protective during this day, as I was alone :). I liked the explanations he gave on the ground, on the bus. He even offered to drop us off at the mall after the tour to arrange things for us! Very Great guide! He waited for me at certain moments to take the photo! I loved his story and his sharing. I'm leaving with a piece of Chile. Merciiiii!❤️ Review of: Full Day Group Tour - Viña Del Mar-Valparaiso -Casablanca -Reñaca Thank you for telling us about your experience, we're super happy to hear you had an amazing time with us and our guide Christian, also it is so good you had great time and felt protected! Don't hesitate to contact us the next time you or your friends want to come to live another gratifying experience in one of our tours. Best regards, MTO Tour Team
title: Recommand 100% made by Christian 🥳

review_text: Everything we got to see on this tour was very pretty. We were only in Punta Arenas for a short amount of time and were happy to have been able to see a few things around the town. Perfect if you’re looking for something to do during the day but not spend your entire day out! Review of: Magallanes Forest and Club Andino Tour from Punta Arenas
title: Pretty sights for a half day tour

review_text: Located in the Mall Costanera Center (Metro Tobalaba), go to the -1 floor and look for the ticket shop. It is a quite new building, and you will enjoy a nice view of Santiago and the region (with free wifi!). Bring your camera! Only tip is to avoid the smog - so make sure that the sky is clear enough for you to enjoy the view! On weekeds, you will pay CLP 8,000 for the ticket (about USD 12).
title: Worth visiting

review_text: We did the cruise on the Ventus last March from Punta Arenas to Ushuaia. It was everything we hoped for! The excursions were so much fun and well executed. The cruise was more expensive than we usually pay for vacations, but worth every dollar.
title: Favorite trip ever!

review_text: Great experience! Our thanks especially for Claudio and the whole team (Jean, Renee and Dania) for guiding us in the Northern Desert. Claudio told us about geology, fauna, flora, cuisine, traditions and the region. Always listening, he answered our (very) many questions. He managed to acclimatize us to the high altitudes and not without some pride that we arrived at the summit of Cerro Toco at more than 5,600 meters, a challenge for the Breton that we are. Claudio is more than a guide, he is attentive, attentive and with little care. Thank you for the different feedback you offered us. We definitely recommend Locaventuras. We wish them an excellent continuation and very beautiful meetings!
title: Thank you for the quality of the organization and exchanges!

review_text: A very good family experience. During the ride we were accompanied by Roxana and Rodrigo, they are excellent guides, they were attentive to our concerns and told us the history of the vineyard. The super docile and beautiful horses, my 7-year-old daughter rode alone (it was her first time doing it) always supervised by Roxana. Definitely an experience to repeat and 100% recommended. Estimado Salvador: Muchas gracias a Uds por habernos escogido y visitado. Fue un gusto compartir con Uds la cabalgata y la conversación; esperamos tenerles junto a Julieta nuevamente de visita acá en Club Ecuestre Santa Cruz. Un abrazo y saludos
title: Family riding

review_text: So we live in Santiago and like skiing. This is the second year in a row that we go up the mountain and stay there for 3 days. Note that we brought our 9 month old baby this time. So here it goes... Service kinda sucks depending on who you get. We arrived there and there was no one to correctly indicate the where to check-in (we stayed at the Valle de Condor apartments). The apartments are small, but clean and nice. We stayed at the 1st floor it was not too loud, but if you're at the 5th floor it will get noisy! Skiing was very good (we are beginners), and the views are breathtaking. I'm giving it 3 starts based on what you get for the price you pay (for everything from meals to accomodation). If you don't mind the waits for everything from eating to buying tickets then go for it. I would streamline so many simple processes that would be so simple to do. For example check-in and check-out. For check-in I spent 25 minutes and there was only 1 person in front of me checking in!!! Just have all the packages ready and give all the relevant information before people arrive by email, or in paper.
title: Skiing + Staying up there

The biking through the vineyard was great, though the bikes are very heavy and bulky. We also did the morning bike tour of Santiago, which was nice but could have been richer in information. All in all, both tours were really fun! Dear Isabelle, Sorry to hear your tour experience was not a 5 star one. We aim to do the best and think you should expect it just the same. We have always had a 100% satisfaction guaranteed policy with all of our tours. Please contact us directly and I promise to refund you the full tour fee immediately. Thank you for your honest feedback. Sincerely, Peter

review_text: Bolivia Desert Crossing to (Salar do Uyuni)/ Travessia Deserto da Bolivia ao Salar do Uyuni I made the crossing to Salar do Uyuni across the Chilean border. My friend and I made the trip alone. It was 4 intense and magical days. We find an exuberant beauty with many surprises and adventures along the way that we will never forget. However, I would stress that our trip could never have been so special had it not been for our guide GILMAR, our guide, cook, photographer and driver, who was waiting for us on the Bolivian border. Gilmar is a sensational and unique person. He introduced us to everything and made the trip even more charming, fun, solicitous, charismatic, always with a smile on his face. For sure, a true friend we made in Bolivia. We realized that we were very lucky to take a trip with him, during the trip we came across other people who were traveling with us and who complained a lot about their guide / driver. And talking to our fellow travelers, we realized that despite being from the same company, their guide did not even half of what our guide did and was always scowling. It seems like a simple detail, but a good guide makes all the difference, after all we spent 4 days traveling with him . I recommend requesting Gilmar's services if you make this trip. The company we chose is one of the best, it went well. But their highlight for sure is Gilmar. Fiz a travessia com destino ao Salar do Uyuni pela fronteira do Chile. Eu e uma amiga fizemos a viagem sozinhas. Foram 4 dias intensos e mágico. Encontramos uma beleza exuberante com muitas surpresas e aventuras pelo caminho que jamais vamos esquecer. Ressalto, porém que nossa viagem jamais poderia ter sido tão especial se não fosse pelo nosso guia GILMAR, nosso guia, cozinheiro, fotografo e motorista, que estava nos esperando na fronteira da Bolivia. Gilmar é uma pessoa sensacional e sem igual. Não mediu esforços para nos apresentar tudo e deixar a viagem ainda mais encantadora, divertido, solicito, carismático, sempre com um sorriso no rosto. Com certeza, um verdadeiro amigo que fizemos na Bolivia. Percebemos que tivemos muita sorte de cruzar a viagem com ele, durante a viagem cruzamos com outras pessoas que estavam viajando com a gente e que reclamaram muito do seu guia/motorista. E em conversa com os “companheiros” de viagem, percebemos que apesar de ser da mesma empresa, o guia deles não fazia nem metade do que o nosso fazia e sempre estava de cara fechada. Parece um simples detalhe, mas um bom guia faz toda a diferença, afinal passamos 4 dias inteiro viajando com eles. Recomendo, solicitar os serviços de Gilmar caso façam essa viagem. A empresa que escolhemos é uma das melhores, ocorreu tudo bem. Mas o destaque deles com certeza é Gilmar.
title: Bolivia Desert Crossing to (Salar do Uyuni)/ Travessia Deserto da Bolivia ao Salar do Uyuni

Our tour began with a guide who is a somelier, Alvaro, and ended with another tour guide, Rodrigo, who was also really great. We had different cheeses, dried fruits (dried kiwi included!), nuts, and five different kinds of wine (with a special bonus wine at the end of the tasting). She was very generous with her time and was able to enhance the tour information with lovely anecdotes and local facts. At the end of my two days with Strawberry tours and Larisa it felt like I've wondered through the streets of Santiago with a local friend. Hello Mahmut! review_text: This is a good way to get s great view and see how large Santiago is. I was going to take the vernacular rail but line was too long so decided to walk. It took about 50 minutes with a few stops along the way. Soon after you start your ascent you come across the zoo. I carried on to the left to climb to the top. The path in the lower section is well paved becoming dirt track further up. The are water fountains and taps along the path should you forget your water bottle. There are lots of facilities at the top including the Virgin Mary statue. I was going to walk back down but spotted a bus down from the cable car entrance which costs £1.40 for a ride down to the bottom stopping at a few points along the way. This meant I got to see some different views from the foot path and some more pics so would recommend doing s different route down.

review_text: If you have your own transport this is a good themal baths to visit and of the ones we looked at, we thought it was the most authentic. It takes about 45 minutes from town in a car. The baths are accessed down a long cul de sac several kilomaters long passing a number of other springs before reaching Pozones which is the last one at the end of the road. The facilities are good but don't expect spa facilities, fancy restaurants, or any indoor pool facilities. There are just a number of large thermal pools located in a picturesque position directly by a river which is also accessable if you want to brave the cold water. The pools and changing rooms are very clean and the grounds well maintained. The baths are very popular with Chilean families and have a relaxed and welcoming feel about them. Access is down a long series of steps. There are changing facilities but you keep your possessions with you depositing them in open lockers by the side of each pool. It cost just 5,000 per person, but it is time limited to three hours. We found this more than enough time if all you want to do is sample the experience of a thermal spring.
title: Authentic thermal baths

review_text: This tourist spot has not been modernized or updated over time, very expensive prices compared to other similar tourist spots, second floor dining rooms, poorly serviced and expensive as well, I do not recommend it to go to eat, in short, it is to visit once and haggle with prices, sometimes it turns out to be

review_text: We had been up since 6 am to prepare for our bus journey from El Calafate across the Patagonian Steppes with all the awkward time-wasting of having to pass the borders of 2 countries that probably hate each other more than most on earth. The journey was dull, the weather miserable, but as we approached the National Park, the rain diminished and patches of blue started to appear. Our 1st stop to catch a distant view of the Paine Massif (Cordillera) was at a view point close to this rather large lake. As we wrapped ourselves, collected the camera, and descended from the bus, that segment of the sky immediately above our heads turned blue, the sun burst through, and the drizzle miraculously ceased. It was an unforgettable moment. The lake was much more densely blue than the sky. I was told that this was because unlike most of the other lakes that feed into the Paine or Serrano Rivers, after which they are carried through the Seno Ultima Speranza fjord to the Pacific Ocean, Sarmiento is a closed lake. Another possible explanation is that it is especially rich in the rock flour and microbial life occurring in most lakes within the park. Finally, it is notable for the thick rim of carbonate that provides its uppermost level and lips with a white chalky surface, arising partly from thermal activity and partly from natural evaporation. Although we did not attempt them, I have seen splendid videos showing the trails that run round the lake at a higher altitude, offering remarkable views as well as intensely windy conditions.
title: Our first view of the Cordillera

review_text: Vina Matetic. Nice combinations of both red and white. Vina Mar. We tasted the flight of 3 Sparkling wines. These were all impressive..especially the one based mainly on Sauvigon Blanc. The server was very cordial and quire informative. His English was excellent Vina Indomitable. Beautiful winery in a Moorish style building that sets high on a hill. We had the least expensive flight which included a Sauvigon Blanc, Pinot Noir and Cabernet Sauvigon . All were excellent and highly enjoyed Vina Emiliana. This was the most HORRIBLE experience of the day. We walked into the tasting room and went to the tasting bar. There was a group of 4 on one side and 2 people on the other side....thus there were only 6 other people tasting. The server totally ignored me. I waited 10 minutes and he still had not spoken to me. Finally one of the people setting next to me informed me I needed to go to the cashier and pay for a tasting so I went to the cashier who was talking to another person and totally ignored me. Bottom line: I was in this winery for 15 minutes and totally ignored. I have tasted wine all over the world and this was the most rude treatment I have ever experienced.

review_text: I was a little bummed that rental cars are so expensive for one person, because I felt like I was forfeiting the freedom to explore San Pedro at my leisure, but man, after touring around with Horizonte, I do not at all regret the choice to tour rather than drive! I booked in their office my first morning in town and Federico was awesome, helped me fit everything I wanted to do in my schedule and work around another activity I had planned outside touring. It was super easy and I got my first tour set for that afternoon. I did Valle de la Luna with Freddy and Ivan, trekking purilibre with Sergio and Piedras Rojas and El Tatio with Camila and Daniel. All were fantastic! The landscapes themselves are gorgeous, and each guide provided a lot of extra information on the geology, complicated hydrology, and animal/plant life we encountered! They were also all so patient with my many questions. Sincerely an excellent time, very organized and super professional. All my guides also did a good job timing and choosing locations to keep our groups mostly away from other groups, so it never felt like one big tourist train, even though it could have. Camila and Daniel also were super great about flexibility on time, when my groups wanted a bit more time to watch birds, or walk around looking at things, they were super flexible to let us take everything in slowly, which I super appreciated as that was a big draw of renting a car. Overall, great trip! Highly recommend.
title: Awesome couple days in San Pedro

review_text: Wonderful place - the wine is fantastic, we had a personalized tour and tasting. THe restaurant is one of the best I've been to. A little out of the way, but charming and uncrowded. Bring home a bottle of the Pinot Noir at least.

review_text: We did the "O" trek in 7,5 days in December 2016. We organised everything ourselves beforehand, reservations of refugios/camping sites through Vertice Patagonia and Fantasticosur (these two companies own the campings/lodges around the trek). We did everything from Norway online, even ordering the bus from Puerto Natales to the park entrance. We did not carry tent/sleeping bags/food, we hired tent and sleeping bags they nights we did not sleep in the refuigios, and we had full board all nights, except at Los Perros which do not have such facilities. We bought a nice waterproof map before we left, but we did not use this. The best map was the one we got at the park entrance. The trail is very well marked, you dont even need the map. The nature is fantastic, ice bergs, glaciers, blue lakes and spectacular mountains. But be prepared for rain, we had one one day without rain. Remember waterproof gloves! And remember that you have to walk counterclockwise on the "O" trek. Despite what people are writing on the internet, no special permit is required (previously only 80 persons people allowed on the "O" at a time, this is not longer applicable). The one you get at the park entrance is enough. You should prepare to carry a backpack of approx 10 kilos, without food and tent.

review_text: This trek is a must for hike lovers, one of the most beautiful sceneries in the world. The W consists of different trails of astonishing beauty that takes you up and down mountains, through valleys, across rivers, side by side clear blue lakes, while rounding Los Cuernos mountains, Torres del Paine or Paine Grande in the Chilean Patagonia. I was worried about the weather, especially because we travelled at the beginning of the fall and we come from a tropical country. Out of five days hiking, we had four wonderful sunny days and one rainy day (so we could experiment the full Patagonian weather) with temperatures between minus 5 (at night) and up to 15 degrees in the day; however, for what we learned, weather is very unpredictable and you should come prepared with layers and waterproof jackets. During the five days we hiked around 80 kms. If you don’t have time to do the full W, I would recommend the trek to Mirador Las Torres (21 kms from our base camp) and Valle Francés (25 kms from Refugio Los Cuernos to Refugio Paine Grande). We booked our excursion with Ecocamp Patagonia and were not disappointed. They took care of everything as we spent two nights at refugios and five in Ecocamp location. It was great to be able to disconnect from daily stress and spend seven days surrounded by this wonderful natural landscape.

After running into another tour agency on the street, he recommended to do the "Piedras Rojas." I was a bit skeptical, because I already made up my mind to do the "regular" tour. Since he offered us a good deal and it was not that much more than the other tour that I planned on doing, we did this. WOW, am I glad that we did. This particular location - at the piedras rojas - was one of the most unreal views I have ever seen. It was a highlight of our trip, and I am so glad that we went to this area. When doing initial research, I saw this as an option, but I did not know what I was missing. This is so worth the extra money that it will be to go to this area and for the longer tour!

review_text: I was in Santiago for business and decided to take a day off to experience Chilean wine country. Wanting to get a more personal experience at "less commercial" wineries, I chose a tour with Chilean Wine Lovers to the Casablanca valley. It was a great choice, so glad I did it! My tour guide and driver, Leo, picked me up right on time and was very friendly and informative. The entire day was planned out well; my favorite part was Emiliana, an organic winery. Good tour and beautiful tasting room. I also liked the lunch at House (casa Morande). The food and wine pairings were great! Mauricio called at the end of the day to make sure all was well - he obviously cares about his customers and his business. I will definitely book another tour with his company if in the area again.

review_text: Absolutely wonderful experience! Better than I expected! A learning experience not just about wines but the history of the region and the local culture. I would do more tours with this group! Review of: Maipo Valley Wine Tour with 4 vineyards from Santiago.

review_text: The exterior of this moderate Cathedral is currently in the midst of having its exterior restored, Even with that happening, we loved stopping here on a Sunday to take a quick look of the interior. It is not over-the-top like many European Cathedrals but is more simple, yet beautiful. It features many gorgeous stained glass windows. BOTTOM LINE: This church is easy to find because it is located directly across the street from the main city plaza, Plaza de Armas. The construction began on this church in 1844 and dedicated twelve years later. The massive front doors are amazing. The Cathedral is named after San Bartolome who is the patron saint of La Serena. MY RATING: 8/10

review_text: After discovering about the block to allow non tour cars into the valley of the moon after 1pm we decided to drive to Tatio geyser at dawn instead. As the tour operators apparently start early from hotels we held back until 6am. By this time it’s light and easier driving. The drive out to the geysers is filled with great views and wildlife so take your time and enjoy them. There are tall cactus, flamingos in a small road side lake, lots of geese and other birds too, Vicunas, amazing colours on the mountains and volcanoes as the light comes up. We stopped many times on the way, allowing tour buses to pass by. The road is sometimes treacherous as the stones are like marbles underneath. The potholes can be pretty big too. Watch for springing vicunas especially after dawn. We did see a donkey who had been knocked down which is so sad. Speed is a problem with some tour operators and has unfortunate consequences. The geysers are amazing. We took a plunge in the hot spring. Felt invigorated afterwards. It is at a high altitude so good to help with getting used to the thin air if you are heading to the salt flats of bolivia after SP.
title: The trip to the geyser is so worth it!

review_text: My boyfriend and I only had 11 days to spend in Chile, but we chose to stay 2 nights in Pucon to give ourselves a full day in this thrill-seeking town. We were hoping to go canyoning, but unfortunately the 2 more challenging canyoning trips were not available. But Miguel saved the day by recommending we rappel down the Salto el Claro, a stunning 80 meter waterfall. Usually there is a minimum of 4, but it was early in the season and slow, so they made a special trip - just the 2 of us customers with 2 very attentive, patient, and professional guides, as well as a photographer (we weren't looking for photos but she gave us a great deal). And we were SO glad they did. Both of us have rappelled a couple times before, but every time is different and this was no exception. I was a little nervous going over the edge (what's the fun of it if you're not??) but once I got going I felt completely safe and secure. The scenery is incredible, both up close with the waterfall and the vegetation, and afar as you take in the views over the canyon. I really want to thank Miguel and his team for giving us the adventure we were looking for in Pucon. It absolutely made our visit there worth it. Guys wht a great review, thanks We had so much fun that day to.. Best regards

Vast vistas, challenging terrain, experienced and attentive guides and wranglers, wonderful horses, great food and drink. This trip was stunning in all respects. Carman was exceptional in her attention to the only native English speaker and less experienced horseman (me - understatement). Tilley was equally attentive and encouraging on the Argentine side. Alejandra and Satu made the start and ends of each portion of the trip special with their meals. Aldo - exceptional horse tender and joyful spirit around the fire. Dense forest trails, cool clear streams, condor escorts, vast open Pampa .... astounding from beginning to end. We set out as four strangers and returned a family. Don't waste time considering.
