review_text: This 100 year old house,palace, museum built by Italian architects and next owned by a Very successful Croatian businessman has an interesting history to its development and where it finds itself today in the historical life of Valpo. ( I am advised that if one has been to Valparaiso twice you may refer to the City as Valpo). I passed by here several times over the past few Canadian winters but today I entered for the first time and was quite surprised by what I saw and learnt about something I took for 'just another building'. To my surprise on entering I noted something I expect to see back home, a special discount for Seniors, which meant entry for $1.00 Cdn / 500 pesos. The Museum is loaded with painting assigned to various levels of the house, one or two get a few sculptures. In some respects there are so many it almost becomes overwhelming to your senses. However that is lessened when you devote some time to the absolutely fantastic detail of the workmanship evident in the details of the wood .. Absolutely Beautiful. Just when that abates you step into the Master Bathroom. Considering the period of construction I thought perhaps I has passed through a time warp. The shower is something else - -- I Want one of those. You can get quite a bit of detailed info on Wikipedia by doing a Baburizza Palace Search. When you have finished you can stop by the resturant for a drink, lunch. A definite Recommend when in Valpo.
title: The Baburizza Palace, Museum - Museo Bella Artes de Valparaiso

review_text: Its an important point, the park is very new and the trees haven't grown yet so many of the play areas are exposed to the brutal Santiago summer sun. The locals turn up at about 5 or 6pm for their evening strolls. There are, however, plenty of free sunshades dotted about with deck chairs if the heat gets too much. There's lots of space, toilets, ice cream, lots of activities for kids and dogs. Flamingos and carp wait patiently for their never ending supply of feed from well placed feed dispensers. It is very much a work in progress and often something new has sprung up between visits, not to mention the regular Chilean food fairs and the annual "Chile Lindo" festival too. Well worth a family visit.

review_text: Highly recommend: both Valparaiso (the city) and “Ruta Valparaiso” (Cristian Blanco and the Ruta V. private tour company). I was a fairly demanding and detail-oriented organizer of a small group of people disembarking from a cruise ship. I corresponded for a few months with Cristian via e-mail over the course of a few months, to develop and settle on a concept for our small group’s tour that would be best tailored to our specific circumstances. Cristian was prompt in communication, patient, and fully responsive to areas of inquiry. Although (due to the itinerary of our cruise) Valparaiso was our final destination, the specifics and terms of the tour we had developed with Cristian and R.V. were well and completely worked-out, so that on the morning of debarkation, there were no worries and there was complete clarity. The result, was a seamless transition “from the custody” of the ship, into the care of the Ruta Valparaiso van/driver/tour guide at the exit Valparaiso Marine Terminal. (You might hear "the terminal" and think "scary, busy" place, but it is actually pretty easy to move around in, and it has some seats, some decent souvenir shopping, and a fairly orderly luggage collection method, so don't foresee it as an overly arduous experience.) At the terminal, the R.V. tour guide and vehicle had professionally-drawn placards that clearly identified them as for our specific small tour group. The signs were easily recognized by all members of our group. Getting our baggage stowed onto the van was straightforward and quick. At that point, our R.V. tour guide, Danae took over; she did a fine job taking us on our desired combination tour of Vina del Mar and Valparaiso, followed by a transfer to the Santiago Airport (or in the case of two from our group, a drop off in Santiago at their hotel). Danae took us to see highlights in both Vina del Mar and Santiago, and her extensive knowledge and clear love for her cities showed through. We enjoyed seeing Vina del Mar; however, I’d be remiss if I didn’t comment that we were simply “blown away” by Valparaiso. The word is overused, but the place is unique. It’s a mind-blowing, visually arresting place – be prepared to get and keep your cell-phone camera working. Very much appreciated Danae’s backup in that regard, as her pictures captured what we didn’t manage to, and more. In our group, we had some folks with slightly limited mobility as well as a couple with a toddler in a stroller: given the almost never ending sets of stairways and hills in Valparaiso, you'd think it would have produced some grumbling, but the place was so interesting and different (as in - when you round a corner, you really don't know what is going to be on the other side), that it really kept issues of the walking-challenged to a minimum. (That, and, the van did a good job of dropping off and picking up - visualize if you will a game of chutes and ladders on a set of hillsides. If after looking at some of the city pictures, you can't visualize what I am saying, don't worry; you will after being there!) Some final advice on tour design: due to our circumstances, we only had about 5 hours total before having to leave for the airport. If I had to do it again, I’d probably trade off an hour less of Vina (fine, but less interesting) for an hour more of Valparaiso. Or, bite the bullet and spend all of the little time we had in Valparaiso. Or best, find a way to spend an overnight there: Ruta Valparaiso clearly knows how to expand an itinerary with worthwhile events, to make best use of more time as it becomes available. Well done, RV! Thank you very much for your detailed comments regarding your experience with us! Your comments are very interesting and I believe very useful to those who don´t know what to expect upon their arrival. We´re very pleased that you were blown away with our city and you´re welcome to be blown away again any time you wish to return. The doors are open for you! Danae sends her best to you and thanks you for mentioning her. Our very best from the Ruta Valparaíso Team!

Then you can do the French Valley (day 1 - 21km), go to Refugio Grey (2 - 11 km), splendid ice hikking + pensil bridge (day 3 - 12km), sailing to the excellent Hotel Grey (day 4) and finally the trail to the base of the Torres del Paine (day 5 - 21km). All this with the company of a very special guide, Tomas, who gave all the tips on how to go up and down the rocks in a technical way, with rhythm, using the sticks and without wasting energy!! review_text: My daughter and I hiked the W from Torres Del Paine to Grey Lago. I am in my 50's and a long distance runner in good shape. I am not inexperienced backpacker. I found the uneven rocky surface challenging because I am so wary of turning my ankle and losing running training. Hiking boots above the ankle were a must for me. I wore them a lot to prepare for the trek but I did not find a place that mirrored the uneven surface. I ended up with a bruised knot above my right ankle from the boot digging into my skin from foot leaning inward over V shaped trail and uneven rocks. That was pretty painful on day 3 but it improved with duct tape wrap for day 4. I am petite and that also presented a challenge when climbing rocks on parts of the trail. I cannot see an unfit person enjoying anything but a day hike (but youth may be able to make up for some of it). We were blessed by perfect weather during our stay. Perfect weather does include a small burst of sleet the first day, a bit of sprinkling here and there and very heavy and challenging wind gusts or parts of the trail. It just made the rewards that much sweeter. We stayed in shelters during our trek. Shelter Torre Norte was a bit like teen camp. The expected bunk beds and hall bath facilities were basic and fine. We had 6 girls to a room. There was hot water in the showers and no line any time we saw. The dinner in this shelter was not even edible although many were managing. Mystery meat and cold vegetables that tasted nothing like anything I'd ever had made us dive for the granola bars back in the room. Of all the bad food we had on the trek this was the worst. Our lunch provided by Shelter TN was typical of all of them but still the worst. Staff was nice enough but not outstanding. The next shelter we visited was Domo Frances. This was our favorite. The gal that seems to be in charge (yikes--I forgot her name!) was very helpful and enthusiastic. The shelter is the smallest that we visited and we enjoyed meeting the fellow trekkers and the food was the best we had on trek. The domes were newer and the only clean place we experienced after campers came thorough. Paine Grande was big, loud (constant door slamming), dirty and old. We were scheduled to camp at this stop and were dreading it because it was so windy and cold. The unexpected vacancy in the shelter made us happy with even the gross accommodations. The front desk girls were nice and helpful there. Vertice Gray was the last shelter for us. It was great when we arrived but the bathrooms were disgusting by 2 hours later. I believe they must be crashed by campers that are supposed to use the building next door. Seriously gross bathrooms--sanitary products (used) left in showers, tp that missed the trash can all over the floor, slushy floors from shower water, mud and tracked in dirt all over the entire floor of bath. This is too bad because the staff housekeeping was left to clean it and they do a good job. (We were witnesses to how clean it was upon arrival.) The staff was nice at this shelter and the rooms were nice. Two sets of bunks to a room. There are a few things that would have made our trek easier and more enjoyable. These are tips for anyone ready to trek the W-- Make sure to have cash in pesos. You must pay the park entrance fee in cash. We did not know this and through a series of traveling challenges ended up at the entrance short of about $1 (for two of us). They would not let us in. Finally, a kind volunteer gave us a dollar of her own money. They will accept dollars or pesos but no credit cards. You also will be asked to tip throughout the trek and may want cash for snacks or drinks at shelters. Next, we were not prepared for co-ed living. A warning would have been nice. I realize that this is not a surprise to many hostel frequenters but we did not expect co-ed rooms. It can be awkward. It is hard to find bottled water at the shelters. If you have a water bottle or bladder to fill you will be fine but expect to haul it around with you. You can refill in bathrooms and we're told the water is fine straight from the streams. (We still filtered.) There was some internet at Torre Norte and we could buy time at Domo Frances in the dining area. However, there was not internet at other shelters. It would have been great to have it at Gray because we had lots of down time and had finished our reading. I noticed many others with the same predicament at end of trek. If you suffer from any hay fever/allergies, travel will plenty of meds. Especially at Paine Grande our allergies really flared up. Medication was a great relief. The catamaran (Grey III) trip back to leave park and see glacier along the way was a nice surprise. The boat staff was excellent and the sights were amazing. I highly recommend this. A couple of ways fixes in the shelters would make them much more comfortable for hikers. More (or any) hooks in the shower areas would be great and helpful. Paper towel dispensers that actually work would be a plus. In every shelter but the Domo Frances, the dispensers were full but not working so nobody could dry hands. I was beginning to think it was intentional so paper was not scattered around! The other think would be to put felt pads on the door frames of doors that slam. An easy fix especially needed at Paine Grande. Yes, these views are from a traveler that prefers a soft bed and a blow dryer. However, anyone that is a few years away from middle school camp might agree with my experience. This is a stunning park and the trek is a don't miss. Just be aware of the challenges and you will have a great time. The park is safe and you do not need a guide to follow the circuits.

review_text: We were debating between Salar Andino and Towanda Tours for our 3-day, 2-night Salar de Uyuni trip from San Pedro de Atacama to Uyuni - ultimately the choice came down to two factors for us: 1. Salar Andino only charged us 100,000 CLP for the trip, compared to 115,000 with Towanda Tours; 2. Salar Andino has offices on both sides of the border, so you know that the company is owned entirely, so you are not handed off to an unknown company when you reach the Bolivian border. I think that Towanda Tours had a specific company they work with on the other side, so it's still not a bad choice. Both tour companies choose to stay the first night at a lower altitude in Villamar, which is a safer option with a lowered risk of altitude-sickness (still a high altitude, and the sickness can affect anyone, no matter how fit you are). Again both companies follow a similar route, and during the wet season spend the second night in Uyuni as the salt-flats are flooded (do not choose a company that states they stay on or near the salt-flats the second night, it's untrue or unsafe either way). We traveled with Salar Andino in the middle of February 2018, right in the heart of Carnival. For those who are already nervous about traveling within Bolivia due to frequent reports of unsafe or intoxicated driving, Carnival is a season which increases the risk (a lot of drinking goes on during this festival). Many companies choose not to tour Salar de Uyuni at this time to minimise this issue, yet when we traveled with Salar Andino, our driver Eddy was a safe driver through and through. On top of this, many of the other tour groups we saw along the way also seemed to have very friendly, and safe drivers with them. The route is not a covered road, so expect a bumpy trip along many of the routes - Eddy our driver was one of the 'slower' drivers who slowed right down to navigate some bumpier areas, when we were overtaken by other drivers speeding over the holes and uneven surfaces - this was one of the more reassuring points for us - he was not in a rush. The food provided by this company varies little from the other tour companies (when everyone arrives at the accommodation or lunch spot, their is a big kitchen run by locals, and they provide essentially the exact same meal for each group - the only differences were the types of fruits given for dessert, or a flavour of yoghurt for breakfast etc. During one dinner we were not given a dessert, while other table had - it just just depends what your company has previously organised with the kitchen.) The food that is brought with you in the car is not usually what you consume - it is to replace what you eat at the remote locations, a great exchange, I think, which lessens the need for delivery vehicles to these destinations. We were asked at the beginning of the tour if we were vegetarian (we are not), so it is good that they are aware of different preferences, should we require a vegetarian meal. The accommodation was completely fine the first night, yet the second night in Uyuni had much to improve on (hot showers were not working on certain floors, and it is a bit of a dark and dingy place - not Salar Andino's fault though). We were worried about altitude sickness before starting the tour, because San Pedro de Atacama's many tours were cancelled due to the rain, so we did not have ample opportunities to acclimatise well beforehand. We carried with us a prescription from New Zealand from a travel doctor for some Diamox (check with your doctor - makes you pee more, tingling fingers, and soda tastes flat), which we think did help with the adjustment, plus we purchased some coca candy (available from many convenience stores in SPdA), and the tour companies all have either coca tea or leaves to drink or chew to help. One girl in our group had a really bad headache and nausea, which the tour guides were quick to make her a hot coca tea, and I offered some iBuprofen to help with the headache. She was mostly ok the next day, just really tired. We all experienced varying symptoms (headaches, dizziness, breathlessness when walking). The sites that are visited are beautiful, which Salar Andino cannot take credit for, yet you are given plenty of time at each place to take photos, breathe in the fresh air, and stretch your legs. There are not many toilet breaks, so take the chance to use a bathroom each time you have the option to. At one point we were still two hours away from our accommodation, so a lovely Brazilian girl we were traveling with took turns with me to hold a towel up for each other while we peed (sorry, TMI? It's a valid point of concern, so...), as there was no shelter in site for miles around. Not everyone is keen on taking a quick dip in the thermal pools, and it is only recommended to spend up to 15 minutes in there, as the heat alters your blood pressure (I think), and may make any altitude symptoms worse (especially as when you are traveling from San Pedro to Uyuni, the highest point of the trip is straight after you swim/have lunch. We had many concerns before traveling the Salar de Uyuni tour, yet essentially all of them were catered for with Salar Andino. We recommended them to a couple we met before we left (just based off customer service in their office in San Pedro), and when we met up with them again in Uyuni, they had had just as good of an experience. The only difference they experienced is that the pick-up vehicle arrived 15minutes early in San Pedro, and expected them to be ready, therefore rushed them. Our experience with the pick-up van was smooth, the driver was kind, and only just a little bit late to collect us, rather than early. Many people complain about having to wait out in the cold for up to 45minutes for their pick-up, but to be honest you will be cold at many points of the tour (standing outside to take photos is colder than waiting to be picked up), and if you are too cold waiting to be picked up, you probably don't have warm enough layers for the trip. Highly recommend Salar Andino! 4 stars instead of 5, because of lack of dessert when others had it (no biggie, just bring your own sweets if you REALLY need them), and not the best accommodation choice the second night in Uyuni (both minor details, we were not too miffed by it, some people were). Thank Eddy!

After taking the group to the train for our ride he arranged to pick us up at the other end for our tour through the park - what stunning scenery. Our guide, Lucas (??), was very engaging with a wicked sense of humour; he gave us so much information on the history of the area, how it became to be set up, and the early indigenous Indians of which we knew relatively little. He also gave the group the option of doing a walk through the area to the lookout overlooking Bahia La Pataia which we thoroughly enjoyed. His knowledge of the local flora and fauna was outstanding, he found birds in trees that even with him pointing them out, we had trouble locating. Dealing with Jamie was very easy, he answered all emails promptly and his handling payments from the group was great as I, being the tour organiser, did not have to do it. If you do not like overpriced crowded ships tours, I can highly recommend Jamie and his group of guides and drivers. review_text: This is a fascinating and spectacular otherwordly landscape, well worth the 2 hour drive from San Pedro de Atacama. Of all the fantastic Atacamean landscapes that we saw, this one was our favourite. A one hour walking trail leads down to the rocks bordering on the aquamarine blue salt water lake. It is not a difficult trail but feels strenuous due to the altitude of 13,000 feet. CAUTION: Do not go directly to Piedras Rojas without tickets, as they will not let you in. It is suggested that you purchase tickets in advance online, but we could not do so due to glitches in the system, and we met others who had the same problem. Thus, we set out and stopped at the visitor centre in Socaire, 90 km south of San Pedro, to purchase tickets for cash. In our case, we had to go through a routine to demonstrate that we couldn't buy the tickets online before they consented to sell them to us for cash. Glorious state of Chile, please reform your ticket purchase practices, as it is not fair to be hit-and-miss when buying tickets for these amazing attractions!

They both went out of their way to make it a great experience - stopping along the way when we spotted llamas so we could take pictures; Daniel jumping out of the bus to get every person on the tour a sprig of a local herb for us to smell (Rica rica). At the salt flats, they set up a lovely spread of appetizers and juice (no alcohol allowed at the National Park). It was a perfect day!!! I cannot recommend Latchir enough. We had already signed up for another company for our excursion the next day and it was terrible...we kept thinking about Daniel and Marcelo and wished we had waited to choose our next tour with them. Thank you, Latchir!
title: Salt flats with Daniel and Marcelo

review_text: We just did this tour with Guillermo as our guide. The tour itself is very interesting, with an historical overview of Santiago, but Guillermo certainly helped making the long walk so much more interesting and funny. The name "free" can be misleading since you're asked for a tip at the end, but we already knew it (did some of these tours before) and gladly paid an amount we could afford.
title: Awesome tour and guide!

review_text: I closed 3 tours with Smart Tour in November 2023 to be carried out in February. After buying and paying, the contact didn't last, I arrived in Santiago thinking that everything would go as planned and in line with them but it was totally different, first we closed the exchange with them to receive the chip at the hotel, we scheduled it for 5:30 pm and it was delayed by more than 1 hour and they didn't notify me or respond to my messages, forcing me and my friends to stay at the hotel and wait, meaning we missed the scheduled city tour. The first tour was ok, as the guide is from an outsourced company we had no mistakes, the second day was chaos, we closed Cajón with hot springs and only discovered in the middle of the tour that they sent us to the wrong one, the one we closed included breakfast morning, lunch and the spa. We arrived at breakfast and had to pay, when we questioned Smart we received no response. Only later, after much insistence from me and my friends, did they respond and inform us that it was a communication error and that we weren't going to do it, we only had 4 days in the city, everything was planned to make the most of it, we had booked another tour with They suggested canceling it so we could hold the spa, which wasn't done. Only hot springs, we chose not to do it because the tour we booked was more expensive than just hot springs and they would not provide any type of refund. We were injured, remembering that until that moment they had not delivered the chip, we had to buy the part so as not to be left without communication. The last trip to Portillo was ok because it was an outsourced company, because if it had been done by smart I can't guarantee it would work. Horrible communication Perfect social media, sells something that doesn't deliver They promised and didn't deliver The experience with Smart was traumatic, we were left without the tour we booked, we were left without a chip and without their positioning, we only got a return on Monday. And we arrived on Saturday morning To be bad you have to improve a little
title: Traumatic experience

review_text: We were very well looked after by instructor Alejandro Garcia and driver César! I recommend their service, very friendly!
title: Alejandro Garcia and Cesar

review_text: We attempted to go on a Sunday which wasn’t a good idea due to crowds. So second attempt on a Monday proved to be worth the wait. There were no lines for the funigular up or down. We were able to enjoy a peaceful time wondering around the gardens. The views are great but it is very smoggy so hard to really enjoy the mountain views.
title: Beautiful spot

review_text: I'll keep it short, you want a shopping mall experience in Santiago head to the (relatively) new Costanera shopping center in El Golf - it's a shopping experience. There are other local shopping malls of the long all in one American style mall but the Costanera has them all beat.
title: A Shopping Experience

review_text: The tour was perfectly organized, with an expert guide who gave us fascinating information about the place. In addition, the driver and guide were key to enjoy the landscape without worry. 100% recommended for those looking for a unique and well-managed experience in Atacama. Don't miss it! Review of: Half-Day Tour to the Valley of the Moon
title: Incredible experience with San Pedro Expeditions to the Valley of the Moon!

review_text: Excelente, atenciosos e exclusivos. Não bastasse excelente vinho, degustação muito descrita, em um ambiente maravilhoso. meus elogios ao sommelier Christian. Excellent, attentive and unique. Not enough great wine, tasting very described, in a wonderful setting. My compliments to the sommelier Christian.
title: Maravilhoso, exclusivo e atenciosos

review_text: A wonderful chance to get out of the city and away from the airport. The horses were kind tempered, very sure footed and strong. Lunch beside a running stream was very relaxing.
title: Relaxing interlude away from the city with amazing scenery!

review_text: Very interesting and enjoyable introduction to the world of astronomy, with a very didactic talk, a 3D video and stargazing with a telescope. Excellent service: glass of wine, hot soup, blankets to protect from the cold of the night, all included in the price.
title: Excellent theoretical and experiential introduction to the world of astronomy

review_text: The experience was Amazing and unique. Fynn is super kind and caring, I have never ridden a horse but thanks to her and her care I had a memorable experience. thank you for everything Thank you so much Rafael! You did great for a first-timer! We trotted and galloped! Thank you very much. Best wishes :)
title: Horse Connection - Full day

review_text: We did the Bridge to Macal tour with Rio Futaleufu Rafting and it was fantastic! Super nice and experienced guides and safety measures that let us feel safe and sound. The trip was a lot of fun and action! In the end we enjoyed some snacks and drinks in the beautiful and quiet Macal area. Thank you!
title: Fun and action with great guides!

review_text: Our Tour with Sergio and Helen was a Great experience. We really enjoyed the well planned trip with the very interesting spots, besides our excellent, funny and friendly guides. :-)
title: Great!

review_text: Excellent chauffeur hermenes and super friendly and attentive Bethlehem flight attendant. Highlights of their work. As for the excursion we do not regret that it did not include the fifth of Vergara. We recommend including the fifth of Vergara and Reñaca in the tour Review of: From Santiago: Valparaíso, Viña del Mar and Neruda Museum Agradecemos de que nos haya comentado la experiencia vivida.
title: Fantastic attention

review_text: An excellent attraction with stunning views and photo opportunities. Make sure you have warm clothing and gloves as it is freezing before the sun rises.
title: Well worth the early morning start

review_text: They were very attentive from the moment of hiring, through confirming the itinerary, and during the tours. Furthermore, the guides were very friendly, polite, and showed special care for the group. I highly recommend it!!!
title: Tours in the Atacama Desert

review_text: Several companies offering basically the same tours so shop around for best deal... can get there in a day, which is preferble to over night tariff. Several companies
title: Expensive but worth it

review_text: The best way to visit Torrez del Paine is by a Provide guide tour, the best experience with extraordinary guide and safety driver and confortable transport. This tour should be on the top of the list Review of: Private Torres del Paine & Milodon, departing from Punta Arenas
title: Top list tour

review_text: Such a great day! Ended up much longer than expected because of traffic outside of anyone’s control, but Daniel was such a fun and thoughtful host, everyone seemed to bond and have a really nice time. We still hit all of the spots and took our time. We laughed a lot, learned a lot, and saw so much! The rest of my time here will be measured against this wonderful experience. Highly recommend! Review of: Valparaiso Port and Vina del Mar Full-Day Tour from Santiago
title: Great Trip with Great Host!

review_text: One of the best walking tours we have been on in our many cities visited. Franco was our guide and he has a charismatic style that keeps your attention all the way through with the knowledge of a local, which he is. It's a great mix of interesting history with relevant tips for your stay in the city. It meant what would normally be a long 4 hour tour seem to fly by. The half hour break is located in a good spot at midday which helps as well. Although the place they stop at charges a bit more dos they can so don't be afraid to walk to Merced street to get a cheaper empanada.
title: Superb!

review_text: I needed to make an adjustment to the return route and they asked me to cancel the reservation and the refund would be automatic. I canceled, I didn't receive the refund/refund, no one answers the chat, they leave you talking to yourself. I DO NOT RECOMMEND. I just want my money back, I only saw later that the reviews on Google are terrible, apparently it's common for them to act that way, lack of respect and lack of commitment to tourists. Do not buy anything from this company. Hola, lamentamos tu mala experiencia, estamos constantemente trabajando para mejorar, por favor déjanos tu solicitud de devolución en nuestra pagina para que nuestro equipo de post venta te pueda contactar https://www.transvip.cl/contacto/ o bien a nuestro correo contacto@transvip.cl
title: Bad company, run away, lack of commitment to passengers

review_text: Set your expectations for this one. You get to look through some powerful telescopes but you're not going to see anything mind blowing. Just sort of an amplified view of what you see in the sky. The English guide was great and knowledgeable and gave a full tour but my group had a good twenty or so people, some who clearly were just doing the tourist thing and didn't really care and you have to wait your turn to look through the telescope. So if you don't like crowds and prefer a more personal, unique experience, I wouldn't say Mamalluca gives you that. If you're in La Serena anyway, it's cheap and easy enough to go (through a tour operator) but not worth a trip specifically for it from, say, Santiago. Also, small point, but it would be nice if they had a souvenir store of some sort.
title: Clearly for tourists but adequate for a quick tour of Chile's astronomy industry

review_text: We found this tour by accident and ended up with 20 fellow passengers in two small buses going where the big tour buses couldn't go or getting there long before them. Saw condors being taught by mum and up close to the sunken timber in the river but best of all was the warm welcome at the small ranch. The young girls were making small scarfs on cotton reels (they are surprisingly warm on a cold day) and the food was marvelous (the whole lamb was being cooked on large skewers in the fir place) and the wine was excellent. Our group had quite a few Aussies in it and we ended up buying all the stock that was left (at $5 a bottle!!!) It was Gato or Black Cat which were able to find when we got home. The dancing demo was most entertaining and I was encouraged to take the male roll in the Cueca (look it up it's quite funny) and I was absolutely exhausted by the time the music stopped (wish we could download video to this site!!!). Great fun. All in all a fabulous time and well worth the money.
title: 20 very happy travelers

review_text: We chose the city tour to have the flexibility and ease to get around, Catalina was very supportive to make this tour a very nice experience. Review of: Cable Car, Funicular and Sightseeing Bus in Santiago one day Estimado viajero, nos alegra saber que tuvo una buena experiencia en nuestros buses y que nuestra colaboradora haya aportado positivamente en el recorrido. ¡Esperamos volver a verlo pronto!
title: Excellent tour.

review_text: Took metro to Patronato and walked to the funicular. You can purchase the funicular only or in combination with the Zoo. Had to wait half hour or better to go up. Great view of half the city, including the tallest building in Chile Dear Visitor, thank you very much for your comment, a hug.
title: Great View from Top

review_text: The view of the city from the top of the hill is a must do in Santiago, but be warned, even at 5 pm in the afternoon there is a long line to get a ticket. It took me at least 45 minutes from from arrival to getting into the funicular.
title: Nice, but be prepared to stand in line

review_text: Excellent we loved the treatment and dedication we saw each star, there was time for everyone until my 10-year-old daughter was fascinated with astronomy! I really recommend it. I suggest wearing warm clothes and a snack.
title: I recommend the experience

review_text: Miguel, our guide and Uldaricio Munoz, our driver made this trip especially memorable. Miguel speaks fluent English and is from Valparaiso, so he was very passionate about showing us the sites. We saw the Swiss click and the Moai statue and sea lions in Vina Del Mar and then headed to Valparaiso. We rise the cable car and saw the street art/graffiti. Miguel gave us the history behind the sites. We had lunch and headed to wine tasting at a vineyard at Casablanca. We were dropped off by 5:30 pm. Review of: Valparaiso Port and Vina del Mar Full-Day Tour from Santiago It's the stops that you mentioned that as a result give a perfect combo of art, culture, food, nature and more. We're glad you had a great time with Miguel. Thank you for your review.
title: Excellent day trip from Santiago

review_text: Unbelievable. Don Pedro's tour is super interactive, you have nowhere to be bored. The place is beautiful and the tasting perfect. Fully recommended
title: Wonderful

review_text: We got from A to B ok in the end, but you need your wits about you using this metro system! Keep a tight hold of your bags too, as we were warned by the ticket lady.
title: Rather crowded and confusing

review_text: Yes this is an expensive day if you are a budget traveller but it was worth every penny... trip to the market, wine tasting, cooking, eating and drinking... a great day! Thank you Ines :-)
title: Looking forward to recreating these recipes back home :-)

review_text: Not the most spectacular sunset I've ever seen but the rest of the trip with all the amazing scenery made the trip worthwhile!
title: Great scenery.

review_text: After a 2 hour ferry ride, you will arrive at Magdalena Island. The island is quite large and heavily populated by a colony of Magellanic penguins. We arrived mid-January to find fairly mature chicks losing their fluff and being extremely active and fun to watch. The penguins are not afraid of people and will cross our path freely. A number of other birds were nesting there as well. Magdalena Island is a great place to engage with wildlife and get some great pictures and video. This was a favorite tour of ours!
title: Amazing Penguin Adventure

review_text: We had a great day in Valparaiso with a trip to Vina del Mar. Pablo was entertaining and had good energy keeping the group going and getting us engaged. He was attentive and guided us through the streets of Valparaiso easily, recommending a great place for lunch. The stop at the winery on the way back was lovely. Super appreciated all the additional information and the willingness to endure everyone had a good time. Shout out to Rodriguez who was our driver. Definitely recommend! Review of: Valparaiso Port and Vina del Mar Full-Day Tour from Santiago It's the details that make the diference. Thats why we have guides that look into the details. We're glad you had a great time with Pablo. Thank you for your review.
title: Great day in Valparaiso

review_text: Besides the very beautiful view of Santiago, there's still a Sanctuary for religous people and a nice 'medieval' stone church uphill.
title: Very beautiful scenic view

review_text: We had a wonderful tour! Our group included two Americans and one Chilean, so the tour was given in both English and Spanish; English was absolutely fluent and I assume the Spanish version was as well. The penguins and other birds (and otters!) at the penguin rookery were the highlight for me, but the other places we stopped were also fascinating, and Cyril was extremely knowledgeable and friendly. Cyril was also nice enough to help us out with contacting our tour for the next day, as we'd been notified of a minor issue but due to internet issues we hadn't been able to respond. We had a great time and would definitely recommend working with this company to organize your exploration of Chiloe! Thank you so much for such nice words. At Chiloe Natural we are always trying to have guests take back home memorable experiences and a bit of Chiloe in their hearts. Anything we can from here, just let us know and needless to say, always welcome to the island. Safe and happy travels. Cyril
title: Full day tour - penguins and Ancud

review_text: Chile Dream Tours provides a good option among the different Colchagua Valley tours offered on-line. We had a private tour, for me and my american guests. As a chilean I was surprised by Sean's knowledge of Chile and its atractions. He provided a well thought selection of vineyards and flexible options for lunch. He was friendly and even took photos of us that then sent after the trip ended! It is a very good option if you are looking for a reliable service and a personalized tour in English. I would trust them for future tours 100% Marcela Review of: The Heart of Chilean Wine Country: Montes & Viu Manent Thanks so much Marcela! We are so glad that you enjoyed the vineyards. It was a fun day with you and your guests to the heart of Chilean wine country!
title: Excelent experience, recommended tour

review_text: Danny was our guide for exploring the streets of Valparaiso. His passion and knowledge for the history, culture, and art of the city made for an excellent outing. If your visiting Valparaiso this should be first on your to do list.
title: Fun and Informative Introduction to Valparaiso

review_text: Chris was our driver. It was my husband and I along with 3 others. Personally I think our group had a great dynamic and that in itself made the tour fun. What I also appreciated was Chris's professionalism and knowledge - not just on the vineyards and the area, but Chile in general. We discussed everything from nature to economics covering history, mining, and energy as well. It was a great conversation and a lot of fun. I think next to the vineyard tour, the car-conversations were one of my favorite parts. Not because the vineyard were bad, but because the conversation was that good. For the tastings, we opted for the 3 tastings. The first tasting was two from Casablanca and two from another Valley that was partnered with that Vineyard. This was a treat as my Husband and I were not able to visit other valleys during our short stay. The second vineyard was Loma Larga and it had one of the best vineyard, winery, and tasting tours we have ever been on. A little background - I greatly enjoy visiting industrial and family breweries, wineries, and stills as I also work with fermentation and distillation. The knowledge on this tour was not only accurate it was presented in an easy to understand fashion. Even better - I learned a few more things I didn't know before. After Loma Larga we went to our third winery where we at lunch. We had the option to taste their wines (not included) but we all just ordered a glass instead. It was a generous pour and another great wine. Pinot Noirs from Chile are probably going to be my new favorite followed by their Carmenere and Malbec. The last tasting and vineard was a beautiful building high on the side of a hill. This one allowed us to taste a Late Harvest which we hadn't had the opportunity to try at the others. It was a great end to the day. You are able to buy wines at each vineyard which we did. I would recommend doing it this way as my husband and I noticed the prices were less at the vineyard than at the stores in Santiago. Supposedly the vineyard all export to somewhere in the United States so we are now on a hunt to find them here as well (Yes - they were that good). Review of: Casablanca Valley Wine Tasting Including 3 to 4 Vineyards
title: A MUST DO!

review_text: It is a tour agency in the Atacama region. They are located on the main street of the village. There are agents who serve in English, Spanish and Portuguese. Negotiate prices with good discount for cash payments. I did the Night Tour to observe the sky. Included the van for transportation, going to the venue and back to the hotel. Presentation/class with astronomer, experience of visualization of elements of the universe with a telescope. Photo session, with the right to 3 photos of long exposure and very high resolution, which reveal a spectacular night sky, recording us in this environment. To complement it is served a cocktail under the clear sky, with hot , cold, salty and sweet drinks. Important warning: it is necessary to wear clothes that warm enough because it is open and nightly. Duration of the tour around 2:30h. I recommend Mitampi. They delivered what was proposed.
title: It is worth consulting and negotiating with this agency.

review_text: Only a short hours drive away from the city of Santiago - all arranged by Rose Deakin and her friendly team, I had a wonderful day horse riding in the beautiful mountains just south east of Santiago. I only made my booking less than 24 hours before, but everything was so perfectly organized, as if it had been planned a long time ago. The guide that was riding with me did not speak any English, so the communication was slightly limited by my inability to speak Spanish. By the end of the day, my Spanish had definitely improved several levels ;-) My Summary: If you have an extra day in Santiago - this excursion is a must! It was great to see you and thank you for such a great review
title: What a great way to escape from the city of Santiago

review_text: NOTE: In the May 31st, 2014 Wine Spectator, all four wineries Michael took us to were in their 30-page spread on Chilean wines. Michael picked my friend and I up at our hotel in Valparaiso on time for our full-day wine tour. It was just the two of us and he gave us some great information. He made it a relaxing and enjoyable experience, even dropping us off at the end of the day at our hotel in Santiago. First, we went to Casas del Bosque where we had a great tour and enjoyed the lovely setting. Next, we went to Emiliana (after he took a scenic route, as we had time to kill). This tour was great and the tasting was outdoors, where we enjoyed the beautiful weather and a cheese and chocolate plate. The third winery we visited was Morande, where we had a multi-course meal paired with different wines. Not only was the wine great, but the food was outstanding. The final winery we visited was the Bodega winery. The vineyards were gorgeous and the tasting room was fabulous. The entire trip was fantastic. Michael was warm, funny and enthusiastic and had so much knowledge of the area. I highly recommend this tour!
title: Full Day Tour

review_text: Place of many stories....I went with the accompaniment of a Guide, which by the way made the question of explaining every detail where we passed.
title: Bohemian life!!!

review_text: We visited this with our guide who explained about the original city and the two rivers. The views are stunning. Well worth the entry price and the shopping malls on the bottom floors are amazing.
title: Fabulous city views

review_text: I recommend this 100% if you like to sample local wines, especially from small batch of vineyards, and work in a day of moderate exercise. The food and stops were very authentic. The whole day had a very personal touch. I also learned a lot. Review of: Full-Day Private Maipo Valley Bike Tour and Wine Tasting from Santiago Hello again Rick! Thanks a lot for your recommendation. We appreciate very much your comment about finding the experience authentic and with a very personal touch. That one of our goals. Also is very rewarding to know that you learned a lot. Thanks so much for your rating. Warm regards, Juan
title: Wine tour by bike was fantastic.

review_text: This was my favorite tour in the Atacama desert! I did it with Ayllu, and it was awesome! I don't think I would have liked it better with any other company! The landscape is amazing, it looks like a painting, although you have to be careful because the altitude is really high!
title: Best tour with the best landscape

review_text: Saltos de Petrohue are a must when going to Puerto Montt. Located near Ensenada town, the place is the center of a huge amount of activities you can do in that area. Inside the Saltos there is a tourist store in where you can book rafting, and hiking activities through the park. Saltos the Petrohue are very impressive, although some of their walkways are closed due to the last volcano activity some months ago. They are fixing them. There are some stores inside the Saltos but I would recommend to buy your water and food far from there because it is expensive. There is a fee to enter. We also went through the El Sendero de Los Enamorados, which is a short trail bordering the river. Don't forget to visit the National Park and Todos Los Santos lake. From there you can go to Bariloche, Argentina.
title: Always a Beauty

review_text: We booked a airport transfer to our hotel through Mozo who book Transvip. When we arrive, they new nothing about our booking, we showed them the paperwork, finally they said because we booked more than 6 months ago it is to old & would not honour our prepaid booking. After an hour debating will they were watching I retrieved my initial email and sent it to Mozo, on seeing that they rang Mozo straight away & agreed to honour the booking. As we had another booking for 8 weeks later, I emailed Mozo & asked them to reconfirmed the booking so we would have no issues on our return. The night before our return we received an email from Transvip confirming our hotel transfer. On arrival we produced the email, the reply was they had no booking & wanted to charge us for the trip. Finally they agreed , we then sat in the van for 30 minutes whilst they tried to muster other passengers for our transfer. We also checked about our return trip the next day, getting a blank look I was concerned, she finally printed another docket, it has the wrong time, 1hr 30 min difference. I have written to both Mozo & Transvip for clarification.
title: Never again

review_text: Very good tour, learning about history, wine processes, and the tasting was excellent. The guide was also very friendly. Review of: Santa Rita Winery Premium Tour Muchas gracias por sus comentarios, sinceramente nos alegra que haya pasado un buen momento visitando #SantaRita.
title: premium tour

review_text: Absolutely worth going. I did prefer the audioguide tour in neruda's santiago house (la chascona) which seemed to have more background information, whereas this tour is just concentrated on the house and the objects inside. Very cool visit in any case.
title: Visit is worth it

review_text: Stpped for a glass of wine and relax after walking the surrounding area. Good 4 people watching. Seemingly over priced souvenoir shops. Went during an afternoon.
title: touristy but good for drink and people watching

review_text: The service was excellent, guides prepared to explain the doubts we had and with knowledge about the region visited. It was presented alternatives to the problems caused by bad weather.
title: Skill and knowledge

review_text: this place is the bohemian place we were looking after a long trip over patagonia and atacama, the best place in santiago, music on the street and art everywhere.
title: nice and clean!

review_text: I have visited other Skyscrapers but I know this is the tallest tower in Latin America. The view from 61st and 62nd floors offers a mind blowing experience with amazing views of the city and little bit of Andes mountains.. was there during sunset and it just enhanced the experience a bit more.
title: Gorgeous View of the city

review_text: If you are visiting Santiago, and you want to get a feel for the Andes in a short amount of time, then this is a "must do" excursion. The hike was exhilarating but not too difficult. The views around every turn were spectacular. The goats and wild horses added some animation to the scenery. We even spotted a condor. Our guides were informative and efficient. My wife and I finished the long day, thrilled with the experience. Review of: Andes Day Volcano 8K - Cajón del Maipo
title: Great way to experience the Andes from Santiago

review_text: Quality information design. Also had some English audio and subtitles on videos to listen to. Visiting Chile it was important to learn about this part of it's history.
title: Glad I went

review_text: I would put this on you list of wineries in the area, the tour wasn’t extensive but I did learn about identifying different varieties by leaf and grape. Marcellos is very knowledgeable about the area. The wines were very good, I’m a red guy but o did buy a bottle of the Chardonnay, the tour did cost 15,000 CLP but I found that was about in the middle of the price ranges. Review of: Small Group Wines and Flavours Guided Walking Tour
title: MontGras

review_text: We went to the square to see the statue and were glad we did. We rubbed the statue's foot and maybe be back? It worked for me in Rome. There is a lot of vendors in the square selling inexpensive handicraft and light snacks.
title: Rub his foot

review_text: My wife and I did the west to east W trek in for our honeymoon in early June 2023 organized by Vertice. It was a winter trek, the first time they were offered since the pandemic. It was amazing, one of the best adventures of our lives. For the first 2 days, we had the whole park to ourselves; we only saw one other group and we were the only guests at the Refugios. On the 4th day, when we did the Torres, it had snowed, and we were the first group on the trail, breaking the path. We got to the base of the Torres, and ate lunch completely alone for about 45min. Seeing the Torres and French Valley in snow was jaw dropping. All of this - the timing, the Refugios, the catamaran and transfers, the excellent food - was possible thanks to Vertice, and in particular their amazing guide Francisco Martinez and your director Juan Pablo. We hadn’t been on a guided trek before, and Vertice and Francisco have set an incredibly high bar. We highly recommend using Vertice and Francisco as a guide! We also highly recommend the winter trek for the solitude and the adventure! Dear Joe and Mira, What a joy to hear from you, and we're thrilled to know that the experience you had in Patagonia with us was good. Walking in the park during winter is an incredible experience. Patagonia is a destination to visit all year round; each season has its charm, and we hope to see more visitors each year during this time. Thank you so much for your recommendations, and we will continue working hard to provide the best service. We will pass on your comments to our guide, Francisco "Pancho" Martinez, who is currently on vacation, trekking in the mountains of Bolivia. Thank you again for choosing us, and we hope to see you back in Patagonia in the future!
title: Amazing winter trek with Vertice!

review_text: We had the pleasure of spending our stay in San Pedro Atacama with Loca Aventuras. 5 extraordinary days with our guide Claudio. He knows his region like no other and is attentive to our slightest needs just like Jean the owner. Claudio is an excellent popularizer for understanding all the geological phenomena of the Atacama Desert. In our opinion, visiting this desert without an expert guide is missing the essential part of the adventure to get the most out of it. During our visits we were also able to observe what other agencies offer and it has nothing to do with the service we received. And what can we say about Renée’s excellent cuisine in the middle of the desert. We highly recommend this company and on our next visit to this part of the world, we will take the opportunity to climb a volcano.
title: An unforgettable experience

review_text: We were pleasantly surprised to be the only 2 people on this tour and thoroughly enjoyed our day! Our guide, Leonardo, was personable, flexible with sights and timing in each place as well as knowledgable. We loved the colorful city of Valparaiso and drive along the ocean. This full day excursion was everything advertised and more! NOTE: as others have indicated, the restaurant in Vina del Mar is expensive but has a great view of the ocean. Possibly your guide would be willing to take you somewhere else if asked (it seemed flexible)? Review of: Best of Valparaiso - Vina del Mar and Casablanca Valley Tour
title: Perfect Day!

review_text: This park was across the street from our hotel, the Somelier Boutique Hotel, which I also highly recommend!!! What a Heavenly little spot to spend a few hours. Although surrounded by traffic, it is beautiful and restful. There is lots to explore, the gardens, the old fort and tower, water fountains and an amazing view at the top. Don’t miss this, easy walk to the top.
title: A slice of nature

review_text: Great horseback ride with my kids and husband, beautiful enviroment and paths. Ian make this experience a great moment. Speaks english and spanish. Highly recomended to enjoy the traditional countryside experience in Colchagua! Review of: Horseback rides Santa Cruz, Chile

review_text: In my vision this neighborhood could be compared to the bohemian, cultural and student area of Paris, the Quartier Latin. There are several restaurants, bars and craft stores. There are walls painted by "street artists". The buildings are mainly old and historical. It is worth the visit. The bars are crowded with people, specially students.

review_text: The metro system is very easy to use! You don't need to buy tickets all the time worrying about the price and handling money! You just buy a card available in nearly all the metro station at the cost of two thousand pesos (about three euros) and charge it as you go along! The card has no name and can be used by anybody meaning that even a party of six can use the same card providing there is enough money on it. The metro is spotlessly clean, people very polite and everytime we used the metro we saw somebody getting up offering his seat to somebody else who was standing!! Viva Santiago!

review_text: This was an amazing hike! Not many places where you can see magnificent mountains to the east and the ocean to the west. Most of the hike is very easy with the exception of the final 2km as you ascend the Boulders and steep trail. Highly suggest doing this hike. FYI it requires a full day. We approached via Valparaiso and into Olmue.

review_text: we really enjoyed our day with our cooking chef boris and our collegues, now friens from germany and the united states!! thanky for this great experience!! two people from austria

review_text: Highly recommended tasting and guide Esteban very well with everything Super prepared I'd come back again I recommend them to come for a walk

review_text: We only booked this trip the afternoon before departure and given other reviews wondered if it would happen given we had the sense we would be the only participants. But for the published group participation price they ran the tour just for the two of us. Our guide Guy was an expert outdoorsman and a true font of knowledge about Chilean flora and fauna. The trip out to La Campania is long and through a lot of ugly industrial landscape but when you get to this world heritage listed(??) biosphere it is worth the trip. We saw not another person all day and the landscape was diverse,spectacular and the flora fascinating. Andoandes provided a good picnic lunch and wine and snacks at the end. It was really worth the money and a great escape from the bustle and urban nature of Santiago

review_text: Be prepared for wetness! We were given really good ponchos and we needed them. The trail is well maintained and easy to follow but can be slippy. Not so much mud as it is covered with gravel. Our guide was full of fascinating info so do join up with a group. there was a neat waterfall to see on the way and we ended up at a lodge beside a big lake where they had lunch waiting - it was quite a long hike - we were out and about for a good 2 1/2 hours and clocked up 6.5K.

review_text: Excellent guide to the city and area, on time , pleasant, informed, sensitive to the needs and ability’s of the client.. I would use the same service again and highly recommend Vicente's professional guidance.. Review of: Viña and Valparaíso's Tour

review_text: My wife and I were directed by our hotel staff to go to the Costerna Center on Christmas Eve, December 24, 2016. The hotel staff told us that the Costerna Center would be better and safer than some of the places in the center of Santiago. We wanted to get a video game for my daughter's boyfriend for Christmas. We took the Metro Line 1 from U. Catholica to Tobalaba station. When we got on the Metro we were treated to the graciousness of the Chilean people. I sat down next to an elderly man and he began chatting with me. He only spoke Spanish (and I did not speak any Spanish) and I replied in English. However, we had enough words in common to communicate on a very basic level. In addition, a young man sitting next to me saw the words "Costerna Center" printed on the top of my Metro map and, even though he only spoke Spanish, he indicated to me that he and his girlfriend were going to the same place. When we exited the Metro we followed the young man and his girlfriend and the led us around a block or so from the Metro to the entrance to Costerna Center which had an elevated walkway across a busy street. My wife attempted to chat with his girlfriend who asked my wife a question and when my wife answered the young girl burst into a good natured laughter. When we got to the point were they were going in a different direction, the young man pointed to the entrance of the Center. As we entered we realized that Costerna Center was a HUGE mall of 5 or 6 stories and very modern. It had every store that you might find in the United States and then some. We found our way to the information center and asked about the specific type of video we were looking for. We were directed to the fourth floor and we quickly found the video store. When we entered the video store, we were helped by a young man. I showed him the specific video type we were looking for and he proceeded to show me several different video games of that type. I selected one and he took me to the cash register to pay. I gave him my credit card when he rang up the purchase and the credit card receipt that I was to sign required a passport (which was locked in the safe in our hotel room). I showed him my driver's license instead and wrote that number on the receipt. That was adequate and our purchase was complete. This huge mall is so different from the many other places in Santiago were you shop for things. This mall was almost exactly the same as any huge mall in the United States, including the bathrooms. It felt very much like being home and it looked like you could find anything there. The mall was very crowded on Christmas Eve as everyone was apparently shopping for Christmas gifts. We returned on the Metro with the perfect gift.
title: A Huge Mall

review_text: This is one of the places you’re sure to go on your guided tour of Santiago given its key role in Chilean history (the name tells you a lot). review_text: We had the privilege of spending time on our own with Frederica for the first hour or so of this tour which took place solely in the vineyard, where she showed us several different varietals of vine of different ages (including some 127 years old) and different types of canopy management. She explained the various processes needed to tend to the vines including pruning methods. In all the years I have been visiting wineries in different parts of the world this was the most interesting and informative tour of a vineyard. The tour ended with tastings of Neyen Espiritu de Apalta 2011 and 2013, both of which were superb. Many winery tours concentrate on the process of converting grapes into wine which is of course interesting, but I would absolutely recommend this tour to learn about the cultivation of grapes. I should add that Frederica was not only knowledgeable and enthusiastic but also a delightful person to spend time with.

review_text: Matias and driver Vincente met us at the hotel at 7 am for our 8:15 flight from Punta Arenas to Porvenir. After a fifteen minute Cessna flight, and a quick stop for coffee, we embarked on the two hour, 100 km ride to the King Penguin colony. Matias is very knowledgeable and particularly an expert on Patagonian birds. Visitors are kept about 50 meters away from the colony. However, Matias brought binoculars and an optic scope which enhanced our ability to observe the penguins. After a few hours of viewing and lunch, we returned to the airport well in advance of our 5 pm return flight. We believe the flight option, although more expensive, is a much better experience than the taking the ferry to Porvenir.

review_text: My wife and I attended the tour today. It was very interesting. The tour guide Alvaro was very knowledgeable and his english was perfect. He told us many fascinating facts about the city and took us to some very interesting places. Highly recommended.

review_text: The museum is really amazing. review_text: We ate here twice at two different restaurants. It is very pleasant place. Restaurants are not super cheap but aren't expensive either.

review_text: Our group of nine did the bike and wine tour, and had a fabulous time. Our guide was knowledgeable, fun, and energetic. Though it was a National holiday in Chile, and some of our access was limited, we were still able to tour some beautiful wineries, bike in the gorgeous grape fields, and have a delicious lunch. Mac, at La Bicicleta Verde, was incredibly helpful via email in recommending restaurants in Santiago as well. review_text: Fernanda was a great tour guide. She was informative and taught the history of chile. The tour was great overall and wine was great. Review of: From Santiago: Viña Concha y Toro Traditional Half-Day Tour Thank you for your kind words! 🌟 We're thrilled to hear that you enjoyed the tour and found Fernanda informative. Her knowledge of Chile's history really adds to the experience, and we're glad you loved the wine too! 🍷 We hope to see you again soon for more memorable adventures!

review_text: This winery is owned by the same people as the casino... and the hotel... and the other main tourist magnets in Santa Cruz. While it's great that they're doing so much for tourism in the region, this winery is not meant for anyone other than those who want a pretty view and have time and money to burn. The view is spectacular, both from the main building and from the hill the tour finishes on, especially in the fall. The colors, clouds, hills, everything, really were breathtaking. However, the wine tour was unremarkable. I had the misfortune of having a guide (in Spanish) who mumbled through his speech and was quickly drowned out by the very machines he was attempting to talk about. The tasting followed, and while the wine cellar is beautiful, we had to stand for 30 minutes and used the same glass for each tasting. After the tasting, we headed up to the gondola to go up the hill. I had felt uneasy about this part of the tour, but I was really blown away by it all. While I understand the mentality of the owners - many tourists to this region are probably coming to Chile only for the wine and to see the vineyards and won't get a chance to go to the Araucania, Easter Island, or San Pedro de Atacama - this is the same family who made the great and very thorough museum in town, which offers a great deal of information on all of the above cultures and other Andean cultures without the gaudiness and tackiness of a fake Moai statue, or a fake Mapuche ruca, or llamas packed into a too-small corral. They would have been better off to focus their energy on creating a quality winery experience, and leave the cultural aspect to the museum.
title: Not so much about wine

review_text: I was the only non-native Spanish speaker so the guide had to speak English just for me. Maybe because I understood a bit of Spanish, the guide started to forget about me and not explain me good. I felt lonely because I was traveling alone... The time was 5:30PM. I believed my guide and thought I had 20 minutes left. Honestly WHY did I pay for this... The other tour which was Miskanti Lake and the Salt Lake( flamingo) was fine. review_text: The Mapuche are an important cultural presence in Temuco. This Museum could be much more culturally and historically significant than it is. My personal preference was the early period exhibits located in the lower ground floor galleries. It is well worth a visit (pleasant cafe also).

review_text: My wife and I took this tour in December 2022 on our first day in Chile after arriving via an overnight flight. It was a nice introduction to the country. Communication via text was smooth beforehand. The breakfast and lunch, both hosted at the homes of locals, were a great touch. Christian was a capable guide loaded with information, not just about wine but about the area and its history. Very enjoyable day. One word of warning: This tour does not feature wine tastings per se. Rather, you show up at each of the four vineyards with a single, pre-purchased bottle of wine (or a bottle that your guide purchases in the moment) that you can enjoy on premises. Given the description, I had expected tastings at each vineyard. Instead of being served a variety of pours in a tasting room by someone who works at the vineyard, you drive up to various producers and open a bottle. That could be good or bad depending on your preferences. We also ended up being the only two people on the day's tour, which made for an intimate experience but also meant we were in the back of a sedan rather than the "little wine bus" in the description. Again, could be good or bad depending on your perspective. Overall we had fun. Christian shows you a great time and there are worse ways to spend a day in Santiago. But if you're looking for traditional wine tastings where you really get a sense of each vineyard, this might not be for you. Review of: Maipo Valley litle wine bus from Santiago Hello! I’m glad you had a very enjoyable day. Thanks for your comment it is VERY IMPORTANT FOR FUTUR VISITORS: you’re absolutely right. The Little wine bus is our only group tour and it does not include a tour and a tasting conducted by the wineries that are visited. Advise: review other Little wine bus comments before booking it. Our guests describe it better than us. It is a tour to have fun, learn about Maipo Valley Chilean wine and try the wines of the different wineries visited. All other tours are private and include tours and tastings conducted by each of the wineries visited. Nevertheless, I would like to mention that all our tours, also the little wine bus, include a wine expert local guide. My apologies if the description was not clear enough. We’ll try to improve it. Thanks for coming. All the best, Juan

review_text: Portilho is incredible, wonderful place, the guide was excellent! I highly recommend it, it’s an experience that everyone has to recognize.

Throughout the trip Roman spoke in great interest and detail about the history of South America, Chile and the attacks in particular. We liked that despite the clear plan of the whole trip - Roman was ready to adapt flexibly to changing weather conditions and our wishes. His excellent knowledge of Spanish helped us resolve any question that arose. Roman was always ready to perform the role of photographer - to help with the angle and to photograph. review_text: Travel around South America and it's amazing the colonizers you run into. The Spanish, of course. But also the Portuguese, the English, the French and, yes, the Welsh, to name a few. In Frutillar, Chile, it's Germans. Museo Colonial Aleman (German Colonial Museum) honors those 1852-and-later immigrants with a park adjoining Lake Llanquihue (see my review, "On a clear day . . .") that recreates their way of life. Founded in 1981, the museum has a country house, a cemetery, a blacksmith's house, a bell tower and a water mill, all set on beautiful forest and gardened grounds (some of the trees are more than 100 years old). Most, if not all, of the items inside the houses are original (but relocated) objects. TIPS: * If you're pressed for time, head for the impressive country house and the fascinating old German cemetery near it.
title: Recreated colony

review_text: Our tour of Chile was organised by Voyages Jules Verne. They arranged our private excursions in Atacama from our base in San Pedro over a five day period through Trekana Experience. This included airport transfers and visits over a 3 day period to Moon Valley, Ckari Lookout, Highland Lagoons, Chaxa Lagoon (Atacama Salt Flat), Tatio Geysers, Machuca, Putana Wetlands and White Geyser (for breakfast). During this time we had two guides both of whom were absolutely fantastic. They were extremely friendly, knowledgable, informative and professional. We were kept informed via a printed itinerary on arrival, our guide each day and text message updates the evening before noting any change to start times. Trekana picked us up and dropped us off at our hotel each day, assisted with baggage, ensured we knew of any important recommendations E.g. clothing, altitude etc. As some visits were at higher altitude where sickness may affect some they were especially attentive to ensure our well being. Our daily tours were packed with amazing and varied scenery, wildlife / bird sightings and an amazing lunch after visiting the salt flats and breakfast at White Geyser after our very early start to see the sunrise in the mountains. That breakfast was in one of the most awesome settings, such peace, tranquility and stunning view. Our guides brought the food and drink with them and set a table / bench and chairs up /- plenty of choice and very civilised. Our only negative comment was that there were others in our very small the group who didn’t get these messages directly, as Trekana treated us as group leaders rather than equals and separate couples. That said, everything worked well for everyone. However our strong recommendation to improve things is that Trekana set up WhatsApp groups from the outset including all participants to make life easier for everyone; especially when those in groups are not connected in any other way than by being part of a tour group. We appreciate Trekana guides’ experience and have many great memories that will remain with us forever. We know there is a lot of choice of tour / excursion operators in San Pedro, Atacama but we would highly recommend Trekana Experience.
title: Incredible excursions, breathtaking scenery

review_text: I did this satisfying boat/ferry excursion on the first day I enjoyed of my Tour Of Patagonia in November last year. We had already visited the Salto Grande waterfall and completed the beautiful hike up to Los Cuernos which was my personal highlight, this boat ride was at the end of a long but full day of interesting and fulfilling activities. For some of the older people in the group the walk to the boat was longer than they would of liked but I enjoyed it as I was at the front of the group enjoying a chat with one of our guides, Diego. The weather the whole day really was incredible, 25 plus degrees all day, dark blue cloudless sky's, no breeze or wind and perfect visibility. Obviously you get excited when you first see icebergs floating in the water and these Glaciers are some of the more detailed ones I've seen, I think you get one free drink, a Pisco Sour which I associate more with Peru, then you have to pay, I had a couple of beers. My Camera battery died half way through and after the Glaciers most people went inside but I stayed outside for the duration and admired the incredible scenery, I even enjoyed the walk back over the huge expansive beach to the entrance/coach, thoroughly enjoyed and a must if your there.

review_text: We chose Lithium for our 3 day tour of the Uyuni salt flats after reading great reviews and receiving a recommendation from a friend. We booked a few days in advance while in San Pedro. The logistics leading up to the tour were disorganized. We worked with a new employee who did not have all of the information we needed and gave us incorrect information (he even told us the wrong start time for the astronomy tour we also signed up for with lithium and we almost missed it). We were also not given all the information we needed about the border crossing into Bolivia. We finally got to speak to Eva, the most knowledgeable person in the office, but she was still unsure of many of these details especially regarding the visas we needed to enter Bolivia as US citizens. She eventually contacted the Lithium owner to help us find the answers but it was a frustrating and lengthy process. We were also assured by Eva multiple times that after the crossing we would remain with the same company. This was not the case and we were passed off to a Bolivian company called Estrella del Sur. This ended up being fine but it seems every tour company needs to pass you off to a partner company when you cross the border. That said, once we were on the tour, we couldn't have been happier with the experience. We were very nervous after reading reviews about unsafe driving and uncomfortable conditions but we found exactly the opposite to be true with our Lithium tour. Our guide, Omar, was excellent in driving cautiously (never over 40 mph), explaining each site and making sure we were all comfortable and happy. Food The food was of both higher quality and quantity than expected. We barely touched the snacks we packed. Each meal was hot and had both meat and vegetable options. Still a good idea to bring snacks and definitely bring a lot of water for all three days (1 liter per day per person) because this will not be supplied by the tour. Accommodations The first night we stayed in a hostel in a remote village. The 4-person rooms are shared and are made up so you don't need a sleeping bag. There are only three bathrooms for all ~20 guests and only one shower. The shower is bare bones and you need to pay to use it and for the hot water and towel (10 bolivianos for hot water and another 10 for towel). The hostel was rugged but fine. The second night we stayed at a salt hotel which was very nice (no sleeping bag needed). All rooms are doubles and you have the choice to pay extra (160 bolivianos) for a private bathroom. It is just 40 minute drive from the location you will watch the sunrise on the salt flats. Cost We were charged $175USD / person for the 3 days / 2 nights originating in San Pedro and ending in Uyuni (does not include transfer back to San Pedro). You will need to also pay for park entrance fees throughout the tour and will need to exchange Chilean pesos for bolivianos prior to the tour while in San Pedro. Schedule Here is a snapshot of the schedule to give you an idea of what you will see and what your days will look like: Day 1 7:10am-8:10am Pick up by bus at hostel in San Pedro de Atacama Drive 5 min to PDI de chile to stamp passport (immigration to exit chile) Drive 30 min to Bolivian migration Eat breakfast prepared by bus driver (fresh baguettes, avocado, ham, two types cheese, banana, tea/coffee, pound cake, cookies) Divide in jeep groups (6 people), meet guide and pack jeep Go through Bolivian immigration Set off in jeeps 5 min drive to pay park fee of 150 bolivianos 5 min drive to laguna blanca 5 min drive to laguna verde 15 min drive to Salvador Dali rock formations 10 min drive to aguas termales for 40 min stop (option to swim but need to pack bathing suit in your day pack) Lunch (raw and cooked veggies/cheese, hot dogs, mashed potatoes) 30 min drive to the Geysers 40 min drive to Laguna Colorada 1.5 hour drive to hostel Arrive at hostel around 7pm Tea and cookies 8pm dinner (veggie soup, pasta) Day 2 7:30am breakfast (pancakes) 8:30/9am on road 5 min drive to Copa Mundial rock formation 5 min drive to camel rock formation 5 min drive to Italia rock formations 5 min drive to laguna tinta 30 min to laguna negra Lunch (potato/egg/sausage casserole, veggies/cheese, rice, canned tuna) 1 hr drive to inca Canyon 1.5 hour drive to small town with coca and quinoa beer (beer not included in tour price) 40 min drive salt hotel 6pm arrive at salt hotel (default twin bed double shared bath, +160 bolivianos for private bath, +170 bolivianos for private bath with full size bed) Tea and cookies 8pm dinner (cabbage soup, chicken cutlet, fries, rice, wine) Day 3 5-5:30am departure 6:15am arrive at first part of salt flat for sunrise 7:30am arrive at fish island to walk around (30 bolivianos for ticket) and to eat breakfast (cereal, yogurt, lemon cake) Pick spot for pictures in the middle of salt flat (1 hour) Visit salt museum 12pm arrive in small town for lunch 1:30pm arrive at train cemetery 2/2:30pm arrive at Estrella del sur tour office to Uyuni to conclude tour Day 4 (Optional if returning to San Pedro de Atacama This day is only for the drive back to San Pedro. If you do this you will need to pay extra and will spend the night before in the same hostel as the first night. All in all, I would highly recommend Lithium but would be vigilant during the planning process.
title: Safe, great tour experience despite disorganized planning process
