review_text: Torres del Paine surely is the crown jewel of national parks and thoroughly deserves to be the 8th Wonder of the World. Its no wonder the Chileans work so hard to protect it! The park has it all. Vertical granite mountains, stunning glaciers, emerald-green forests, turquoise blue glacial lakes, icebergs, guanacos, condors, pumas. There is no shortage of things to see or do. Driving around the park... I cannot recommend hiring a car and driving around the park enough. I hired a car with a friend in Puerto Natales. It takes at least two hours to get to the park entrance from Puerto Natales and two hours to get back. If driving in from Puerto Natales, it will take a full day. Having done the W, I can say with confidence that some of the views from the road cannot be seen on the trek. Some of the views from the road are the most iconic of the park particularly of Los Cuernos ('The Horns'). The landscape views from Lago Pehoe and Salto Grande will break hearts! There are numerous other view points along the road. Views among the icebergs at Lago Grey at the end of the road are particularly stunning. Regarding the W trek... The W can be done from East to West or West to East. There are pros and cons for doing either. I spent five days going from East to West to get the hard ascent to the Torres out of the way. The views on the W for each day are varied with each view as unbelievably beautiful as the last. From East to West the high points are the Torres, Los Cuernos, Valle del Frances, Lago Pehoe & Glacier Grey. It is as if you are rewarded with a daily crescendo! The reputation of experiencing all seasons here is well deserved and impressive! In my 5 days of trekking the W, it rained, there was a blizzard, clear weather with sunshine and hurricane-force winds. Pack and dress appropriately! You can drink water from any stream or river in the park. There is no need to treat or filter the water. Its fresh & clean. There are refuges scattered along the W trek. They are comfortable, well-heated, serve hot meals & hot showers. Overall, excellent. Camping options are available in the park. There are designated camp sites along the W and around the refuges for $10 a night. However, if you are camping and some serious weather rolls in it might be worth thinking about spending the night indoors! Be aware though prices per night per person can be upward of $40 USD. It is impossible to get lost on the W. The trails are very well marked and you even get a map of all the trails as you enter the park. There is no need for a guide unless you are looking for information on the park, fauna & flora. If time allows, trek some of the trail called 'The Tail' along Lago Pehoe from Refugio Paine Grande. The views from the lakeside are gorgeous. I have never been to a place quite as special as Torres del Paine. In all my travels so far, it is the most beautiful place on Earth. Pack your bags & go!
title: The Crown Jewel of National Parks

review_text: We spent 9 fabulous days in and around Torres del Paine. I won’t add reviews of our time hiking in the park, as there are countless sites and blogs that offer incredibly useful and detailed information about trails and hikes to suit every interest. Our trip to the park began with 3 days in Puerto Natales. We checked in to Keoken Bed & Breakfast where Rodrigo guided us to things to see and do in the area. (A great place to stay near the lake and the center of town.) We rented a car from Newen Rent a Car. They are THE BEST company. Maria and her mother will deliver perfectly clean cars and add lots of information about the park and hikes in the area. The only thing we would have done differently is rent an SUV instead of a smaller car. The roads in the park are manageable without an SUV, but it would have been so much more comfortable and relaxing on those dirt roads (no paved roads in the park or leading to it for many miles from the south entrance at Serrano) in a larger vehicle. We spent the first 3 nights at Hotel Rio Serrano just outside the southwest entrance to the park. It’s a beautiful hotel in a perfect setting and offers great services. We did the bed and breakfast program instead of the very pricey all-inclusive plan that they offer. We had food with us from Puerto Natales, so ate a hearty breakfast that is offered at the hotel, a light packed lunch and sandwiches for dinner. The refrigerator in the room was a bonus, but we could have managed without it. The food in the park is absurdly expensive and not the reason for being there, so we felt good about our choice to create our own meals. The spa is a treat after long days hiking and included in your stay. Great weather (although really windy!) made for some great hikes in that end of the park. Then we spent 2 nights at Hotel Las Torres at the northeastern end of the park. The roads leading to this entrance from Puerto Natales are all paved but it is a longer journey than to the Serrano entrance - worth the extra miles and time to be on paved roads! We were already inside the park, so we traveled along the main park road toward the Laguna Amarga entrance. Hotel Las Torres is a working estancia where horses are set out to pasture and then corralled daily. It’s fun to watch. This is also the passing point for the Las Torres Mirador. We treated ourselves to the Lamb BBQ that was a meat lovers dream come true. From there we headed back to Puerto Natales for a night before making our way back to El Calafate. The park is magnificent and exciting. We avoided crowded hikes by starting early - 9:00 or so. We rarely ran into people along our hikes but noted the numbers arriving as we were leaving some areas. The greatest number of people appeared on the only section of the W route that we hiked from Hotel Las Torres along Nordensjkold Lake. It was fun to join them for awhile and then turn around and return to our cozy hotel. However you choose to see the park, you will not be disappointed.

review_text: I have visited many National Parks around the world, but none comes close to the fantastic scenery of Torres del Paine. The first time I saw the magnificent granite spires of the torres( towers ) and the cuernos (horns) , I was in awe!!! And, to see them at sunset is a photographer's dream! No photo can truly capture their magnificence. It is a site that does not disappoint, even after all the build-up it gets. It is not an easy task to get here, but well worth it! I stayed at Hosteria Pehoe, a small hotel in the middle of Lake Pehoe. It features great views of the mountain peaks( torres & cuernos). The hotel has a nice bar and a fine restaurant. Besides the incredible scenery, there is much else to photograph. The area has a high concentration of guanacos and nandu birds, which are quite photogenic. The only negative comment I can make about Torres del Paine is the weather. You can get all 4 seasons of weather in one day!! Plan your trip carefully, but definitely GO!!

review_text: If you go to Santiago, Cerro San Cristobal is a must. You´ll be able to see the whole city and also take quite nice photos of the Andes from there aswell. Beware of robberies, especially if you climb via non transited routes. Plase take the roads, which are usually guarded and many people walk up and down all day long, so it´s very very safe. There´s a funicular aswell if you are lazy enough not to walk yourself up there. This funicular runs from the very lower part of the hill to the summit, with a stop for the Zoo in the middle. There are also 2 big botanic gardens, two public swimming pools a restaurant with the best city views. A down side is that the cable car system was shut down few years ago, so it´s not possible to get to the summit using this service which used to be a lot of fun... Make sure to bring your camera with you, do not litter and take care of this beautiful place. Do not smoke and throw your cigarrettes to the forest as it might cause a big fire.

review_text: Grey Glacier is an excellent contrast to the Perito Moreno Glacier. Where Perito Moreno is surrounded by tourist infrastructure, and is a very active glacier, Grey Glacier is the exact opposite. Before you even get to the glacier, you will see a landscape like nothing else. There is a large flat expanse in front of you which the glacier has carved out when it was much larger. This expanse is covered with skree and then you see the lake. The wind seems to roar down the lake from the glacier, ensuring you will receive an icy blast. However the wind also drives any large 'icebergs' down from the glacier to the edge of the lake. Its surreal and we took a double take to get our dimensions. From the hotel, you see the lake, and the large icebergs (many times the size of a house) right up near the edge of the lake. You then realise those little dots in front of you are people in the distance. Hard to describe but if you've been there, you'll know what I mean. You can walk or get a tour bus down to the lake departure point. A word of caution. The day we were there was a very windy day and the waves coming down the lake were very big. They do a transfer to the tour boat via smaller boats. The large waves meant you need to be careful. We did have one person fall within our group. Nothing serious, but its a remote place so be careful. The wind racing down the lake means that sometimes the tour boat gets canceled. I didn't find the ride excessively bumpy even though they were very close to canceling the day we were there. Its a bit of a journey (I guess it felt like about 40-50 minutes going to the glacier). The boat was comfortable enough and offered good protection from the weather. We weren't there in peak season but our trip was full. Once you get there, you'll see an impressive glacier. Our guide told us the glacier used to be much larger, and this was borne out by the surrounding landscape. This glacier is not calving constantly, however there are plenty of ice chunks floating near the edge. Its a great opportunity to get up close and the blue color is mesmerising. You'll get the obligatory scotch with 'glacier ice' (who knows if it is, just go with it) when you get there. The boat ride back was much faster as we virtually surfed the waves. All up, we enjoyed the whole experience and I recommend it.
title: Another must visit attraction

review_text: One of my favorite things in Chile. ALMA is the reason why I traveled to the Atacama Desert part of Chile. The tour gets you up close and personal with the antenna control room and you might get a close-up of one of the out-of-service antennas. They've got a GREAT visitors center hallway, but it's underutilized. From the hallway you get a nice view of the antenna maintenance area and there are some interesting photos on the wall. But the hallway is so long and wide that it would be a GREAT place to put some multi-media, hands-on stations. The most challenging thing about running tours to ALMA is that you can't go to the antennas atop the mountain. That's where the REAL exciting stuff is. It would be fantastic if ALMA cold somehow figure out a way to get a pressurized bus up to the top of the mountain. I'd pay money to do that. The tour guide was VERY knowledgeable and answered every question. ALMA just started doing public tours, so they're still working out the bugs. The 40-minute bus ride from San Pedro de Atacama to ALMA could have been more productive. The tour guide was so knowledgeable that the ride would have been a great opportunity to pass some interesting information.

review_text: We did the day tour with this company to the Andes and volcanic hot springs. A very memorable day. We drove for a couple hours from Santiago to our main stop in the Andes. The final part of the trip is on unsealed roads. The trek was perhaps a 2-3h return on gravel, rocky surfaces was moderate incline/decline. We rested at our high point for snacks and photos. You need at least an average level of fitness and mobility. Bring plenty of warm gear, layers and trekking shoes. After the trek, we drove to the volcanic hot springs. There's change rooms, toilets and showers there. Several baths of varying temperatures. You might even give yourself an application of volcanic mud. On the drive back, we stopped for a (late) lunch and wine in the valley. Definitely recommend AndoAndes for this particular tour.

review_text: Its my favourite tour in Atacama. Its really unique. The tour starts at 5 am and ends at 12 pm. It cost usd$30 + ticket to national park usd$7. They pick you in your hotel and they take you straight to the geysers. Some considerations of what you have to bring. Water, sunblock, sun glasses, swimming suit, flip flops and towel. About your clothing you should use 2 pairs of socks, first layer of pants and shirt, thick pants, gloves, thick shirt, mountain jacket and something for your head and ears. Altitude there is 4.300 mts over the level of the sea. Drink a lot of water and move slowly. If you feel bad some aspirins will help. Temperature is very low - 8 degrees in celsius. When you get to the spot its kind of dark so you will be able to see the sun rise in the middle of the Andes. Beautiful They will give you breakfast and after that they will show you the geysers. Very cool. After a 100 mt hike you will get to the thermal pool. You can swim there for 30 minutes. It sounds a bit crazy considering low temperature but its worthy. Do it, you wont regret. You leave the place heading to Rio Putana. A short stop there to take pictures of tha flora and fauna of the place. After that you get to a small town called Machuca. Please try their food. Specially fried empanadas stuffed with goat cheese and "Llama anticuchos". An anticucho its wooden stick where they put chopped meat and onions and they cook them in a grill heated with coal. Outstanding flavour!!! Then you leave Machuca straight to San Pedro and thats the end of the tour. Did it through Altiplano Aventura agency. Again I must say that the guide, Arturo and the driver Ruben, they rock!! Do this trip through and ahency, roads to Tatio are rough.
title: The best in Atacama

review_text: We're just back from a Sept week in Portillo, and we enjoyed it. The warm Chilean sun, the spring corn snow, the friendliness of everyone we met, the good food and wine, and seeing the Canadian ski team and US women's team train, all combined for a great week. Most of my group wants to return. As North Americans, we appreciated the opportunity to ski at this time of year! We also appreciated how well we were treated. We wished we could do more off-piste skiing but understand we need to come earlier in the season to catch fresh powder. The resort's guest rooms need some refurbishing -- think 1970s European sports hotel, but the rooms are clean, and the common areas were just fine. The scene was international and fun. The hotel had a great band in the bar for 2 of the nights we were there. The other nights also had live music. Some of us did a one day snowshoe trek at the base of Mt. Aconcagua with a guide (booked in the hotel). I highly recommend this excursion. The scenery was breathtaking.

review_text: I did the "Tatio geysers" and "Lagunas Antiplanicas" tours with my girlfriend, and both of them are a must do at San Pedro de Atacama. When you arrive at San Pedro you will see that there are a lot of agencies for going on a tour, but do not get confused, and just choose Grado10. Even though it can be a little more expensive, if you take more than a tour, you will may get discounts, and apart from that, it is totally worth it. When we arrived at the agency, we had the pleasure to meet Inés, who was very nice to us and gave me a lot of information and tips about the tours. Then troughout the two tours Santiago, the guide, and Alfredo, the driver, formed an excellent team and made the tours to be an outstanding experience. They gave us a lot of information, and were all the time trying to make the most out of the tour. Both of them prepared breakfast for us, they were concerned about every detail of it ( it was cooked there in the middle of the desert in a grill they have) and it was delicious. It included panqueques, toasted sandwiches, coffee, etc. It is important to mention that the truck is very comfortable,and since the tour starts around 5 am, it is great for sleeping until the trip to the first stop. Oh and they give you blankets for staying warm!

review_text: We (2 adults and 2 teen aged children) just returned, (yesterday) from a two week trip to Chile, all arrangements made by Cascada. I couldn't wait even one day to rave about the brilliant job they (Cecelia) did with our itinerary. We flew to Punta Arenas where we were met at the airport and transported to town. The town is small but we found several nice restaurants and it functions mostly as a gateway to the Patagonia region. We were picked up and transported by small bus to the Ecocamp office in Puerto Natales, where we were given lunch in a nearby restaurant (good meatless options) before continuing to the camp in Torres del Paine. Torres del Paine is absolutely beautiful; the Ecocamp is clean and the guides are great. There were always meatless options, and the food was very good. We had three great, full day, treks on the amazing "W" circuit. Following our stay at Ecocamp, Cecelia booked us on a 3 day sea kayak trip through the southern part of the park. (specifically along the Serrano river). We camped and utilized one Hosteria in the most remote and beautiful locations. This is camping in the wilderness; oh so beautiful. We did not have a lot of sea kayak experience but our guide was fantastic and very patient. (this is a strenuous and very rewarding trip). This part of our trip concluded with 2 nights in Puetro Natales at the IF hotel. Puerto Natales is a very small (also gateway) town. There are good restaurants and out hotel was clean and comfortable. When our flight time was changed (on Christmas eve); the hotel called Cascada to arrange for a change in our airport pick up. We flew out of PN on Sky airlines. I think there are only a few flights a day, but this is a good option which I would recommend. Every transport was on time, all hotels were great; Cascada did an amazing job with our entire itinerary. We continued on to Pucon in the lake region; where, again, all accommodations were exactly as we had hoped. (including car rental pick up on New Year's Day) The entire trip went with out a hitch (amazing). I can't thank Cecelia and Cascada enough for making this trip possible. I would strongly recommend using them for travel anywhere in Chile. Hola, Thanks for your comments. We are delighted to know you had a once-in-a-lifetime experience with Cascada and that you enjoyed the quality of the services provided at EcoCamp. We are proud to work with such a sustainable and guest-friendly destination. Every guest feels at home "far away from home" at EcoCamp and our staff is dedicated to making our guests feel as comfortable as possible in the wilderness of Patagonia. We hope to welcome you again in Chile! Best, Timothy

Bathrooms were what you would expect from a campsite and had two dishwashers outside to wash earthenware. review_text: It was the first tour that I've had at Atacama. You must wake up really early (I think it was almost 4am) and it takes one hour to get to Tatio. And its close to the first hours of the morning that you have the best sight from the geysers. It's amazing the landscape....the sky all blue with no clouds you surronded by the mountains, some of them, with snow in the top and, of course, the geysers. There are a lot of them. Some "angrier" than others but they are all around the place. Must take care where you put your feet. Be prepared for the temperature....in my case, It was -9º celsius....freaking cold!!! And dont lose the opportunity to swin by the lake with hot water....forget the cold outside and dive into the lake. You wont regret....

review_text: We did two tours with this company - the first we had booked months in advance via Tempo Tours from home and the second we booked upon arrival into Chile before we had done the first. Our first tour was the city tour of Santiago. We got picked up at 8am, driven to a central depot where we didn't leave until 9:20am! Our bus driver joked about how we were running late again, as they did every single day. I double checked with a staff member in the pick up car on the way to the depot what time the tour should finish that afternoon as it was advertised as 3 hours. I was told that we should we back at our hotel by 12 - 12.30. Due to leaving so late, our tour still had 2 stops to go at 12.15 so we had to ask to be dropped back to our hotel because we had another tour booked for pick up at 2pm and we wanted to have lunch in between. They kindly obliged and dropped us back on the way to the next stop at about 1230 which was good of them but meant that we missed 2 stops due to the poor time management of the company. The tour of the city was a mixture of bus and walking. We saw some of the main sites including the main square, the president residence, the cathedral & got to see the changing of the guards. My husband and I were the only English speaking. The other 10 or so guests were Spanish speaking so our tour guide gave them the majority of attention. He also didn't speak great English so it was difficult for him to understand our questions. There was one time where I had to repeat my question to him multiple times. He then got another member of the group who spoke English as a second language to help translate and then provided a really unhelpful, minimal answer and moved on. At one stage, my husband asked a question about Pinochet to which he said 'I don't have time to explain, sorry'. He easily could have taken a couple of mins during our bus ride home later in the day. The next day, on a different tour with a different company, our guide provided a great short explanation of the history of Pinochet without even being prompted which answered his very question. Later on, we did the second tour with them. It was a winery tour so it was fine because the guide and entire tour experience was facilitated by the winery and not TurisTours. They simply picked us up from our hotel, took us to the depot again (no idea why they don't just pick people up from their hotels using the minibus in the first place?? I think they just want you to buy stuff at the 'depot' which doubles as a large, very expensive souvenir shop) where we only had about a 10-15 minute wait this time and were then driven to the winery where the tour was conducted and then we were brought back. Overall, I definitely would not rate this company - book through someone else!
title: Would not recommend
