review_text: There are several historical places of interest, charming passages and heritage buildings that you can visit. We found very good infrastructure for work meetings, events and quality cultural spaces. Really recommended for work days; very good prices.
title: Work spaces in a historical and cultural sector.

review_text: Our trip to Santa Rita winery was very enjoyable. We spend a few hours in this lovely Maipo Wine Valley vineyard and winery. The exploration and tour, the forest walk, visit at the small historic church - all activities were very interesting. The active portion of the visit was followed by a great lunch in Santa Rita winery and browsing at their gift shop. The wines they produce are quite tasty and during the tour there is time to both taste them and learn about them. The staff of Santa Rita is very competent and knowledgeable. The dinner was delicious. There is a hotel on premises, and it undoubtingly would be interesting to stay there for a few days. Thank you very much for your congratulations! It is very gratifying to know that you enjoyed your experience at Viña Santa Rita and we would love to welcome you again.
title: Santa Rita winery tour and dinner.

review_text: The color of the water is so beautiful! And you can see the Osorno Volcano from there. What a fascinating landscape! There are hiking paths. You can take great pics.
title: Fascinating landscape!

review_text: Our guide was fernanda coin and the views were very nice and very entertaining everything, super good guide explained very well Review of: Official Tour of the Metropolitan Cathedral of Santiago Muchas gracias por sus comentarios.
title: Maravillosa

review_text: Beautiful! Fun games for the family, incredible views from chairlifts. Fast food places in the park are a good option Review of: By do Sol nos Andes Chilenos
title: Highly recommended!

review_text: We booked this tour via the Vacations to Go web site. Our tour was to depart on March 10, 2019 at 9 AM; we got in the tender line on the Holland America at 7:45 AM (tender tickets were given starting at 8 AM)but did not get off the ship and onto the pier until 9:45 AM. That was our mistake, not understanding how long it would take to get off the ship. We immediately found a guide we checked us in and told us to race after him. We ran and then were stopped by another woman who encouraged to go on the shuttle instead of the bus. We asked quick questions and found that she was with the same tour company and wanted $30/person more for the shuttle, so we quickly declined and raced toward the bus that took off without us. Consequently we raced back to the shuttle and were allowed on without an extra charge. We enjoyed the sites, but the guide provided very little narration. We asked her to increase her narration but she did not do so. We enjoyed seeing the waterfalls. The shops at the Petrohue waterfalls were most reasonable in price and quality but we had no time to shop as we spent our time at the falls. We also made a stop at an overlook to have our "snack" - some wine and empanades. When the snack was taken out, we were surrounded by bees and one stung my husband on the left side of his tongue leaving him with a swollen tongue and unable to speak and eat! We reported this to the guide and was offered water. Another site is recommended for a meat snack stop! Frutillar is not impressive but more history of the town would have been useful. All-in-all, this can be a very nice tour, but a better guide and consideration for guests is very important. We also will be mindful of how long it takes to get off a ship which uses tenders. Review of: Frutillar, Puerto Varas, and Petrohué Waterfalls Excursion from Puerto Montt Hi Ann! Thank for your feedback. We always love to read what our customers have to say about tours so that we may improve. I am actually dissapointed and sad that you didn’t appreciate or acknowledge that we waited for you since, as you stated, you arrived at 9:45 am. The meeting instructions said 9:00 am as you stated and you were the last person, but since you prepaid we didn’t want to waste your day and we were considerate enough to accomodate you on our semi-private tour. Your guide’s name is Paloma who has worked with us the entire season who which by the way if you look just three reviews below you and one above you, has amazing comments. So this is a first, but I will make sure to let her know of your feedback. I understand you are upset over the bee stinging situation (which only happened to your husband) and I am sorry for it. Thankfully your husband did not say that he needed medical attention, so more than an apology that you received from my guide I am not sure what else we could have done in this very unique situation to make things better. As mentioned by yourself, you were so late the bus left you (you booked the bus tour) and we accommodated you in a semi-private tour which is $30 dollars more per person which you refused to pay, so we just let you go at no extra cost. I understand you didn’t appreciate that or the free wine and empanada or more importantly that we didn’t leave you. I apologize again for the bee, but it’s something that hasn’t happened ever before so it hasn’t been a problem. I will make sure my guides warn anyone if they see an insect that you cannot see for yourself so that you are aware of them. Chile is the only country in Latin America that doesn’t have any insects that carry diseases, so you are quite safe in our country. We thank you again for keeping us in mind and hope you enjoy the rest of your trip. Kind regards, Victoria Stein
title: Tour Issues

review_text: There are four main ways to get to the statue of the virgin Mary at the top - furnicular railway from the west; cable car from the east; driving from the main entrance; or walking. We walked from the south but not from the main entrance. We eventually found the way to the top with the help of Google maps. The paths we used were shorter than walking up the roads and took just under an hour. Be careful as some 'paths' are actually mountain bike tracks. Also, if you rake the wrong path you can end up on completely the wrong ridge. From the top there are views of the city and the snow capped Andes behind. From here you can also really see the smog; apparently it is better after it has been raining but I don't know about that. We went twice as our hotel was very close and it was better early in the morning before the sun was too hot. There is a small shop at the top but I would recommend taking some water. There are toilets but we didn't use them. There is also a small church with amazing stone carvings on the interior walls. Definitely worth the climb (or pesos for the train/gondola).
title: Great views of the city from the top

review_text: Right and personalized recommendations that allow you to make the most of each day, making the experience unforgettable. Review of: Private Pumas and Wildlife Watching Experience
title: Excellent

review_text: It is an unmissable attraction for adults and children, learning firsthand part of the history of Chile, often only read or listened to. Many objects and letters from the period, all very well cared for. We thank the Navy personnel for their dedication and care of this ship with relevant participation in the Pacific War. One point to consider is to buy and reserve the visit on the Huascar page, otherwise, arrive before 11:00 to wait in line and buy them at the ticket office. Parking is public, it is located in the central parking lot, before entering the base. Adults: $3,000. Children and seniors: $500. If I was useful, 👍🏼
title: A little history

review_text: I crossed Lago Todos Los Santos on the 1 day trip by 4 buses and 3 boats/catamaran from Puerto Varas to Bariloche, Argentina. (It's a long and very costly trip, but a day of sights to remember for life). The day was glorious - sunshine and blue, blue sky which highlighted the turquoise waters of the lake. And the waters reflected the perfect cone of Orsono Volcano and other snow capped volcanoes and mountains. If travelers don't have time for the full crossing to Argentina there is a return boat tour from Puerto Varas to Puella. This crosses the lake, gives you time for excursions around Puella then returns to PV. It's a less expensive way to cross the lake - which is the most beautiful place of the full crossing. But it's worth waiting for a sunny day to see the best of the lake and surrounds.
title: Sublime

review_text: If you like shopping, thats the place. A lot of shops and plenty of restaurants in a beautiful patio. A little too comercial, but still worth a visit.
title: Very tourist-friendky

review_text: This was a 5 star experience all the way. We cannot praise Thomas Poussard, our tour guide Vincent and his company Chile Private Tours enough. Our cruise ship Celebrity Infinity arrived in Valpariso in the early morning hours of December 24. Our plane back to Atlanta wasn't until 10 that night. We had all of our luggage and 14 hours of time to spend in the area. So A friend had recommended Chile Private Tours to me and I contacted them. I was worried that everything would be closed because it was Saturday and the day before Christmas. Thomas was right on it and planned a day for us that we will always remember. His guide Vincent (and definitely ask for him) was fabulous. He speaks beautiful English, Spanish and French. Vincent met us at the Departure Terminal in Valpariso with a van and a driver. There were six of us and the van held us and all of our luggage with room to spare. We spent the morning in the Valpariso area and saw some of the most amazing sights. Everything was explained beautifully. Then we stopped for an amazing lunch on the way to Santiago. The afternoon we toured Santiago which was crowded with shoppers in the downtown area, and we walked through the area, visited the Presidential Palace and a number of other sights. Then late in the day when we were all exhausted, Vincent and the driver dropped all of us and our luggage at the Santiago Airport for our trip back to the U.S. What a wonderful day and tremendous climax to our 15 day trip to South America.
title: The Highlight of our trip to Santiago area

review_text: Bario Italia is a surprise. Every corner reveals something new, unique or fun. Nice cafes and a variety of restaurants. One of my favorite places. If you like antiques, this is a must.
title: Ecclectic and fun neighborhood

review_text: The city is amazing and the sights are breathtaking. The guide was very attentive and available. I will definitely return to Santiago.
title: Cultural enrichment.

review_text: It was a good change to get out of the city and explore the country. The driving wasn't long and the tour guide kept us entertained along the way with his extensive knowledge of the region. Valparaiso is beautiful and an artist's dream, very bohemian and groovy. There is just lots to see through all the streets. The winery tour was also good and you get to choose to keep the actual glass you are taste testing with. Review of: Full Day Guided Trip to Valparaíso Viña del Mar & Reñaca from Santiago

review_text: Loved our guide Nata! Very enthousiastic and passionate about her lovely city. I did the afternoon tour (3-6pm). Without this tour I probably wouldn’t have seen as much of the city. Lots of interesting info about the city’s history and Chilean history in general. This tour got me exited to do the morning tour through the markets as well, to visit more neighbourhoods and centros cultural. Yep, would recomment! Hi nichting, Thanks so much for leaving such an awesome review! Nata is such a fantastic guide. I don't think I've ever met anyone who was more full of energy than her, and it's clear why she's an actress. I'm so glad to hear that this tour got you so excited and interested in Santiago and Chile's culture, history, and politics! I guess that means we're doing our jobs well, and that's just awesome! All the best, Peter

review_text: I had the chance of going to Cajón del Maipo during the summer and the winter and both landscape scenarios were amazing (with and without snow). It's definitely your best choice if you have a short time in Santiago and want to see some amazing Nature gift.
title: Incredible place

review_text: Based on this experience I can recommend Turistik tours. Picked up at 8:15am from hotel, in mini-bus taken to back of shopping mall at Las Condes where the Turistik buses merge and you join the correct on for your chosen tour - organised and works like clockwork. Luckily the bus I was on was the one for this tour so stayed seated. Left around 9:15 and due to time of year, the wine tasting was first on the stop-off at around 11:30. Matetic vineyard is beautifully surrounded by hills and vines (obviously) and is an organic producer - quality over quantity. There were 9 people on this tour and a perfect size for being shown around by our guide. Tasting at the end of a white and a red, very small gift shop here. Then just a short ride to Matetics own boutique hotel/restaurant for lunch (price not included in tour) but you will want to eat here - looks like it is going to be out of price range but I found it reasonable and probably the best meal I had in Chile this year !! Probably around £25 for the 2 courses with a glass of their wine The surrounding is beautifully presented and there is a boutique hotel they own too. After lunch just a short trip to the coast and Isla Negra to Pablo Neurda's house (see separate review) Then back to Santiago mall, before coaches take you back to your hotel Excellent throughout our bus driver Rodrigo and guide Cristima, would definitely try a different tour with these guys next time. Review of: San Alfonso del Mar, Veramonte Vineyard, Isla Negra and Algarrobo BoeingAde, we are very happy to read that you enjoyed the turistik experience with our partners Cristina and Rodrigo. Thank you for sharing with the rest of the travelers the quality of our service and your memorable memories. We will be waiting for your return to Santiago to continue enjoying incredible experiences. Greetings to Birmingham, United Kingdom!

Opens 10am and you can spend a good couple of hours here.

review_text: Lago Chungara is easily reached via the main road by normal car. The best way to explore is to park at the Ranger station about midway along the lake and follow the flat interpretative trail that starts there. Lots of animals along the shore. Even though the lake is right next to the road, it is far of the main tourist hub of Atacama and thus very quiet.

review_text: Cerro Concepcion is one of the neighborhoods in Valparaiso. It is also the best place in Valparaiso to stay, eat, drink and hang out. The streets and buildings are colorfully painted by street artists. The restaurants are awesome with many rooftop choices. Nightlife is classy and safe. It is worth a 2 or 3 day stay.

review_text: It's a short road from Santiago (1 hour 45 min trip). I went by myself, so my recommendation is to take care of buying the bus tickets in advance. I got to the bus station - metro Universdidad de Santiago - at 11:00am and they had tickets only from 1 pm on (it was a Saturday). So I had a shorter than planned stay in Valparaiso, but it was worthwhile. The city has a late 19th-century urban and architectural development in Latin America. Not to mention that is is classified by UBESCO as World Heritage. In its natural amphitheatre-like setting, I just made a tour by the historic center, taking two "funiculars": Artilleria was the first, where you have a beutiful view from the city, and the Concepcion, where you just can go for a walk in the charming and historical quarter of Concepcion, with lots of good restaurants to eat.

review_text: Wonderful experience!! From Gulia's mega efficient coordination and the friendliness of Jony and the super driver!! We arrived first at the lagoons and enjoyed some BEAUTIFUL views! And the breakfast….WOW!!!! 200% recommended😍😎 Review of: Tour to the Hidden Lagoons of Baltinache

review_text: Laguna San Rafael is like nothing I have ever seen before. The huge granite mountains, the bright blue rivers, and the abundant hanging glaciers at every turn. If passing through or staying in Rio Tranquilo, you cannot miss this park. This is Patagonia. This is what people dream about seeing. Take my word for it, and find a way to pay a visit.
title: My favorite NP in all of Chile

review_text: Bella vista has gone from artists' quarter to run down, crack peddlers, bad restaurants to what it is now, a very nice area between downtown and the Cerro San Cristobal. Patio Bellavista has gone from very good to better and better. Great selection of restaurants, pretty crafts stores. On the way to the cable car that takes out to the top of te hill (recommended) make a small detour, if you haven't seen any of the other Neruda houses, and visit La Chascona. All in all, it's all very touristy, but that's what you are doing, tourism, no?

review_text: Excellent, super coordinated and responsible. A 7 for Tour SCL. Mr. Pablo was the person who took us to the Vineyard and returned again, leaving us at our home. Very good service and punctuality. On your next trip, hire SCL Tours and see for yourself their excellent service.

review_text: We took a walk with Pukarumi. It was all wonderful. The guide Maurizio and the driver Andres were sensational. review_text: Although we have some suggestions for improvement of this tour, this still was the highlight of our trip. What better way to earn our wine than by biking through a huge, beautiful vineyard at the base of the Andes? Our tour guide, Philippe, was outstanding and very considerate with us English speakers. He went above and beyond to ensure we were comfortable, informed, and having a good time. He gave us a history of the region on the way to the vineyard (around 40 minutes) and in no time, we had our bikes and were off to tour. The vineyard was flat ground, and although the bikes had gears, they were not needed. We rode around for about an hour or so (no wine at this point!) and then got a mini-tour of the winery. Very interesting. Would've been more interesting if we were sampling the wine that we were talking about :) We then biked over to a pretty spot and heard more about the history of the grapes and the region and Philippe opened a bottle for all of us to taste. Very idyllic! Then we rode back to the winery for the official tasting. Although informative and intimate (photo attached), we felt pretty rushed during our extremely short wine tasting. We sampled three provided wines that we did not choose and then we had about 15 minutes in the store to purchase the wines. We received assistance and they bubble-wrapped our wines for us since we we planned to put them in our suitcase. My husband and I liked the fact that this was not an all-day tour, but the fact that pick-up was at 8:15 am and no food was provided was brutal for us night-life lovers. We knew they weren't going to provide food, but since we spent the morning biking and then drinking by about 11:30, a light snack or time to stop at the cafe would've been perfect. Overall, quick and fun way to learn about Chilean wine and see the vineyards, but lacking on the actual wine tasting. We thank you for all your comments. We will consider each of them to improve our service. We want to make our experience memorable. We hope back to his country has many fond memories of our walk. We hope to see you again soon. Turistik Team

review_text: We did the W Trek from west to east. A park ranger came onto the bus when we entered the park and told us that the catamaran wasn't running that day but that it was going to be replaced by small boats - so far so good. It was only when we'd already got to Pudeto (and the bus we took in had already left) that we found out (from other hikers, not the rangers or anyone who worked at the park) that the small boat could only take 20 people an hour... and we had about 80 people in front of us in the queue. If we'd just known before we got off the bus we could've stayed on to hike from Administracion or got the other boat from Hotel Grey with time to spare, but instead we had to piece together the situation from other hikers, pay the driver of the one remaining bus an extra 5.000 CLP to drive us to Administracion and try to make the 5 hour hike in 4 hours in order to get to Paine Grande before the trail to Refugio Grey closed. If anything we got lucky - apparently when the small boat ran out of passengers in Paine Grande to ferry on the return trip they just stopped running it and told everyone still on the wharf to walk to Administracion and then to Paine Grande (eta 10 hours... starting at 3pm). The leftovers who didn't take the bus back to Puerto Natales had to hitchhike to Administracion, start hiking and get to Paine Grande at 9pm. Cheekily, the ticket office was even handing out catamaran timetables with the park tickets despite knowing it wasn't running. I guess whoever owns the catamaran was still pretty keen on collecting their 22.000 CLP fare even if it meant stranding a few dozen trekkers. Just getting in costs 20.000 CLP and it's not entirely clear where the money is going... trails except the main Hotel Torres -> Torres Del Paine route are poorly marked, bridges are falling apart or poorly signposted (many have signs with the maximum number of people on them... but only on one side of the bridge!?), the map will tell you to be sure to register yourself on each sector of the trek but we only ever saw a single registration book the whole time. Then there's the refugios - some are better than others, but they're all insanely overpriced. It's easy to think "it's worth it to be in this amazing place", but there is a point at which it's not worth it anymore, and 240USD per night to sleep in a tent and eat boiled eggs for breakfast is way beyond that point. The genius of the refugios is that they're so insanely difficult to book that by the time you get given the price, you're so grateful to have gotten any response that you'll pay anything. It's a beautiful place - but the ridiculous prices you'll pay for every single thing, the obvious lack of reinvestment of that money back into the park, and the general lack of any care given by anyone who works there leaves a pretty sour taste in the mouth. There are other beautiful places in the world where you aren't left feeling like the mark in a con job - go there first.

review_text: The ride is long, but we enjoyed every minute (even in the cloudy weather!). Guide Rodrigo and driver César made the experience unique, presenting the political, social and cultural history of Chile throughout the day, and presenting interesting tourist attractions in both cities. In the morning, the transfer was punctual at our meeting point. The place where we stopped for breakfast was a little expensive and crowded, but we took the opportunity to meet the llamas, feed them and pet them. Lunch was at a restaurant north of Viña, with a spectacular, tasty menu that was worth the price! The whole experience was very worthwhile and we believe that Rodrigo was the main reason for this, because of his concern in keeping the group together during the walks and contextualizing the local history.

review_text: World class fly fishing on a variety of rivers and lakes. Natural beauty beyond anything that I have ever seen. Glacers, blue green water, mountains, valleys, lakes, and rivers so beautiful it takes your breath away and makes you cry. It’s a place where my cup runneth over and it restored my soul. Five star meals prepared by Chef Carolina, the finest chef in Chile, and served with fine Chilean wines. First Class Lodging on the bank of the Rio Futilafu with beautiful snowcap mountains and meadows all around. Our guide, Nick Lawton, provided ten days of fly fishing on rivers and lakes that were varied in their challenges, beauty, and techniques. Walking and Wading, drift boats, and trolling for big trout on two spectacular lakes. Gourmet stream side lunches with table and chairs, homemade hot chili, grilled sausages, potato salad, and grilled skewers of beef/vegetables. Nick navigated the boat back and forth across streams, lakes, and through fast water with the greatest of ease. He shared many techniques on flies, knots, strategy, casting, and where the fish feed. He shared many stories of his incredible life as fly fishing guide around the world. Nick, Carolina, and his staff worked so hard from first light till late night insuring that every detail was covered from equipment, gear, clothing, glasses, food, and so much more. It was truly a privilege to get to know this crew and to have experienced the most wonderful vacation of my life. I will keep a place in my heart for all of them and all of the Chilean people that I met on this trip. They are all so beautiful and such great ambassadors of Chile. And to Nick’s partner, Avear, I say Ol Boy! Stephen, Thank you so much for taking the time to write this review. We appreciate your feedback and thoroughly enjoyed sharing the real Patagonia fly fishing experience with you. We are very pleased to know that you enjoyed your trip with us. Chef Carolina and the whole crew really enjoyed your company and we look forward to the opportunity to share this experience with you next season. Saludos
title: World Class Fly Fishing Adventure at Its Finest

review_text: Its a bit of a delayed review, but I have just finished my travels, but definitely needed to send my review of such a wonderful adventure. I am not an experienced rider, but have ridden a number of times before while growing up and as an adult. I disclosed this and it was looked after with my ability in mind. The Antilco ranch was beautiful and an amazing couple of days there. The horses were so sweet, and I loved riding Romero for the first 5 days. Our guide Kati was fantastic and our Gauchos, Aldo and Luis, looked after us well on the path, and Alejandro was an absolute star as our back up team, cooking, pitching tents, cleaning and keeping us in wine. The terrain was difficult at times, but those horses are absolute heros and climbed their way to the top. Changing teams for Argentina was hard. New horses and new guides. But a completely different experience. Who knew terrain could change literally the second you cross a man made imaginary border. Hernan and the team were great too and my new horse, Truco, was very different but just as loyal and protective. I did get a bit of stick from one of the other riders for not being more experienced, but as i fully disclosed my abilities, I felt her comments were unjust and impatient, as the staff were fantastic and ensure everyone gets any assistance they need. The run up tot the trip there were a couple of hiccups as I kept being left off email updates and wasn't sent the itinerary and pick up details etc. But Mathais and I were both able to see the funny side, and Alejandro picked me up on time. All in all, a trip of a lifetime, hugely recommended.

review_text: When I visited San Pedro I thought we had to take a tour to the Geyser del Tatio, but I am so glad we did not do it. We started driving from San Pedro around 8 am. It was a stunning drive and I was so glad we did not do this before sun rise, as all the tours do, because the drive on its own is worth it. When we arrived around 10 am at the Geysers all the tours were about to leave, so we had this stunning place almost to ourselves. Yes, maybe sunrise at this place would have been stunning, but it is stunning anyway, seeing the geyser with the clear blue skies and the Andes mountains in the distance. So colorful. I have one regret and that is that I did not take my bathing suite, as there is a small hot pool. The road is reasonable. couple of huge pot holes, but overall good to drive. I would not do it in the darkness. So if you want to see the sunrise you need to take a tour. But as I said I loved the drive, we saw lots of animals, even a fox. Dont expect any luxury. No coffee or anything. So take lunch. But GO

review_text: Recently I had a chance to visit my son in Chile who was spending 6 months studying as an exchange student at the Chilean Naval Academy. Having limited time to spend in Chile, I booked at the last minute a tour with Al Ramirez Wine Tours . Big mistake. Our tour guide was not familiar with wines and actually said he preferred beer to wine. Half way through the tour, I also realized the tour guide was taking us on the wrong tour. When I brought this to his attention, He ended the tour and said I was to pay extra if I wanted the tour to continue. At the end, Our tour guide was also very unfamiliar on how to accept our payment of cash. If you take this tour, be prepared to pay extra cost not being told about and having a guide who knows nothing about wine. At Valparaiso Wine Tours, we work with bookings which are carried out 48 hours ahead of time. This person was doing things last minute and the wineries she wanted to visit were not taking the reservation, and unfortunately she didn't like the Indomita Winery. So, I offered her a refund for the OPTIONAL (meaning not included) winery, where she had to spend $20 USD per person for a tour. Thats's what this complaint is about. The whole thing about the guide not being a wine lover or things being unclear in the email... if anyone writes me an email, everything is crystal clear in the first response. If the guide says he is a lover of beer more than wine is because he makes beer and not wine! but that doesn't mean he can't be a wine lover; that shouldn't even be in this complaint. Also, we include two wineries, and the third is optional. If you don't want a thrid winery, we can return to your hotel. If you want to have lunch, we can take you to lunch... everyone, since 2009, when that route was created, has understood this, but this person obviously didn't take the time to read the tour description. We had over 150 clients that week and not one group was dissatisfied, except for this one, and obviously if you book last minute, the premium wineries will not be expecting you with a red carpet. And finally, there were three people in that group, and two out of three did not have a compalint; in fact they thanked the guide for a great day.

review_text: NOTE: Our visit was actually Feb 2017 (summer in South America) If your time is limited, you can see a good bit of the park in one day, but to really experience it, you should stay either in the park or close by. We took a bus tour from El Calafate leaving at 7 am and returning at 9 pm. The bus was comfortable and we stopped at a local souvenir store on the return trip for expensive snacks (if you wanted them). A sack lunch was included in the tour. Arriving from Argentina, we had to stop at the border and pay for our Chilean visas. (It is better to use American or Chilean money; the exchange rate for Argentinian pesos is terrible.) The iconic Blue Towers (Torres del Paine) are tucked in a massif in the middle of the park. Our route took us around a good bit of the massif, but we were always viewing the towers from a great distance as the road is in the surrounding plains and foothills. Our first stops were two lakes and a beautiful waterfall overlook where we ate our sack lunches and stretched our legs. Farther down the road we encountered a guanaco herd and got out to take photos. We enjoyed a 2-hour leisurely stroll to a view of the Horns across a lake and then to another waterfall. (It was not a strenuous walk, but is a dirt path.) It was a full day and I was left wishing we could have stayed overnight at least. I imagine the towers can be quite dramatic in changing light. (Clouds rested on them most of the day.) One couple on our bus took their luggage and was staying in a cabin. There was also a camping area with many backpackers. Our tour was organized by Say Hueque and the guides on the bus and in the park were excellent.
title: An Full Day of Variety

title: Peaceful Half Day of Kayaking

review_text: Beautiful place with snow is simply wonderful. It's pretty tired to get there, but the view is breathtaking. It was one of the places I most wanted to see and I really liked it.
title: Laguna del inca

review_text: We spent an afternoon in the Parque while staying Puerto Varas for a few days. It's a really beautiful place and seemed to free. The ranger station was closed on the day we visited which was a bit of a bummer as we were looking for a hiking recommendation. We ended up doing the Desolacion track which we didn't love. Probably only made it halfway to the turnaround point. Nice views of Mount Osorno but other than that it was a bit boring and monotonous. The ground under foot was squishy, sandy ash -- perhaps from the recent eruption nearby -- but it made for tough walking. Enjoyed walking around the lake near the parking lot a bit more. And the waterfalls up the road are cool. Worth pulling off for a quick look. It looks like you can also book boat trips but we didn't do that.
title: Beautiful park

review_text: Julio gave us a private half day city tour of Santiago. He stood out from other guides that he is very comprehensive and detailed about the introduction of the city. We went to Valparaiso the next day with another tour guide who just provide the essentials to check off the boxes and try to keep the schedule. Julio just take his time and our 4-hour tour ended over 5 hours. His introduction of Santiago gave us a better understanding of Chile as a whole.
title: Highly recommended.

review_text: The museum located in Santa Cruz offers a lot to know, learn and delight in everything it has. Very tidy, clean and excellent service. Good introductory video. I advise making the visit in advance or taking advantage of doing it in 2 stages.
title: Excellent

review_text: Visited his house in Valparaiso & enjoyed it so much, decided to visit this one also, & will be visiting the one in isla negra in a few days. This one is very easy to get to, we walked to his house. This one doesn't have a spectacular view or gardens where you can sit & enjoy the gardens but nevertheless we enjoyed visiting the house, furniture & collectibles.
title: Enjoyed visiting & learning more about Pablo Neruda!

review_text: The drive through the park was very picturesque, with different scenery round every bend. Snow capped mountains, Alpacas, Condors, Orchids and the Grey Glacier with fluorescent Blue Ice Bergs.
title: Stunning Scenery

review_text: Excellent service, it was a gift from my coworkers and totally exceeded my expectations. Upon arrival it is very welcoming, they offered me iced tea which is appreciated in this hot season and the service was a 10 (I chose a facial treatment). Everyone is very friendly from the reception to the guys who perform the services. I will return to continue my treatment. Totally recommended
title: Excellent service and very welcoming

review_text: we did the tour with Andres and had a fantastic time, the scenerie and lake is one thing, what made a big difference were the explanations and comments from Andres about Flora & Fauna very knowledgeable and authentic ! Review of: Andes Day Lagoon in Cajón del Maipo & Embalse el Yeso Private Tour
title: What a fantastic experience & guide

review_text: Our Chiloe Natural tour was a highlight of the various port/shore excursions we took during our recent South America/Antarctica cruise. Cyril is a knowledgeable, articulate guide whose funny stories and passion for Chiloe made this a memorable day and we particularly liked being part of a small group of four rather than a tour bus of forty. With the limited time allowed by the cruise stop, we enjoyed a variety of experiences - the unusual cemetary in Huillinco and the view over the lake, the Chiloe National Park visitor's centre and Tepual hike, Cyril's description of folklore, plants and birds. Cyril took extra time to drive us to see the magnificent 25k beach although this wasn't part of the official itinerary. It was on my wish list and I appreciated that he accommodated my request. In Chonchi, we enjoyed our lunch stop at Ventanas de Elisa, the market, the accordian museum and visiting the UNESCO church, with the explanation of the architectural restoration and how churches are the hub of community activities. Due to some techinical glitches, we found it somewhat challenging to book the tour, because we had difficulty arranging the PayPal deposit, however, we are very glad that we were able to make the booking. Highly recommended!
title: Amazing excursion

review_text: Excellent tour guides, the winery we visited was excellent. Had a great host there and were able to walk around to see the set up. Unfortunately part of the excusion we were unable to do. Did see Valapresia, interesting but no time to eat Review of: Transfer to San Antonio port prior cruise with tour in Valparaiso and Casablanca A great option to take before you embarc on the cruise ship. Regarding the lunch break. Unfortunately depending on what time is last call to embarc on your cruise ship the times will not do. Still we enfasise on the important part that is the tour itself. Thank you for your review.
title: Santiago to port

review_text: We took a tour to Portillo with Guide Matheus. And we just loved everything, we had stories lessons about the places we knew. Besides finally seeing the snow, which was our dream. We had a picnic with a chilean wine and various meals. =D Matheus took sensational photos, which will definitely stay on the family albums forever. Hahaha The alfatur helped us a lot and made our trip more peaceful, thank you very much.
title: Tour to Portillo

review_text: Not your average Cathedral but I guess it is still a place of worship. I think the Priest must have slept in because there were a lot of tours waiting to go in and everything was locked up tight. Even the overnight guests sleeping outside were still at rest.
title: Different to say the least

review_text: Mother and daughter trekked this on our own. Someone needs to put time and effort into making the reservations, but after that it is straightforward. Stunning landscapes, from meadow to glacier. Embraced the peace and quiet and wide, wide space.
title: O trek, Outstanding!

review_text: We highly recommend this tour to all Puerto Natales vistors. It is very informative - you learn a lot about the history of this region. The tour is run by three friends who are very happy to share some stories and legends. You can ask as many questions as you want and get insights from locals. Loved it!
title: Puerto Natales is more then just the entry point to Torres del Paine!

review_text: This was a really amazing tour that made us feel looked after and catered to. Kylie prepared a totally customized tour for us, with an amazing price-value, specific to the locations, times, and days we could go (limited in time). She did everything to make sure we were comfortable, having fun, and fulfilled all our wishes and requests. On our tour, we were picked up on time in a BMW (tour was only us two and one other woman) and whisked away to Santa Rita as a first stop. Although this is a major wine producer in Chile, the tour was a good size and the grounds were absolutely gorgeous. We tried a few wines and Kylie, the tour guide, even bought each of us some snacks and another glass of wine to enjoy in the gardens before heading off to the next stop. We next went to a small but amazingly tasty restaurant and were treated to a three course lunch with a bottle of wine, water, and coffee. We couldnt get over how good the food was and generous the tour was. Our next stop was a smaller winery, William Fevre, where we got to see the production area, speak with the manager, walk around the grounds, and try some of their best wines. We would recommend this tour to anyone staying in Santiago or going to Chile! We thouroughly enjozed the day and tips for Santiagos wine bars afterwards! Thank you for taking the time to write an amazing review. I truly enjoyed having you along for the day, and hope you enjoyed the rest of your time in South America. Hope to see you down here again some day!
title: Wonderful wine tour, lovely company, and great food

review_text: An honest and well laid out museum enough to while away an hour or more looking at the multi lingual exhibits. Not expensive and quite easy to find
title: Well laid out museum

review_text: Tremendous experience, grateful to Guide Francisco. Very kind. Go with comfortable clothes and shoes...... Review of: Tour to Vallecito and Magic Bus

review_text: We had a great day seeing the sights in Santiago with Hector. His command of English is excellent and his knowledge about Chile and its capital city is extensive. He is kind and personable and we recommend him highly. Review of: Private Day Tour in Santiago
title: Excellent Santiago city tour!

review_text: I loved this stop during my trip to Atacama. It was absolutely beautiful during sunrise. I am from Wisconsin so very used to cold, but I felt chilled to my core. Double up on socks and make sure you have gloves and a hat!
title: Absolutely beautiful but very cold.

review_text: We had an excellent day with our guide, Diego and just one other couple. The organic winery in Casablanca valley was in a beautiful setting and provided a generous pour of two of their wines. The walking tour of Valparaiso was mostly downhill and the wall art and views were stunning. We had a leisurely lunch in a seafood restaurant recommended by our guide and it was delicious. We were well looked after and there was no rushing, can recommend this full day tour Review of: Street Art in Valparaiso and Wines in Casablanca from Santiago Thanks for your detailed review. We have the instruction of giving free time for lunch and point you some options as guidance but making clear that everyone can go and do whatever they want. And the "no rushing" part of your review is essential and we're very happy to deliver services with that touch, permitting you to enjoy the place properly.
title: Leisurely day in Valparaiso with a wine tasting on the way.

review_text: Very nice to visit in Castro, we went to the church and we toured it and everything is very well maintained, the wood and the images in very good condition. It is obligatory to pass if one walks through Castro.
title: Well maintained

review_text: Another incredible day in Chile! Because of our experience earlier in the week with this organization, we signed up for another day trip to explore Chile. We headed to the Andes mountains where my 15 yo son and I enjoyed a great horseback ride with killer vista. The weather was perfect and the views were breathtaking! We finished our week off at the Santa Rita winery which was perfect- not crowded and felt very private. Sean was our guide again today and he didn’t disappoint- his knowledge of Chile and its history should be commended. Woohoo for a great day! Review of: Maipo Canyon: Andes Mountains Horseback Ride and Wine Tour & Tasting Thanks again, Amy, for being such a wonderful guest. What an awesome way to end your stay in Chile! The views of the Andes were amazing and what better place to see them than on a horseback ride. We hope to see you here someday again for more adventures and, of course, wine! You have a friend in Chile!
title: Incredible views of the Andes from Horseback

review_text: The incredible guide and driver! Very attentive and friendly throughout the tour. The guide provided all the information and more about each place. As well as the very rich and filling food.
title: Excellent.

review_text: During services or events you have to enter from the side entrance, not from the Plaza. It is an amazing building in many ways, the size, the painted ceilings, the people in quiet contemplation and prayer, but also how quickly parts of the ceiling and painting have deteriorated. Read up on your history before you go and check out the list bishops/archbishops at the front.
title: Well worth a look

review_text: Had a wonderful day between Santiago and Valparaiso with many stops in between. We were visiting during the holidays so some things were closed but the tour guides did not miss a beat. Natalia, our guide and Carlos, our driver were on time, super friendly and ensured our safety the entire time. Working with Claudia before the trip to ensure an easy booking with all their recommendations was super helpful. We definitely would recommend working with Chile Vive Tours for future trips. Review of: Santiago to Valparaiso & Casablanca: Port Drop-off
title: Great way to see the highlights between Santiago and Valparaiso.

review_text: This was my first experience with real snow, and it was unforgettable. Much of it was thanks to our guide, Luciano, and driver, Mario. They were extremely kind and attentive. The road to the park includes 40 very steep curves, which might make some people feel sick. During our tour, a little girl felt uneasy and Luciano and Mario were perfect: they looked for a safe place to make a stop, attended to the little girl's family, and only when everything was OK, they summarized the road. Luciano gave clear instructions about the park attractions, and food facilities and was reachable throughout the entire time. Mario was a careful driver, both going up and down the mountain. They also left us closer to our hotel than the original endpoint and gave us clear instructions to return. The park is organized, ideal for kids of all ages, and perfect if you have no experience with snow sports, but want to learn. Restrooms were clean, and there was room for people who wanted to rest. There are food trucks all along the park and even my husband, who needs a gluten-free meal could find something to eat. There are attractions for everyone, excellent infrastructure, and a gorgeous place. The only thing I would change is the loud music in the main attraction area. It is unnecessary, and prevents you from listening to the sounds of nature (but that's my personal opinion). Will definitely be back! title: Amaizing!!!

review_text: The kind of place I wish I could go to back home. All restautants and bars look sharp, the waiters are all very nice and the food and drinks are delicious. It's a nice place even to walk around and maybe sit down for a beer. One of the things I'm going to miss about Santiago.
title: Awesome

review_text: Very interesting tour with a focus on chile's recent history. Lively and very friendly guides. Probably the best way to see a variety of the sites of Santiago.
title: 5 hour Mike Tour

review_text: My husband and I just did kayaking and glacier trekking with Big Foot, and had two incredible experiences. Both activities were well organized and we felt safe the entire time. I could not believe the amount of gear we were given for kayaking, but certainly kept us warm! We kayaked through ice bergs and had great views of Glacier Grey. I must say though if you could only choose one activity, the glacier trekking was one of the most incredible experiences we had ever had. The whole experience was about 5 hours - we took a 10 minute boat ride and then a short hike to the glacier, where put on our crampons before climbing up. We had 6 people in our group and were mostly inexperienced, and our guides were fantastic and helpful. They took us out pretty far too - we must have hiked about 3 miles, and did not see a single other soul out there. Perfect way to end our experience on the W trek, and can't recommend this company highly enough.
title: AMAZING!

review_text: Company fully focused on providing total comfort to its customers. Punctual, polite, caring, bringing all the safety that customers so need when they need the services. I highly recommend HBTurismo, one of our best choices in Chile.
title: Excellent company, note a thousand!

review_text: The visits were very entertaining, well guided, we saw a representation of the defense of the fort, very novel. Good meals without being the forte of the walk. Excellent guide handling.

review_text: This is a must for anyone visiting Santiago. It's a lot of fun exploring the nooks and crannies of this zany house of this renowned Chilean poet. I loved hearing about how Pablo used the spaces in the house and seeing his impressive collections too. It also gives a good background into some Chilean history.

review_text: I did this tour the day I landed and it was a great intro to the city! Our guide was Alejandra and she was very knowledgeable and spoke great English! We had 12 in our group and Alejandra was in front and there was a gal sweeping in the back as well. It was fun to ride through the bustling city, the parks, etc and learn along the way. I wish we stopped at more tourist spots, but that was probably my fault for booking the political tour vs a highlight tour (if there is one)! There was a bike malfunction, but one guide gave her bike up for the rider and we weren’t delayed too much. The Moneda building was my fave. It was a great tour and the ice cream stop at the end was a wonderful surprise! Review of: Santiago Highlights, Parks and Politics Bike Tour

review_text: Excellent experience. Very friendly service, from the booking to the day of the tour, all staff well prepared and careful to the details. Guides prepared to tell about historical, geographical, cultural aspects. And destiny is to take the breath. I highly recommend

review_text: We did the afternoon tour with Liz, and it really made me love Santiago! Having arrived the evening before, we hadn't had a chance to explore the city ourselves and this tour was perfect. There was a great variety - from art to history to stray dogs. I learnt so much, and Liz's approach (especially condensing Chile's recent political history) was really impressive. Really interesting and well done tour - would recommend to anyone looking to explore and understand Santiago! Hola Rachel. We are so glad you have fallen in love with Santiago as much as we have. Have a great day, Peter.

review_text: After visiting Lago Todos Los Santos (booked as a day excursion from our cruise ship) , we then visited this National Park. While riding our tour bus from Puerto Montt to these 2 attractions, I kept seeing the Volcan Osorno from my window at this bus. I said silently to myself, " wow, wow, wow!" as I snapped several pictures of this volcano. Parque Nacional V. P. Rosales is big National Park. From the signs at its entrance, it seemed that there are more attractions that one can see at this Park. See attached pictures. We focused our visit on the waterfalls or the "saltos". Our tour guide kept reminding us to stay on the left side of the trail and not to go astray.There are restrooms near the park entrance and a gift shop where one can buy some souvenirs and refreshments. How I wished we had more time to spend in the Park and explore its other areas!

review_text: The views were great, we are from Ecuador. The photos we took are the best memories of our trip to Santiago. Miss Guide Cristina Caro was the best, excellent way to guide us and help us with what we needed. review_text: The landscape here is fascinating and for a second you feel like you could be looking at the moon...until you see the next bus load of visitors with their guide. Sunset was pretty but there were people everywhere. There were many other places and landscapes that we enjoyed far more in this area. Alternatively it might be worth visiting at another time and perhaps returning for sunset. If thinking of biking it is quite a tough ride bearing in mind heat and limited shelter. Entrance was reasonable but try to have exact change.
title: Very busy

review_text: I had organised a group of people from a cruise stop in San Antonio on 7th March. Kylie had been great with communicating before hand and dealing with my requests promptly. It proved to be a great day out. Two wineries in good locations. The second included a barbecue and the wine flowed. My group gelled together. Kylie was on hand and proved to be personable and passionate about the wines and area. I should also mention the guides at both venues, knowledgeable and informative. The transport used was very good, great driver and everybody commented on the standard of the vehicle used. Not always the case on some of our trips. This is great option for folks interested in wine. Great job Kylie Thanks so much for your great review, and for organising the tour and bringing the group together. It was great to work with you in the lead up, and to have you all along on the day. The Chilean BBQ is a personal favourite of mine when we can get a group together and a perfect "land-legs" outing from the ship. I'm glad you all enjoyed it so much. Happy future travels and please let me know if you're ever back in this part of the world again!

review_text: Tour that starting from the chaos of the city took us along the adjacent Maipo valley crossing various small towns until reaching an altitude of 2,500 m. altitude and ends at the thermal springs. The springs could be better maintained, with stone embankments rather than in sandbags which give the impression of a construction site; on the other hand, the experience is still positive. Tip: start swimming from the basins further downstream. The toilet and changing rooms are decidedly poorly maintained, but perhaps this is the price you have to pay for this trip to a wild location far from so-called civilisation. The tour operated and the guide have undisputed professionalism and above all they are precise and punctual: good. Review of: Santiago: Cajón del Maipo, Hot Springs, Waterfall & Chilean BBQ

Would highly recommend this adventure to anyone interested (regardless of ability, as this was not too strenuous and very enjoyable). Review of: Andes Day Volcano 8K - Cajón del Maipo

review_text: This is a magic place!!! Its unreal!!! Has a unique beauty, mixing the salt desert to the desert and making this an unforgettable place. And to make this tour i recommend "Worl White Travel" that is located in Uyuni. The owners of this agency are so cool and our guide (Dione) was perfect. review_text: If you are interested in Chilean history or literature, a stop at one of Pablo Neruda's homes is a must. This is the one he built for his last wife. It's been put back to together beautifully since it was vandalized in the 1973 coup. The house can be both elegant and flamboyant at the same time, reflecting Neruda's unique tastes in furnishing and design. review_text: I cannot speak highly enough of Antilco. My boyfriend and I visited Chile in November, 2011 for 5 days. I am an avid horse back rider with over 20 years of experience riding and training in the US. I love riding in other countries, but I am a stickler for safety, good horsemanship, and EXCELLENT horse care. I will not hesitate to walk out of an establishment that is lax about safety or the well being of their mounts. Antilco was FANTASTIC. Way beyond my expectations. When we arrived, I was happy to see a string of very well cared for Chilean horses (healthy well trimmed hooves, clean shiny well groomed coats, appropriate weight, and excellent muscle tone on ALL their horses) hanging out calmly in a clean shaded paddock with access to hay and water. Further, none of the horses had that "dead- eyed" look of being overworked. They were all alert and interactive with their humans, seemed to enjoy their jobs, and moved out easily away from the barn with no hint of the "barn sour"-ness that unfortunately happens to so many overworked trail horses. The healthy horses were followed by a neatly arranged tack room with well conditioned bridles and saddles in good repair and (much to my joy as I didn't have any gear with me)... half chaps! Another good sign: nearly all the bridles have gentle snaffle bits or hackamores, indicating very well trained horses with happy mouths! :) It was pouring rain the day we rode, but they provided rain ponchos as well, in part to keep the riders happy and in part to help keep the 30- some layers of wool in their incredible saddles dry (more on the saddles to follow). Antilco also provides ASTM approved helmets to anyone who wants one. Our guide was extremely friendly and a very knowledgeable and accomplished horseman (I believe he was German?, but spoke impeccable English and Spanish). He spoke with everyone briefly and easily matched up the guests to appropriate horses. My boyfriend has ridden a grand total of 4 times in his life, so when we travel, it is imperative for me to find a trekking company that will provide him with a safe mount, not only so he doesn't get hurt, but also so I can keep him happy enough to continue riding with me on our vacations :P Our guide at Antilco did an excellent job assigning horses. After a brief warmup walk on the trail, our guide announced we were going to canter up the hill on the road. I panicked thinking "there is NO WAY my boyfriend can canter! He barely knows how to steer or stop!" But my fears were quickly allayed when his horse slowly and carefully picked up a gentle rolling lope and followed the others up the hill without so much as coming close to unbalancing my boyfriend and totally unaffected by my boyfriend bouncing awkwardly a bit on his back. I wish I could remember the name of his horse, because that fantastic animal deserves some kind of medal or at least a few extra carrots :) My horse was lively and moved forward easily, but was also very calm with excellent response to all my aids, something I really did not expect in a career trail horse, who, in the US at least, typically walk nose to tail and ignore anything the rider asks for. He was really a pleasure to ride. Another helpful thing for beginner riders (or anyone going on a long, multiday trek): the Chilean saddles are like COUCHES! I'm an eventing rider and used to shallow seated English saddles. These were the exact opposite. I'm pretty sure it would be impossible to fall off of one. It felt like I would literally have to dive off the side of my horse to come loose. They are WAY deeper seated and more secure even than any Western style American saddle I've ever sat in. Although this was a really strange feeling for me, the saddles are extremely comfortable and PERFECT for an inexperienced rider who needs a really secure saddle to handle some of the tougher terrain encountered on the trail. They were comfortable enough that my boyfriend, who is usually sore and tired after a couple hours, was able to ride for 4 hours with little complaint. We rode for about 2 hours on trails and back roads, through the woods, the mountains, and several traditional villages. The ride is not simply a "nose to tail" follow along on a flat road (nor was it too difficult for beginners). There was plenty of trotting and cantering and lots of varying terrain. There were also 2 challenging, rocky creek crossings that those amazing little Chilean horses handled beautifully. They are SO surefooted and fit! We stopped in a sheep field, tied the horses to some trees, and had a lovely lunch provided by Antilco (vegetarian options available!). Then we remounted and headed back by a different route that included a nice (optional!) gallop on a volcanic sand beach. And finally, the scenery is AMAZING. The small taste of Patagonia we got on this half day trail, and the excellent experience with Antilco, has made me think very seriously about returning for a week long trek. I really cannot say enough good things about their guides and their horses. Such a fantastic experience!
title: FANTASTIC

review_text: My husband and I hiked the W at the end of March 2014. We booked everything ourselves. I'll provide a report based on components of the trip, which is likely to be most helpful for those planning the hike for themselves. Transportation: We didn't book any of the ground transportation to or from the park in advance, and this worked fine. When I arrived in Punta Arenas, I went straight to Bus Fernandez and booked our bus tickets to Puerto Natales for the following morning. We were then able book the bus to the park when we arrived at Puerto Natales, and so on. Don't bother paying a company to book all the transfers for you - you'll only pay more than you need and it's so easy to arrange on the ground. Accommodation: We stayed in refugios every night (Refugio Torres 2 nights, a cabana at Cuernos, Paine Grande and Lodge Grey) and were glad we did. The wind is blustering in the park and it was wet a few days of the trip and we would have been miserable if we had to set up tents in this and try to sleep through the wind. We even saw some tents had blown away! We booked beds without sheets, so took our own sleeping bags and this saved a bit of cash. Food: We booked full board at every refugio. We are good eaters with solid appetites, but it was consistently too much food for both of us. I recommend buying your first dinner in Puerto Natales from the supermarket and taking it with you into the park - I saw a group who'd brought in a roast chicken with salad and bread rolls, and it looked better than what we were eating in the refugio (and probably cheaper). Dinner most nights was rice with meat and a very salty gravy/sauce. Vegetables were scarce. I didn't like the food much, it was too salty for me. Lunch was always a large white sandwich with meat, mayonnaise and maybe a slice of lettuce. Again, salad was very minimal. Snacks in the lunch pack included a small bag of mixed dried fruit/nuts (enough for two of us in a day), an apple or orange, sweet muesli bar and chocolate bar. We didn't get through our snacks on any day of the trip. Others on the hike took their own snacks into the park to have for lunch, and this worked fine for them. You don't actually need to prebook your meals, so I'd suggest only reserving breakfast and dinner for the second day onwards and taking your first dinner and snacks into the park. If you run short, you can always order a lunch at the next stop or buy more snacks from the kiosks at each refugio. What to take: waterproof jacket and pants (essential), hiking boots (obviously), 2 pairs woollen socks, enough underwear for the hike (you won't be able to handwash it as it won't dry in time overnight), something to sleep in, thermals (top and bottom), a fleece top, beanie and gloves. We took head torches and only used them once at Lodge Grey as the generator doesn't turn on until 7am so you don't have any light. Route: we did it east to west (starting with the Torres) as we were most looking forward to the glacier at the end and Lodge Grey proved to be very rewarding and the nicest refugio of the trip. It was a great way to finish and we enjoyed the catamaran ride at the end. Any questions, feel free to ask. We absolutely loved the trek and are so glad we did it!

review_text: Just finished trekking the W circuit from east to west. Flew into El Calafate from Buenos Aires and used Always Glaciers to transport me directly to TDP, bypassing the need to go to Puerto Natales. TDP is VERY busy and reservations at the Refugio's are HIGHLY recommended. There are two companies that operate the Refugio's in the park: Fantastico Sur and Vertice Patagonia. Fantastico Sur operates Refugio's on the east side of the park and vertice on the west. You can book directly via their websites. Calling or emailing is terrible. You'll be lucky to get a response. You can either stay in their "lodges", camp using their tents and equipment or bring your own tent. Given the unpredictability of the weather, I'd recommend staying in a Refugio. If you're insistent on camping I recommend using their tents and sleeping bags and food so you don't have to carry it. You can book all of this directly on their websites. The weather is hard to predict. Google will say it's sunny but it's actually raining. I wouldn't rely on a weather forecast unless it was 24-36 hours in advance. So with that, it's best to be prepared for multiple days of rain. On a sunny day Patagonia is beautiful. But on rainy days it can be a nightmare if you're camping. It's best to over prepare for rain. Your tent should have a rain fly that goes all the way to the ground and it should be able to hold up against strong wind gusts. You'll want some flex in your guy lines to avoid anything from ripping. Most of the Refugio's have wood platforms for tents. They'll give you a hammer and some nails for stakes. But bring a few stakes to tie your rain fly down. Pack a quick dry towel to wipe the rain off your tent when you have to pack it away in the rain. When it rains, it rains for a while and unless it clears up, the sun won't ever have the chance to dry anything. And because you can't have fires in the park everything stays wet. So be prepared for this. Be sure to have a heavy weight rain cover for your back pack. Parts of the trail have low hanging branches that will catch your rain cover and tear it. Plastic bags will shred on this stuff. Pack your clothes, sleeping bags, tent and other items you want dry in plastic bags. Once it gets wet it will be very hard to dry in Patagonia. The Refugio's have stoves but they're overcrowded and it's impossible to find a spot to hang things inside in the common area. Drying out a sleeping bag? Forget about it. Make sure you have good boots with good gore tex. Some parts of the trail have sharp rocks and will tear your soles to pieces if you're wearing tennis shoes. Additionally, on rainy days many parts of the trails turn into streams and mud pools. So be prepared for getting dirty. Bring a large poncho big enough to cover yourself and your back pack. This is the safest way to ensure things stay dry. If not, bring a poncho at the minimum in addition to your waterproof coat. You'll want a dry coat once you get to camp. And if it rains multiple days back to back, nothing will dry and you'll wish you had a dry coat. Bring good water proof pants that are also breathable and can quickly be pulled over your boots and pants. The cheap pants don't breathe and you'll just sweat in them. You'll want water proof pants because the trails can be narrow and brushing up against the grass and bushes on the side will unload all of the rain water onto your pants. Bring hiking sticks. They'll help you keep balance and help you move faster through streams and mud pools. You can drink the water from the steams. Just be smart about where you're getting it. Food in the Refugio's isn't bad (except for the packed lunches). They do have wifi for a cost. If you're staying in the Refugio's, expect staying in an overly used hostel. Wash your hands regularly. Nola virus is there. Overall, Patagonia is beautiful on a good day. On rainy and cloudy days it can be miserable. No views. Just rain and chill. So be prepared to give yourself an extra day or two in areas where you want to really see the views. Otherwise, you can do the W in four days. Catching the catamaran is easy. Schedules are posted at all Refugio's. You buy tickets on the boat. You can hitch a ride a pudeto on one of the many local bus companies to Laguna Armaga or to Puerto Natales without having a ticket. Just bring Chilean pesos. Patagonia is a lot like the Tetons in Wyoming and the rolling mountain hills you would find in the Rockies. Add some Glaciers and worse weather and you'll be in Patagonia.
title: Be over prepared for unexpected weather

review_text: We visited the geysers via a tour, as the road up is a bit difficult and we didn't have our own vehicle (although we passed one brave soul biking and a few more trying to hitchhike!). It was only 18,000 CLP per person, not terribly expensive (about 30 USD). However, since the geysers are at about 4,500 meters above sea level, it is COLD before the sun comes up (for us, 6 degrees celsius below zero), so wear warm clothes and bring gloves. But also bring a swim suit for bathing in the geyser-heated pool later! They geysers themselves are really cool to see. My girlfriend has been to Yellowstone and seen the big ones there, but even she got a kick out of watching these smaller ones shoot up out of the ground. Also, you can get much closer to these geysers than some in other places (but be careful not to get too close!). Just mind the altitude and the cold, but otherwise definitely worth a visit! We also saw some fauna, such as vicuña and flamingos, on our way back down to San Pedro.

review_text: If you think you’ve seen amazing landscapes, wait until you get to know the Atacama Altiplanes Lagoas. This is one of the most magical tours in the Chilean desert — and also one of the highest: you reach more than 4,000 meters altitude! The tour begins early, and the first stop is in Socaire, an Andean village where you can taste the typical local breakfast and already feel the coldness of altitude. From there, the road rises towards the protagonists of the day: the Lagoas Miscanti and Miñiques. The intense blue of the water contrasts with the snowy mountains and volcanoes in the background — it’s so surreal that it looks like a hand-painted landscape. These lagoons are within a protected reserve and are home to flamingos, vicunhas and other animals you can’t imagine seeing in a desert. And a curiosity: they formed thousands of years ago, after a volcanic eruption that blocked the flow of water between the valleys. Prepare for the cold wind, breathtaking views — literally — and a peace that only the silence of the desert can offer. Tip: go snug, bring water and don't forget the camera. Because this is the kind of place you never forget again.

review_text: Now let's face it..... Futalelufu is not on many peoples radar screen as a travel destination....by car from Bariliche it is a good 5 hrs including time to cross the border...fortunately the road trip from Bariloche is visually stunning , the roads are paved 85% of the way so the travel time passes quickly..... But given the rocks that were flying on the unpaved road if you are renting a car you should get insurance for covering at least any small scratches from flying stones.... The roads are relatively empty with seemingly safe drivers.... Another challenge that Futalelufu has is a shortage of high end lodgings...Uman Lodge (see my review) is the only place that I'm aware of .... BUT all of these shortcomings are worth it if you are an avid fisherman, lover of kayaking or river rafting of just hiking. I've travelled all over the world...the closest Futaleufu comes to visually....would be a remote part of Switzerland with snow capped mountains in the summer, beautiful expanses of pasture for milk cows and sheep and the ocassional lama..brisk clean air, almost no people AND what separates it from Switzerland is the magnificent Futalelufu river. A sizeable, powerful , turquoise colored, pristine river flowing through the valley ...absolutely stunning. During our stay in Futalelufu we went fishing, rafting and hiking. One guy in our party, an avid fisherman, claimed that it was one of his most memorable fishing experiences having caught 30+ trout in one day. The white water rafting..including class 5 Rapids...was over the top....see my review. For three relatively inexperienced rafters pushing the envelope.....we can all highly recommend the experience.....and lastly there is the hiking ... Down mountain sides, through fields of wild flowers and beautiful pastures .... all so pleasant. Lastly the town of Futalelufu can't be more than 5 blocks square.....it has a very nice park at the center off of which one can find "simple" restaurants , a church, B&Bs , etc. for one of the best views of the Futalelufu river venture up to Uman Lodge, order a glass of wine or coffee, Go sit out on their terrace and soak in the wonders of nature. Futaleufu and its river have clearly remained undiscovered due to its isolation and possibly the few upscale lodges that are located here ...but this is also an advantage for those seeking the very best that nature has to offer without being over run by tourists. If you plan to drive allow for four nights in Futaleufu ...your arrival night, then 3 days of activity...hiking, rafting and fishing and then returning to Bariliche..,and yes, there is a gas station in Futaleufu to fill your car up for your return trip. If you rent a car in Bariliche make sure you get the proper documents to cross the border into Chile ... Depending on the number of people the border crossing will take 30-45 mins ...but both in Chile and Argentina there were 4-5 people manning each border crossing.

review_text: The quality of the La Serena and Coquimbo City Tour provided by LST tours on behalf of Viator was not at all good. The guide, who gave her name as Giovanna, was badly organised, lacking in knowledge and certainly not the expert bi-lingual guide promised in the tour description. The offering we experienced,could in no way be described as a 'guided' tour. Giovanna offered no information or commentary of worth as we moved from place to place and instead acted more as a courier simply telling us what we would visit next and how long it would take to get there. Upon arrival at each of the stops her input was limited to 'it is beautiful, we have ? minutes here, be back at the meeting point by...! She spent most of the early part of the trip taking orders for lunch and gave no information of worth about local life commerce and culture and that which she did offer, she had to check for accuracy on her mobile phone! She offered no information at all about city square in La Serena and at the cultural museum when questioned about the Easter Island figure, she told us that it was a replica, before once again consulting her phone and going round to tell people that it was an original. Her time and group management were both very poor. We spent a very, very long time, well more than an hour, at the Cross of the Third Milenium, while waiting for a very slow lift to take people to the top. People would have actually accepted being told that there was not enough time for this. We then spent almost half an hour at the Lighthouse in La Serena, which was far too long in the poor weather and visibility today. Unfortunately that meant that when we arrived at La Recova Market were allowed only ten minutes! Finally upon arrival at the Japanese Garden, we were all asked to leave the bus and then we were immediately asked to get back on, as she had decided that because of time constraints we should go straight for lunch and return to the Japanese Garden later. Lunch did not start until almost 3 pm and we did not finish until 4 pm The lady clearly had limited skills as a guide and when I asked her whether we would be receiving a refund for the tour she seemed genuinely ignorant of the abysmally low standard of experience that she was responsible for! Based on everything described so far, a good third of the group asked for the tour to be concluded at this point and she agreed that the bus driver would return us to the ship - after which he would return to the restaurant and complete the tour for those who wished to continue. After agreeing this, she even had the temerity to request a group photo and ask that we all smile!! Whilst awaiting our return, things changed again and she asked everyone to get back on the bus and that the tour would continue in a shortened form once we had been off loaded - in the end, and as we left, barely a third of the group opted to stay on board. This was not a cheap excursion and as we booked through Viator we asked for a refund less the cost of the meal, which in itself was good quality, and frankly the only highlight of a wasted day. Picking up a taxi driver at the port gate would have been a less expensive and more informative option. Viator bounced the complaint on to LST who refused any form of refund, as we had chosen to leave the tour early In summary, the tour was not as described, the quality was not what we'd paid for and I would advise caution when booking this tour Review of: La Serena & Coquimbo City Tour - Short Cruise Excursion
title: Beware when booking this tour

We came in March and they were actually bottling wine. They brought in a semi-trailer of wine equipment and they used specialized vacuum hoses to take the wine from the caves below and then applied whatever winemaking expertise that was required to get them into the bottles. It was fascinating to watch.

review_text: When we found a special airfare to visit Santiago from Los Angeles, the pressure was on to put together a short but great trip with as many memories as possible. We compared tours listed online and emailed with many companies. We selected Thomas based on his fantastic email response time and his willingness to accommodate our requests rather than suggest a preset itinerary. My husband and I toured with Chile Private Tours for 2 days. The first day with Julio we went up into the mountains to see El Colorado and Montana (2 ski resorts). There had been quite a bit of snow and Julio knew so many places to take amazing pictures, patiently allowing us to "reshoot" to be sure we got the best shots. In the afternoon we went back down to a very special vineyard in the middle of Santiago. The family owned vineyard is a wonderful refuge tucked away behind big walls just inches from the freeway. We had a personalized tour of the entire grounds and a special tasting at the end. Julio spoke perfect english, passionately shared great history of Chile and South America, and most important helped us take lots of photos. A perfect trip to the mountains! On day two we lucked out and got Thomas all to ourselves. We began with the Loma Larga vineyard and one of the most special tastings ever, an entire hour focused on us - with reserve tastings and so much education. We were met as we got out of the car by the master sommelier Alejandra who shared almonds that she had just harvested and roasted. An extensive tour was ended with some of the most impressive wines we've ever had. Then off to Valparaiso and Vina del Mar. The pictures can't prepare you for the awesome sites - so much history and color. Allowing for our picky palates Thomas arranged a very special and delicious lunch. 10 hours flew by so quickly, we packed quite a bit into the day. Later that night we were so excited to receive a special treat from Thomas - an email with a suggested city-tour for our last day, including options for lunch and guidance of the best time to leave for our flight home that night. On both tour days we were picked up promptly on schedule, and delivered back to our hotel just in time for dinner. The tours are reasonably priced, well paced, full of photo ops, and you're on the tour they are flexible to accommodate last minute inspiration (translates to "Oh wow can we see that???). Both Julio and Thomas are brilliant historians and can answer all questions. Touring with Thomas and Chile Private Tours is the best decision we made on our trip, and in the end gave us most of the lifelong memories we take from our vacation. Seemed no end to the careful focus on little things they did to create special stories we'll be sharing for years. Call or email Thomas today and let him create a special trip for you.
