review_text: Do not miss the chance to explore this distant area if you are in San Pedro de Atacama. Many tours do not include the Piedras Rojas and those who do include it as a particular attraction, but in fact it is a beautiful area beyond the famous Miscanti and Miniques lagoons. The area is perfectably suitable for self driving, which is in my opinion the bust way to explore natural wonders.Follow the Chile 23 road and you will drive into wonderful areas.The Piedras Rojas is just an interesting rock formation inside the huge and astoundingly beautiful Salar de Talar. Driving even further, you shall find the Laguna Tuyaijto, which is as beautiful as Miscanti but far less visited, less crowded, and with no entrance fee. The road itself, and the mountain scenery, are also breathtaking One thing that must be taken in account is the risk of altitude sickness, for this area is above 4550m

review_text: This is a dramatic and beautiful site that amply repays the time and effort required to visit. And it can be seen from many different vantage points within the park as well as from ranches outside the park. One word of caution: the pictures one sees invariably display a beautiful sunny day, but the typical weather in this part of the world is rain or cloud and sunny days are a distinct minority. Unfortunately clouds generally are low enough to hide the bbest parts of the range. The only solution is to take a trip of some length and hope that there is a sunny day or two. And investigate whether the rain and clouds situation is better or worse at different times of the year.

review_text: I have taken quite a few Hop on Hop off bus tours throughout the world. This was not one of the best. The second stop where you get off to go up the mountain to the statue of the Virgin Mary was the best. After that mostly just a lot of buildings to look at and history to listen to, not a lot of sights to see. Santiago takes a long time to drive around, it is a very sprawled city and the bus had to go very slow to give all of the history information. We purchased the Premium tour which included the ride up the mountain on the gondola, and down the funicular. It also included a walking tour. I would not recommend the walking tour. We got poor directions from the bus attendant, to find the walking tour, but eventually found it 2 blocks away from where the bus drops off. The walking tour only walked two blocks and it took an hour and a half. A lot of time sitting and waiting, some of which was to allow the guide to first do the tour in Spanish and then repeat in English. When we got back on the bus, we realized that the bus gave us the same information that our guide had, as we drove by these same two blocks. There is a beautiful cathedral in the old part of town, that is worth seeing, so get off at stop 5 and see the cathedral and wander around instead of the walking tour add on. We were told that the whole tour with stops to the Virgin Mary and walking tour would only take 3 hours; 7.5 hours later, we finally caught a cab back to our hotel. We will take into account each of your appreciations in order to improve and continue providing a quality service to each of our visitors. We wish you a happy return home.

review_text: My husband and I had the good fortune to book multiple tours with I Love Chile Tours prior to our visit to Santiago in late January 2018. Fran and Seba met us at our hotel for the first tour--a Day in Valparaiso. Two others were on the tour. After a friendly greeting and the offer of fresh fruit and water, we headed to our destination city. We stopped at a lovely winery in the Casablanca Valley where we were offered a small wine tasting and a "comfort stop." We arrived in the charming and colorful maze that is Valparaiso, and Fran guided us on a walking tour that covered the harbor, many streets at sea level and then climbs up the populated hillsides. To reach the pinnacle we used a funicular and were able to have great views of the city, harbor and the tony neighborhood of Vena del Mar across the harbor. Fran gave a running commentary on the history and current changes taking place in the City. Outdoor art plays a very important part of the Chilean culture and no more than in Valparaiso--murals, attractive graffiti, and unfortunately...some ugly "tagging." We lunched in a local restaurant, and the fondness displayed by the owners toward Fran and Seba was typical of interactions they had with other native City natives. Because of Fran and Seba's excellent command of English, we were able to communicate all day long and ask whatever we wanted...including topics such as politics and religion. It was long day, a fun day, and an important part of our memories of I Love Chile Tours. We also took a walking tour of Santiago with their associate Clara and spent another day in Vena del Mar with Fran Seba. GREAT tours! Review of: Valparaiso Day Trip from Santiago - Private Tour for Small Groups

review_text: Jose was our Uncorked guide for our full day wine tours in Maipo and Colchagua valleys, and we were pleased with the vineyards he had selected. In the Maipo Valley, we visited Perez Cruz, a very large winery with an unusual architecture, including big arcs. The tasting room was small and we tried three different red wines. The second visit to William Fevre was led by an energetic and enthusiastic host. He had set up a table along the path leading to the winery with a vase of flowers, bottle of chardonnay, and two glasses. We proceeded to try wines from the tanks, two from barrels, and three reds with some cheese and crackers. (At the end of the day, Jose gave us the opened bottle from the tasting, which was a very nice touch.) The last “tasting” was at the restaurant at Haras de Pirque where we had a fixed lunch of shrimp with tomatoes, salmon with potatoes Anna and some sort of custard. The “pairing” was a glass of chardonnay and a glass of their red wine. The restaurant overlooked part of the vineyard. It was not really a tasting. Jose was our guide again into the Colchagua valley where we first stopped at the Lugarejo winery, owned by a History professor (PhD from UCDavis ...) and his wife. The winery is tiny but they are clearly passionate about their hobby, most of which is in a sort of garage with a single bottle bottling machine! We had a lovely time with Elina and tried three of their wines. She had a plate with olives and crackers. The second winery was Neyen where we could see vines growing up into the hills of the valley. A young lady walked us (and another tour group) into the vineyard and explained how the vine stems were made to root on either side of the “mother” vine for cloning. Then we tried three of their wines. The larger, second group also seemed to be an EcoChile or Uncorked group that had come for a day tour from Santiago. This was definitely a premium (or, as they tend to describe them in Chile, "iconic") wine, and very good. The last vineyard was Viu Manent where we first had lunch of grilled tenderloin (not too tender) with two wines. After the lunch, we went across the road to the tasting room to taste seven (!) different wines! At the very end of the day, Jose left us at the Hotel Santa Cruz in Santa Cruz. The wine tours were the best parts of our two-week visit to northern Chile.

review_text: We did the 10-day north tour. I loved it - we talk about it all the time, and I would kill to go back and do it all over again! From reading these other reviews, we were hesitant to book, but we took the plunge. I think Pachamama tours can be hit-and-miss. My experience was definitely a hit. I went with one of my best friends, and the only other people on our tour were another set of 20-something best friends and a recently married couple (there were 6 guests total). This made the tour really familial and intimate. We loved it, but I can see how it wouldn't have been the same if the people in our group weren't great. If you're looking for a tour in an official charter bus with tour guides in matching polos who maintain an arms-length relationship, this isn't for you. It's definitely more South American in style - remember, you're in Chile! The guides and driver were very kind to us, and chose to have dinner with us and hang out with us most nights. Our guide, Jorge, was extremely knowledgable, and was training another amazing guide, Paulina. The driver, Pedro, was one of the kindest people I've met - he buys food for the stray dogs along the 10-day route and tirelessly cares for them each time he completes the loop. We saw beautiful, remote places we would have never seen if we hadn't taken this tour. I really feel like I've seen most of the top half of Chile after doing this trip. Jorge really pushed us to get out of our comfort zones - riding horses on steep mountain paths, riding in little boats in the Pacific to see penguins, arguing about politics, etc. This was an incredible experience, and I wish I could do a tour this style in every country I visit.
title: Unique Experience - Would love to do it again

Last stop was a little boutique winery in the country, They had an interesting garden, horses, alpacas, various farm birds (chickens, ducks, geese) and experimental gardens growing various nuts and fruits. Fantastic people and incredible wine! Could only fit two more bottles in our suitcase. If only they had wine shippers there I would have bought much more. The one in Rio Gallegos , Arg. is better presented and free. Dear Sir, from your review, I can assume you haven't entered my museum, is also easy to understand you do not even visited the other replica which is in San Julian not in Rio Gallegos (same 780 km north of Punta Arenas) and is not free at all (price of admission being 3,5 US$). In our case, you have the possibility to visit the 1:1 replicas of three historical ships, such as Magellan's Nao Victoria, Shackleton's lifeboat James Caird and the Schooner Ancud (ship that brought the first Chilean settlers in Patagonia), and you think 6 US$ is paying heaps, i am afraid is just your opinion. If you add that we are now building the full size replica of the HMS Beagle (first ever in the world), and allow all visitors to see how we build it without extra charge (www.hmsbeagle.cl), I think your opinion is not really accurate as you did not actually visited the Museum. I am really sorry you had not time enough to visit the museum and stayed outside where, yes there is some ponds of water when is raining (yes, is Patagonia, it does rain sometimes in summer), and not, we are not in a backyard, but in a private venue, right at the entrance of the town from the airport, connected by public transport to the center of the town.

review_text: This tour is great. Sure you have to leave San Pedro at 4am but set your alarm and bring a warm jacket and gloves. The ascent to the area of the geysers takes about 2 hours and is in darkness so just close your eyes and rest. Tour arrives at the geyser plain at about 6:45am and the temperature was -8 degrees C. The guide gave a good explanation in spanish and english of the geology and processes involved. The reason to be so early is that the extreme temperature differential at that hour creates more impressive clouds of steam. It is like walking on the crater of a volcano with multiple fissures erupting with boiling water. The emergence of sunrise through the plumes of steam create a spectacular sight. Sunrise also prompts time for a breakfast to be served with welcome hot coffee greeting the rising temperatures. After a good time to wander we move on to another close-by area that also features a pool of naturally heated water where it is possible to bathe for awhile. The trip back to San Pedro features spectacular mountain scenery and the multi-coloured peaks are amazing. There are a few stops for photo ops especially when the animals such as vicuna and llamas are present. The final stop is at a small settlement called Machuca for souvenir purchases, water and snack replenishment, restrooms or just photo ops.We were back in San Pedro at about 12:30pm. An early start, a bumpy bus ride but a superb experience. The guide from Touristour, Salvador, was both friendly and informative.

review_text: We tried so many ways to find information on boat tours around Penguin Island! We even had American Express Platinum Concierge helping us! So to save future travelers the trouble, there are no commercial tours that go to the island. You have to take a private fishing boat. Ultimately, our visit from Santiago was arranged through a tour guide named Cristian Herrara. He was able to secure a fishing boat for our date and time, drove us from Santiago and came with us to interpret as the fisherman only spoke Spanish. The trip from Santiago was a day trip to a beautiful area of the Chilean Coast. The boat ride was about an hour and a half. To save you time, if you want to set this adventure up, we highly recommend contacting Cristian Herrara at +56 9 9237 0631. It literally took us weeks to find Cristian! He is an excellent tour guide. We used him six times during our trip to Santiago! Humboldt penguins are the smallest and are also endangered. Have a good zoom lens with you. They are adorable. This is also the only place to see penguins near Santiago.

review_text: The guide and driver were great (Allef and Walter). Very lively and attentive. But some negative points of the tour (Laguna del Inca in August 2023): 0. I discovered Zerando o Chile through YouTuber Estevam pelo Mundo. In the video, he said that his followers had a discount. Lie. I asked for a discount, they disagreed, they said it was already discounted, but that's a lie. Terrible. 1. Breakfast: not included and very expensive. 6 thousand pesos for a mixed drink with a choice of drink or 10 thousand pesos for an all-you-can-eat buffet, but with very few options. I passed Wise and was still taxed 600 pesos. There was a huge queue and a terrible bathroom. The place is terrible. 2. Rental of cold weather clothing: 180 reais per person. Clothes weren't necessary, as there was barely any snow and it was hot... of course the guide must have already known this information from visiting the place several times, but he still didn't mention it. He let the group rent it for nothing. Furthermore, the rental takes time and delays all other passengers. We spent more than 1h30 at this coffee and clothing rental place. 3. The trip to Laguna del Inca: the Laguna itself is in a private area of a hotel. People can only get to a kind of balcony and look from afar. And then there's that Farofa and he pushes and pushes to take a photo. To use the bathroom, you have to pay 500 pesos, a dirty, container-style bathroom... terrible too. I don't recommend the tour. It's worth renting a car (if it's snowing, rent chains) and going there yourself. Soooo much more game. You'll enjoy it much more. I did this to go to Valle Nevado and it really paid off. Agradecemos pelo seu feedback sincero e detalhado, Lígia. title: SPECTACULAR !!!

review_text: The park is a wonderful to wander through and spend several hours. The museum of Natural History is located in the park, as is a photo museum, a rail museum, and the Modern Art museum is just outside the park. There are playgrounds for the children and plenty of open spaces to enjoy.
title: Wonderful way to spend several hours

review_text: It was amazing. Guia Francisco was phenomenal. Our thanks. The driver Luis is a grace of person. Everyone very attentive. Sympathetic. Solicitors. Chefs rsrs. The cocktail watching the sunset was beautiful and delicious. Note 10,000 Review of: Tour to Vallecito and Magic Bus
title: Sensational

review_text: Simply amazing experience with Araya. My honeymoon trip was wonderful with all the impeccable service, excellent guides, plus the wonderful meals! I already miss the landscapes and take care of every detail. I am lactose intolerant and have had attention in my restrictions feed on every walk. Thank you for everything and congratulations on excellence! I definitely indicate too much!
title: Super recommend!

review_text: When I asked my kids to do some research for our trip to Santiago, they found this cat Cafe. So we had to go! You make a reservation for a 1 1/2 hour timeslot. You’re given instructions before entering the café, what to do and not do with the cats. It costs 5000 pesos and includes a drink. There were 13 cats. They roam around, come to visit for a pet or snuggle or playtime.😊 it was a fun way to relax from the hustle and bustle of the city.
title: Cats, Cats and more Cats

review_text: We had an absolutely wonderful time on this tour! The train ride was really fun as we enjoyed the beautiful scenery, traditional music, and tasting of delicious wines. They even included coffee and a snack for the ride! We had a pleasant lunch in Santa Cruz, strolled through the museum, and finished the day with a tour and tasting at Montes! The day flew by with all the fun activities but was also a relaxing escape from Santiago. We had always wanted to do a wine tour, but going by car means someone is missing out on the fun. This way both of us could try the various wines and get home responsibly. Everything was very well organized and ran smoothly from beginning to end. The tour guides, staff, and even musicians were so cheery and attentive. I would recommend this tour for couples, families, or even solo travelers!
title: A wonderful day in the countryside enjoying amazing Chilean wines!

review_text: Wonderful experience! Jacqueline was very informative and friendly and made sure everyone was included. I loved the wine tasting in the beautiful Casablanca vineyard. Review of: From Santiago: Valparaíso, Viña del Mar and Neruda Museum Glad to hear you had a wonderful experience and that Jacqueline made the tour informative and friendly for everyone. The wine tasting at the Casablanca vineyard sounds really lovely. thanks for sharing your experience!
title: Tour

review_text: This superb new centre built only a few years ago, has something for everyone. It is top-notch smart, has a full food court on the top floor which incorporates a cinema. On the bottom floor there is a jumbo supermarket, slightly more pricey than other supermarkets but if you wish to do all your shopping in the one area and then just get a taxi to your hotel, then it's extremely convenient.
title: Shop till you drop!

review_text: Franco was my english speaking guide. He was fantastic! Loved the history of the city provided. I also loved the food, drink and shopping tips Franco gave us along the way. This was the best way to spend a morning! It is 4 hours but we stopped for lunch which I needed. We were recommended a 5000-7000 tip which was well worth it! Great way to mingle with other travellers too and you can leave the tour at any point if you don't have a spare 4 hours.
title: Great introduction to Santiago

review_text: Beautiful tour and free. It has a system of ramps that greatly interfere with the spaces but its purpose is to protect the land. There is a very nice llama living there. I want to highlight that upon arrival Alejandro spoke to us dressed as a pirate and offered us a guided tour with a voluntary tip, we took it and it was spectacular, he is a very good guide, he handles a lot of historical information and makes the tour very enjoyable, I fully recommend it because we got to know each other fully the history of the place.
title: History on demand

review_text: We signed up for this tour not really knowing what to expect, but hoping we’d learn more about the artists than previous tours we’ve done in Latin America. It didn’t disappoint. Sebastian certainly knows his stuff and delivered the tour in perfect English. He’s also really kind to the street dogs that accompanied us for the 2.5 hours, which was good to see. I wouldn’t hesitate to recommend this Graffriti tour - and it’s definitely worth a good tip. Review of: Valparaiso City History & Graffiti Tour
title: Excellent tour, expertly done

review_text: Benjamin was an excellent guide, his diction and level of English was quite clear. We had a great time at the Laguna del Inca. Recommended Review of: Inca Lagoon in Andes Mountain Range - Visit Local Vineyard with Tasting included
title: Good Time in Inca Lagoon

review_text: The Cerro San Cristobal is deceptively higher than it looks from below, the views across Santiago to the Andes is spectacular. There is a cheap cable car available or a funicular railway, take your choice. Choose as clear a day as possible, the smog will dictate how far you can see
title: Best views of Santiago along with the Sky Constenara

review_text: The places visited, the attention of the team, the accommodation, the food, all very nice and delicious, many photos and very good, without a doubt I recommend it to everyone, a beautiful experience. Muchas gracias Victoria. Nos esforzamos por ofrecer una experiencia inolvidable y es gratificante saber que lo hemos logrado. ¡Nos encantaría verte nuevamente y seguir creando momentos especiales juntos!
title: Wonderful weekend :)

review_text: A wonderful 3hour private walking tour with Johan today. I arrived into Santiago from the US at 6.30am. Walking tour at 11am. Johan was knowledgeable and his narrative interesting on all the questions I asked of him. I would highly recommend this tour to familiarize yourself with the history of Chile and Santiago. Thank you! Review of: Private Santiago 3-Hour Walking Tour Thank you for your lovely review! We're glad you enjoyed your private walking tour with Johan, especially after your early arrival. It’s great to know his narrative and knowledge of Chile and Santiago were so engaging. We hope you’ll recommend this tour to others and come back to explore more soon! Elena &Patricio
title: Excellent private walking tour, not to be missed!

review_text: The Blanco River is world class for rafting and kayaking. The guides are excellent. Rafting in Hornopiren was a very good experience. Thank you Colimahuidan Aventura!
title: Rafting in Hornopiren

review_text: It is so breathtaking and wonderful to be able to see so much beauty in nature here in Chile. This park again is a gem.
title: Beautiful

review_text: Its a very nice place in Santiago! You can climb by yourself, its a nice walk and you will enjoy the view. Its great to see Cordilheira dos Andes and the city!
title: Nice View

review_text: I visited today so that I could go to Mass (I went to the 0945 on Sunday). It was in Spanish (as they all are) but it’s nice to experience being one family in faith! Afterwards I wanted to find out a bit more about the cathedral but none of the signs had any translations which was a shame. I’ve since read up online. It’s beautiful though and is worth a visit despite this. It feels like a pearl of calm.
title: Beautiful but I wish there had been more info

review_text: I booked a rafting trip on short notice. I have never rafted before, but lots of paddling experience otherwise. This trip blew me away. It was a perfect day with stunning sunshine and humongous waves on the river. The equipment and guides are top notch. They have a safety catamaran for every raft plus a safety kayak. But we did not need any of their assistance, as the guide navigated us through even the biggest rapids with confidence. A must do when in Futalafue. I highly recommend Futalfeu River Rafting!
title: Perfect rafting trip!

review_text: The convenience of making stops along the way allowed us to hop off for lunch, coffee and other attractions, then hop back on. Maria was an awesome guide, and Rafael was helpful with our shopping. Sensational Santiago! We totally enjoyed it Review of: Cable Car, Funicular and Sightseeing Bus in Santiago one day Thank you very much for sharing your experience with us.
title: Sensational Santiago by bus

review_text: This was one of my favorite spots in Atacama! The views are insanely powerful. It might get crowded as it is one of the most famous spots in Atacama, but tourist flow comes and go pretty fast...
title: Epic views!!

review_text: Beats climbing the hill. Don't charge much and it is worth every penny. If you are here, why would you miss out on the experience? Afraid of death, perhaps?
title: Worth every Penny

review_text: Relatively new attractive spot of Santiago with great view. If you don't have enough time to see all around Santiago, then this place is worth to visit. It's quite different view compared with San Cristobal hill. The expense is 10,000pesos (approximately USD 15). * 7,500pesos on Wednesday.
title: Worth to visit

review_text: It's worth it for the experience! The space itself isn't all those things, but the contact with the herbivores is magical, the felines being so close to us in a cage is incredible... there, we also ate a complete one that was delicious, but it wasn't cheap (by the way, no there is practically cheap food in Chile).
title: Magic!

review_text: We arrived in Santiago with rain and snow and none of the tours we had booked could be done, but still the trip was wonderful! As it was 4 days of travel, without their help ⁇ would not have been so fun! Thank you very much for the caring, the attention of the drivers and the care with the choices. We really love it! Review of: Casas del Bosque y Bodegas RE
title: Good surprise

review_text: We went with Vulcano Expediciones based on Lonely Planet’s recommendation. Our guide Christian was awesome. He taught us how to walk slowly and breathe deeply (very yoga like) and we had no problem making it to the 18,386 foot summit of Cerro Taco. The ride up to the trailhead is in a 4WD Toyota Hilux and the trailhead itself is about 1,500 feet from the summit. I would consider this to be a moderate trek without altitude. I felt some lightheadedness on the climb, but poles (and coca leaves which we found in town) mitigated any problem. I believe they have extra poles if you didn’t bring your own. Make sure you eat a good breakfast before leaving because you just get a light snack at the top.
title: Amazing Cerro Taco trek!

review_text: Alonso was very knowledgeable about the city of Santiago, particularly the political history. This tour complimented the other w walking tours available. I highly recommend it.
title: Great highlights tour of Santiago by 'Tours for Tips'

review_text: Simple people, simple needs! Cheap & accessible place. Very peacefull and surrounded by mountains. There are 5 different bath from 20 to 45'C. No service around.
title: Peaceful

review_text: This was on my must do list while in Santiago. The ride up was nice--- try to get in the lowest car for the best view. The city views are beautiful.
title: Must see

review_text: HIGHLY HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!!! Patricio and his dad offered a great personalized tour around Atacama for us. It was one of a kind and impeccable service! Patricio not only was our guide, but our professional photographer along the way. You are getting great value for your money by booking with them. Patricio even dropped off a few prints of pictures for us at the hotel before we leave. Lunch was also amazing as we were expecting a boxed lunch. Little did we know that Patricio has a secret spot to bring us too. His dad cooked us a chicken and rice lunch served with fresh juices and wine. We had such a great time and it’s all thanks to Patricio and his dad!
title: BEST PRIVATE TOUR EVER!!!

review_text: Good way to see city and stop where you’d like. Only thing was, no signs where just stops, therefore have to remember return to exact stop and watch for bus Review of: Tourist bus around Santiago for a day Hello dear Cindy! Thank you for leaving us your comment as this lets us know what improvements we need to make. On the other hand, we are glad you enjoyed the Hop On Hop Off bus experience. Best regards!
title: Good experience

review_text: Excellent trip, good food, very friendly guides, I searched it on Facebook and I don't regret, they went to look for me at the house.... Review of: Tour to Huilo Huilo from Pucón, Villarrica
title: Tour huilo huilo the best

review_text: The best experience of life. The motto “the factory of happiness” fits them precisely. Will you repeat? Of course, a thousand times
title: An unforgettable experience

review_text: Excellence!! In Everything !!!!!from the reception and the tours! Friendly staff, delicious food and lots of Comfort, knowledge and fun on all tours!!!
title: Excellence

review_text: This trip was my first time in Chile and after researching I knew that I couldn't miss seeing Valparaíso and Viña del Mar for myself. I contacted Stamp's Tour and reserved seats for my group in advance by contacting them via email. Their response time was very quick and very clear. Stamp's was also flexible in that they were able to pick us up from our apartment since we were not staying in a hotel. Our guide Frank was exceptional, he was full of knowledge, kept us interested and was very personable. A day tour can quickly become very dull but Frank had no problem keeping us interested. After visiting the walking portion of our day tour we had lunch at a cozy spot in Viña del Mar. They had a special menu for us but you can order from the main menu if the selections don't include what you'd like. The meal was a great way to get to know the people we were on the tour with and the food was delicious. The cost for the meal was 21000 CLP plus tip. Our last spot was Viña Indómita, Casablanca & Maipo Vineyards. The vineyard is beautiful and wine tasting is optional but when in Chile, why not? The wines were amazing, the sample size generous and the price very reasonable. I would definitely recommend Stamp's Tour.
title: Valparaiso, Vina Del Mar and Casablanca & Maipo Vineyards for the day

review_text: The kayak tour was a great experience. A clear recommendation. The guide was extremely helpful with tips and information via WhatsApp before the tour. The lady speaks perfect English and can answer any question. Your expertise in kayaking, weather, tour guide combined with your English skills made you one of my most valuable people on the trip. You will receive mobile photos of your tour after the activity. Review of: Marble Chapels Kayak Tour Thanks so much for this beautiful review <3
title: 10x better than boat tour

review_text: very expuriance and safety stuff the expariance was amasing Pedro is a super proffesional and good vibes Review of: Rafting Futaleufu River Bridge to Bridge Section
title: go and do it

review_text: I knew the true history of the Piscus, an excellent teacher. It is the oldest pisco vineyard in the region, possibly the oldest in Chile
title: A great class

review_text: Did an independent bicycle tour into the Valle and was utterly disappointed. Guards are patronizing from the moment of using their ticketing machine and otherwise take pride in preventing visitors from seeing the sights. After the ascent from the road, the most important viewpoint was blocked for no apparent reason. It's not possible to drive through the valley either, as the round-trip is fenced off again for no good reason. Even though every geological formation is certainly unique, given what it was, everything I saw is equally as well or better seen elsewhere. If you haven't been to a high altitude desert before, maybe worth visiting, otherwise do your valuable time and wallet a favor and skip Valle de la Luna.
title: Utterly disappointing with patronizing guards, viewpoints fenced off, and passage through the valley blocked.

review_text: As a human rights student, this was a must for me! I'm so glad I went - the museum is informative but not boring. Entrance is free, but the museum relies on donations. The english audio guide is well worth the 2000 pesos. It's right across the street from a metro stop, so easy to get to as well. On the other side of the street is a beautiful park that is nice to chill out in.
title: One of the best!

review_text: Feeling like you are on Mars! make sure you include some hiking into your excursion and go early morning or late in the afternoon to take best pics because of the light. Take your time, the landscape is awesome and changes all day long depending on light.
title: Feeling like being on Mars

review_text: Very beautiful place!!!! What a pleasant atmosphere full of history, perfect to go for walks with family and friends, all very nice

We made the tour geyser del tatio, very nice experience, Valentine and Ignacio very attentive and friendly, concerned with the well-being of everyone at all times, exquisite breakfast and abundant. Recommended 10/10.
title: Beautiful landscapes and concern to explain in different languages.

review_text: Guide Allef is a highly qualified professional. I made tours in Chile with another agency and I can guarantee that the guide Allef is a distinguished professional. He can manage the diversity of people, cultures and can easily maintain the harmony of the group. No doubt, for the excellent experience on the tour I will indicate the agency and give as a reference the guide Allef. Olá! Muito obrigado pelo seu comentário tão positivo! 😊 Ficamos felizes em saber que teve uma experiência excelente conosco e, em especial, com o nosso guia Allef. Ele realmente tem um talento incrível para conduzir grupos com leveza, respeito e profissionalismo — vamos repassar seu elogio com carinho! Agradecemos pela confiança e por nos recomendar. Esperamos te receber novamente em novas aventuras pelo Chile! Um grande abraço.
title: Party Farellones - amazing

review_text: This is a very pleasant attraction that is quite accessible to those who can't do longer hikes. It is best to go early on a weekday not in February. There are two entrances... we prefer the second one leaving from Pucón.
title: Lovely falls, nice and easy walk in nature.

review_text: Due to the helpful audioguide we learned a lot of the life of Pablo Neruda. The added value for us was the commented photos of his cultural and political life that met us om the ground floor of the house. During our visit we read two of his poems and inspired by this we bought a poem book of Neruda. It is recommendable to show up around opening time because a lot of school groups also visit this remarkable house.
title: Valuable visit

review_text: Beautiful beach for a walk, walk, sunbathe and admire the view. You can't go into the water, it's too cold! It's not cold, it's really cold. There are many food options, ice cream, coffee, beautiful place.
title: Beautiful beach to stroll, sunbathe and admire the view

review_text: Wonderful tours polite attentive guides, agency gave complete support on tours and transportation. Santiago city is beautiful. Review of: Inca Lagoon in Andes Mountain Range - Visit Local Vineyard with Tasting included
title: Best experience in Chile

review_text: This little hill in the middle of Santiago affords a great view of the surrounding barrios. It is a public area, and has some level of security, as you are supposed to sign in with the guard as you enter. Don't be intimidated by that. Be aware that the hill is covered with a variety of stairways and walkways, and provides a pleasant entertainment for young and old alike. some of the stones in the stairways are uneven, and some are slippery, so use caution. It is well worth the visit. There is something beautiful to see in every direction. It is located on O'Higgins just next to the Biblioteca National, and the Archivo Nacional.
title: Great view of Santiago!

review_text: With my friends we did a tour to the lagoons, with Juan Carlos, Marietta and Gustavo and it was an incredible experience loaded with emotions and valuable learning, we were very happy with the boys, you can see a lot when people love their work and do it from the heart, yes I highly recommend taking tour with them, it was a magical experience ✨😁 Hola Camila! Muchas gracias por tus amables comentarios. Me aseguraré de transmitir tus comentarios alentadores también al equipo. Estamos muy contentos de que hayas pasado un momento maravilloso explorando Atacama con nosotros! Esperamos darle la bienvenida nuevamente! Gracias :)
title: Excellent recommended experience

review_text: Great tour with Carlos, you can go there with your eyes closed! Big thanks !! We had the luxury of only being 2 with him, and were able to make this tour a Spanish lesson in addition to learning so much about the history, politics, art and architecture of Santiago , THANKS !
title: Excellent tour!

review_text: Early morning can be plagued by mist before the sun has burnt it off. Recommend you go up by cable car in the afternoon when it could be clearer and the sun is at a better angle for photo opportunities of which there are many. Take the funicular down. A very worthwhile attraction.
title: Late afternoon is the best time to go

review_text: The agency was super organized! We always knew where we were going and when. The guides were great, all very helpful and passing the knowledge clearly, but Benjamin, there at Salar do Uyuni, stole the scene! The guy is a separate show! Explains everything right, takes care of us as if we were family and still makes us laugh. The Uyuni Salar with mirror effect? Surreal of beautiful! The food was a delight too. Atacama was great, the whole of Bolivia was amazing, but Benjamin made all the difference.
title: Atacama and Salar do Uyuni

review_text: What surprised me was the number of Croatian Mausoleums, was not aware of the large immigration of Croatians to southern Chile in the early XX Century. There is a statue of the "Indiecito" that is famous and always with fresh flowers. Also the Menendez, Braun and other families have prominent mausoleums. In the back to the right side of the entrance are a series of 2 and 3 stories buildings filled with niches. a more recent development. There are lots of singularly shaped trees that add a unique ambience to the place.
title: A must see place.

review_text: I travelled up the Funicular railway, stopping at the zoo on the way, and then walked down. The funicular railway is a fun experience, even if it is very short. It's not too expensive, and don't be put off by the queues - they may appear long and slow at first glance, but in fact they move at a reasonable pace in bursts (as the funicular cars are loaded). Walking down is an exercise for the energetic (and I'm told that walking up is even more so). That said, I really enjoyed a relaxing walk by the road - but you'll see other reviewers who did not. There's not a lot to do at the very top of Cerro San Cristobel, but there are good views of the surrounding city, and a garden that is well maintained, and on the day I visited was warm and quiet despite the large number of visitors. There are a few food and souvenir shops (good if you are hot or hungry!). The zoo is not stunning but worth a visit nevertheless.
title: Take the funicular and enjoy the views

review_text: Today the tour to Embalse El Yeso and Termas de Colina was sensational with our Guide Leo who did not lack animation, charisma and explaining our script from beginning to end and Kevin who was super attentive on the road. Thank you Morande!!!
title: Fun and Trusted Tour

review_text: Excellent tour, we thank Don Pedro for his friendliness and hospitality. The interaction he has with tourists is appreciated and he makes sure that everyone is learning.
title: Entertaining tour, simple in explanation and very dynamic

review_text: I was staying Las Serena following suggestions from the LONELY PLANET guide. Yes, I know I could Google such things, but I enjoy a hand held book. Just a quick warning. There are two entrances. No Uber driver could find me. And very few Uber driver's speak English. This lead to a great deal of frustration and gave me the opportunity to explore on foot. There is a grand earthy staircase on the hillside of the garden. This is easy access to and from town. There was parking and an entrance fee. I was delightfully surprise to find a Japanese garden in the middle of a town in Chile. There was many local residents a.k.a. ducks. It was a great place to collect my thoughts and enjoy a chilly day in Chile. Look for signs to stay on the walk way and off the grass. My favorite part was the green house. I would return here again.
title: Walk Down the Stairs to Serenity

review_text: It is possible to ride a pushbike out to here if you wanted to but beware of the heat, take plenty of water and use sunscreen often. There was some damage out here when we visited because there had been record rainfall only a couple of moths ago. When you looked up at some of the rocks and clay they only had a very tenative hold which may well have been easily disrupted by a person walking past. it was fascinating to stand quietly and listen to the creaking sound created by the effect of heat on the minerals in the walls of the valley. The massive sand dune was fantastic and loved the fact that people were not permitted access so you get so it in its pristine state.
title: Walking on the Moon

review_text: Antonio was a superb, knowledgeable guide! Perfectly paced day with a variety of stops and free time for lunch. Communication was excellent. Review of: Santiago: Viña del Mar, Valparaiso & Casablanca Valley Tour
title: Fantastic excursion from Santiago

review_text: I had a great day in Maipo Valley. Mick picked me up on time at my hotel in Santiago. Got to taste wine right from the barrels. Highly recommend to anyone.
title: Amazing day in Maipo Valley

review_text: A very nice overview of Santiago, a bit of history, bigger bit of markets, lots of interesting information. Highly recommended. Thank you, Vanessa. Note: the tours are free, but they expect tips, around 10000 CLP
title: Really nice tour

review_text: This tour was great as was our guide Franco! You learn much and see a lot of the city in a short period of time. Some people have complained about the sales pitch aspect that occurs occasionally for restaurants, but usually it comes with a cultural side note about the different types of food or history of it within Chile. It's a free tour. Who cares if they are plugging a specific restaurant or two along the way, but I digress. Our tour lasted about 3.5 hours. You're walking on flat land for most of it with maybe a few stairs thrown in. It's not like the tour in Valparaiso where there are lots and lots of (mostly downhill) stairs. (also a great, free tour). Overall this is a great way to see the city and learn some of its interesting history.
title: Franco for President!

review_text: 4 of us went to Valparaíso with Matias as our guide. We all enjoyed the day very much and felt very lucky to have Matias as his English was excellent and his passion for Valparaíso was evident. He brought the city to life for us. Our driver was also excellent. Review of: Full-Day Mahout's Life Experience
title: Valparaíso in one day

review_text: Remember your water, sun hat and sunscreen. If you wear closed shoes or boots, you won't get quite so much sand between your toes.
title: Delightful downhill walk

review_text: I visited Aldea de Tulor along with Pukara de Quitor (see separate review) on a half day tour out of San Pedro. It was well worth the time to visit these culturally and historically significant sights. You learn about the history of the region and the indigenous peoples. A good balance to all the landscape destination tours in the region.
title: Great Site for History and Culture

review_text: The tours we took with Feel were spectacular! Mari attended to us and organized an incredible itinerary, which exceeded all of our expectations. I highly recommend it!
title: Incredible experiences!!!

review_text: I wanted a guide to go with me to climb a trail that Charles Darwin is said to have climbed when he was in this area in 1835. A helpful travel agent at the bus station in Valparaiso suggested Ecomapu and we contacted them to book a guide. They sent a student, Manuel, who was a great guide. We spent the day going to and from the park and hiking in the park. He could not have been more helpful! I intend to go again and ask for his guiding help.
title: Guided hike on trail in the park

review_text: Overall, our trip was excellent and we brought back home unforgettable warm memories of Argentina and Chile. Our trip included certain segments arranged through EcoChile Travel services and other segments which we booked directly ourselves (namely, Australis cruise and Explora Torres Del Paine). This review covers only EcoChile segments. We believe EcoChile services were commensurate with the price and met our expectations. We would like to thank Oxana Protchenko (Sales) for her effort in working with us to design the itinerary that met our requirements which included various reservations for hotels, show and tours in Buenos Aires, El Calafate, El Chalten, Ushuaia, Santiago, Valparaiso. Oxana handled our requests timely and with professionalism and good sense of customer care. We also would like to mention specifically Patricia Rosas (Operations) who was punctual, answered promptly our phone calls and messages via Trip Plans app and resolved all our inquiries to our satisfaction. We had four travelers in our group and all four of us agreed that the best local guide (by far!) throughout the entire trip organized by EcoChile was Javiera Zambrano (Santiago city tour) – flexible, knowledgeable, informative, helpful and we could not have had a better experience, especially on the last day of our trip. The availability of the EchoChile technology – having our itinerary available online and in PDF form, and also in the Trip Plans app – was helpful in providing a smooth and enjoyable travel experience, including real-time updates for each day. We felt well connected to EchoChile and local providers throughout the entire trip. One area of recommendation is obtaining more details / specifics from the local operators / tour guides on the content of the suggested tours. This is particularly important for private tour small group, like ourselves, Many of the descriptions in our itinerary were either too generic or standard and repeated what one can read on Viator or other tour aggregator websites. We enjoyed all things on our itinerary with the glacier Perito Moreno and tango lesson being example highlights for us. We are satisfied with the services provided by EcoChile and we would not hesitate to provide positive referrals for EcoChile to others. Thanks for your review and feedback! It's great to hear that you enjoyed your trip. I hope you can continue tango lessons at home too! All best, Emily EcoChile Travel Team
title: Patagonia at the Best -Argentina & Chile travel experience.

review_text: The consultant Diego was mto attentive and helpful in hiring the tours, I recommend the agency with all certainty, not to mention in super responsible and inquisitive guides and drivers. Nossa equipe fica extremamente feliz sabendo que sua viagem se concretizou e que pudemos gerar a melhor experiência que o Chile pode proporcionar ❤️🇨🇱
title: Experience met all expectations

review_text: We did the "Good morning Santiago" yesterday with Sandy and it was great. Our guide was a smiling one, with a lot of energy and who really loves the city. I only regret a little bit the lack of historical informations. They are good at the beginning, in front of the Moneda Palace and beside Santa Lucia hill, but the rest of the tour is sometimes quick. Maybe more informations, or a longer tour, or a shorter distance (I don't know) should be better. Thanks !
title: Good and funny tour

review_text: Without a doubt one of the best experiences of my life! Pay attention to details, super experienced and professional guides, punctuality, wonderful meals included.
title: Professionalism and care in every detail.

review_text: Did the Casablanca region and Couchowa Valley (pls excuse the spelling), and found both days fascinating in the variety of wineries, styles of wine, and very nice lunches. Both guides were excellent and the transport van/mini bus and driver comfortable. I’d reco to a friend and not worry.
title: 2 excellent days of Wine

review_text: My tour guide, Eduardo, was very obviously well-informed on all things Valpo and all things street art. My only suggestion for the company (and this only applies to private tours) is that they take the individual's purpose more into account throughout the tour. As it is a rather steep price for an afternoon between two people, it'd be nice if we were asked more explicitly why we booked the tour. Where we come from. What experience we already have with street art or art in general. Clearly, the customer is not the expert here. But the exchange would benefit from a little more dialogue. It got there eventually, but only after I pushed for it to get there. That being said, my experience with Eduardo was great! I booked the tour for research and got more than all the information/perspectives I had hoped for. I would highly recommend booking a private tour if you can; you can ask more questions, take more pictures, even stop for a quick cup of coffee as I did in my Santiago tour. review_text: The tasting we arranged for CLP 20,000 per person consisted of 5 premium wines, three of them being from the Casa Marin label (thus under the supervision of María Luz Marín) whereas the remaining two were of the Litoral label (creations of her son, Felipe). I am mentioning the above because it is a tasting that while not in their webpage, can be arranged as this winery is flexible in that regards, which is a very good thing. Our guide was Fernanda, which sitting us in the wine bar thoroughly educated us on the different wines being served: a Sauvignon Blanc, Sauvignon Gris, Riesling (rare thing in Chile), Pinot Noir and Syrah. Leaving aside the great quality of the wines, a positive thing of the tasting is that Fernanda is very knowledgeable of wine. She is an English teacher graduate (thus making an English tasting possible) and has also taken sommelier courses in Santiago. Hence, this was not a scripted tasting but rather a conversation on the different wines being tasted. Personally I think their Pinot Noir and Riesling are very interesting and full of life and expression, something that most of us as amateur consumers appreciate (in opposition to a somewhat complex wine filled with hints maybe too subtle, as their Syrah probably is). Although you can buy wine after, I am conflicted by the pricing of this vineyard as I think is a bit off market-price (on the higher end of course). Nevertheless, buying wine directly in the store is certainly cheaper than doing it in a supermarket or specialty store anywhere else. We did not do a tour but the grounds seemed pretty and with a feeling as if you were in somebody's home (actually, I think part of the building was María Luz's house). If doing the tasting, we suggest you to request the fire of the wine bar being lit, as it is a pretty cold and gloomy room which can use the extra light and heat.

review_text: With adventure travel comes the possibility of upsets and changes in plans. How an agency cares for their clients in such situations speaks volumes about their integrity. In our situation our trip had to be cancelled due to a severe low pressure system in the Antarctic peninsula region. Leading up to the cancellation it looked like there might be a possibility of getting in with an abbreviated schedule. They offered us that choice with a discount, complete cancellation or shifting to a future trip. When weather conditions did not improve the sent representatives to our hotel in Ushuaia who waited there for three hours awaiting our return from a day trip so they could speak with us and support us personally. They worked with us on options to get to Punta Arenas including air options, bus options and a cruise option through the fjords ... Which was due to depart in ninety minutes. We chose the cruise and the representatives handled calling to confirm availability and worked with a local agent to stay late so we could pay. In addition, they paid for one of our nights in PA AND sent us a transfer on our day of departure. There's nothing they could have done better in such a situation. Very well done!

review_text: We booked the 5 day/4 night W trek back in June via email. Carlos the owner was responsive and professional and answered all our questions. We paid through Pay Pal and waited for our trip to begin in December. Carlos picked us up from the bus station in Puerto Natales. His nephew was visiting so we met him and Victor who would be our guide for the trip. As we headed to our hotel, Carlos and Victor gave us a rundown of what to expect and what to pack. They pointed out some restaurants for us to try as we drove through town and then dropped us off at our hotel. The next day they arrived at the hotel promptly at 2pm. After a beautiful 2 hour drive through the country (mountains, lakes, guanacos), we arrive at the park and immediately see the iconic Towers. We bid farewell to Carlos and the 3 of us start our trek. Everything about the trek was wonderful, there was challenging terrain (moraine and boulders) and easy terrain (forest path). Poles helped a lot. The views were spectacular and ever changing and the weather held up for us for the most part - our last day was extremely windy. Definitely dress in layers, we ended up in short sleeve shorts many days. The Refugios were as expected - bunk beds for 6-8 people, hearty food and lots of Europeans and Aussie/NZ travelers hiking without guides and camping. Victor was a spectacular guide. Due to his frequent trips he knows many employees at the various refugios and he was always able to score us immediate seating at the restaurants, more food and special coffee. He totally took care of us and checked up on trail conditions and weather in advance and explained what to expect each day. He also told great stories and provided us with lots of chocolate. We could not have asked for a better guide. Do not hesitate to book with Extremo Chile - you will not be disappointed. Thank you Carlos and Victor!!
