review_text: If you have a bit of patience and want to save a lot of money! I followed the very good review of 'Corderio' from 16th June 2014'. His instructions were so so simple!! I'm not a big wine fan...infact I rarely drink it..but this tour was amazing as I learnt so much about the different varieties etc. I'm not there for the wine so it's a skewed review I suppose ? MY wife drinks wine and she wanted to go to at least one winery. We decided Undurraga over the other main stream ones. The day before, just book your tour with an English speaking guide : http://www.undurraga.cl/ It's just an email, very simple and quick reply. Getting there allow just over an hour to be safe...we JUST got there 5 min late and it was ok. -Take the train to Estación Central. You will need a Bip! card if you haven't gotten one. Easy to do at the station. The train network is really easy to figure out. -From there walk to the shopping centre and through the shopping centre towards San Borja which is the bus terminal station. It's about a 5 min walk in the really large mall. -Take the no. 75 bus to Talagante. However, ask the bus driver 'Undurraga?' and they will direct you to which no. 75 bus it is (there were 4 when we were there...they must take different routes). -From there about 30-40 min bus ride..try to sit at the front to tell the bus driver..I just had google maps open so I knew when it was coming up. -The bus stop is right outside Undurraga....couldn't be easier. Go in to reception and find your guide. -To come back is a bit of a drama...the bus stop is on the other side but the buses may be full and you may have to wait about 20 min until one comes that's empty. Most people get off after 15 min in so you'll get a seat afterwards. -Drops you off just outside that mall and you can make your way to the station or food court as we did to grab a bite to eat. So the bus costs 1000 Chilean peso's each way and the tour 8000 Chilean pesos...so compared to all those organised tours...you get the same out of this. You just pay for transport the other way. The guide was very informative, we only had 3 people in our tour so could ask a lot of questions. I was amazed at how he talked about the different types of grapes etc which ones do well and why. How they store and create the wines. There is some wine tasting at the end of 3 or 4 wines and you can purchase more at the gift shop. It's nice of them to give you the wine glasses in a nice box to take with you as a gift. By the way, there is no food available there, we were hoping to have lunch there so don't make that same mistake. No restaurant

review_text: La Arena Cove (Caleta La Arena) is located 45 kilometers south of Puerto Montt, Chile. The small town is near the entrance to the Reloncavi Estuary and although the population is small there are several restaurants and a tiny yellow church. Ferries link La Arena with Puelche Cove to continue on Route 7 to the town of Hornopirén. The trip takes about 40 minutes offering wonderful views to the wooded coast and this beautiful fjord. This is a section of Route 7, known as Carretera Austral (Southern Way) which runs about 1,240 kilometers through the Chilean Patagonia. This is a really wonderful place. Make sure to visit if you come to the Puerto Montt area, Los Lagos Region, Chile.

review_text: Santiago seems to be a city where Arts and Culture find ready patronage amongst its residents- and what better way to experience this than the Municipal Theatre of Santiago, which is well known for its historic lineage, having been built in the 19th century, before being almost completely destroyed in a fire, then an earthquake, and then again in a second fire, before being rebuilt and modernised in the 1970s. The theatre retains its old world charm, which in a way, is it’s main problem as well, with narrow passages between rows and tiny seats, even in the more expensive seating areas. But the over hanging box seats, the opulently designed roof, the statues in the hall, with wine being served... they all are an experience to cherish. Tickets are very reasonable- I managed to get the Second row seats for a concert (Amengual/Penderecki/Brahms, with Luis Alberto Latorre of the Chilean Symphony Orchestra on the Piano and conducted by Maximiano Valdes) for about 40 USD, a couple of days in advance. The theatre is easily accessible by metro - the nearest station, Santa Lucia, is about 7-8 mins walk. The acoustics are expectedly wonderful, and I would strongly recommend box seats for a better view. All in all, I had a very entertaining and memorable experience.

review_text: Unfortunately, we never got to try any of this vineyard so I can’t tell you whether the wine is good or bad. But if the wine is anything like their service, it’s terrible. We booked two days in advance and when we got here, we got a guy coming toward us telling us all reservations were full. They couldn’t pull up our reservation and spent a lot of time saying that they would fix in. In the meantime, they refused to let us eat (at 3pm) because the restaurant was full (even though it was clearly not) and the kitchen was too busy (even though everyone had their food already and were leaving). We even sat at the bar where we were ignored the whole time while sitting there... they didn’t even ask if we wanted coffee or a pastry. I’ve never felt so unwelcome at a winery before and even though they told us they got us on a tour (like we should be grateful that they made good on our reservation after losing it??) it was the worst end to our trip to Chile. I would avoid this place at all costs and never recommend anyone I like to visit this place. Go to Kingston, they’re much friendlier, actually remember your reservation, and aren’t trying to make a buck off everyone who comes. Dear Jessica L, We deeply regret that your experience was not what you expected, it was never our intention to make you feel unwelcome and ignored, considering even more that we told you that the tour was going to be done for you at the same time it was originally booked. Also it was never our intention you feel like you should be grateful that we made good on our reservation. Only we wanted respect you original tour booking. We will take the necessary measures so that it does not happen again. Best regards,

review_text: Rather than crossing the river as in the past, the new trail stays on the east side of the river the entire trip. To get around the sections where the river is against the east bank, the trail goes up through the forest in two short sections--these include some big steps, a few steep 2-m vertical sections of slippery sand and mud, and lots of roots. Overall the trail is very easy but farily long; we took 7 hours including some fairly long breaks. The unmarked trailhead is a few right of the restroom in the Ventisquiero Campground and the trail begins with a few stone steps. We enjoyed the views and seeing the raw landscape of the glacier, the icefield above, the trees (coihue_) killed by the 2008 eruption, and the many landslides caused by earthquakes. Recommended.

review_text: This was a very interesting experience - to ride local buses, see the local food market, see an old restored house in the city where the kitchen is and to participate in some cooking, as well as a generous meal with drinks. This was less participatory in some ways than other classes we have taken. The chef had to move through the market quickly to buy food, for example, and was a bit too busy to be 'touring the market' with us. Similarly, with the cooking, the chef did a good deal of the cooking without us seeing or participating, though we did a lot of preparatory chopping of vegetables etc. The dynamics of deciding what dishes to prepare were a bit complex - the guests participating had to come to a consensus among themselves, which was awkward at times. It might be better to have the chef indicate what was being cooked that day, taking into account some alternatives if some guests had food allergies etc. But at the end of the day, this was a very valuable window into Chilean cooking, food preferences and the like. Thanks for your comments. We appreciate the feedback as we are always striving to improve the experience. review_text: My friends and I traveled to Chile for the new year spending the actual New Year in Vina before heading down to Puerto Arena. We caught a 1.30AM flight out of Santiago arriving in the Punta Arenas early in the AM. We had already reserved the 2.5 hour bus ride to Puerto Natales, and basically slept in the lobby with a bunch of other backpackers awaiting the first bus at 7AM. We bought our tickets ahead of time with and it was nice b'c you could pick your seat! We arrived at the bus deport on time and checked into our hostel for the night to prepare for the trek the next morning. It was nice to have the full day, to get equipment we were missing, check tents, get food, and make sure we had enough cash to pay for everything in the park (entrance fees, catamaran). We stayed at erratic rock, and also attended the information session they do every day at 3pm. Def informative and gives you a good background, esp if you hadn't already done your research. They recommended we buy our bus tickets to the park ahead of time, b'c in the crowded season they were selling out. If you miss the early bus (7.30AM it will mess with the rest of your schedule esp if you are doing west to east and also need to catch the catamaran). You can buy them online, or at some of the hostels. Day 1: We arrived at the entrance to the park along with what seemed to be about 50 other buses. It took about and hour and a half to buy entrance tickets, receive map and watch short video. B'c we were hiking west to eat, we had to take another 35-40 min bus ride to the catamaran site. We ended up missing the 11:00 clock catamaran b'c it was too full. We waited about and hour and half and were able to get on the next one. (Please note they don't always run and extra catamaran, but it was crowded so they decided to do so. Otherwise we would have had to wait until 2pm) . You pay the entrance to the catamaran on the boat. When you arrive an Paine Grande you would have option to stay there at the Refugio or continue hiking with your pack. We had reservations to camp at Grey and so we continued up the path. There is a ranger at that station checking your reservations. We had them, so it wasn't an issue, but I think it all depends on the ranger and how you approach the situation. They are def attempting to limit the ppl on the trails though. The hike is supposed to take 3.5 hour, took us about 5 (11KM). We had some ppl with injuries and the weather was not in our favor day 1. We finally arrived at Grey, and being we were one of the last larger groups there, we had to set up camp in the middle of open field. Tip- take your time on trails, but get up early and make it to campsites early. Day 2: We slept in a bit and headed out on the trail around 11.30AM. (There are some trails to go up and get a close view of Glacier Grey, if you have time some of the pictures I saw were incredible). Going back it took about 4 hours with stops for us to arrive back at Refugio Grey. We took a short break there as they have a place to purchase food and a beer if you like. We parted ways with some of our friends that had injuries. They took the last catamaran back to wait for us at Camp Central. The rest of the group continued on the trek to Camp Italiano. It was about another 7.5 KM and 2 1/2 hrs but much easier than the hike to and from Camp Grey. The scenery is beautiful and even taking our time we were able to make it in just short of 3 hours. Camp Italiano is a very primitive camping site. There is no running water, electricity, or amenities other than a place to put your tent. They have a small shelter where you can cook and a river right next to the campsite for water source. It is def chilly in the campsite as you are so close to water and hidden under a bed of trees, and the ground can be a bit wet. If you can fit a tarp in your tent bag, its a good thing to have. Again we arrived late and there wasn't much space. We ended up behind the latrines, and yes it smelled! If you arrive at camp early enough you can take a short hike over to Domo Frances and get hot food and possibly sneak in a shower! Day 2: We got up early as we took an hour hike up to see Glacier Frances. The hike is uphill the whole way, but with out the packs not too bad. We got back and started off on what was to be the longest day, hiking to Camp Central to meet the rest of our group. It would have been about 16 1/2 KM and about 7 hours with no stops. Unfortunately we didn't make it. We stopped at Cuernos (2 1/2 hrs) to get a bite to eat and a beer. We enjoyed it so much we spent a little too much time there and the 4 1/2 hours we had ahead of us seemed to be too much. Fortunately for us, the front desk was very helpful, and they quickly changed our reservations from Central to Cuernos for the night! Hot showers, food and a shelter to cook in was a great treat after Italiano. We camped on the floor vs a platform as those were all taken, however it ended up working in our favor. There was a terrible wind storm out there and ppl who had no barrier to their tents (aka trees/ forest) and were sitting on platform got their tents shredded to pieces. Many ppl ended up sleeping in the cooking area that night and were left without a tent. Day4: We got up early and started our 4 1/2 hour hike to central. The scenery was stunning and although there were some steep hills, the majority of the hike wasn't too bad. We made it in about 5 hours and set up camp with out friends who were patiently awaiting our arrival. We treated ourselves to a delicious meal at the hotel and some drinks! We then decided to relax for a couple of hours before we started our night hike to the Torres. (Originally we would have spent 1 night in Central, then hiked up to the Torres campsite with our packs to see the sunrise and be only an hour away. However b'c of our stop at Cuernos, we chose instead to stay another night at central, leave our packs and hike up at night to get to Torres by sunrise). We started our hike around 10.30 to ensure we had more than enough time to get up there. The hike takes about 4.5hrs, but in the pitch black dark, you never know! Leaving our bags behind ended up being a blessing as much of the trail is straight up hill. We brought some food layers and our sleeping bag, which was much lighter. The trail is marked fairly well, although we did loose it a couple of times and had to backtrack. Just make sure you are always looking for the trail markers, esp at night. Once we finally reached the Torres and our body temperatures cooled down, it was freezing! Sleeping bag was a savoir up there waiting for the sun to rise. In the end it was all worth it! Breathtaking! We then hiked the 4.5 hrs back to Central. We arrived to camp around 10 AM, 12 hours later! It was enough time to shower, eat and get on the 2'oclock bus out of the park. Overall it was a fantastic experience and can def test your limits at times. Just go with an open mind and realize things don't have to go exactly as planned and still be a great experience. On the way to the mountains we stopped at a vineyard for some tasting and although this was a memorable part of the excursion the timing of it ie. wine tasting at 10am was a new experience. On the way back, we stopped at a small farm to see and feed a few old llamas but this was rather disappointing as it felt more like a short stop thrown in en route. Organisationally, I think this could be improved upon and perhaps wine tasting on the way back would be a better time and something a bit more interesting to replace the llama 'farm'. In any case, both the guide Hector and Jorge the driver were very good at their respective jobs. Review of: Inca Lagoon in Andes Mountain Range - Visit Local Vineyard with Tasting included We thank your feedback. According to the winery : The reason we do not visit the winery in the afternoon : 1- San Esteban is hotter than Santiago in summer season. Meaning we would not enjoy it as much as we do in the morning. With shade and nice weather. Afternoon can not be in the park of how hot it is. 2- Afternoon winery receives more people. And its nice to have the winery park to ourselves. And as you where able to notice we had the park to ourselves. And privileged of an excellent atmosphere . All our stops have a statistic and reasonable reason about the times or moment. And this makes us enjoy a wine tasting with an excellent weather. According to the llamas. * We appreciate to be able to feed and interact with the llamas. And yes there are young and old ones. * It is also a stop for restrooms before we go back to the city 1 hour and 30 minutes. And we are grateful that these local people have llamas and we are able to interact with them. We are very glad as a team that you enjoyed of the majestic of the andes. And we thank you for sharing your personal feedback. regards Isto e Chile Team
title: A nice day out.

review_text: An excellent way to get to Puerto Williams. 32 hours of mostly calm seas in channels between islands. The meals were ok, you may want to bring snacks if you're a vegan I think the vegetarians were ok. Passed numerous glaciers & saw a host of bird life. When we arrived in Puerto Williams we were able to stay & sleep on the boat until 7:30 or so.

review_text: This was one of the hardest but best things I have ever done. The road was shut due to a landslide so we hiked a different area. You need to have a good level of fitness but the reward of the views, mountainous scenery and the glaciers themselves is just amazing. Our guide Niko was outstanding and as well as having such great knowledge of the area he made the day fun and gave us a wonderful surprise at the end which finished our day perfectly. Andoandes the tour company were efficient and sent wattsap messages the day before confirming pick ups and all were on time. I would highly recommend this trip. Review of: Glacier Hike at El Morado Glacier, from Santiago

review_text: My wife and I did the free walking tour with Jorge McKenzie in mid-December 2018. We try and do these walking tours in most of the cities we visit. They are usually great, but occasionally not so great. Anyway, this was one of the best we've done - a very memorable tour. Jorge was highly knowledgeable about a wide range of things - the history of Valparaiso, the various murals and public artworks we saw on the tour, the buildings of historical interest and much more. He also had some keen insights into Chilean culture, history and politics. Jorge was very entertaining and was a natural for the role. He has excellent English and if memory serves he had a Scottish grandfather. On the tour our group of 10 or 12, accompanied by our pack of street dogs, covered the highlights of Valparaiso and got a good overview of the place and its history. I'd encourage anyone who visits this area to do the tour.
title: Great tour with Jorge

review_text: On your cruise to Antarctica you have to pass (Cabo de Hornos) Cape Horn. This place looked very desolate and I was glad that we only went past it and didn't stop. All the passengers received a certificate to say that we had indeed passed by the cape.

review_text: It's one of those things you "have to do" when in Chile but... We did some kind of an abbreviated version of the winery your, and it felt rushed. We got to sample three wines and they were truly delicious. Then had some empanadas to share at the restaurant because, even though we wanted to stay for lunch, we were about 20-30 minutes too early and they were not about to move the lunch service by one minute... The prices at the gift shop were surprisingly fair. Some items were actually on the cheap side! In terms of winery tours, I have seen better, although this is the only one I have done in Chile. There are many other things to do and many other vineyards, but CyT is a classic. Maybe we should have done the "unabbreviated" tour...

review_text: I guess this is the tallest building in Santiago, a mark of the modern city and visible from everywhere, provided that there is no smog, but good luck with that. I was not impressed.
title: The Tallest Building

review_text: This cooking class with Connie was amaze balls. It started at the central fish markets and crossed over to the fruit market. We also got to see other areas such as where you can purchase clay bowls that you later cook with. We are going back to get some of these! This goes for about 2 hours. Connie paid for us to get a taxi to where the workshop is held, after shouting a delicious homemade sopapilla from a stall at the markets. Connie was extremely hands on with us as we got to chop and prepare different elements of each dish. The Pisco Sour was delicious and will definitely be made back home. We had a local white and red wine from Chile which Connie explained in detail. The prawn ceviche was great, as was making and consuming the beef empanadas. A definite winter food for back home. We then finished with red wine soaked pears with anglaise. For someone who never eats pears it was a pleasant surprise and something I'll eat again. We both loved this class - Connie adapted the menu for my partner who is vegetarian and who also loved this class and thought it very worthy of the cost. Cheers Connie!
title: A must do cooking class

review_text: Wow! Entertaining, beautiful, educational, and outdoors! This is a terrific tour for interpreting and understanding one of the essential elements of Valparaiso -- street art. Whether you already know a little or a lot, you'll walk away from this memorable tour with an appreciation for street art, murals, tagging, graffiti (letters and art), and you'll see nooks & crannies of the city that you otherwise wouldn't. Ask for Sebastian and his trusty street-dog, Linda. Lots of fun, so much knowledge, and a local's flair for adding back stories, exploring disused water towers, checking out colorful cobblestone ways .... would do again!

We went there after 2pm, as the entrance fee is relatively high and we get a discount (9000CLP instead of 15000CLP) after 2pm ( note that the place closes around 5.15pm. I would also recommend you not to go there on week-ends, as it will probably be very crowded. Lockers are available, if you take a locker with you!

review_text: The perfect activity our last day in PA before heading to the airport. We were greeted by the Park Steward when we arrived who described the different hikes, lengths and how long they would take. There is a big map displayed outside the office you can take a photo or scan a code. In a separate window you pay a fee and log-in your name. When your hike is over, you should log-out as well. Restrooms available on-site and plenty of car parking. Everything was very organized. I wouldn’t say the trails are gorgeous, more like a dark thick forest with lots of mossy trees and good shelter from the wind. Each trail leads out to a rewarding vista (mirador) with beautiful and expansive views of the city, river and straights. We saw a hawk with prey and some song birds.
title: Nice place to get out of the city and into nature

review_text: We went to El Colorado on 18/07/2014 with the Guide Belen M. I want to congratulate the touristik for the punctuality and the professional Guide Belen M super attentive, friendly and organized even if it were not for her probably our experience would have been quite difficult for several reasons that I explain below. First of all, the rental of clothes is absurdly chaotic! An extreme mess, I know we went on a holiday period where the number of people in these places are bigger but besides the lack of education of many tourists there is an extreme disorder in the place (and although the employees have a lot of good will to help us disorder is very big), another point of great despair was when arriving in El Colorado to pick up the boots and ski - if in the place of clothing rental was a mess in this place the mess was much bigger - almost a despair! There is no guidance on the size of ski boots (because if you never skied, as our family had not skied do not think that if you pants 32 your ski boots will be 32), the place is small to carry a large number of tourists without experience, few attendees to “adjust” the ski, not to mention the lockers we rented and we could not use because they had no more locks! (if it wasn’t for Belen we ⁇ ’t have got the refund). We arrived around 10:00/20:15 in El Colorado and we went to enjoy the day was already over 12:30. I saw many people missing the ski lessons (already purchased previously for this lack of organization of the site). I thank our Guide Belen for the sympathy, calmness and security in helping us (even because we were with a child). review_text: This was a great way to do the W trek. Ricci and the team were fantastic - they took all the hassle out of organising the trip. Transport in and out of the park as well as accommodation in refugios and campsites during the trek was all sorted. Ricci was very knowledgable about the park and the region - you can really see his passion for the place. Having now been there, I can understand why! As for the trek itself, Torres Del Paine is probably the most spectacular place I've ever been, and I've done a bit of trekking in the past! Can't emphasise enough how much I enjoyed it. Thank you Bryce for your nice review! So glad to know you had a great time in beautiful Patagonia Hope to see you soon sometime! Kind regards from all the ChileTour team
title: Fantastic, hassle-free W trek experience

review_text: Basically it's one of those places where you have little expectation, as if it will be some guy's garden shed, but in reality turns out to be a gem of a place. There were only a half dozen other people but the presentation was fantastic, from what meteorites are, exactly how they are formed, different types. The most interesting part was the link to possible life. The tour is an audio guide and you walk from one section to the other when prompted by the guide. The last part is interesting as one of the people at the museum will come and explain some of the interesting properties of the meteorite, where you get to touch them and test their magnetism. needs a little better signage from town but once you see it it's obvious, a little gem, especially at 3,500 pesos
title: Surpassed all expectation

review_text: The place was amazing. Both the guide and the driver were super attentive and great. At the lagoons they gave us our time and explained curiosities and information about the area. Since we started early, they gave us breakfast in a beautiful place and everything was delicious. Great excursion. Review of: Tour to the Hidden Lagoons of Baltinache
title: Great experience and fantastic guides!!

review_text: We went with Miguel along a trail he personally discovered and it was just amazing. It was a great combination of hiking, zip-lining, rappelling, jumping in the water. The guides were extremely nice and fun. We also had some snacks and juices at the end. We felt very safe the entire time thanks to the very experienced staff. The volcanic scenery was fantastic - black rocks, clear water and nice vegetation. Must do in Pucon!! Thank you very much guys, it was an awesome trip with wonderfull people !! Thanks for the advices and the good vibe.. Miguel & Thibau
title: AMAZING experience

review_text: I had a great day at La Peninsula! I did the horseback riding, and as it was a first for me, I was a bit nervous. But the guides were very professional, and the horses calm and friendly, so I was quickly relaxed and could enjoy the amazing nature. After enjoying a really nice lamb barbecue, we got to see a sheep shearing, and learned about the different qualities of the wool. The crew around La Peninsulva was very friendly, professional, and they shared their knowlegde about the culture and history of the area, which was very interesting. Such a great experience, a favorite in Patagonia!
title: Beautiful nature, lovely animals and very professional crew

review_text: I loved the tour!!! Very handsome! Catalina Reyes was very attentive and kind. We took a lot of pictures. It was worth the trip. Review of: Cable Car, Funicular and Sightseeing Bus in Santiago two days Olá, muito obrigado por deixar seus comentários. Ficamos felizes em saber que você gostou. Nossos melhores cumprimentos!
title: It was wonderful to meet Santiago!

review_text: We are a small group of 4 Texans, that just came back from a 21 day South America cruise, and stayed 2 extra days in Santiago. I found IloveChile Tours by researching online and reading reviews prior to our arrival. We booked 2 tours, back to back days and had an amazing experience. The Andes Mountains, and Wine Tasting in Casablanca. Both were equally as enjoyable and our experience was made to feel personal and customized to our schedules. The last day we had the tour end at the airport, since we had late flights back to the States. The vehicle was very roomy, and fit our 8 pieces of luggage, plus we had plenty of extra space left. Sebastian was our guide and he also had a driver, which was an extra plus. He was able to focus on the actual tour and our questions without having to worry about driving. I highly recommend IloveChile tour company and would say its one of the best we have used for tour guides. We are all big travelers, so thats a huge compliment. If your looking for a tour thats not only informative, but tailored to meet your expectations, this is a perfect choice. Review of: Valparaiso Day Trip from Santiago - Private Tour for Small Groups
title: IloveChile tour for Texans

review_text: My 20 year old son and I planned a trip for 3 days to trek and see as much of the Puerto Varas area as we could in our time allotment. Andres was easy to work with and gave us options before we came down. He greeted us at the airport and handled everything for us until our departure tickets were issued. Our trip was in the winter so changes had to be made as the weather conditions wouldn't allow all that we planned but he came up with alternate tours for us and we had a great time. Andres is very professional and easy to work. He can also help you plan flights and treks and tours in other areas of Chile also. We hope to use him in the future on a return trip. I would highly recommend him.
title: Three day tour and trek in Puerto Varas area

review_text: My mom and I had an amazing day visiting unesco site Torres del Paine, with Jhon Pineda as our tour guide and Alex Rodriguez as our driver! they showed us highlights of the park, spotted animals including guanaco, condors, and a puma along the way and left us wanting to come back for additional visits. Couldnt have asked for a better experience with this team. Timely, patient and knowledgeable providing geographical and historical info. Thank you!!!!
title: Breathtaking panoramic views and wonderful guides

review_text: Entrance is via basement. Cost $15000 per adult. Choose a day that is smog free. The 62 floor is a short lift ride (7 m/ second) . The view is behind glass though is open at the roof. There is no wind! Telescopes cost. Binoculars are useful. View the snowy mountains and the city layout. A good orientation point. Toilets are at the top. Exit via lift to the shopping mall 5th floor . Take the escalators down. Cafes +++ on the 5th floor and a bit of a souvenir shop. There was no queue when we went up at 11 am. The time for this activity is about 1 hour .
title: 62 floors offer a view

review_text: You can hike or take the cable car to the top of San Cristobal for a spectacular view of the city in all directions. You can see the Andes in the background. The statue of the Virgin Mary is at the very top where many visitors stop to pray or pay respect. There are benches among flowers & shrubbery where you can take a break and enjoy the views and the peacefulness in this special place.
title: Best view of Santiago

review_text: An excellent agency, with great guides, punctual, very organized, with a surprising food service on all tours, both breakfast, lunch and cocktails depending on tour times, all prepared with great care and care. The bathrobe at the end of the bathing lake tours makes all the difference! We booked 7 tours with the FlaviaBia Team from Brazil, two weeks in advance, so that we didn't have any worries about wasting time choosing agencies in San Pedro do Atacama. All tours were great! The prices may not have been the best, but the quality and difference of the food served and the services provided made the difference, making the investment worth it and making the tour a memorable experience.
title: An incredible and memorable experience in Atacama!

review_text: This was a fantastic tour of the Maipo Valley! Our tour guide Nacho was super friendly, personable, and energetic. Although, at each winery, Nacho left us with a local guide which was a great way to learn a lot of information about each winery. Overall, a great choice for a day away from Santiago. Review of: Maipo Valley Wine Tour with 4 vineyards from Santiago. Our guides in this tour are there to ensure you arrive at each spot understanding about the context of the place. All while having fun and learning in between. We're glad you had a great time. Thank you for your review.
title: Fun and variety filled tour!

review_text: We visited this mainly because of the quirky architecture but it houses an interesting art collection. Really cheap entry fee for over 65s too!
title: Fantastic architecture

review_text: Gregory was excellent with us! The attractions were well presented, a good companion! Amazing experiences... Thank you!
title: Amazing

review_text: It's interesting to visit a large mall like this at Christmas time. Hey six-story mall with Christmas decorations reminding one of home, Christmas songs in Spanish, and families shopping together allows one to feel at home. Stores from all over the world give a shopper every option that's needed. A great place to visit and to complete any shopping for gifts to take home.
title: Felix Navidad and shop til you drop

review_text: I thought that the Spanish audio tour was excellent. It might be a little long, depending on your interest level. At the risk of making myself sound stupid, I didn't notice the little numbers next to the places until 4 or 5, so look out for that. I took off a point because the Sala de la Memoria was locked. At first, I was a little put off by the public transportation issue, but the bus was actually pretty easy. I got off too soon, so make sure that you go past the Sodimac Homecenter and Sagrado Corazon school. If you take the D09 back, it ends pretty close to Manual Montt and Pedro de Valdivia metro in Providencia (where lots of tourists are probably staying). It is probably faster to get back on the blue line, but the neighborhoods you go through are interesting.
title: Interesting afternoon

review_text: Puka Rumi is the best tour agency. Attentive, helpful guides with a lot of information to share. Congratulations to the guides Francisco, Larya, Lolo and Giulia. Ahh… the meals and snacks are always delicious! Review of: Half Day Tour to Geysers del Tatio
title: Geyser el tatio, Valle del la Luna, Piedras Rojas and antiplanicas. Incredible beauty of the desert

review_text: Eugene was a friendly, thoughtful and very knowledgeable tour guide and host. He gave us a good understanding of the history of the country, and was very proud of the classic architecture that remains standing in spite of several serious earthquakes! Good value for the cost, and you feel like the time has flown when you are finished and standing in Bellavista ready for lunch - for which he made an excellent suggestion. Review of: A Fabulous Walking tour by the Old Santiago of Chile -small group
title: Essential Tour

review_text: This was an experience we never been throug, totally amazing with super good guides, u could see thousands of stars and even planets with ur own eyes, we got an amazing pic of the moon throug telescope.
title: Stars is the night

review_text: This hill offers a nice view of the town but not much else to do there. The tickets to go uphill with the cable car are overpriced (like in every other place in the world that has a cable car). If you like biking there's a nice road to venture up and down hill
title: Good view of part of the city, but not much to do there.

review_text: An amazing experience riding the Carretera Austral. Claudia and the team provide an exceptional service. Cicloaustral helped me at very short notice and were always available with information before and during my ride. You meet many cyclists and friends along the way. Perhaps the best time I had in 7 months in South America.
title: The ultimate Patagonian experience.

review_text: Viña Veramonte, Viña del Mar and Valpariso were a great ride, specilme te for the human quality of Jorge Garrido; his professionalism as a guide, the knowledge he has of the environment in all areas, the equanimity in dealing with passengers make the ride live as a family. In Colombian expression, Jorge is “people who put the soul in him”. Review of: From Santiago: Valparaíso, Viña del Mar and Neruda Museum Muchas gracias por compartir su experiencia junto a nosotros.
title: Valparaiso and Viña del Mar

review_text: Having previously considered hiring a car to take myself on a day trip to Valparaiso and Viña de Mar, I'm so pleased I decided instead to jump onto this tour. Pablo was a charming, generous and knowledgeable tour guide, and we felt very safe with him and with Osvaldo behind the wheel. Really great communication around pick ups and what was happening when, and certainly can't complain about the door to door service. Recommended! Review of: Valparaiso Port and Vina del Mar Full-Day Tour from Santiago There are many options, you can take to Valparaiso. With us you will have the chance to meet other people and enjoy learning about its history culture and more. Thank you for your review.
title: This is how you do Valparaiso in a day

review_text: beautiful nature, unspoilt nature, accommodations are well organized, 'well maintained' nature reserve, worthwhile
title: much worthwhile !

review_text: Portillo is the most wonderful thing I have ever known and the trip became even more special with guides Yuri and Álvaro. The tour was amazing, very fun and full of valuable information. Unforgettable! I recommend demaisssss!
title: INCREDIBLE ⁇

review_text: I recommend 100% to the agency, they always were and answered each of a few questions, in addition to providing solutions to certain situations. In particular, I would like to highlight the work of our tour guide Jonathan, who was responsible for making us live a unique experience. With great knowledge of the place, a great disposition and an always friendly attitude, he also made sure we were comfortable , concerned for our well-being so that we enjoyed every moment. I would definitely recommend the agency and especially Jonathan as a guide. They made our experience unforgettable.
title: Excellent service

review_text: I do not recommend this trip. We arrived at the company office at 6:00 AM as requested. People arrived until 8:00 when we finally departed on our bus to a location 45 minutes out of town, where we entered our small catamaran to travel the 45 minutes to Isla Magdalena, ostensibly to see penguins in their "natural" habitat. The small island was comprised of a roped path around the island where we observed hundreds of penguins cowering in their holes, probably as frightened from our presence as from the blowing wind and rain. After 45 minutes of admittedly interesting observation of these molting, dung covered creatures, we returned to our boat for a twenty minute failed effort to reach another island to observe sea lions (wind and waves too rough), and a 40 minute ride back to the shore, where we caught our bus back to town. So...if you want to ride in a bus and boat for three hours to see a few penguins for 45 minutes, hop aboard. Otherwise, save your money for a trip to Antarctica, or take your grandchild to see "frozen" again.
title: Penguins: Not the "Frozen" variety

review_text: So many wonderful things about this wine tour -- flawless process and fantastic experience. Cata was a fun guide and our driver was great. The vineyards were beautiful-- from the small scale family run winery to the large, big business winery. Zinfandel restaurant was a lovely lunch stop and we met such fun people! Also, as a person who suffers dietary restrictions ( celiac disease) this tour was very accommodating and safe for me. Highly recommend. Review of: Maipo Valley Wine Tour with 4 vineyards from Santiago.
title: Wine Wow!

review_text: Pick up was fine and on time. Guide was very good with knowledge. Torres del Peine is a must-see. There was little walking so this is good for everyone. I thought Molodon cave was a bit disappointing. Overall very good. Review of: Full-Day Tour to Torres del Paine National Park from Puerto Natales(First Class)
title: A must-see from P. Natales

review_text: Today (18/11/24) I eminha family we traveled with the guide Johana, and it was great. We visited the main sights of Valparaiso and Vina del Mar, we had information about the places and we received all the necessary assistance. I recommend here in Santiago, Chile.
title: Tour to Valparaiso and Viña del Mar

review_text: Roman offered us a short tour to the ocean, to a little-known beach. The beach was adjacent to a strip of sand with dunes. There was an opportunity to ride bikes. I especially want to mention the excellent barbecue. Thank you very much for the review!
title: Small trip to the ocean

review_text: This was a blast. We really felt like this tour gave us a feel for Santiago that we would have never gotten on our own. Joanna and Pyrate were excellent guides, and they were watching out for the group constantly. Outstanding English made Joanna easy to follow. She helped us to more understand the different worlds that exist in the city, and some of the differences and similarities. It was a pretty easy ride if you ride a bike every now and then. Review of: Santiago Markets Small Group Bike Tour
title: Fun,educational and you get a little exercise along the way.

review_text: The tour was ok but not worth the money. The tour had the potential to be great but we stopped at 2 places only. The 1st place we stopped at was a candy store which was great but we all wanted to purchase Calafate Tea but they ran out. The tour was $110 per person which also included a tour of the area. I felt the guide couldn't wait to get rid of us.
title: Gastronomic Tour

review_text: The closeness and quality of care at this agency make a difference. Plus good prices and various alternatives! I recommend 100%
title: Highly recommended!

review_text: Very good guidance and explanations. Very friendly and pleasant handling. Always attentive and very good recommendations. Review of: A Fabulous Walking tour by the Old Santiago of Chile -small group
title: Great.

review_text: Unique lovely scenery that often has an extraterrestrial feel, living up to the place's name. I found the Valle del Arcoiris and the Geysers del Tatio to be more interesting, but this is still well worth seeing.
title: Extraterrestrial feel, just like its name

review_text: We really had a great time in Punta Arenas ... Kayaking and hiking. Both activities were really 5 stars. They were fun and met all expectations. What was challenging was that we were actually booked on two separate tours ... With different guides ... And didn't know it! This lack of understanding ... And a slightly Awkward hand off between tours was a bit rough. That being said ... As long as you fully understand the logistics ... I highly recommend the kayaking and trekking. We had a blast and the guides were exceptional!
title: Great experiences

review_text: Awesome excursion. The park is absolutely stunning, everything I expected from Patagonia. Our guide, Juan, and driver were professional and knowledgeable and I really enjoyed the whole day. I’ll note, it’s a long day with an early start (530-6A) and late (745P) arrival back in Punta Arenas. Plan to take some food to munch at the camping area at Lake Pehoe. I took an apple, some trail mix, a protein bar and water, which was perfect for me. Pro tip: look for the bench (contemplation spot) on the overlook along some trails just outside the campground, it’s might just be the most perfect spot for lunch on the planet. Review of: Full Day Torres del Paine Dear passenger We are so glad you enjoyed the tour Thank you for sharing!! Best
title: Great day trip, absolutely beautiful country

review_text: Pretty interesting with a nice guide called Alvaro and his "wolve pack". Pretty good english and if you like street art you absolutely should do it.
title: Gracias Alvaro

review_text: This delightful boutique vineyard is pushing the boundaries to take organic wine to the next level. Patricio and his family are passionate about their wine and telling their story. The setting is beautiful and the restaurant serves delicious local fare. You leave with some of Las Araucarias forever in your heart
title: Passionate and innovative wine maker tells his story in beautiful setting

review_text: It was a nice experience. Staff and drivers are very friendly. We were unlucky to have bad weather and recommend to avoid it when raining or windy (we were super cold upstairs and there was no place downstairs). The information from the tour was not that interesting. Review of: Tourist bus around Santiago for a day Dear traveler, we are glad to hear that you had a pleasant experience, we are sorry to hear that your experience was affected by the bad weather, thank you very much for sharing your opinion with us. We look forward to your next visit!
title: Nice experience but avoid if cold/rain

review_text: This is a 4AM wakeup in San Pedro de Atacama, with about 2 hours driving to get to the park. The last 10km is "worse" than the mostly-paved initial route. There are toilet facilities at the park entrance, so you and a hundred others will be vying for a "seat". Actually, the line moves fairly well, but you may need to bring toilet paper. (Better than Cuba where you have to bring paper AND toilet seat!) The geysers are beautiful in the early morning light, and there is quite a variety in their appearance. Our organizer brought breakfast!
title: An early morning, as the geysers quit after sunrise

review_text: The tour was top, I went with my mother and our guide matias was always attentive and very friendly. Our driver rodrigo made our trip very comfortable. I would definitely take a tour with them again Review of: Valparaiso Port and Vina del Mar Full-Day Tour from Santiago Una muy buena opcion para hacer estando en Santiago. Como mencionas tomando el tour con nuestra empresa tendras los mejores guías y conductores. Nos alegra que lo pasaron bien. Gracias por su review.
title: Pleasant visiting experience in santiago

review_text: The place is wonderful, an unparalleled natural beauty, preserved and enchanting! We loved our guide John and driver Alex, they made our experience even more unique! Review of: Full Day Torres Del Paine
title: Amazing place!

review_text: The tour is very interesting, you learn and have a good time. The attention of the spectacular guide gives a very close seal to the tour. Exquisite wines. A complete experience, highly recommended 🙌 Muchísimas gracias!! que bueno que hayan tenido una linda experiencia.
title: Excellent experience

review_text: Highly recommended! After a bad experience with another agency we met Ronald and thanks to him we were able to enjoy the rest of the tours with great attention from the guides Luna and Nata and the drivers Migue and Marcos. We also tour with them to the salt flat of Uyuni, with Gualberto as guide and driver and very good experience as well. Thanks for everything!! Review of: Multi-Day Tour in San Pedro de Atacama with Pickup
title: Highly recommended for all tours in San Pedro de Atacama

review_text: Excellent walk, the chauffeur and guide loving and very responsible. We visited several places that we did not think, llamas, panoramic views besides the lagoon Review of: Inca Lagoon in Andes Mountain Range - Visit Local Vineyard with Tasting included
title: Excellent

review_text: Pick up time (6:40am) was informed the night before by e-mail and confirmed by WhatsApp on the day of the visit before arrival. There were already a few visitors inside the van and others to be picked yet. Driver (Miguel) and guide (Salvador) were nice and the visit was awesome. First stop was on a restaurant for breakfast, 2nd on tunnel, 3rd on a viewpoint, 4th on a camp with small trade and toillets and last one at the dam. After time for photos, there was a picnic with chips, cheese, water, juice and wine. Returning to Santiago there was a stop in San Jose del Maipo for lunch. Drop-off at the hotel was around 5:00pm. I’d recommend this day-trip. However, stops for breakfast and lunch could be shorter: they last around 1 hour each and most of the people were idle during them. There could be at least two types of wine for tasting, as Chile produces amazing wines. Review of: Small-Group Cajón del Maipo Full-Day Tour and Picnic Thank you for your comment, we're glad you had a good time with our staff and in general with us, thank you for recommending you and glad you got to taste Chilean wine, it's really good! Don't hesitate to contact us the next time you or your friends want to come to live another gratifying experience in one of our tours. Best regards, MTO Tour Team
title: Amazing landscape and professional tour

review_text: A lot of new construction in and around the building went in to place to get it up to speed. Wow! Excellent job - great events, nice area all around with cafe's and places to park right downtown. When coming to Santiago - book a concert - quaint, but worth the live music.
title: Refurbished and to be enjoyed

review_text: We did the tour to the lagoon with no hike. Communication prior to the tour was poor leaving questions unanswered or mis-information. We were e-mailed a carbon copy Pick up (generic time 7 -7:30) but were picked up right a 7. The people at the next pick up were told 7:15 as were given a personal reply and were picked up at this time. Failing grade for the main office. Pick up of all passengers at various hotels was quick and efficent. Two bano stops on route and a stop at San Jose Plaza de Armas. A few photo stops on route. Our guide Andres was excellent and highly informative. Our driver was respectful and polite. Once at the lagoon at 12 we were given 1 hour to do as we pleased. A box lunch with wine, juice or water was provided. We took our lunch to the edge of the lagoon. Dress warm as it is cool there with plenty of wind. If you wish to walk to the water wear hiking boots. Long drive for 1 hour of lagoon scenery but this is an individual choice. We felt it was worth the drive for the beauty of the lagoon, fresh air and a view of the rural area around Santiago. Andres is a great guide! We are glad you had a good experience in the Andes!. And we work daily to improve everything we do. So your review its always well taken. Thanks!
title: Great tour but poor prior communication.

review_text: Adeline spent time with us to go through the whole route in detail with a map before we rented the bikes, she was so helpful, and then gave us tips on the rest of our Chile travels as well. She even shared her contact details in case we had any further questions. This is the most welcoming bike shop I’ve ever encountered 😁 plus a bonus that they speak English and French, it is not so common in the region. We saw some beautiful views and had cool stops along the route, would definitely recommend for anyone visiting Elqui Valley
title: Most helpful and friendly bike rental shop!

review_text: We were there with our young kids and they loved it. You get to see 3 ships right at the beach. I definitely recommend it for families. For adults its nice too but you'll probably won't be there longer than 20min 😉 Thank you for visiting us, we are glad you enjoyed the boat replicas. Thank you very much for writing
title: Kids loved it!

review_text: A large covered collection of stalls with a variety of handcrafts, lots of chunky knits, wooden and woven items fair amount of leather goods. Stall holders don't seem to do hard sell which is refreshing.
title: Extensive

review_text: Excellent Mario. Punctual, friendly and transmits the knowledge very well!!!. He looks great lover of nature, as soon as he can he tells us everything about birds and vegetation, and especially his explanations of the Maipo Valley and the Gypsum reservoir. Thank you. Review of: Small-Group Cajón del Maipo Full-Day Tour and Picnic Gracias por compartir tu experiencia! Nos alegra mucho saber que disfrutaste de tu excursión junto a Mario, quien está lleno de conocimientos y es excelente en su trabajo, le transmitiremos tus amables comentarios. No dudes en contactarnos la próxima vez que vengas, estaremos encantados de recibirte, MTO Tour Team
title: Fantastic Maipo and Gypsum Reservoir

review_text: I visited the lakes in August, 2014 and the scenery there was great. Though they are located high at 4200 meters high, I took a pill for altitude sickness before I went there and I was fine. The guide told us drinking water also helps as it contains oxygen. I went with the travel agency called Vive Atacama, with the very friendly driver Freddy and and the guide Jimena, who loves nature and is really passionate in her work. She gave detailed introduction about the places in the minibus before we got there, and left us some quiet time to enjoy the view. On the way there the guide spotted a fox. Some vicugnas were drinking water by the lake. It is a serene place and I really want to stay there longer.
title: A must-see in Atacama.

review_text: Just based on the location it was obvious that this was going to be fairly basic but we were pleasantly surprised at how clean it was. Our room was spotless – very small but absolutely fine. Hot water as a bit limited on the second morning but the pressure was good. Breakfast was pretty basic but we were nervous about eating and drinking up in this area as it is so easy to get aa bug or something so we were happy with ‘basic’ and made out own tea and coffee from bottles water. I would stay here again.
title: Quite adequate

review_text: Excellent experience! I have never seen such big water and was so impressed with the skill of the guides and ability to keep everyone feeling safe and having fun at the same time. They have very complete safety checks and are committed to creating an exciting trip for their guests. I took two trips down with Niko. He had great charm and was cheeky and joking with everyone while maintaining quality commands. I took one trip with Gabriel and felt the same he was super helpful with his clients and felt safe and had lots of fun. I should also mention that they are accommodating with both English and Spanish commands and directions. After the trip we went to their base camp cabin and had pasta with curry sauce and veggies which definitely hit the spot. Overall such a a great crew and company highly recommend.
title: Fun exciting safe

review_text: I was first a bit sceptical as the winery seemed very close to the city center of Santiago. But I am glad we still went. The Cousiño winery has a great history to tell and was founded when Santiago was still a bit smaller. Nowadays they own another vineyard outside the city. Our tour was in English and our guide even spoke some German. He was very knowledgeable and did a great job on explaining the history of the vineyard as well as talking about the process of making wine in the past and in our time. At the end you get to taste some wine and we could even take the wine glass with the Cousiño emblem home, a great gift. It's easy to reach. For us it was a 40 minute metro ride and then a 3 minute UBER/taxi ride (or you take a bus it you walk 30 minutes). We totally recommend it!
title: Great winery tour

review_text: We took the green tour in the residential neighbourhoods of Santiago. We were also lucky to be in a small group. This tour will help you to understand how the Santiago people lives and also a glimps of how the coup and the following era of dictatorship had its impact on the people of Santiago. Thanks Fran for a great tour!
title: Deeper into the Chilian spirit

review_text: I arrived in Santiago on the 10th of May and by the 11th I was ready to see the sites. I had come with a group and had no set plans for our trip. I found this free walking tour and suggested it to the group, not many were interested because the were scared off by the 4hr part! So I ended up attending by myself. The title of this tour was perfect FREE WALKING TOUR! It was awesome, and completely free (tipping the tour guide is the only expense) I learned so much about Chile and the city of Santiago. Yes we walked for 4hrs. But it was always a stroll and never rushed, we had a break in the middle to sit and eat/have coffee. It definitely did not feel like 4hrs. Our tour guide was exceptional, Franco was articulate and full of wonderful facts about the city, the history and the culture. I left Santiago with this being the highlight of my trip, I made a new friend on the tour and all of my coworkers were jealous of my beautiful pictures. I highly recommend this tour to anyone wanting to see and know more about Santiago! Thank you Franco for making my trip a fun one. I will be taking others to do this tour next time I am there! - Jess R. - Fort Worth, Tx
title: Facts, Fun and Fun Facts for Free!!!

review_text: It was amazing! Guides Francisco, Lorena and Jorge are sensational! Super attentive and made our trip even more special! Unforgettable experience! They will be eternal memories! Hope to come back again
title: Sensational

review_text: A gentle uphill walk of about a mile to the top giving great views over Santiago. The statue itself is quite breathtaking. Grounds very attractive as is the little church on the top. On the path up we saw a group of people looking down at something......a tarantula walking across the path! One let down was the coffee from the little kiosk, awful, it was ordinary Nescafé without milk. review_text: We decided to self-drive and left our hotel at 4:45am with the sunrise scheduled for 6:38am. The drive is mostly straightforward and can be done with a regular sedan, even though there are a couple of fairly steep climbs. There are a couple of forks and all but one have visible signs that direct you to El Tatio. At the fork to Baños de Puritama, however the sign is not visible from the angle you are coming and most drivers will follow the road along to the right. That is wrong and a long detour! My advice is to download a map for this area in google maps and use it offline. Be aware that you are going from 2400m above sea level to 4200m. The lower air pressure at 4200m will exhaust you quicker than in San Pedro de Atacama. We did the drive in late November and it was around freezing at El Tatio before sunrise, while it was 45 F in San Pedro de Atacama. We arrived at 6:15am and the geyser field was only visible a few minutes before we arrived. We actually saw the sun about 25min after the official sunrise, because it had to get above the mountains that encircle the geyser basin. Most tour buses appeared to arrive at around 6:50am. Interestingly, the geysers fume output appeared to triple or quadruple for maybe 15min starting shortly before the sun peeked over the mountains. After those 15min, the output was back to how it was when we arrived before sunrise. I have been to Yellowstone and the geysers in Iceland, and I can say that El Tatio is different - the geysers are constantly fuming or erupting (hot water is spilled maybe 1ft to max. 2ft high) and not erupting on some schedule - and I think it is definitely worth seeing them. If you don't want to get up super early, then don't hesitate to go there later in the day. After sunrise, the temperature quickly rose to above 50F, which is much more bearable but still cool. Admission was 20,000 Pesos per person. There is also a warm pool where you can swim. The pool is fed by 2 small hot springs which heat the water to only luke warm temperatures. So, don't expect a nice warm or hot pool. Some changing cabins are near the pool. Long story short: I consider El Tatio a must-see.

review_text: We met our guide in the lobby of our hotel in the morning and proceeded north, out of Santiago and into the countryside of some of Chile's prime agricultural land. It was interesting to have a glimpse of how the growers work the fields (we're interested in that sort of thing). Our first stop was in a town called Llay Llay; a native phrase meaning "Big Wind." We visited the Quintessence Alpaca farm where we saw Alpacas and the process from wool to garments. Next, we drove over to the coast to see penguins. This would have been extremely interesting if we hadn't just completed a cruise to Antarctica and the Falkland Islands, where we observed penguins mere feet away. Still, it was fun to see a different kind of penguin, and it was especially fascinating to see the Pacific coastline. We couldn't help thinking how much like California the coast looked. We walked along a trail by the rocky shore for a bit and took in some scenery. Finally, we had reservations at a seaside restaurant for lunch. Our seating was outside where we could see divers harvesting clams as we had lunch. Below, we marked this tour as for couples because TripAdvisor only allows one box to be checked, but the truth is, this tour was suited for everyone, in pretty much every combination. The restaurant was a bit sophisticated for very young children (we didn't see any Happy Meals and Mac & Cheese on the menu), but still doable. review_text: “The story of Chico Mineiro and his faithful leader Edgar: After a day of hard work and intense cold, go down the Chico Mineiro and Edgar mountains. The van is full of adventurous tourists, but Chico and Edgar face the mountain range’s biggest challenge “The tourist who bought his driver’s license and rented a car”. Facing the eyes of the beast, in the steep and narrow passage that would lead them towards the happy destiny, Chico and Edgar have the growing fear that that tourist imbued with perverse intentions, will not cooperate by crashing along the narrow road and climbing the snow, which precedes the fall to the endless precipice, tries to pass through the van and continue towards his dark fado. Chico goes off the van while Edgar struggles behind the wheel, the battle will be intense, and this becomes evident when the driver slides with the car over the ice that covers the road and the passage is closed. Chico, imbued with heavenly powers, holds Van with his hands and avoids the fatal collision, but not for long because as if he challenged fate, the perverse tourist speeds and gets trapped between the van and the precipice! The traffic accumulates, and the two vehicles block the road, NONE BACK AND NONE UP, there are two options left: push the tourist's car slope down, or Edgar miraculously drag the van through the opposite snow wall and get rid of the demonic car. Here the adventurous tourists come down from the Van, and against all the hypotheses of fate they push the car, not towards the precipice, but towards the road, liberating the Van from its deadly enemy. The price paid for this courageous effort was an enormous scar left in Van's bakery. ⁇ Eyewitnesses saw the moment a police officer pulled out his pen and noted the data of the unregulated driver, muting the same. Chico Miner and Edgar were finally free to guide their troupe to a new adventure! After all, it was just another day of work in the Mountains. Legend has it that the driver of the car is still in the mountains, trying to climb the 56 curves.” Thank you for the adventure friends! Who is wondering if it is worth renting a car to climb the mountains, not worth it! Agenda with Chico miner and Edgar!

review_text: Gabriel and Dani were the best hosts and accommodated everyone’s needs. The tour was incredible, amazing not-to-be-missed views, shows a glimpse of what the Andes and Chilean nature is about. We loved it. Review of: Cajon Del Maipo Including Wine with Picnic and Empanada

review_text: Took a great guided tour here in February. It's a very early start, pre-dawn but I can't quite remember when. As the sun rises, you'll see the geysers emitting their steam, however this activity is highly weather-dependent. While I'm glad I took the tour, other photos of the landscape on various days produce varied results so best check the weather forecast beforehand. Guide was bi-lingual, relaxed and knowledgeable.

review_text: I am Canadian and have been living here for three years. He is highly educated about everything “Chile” and is a genuinely nice and fun person. Emanuel was a safe driver (not commonplace place) as well as a friendly and kind person. Review of: Valparaiso Port and Vina del Mar Full-Day Tour from Santiago

review_text: We arrived early at this popular attraction, hoping to beat the queues. We arrived early, well before the opening time but a small quite had already formed, which we joined. When it opened, we were told that it was being repaired and that a replacement bus was being provided. This is fine, but surely the sign indicating the closure could have been mounted outside to avoid the unnecessary and pointless queue? ¡Thanks for your opinion! Take Care.

review_text: Read the story of Magellan and decide for yourself if he deserves a statue. Yes, he was brave, a good navigator and lucky, but he was also cruel and died at the hands of natives in the Pacific after burning their village when they refused to convert.. Only one of his ships, the Victoria, actually made it around the world. Only 18 of the over 200 men who started the three year trip made it.
title: Worth a visit if in town

This house is the one his lover had lived and he would visit her when he was in Santiago. The architecture is very uncommon and beautiful. Take the audioguide and have fun with the stories about every detail in the house.

review_text: The hotel pick up and drop off was on time and I met some amazing people on this tour - the views of the reservoir were also incredible - however the guide Salvador was quite unprofessional - we took so many unnecessary stops and had to get off the bus to listen to his 'life reflections' which were painful to take in. He also had a side hustle going on taking photos of people (who were willing to pay him) and this included people on our bus and many people on other buses. At one point the lovely driver had our picnic ready to go and we waited a solid half an hour for our guide because he was off making money from his photography hustle. We were so hungry and thirsty but were unable to dig in until our guide returned. At another point he was late to meet us because once again he was off taking photos of other people. A lot of the information he gave us about Chile/the lakes and mountains were also completely inaccurate and myself and the other English speaking tourists could do nothing but shake our heads and laugh. Worth it for the views but there are so many other companies offering similar more organised tours to the same place. Review of: Small-Group Cajón del Maipo Full-Day Tour and Picnic Thank you for your comment! We're happy you enjoyed your tour, we're deeply sorry about the inconveniences and we'll look into it to make sure this doesn't happen again. You help us be better, MTO Tour Team

review_text: The beauty of the volcano can be seen from many vistas in the town of Pucon. After three completely cloudy days, we suddenly looked up and there was this magnificent sight: a snow capped volcano against a precious blue sky. The contrast was stunning. We watched the sun set on it, and it was something to remember, a choice moment in anyone's travels through Chile. On the back side of the volcano you can take a lovely hike through a monkey puzzle tree forest that leads to a lava field area which extends to a glacier. Highly recommend this for its vistas and its uniqueness. Great hike!
title: A spectacular sight with a glacier hike too

review_text: We went with Politur agency in Pucon, with guides Guido (Swiss) and Juanito (Chilean). They were very professional and a perfect combination of pushing us to get to the top while allowing us the occasional rest. Most equipment was provided - you just have to bring your lunch, sunglasses and sunscreen. We had a beautiful, clear day, but it was very windy, which prevented us from taking the chairlift. This added a significant amount of time to the hike - it was seven hours hiking up and two hours sliding down on either small plastic discs or your butt - depending on the steepness of the slope. Our group was small, just four climbers and two guides. We would highly recommend this trip, it provides you with a great sense of accomplishment. And they give you a beer back at the shop when you're done to celebrate. Cost was about 42,000 CLP per person

review_text: This is the oldest pisco distillery in Chile. It is well worth a visit and has a much more interesting history than the big industrial Pisco distillery's in the region. Our guided tour took about 1,5 h and we got to see how the work has been done for more than 100 years. The tour ended with a tasting of two different piscos and one dessert wine. Good value and interesting!

review_text: It was difficult to find some of the stops as they are not properly signposted. However, once that hurdle had been overcome and we were on the bus, we had to move several times in order to find a working commentary point. The route was pleasant and the commentary interesting but our main gripe was how long we had to wait for each bus - on one occasion it was around 40 minutes. At $23 a day ticket, we didn't feel that the advertised 30 minute wait was an acceptable one - the company needs to have more buses so that people don,t have to wait more than 15 to 20 minutes at most. Jacqueline2, we regret that your experience with us through the Hop On Hop Off has not been entirely satisfactory. We will take into account each of your observations to analyze them with the operations department. In turn, we inform you that the stops that are not marked is by prohibition of the municipality. As for the waiting time of each bus, we inform you that we have a good fleet, what happens is that the traffic of the city often influences the delay of the same. We wish you a happy return home. review_text: This is a fairly small museum, run by the local university. It has 2 parts, one mostly detailing the culture of the different tribes that populated this area throughout history, showing well preserved objects such as ceramics and tools. There is a decent amount of information, but only in Spanish. The objects are well presented. In the second part the focus is on the mummification proces and tools used, as well as the mummies themselves (some are naturally mummified, others went clearly through an elaborate process). In this culture, even fetuses en new born were mummified, unlike in ancient Egypt, where only the very rich could afford mummification after dead.
title: Small university museum, oldest mummies, good other collection

review_text: We were in Antofagasta for work and had an extra free day. We heard about “Hand of the Desert” and thought that we should see it since there seemed nothing much to do here. We were lucky to find Ruhiscos Travel. Maglio from Ruhiscos was our tour guide. He picked us up from our hotel in a comfortable van, and dropped us back at the end of the tour. We bought a half-day tour to see Hand of the Desert, but the tour included visits to the other top 3 popular tourist attractions of Antofagasta which are the Tropic of Capricorn monument, La Portada, and the National Historical Monument Huanchaca. At each place, Maglio provided detailed, interesting commentary. We impressed with a big hand sculpture popping up in the middle of the desert, a must-see site for visitors. But we also liked our visit to La Portada, the sea rock formation in the ocean. We also learned a lot about the history of Antofagasta and Chile at the Huanchaca museum. This tour covered high spots in Antofagasta and let us see the other side of Antofagasta besides the beautiful ocean. Maglio can provide tours in both Spanish and English. We highly recommended Ruhiscos for your Antofagasta tour.
title: Amazing Site in the Desert!

review_text: I was here just last night and I still can't stop thinking how awesome it was. Was originally booked to go to mamalluca observatory but after a cancellation by the office and reading the reviews I figured I would not have enjoyed it anyway.. Mamalluca tours consist of at least 50 people, the guides are just that, tour guides - they are not astronomers. You spend more time watching videos than observing.. A lot of kids and a lot of queuing. A very weak telescope as well that won't allow you to see anything interesting.. HOWEVER, the observatorio del pangue on the other hand consists of small groups of only 10 people. The guides are true astronomers that have a huge depth of knowledge and explain everything so well.. Its a very cosy environment and you feel welcomed to ask questions and converse. Most importantly, you spend the entire time observing the stars and then looking at beautiful nebula's, a super nova, far distant galaxies and the remnants of an exploded star (supernova).. My wife and I opted for the English tour and our astronomer Eric spoke perfect English.. He made sure everyone got to see every object through the telescope spending a good few minutes on each object. There was no rushing you could spend as long as you wanted looking through the (big) powerful telescope.. Our group was only 5 people and everyone was so friendly. On this rare occasion because of the cloud cover on the previous night it was moved over to tonight. The group was originally around 12 people and they split it up into two groups. That's how seriously these guys take the importance of your experience. And on this rare occasion we were allowed to use the telescope that wasnt for the tourists because of the group being split into two. A bit more powerful but manually operated..Eric showed us how to move it around and use it which was super easy and honestly it made the experience for me even better.. If you're serious about seeing the beautiful night sky, want a tour that is not rushed, want to be able to see the most beautiful things the cosmos has to offer, want the most polite, friendly and knowledgeable astronomers to teach and show you the cosmos then this is the tour for you.. It costs more than mamalluca but it is worth so much more and it's true value for money.. To everyone at the observatory and Eric, thank you so much for such a magical experience.

review_text: We booked with Chile Nativo and I was nervous about it in the beginning as I couldn't find much information on them prior to booking. After doing the 5-day W Trek in Patagonia with them, I highly recommend them and understand why there's not too much info on them. Chile Nativo has been around for over 10 (maybe even 15) years. It started off as a small operator and I think they've grown their presence and team more in the last year or so. We actually got connected to Chile Nativo through Swoop Patagonia, which has a bigger marketing presence and are basically third party sales agents. Swoop Patagonia is based in the UK and I guess have their own operations or other vendors they use as well depending on what tour package you do. Anyway we booked this trip back in May 2018 to do the W trek in early Nov. We had an amazing time and were well taken cared of. Communication prior to the trip was generally pretty good, though sometimes I had to follow up with them first if I hadn't heard from them as the trip approached or if someone didn't get back to me on something. But overall they were very responsive. We were a larger group than normal (10 guests) so we had two guides, Pelin and Fernando. Both were super amazing at their job. They made us feel very comfortable, answered all our questions, were very patient with us during the trek, and looked after all our needs. Felt like friends as well as teachers. One of the reasons why we booked so early is because we didn't want to be stuck tenting outside at the refugios or deal with the refugio bookings which sound like it's getting more complicated! Anyway while my group of 4 had beds at every refugio, there were a couple of guests who booked closer to Nov. who had to sleep in tents outside due to no more room. Luckily one of the nights we also got to switch refugios from the one most people dreaded (Domo Frances) to Los Cuernos, as they had room and could take us. So, you never know what you might get. We were also super lucky with the weather! I really braced myself for awful rain and windy Patagonia weather but we had three straight days of sun and no wind, which is rare! On the fourth day it was pretty windy and drizzly but still not too bad. The hike from east to west was good, as we got the hardest part of the hike over and done with on the first day (Blue Towers) and we were going without the sun in our eyes for the most part. The food provided by Chile Nativo on the first day was SO GOOD too. The rest of the packed lunches are provided by the refugios and some were better than others. We made all the hikes in good time and got to relax after a long day. I really don't know how the guides have the energy to do back to back trekking hikes (one of them started all over again right when we got back to Puerto Natales!) but they were lovely and had great energy and if they were ever tired or irritated they never showed it. You can tell they really love what they do. I would highly recommend booking with them; they really try to address all your concerns and find alternative suggestions if something doesn't pan out due to the weather (some side activities got canceled). The refugios we stayed at included Torres Central, Los Cuernos (but it was supposed to be Domo Frances, which I'm glad we did not stay at based on reviews!), Paine Grande, and Grey. Review of: W Trek Torres del Paine Hello!! Many thanks for taking the time to write a review of your trip. We are very glad you had an amazing time in Torres del Paine! We'll let Pelin and Fernando know of your kind words. Chile Nativo is actually 17 years old, but it did start as a small tour operator with few trips per season, and started to grow in presence over the last 5 years approximately. =) Hope to welcome you or any friend of yours into Patagonia in the future. Kind regards, Chile Nativo Team
