review_text: I've been in this city many times,and always has something new to show me. Constitución is 5 hours by bus from Santiago, you can find a bus in the bus terminal in Santiago (Universidad de santiago metro station) . The price of the ticket is around 10.000 CLP TO 16.000 CLP one way depending on the bus agency. This small city in the coast of the Maule Region has many enchantments, it has nice beaches cover by black and thick sand, the waves are nice so here you will find some surf and body activities. This city has a nature national monument which is La piedra de la Iglesia , and also has another famous stone named as Arco de los enamorados. Cerro Mutrún is a popular spot for the locals, here some parties are done in summer , and also is famous because there were a tribute in honor to some deceased people who died in the earthquake of 2010.In this place you must have a camera , there is an excelent view ! Some other attractions are kayaking through the Maule river, visit the market in the harbor which is really popular because the fresh fish.To get to the market you travel trough the costanera which also has a spectacular view of the ocean. If you decide to go to the other side and to discover the green areas you have the way to putú , this path is cover by green fields and forest. Also there is a road beside the maule river ,which also is full of green and here you pass by the Puente ferroviario Bancos de Arena( built by Eiffel). I also want to recommend a place which owns of a relative, Aqua perfect gym is located going to Putú and is an excellent place to enjoy with the family and friends, has pools, games,music, barbecue spots, and they sell snacks. You can get to the place by bus or by car. The weather is cold mostly all year, it has lot of wind , summer is nice weather but at night is cold. The principal square has a lot of night life for everybody, kids,youth and adults , in summer there is always a little amusement park ,other games a handicraft market. Also the shore is cover by many pubs and discotheques.

review_text: Coquimbo’s Cruz Del Tercer Milenio, Third Millenium Cross, was built to commemorate the birth of Christ over 2000 years ago and was blessed by the Pope John Paul II. Construction began in 1999 and was completed in 2021. The cross is made of concrete and is 272-feet high and 131-feet wide and sits on the El Vigia Hill. Besides being taller than Rio de Jannero’s Christ the Redeemer statue, it is one of the largest crosses in the world. Designed by architect Gabriel Guarda, the base has three pillars that form a tripod, a reference to the Holy Trinity. There is a 2,000-step staircase or use an elevator to have a remarkable 360 ° panoramic view of all Coquimbo, its bay, and the Pacific Ocean.
title: Monument to Christianity

review_text: Salar de Uyuni Even though the service at the agency itself was excellent, there are a couple of issues that I'd like to publicly address. First, I was added to the whatsapp group with information regarding pick-up and Bolivian customs very late and so I did not receive the messages in the chat. The other people showed me because they all had filled out the custom form online already (in the end there was no problem at the border, but still!). Second, the agency is one of the more expensive ones and for Salar de Uyuni, they cooperate with Sajama Expediciones from Bolivia (which did an excellent job btw) and they openly communicate that. However, other agencies cooperate with that agency as well and they offer way cheaper tours. I paid 235.000 CLP while others in my group only paid 160.000 CLP (even with a private room!). Most of the money you pay stays with Horizonte Atacama. They only pay 150.000 CLP to the Bolivian agency. The only thing they do is that a driver brings you to the Bolivian border and provides you breakfast at the Chilean border. This is not only rip-off against the Bolivian agency, especially the guides/drives, because they have 3 days of work and get paid very poorly. But also, it is a rip-off against customers. Hence, I recommend asking with which Bolivian agency they cooperate and rather look at their reviews when making a decision.
title: Rip-off of customers and Bolivian partner agency

review_text: This tour was really enjoyable with some stunning scenery, within a short drive of Santiago. Javier the guide was great - very enthusiastic and excellent bilingual (English and Spanish) commentary, explaining the geography/geology of the area really well in particular. I saw that some other reviews complained about walking, but there wasn't really that much. The bus stopped at a viewpoint on the way up for photos, then at the edge of the reservoir for around 40 minutes, and we were given the option to walk further around to the end if we wanted to...this was a flat path (no incline!) and an easy stroll (worth it for views too). I had been out really late the night before (beware of the very friendly Chilean people and their generous measures of Pisco!!) but found the trip to be pretty laid back/easy going, as did one of my fellow passengers who had been similarly way-laid the night before by the infamous "terremoto" drink! :-) Meanwhile, Javier and the other guides set up a snack table with juice and small plates of cheese/nibbles. The scenery was lovely - quite windy at the other end of the reservoir so maybe bring a light jacket with you (and some sunscreen!) As it is in the mountains and part of a national park, the main draw of the tour is the scenery (no shops or anything else, as you would expect!). There is a stop in a small town on the way up, but the main point there is to pick up any extra snacks you want as lunch is around 3pm on the way back (and for the guide to register with the tourism office there). I thought the lunch was pretty good - we were given a discounted price of 16,000 pesos for an all you could eat buffet (including a glass of wine/beer or soft drink and a coffee/tea). Again, this was optional so you could take a packed lunch if you wanted to skip it. The food was really tasty though (and not having had breakfast due to aforementioned late night, I think I got my money's worth!). There was a glass of wine included in the tour too (we had it at the lunch location as you're not allowed to drink in public/at the reservoir). Other details - I got picked up from my hotel pretty much on the dot at 8.15am. This is a shuttle service and they take you out to the main Turistik loading bay at the big Parque Arauco shopping mall to the north east of the city centre. You then join the main bus for your tour...there were lots of other tours leaving around the same time, but each bus has a sign in its window with the name of each tour so you can look out for yours there, and there were also lots of guides with clipboards to show people which bus to take. You then get driven up to the Maipo Canyon, with a stop in the little town for snacks, followed by a stop for toilets (at the place where you will have lunch later), then it is on to the reservoir (as mentioned above). If I remember, we left the reservoir around 2pm(?), and got back to the lunch spot around 3pm. I was dropped back at my hotel by 5pm ish (roughly!) It also looked like there were good places to do other outdoor activities if you have more time to spend in the area and are into these things (e.g. rafting/kayaking/skydiving/bungee jumping). So if you want an easy way to get out of Santiago for a day and see some of the Andes scenery, then this is a pretty good way to do it. review_text: I did the 5 day W trek. There are different bus companies that pick up from Puerto Natales and take you to the park. First you have to register yourself and get a pass and pay the national park fees. Then you have the option of either taking a bus to the accommodation or walk there. I took the bus (costs about 6000 Chilean Pesos) to the Las Torres Central and checked in. I did the hike to Base Las Torres taking nothing but my camera and bottle of water. It was the most difficult hike due to the steepness. It was cloudy so we couldn't see much of the three towers. On Day two, it was raining and cloudy but it was a pleasant walk to Cuernos. It took a bit longer for me since I was really sore from my hike on day one. I did some leg exercises and recovered fast for Day 3. On Day 3, the highlight of the day it was sunny and we got to see the real beauty of the national park and I got really excited and started sprinting on the track. It got a bit steep towards the end. I got to the lookout near camp Britanico and the lookout was amazing. Not be fooled, there are two lookouts on this point. One is pretty flat where you can have your lunch and admire the mountains. The second one (about 30 mins walk) is a bit further but a better lookout. On Day 4, it was cloudy again and I walked from Cuernos to Lake Refugio Grey, was another struggle due to sore legs and steepness but made it :). On Day 5, it was cloudy but it was a short walk (about 3 hrs) to Paine Grande. I rested there on that day. Later that day the it got sunny and again the beauty of the park was revealed. I took my camera and rushed outside and took as many photos as I can. On Day 6, it was sunny and waited for the boat (tickets can only be purchased on the boat) back to Pudeto to catch the bus back to Puerto Natales. During the boat ride, what I would say is the most photographed picture appears before your eyes. Overall, it was a really good hike and I encourage people to spend extra time to appreciate the beauty of the park rather than joining a one-day tour. FYI, please take appropriate clothing, the weather in the park changes very often and it gets very windy. Take enough cash with you, national park fees and boat fees can be paid in cash only (USD or Chilean Pesos). Book your Refugios very early in advance. These get booked very fast especially during peak season and your meals as well. There are no powerpoints in the hostels, there are only one area in each Refugio where there are limited powerpoints and they are normally full with phone chargers. Please be considerate of others and decide whether you want to charge your phone or camera battery. BTW There is no phone signal in the park :)

If you were staying at this property for three days or less, there would really be very little reason to leave. They have fantastic wines to sample, every type of Grand Marnier ever produced, since the owners also own Grand Marnier, hiking trails, horseback riding, beautiful pools for swimming, and perfect casitas from which to relax with a glass of wine, read a book and take in the incredible scenery of this picturesque valley with the surrounding mountains. When you do venture out to tour some of the numerous surrounding wineries, there will be no shortage from which to choose. Our favorites, besides Lapostolle, were Montgras, Neyen and Montes. If you are into the finer wines, be sure to request a special tasting of their top wines. Most of the vineyards do offer this for a bit higher price, and it is well worth the freight. Otherwise, you might be stuck tasting the more pedestrian wines that you find in the discount stores back in the states. Huge difference in quality. The last thing I would suggest is to hire a driver for the day if you are going tasting from winery to winery. Some of the roads are not marked well, and it is a pleasure to be able to imbibe and have someone else take care of that task. The hotels can recommend bilingual drivers if you need them.

review_text: Review for spa one and only I visited Santiago for two weeks and one of the absolute highlights of the trip was Spa One & Only. The environment is soothing and peaceful, the spa is beautifully designed, everyone who works there is friendly and accommodating, and the treatments I received were fantastic. I booked my appointment a few weeks before I arrived and somehow (totally my fault) I saved the appointment in my calendar for the wrong date and didn’t realize until the day before when I got an appointment reminder. At that point I was double booked and had no way to cancel my conflicting plans. Originally when I contacted the spa about my dilemma, I was told they were booked the next day (the day I thought my appointment was) but they went above and beyond to shift things around to get me in. Instead of seeing one therapist for the various things I booked, they split my sessions between two which I didn’t mind at all. It actually ended up being a blessing in disguise because I got to experience two separate therapists who were both incredible! I started with a 60-minute aromatherapy relaxation massage with Victoria and honestly I went in thinking it would be a “fluff” massage (that’s what I call it when the therapist just lightly glides over you and goes through a set routine rather than tuning into your body and finding/working on actual problem areas). I have some pretty serious back pain due to previous injuries and usually anything under 90 minutes doesn’t cut it since I need some pretty intensive work. Let me tell you that this was anything but a fluff massage. From the start, Victoria’s pressure and technique were perfect…and she somehow managed to work on more areas in 60 minutes than some people do in 90. She definitely moved quickly in order to do as much as she did but I didn’t leave feeling like she neglected or rushed through a single area. I can only imagine that a longer massage with her would be even more amazing but I was thrilled with the experience I had with her. Next up was a 90-minute Holistic Energy Clearing Ritual with Daniela. I originally booked the Holistic Experience with her which was 2.5 hours so initially I was bummed at missing out on the full experience…but that was before my actual session…and trust me, I didn’t leave feeling like I missed out on anything. The entire session with Daniela was so incredibly beautiful that I’m finding it hard to put into words. I’m an energy healer myself but I rarely take the time to get treatments from other healers and this was much needed on so many levels. I had a few specific areas where I was looking to release energy/emotions and that definitely happened during the session. Daniela spoke throughout the entire session and gave the most beautiful explanations along with guided meditations and breathwork. The session also included reiki, crystal healing, singing bowls, smoke cleansing, and beautiful songs. One big surprise is that a massage was also included and I had no idea so that was an extremely pleasant surprise. The session ended with a short reading from an oracle deck and the cards were so spot on for everything I was going through. Another nice touch is that she opened a window during the session and I could hear the birds singing the entire time which added to the overall soothing experience. I thoroughly enjoyed both of my sessions with Victoria and Daniela and highly recommend both therapists. Whether you live locally or are on vacation and looking for a reason to pamper yourself, do yourself a favor and book yourself one (or hopefully more) sessions at Spa One & Only. If you’re not a Spanish speaker (which I unfortunately am not) you’ll definitely need a translation app to book your appointment through WhatsApp and be prepared to have it handy for checking in/out. Both therapists claimed their English was terrible but I disagree completely. We had no problems with communication at all. Daniela especially speaks phenomenal English and I was astounded at how deep she got with the topics she spoke about during the session, especially for her claiming to not know English well. I left the spa feeling so much lighter and stress-free. I haven’t felt that level of peace in a long time and wish I could transport myself back right now.
title: The highlight of my trip to Santiago

review_text: I highly recommend the w-trek and hiking it from west to east so the wind will be predominantly at your back. If you hike east to west, your first day is a brutal 4 hour ascent, not the way I'd want to start! Each day is very manageable on its own, but by the end of day 5 we were exhausted. I would not do this trek without a neck warmer to block wind from your face and ears (I couldn't keep a cap on my head or scrunch in my hair since winds were ferocious), a water bladder so your hands are free and you can stay hydrated while moving instead of a water bottle, and trekking poles to save your knees! It barely rained in November, but a waterproof cover for your pack is a good idea just in case. Be sure to have a small pack (for your water, lunch, etc) that you can take with you when you hike up to Brittanico as you can leave your large pack at Italia. We stayed in the Refugios each night which are clean and comfortable. However, be aware of your belongings! I had a Patagonia fleece jacket stolen off the hook outside my shower at Chileno. I'm pretty sure it was the girl cleaning the washroom at the time as she would not make eye contact with me after this incident, yet was super friendly upon my arrival. I don't like making such an unkind assumption, but I really do not believe any hiker wants to add more weight to their pack and staff are paid very poorly. In the end she likely needs the jacket more than me, so I hope she's the one who has it. Other women told me they had things stolen as well when they were showering. We had all meals provided by the Refugios, the bagged lunches are plentiful. Each refugio has a bar to relax in during the evenings and reminisce with other hikers about the day's adventure. Patagonia unites diverse people from around the globe while being surrounded by the most stunning scenery. This was an amazing experience. We booked through Experience Chile as trying to reserve Refugios online wasn't working for me and this was a last minute trip so time was not on my side. Charles was my contact and was so so helpful! He even gave me his personal mobile number to contact him during our visit in case anything went wrong. He booked other tours for us, transportation, accommodations, and was very responsive from beginning to end. This is a must hike for anyone who enjoys the outdoors. I also recommend flying to Calama, renting a car (Chile appears to only have manual cars which was an unfortunate surprise to other visitors we met), and drive to stay in San Pedro de Atacama. The desert is so different than Patagonia! The Valle de Luna is a must visit, as well as driving to El Tatio to view the geothermal field with more than 80 active geysers! review_text: It's a pretty unique experience! Don't expect a cruise-ship experience. This is a ferry. As ferries go, this is a pretty basic ferry. We've been in much nicer ferries in many parts of the world.... We chose a Triple A cabin. This included 2 single bunk-beds (which were comfortable), private bathroom in the cabin, a fully openable outside porthole (with no outside deck), a wardrobe, desk and bench. It was quite austere - basically painted metal walls, with utilitarian furnishings. The bathroom was essentially a wet room with exposed shower, and flickering fluorescent light, which did give it that unique "horror-movie" atmosphere. (Watch Das Boot, and expect a little bit better!) I could not have imagined sharing cabins or bathrooms with strangers on this trip. The rooms are very small. I overheard someone, while standing on deck in the cold rain, say of their cabin, "It's like a prison cell." But, with the Triple A private cabins, it's a better experience. Ours was right next to the Officer's Mess, so there was some noise, plus this is working ship - so expect to hear industrial-type noises. The ship itself, and the decks are well-maintained. The bar area for presentations is bright, and comfortable. But then.... we get to the dining room.... Picture a 1970s hospital or school cafeteria. Long metal tables, cavernous fluorescent lit, bare room, and food that borders on gruel. Our first breakfast set the tone, when the cooks ladled a spoonful of runny, thin porridge onto our tray. Little did we know at that time, we were actually having a treat, with 5-6 raisins in our portion for this time! (Bring your own snacks to supplement the bland meals.) The common areas can be quite noisy as they tend to have TVs running, in Spanish. The truck drivers all hang out here. There is no wifi, no safe in room. Lectures were given daily in Spanish and English on the geography, culture, flora and fauna of the region. The guide was enthusiastic and had a great sense of humour. Potentially, this trip could have amazing views, and is a worthwhile way of seeing this area of Chile. The weather on our trip was rather poor, but there were glimpses of huge mountains and waterfalls, whales and seals. Thank you for taking the time to comment about your experience with Navimag ;)

review_text: My husband and I just completed the W trek with Ricci and team about a week ago, and had an incredible experience overall. We were picked up from the bus in Puerto Natales and then taken to the beautiful Garden Domes, where we had upgraded to the private ecodome (highly recommend). After some tea and snacks, we went to our group dinner and briefing with Ricci at El Brisket. Food was amazing! Ricci gave some helpful advice about the trek and offered some wisdom to help ensure we'd have the best time. Then we went back to the Garden Domes, and we managed to get a nice soak in the hot tub with the most breathtaking views before we were off on our adventure. The next morning we stored our luggage and had a delicious breakfast before leaving for the park via private transportation. We absolutely loved the guide Andy that trekked with us on the first day, and from there the path was extremely easy to self navigate the rest of the way. We enjoyed our refugio experience overall - there was one miscommunication with Domo Frances, where we were supposed to stay in the dorm but instead had camping, but it turned out to be super fun and Ricci made it right by refunding us some money, since camping was less expensive. The only reason I am not giving a 5 star rating is that communication between Ricci/team and guests could be improved upon. We returned from our trek at about 10pm with the expectation that we were going to a pizza party with our group and some other groups that had completed the trek that day, only to find out that they had overbooked the Garden Domes that evening and most of the group did not have a place to stay. Some people were panicking out about this, which caused a tizzy - this is understandable, especially after a 5 day hike, a long journey back to Puerto Natales, and how late it was. Ricci made it right immediately by booking all of us in the nicest hotel in town, but the whole situation could have been avoided had his team given us a heads up about this a day or two in advance so we'd know what to expect upon arrival. My husband and I gave Ricci this feedback directly and he was very receptive, but I do believe in writing honest reviews so think it's important to share our whole experience. We initially chose Chiletours due to pricing, as they were much less expensive than other tour operators that we researched, and they ended up really surpassing our expectations. Overall, Ricci/team took excellent care of us and I would absolutely recommend Chiletours to anyone that wants to do the W trek and not have to deal with the logistical hassles that come with booking (ie booking refugios individually, transport to and from Puerto Natales, etc.). We travel a ton, and this was one of our favorite trips yet! Review of: Full-Day Torres del Paine Mountains Advanced Hike

review_text: I was on the same ship's tour as Elisabeth. After making the effort to be on the first tender, we had to wait over an hour for the rest of the tour group to arrive. No time limit was given at each stop and much time was wasted standing around talking. One other couple on the tour had come from the same area in England as Jackie and she was distracted all day by these people. I took very few photos as I was expecting to see what had been promised in the published itinerary and waiting to visit the National Park and see three waterfalls and the stunning Simpson River Valley that had been described. At 2pm we arrived at the farm for lunch - one pisco sour, one bottle of wine per table of four, bread, lamb and salad. Extra lamb was offered but there was still one half of lamb on the spit when we left at 3pm after the dancing display, to be back at the ship by 4pm. It was a very expensive day for what was provided for US$130 paid in advance, with extra costs through PayPal. A friend who did the ship tour to Coyhaique and Scenic Simpson Valley said that the highlight was driving through the Andes and into the town of Coyhaique. Other friends paid US30 each for a van with five people, picked up at the meeting place near the port. They left promptly and had a great day visiting the National Park, Virgin waterfall, Indian head, seeing condors, travelling through the Simpson Valley into Coyhaique and spending time at a handicraft market and buying lunch. I contacted Ann Hedderman after this tour and voiced my disappointment but the only excuse given for not being given an extensive tour of the Simpson River Valley was time constraints. My advice is to do your research if you want to experience the natural beauty of the Simpson River Valley and travel into Coyhaique, rather than just a cultural experience with lunch. Thank you very much for your review. We sincerely apologize that you experienced some disappointment during your day with us in Puerto Chacabuco. We want you to know that your feedback is extremely important to us. Because the ship NCL Sun has less time in port than other ships, we have adjusted our 6 hour tour to 4 ½ hours in order to prioritize the highlights of our tour and ensure you are back to the port in good time. It is our intention that this itinerary is clear in the emailed tour description. We wish that this ship had more time too! Our coordinator watches the time throughout the day and while we do not like to cut anything- we prioritize having your back to the port on time. review_text: We took the 7 day cruise from Ushuaia, Argentina to Punta Arenas, Chile and back to Ushuaia and are incredibly happy that we did! The highlight was to land twice on Cape Horn! The first landing, by zodiac boat, was, remarkably, in absolutely still seas, with clear blue skies overhead. The second, in 3' - 5' waves, was with overcast skies and a bit more wind. The climb up the stairs was well worth it when we reached the Albatross Monument & took photos of the view from the lighthouse. Those visits would have justified the cost of the trip, but there was MUCH more to see on this journey. Walks among the penguins, and treks for closeup views of two glaciers (including Pia), and walking along the coast of Ainsworth Bay offered a bit of excersize. And the viewing of countless glaciers along "glacier alley" was priceless. The "Stella Australis" offers comfortable cabins with very comfortable beds, and an uncommon number of common lounges. The meals for us were only adequate, but we did appreciate the open bar and snacks that were available from 11:00 to 11:00. The crew were remarkable - doing everything and anything to make our trip better. If you want to actually land at the "End of the World" - the Stella Australis is definitely the way to do it!
title: Australis Expedition Cruises - THE way to actually land on Cape Horn!

Finally they will drive you to your start point at Santiago or wherever you want (if there’s a Turístik stop, just ask for it. review_text: As a couple on a budget, this was a great way to see Valparaiso and find out more about its history. Our guide, Alvaro was really polite and full of knowledge. During the tour you will not only see the art, but you will also stop to taste a complimentary pisco sour and have a chance to try one of 80+ types of empanadas (for purchase, but you are not obligated). At the end, it will be explained that tips are appreciated, but not required. Just used your own discretion and tip what you think the tour was worth. One side suggestion: after the tour, catch the local "O" or "612" bus at the bus stop next to the port for an inexpensive way to catch the beautiful views that overlook Valparaiso!

review_text: Two friends and I used an outfitter called Antu (they were awesome) to climb Villarrica in May 2017. We have no proper climbing experience but are all in good physical shape. This is *not* a walk in the park. It took six hours to the summit, then we spent a short time at the top, and the way down was probably two or three hours. We chose an outfitter the afternoon before, when we got fitted for all of our climbing gear and outerwear. I wore a long sleeve tshirt/heavy sweater/down jacket on top, a base layer/cotton pants on my legs; two layers of gloves; one layer of wool sock. They provided everything else. (Also, you bring your own food and water.) The climb up is steep, often icy, sometimes perilous. You have to concentrate on every step for probably three-fourths of the way. There were six climbers in our group (with three guides from Antu), and two of them had to slow down while the other four continued on. I was exhausted that evening. The experience, though grueling and often nerve-racking, was totally worth it. Our stay at the summit was probably only 10 minutes, but that was enough. There were crazy strong winds up there blowing us around, the crater gives off clouds of sulfur gas, and it must have been 0 degrees (f). Three highlights: Views along the way were spectacular (we paused many times to admire the views and take pictures). There's a solid river of magma towards the top from a previous event that's frozen over. Assuming it's not too icy, on the way down, we sledded instead of walking.
title: The best part of my two weeks in Chile

review_text: I have been working in the area since 2005 and visited Laguna Cejar several times year ago. It's a beatiful system of a few lakes, worth a visit of max an hour. Yesterday, I returned there with my family after a long time, to watch the sunset, to find you have to pay in the afternoon 15,000 CLP (23 US$) EACH PERSON just for access. 10,000 CLP in the morning. This doesn't make sense!!! There is no maintenance for the place, nothing installed, no services - nada! Just a natural resource like many others. The lakes are a gem in the desert, sure, but about 30 minutes drive South you will find a much more interesting Laguna Chaxa, with flamingos, good explanation. Access costs 2,500 CLP per person. Plenty of explanations, a really nice walk. I am sure is the most beautiful place in the Salar. It's a shame that a natural beauty like this is banned - de facto - to families (we were 4 people: 60,000 for a max 1 hour visit???). What if such an exorbitant fee would be required to access all the beautiful natural beauties all around the world? And don't trust to the popular story that the moneys go to the indigenous population: they just go in the pocket of a few families in the area. I think the municipality of San Pedro should immediately stop this shameful exploitation of a natural beauty like that. But San Pedro changed so much in the years. The surrounding area is really wonderful, but totally uncontrolled exploitation of tourism transformed the village and some of the natural resource in a mean bazar. What a pity... In 3 words: DON'T GO THERE ANYMORE!!!

review_text: As we were pushed for time so used a travel company highly recommended to us by friends called Imagine Latin America, who were able to tailor and a programme covering the best attractions the Atacama Desert had to offer. Based in San Pedro de Atacama, La Casa de Don Tomas, a very comfortable and friendly hotel - all our internal flights and pick-ups were taken care of by local operators booked by our travel company, which took all the stress out of paying for guides, entry fees and coaches. On the first afternoon we were taken on the fascinating Valley of Mars (also known as death valley) tour ending up at the a huge sand dune to watch the sunset over the Andes, unforgettable. Day two included two excursions, the morning was taken up with an Archaeological tour of a pre-Columbian village from around 2.800 b,c. In the afternoon we visit to the largest and driest salt lakes in the world which is home to various species of flamingos. Another spectacular sunset with the backdrop of the Andes, changing colour as the light danced and faded. On day three an early start 4.00 AM was required to experience a full tour to the El Tatio Geysers and Machuca. Arriving early allowed for an amazing view of the sunrise over the Geysers and raised the temperature from a very chilly minus 20! After breakfast at the Geysers we took a bath at the hot thermal pools located a stones through away and outdoors! On the way back we stopped of at small traditional village for lunch. Be aware the altitude is very noticeable on this trip and alcohol is not recommended before you travel. The fourth day was free and we hoped to book a star gazing tour form one of the many tour companies located in San Pedro de Atacama, however this was the one evening it was cloudy so alas this was not possible. it was some consolation we had experienced many clear evenings - the local guide on the previous trip to the Geysers gave us an impromptu star tour! We flew to Santiago the next day but had an amazing trip and toughly enjoyed our visit I would highly recommend .
title: Tour of the Atacama Desert booked with Imagine Latin America.

review_text: Literature Nobel Prize winner Pablo Neruda's very interesting house, great location by the sea. Of the three Neruda's houses, this one is the most interesting to visit. Has sections that look like a ship since in his earlier years he had been a ship captain, another like a train carriage, and vast amounts of different ship artifacts, shells, ships, butterflies... The electronic audio guide explains every room of the house in different languages that explains interesting facts, objects and stories about the poets life and personal life. review_text: We are a super fit adventurous Australian family of 3. Our son is 12- but your outdoor, adventurous, nature loving very fit and able 12 year old. My husband and I have a high and constant level of fitness. We have just finished this trek today ( sept 19)...... This trek to the top point- the 360% Mirador is not for the half fit or low active people at all. The first 1 to 1.5 hours ( if u r fit) is Brutal and straight up hill- there is no let up, it is relentless and on an old unused road. Once you reach the Refugio your walk into the Forrest growth but it is still very much up hill walking. Currently the snow starts to become visible after about 20/30 minutes and then you arrive at the first lake. From here on the snow starts to increase and within 20 mins of walking past the lake u r walking in full snow.... The snow is at times on the flat ankle deep but the terrain is flat. Once you pass the frozen lakes you start the long climb to the mirador and at times currently this is and can be snow to knee deep depending on your choice of where u place your feet. We wore gortex trekking shoes, gators and had walking poles and were ever thankful for them all. The climb of course get thicker and thicker with snow.. This is tough- it's not something anyone should take without being well equipped and have enough food and water. The view once you get thru the snow and finish the relentless uphill will forever be simply a 360 degrees view that words don't and can't describe. This trek is brilliant if u have the fitness level to take it to the top. Our son was brilliant and made it with complete ease and enjoyment . We stayed for 1 hour at the top to have lunch and lap up the view. The slide/ walk down the snow was at times even tougher- this is where u need to have your wits about u as u r fatigued. So take care . But with 1 hour at the top we returned to our car in 6.45. This was and will forever be one of the best treks we have done... The snow factor truly made it a snow drenched wonder land of wow wow wow..
title: Brilliant- with the magic of snow.

review_text: The Atacama is breathtaking; I love deserts and have been to many, and was very excited for a 5 day camping trip around this area. I am definitely glad I went, but I wish I had known a lot of things beforehand, so that I would be prepared for what it was, not what I expected it to be from my research. I'm going to share those things with you, so you don't have that tough acceptance period, where you grapple with the fact that your carefully planned itinerary is blown up due to closures, and you're in for a very different trip than you'd imagined. We'll start with closures. I'd carefully researched the things to see in the Atacama, and crafted an itinerary that would allow me to see the ones most important to me, and minimize driving. When I picked up my truck with a rooftop tent, they handed me the daily closure report. Half the places on the list were closed, including the places I'd planned to hit those first few days. The lesson here is just to not get SUPER attached to visiting specific things. There is a lot of beauty to be found in that desert, but if weather and road conditions aren't on your side, you just might not be able to see certain ones. Go in with a flexible travel plan if possible. It is pretty hard to come by reliable and current information on where you can and cannot camp in the area. That's pretty standard for this kind of travel, and is part of the adventure - the great unknown/surprises! But that said, finding a spot to camp each night ended up being a huge source of stress, as it seemed that many places it was not allowed, some places it was allowed but very unsafe (risk of rain stranding you, temps way below zero/snow, lightning storms), and then there's a lot of grey area. The point of camping in a desert, for me, is to be away from other people, and away from the town/light pollution. The only places that I was told it was acceptable and safe to camp were places that were close to town and sure to be full of other campers. Now, I didn't camp in any of those places, and did manage to find cool secluded spaces - but it was stressful, time consuming, and just hard damn work. I'm not sure if where I spent each of the nights was technically allowed (they were not any of the spots I was specifically told were NOT ok to camp in) and that added to the stress as well. I don't really want to get into trouble in a foreign country, as a rule. Crowds! You will rarely to never be at a laguna or other attraction alone. That might be what you'd expect, but add about 50 people to whatever you were expecting. I understand other people want to do exactly what I'm doing - totally fair - just saying, know that there are buses arriving full of people to almost every location. You can't get close to most of the attractions. Most of the lagunas and salt flats I checked out were surrounded by markers keeping you well away from them. Totally understandable - preserving the environment. It just wasn't in line with the photos I'd seen online before my trip, with people getting to sit alongside these gorgeous lakes and enjoying them up close. It is more like being in a museum, and being herded down a hallway with a bunch of other people, looking at the art behind ropes as you pass. Still beautiful - but be prepared for the art museum, not the nature hike. There are a few exceptions to this - but the vast majority of places are as described above. Weather. This is totally my fault. I read driest desert in the world, and a dark sky area great for stargazing and astral-photography. I should have looked closer at a breakdown of specific months. I did look at temps (usual desert stuff, be prepared for hot days and freezing nights), but didn't realize how much rain I'd see during my time there (almost daily), and how cloudy the nights would be (saw the sky clearly less than 50% of my total nights there). It was just a bummer. Apparently from January to March is the "winter" where occasional showers are to be expected. Plan accordingly, research your dates, don't make assumptions :) San Pedro de Atacama - loved this quirky little town at first, it's like stepping into an old western! But once I had a vehicle in my possession, and needing to find food supplies and gas, I came to think of it as my own personal hell. Navigating the town in a vehicle SUCKS, and you can't park anywhere. You're basically forced to park on the outskirts of town and walk in, leaving your rental and all of your gear and hoping it doesn't get broken into. You can only get really super basic supplies - there is not really what I would think of as a real market or grocery store in the town. There IS a great little produce market that popped up on the eastern side of town center - in a dusty lot near the intersection of the B 245 and Licanbur/R23. You can find ice at the liquor store on Licanbur, and basic stuff like water and TP, a little produce and chips/chocolate bars/hot dogs at the "grocery store" a block from that. Gas. Oy. There is one gas station in the entire area. None of the other little towns have one, it is SUPER weird. The Copec station in SPdA is hard to find - it's down a dusty alley that is a minefield of ginormous potholes, and is marked only by a small sign reading "combustibles". As soon as you turn in, you are in a line. That's how you know you're in the right place. There is always a queue for gas. It's not too long of a wait usually though. You'll notice I still gave this place a 5/5 - because it IS awesome. I just want other people to maybe see this, and know what I'd wished I'd known. I managed to let go of my expectations pretty quickly, and enjoy this for what it was, but my travel companion had a much harder time with this. She was more excited for this part of our trip than even myself (we were traveling through Bolivia and Chile), and she would probably rate it a 1 or 2 now. If she could have seen a review like this ahead of time, she may have opted not to go, to go at a different time, or would have arrived with a more realistic picture of the whole thing - and had a better time for it.
title: Amazing - but manage expectations!

review_text: We bought a full-day trip to vulcano Pili. Due to road opening times, we had to convert it to a 1.5-day trip (additional fees). We left the hotel at 4pm to go to the base camp. The guide decided to start walking at 2am. We started to walk in the scree (the whole mountain is a scree) in the night with a very cold wind. The guide was walking very slow and stopping each 10-15 steps. We asked him about this; he answered : "I must breath!". As he was not following the best climbing line, we started to climb our own path, before him. After 2.5 hours of walking in the night, we reached the middle of the ascension. In the second part the wind was forcing and we were upset with seeing the guide climbing like a snail and waiting for him (we had to wait in order to know the rough direction to take in the night). We also remarked that at this "speed" we would have reached the summit before the sun. We decided to stop this awful situation and get back to the hotel. When we were back at the base camp, the sun was gently rising and the wind had gone; this could be the good time to start the tour, as initially booked (walk starting at 6am). Back in San Pedro, we went to Vulcano Chile at 10am (opening schedule) which opened at 10:45. It was not possible to discuss any partial refund. The guide told us that we woke up at 2am in order to avoid avalanches. We think he did not mind that there was no snow at all in the region! 600 USD for that is a shame! que tu no puedas subir un volcan , no quiere decir que los guias no sepan! ellos organizan y hacen cambios si es necesario de acuerdo a lo que saben y conocen Hemos hecho aqui miles de expediciones , pero nadie puede garantizarte que subas ! o no xq depende de ti , de tus condiciones , no de la hora , ni de otros agentes

review_text: I think overall if I could choose again I might not do the tour and just do a one day tour of the salt flats. We booked a couple of days in advance in the store which was an easy process. We wanted to know specifically what guide we were going to have and he said Omar. We then agreed as the reviews with him were great and we were nervous about getting a good guide as we would be with them in the desert for 3 days! Day one overview: Minibus was due to pick us up at 6:30, arrived at 07:05 but have come to realise that this is generally expected. Guy in the van initially spoke Spanish and then English. Then I think he got bored and only spoke in Spanish. When we got to the border he gave all the important information about passports and documentation in Spanish. When we asked what he said he rolled his eyes and gave the very shortened version. When we got past the border and were assigned to the drivers and guides, our driver was called Joel and our guide Izequiel. I then began to panic and I didn’t know anything about this guide. I asked the guy that had taken us to the border where Omar was. He then pretended to not speak English and said ‘I don’t understand sorry’. Another passenger translated into Spanish to him and he then said ‘who’s Omar’ and then quickly walked off. He then started whispering to the guide and then left. So basically we were stuck and had to go on the tour. Our new guide then said ‘just to warn you guys I’ve had no sleep for over a week so I’m really tired and we are going to have to take it slow today’. Really really bad first impression. We then got in the jeep and there were no seatbelts! Even worse impression as we were completely stuck. The next 3 days were a mixture of highs and lows. Positives of 3 days: Joel the driver was really safe. The majority of the time Izequiel was really nice and had great English. The accommodation was basic but clean and quiet (no one else was in either accommodation each night). We even had a double room the first night without paying extra. We covered all sights and even finished late the last day as we were given loads of time. Negatives: No seatbelts The food was honestly disgusting. We had the vegetarian and mostly had cold undercooked potatoes and egg. One lunch consisted of tinned sweet corn, bad feta and avocado?? My boyfriend was vomiting a lot the first night. As we werent sure if it was a bug or altitude in the morning I asked if we could try the emergency oxygen ... he said it was empty? We were then given random pills that were really old which he wasn’t completely sure what it would do. We were then taken to the doctors which was closed. Luckily he wasn’t that ill so we said not to bother and to continue with the tour. Note: It’s luck as to whether you will get along with your group. We were put with three immature, selfish girls. On the first day we made a huge effort to make conversation, they would answer short answers and never ask a question back. By the second day we just gave up and didn’t talk anymore. They didn’t respect the wildlife despite explanations from our guide and were late for everything. This didn’t effect my rating but just a warning it’s not always happy families :) To be honest there isn’t much choice in Atacama for good tour services but if you are sure you want to do the tour have a look around and bare in mind you won’t necessarily get the guide you want.
title: Mix of emotions!

We saw the old city, the markets and some beautiful buildings as well as learning the political history of the country. The price included a picnic in a park with some local fruit juices. We thoroughly enjoyed the day. You don't have to be ultra fit for this tour as stops are frequent to learn about the sights. Certainly a great tour and highly recommended.

review_text: A very good trip with TurisTour which included the Domeyko Mountains named after a Polish surveyor, Yerbas Buenos with ancient rock art ( petroglyphs), Rainbow Valley & finally the very small village of Rio Grande with their terrace farming. Throughout the trip you have great vistas & climbing the rock to see the petroglyphs was interesting and fun. As you cross Matancilla which is green due to the river and actually has trees - you enter Rainbow valley -stunning. The various colours of the rocka are due to the composition of the minerals - we stayed about an hour and the camera was on click overdrive.We also saw vicuna & llama which was an added bonus. Finally what made the trip so great was that we were only six -" Totti " our Argentinian guide was fantastic as she kept up a running steam of information, switching from Spanish to English without skipping a beat.We also had a delightful Chilean family onboard -a great morning out.We saw nobody else on our trip -just us & the landscape.

review_text: What can I say.... Impressive, exhausting and challenging. My wife and I have lucky with a marvelous Clima, not usual for Patagonia. Rain and wind at night... And sunny days for excellent trekkings. In importance of choice.... First: a good pair of trekking shoes, waterproof and double layer of socks... Inside a thin one, and outside a rough one Second: a good sleeping with a self inflating mattress Third: a good tent, windproof with aluminum poles... Especially for Gray and Pehoe winds Fourth: a comfortable backpack, with dry sacks inside

review_text: We (two girls travelling together) booked this course on a very short notice but it wasn't a problem at all for the team of the Chilean Cuisine Cooking Classes. Everything was well organized and ready for us the next day. Out of a big selection we chose 5 dishes of our choice. Together with our chef Inés we bought all ingredients fresh at the local market. She explained everything in detail and it was really easy to follow her instructions. She made us understand to not only "cook" as it is written in the recipes... but to give more attention to the smell and taste and also to the consistency of each dish while preparing the menu. In the end we had a very delicious and fresh meal including a starter and a dessert. Also included in the price for the cooking class was a selection of different wines from a very nice wine yard not far away from Valparaiso. We have been lucky cause we even went to this wine yard, called Emiliana, in the morning together with Rafael. We had a tour around with a guide who explained us the different sorts of their wine and each single step of their wine production. And in the end we also tasted a selection of their wines. So if you have the chance I recommend to do a combined tour of a visit to the wine yard and the cooking class. It's really worth it! Thanks to Inés and Rafael! We really enjoyed the day together with you! Thank you for sharing all these information with us!

review_text: I had three great days of fishing with Diego . Booking was easy online. Diego was a very good communicator. We had three very different fishing days. We fished for Sea Run Brown’s with streamers and local brown trout on dry flies. We fished bigger rivers, small, rivers, and spring creeks. Diego found fish each day. We caught a couple of trout over 25 inches which makes for spectacular pictures and great memories.

review_text: We did a 6-hour backcountry skiing tour near lonquimay volcano with APEX and it was honestly the highlight of a two-week skiing trip in Chile. Forrest was an amazing guide! it was our first time using touring (randonee) gear and setups and he was super helpful with tips and advice, he also brought a second guide along so it was just the four of us which really made us feel very looked after. We had an epic day hiking up and skiing down several very impressive lines, they knew just where to find the best snow at the perfect difficulty level, and Forrest was clearly very safety conscious, adjusting the tour to changing conditions and evaluating risk. Everything was very well thought through too - from lunch (provided and delicious) to the prep (we spoke before to check our level and goals). These guys are total professionals and just really fun to spend the day with too. Highly recommend.

review_text: I can't say enough about the great team at Summit Chile, the trekking group I went with on a hike up Villarica Volcano a few days ago. A few great things in particular about Summit Chile: 1. They were very easy to work with -- the information they provided was very clear, and they lived up to everything they indicated. They also didn't waste a minute of time, which I really appreciated given that we were already committing 3/4 of a day to the hike. 2. Where other guides were taking groups of 20+ people up the volcano, Summit Chile only takes a handful of people in each group, and has a ratio of no more than 3 guests per guide (our group consisted of 5 of us clients and 2 guides). 3. Claudio (co-owner) was our lead guide, and he was great -- interesting, fun but focused on our hike and especially our safety. I highly recommend Summit Chile and hope to be back later this year to do another volcano summit with them!

review_text: First of all - there's free transportation to Viu Monnet and Lapostolle from Santa Cruz hotel. You need to book in advance at the agency inside the hotel, one day ahead was enough (in April). We spent 2 days in Santa Cruz and wanted to visit 3 wineries (and save some money) so this is what we've done- First day - visited a small winery called OWM. Was fantastic, the owners shared with us their experience in creating a new winery. For us this was the best tour of the three. Second day - we took the free transportation at 09:45 from Santa Cruz hotel. Got to Lapostolle which was very beautiful and impressive. The tour was good and revealed how premium wines are made. From there the free transport took us to Viu Monnet (but you might need to get back to town to switch transport depending on the driver). We ate at the restaurant which is very beautiful. The tour was fine. Really gives you the opportunity to see a high scale traditional winery. This way we got to see different kinds of wineries in this valley and managed to save some transportation money.

review_text: After reading about the clear skies in the Atacama we had planned a family holiday to Chile to do some stargazing. I found Atacama Desert Stargazing after a good bit of web research and they did not disappoint. Jorge was easy to get ahold of, very flexible and made it generally easy to book, even when we had to reschedule after a missed international connection. As we are neophytes we booked the SAT1 course and it was a great experience. We were picked up at our hotel and driven about 20 minutes out of town. The evening began with a lecture on the history of astronomy and a discussion of telescopes and optics. We then spent the next several hours viewing 17 different astronomical objects (stars, globular clusters, nebulae and planets) through five or six different telescopes. The group only included nine people so we each had ample viewing time. Jorge also provided a full menu and an open bar as part of the evening. We would absolutely do this again and highly recommend the experience. Jorge is both highly enthusiastic, and while he is not a professional astronomer, he clearly knows a great deal about astronomy.
title: Great Experience with Atacama Desert Stargazing

review_text: We schedule all our Atacama tours with We Love Chile (8 scheduled, 7 carried out). From the beginning they were very attentive and helpful, answering questions, showing flexibility and helping us organize our trip in the best way. Overall, we really liked the tours, both the guides, the food offered and the general structure. They have good service via Whatsapp and the staff at the agency located in San Pedro is also very attentive, especially Felipe, who helped us several times. Negative points: - Twice we caught drivers who were racing a lot, and we are talking about dirt roads and often driving in mountains. We found it dangerous and reported it to the organization. - They always inform you of a pickup time at the hotel, which has an interval of 30 to 40 minutes so that you are available. This was a bit uncomfortable because we had to wait on the street without knowing when exactly they were going to pass by. This often happened in the middle of the night. - Most of the tours we took were outsourced by them to another local agency, and this was never informed during the hiring process. In fact, they always made it seem like everything was operated directly by them. They weren't bad, but it made us feel like we were paying extra for the We Love Chile structure and not getting exactly that. - We pay part of the package in advance and with a discount. However, by hiring directly from the agency in San Pedro, the cost of the tours was cheaper. So it's not worth booking in advance, I didn't feel there was any risk of us running out of space on the tour. - Super positive point: When we arrived in Atacama, we decided to cancel the trip up Cerro Toco (already booked) as we believed we wouldn't be able to climb the altitude. They canceled it promptly, without imposing any difficulties on us and refunded our money. Excellent experience. Oi We Lover! Ficamos felizes que, no geral, a experiência tenha sido positiva, especialmente no que diz respeito à flexibilidade e ao suporte da equipe. Agradecemos os pontos de melhoria que você compartilhou, pois são super importantes para continuarmos aprimorando nossos serviços. Esperamos ter a oportunidade de receber vocês novamente e proporcionar uma experiência ainda melhor! ❤️
title: I highly recommend it!

review_text: If you have decided to go for a walk of the city, Tours 4 Tips do an excellent walk in Santiago. The tours are in English or Spanish- separate guides. Be prepared to see all of the good stuff and walk for miles....so put on a good pair of shoes, take water, and do a toilet break before you start ! Its about 2 and a half hours long, with a Metro ride I advise you to do one of the tours on your first day of your holiday, that way you get a good bearing of the city, and can revisit any of the places the next day. We passed many places that we wanted to go back to, but then didn't have time to revisit everywhere The tour itself is very informative with the history of both the city and country Its totally feasible with children, ours are 6,8 12 and 13. (don't forget the water and toilet break comment) Dont miss this tour, just turn up at the right time in the right place in the right town ! We loved it :) Hey Ruth, Brilliant! review_text: Really exceptional! The guides are excellent. I had the chance to rub shoulders with them for a month, they invited me on several of their outings including a climb of the Villarrica volcano at dawn in ski touring. It became by far my favorite ski day. The ascent began in the dark, the column of glowing smoke makes the mountain almost alive, we quickly understand why the Mapuche gave it the name Rucapillan, or home of spirits. The clouds, very low that morning, cut us off from cities downstream, which intensified the Impression of greatness that the Milky Way brought above our heads. I imagined the sun rising over the Andes for a long time, but none of my dreams came close to what I had the chance to see. The warmth of the new rays and the vastness of the landscape are indescribable. The descent was long and the terrain very varied, the snow was powdery and reminded me a lot of my native Gaspé Peninsula. I loved my trip to Pucon and Mawida is largely why. 10/10
title: Exceptional!

review_text: I was anticipating a short hike or something similar to a hike, however this tour was essentially a ride up the Andes Mountains, we passed a couple of waterfalls (which we stopped at on the return to take pictures of) and a short walk around the bend of the lake (or lagoon). The scenery is wonderful and a sight to see, but I remember reading that we would go through a waterfall and tunnel, which we did not. We rode past a tunnel and stopped to look at a waterfall. The website states you can receive a $5USD discount if you meet at the office, which I did but did not receive a discount. Also the restaurant that they stop at for lunch was limited in choices of food, I will commend them for supporting local restaurants however. I had gone there to be able to take a few photographs of the puma and the condor, the most iconic wildlife in the park, but I ended up with literally 1000's of photos of both. It blew my mind how Miguel and his team could spot puma's from what seemed like km's away and could with precision determine where they would be after some time. I had, thanks to them, close encounters with the Puma and succeeded puma and condor, and all other wildlife there during the 5 days I did spend with them. We layed flat on our stomach to photograph armadillo in a meadow, and they took me to far-away places to try to spot and photograph waterbirds. Miguel is always in a good mood and "delightfully loco" but he took care of me with coffee and tea and maté ... picked me up by car at 06:00h in the morning after a 2 hour drive from Puerto Natales and dropped me back of at the Estancia where I stayed at 06:00h in the evening. He is a wonderful person and a joy to be with, he is an expert guide and goes to great lengths to show his world, his Patagonia. I can only hope that we will meet again, by preference in his backyard, Patagonia.

review_text: I booked a trip for our family of five, all adults, to Pumalin online through Alsur Expeditions, based in Puerto Varas. Gerardo and his team were first rate, and very accommodating to our needs. We booked well in advance, since we were combining this with a trip to Antarctica. This was good and bad. The bad: South American airlines are notorious for changing flights, and since we had scheduled only 36 hours to get from Ushuaia to Chaiten, there were some anxious times rearranging schedules because of flight changes. We were aware of the recommendation to add a lay day to the schedule, but ours was complicated with meeting the rest of our family in Santiago and a lay day wouldn't work. I used Despegar to book flights, and despite some interpretation issues, this worked well. The good part was that I was familiar with the procedures for rearranging plans. This proved helpful when we encountered an air traffic control strike in Santiago. Our flight to Puerto Montt, connecting to Chaiten got cancelled and we missed the Chaiten flight. An overnight bus, which was surprisingly comfortable, got us to Puerto Montt a day late. And on that day, a Sunday, there were no scheduled flights to Chaiten. We were in contact with Gerardo from Alsur through all this and he stayed on top of everything, including arranging a private charter to Chaiten. The Chaiten carrier, Pehuen, gave us nothing back for our missed flight, which I understand is standard practice. Just a word of caution on that point. As I kept repeating to our family, that's the nature of adventure travel. An English speaking guide from Alsur, Colin, accompanied us to Chaiten where we met a native gentleman, Alex, who drove us around the park and surrounding areas. Distances between trails and other features are far, and there is little public transportation. After getting to the cabins, which were unique and very charming, we had time for a hike to the catarats, double waterfalls each hundreds of feet high. The vegetation was lush, as this is a temperate rainforest. Both guides were very knowledgeable in local flora and fauna, and were a pleasure to be with. Dinner at the restaurant was a very cozy and an almost family like experience. Colin knew the managers well and pitched in to help out in the kitchen. The cabins were special. Rustic yet comfortable. We noticed that the door openings and ceilings were low. The doors were less than 72 inches and I could touch the loft over the ground floor. We later learned that this was an intentional feature to give the feel of old European cabins, built when our species was smaller. The were also Frank Lloyd Wright touches like a tree encompassed by a patio and a brook running underneath our cabin. It was a great place to cool beverages. The next day, as predicted by both our guides, the weather turned to rain. We enjoyed an ample breakfast and as a bonus our daughter, an amateur barista, had brought coffee from Santiago. With assistance from the kitchen, she treated us to wonderful fresh coffee. Not that the restaurant coffee was bad, it's just tough to beat fresh dripped brew. Later Alex picked us up and we hiked the sendero to Volcan Chaiten and nearly made it to the vista before turning around. We were socked in by the front, but it was still a presentation of erie beauty and other-worldiness. We all had good rain gear, but after several hours of steady rain, we were soaked. The perfect antidote for that condition was a drive to the local hot springs and a restorative dip. On the ride to the hot springs, Alex drove us past his old home, which had been destroyed in 2008 by the eruption of Volcan Chaiten. Volcanic ash covered it up to the window sills. Then to his new home a few blocks away, where he got towels for all of us, saving a long trip back to the cabins. Resilience is a strong characteristic of the area. The hot springs were convenient, encompassed by a concrete basin. An hour there and we were renewed. Back to the cabins to fire up the wonderful gas stoves and rig some clothes lines. Then a delightful dinner at the restaurant. We were the only Americans there, and although there were visitors of Chilean and many other nationalities, that was pretty much true for our entire visit to Pumalin. We missed the lost day in Pumalin, especially since it would have been sunny. I think the 3 days we had scheduled would have been about right for trekking. Alternatively, some extensive backpacking in the park would be a wonderful experience. The last day we had a 10 am ferry departure, which gave us time for more breakfast, and fresh brewed coffee. The managers were very accommodating and with Collins familiarity we felt warmly welcomed. The ferry ride was longer than normal, as a loading ramp in a nearby inlet that would have shortened the route was being repaired. Ah, adventure travel. The ferry was crowded with workers heading back to families in Puerto Montt for the Christmas holiday. It was overcast and the seas were up, conditions that have their own special attributes. It is a rugged and sparsely populated coast and we wondered how the isolated cabin dwellers spotting the hills managed. Alsur had arranged for a van to pick us up coming off the ferry in Hornopiren. It was clean, well maintained and very comfortable, as was Alex' van in Pumalin. Collin suggested a stop at some hot springs not far from the ferry landing, and we all agreed it would be welcomed. The hot springs were called Pichi-?, the local prefix meaning little or diminutive. Not sure of the rest of the name. The tubs were freshly rebuilt after a flood that had destroyed the old ones. They were naturally bedded pools demarcated by wooden staves There were many basins and a large changing hut. Collin talked with the manager while we were tubbing and told us later that the very large (some many square miles) surrounding property had recently been bought by an American from California, to be maintained in conservation. Part of the agreement was to allow the hot springs to be operated but no other development is to be permitted. We were quickly learning that frequenting hot springs is a lovely local past-time in this geo-thermally active region. Another ferry took us in the van on a short but thrilling ride over to Puerto Arena where Collin recommended stopping at a locally famous empanada cafe, a boliche de las empanadas. It is on the east side of the road about 200-300 yards from the ferry landing. Fantastic seafood empanadas in a rustic but clean setting. It even had a classic Chilean wood stove in the dining area. Then onto Puerto Varas and more adventures. Pumalin is a special place. It is currently immaculately maintained by a staff of volunteers who keep many of trails as neat as a country club, without affecting the feeling of being in the wilderness. There is much local pride in keeping this area place in it's natural state. A recent proposal to string power lines across it was fought and defeated. In the next few years, the current private status will yield to a National Park status as it passes from private to national ownership. It will be interesting to see if the same devotion to maintaining the wilderness feel will be maintained.

review_text: We have been travelling for 6 weeks around South America and this is by far the best thing we have done so far. A couple of points to be aware of. The website link on trip advisor doesn't seem to work but you can find the website at the same web address just using .com instead of .cl. We arranged this at really short notice but it wasn't easy to get in touch by phone as we think the numbers are mobile numbers and they are not often in range, keep persevering or email them. We sent an email the day before the trip and got a response in the evening with the trip sorted for the next day. We were after a full day trip but the morning session was booked so they arranged one for us with a 2pm pick up from Puerto Natales so assumed we were doing a half day trip but ended up doing a full day with a drop off at 9pm. Definitely worth it. The transfer cost 20,000 CLP (for the two of us) which is £20 there and back which is good value. The trip was 60,000 CLP each which was great value. If it's raining stick with it as you never know. When we got there it was throwing it down and looked like it was going to rain all day. The rain stopped in 30 mins and we finished in bright blue sunshine. Okay now the trip. Our guide Cristian was absolutely fantastic, really helpful, really knowledgeable, spoke great English which helped and was generally just a great guy. We can't thank him enough for making it a memorable trip. The ranch is in a really beautiful valley that most people wouldn't know existed as they generally fly past it heading to Torres del Paine. You can stay down at the ranch and do a multitude if other activities and if we had known this, it was something we would have done (you would probably want to have a car if you were going to do this) The trip was amazing, the views were some of the best we have seen even compared to going into the park which is probably due to the fact that you are just there on your own and also the sunlight that we had at the time. You head out of the valley up on to a ridge with great views along the way. On the ridge we had condors flying just above our heads. They are huge.... On the trip we saw parakeets (bizarre) and eagles. We stopped for lunch, bread, meat cheese, coffee,tea and there were snacks I.e. Cereal bars and fruit and nut mix. The horses were great, we did some trotting (optional) and there was potential for galloping In summary this is a great trip and is worth doing.

I went to Le Pangue observatory - very knowledgeable guide ! It was a very enriching experience !

review_text: Not a religious person, but this church was a beautiful thing to see. None of that boring old stone feel that makes everything feel like a medieval castle. The outside of the church is a beautiful yellow and purple combination. The inside is warm wood all over. Might be a short visit but something not to be missed especially when visiting Chiloe, as their churches are unique in the world. Located directly in front of the plaza. Fun fact, the bell towers on all churches in Chiloe always point towards the ocean.
title: Beautiful & Unique!

review_text: Tomas and his team were so professional and created a great experience for me and my family. They picked us up from the hotel, led us on a great adventure and ended the trip with a pizza and cold beer. Would recommend this to all friends visiting the area.

review_text: We booked through Viator, a private tour with guide Franco and driver Pablo. The whole day was great from start to finish. Franco met us promptly and Pablo’s car was clean and comfortable. Franco was engaging throughout. We stopped for breakfast and a toilet stop and fed some llamas. On to Valapariso, some history about the city and a really enjoyable walking tour with lots of interesting facts that perhaps other guides won’t tell you. Plenty of murals and lots to see and learn. Lunch was a short drive on in attractive Vina Del Mar, looking out on to the Pacific Ocean. Before heading back to Santiago we enjoyed a spectacular viewpoint of both Valapariso and Vina Del Mar. Would highly recommend the tour and especially Franco and Pablo. Review of: Santiago: Full day tour to Valparaiso and Viña del Mar city

review_text: Colchagua wine tours provided our transportation while we toured the wineries of Colchagua Valley. We had our own rental car but did not want to drive under the influence. The DUI laws in Chile are very strictly enforced with very stiff penalties. Francisco met us at the hotel and he was early each day. Even though we had only paid him for the wine tours when he found out we were going to walk to dinner he insisted on driving us each night at no additional charge. This was so nice of him. The drivers were very warm and friendly. We had Fidel who has such a beautiful smile and Victor who is really a nice guy.

I also went on the market tour with Rodrigo which was an excellent walking tour experience and learning of the market spots and their history behind. The architecture blends beautifully with the natural environment, and you'll feel like you're in Europe most of the time. The volcano dominates the landscape and if you have clouds...have patience! Clouds generally burn off in the afternoon.

review_text: We bought our ticket at the airport when we arrived, straight out of the baggage collect area. It was discounted 15%. Normally it sells for 20.000 Chilean pesos, we got it for 17.000. We bought it for the following day, so they can set it for the day you like. We received a booklet, map and a set of earphones, which we plugged in and chose the suitable language option on the bus. The commentary was informative without being overloaded and easy to understand. The trip itself was interesting, although slow in places due to the traffic, particularly in CBD and roadworks areas. There were enough stops, although not all were readily signposted in the same signage ... Some had coloured ones (red E like the company bus), others were just a big blue E on a white background. Not easy to spot initially. Overall I would recommend the trip as it allows you to see the best places in a very large city. If you use the hop on hop off then the time varies, but the round trip is about 2 hours. Dear Sasha: We appreciate your feedback on our Hop On - Hop Off and we thank you for recommend to other customers to make the tour of Santiago with Turistik. We try to provide the best service to give the best experiences to our passengers!

review_text: Inspiring but not instructive / interessante mas pouco informativo It’s a beautiful and organised museus. The exposition had interesting projects but there was a lack of explanation to the public as the science behind them. The price was good but it was very full. I recommend get informed on how to come back to the hotel With the metro and the bus, because it’s a long walk to the metro station, some taxis in the area refuse to get you to a distant hotel and there is no WiFi for uber. I recommend to arrive early because the touristic public in Santiago tend to quadruplicate around 11AM. Bom bonito e interessante, mas faltou informação científica por trás dos experimentos interativos para que o público entendesse do que se tratavam. E bom se programar pra voltar de metro e ônibus visto que a estação de metrô e longe do museu, os táxis do bairro se negam a te levar até o hotel na volta e não há Wi-Fi para chamar uber. Sugiro chegar cedo porque o público turístico de Santiago quadruplica próximo de 11 da manhã.

review_text: MMHR is free and it is entirely in Spanish although an English audio guide is available for a fee, which I found to be it very helpful. The museum tells the story of the Pinochet coup and the repression, exile, disappearance, incarceration, torture and murder of mainly young and educated and the resistance - both armed and passive - and eventual success in voting out Pinochet and his henchmen in 1989 - 16 years later. It gives a very good account of how Chileans dealt with the dictatorship and the class differences in opposition and impact not just political differences - although apparently not unrelated. It is a very good account of the resistance and the repression practices. Recommend hughly.
title: Excellent presentation of the 1973 to 1989era dictatorship

review_text: Last Sunday, December 28th, I was part of the al day wine tour of Colchagua valley. I like wine, but am by no means an expert. I know hat I like and what I don't and I wanted to get some experience with Chilean wine, which I don't normally drink. For me, this tour was perfect. The group was small - eight people, and I think we all had similar experience with wine. The day started early (7:30am) and we arrived at the first vineyard around 10:30am after picking up all the people and driving South. Over the day, we visited Apalta, Laura Hartwig, and Viu Manent. Each vineyard was different - from modern boutique, to local, to sprawling ranch style. Along the way, our guide Jose gave us some Chile wine history during the drive down, and each vineyard tour added there own personal pieces. All wine tastings were included in the tour price, as was lunch which we had a Viu Manent. The restaurant was great, with each person being ale to order off the menu, rather than having a set lunch for everyone. The pace of the tour was good, with time at each winery to taste and purchase wine. Laura Hartwig was a highlight for me. I found the wine there to be some of the best I tasted. I would recommend the tour to any of my friends traveling to the region, but see this being a great tour for anyone wanting to explore and get to know more about Chilean wine. Review of: Best Wine Tasting in Santiago
