review_text: I did The W from West to East. I stayed at Refugio Gray, Camping Paine Grande, Domo Frances, and Refugio Torre Central. I did the full-day Ice/Glacier Hike and the half-day Glacier Paddle Tours with Bigfoot Patagonia while at Refugio Gray. Both were incredible experiences. I believe that hiking The W from West to East is the better direction because the winds, in general, blow off the glaciers and through the park from West to East. I could not imagine hiking with a backpack, on the roller coaster terrain, with a head wind of 20 - 80 miles per hour. The facilities in the west half of the park(run by Vertice Patagonia) are generally nicer(and the food is better) than the facilities in the East side of the park(run by Fantastico Sur). The weather, as everyone will tell you, is unpredictable. In one 24 hour period I went from trying to stave off dehydration and heat exhaustion to worrying about thermal exposure and hypothermia. If you are interested in hiking The W don't do it as your first backpacking trip and come well prepared.
title: The most difficult but most incredible adventure of my life(so far)...

The Riverside Camp was really nice and very convenient to get into the park for each day's adventures. The beds were VERY comfortable and each Lotus Belle tent had heating, lights, power and wifi access. The private bathrooms had individual hot water heaters (hot showers!), towel warmers and even luxurious bathrobes. We enjoyed the group meals, the food was excellent and we sat with our tour groups and guides and were able to really enjoy each other. The views, wildlife, and daily adventures were fantastic. The team did a great job communicating with us on all aspects of planning for the trip and helping us during the trip when we had questions. We had a great time and would highly recommend! A great way to do with W Trek without having to go point-to-point. Wow! Thank you for such a fantastic review! We’re thrilled to hear you had an amazing time on the Fast Track W Trek and that Javiera, Cristóbol, and Vicente made the experience so fun and memorable. It’s great to know you loved Riverside Camp, the cozy tents, and delicious group meals. Patagonia is truly special, and we’re so glad we could help make your adventure smooth and unforgettable. We’d love to welcome you back for another trek someday! The Chile Nativo Team

review_text: This is a quick stop along the road for great photo op and a cool look at the road signs pointing to all the worldly cities. Worth if for anyone who has a little free time in the city
title: Always good to visit a mirador of an city you visit.. if at least for the photos

review_text: Went on the 10am tour with Max and had a wonderful time. Great mixture of practical modern information and history. A must do in Santiago Hola Scott R, Wow - A 5 Star review! Thank you so much. It means a lot to me and our whole Wally Team that you liked the Morning Tour in Santiago. Also our Afternoon Walking Tour at 3PM is a good opportunity to see our city with more historical informations. Hope you will have a great time in Chile. Saludos and enjoy your journey, Peter
title: Wonderful job by Max

review_text: The clock actually works. And the flowers are beautiful. Very different part of the Valparaiso area.
title: Unique scene in Valparaiso

review_text: Booked through our hostel, which used this company. Our guide, Jefferson, was awesome! So enthusiastic and knowledgeable about the rock and salt formations. His English was also great. He was enthusiastic about everything, including a small plant at the side of the road, and his enthusiasm rubbed off on everyone in the group.
title: Valle de la Luna tour

review_text: Fabulous experience, Jorge is a love of person, a great guide, the best part is that he is a teacher and teaches you many things about this wonderful country. I took 2 tours with Jorge, both excellent. Review of: Portillo and Laguna del Inca Tour Muchas gracias por compartirnos su experiencia, nos alegra mucho de que haya disfrutado junto a nosotros.
title: Maravilloso

review_text: It was a really good experience to make this tour with Nico & Co. The tour has include the right post to see and we try a lot of good typical food with was a lot of varieties! I recommend it a lot!
title: Santiago tour

review_text: Visual spectacle of the Atacama Salar. Dry, arid climate and yet a lot of beauty in the rock formations, mountains and lagoons. Too top.
title: Unique beauty in the region

review_text: We felt very well taken care of from the very first moment we arrived. Very well organized all together. The guides are super friendly and easy-going. Whenever we had any questions we had instant communication via WhatsApp, and we always got reminders and updates daily. Would definitively recommend this service to others!
title: Great experience

review_text: It was very touching for me to stand in front of the bust of president Salvador Allende.This place is definitely full of history!
title: Touching

review_text: Took a few hours at La Moneda to check the Egypt Exhibition at La Moneda. That was for sure one of the best exhibition I went to. It was totally worth attending.
title: Egypt Exhibition was great

review_text: We had a wonderful time on this tour. The pictures and history really give you a sense of how this city has come to be the way it is - and how destructive earthquakes can be. Reni was an outstanding guide. Would highly recommend this tour to anyone that wants to understand Valparaiso better and wants to have a fun afternoon.
title: Great tour with excellent guides

review_text: Excellent service. Cultural explanations and a friendly atmosphere of the group with which we visited many places. Very happy with everything.
title: Valle del Elqui

review_text: This was a very well organized trek with plenty of assistance (3 guides), who were all good hiking instructors and knowledgable about regional information. The size of the group was ideal for getting to know others without being slowed down by a large number of hikers. The drive from Santiago was also a good way to see local scenery. It's definitely an all-day adventure and not for travelers who are not in good shape. Review of: Andes Day Volcano 8K - Cajón del Maipo
title: Beautiful way to enjoy Chile

review_text: The experience had a rocky start as our tour guide, Fernanda, at first seemed to be a no-show. She showed up roughly five minutes past the stated 10am start time and seemed to think the tour started at 10:15 or 10:20am, but luckily everything improved from there. Apparently it was her first time officially leading the tour but she did a really great job. She was very knowledgeable about Chilean history, answered all the questions our group had (there were six of us in total, so we lucked out with a more intimate experience), and shared a lot of stories and experiences with good humor, insight, and charm. We appreciated everything she shared with us about Chilean history, politics, and culture and really enjoyed the four hours we spent with her.
title: Rocky start but ultimately a great experience

review_text: Wow Wow Wow! Pilar and her crew rock the kitchen. We foraged three different locations for 3 hours and then came back got to cook in her kitchen. The food was amazing. She should be a Food Network Star. I loved the experience with her and she is amazing.
title: Simply Amazing

review_text: I found too much! From the reception of the guides Bráulio and Janet to the experience on site. It was amazing to try the wines and cheeses and learn about the history of the place. Review of: From Santiago: Viña Concha y Toro Traditional Half-Day Tour Muito obrigado por compartilhar sua experiência conosco!
title: Very good!

review_text: Juan was terrific. He led us up to the highest viewpoint in Santiago and down through the streets of the city identifying landmarks and discussing the history of each. We felt safe and comfortable walking through Mercado Central—it seemed that Juan could be the mayor of the city. Ask for him! Review of: Private Santiago 3-Hour Walking Tour
title: Great walking tour!

review_text: We checked out of our hotel to catch this tour that was supposed to pick us up at 9am. At 9:10 we contacted them as no one arrived. They said something happened to the driver and they were looking into it. By 9:30 they contacted us to so they could not reach the driver and would have to cancel for the day. What an inconvenience - we checked out of our hotel and had no place to stay until we could check in at next location at 3pm. This company is terribly unprofessional and unreliable. Even worse still waiting on a refund… Thank you for sharing your experience with us! We're truly regretful of the inconveniences that took place and we promise to work much more so situations like this don't happen anymore. We'll work hard offer you a better service in the future, MTO Tour Team
title: Cancelled after tour was to begin

review_text: Overall Impressions - Chile Off Track would not be my first choice when booking a tour in Chile. I spoke with various western branded hotels during this situation and none of them had heard of this company. - If you are looking for someone to coordinate your activities for a smaller-type group, Chile Off Track may give you a better experience. - As the organizer, I will say that I did not have issues working with the management and I hope that this becomes a learning lesson for them. - In regards to the tour operators, I was very excited to work with Tessa and left unbelievably disappointed in her service and behavior. - They handled our complaint very poorly, and it has resulted in many upset students and a lot of time spent after the end of the trip. Key issues: 1. They were the wrong fit for our group: -- We were a group of 23 international graduate students and two faculty who hired Chile Off Track for our fun weekend events in between two weeks of our studies. -- Chile Off Track is a small operation that although emphasizes personalized tours, are really more a point to point tour company. I imagine they are great for tourists who need help arranging and coordinating fun activities in a foreign place. -- Chile Off Track is knowledgeable about the different sites in Chile and accommodating to your group needs. They will work with your group to get you the activities you want at a reasonable price. -- Although I had had a call with our tour guide, Tessa, prior to the trip to highlight that we wanted a tour that focused on the history/information of the places we were visiting it was clear that this isn’t their forte, and if it is, it wasn’t indicated in their performance. 2. Terrible attitude of the tour guides -- We got off on the wrong foot due to our large group being ~20 minutes tardy but despite a number of attempts to assuage the situation, the tour operators did not act professionally. I had several talks with our guides Tessa and Juana, regarding their tone of voice and their abrasive attitude towards the students. After three separate attempts early on asking them to change their behavior they continued to talk down to the students, scold students who needed to use the bathroom, etc. -- Considering that we had faculty and a clear tour leader, and I had discussed with them on the objective of the day – to learn about the history of Valparaiso, it would have been very easy to start over and enjoy the remainder of the day. -- The tour guide unprofessionalism is the biggest issue that I have with the tour because there were a number of chances to rectify the situation. There was no need for it to escalate. This was an unfortunate situation that should have been turned around considering that we were paying clients who were alerting them to the fact that we were not getting the service we were looking for. 3. Behavior of management towards the customer complaint -- We filed an official complaint with the company after the first tour. The way the company handled the situation after the trip has been very unprofessional. Regardless of the size of the company, when you have a disgruntled customer it is important to understand what went wrong. -- Instead, the mangement chose to take sides and aggressive actions such as recording the telephone conversation with us without letting us know it was being recorded. -- I do believe that because they are a relatively small company their first response might be to get defensive, and when you feel that way you often react without thinking. Also, we held the conversation relatively near the date of the tour, I believe that emotions were high on both sides, which usually leads to less productive conversations. -- In the end, I currently have a number of upset students who paid for a less than fulfilling tour not to mention all the time that I have had to dedicate to resolving a situation that could have been easily rectified. Overall, Chile Off Track wasn't the tour company for us and may be better suited for your needs. I would strongly recommend stating your travel objectives and getting a clear breakdown of your trip should you work with them. I do beleive that they gave us a fair price and had the tour day been managed differently, we would have had a different outcome. Some individuals of this group have behaved in such unpleasant way that these 2 days are marked as black pages in our 6 year history. They arrived late for every tour which caused logistical problems in the planning of the tours, delayed the tours while we were on a walking trip, did not assemble when the guides were giving information, in summary: it felt for our guides as if they were managing a group of young children rather than adults. As management, we proactively sent an email after the first day suggesting a feedback conversation with 1 representative to help us to understand what had happened. In the mean time we offered the group a drink on the house for the next day in response upon their request for Chile Off Track to pay lunch for 25 people as they were not content with the tour. Unfortunately they declined the gesture of a drink. On both days we had our 2 desperate guides numerous times on the phone asking for help to manage the situation as they have never been treated in such a disrespectful way by any of our clients. With a member of the Faculty Management Team we have decided to waive the participation costs of the 2 last minute passengers (417 USD in total) on the first day not to cause any more dissatisfaction. The member of the Management Team has also admitted to our guides that this behaviour of the group has been a pattern throughout their trip. With already having received the feedback from our guides we entered the feedback conversation with the representative. After having heard his feedback we shared with him that we have received the same comments from our guides about the group’s behaviour. We explained to him that we have been working for a number of years with these 2 expert guides in particular and that we have **never** received a negative comment. We told him we would check back with our guides again and meanwhile contact the Faculty Management to find a possible solution. The representative told us he was not interested in feedback about his group’s behaviour and that he could perfectly manage his group. He gave way his true intentions of the “feedback” conversation and claimed a partial refund of the tour, otherwise he threatened to post negative comments about our “little tour company”. Meanwhile we have contacted Faculty Management and addressed the misbehaviour of this group of students, to explain how they have used the Faculty’s name to enforce discounts and finally to threaten a small company with negative reviews on TripAdvisor. In the mean time we have reached the agreement that only one person would write a review representing their group in order to stop the stream of libel by the other students, which for us seems fair. We have worked very hard in the last 6 years to establish the boutique brand of Chile Off Track and as an owner I find it very disappointing that the tours with this group has not worked out the way we both would have wished for. Chile Off Track is a Boutique Tour Company that organizes semi private tours for the sophisticated traveller. Most of our clients stay in boutique hotels or bigger 4 /5 * Hotels and we work closely together with their international concierges. We have been awarded 4 years in a row the Certificate of Excellence on TripAdvisor and have received 156 reviews, of which 143 are 5* reviews. Most of our clients have enjoyed higher education and are well mannered which contributes to a pleasant trip experience.
title: Not the right fit

review_text: We went with my daughters and my husband to the Osorno volcano. We rent a car. The road is all paved and in perfect condition. From the beginning the beauty of the place seduces you. You can make stops to take photos and little by little you can see Lake Llanquihue in all its splendor. When we arrived at the ski center we took the chairlifts (cost 27 thousand to go up two sections) and up there we could even play in the snow. The guys in charge are very friendly and cordial. An unforgettable experience!
title: Trip to the Osorno volcano

review_text: My husband and I spent the first full day of our marriage hiking to Cerro Castillo with our fly fishing guide, Nico, and a hiking guide, Leo, who was working for Mary Brys' Senderos Patagonia. The scenery, the accommodations, the pace of the hike, and the company were all outstanding, but there was one moment in particular we know we will cherish forever: When we finally reached the glacier after several hours of hiking, Leo surprised us by pulling a bottle of champagne from his backpack and toasting our wedding. Apparently, Mary Brys had hid the bottle in Leo's backpack before our hike just to make our trip that much more enchanting. That's the kind of personal touch that turns 'vacations' into memories. Thank you Senderos Patagonia!!
title: Full of surprises!

review_text: Excellent agency very good drivers with the best guide Francisco providing with culture and knowledge excellent food and good recommended slingshot 💯% Review of: Tour to the Hidden Lagoons of Baltinache
title: Unforgettable magical landscapes knowing the licanantay culture and the resources of their lands beautiful and rewarding

review_text: The museum presents the history of the miltary coup in Chile in 1973 and the subsequent human rights violation perpetrated by the Pinochet regime in a very powerful and moving way. The stories of Chileans tortured and murdered by the regime are compelling and heart-breaking, especially those who "disappeared." Highly recommended.
title: Powerful Presentation

review_text: I enjoyed our visit and esp. liked the tiled floors with a great pattern. Other than that, I felt the church was not as impressive and others I have visited in Mexico.
title: Nice cathedral but not as impressive as those in Mexico

review_text: Very cordial in agenda the time and respect this same. Plus very good massage therapists. Excellent place to take a break.
title: Very good, 100% recommended.

review_text: In addition to transfers from Santiago Airport to Valparaiso, Michael suggested the scenic route including the Emiliana Vineyards in Casablanca Valley, and an authentic seaside lunch in Quintay (he of course had eaten at all the restaurants there and knew the best value). After lunch he took us to a private museum of Chilean artifacts and off beat inventions, and introduced us to the owner. What a great way to start our vacation instead of dealing with car rentals in a foreign country. And when the time came for us to rent a car 2 days later, Michael took us to a local company and negotiated the deal at a good price. To top it off, 3 days later he met us in Santiago, took the car off my hands, and returned it to Valparaiso (his idea). How nice is that? If you want to land in Chile and start on a relaxed fun note, do yourself a favor and get Michael to pick you up. Review of: Discover the treasures of Valparaiso with a local
title: Fantastic way to start our trip in Chile

review_text: Passeio excepcional para Portillo com o guia Matheus Andrade. Unique experience from beginning to end. Definitely one of the best guides I've ever had the pleasure of meeting.
title: Unparalleled experience with the Guide Matheus Andrade

review_text: My husband and I booked the Marques de Casa y Concha tour for us and our inlaws who are in their 70s. There are 2 of these tours per day offered in English. Book the late tour. Then you will not be rushed. The tour consists of walking around the vineyard, seeing the outside of the house, tasting the grapes and getting fabulous photos. There is no information on the making or bottling of the wine. This is more the history of the vineyard. After, there is a flight of wines to try with bread and cheese. The sommelier was very informative and friendly. We were not in the least bit rushed. There is a restaurant on site, but we didn't visit it. If you have to stay stay in Santiago, this is a good tour.( If you have an entire day, get a driver and go to Santa Rita winery and book lunch.)
title: Fun for older travelers

review_text: Excellent guide, fun filled walk in small group to major historic attractions. No set fee but suggested "tip" makes this a good vale
title: Take a fun walking tour

review_text: This attraction is only interesting if you're really, really into Neruda or in architecture. The view is great, and that's about it. I'm certainly a poet fan but you won't find a lot of poerty here. There is an audio tour (in English too) that tells all kind of uninteresting details about the house and Nerudas life. For example about a wooden horse in his living room, or about the shoes his wife wore. Students pay 1.500 pesos Normal price 4.000 pesos Prices include the audio tour.
title: Only for the view

review_text: Very nice place. The paths are very well marked. You can take the tour on foot as by vehicle. It is a place where it does not require much effort to reach the viewpoints and is highly recommended for the whole family. The circuit is completed between 1 and 2 hours approximately. It is important to purchase tickets online before arriving at the place.
title: Beautiful landscapes

review_text: This walk in Huerquehue national park was pretty strenuous!! It was mostly uphill but worth the views at the top!
title: Good walk

review_text: You must have a really nice day if you are to see the mountains, the shopping centre attched is excellent and worth a few hours inside.
title: Good views

review_text: I rented a bike for a day with Elki magic and I couldn’t recommend this experience enough. First, the consultation with Adeline was great, she gave a map and explained everything patiently and in detail. You’ll even get some discounts for the beer tour and the solar restaurant when showing the map. The bike is in excellent condition, equipped with a helmet, lock and spare tire and pump. Then the trip itself was amazing. I particularly enjoyed the tasting tour at Aba and the views along the way. The weather was amazing, sunny but not too hot. The road was also pretty quite, the perks of traveling low season. Thank you Elki magic for offering this amazing experience. Special thanks for Adeline for all the great tips she gave (food, how to go to the different vineyard and distillery independently, and esp. how to get cash without commission :)). My recommendation for those who will do the bike tour is to download maps.me (if you don’t have online gps), esp. for the beginning of the trip as there are some intersections (unless you have an amazing brain memory that can remember every detail explained earlier).
title: Amazing day with a bike tour

review_text: Such a beautiful experience!! Will never forget it and is definitely worth your time. I learned so much about the land, culture, and myself ❤️ Review of: Gong Bath in the Magic Forest in San Pedro de Atacama
title: 10/10 experience

review_text: Located 30 minutes’ drive from San Pedro de Atacama, at 3.500 meters altitude, it is a beautiful place to relax. These hot springs have a temperature of 30 ºC and consist of 8 pools, some with waterfalls ! To avoid crowd, I recommend you to arrive around 10 o´clock in the morning and during the week. If you are lucky, you will get a whole pool just for you ! Rooms to change are available and toilets. Bring water and food.
title: GREAT EXPERIENCE !

review_text: Trip name: Ruta de los Salares The landscapes during the Rohas de Salta trip were breathtaking, and we had the chance to enjoy a breakfast and later also lunch with a great view of a volcano in the background. Our guide shared with us a lot of interesting information in 3 languages English, Portuguese, and Spanish, which made the experience accessible and engaging for everyone. Important! the tour doesn’t include entering the lakes, only admiring them from viewpoints. One suggestion for improvement: it would be helpful if the organizer sent a quick message via WhatsApp a few minutes before arriving at each pickup location. Currently, the driver only calls upon arrival. A brief heads-up could make the process of gathering the group smoother and more efficient.
title: A scenic adventure worth taking

review_text: This is a great trip if you are properly prepared for the amount of time it takes to get there. The road up and over the foot hills (12,000 ft foothills) is amazing all by itself. To see some of the larger tour buses that actually make it through is even more amazing. Once there, the view of the lake, and Llama like Vicunas (if they are there, as they were for us) was awesome. One thing that was not clear when we signed up for our tour in San Pedro was the fact that we needed to have additional pesos along to pay for the admission fees into these park areas. That said, we are glad we took the tour vs driving there on our own. The guide provided significant amounts of local information.
title: Very High Country Adventure

review_text: Lovely park in the center of Santiago, near Lastarria. Beautiful landscaping and fountains. There are great views from multiple spots but the best is from the top.
title: Beautiful views!

review_text: Look, if you don’t want to experience a huge and busy mall, don’t go. If you want a “rustic” Chilean experience, don’t go. If you need to shop in large department stores or want to people-watch and you don’t mind the upscale environment, US-like consumerism, and chain stores like H&M, go for it. I actually appreciated the Jumbo grocery store on the ground floor. Word to the wise, the food court (on the top level of the mall) gets crazy in the afternoons. The cinema was great, I’ll add. Overall, it’s a monstrosity but it is what it is.
title: It is what it is...

review_text: We have never seen so much salt before that was carved into so many different shapes. A pity that so much of the area is now off limits.
title: Certainly a different experience

review_text: As most of the museums of the world Bellas Artes is closed on Monay. Bellas Artes is an museum that is arranged to get classic education. You see the development of art in Chile also you can admire pictures of European artists.
title: Never Mondays

review_text: I wouldn’t say this was a pleasant experience by any stretch. I booked this tour, looking forward to it, but was informed a day in advance that it had been cancelled due to insufficient participants. What irked me more was the lack of proactive communication from their end. I wasn't notified about the cancellation until I reached out to inquire. I attempted to contact them through WhatsApp and sent over a dozen messages but it seemed like they were not even checking their messages. It was utterly frustrating and a complete waste of my time. The lack of professionalism and courteous communication left a very bitter taste. Review of: balmaceda and serrano glacier navigation with lunch
title: Disheartening Experience with Unprofessional Handling

review_text: Nice park to stroll through although as is often the case, many stray dogs around. The public have nicely made little dog houses for them though. It's very big and well maintained so you should always be able to find a clean and comfortable spot for a chill.
title: Nice for strolls and monuments

review_text: I hired this agency to organize tours for six dear friends on vacation in Atacama and Uyuni. Everything promised was delivered. The value for money was excellent. In Uyuni the quality of the accommodation was surprising, simple but with nice beds, blankets, towels, hot water and excellent food, including cafes and picnics on the road. I recommend it and would repeat it.
title: Value for money, quality and honesty

review_text: We were there on a Saturday morning. Entrance was free and much of it was in retirement. There was an exhibition of articles from Morocco. The building is very beautiful, with a huge central hole.
title: Interesting place, but was in retirement

review_text: Turismo Layana provided the bus and driver for our tours around the Atacama region. The driver Miguel was cheerful and knowledgable explaining information about the different herbs in the region and what they would be used for by the indigenous people. Would highly recommend this company for its safety and relative comfort when in this region.
title: Great quality tour company with knowledgable drivers

review_text: Driver Felipe is congratulated. Always went well, without running, taking care of everything. Best tour driver. The guide Ivan was sensational. Congratulations. They deserve a note of 11.
title: Guide Ivan and driver Felipe are congratulated

review_text: I took this tour with 3 friends, it takes all day and it was amazing. Valentina was the guide, she is so nice, she helped us when we got lost in the city, she is very clear with the explanations, she knows a lot and it is evident she loves what she does. The timing was very good at every place we visited, the driver was very good as well. Congratulations, i loved this tour and i plan to take the others next time i go to Iquique!
title: Great guide and beautiful day for Pica&Salitreras

review_text: We were running late... no problem. Very clean car, curteous driver. Well recommended rather than the local drivers harassing as soon as you exit Review of: Private Transfer from Santiago Airport to Santiago Thank you for your comment, we're happy to know you had a good time with us! Don't hesitate to contact us the next time you or your friends want to come to live another gratifying experience in one of our tours. Best regards, MTO Tour Team
title: Welk looked after bu Raul

review_text: My favorite spot in Santiago is the Parque Metropolitano and -among its hills- the Cerro San Cristóbal. Next to the zoo one can take a funicular or cable train to the peak of the hill, although some athletic minded youths do cycling or jogging all the way up. On top of the Cerro there is a Virgin statue, a chapel and of course souvenirs stores. From the terraces one can enjoy the best view of the city, and unfortunately watch the air pollution that still plagues Santiago. Years ago I also enjoyed taking the teleférico, a cable car to another hill, but this service has been suspended for safety reasons.
title: My favourite spot in Santiago

review_text: Punctual, friendly and professional drivers. I would just add that at the airport they have to say where to take the transport, as in the app it said nothing.
title: Good experience

review_text: Incredible tours, all the guides were polite and helpful, especially guide Sara on the Portillo and Laguna del Inca tour, she is wonderful, super intelligent, she spoke at every point of the tour, giving explanations and stories about the place, attentive to everyone, she provided us with a Beautiful and delicious picnic, the group was super interactive, in short it was unforgettable ♥️
title: Portillo Tour

review_text: We bought tickets from the tourist office outside our hotel and despite some misleading directions we flagged a bus when it stopped at a traffic light! This is a great way to get a feel of the city and to see where the main attractions are. The headphones are in various languages and we managed to get off at the funicular and complete the tour from there. Highly recommended for anyone passing through Santiago with limited time to hand. We appreciate your comment dear traveler, it is very important for us to know about your experience.
title: A great way to see the sights

review_text: We rented snow gear and it came in poor condition. Holes patched and paying a higher price than others. 30,000 pesos for the entire set. Gloves came with the inside tips torn apart, the pants of one person in our group were patched and tore when we arrived at the park. The zipper on the blouse fell off A child's torn glove got wet in the snow.
title: Avoid clothing rentals

review_text: Pablo was a great tour guide. He was engaging, attentive and very knowledgeable of the area. I would consider him top notch and highly recommend him. As a side note, Alex was our driver and he was exceptional. He nevigated the traffic and narrow streets with ease. Review of: Valparaiso Port and Vina del Mar Full-Day Tour from Santiago In Stamps we count with a team of passionate profesional guides and drives such as Pablo and Alex. We're glad you had a great time with them, thank you for your review.
title: Tour from Santiago

review_text: The Valle de la Luna is close to San Pedro de Atacama and is a great evening trip. We started our visit after 6 pm and got a chance to do everything, including climbing to the top to see a great view of the big crater and the entire area. They then take you to a wonderful overlook to watch the sunset. Nice trip and a good introduction to the incredibly weird landscape of the Atacama.
title: Sunset in the desert

review_text: Jose is a very good trainer and a very nice person. Sandboard was hard for me but i had lot of fun! Highly recomended. yes that is what we looking for adventures who want to have lots of fun in the dunes !!! thanks for your comment we feel glad to have enthusiastic visitors like you ,
title: Sure you'll have fun

review_text: Great tour to give you an overview and background of Santiago! Nicole Gutierrez was very helpful with directing us towards the best things to experience! Review of: Tourist bus around Santiago for a day Good afternoon, thank you very much for your comments regarding your experience with us. It is a pleasure to know that you enjoyed the experience, the service in general and the staff. Best regards!
title: Great tour!

review_text: don't miss this house! La Sebastiana in Valparaiso may be the strangest of the three Neruda houses. Built to look, in many parts, like a ship, it has some narrow stairways and five floors. Amazing collections of antique maps and things like music boxes and an old merry-go-round horse. This home was looted after the 1973 military coup, but beautifully restored and re-opened in 1992. Highly recommended!
title: If you love Pablo Neruda...

review_text: Great trip and we also went on the Valle de la Luna. Well organized, great scenery and fantastic guide called Marlon. Would do it all again so book with Inta Para and have a fantastic experience. Review of: Red Stones and Altiplanic Lagoons
title: Great time

review_text: Everything is very beautiful, each tour is a wonderful experience!!! Very well prepared team!! Our guide Bastian was TOP! Trip to Portillo was what we liked most 🥰 Oi We Lover ❤️! Ficamos felizes que o passeio tenha sido incrível, especialmente em Portillo. Agradecemos pelo carinho e por compartilhar a experiência com a gente! Até a próxima!
title: Wonderful tour!

review_text: Unique cemetery is worth walking through. Interesting variety of memorials. One section is devoted to all German "residents."
title: Lovely & interesting cemetery

review_text: This was my second tour with this company and it came at the recommendation from another tourist and it did not disappoint. We got to see the sea lions! Then onto the beautiful Valparaiso. The colors and artwork are so beautiful I could have wandered that town for hours. Our guide Pablo was so knowledgeable. I was lucky enough to have him for 2 tours, this and a wine tour! Our driver Mr. Pipe was able to navigate those Valparaiso streets like a pro. I highly recommend this tour and if you get Pablo, you will have a blast! We had an unfortunate experience for our of our tour members and Pablo handled it with grace and compassion and really worked to continue to make the experience positive for all of us. 10 out of 5 stars! Review of: Valparaiso Port and Vina del Mar Full-Day Tour from Santiago Our guides will go above and beyond to ensure great experiences no matter the circumstances. We're glad you had a great time. review_text: Torres del Paine National Park is being loved to death and the concessions (like Fantastico Sur and others who run the refugios) control seem to outweigh park management and habitat concerns. This is a truly magnificent and biologically important area and I can understand everyone’s desire to experience this place. Despite researching the park, reading reviews and travel guides we still weren’t prepared for how very very crowded the W-trek was. The sheer volume of people and supplies brought in to the refugios made for constant traffic. We visited at the end of the main tourist season in mid-March. Torres was our final week in Patagonia after spending a week hiking at El Chalten and the another in the Bariloche region. We started our W-trek at Refugio Paine Grande, staying 2 nights, then hiked eastward, staying 2 nights a Domos Frances and 2 nights at Refugio Chilano. We hiked to Glacier Grey the first day and back to Refugio Paine Grande for the night. On all trails we were constantly jostling with other trekkers, passing them, some passing us, other going the opposite direction. The weather started out rainy so major portions of the trails were muddy or had running water to wade through that people tried to skirt thus widening the trails. Between the trail conditions and the people, it was hard to get into a “hiking rhythm” and immerse yourself in the beauty of the landscape and the place. This was NOT a wilderness experience. The only day that was relatively free of people was when we took the “short cut” (atajo) trail from Domos Frances to Refugio Chilano. We weren’t able to hike the French Valley (Valle del Frances) during our stay at Domos because it was closed due to rainy weather with possibility of erosion and landslides. Not surprising given the use these trails are getting. Both arrival at and leaving the Park was pretty confusing and park personnel were not helpful about shuttles or travel to trail heads or catamaran dock but they do take your fees and give presentations about park safety. We were grateful to have organized everything way in advance. In reality schedules aren’t really reliable or even accurate but somehow work. We managed after some persistence and lots of waiting. This park is not that easy to get to, it is almost at the ends of the earth, it is very expensive and the trails aren’t that easy to hike so it is amazing that it is so crowded. Not all trekkers/hikers looked well prepared or familiar with wilderness ethics. The O-trek is more challenging so I imagine you can get away from the crowds in that area of the park. Our last full day we spent hiking up to the iconic Torres, joining 100’s of other folks mostly in awe-struck admiration for this place. It was a beautiful day up a somewhat steep trail through very special southern beech forests to stunning vistas. We were used to the crowds by then but it would have been much more peaceful with fewer people who were clearly there to “party”. I guess we expected more of the sense of wilderness we experience in the western United States in the Sierra Nevada or Cascades mountain ranges. Not even close at Torres! Maybe the Sierra would have been like Torres if Disney had developed Mineral King those many years ago. Thank the wilderness gods that did not happen!
title: Unprepared for the Crowds

review_text: At the end of March, my husband and I booked a daytrip from Santiago to Aconcagua National Park with Andes Wind. Guide Christian picked us up at 07h15 in our hotel, to which we returned around 19h15. We paid in Euro’s (€100 p.p.). There were 2 other couples on the trip, making the total of participants 6. This was a comfortable size of the group, for both the drive in the van and for the walk. The drive to Argentina is scenic and doable (3h each way). Christian was of great help by getting us swiftly through border-control. The walk itself was short (5 km) and easy (indicated paths), but very beautiful. It was impressive to see the highest mountain of the Americas, and the vistas on the surrounding landscape are simply stunning. Due to this, we even consider this walk as one of our best, after having hiked for 3 weeks around Chile (Atacama, Easter Island, Patagonia). Personally, I would prefer to hike longer and this may be requested if you are travelling in a group. However, this means that you will be back in Santiago much later (+ 2,5h). On our way back we stopped at a classic ski-resort and a small food market (with fresh fruit and vegetables). Make sure you bring your passport (incl. Chilean border paper), sunscreen, warm clothes and wind jacket, and enough water with you on this trip. To conclude, we recommend this beautiful and easy-going daytrip if you are looking for an activity (after having spent already 1-2 days) in Santiago. It is fun to go to Argentina. It is something you would not easily undertake and arrange yourself (with the hassle of car hire, self-drive, border control etc.). Very much worth it! Thanks for your description and opinon. Going with small groups is the best way to enjoy places like this.

review_text: Joaquín did a great job showing me around Valparaiso in November. I had contacted him on the web before heading down to Valparaiso and set the plans in motion. Honestly, I knew everything would go well or hoped so but being 5,000 miles away it crossed my mind that maybe setting up everything for the tour in advance and out of the country was not a good idea. THAT feeling was completely uncalled for on my part. Joaquin sent an email the day before and picked me up at the home, showing slightly before his schedule, just so he would be on time. At this point in my trip, my friends had went back to the states so it was just me. I mentioned that to Joaquin and instead of getting another vehicle for the trip, we used his truck. It was awesome. After arriving in Valparaiso he found a great parking location and we started to tour the city, and what a beautiful city it was especially the street art. Joaquin grabbed a couple of pic of me with the street art and later brought me to an excellent restaurant for lunch. The restaurant had the most awesome view of the city and port along with out of this world food. The restaurant was at the Fauna Hotel and, if you are in the city, at least have drinks there the view is awesome. I can't thank Joaquín enough for the great tour! I do plan to go back and do more in and around Santiago, the country of Chile is outstanding. I love it. Hey Gary! Thanks for trusting us! I'm very happy to hear that you enjoyed our country and the perfect day we had in Valparaiso. I hope you can come back so we can visit other destinations of this unique country. Take care, Joaquin

review_text: I used to live on the east coast and used the subway to commute for years. This metro system is easy to navigate, clean, and the Chileans are orderly and polite on the cars. You have the option of buying a transfer ticket to shift over to the bus system and extend the range of your trip outside the metro. The stations and cars are clean, safe and easy to navigate. I recommend this as the primary way to see Santiago, because there are stops very close to all points of interest.

review_text: We had a great tour with Felipe! There were only 4 people in our group. Felipe provided a lot of information. We heard many facts about the country and culture on our way to the markets. Felipe was always very mindful of the traffic and safety. The biking was easy and enjoyable. At the market we tried delicious local food (Sopaipillas) and were able to purchase fresh fruits. Felipe answered all of our questions in great detail. He knows his city and country very well and has a good sense of humor. We can strongly recommend him as a tour guide. review_text: Our group of 13 took part in a 2 day trip out into the hills. Although I think that they don't normally run it during the winter period, Ellen & Harry were happy to move things around to offer an adventure that worked for us. Everything was really smooth from the start; Tito the driver picked us up from downtown Santiago to take us out to the ranch with no problems. After a delicious welcome lunch we saddled up (complete with hats and ponchos) and headed into the hills on the horses. The animals are all great, very sure-footed and easy to control, even for complete novices. A fantastic dinner, home-made pevre and pisco sours, and the BBQ was genuinely some of the best food that we'd had during our 3 weeks in Chile. Rigo, Victor and the rest of the arrerios are all excellent with the horses and you feel like you're in safe hands throughout - they even tolerated our (fairly dubious) fireside singing with a smile! A great bunch of guys and very professional. If you're after something like an authentic Chilean horse-riding experience, this will definitely not disappoint. I'd recommend this to anyone who'd like a bit of adventure or just to escape from the bustle of Santiago for a day. Great stuff and many thanks again to Ellen & Harry for making this such a special trip! Thank you. THis was a big experience for us too as we don't often take such a big group and we have never camped out in August (midwinter) before so it was a learning experience for us. So glad it all worked out!

review_text: Juan was the best tour guide I could've asked for! Knowledgeable, incredibly kind-hearted, and genuinely loved showing us nature. 10/10 experience Review of: Glacier Hike 16K- El Morado Natural Monument, San Francisco Glacier Private Tour

review_text: Maria Abud – Patagonia Trails We just returned to the US after a visit in Puerto Varas and want to tell you that the best time of our trip were the two days we spent with Maria Abud of Patagonia Trails. Briefly we were looking for low-medium trekking with Maria and she took our group on a rainy day hike to Alerce Andino National Park and the Salto Rio Chaica and a sunny beautiful day hike to the Vicente Perez Rosales National Park where we hiked up to the red crater of Osorno and continued with a walk along the Solidaro trail to Petrohue Falls and one of the nearby lakes. It was incredible, good for individuals in the group who had not done much hiking before (but got the appropriate shoes and gear before getting there) as well as myself who has done a number of trails in the pacific northwest. She was able to communicate and discuss the flora and fauna we encountered and engage the group. Communications throughout the process, as we booked her earlier on, were just right. When we return to Patagonia we will not hesistate to book with her again, nor will we hesitate to book a more extensive trek now that the group has more confidence in themselves. Andy K

review_text: Our tour group made a too short visit to the Fonck Museum on our recent trip to Valparaiso and Santiago, Chile. We only had about 45 minutes on the schedule, but we could easily have used two or three times that long to adequately cover all the exhibits in the museum. Although the Museum is small and compact, it is filled with many fascinating and informative exhibits - just too many to cover thoroughly in the time we had allotted! Even disembarking from our bus, we were met by one of the Easter Island "Heads" placed outside the entrance. After entering the small and compact museum building, the exhibits are laid out in four main gallery rooms with much detail and explanation. This is definitely something that must be seen. And don't miss the discreet display of the three shrunken heads. Fascinating throughout.

review_text: What a lovely surprise in the middle of urban, industrial Santiago! We took the metro and walked a few blocks to the winery, where we were greeted by Andrea, who then took us on a bilingual (English and Portuguese) tour of the historical winery. There were about a dozen people in our group, half Brazilians and half Americans who turned out to be Cuban and Argentine. I particularly enjoyed that the tastings occurred at different points throughout the tour: A white in the restored dining/meeting room, a red in the upstairs storage and processing room (now an events area) and another two reds in the Bordeaux and Bourgogne-style cellars. This winery has a lot of history and is one of the oldest and most traditional in Chile. It was a great place for our first winery tour, as they tend to get more modern (in every sense) as you go into the valleys. Plus we got a half-bottle of Santa Carolina Reserva Carmenere each as a thank you gift! At 24,000 pesos total, accessible by metro and with a take home wine, this was great value and a wonderful experience.

review_text: We were a bit unlucky with the snow conditions and only half the resort was open which limited the amount of skiing we could do however it is obvious that this would be an excellent short stay (maybe 3 /4 days) resort if everything was open. The restaurants are expensive by chilean standards but I guess this is what you expect 3,000m up a mountain. Ski hire and lift passes are expensive so if you have the time, rent your kit down the mountain on the outskirts of Santiago. There are a few things you need to appreciate before booking here 1) It is 3,000m at the base of the resort and even though we'd been at 2,000m plus for the previous week, we still struggled with the lack of oxygen. 2) The road up to the resort is not for the faint hearted. There are 40 switch back turns (that's not counting loads of 90 degree bends) before you turn off to Valle Nevado. There are then about 17 more up to the resort. 3) the road is one way up on weekend mornings and one way down on weekend afternoons. This means that if you have a morning flight to catch on Saturday, you will have to leave the resort on Friday night as you can't get down the mountain until 2pm on Saturday afternoon and transfer companies will not pick you up as the driver has to come up in the morning and then wait until he can take you down. 4) bring everything you need from Santiago if you are staying in a appartment as the shop in the resort stocks nothing - no beer,no wine,no fresh veg,no fruit or meat. 5) even though it is high do not assume great snow. The Andes are a pretty dry mountain range so early season can be marginal Overall good resort but not to North American or European standards but you'll have fun for a couple of days if the snow conditions deliver
title: Nice resort but expensive

review_text: The trip to Isla Magdalena was definitely worth it. My husband and I visited the island after our Torres del Paine hike. The penguins sometimes come right up to you! Our boat (with Solo Expediciones) also rode by Isla Marta with hundreds of sea lions. While we didn't get off the boat, it was neat the see the sea lions from afar.

review_text: During a visit from my niece and her friend to Chile I booked a cooking class and tour with Boris from Chilean Flavours. Boris came very highly recommended by friends in Santiago so this was the perfect opportunity to go! We were collected from our hostel by Boris in the morning. We explored and wandered around this colourful port city listening to Boris's insightful stories and interesting history of Valparaiso. We discussed menu options on route and then shopped local markets for ingredients to create the dishes we had chosen from Boris's very own cook book. Back at Boris's home we enjoyed every minute of the afternoon. Boris's love for Chile and its cuisine is infectious and we all laughed, cooked, ate and even danced together. This experience was educational and fun for all. Our children, 9 & 11 loved the day and were involved in the preparation and cooking just as much as we were. While we made Piscos, they made their own special Pineapple drink, for which they say was the yummiest drink ever! My niece and her friend, both in their 20's had one of the best days in the 5 weeks of their South American travels! In summary, Chilean flavours is for all ages and I strongly recommend Boris to anyone visiting Valparaiso. All amazing!!!

review_text: We had a mixed experience with Ciclo Austral during our 30-day cycling trip through Patagonia along the Carretera Austral. We initially rented gravel bikes for the first half of the trip and switched to mountain bikes due to changing road conditions. Our experience started off on a rocky note. When we arrived in Puerto Montt to pick up our bikes, the mechanic, Rodrigo, was behind schedule and had to rush through the final bike preparations. Despite being assured that this was for our benefit, we quickly encountered issues: in the first 5 days, we had 5 mechanical failures (4 flat tires and a broken spoke). The spare tubes provided were even double patched, and the tire quality was bad. Additionally, the bikes weren’t supplied with chain oil, which proved essential given the rough road conditions(dusty muddy and rainy) . Thankfully, some fellow cyclists helped us with their own spare tubes. After providing feedback, Ciclo Austral responded promptly and gave us new mountain bikes, checked all our equipment, and provided more spare tubes. This made the second part of our trip much smoother and more enjoyable. The company also offers a helpful app for trip planning, though it could benefit from more detailed maps and bug fixes (particularly missing part from Lago Yelcho to La Junta). Overall, while our experience started off poorly, Ciclo Austral made improvements and provided a great second half of the trip. We would recommend the company, but we strongly suggest double-checking the condition of the equipment, especially gravel bikes, and requesting extra spare materials to avoid any issues while cycling through remote Patagonia.

review_text: If you are comfortable hiking for 4-6 hours, then you can (and should) climb Volcan Villarrica (mispelled above). This is essentially a hike with crampons on--nothing technical about it and very straightforward. The views are incredible the entire way up and you get to summit one of the only volcanoes with an active lava pit (thanks Wikipedia). Also, the way down was the most fun descent I've ever had on a hike/climb. You basically slide down the entire way on your butt, which takes 30-60 minutes depending on the time of year. Awesome. Outdoor enthusiasts: do not miss this Tips: 1) Bring a balaclava to cover your mouth in case the winds shift and blow volcanic gas in your direction. It's safe (so I've heard) to inhale this for short periods of time, but it's also pretty unpleasant. 2) You need a clear day to make the summit, so give yourself a few days of wiggle room in case you get a string of bad weather. 3) Pack lots of high-calorie snacks (in addition to lunch).

review_text: We did the W trek in December 2016. While we were planning (a few months beforehand) we couldn’t find all that much information on the trek so here are my experiences, which I hope will be helpful. I think that West to East is the best way to do the trek, it starts more relaxed and you end with the highlight of Torres del Paine Lookout on your last day. I also think the hike is a bit easier as you don’t have to do the really big uphill from Los Torres to Chileno if you are coming from the West. However, whichever way you do it, it will be great. Our Route Day One: PUERTO NATALES- PUDETO -REFUGIO GREY. We took an early morning bus from Puerto Natales to Pudeto. The bus will stop at the park entrance so you can pay your entrance fee. Our first night booked was at Refugio Grey. Initially we thought we’d be able to get a boat there and also get up close with the glacier. Hotel Grey apparently does offer this service but we found out after we’d booked that it was really expensive and not that accessible to get this boat by regular bus. So instead we took the 11am boat from Pudeto to Paine Grande and walked to Refugio Grey. This took about 4 hours, with lots of stops for photos. We arrived at Refugio Grey at about 4.30. We left our bags and went to the mirador close to check out Glacier Grey. We did a short walk around the mirador then headed back to the refugio for the evening. Day Two: REFUGIO GREY TO REFUGIO PAINE GRANDE. We walked north up to the suspension bridge to get better views of Glacier Grey than came back to Refugio Grey to get our packs and begin our return to Refugio Paine Grande (where we had landed on the boat from Pudeto the day before). It didn’t take as long to get back as we weren’t constantly stopping for photos. The hike back took about 3 hours. We also did a 2 hour walk down towards Mirador Pehoe that afternoon. Day Three: REFUGIO PAINE GRANDE TO REFUGIO CUERNOS. We were expecting this to be a big day- we were going to go from Paine Grande up to the Camp Britannico mirador then head back down to spend the night at Refugio Cuernos. However it was pouring with rain that day. Figuring that the view would be terrible, we decided to make a beeline for Cuernos and see if we could go on to Refugio Los Torres but Refugio Los Torres was full so we couldn’t change our plans. Cuernos is probably the least comfortable refugio we stayed at. It was much smaller, very full with minimal bathroom facilities. The refugio had 2 working toilets (that flushed 50% of the time) for about 60 women, which was not fun. Day Four: REFUGIO CUERNOS- TORRES DEL PAINE LOOKOUT-REFUGIO LOS TORRES. This hike was about 30km, but it was a great day. We walked first to Refugio El Chileno and left our heavy packs there. With little day packs we walked up to Torres Del Paine lookout. The hike is a challenge and very steep in parts, but we were there within 2 hours. We spent about an hour at the lookout as it is simply stunning (lots of photos to take and you need some time to take it all in). We were back at Refugio Chileno by about 3pm that afternoon and began the descent to Los Torres. It was at this point that we realised how lucky we had been not to be making the hiking from Refugio Los Torres up to the Torres Del Paine lookout, as it was really steep! Since we had come from Cuernos that morning, we basically avoided about 2 hours of steep uphill walking. Day Five: Bus out to Puerto Natales. From Refugio Los Torrens there is a bus that will take you directly back to Puerto Natales. You can book on the day, no problem. We went directly on to Punta Arenas. We could not get on a bus immediately from Puerto Natales to Punta Arenas as many were full, so had to wait a few hours at the bus station, but there are several companies that make the trip and buses are regular so there is no need to book in advance. Other useful information: We stayed in refugios (hostels) during our stay, though many people chose to camp. The W trek requires you to book all your accommodation in advance, which means there is very little room for error. The refugios and camp sites tend to fill up (they were definitely busy in December) so don’t count on being able to change your bookings once you’re there. We tried to change one of our bookings due to bad weather and simply couldn’t. I’m sure that it would depend on your luck, but when planning, think about your days carefully and what your plan will be if the weather’s bad. If you want to be safe, it makes sense to take it slow and give yourself a buffer if you run into some rainy days. There are 2 companies that run/own the camp sites and the refugios. Fantastico Sur is the better of the 2, but don’t expect too much from either. They have a captured market, so there is little incentive to provide good service or facilities. Also, you’re there to hike in the wilderness, not hang out at the hostel, so it won’t dampen your trip too much. Another point to note is that if you don’t pre-book your meals, there is a chance you won’t eat much. We wrongly assumed that refugios had restaurants/cafes that you could order food from once you arrived. At Refugio Grey and Cuernos there were no meals for those who didn’t pre-order. You could buy a big empanada for $20 at Cuernos, but it felt like money poorly spent compared to the set dinner. At the bigger Refugios like Paine Grande and Los Torrens there were more snack options.
title: Tips for doing the W from West to East

review_text: Writing another raving comment won't help. All has been said and whatever I could add, would be no news. This IS the trip of a lifetime. Every dime (and it's lots of them!) is worth it 100%. So, instead, some recommendations that can be useful: Don't overpack and if you do, leave stuff behind in Punta Arenas and collect it on return. One pair of tennis shoes on the boat is enough; the boots provided are outstanding (go for one size larger). Pack warm, thermal underwear and a very good parka, cover your head and hands. Walking poles are useful. Reserve well ahead. Not everyone is so fortunate: we decided and asked for a cabin in October and traveled on February 1, only because a cancellation! Don't get anxious about possible delays of flights: it's safety first and leave yourself some slack on the continuation of your trip (2 days maybe). Get ready to enjoy no-end. Although everybody says it, I can't finish this review without expressing my highest praises to all and everyone on the ship, crew, hospitality team, kitchen, trip planner, guides, absolutely everyone. Go, go, go!

Overall it was a magical experience, not only because the Atacama desert is one of the best places in the world to see the stars but because of Jorge. His tour is a must-do.

review_text: This stunning National Park is divided into three parts, which include Osorno, Petrohué and Peuilla. As a one-day visitor from the cruise port of Puerto Montt the choice as to which area to explore was a difficult one. We decided on the Lake Llanquihue circuit drive that took us in the opposite direction away from the emerald coloured Lago Todos Los Santos and the Saltos de Petrohué waterfall - the latter two are the most popular and touristy places to visit in the National Park. After Fruitillar and Puerto Octay the drive again ran parallel to the lake, then veered onto a separate road that climbed steadily so that we got a closer look at one slope of Osorno Volcano. This was paved so a little better than one rough area on our drive but there were some road works that held us up at one point. What we experienced on the ‘other’ side of the mountain was less traffic, fewer people and some extraordinary views of snow-capped Osorno amongst natural forest and some of the cleanest air imaginable! No notable stopping areas or services here but the lack of traffic meant we could pull over safely to take photos and absorb the backdrop of the volcano against a blue sky. It’s a pity we only had one day, as this park deserves several days to appreciate the serenity, the wilderness and the overall picture postcard magnificence. Hiking is an option but you need to plan for this and the ski area also has a road that gets you even closer to Osorno. Two other notable volcanoes Tronador and Puntiagudo also have commanding peaks within the park. Best of all though the park is free – except for Petrohué. We loved it here! Enjoy your experience!
title: Clean air, picture postcard magnificence....

review_text: At $85 for the market tour I almost didn't do it but it was a great experience. Totally bilingual tour with only a total of 3 people, lots of different tastings along the way, good flexibility in meeting interests of the group (the 3 of us agreed that the fresh coffee was a better option for us than alcohol) , and a willingness to share the expat experience of living in Santiago. Well worth the price - I'd sign up for another one of his tours on a next trip.
title: excellent experience

review_text: If one visits Punta Arenas, one is clearly aware of Maggelan's visits and his history. The replica of his boat is fun to visit. It is well presented in a very nice quiet area, not far from the city centre and the cruise harbor.
title: Fun to experience

review_text: Very well served by the guide Constanza. I went on the Santa Rita Vineyard. Everything was perfect since the punctuality at'e the pleasant way of the guide. I'll use it other times.
title: GOOD TRAVEL COMPANY IN SANTIAGO

review_text: Santa Rita winery is well known for the quality of its products, and the place is very beautiful and full of history. I made this trip with Touristik, which provided the bus trip and the bikes. We cycled around the winery, stoping in some places where the careful and friendly guides Jorge and Alejandro explained about details of the different grapes available and wine production. After this overview, you are brought to the main building to attend a short movie about the history of the winery and then after you join small groups to start the tastings with a local sommelier. You can spend time in the winery shop, taking advantage of the promotions and discounts to improve your wine cellar. Indeed, a very nice morning! Review of: Tour Viña Santa Rita: History, Wine and Picnic Outdoors We appreciate your comment dear traveler, it is very important for us to know about your experience.
title: A pleasant morning pedaling and tasting wine in a beautiful place

review_text: All round an excellent day with a skilled driver (Roberto) and guide (Nacho) who was knowledgeable and shared lots of information, but was also amusing and gelled together the tour group of 15. I’d done this same day trip in November 2023 and this time brought my wife so she could enjoy this amazing day for herself. Which surely speaks highly of this tour! We took lots of photos but Nacho shared many of his own, taken from his own experienced perspective, with us which was great. Beyond the main sights e.g. the Vina del Mar clock we had an excellent walking tour of Valparaiso during which Nacho pointed out so much of interest and also gave a wealth of further information. The vineyard stop was also good - tasting wines in a beautiful location even if this vineyard didn’t have Alpacas as on the previous tour. Personally I’d have preferred the wine tasting in the afternoon, as on the previous tour, but in hindsight it actually didn’t matter and maybe allowed better overall timing for the day. To repeat: an excellent day, with an excellent tour guide (Nacho) who surely rates higher than 5* Review of: Valparaiso Port and Vina del Mar Full-Day Tour from Santiago We just love to read that our tourist do a repeat on this tour. This just shows how great of a time people can have. Best part, as you mention still on the second time around you had a great time. We're glad you had a lovely tour with Nacho and Roberto. Thank you for your review.
title: An amazing, very informative and well organised tour

review_text: I have been to Concha y Toro Winery twice and both times it was fun. If you have the option, go when the grapes are on the vines. I went in the end of winter, and it was still fun, but not as fun as when everything was growing. The lunch here is top notch. I have eaten there both times I visited the winery. If you can find the Amelia Chardonnay buy it, as it is the best Chardonnay I have tasted. Very buttery.
title: Fun

review_text: This area was recommended by a fellow passenger on the flight from US to Santiago. Great choice. Many restaurants and shops with a wide variety of food.
title: Great Restaurant Choices

review_text: I was expecting something impressive but it's just an amphitheater and a park that have nothing special. Even if you go to a concert, there are more interesting places to visit in the region. So if it's not in your way, don't take the trouble to go there.
title: Completely overrated

review_text: I had a day to fill in in Valparaiso and with nothing better to do, I signed up for the Chilean Cuisine Cooking Classes, through my B&B, The Yellow House. I'm not a very good cook and wouldn't normally do a cooking class, but gosh, I'm so happy I did! Boris is such a fun loving person and you can't help but have a fabulous time. First, our group met each other and discussed what recipes we would try, then we all caught a bus to the fruit/vegie/seafood market to buy the ingredients. Back to the kitchen and Boris gave each of us specific jobs to do (lucky mine weren't too difficult, I think Boris knew I wasn't too skilled!) The dishes that we sat down to eat were scrumptious, I especially loved the clam entree. The cheese empanadas were pretty yum too. Oh, and also the pear poached in red wine. I highly recommend this cooking class with Boris, you will have a really fun day. Boris emailed the recipes to us after the class, and I MAY even try making some at home :-)
title: A fantastic experience!!

review_text: Top notch tour. Very comprehensive, informative and enjoyable. Frank was fun to be with. He speaks very clear with excellent English. A must when in Santiago.
title: Valparaiso and Viña del Mar

review_text: My husband and I did not know this place even existed until a few days before we arrived in Chile, thanks to rough guides. Once we got to Santiago, we started researching how to get there and all the over-land options were too expensive. A few weeks into our Chile visit, we found cheap air tickets with sky airlines and we were on our way to exploring Patagonia. Seeing Torres del Paine has been the best thing that ever happened to us!!! We are forever changed. This mountain range is breath-taking and it does not disappoint. The Pehue lake, right in front of it, is amazing!!! We are even more in love with nature after seeing this and we will for sure be back to do the W-trek. If you are not a trekker, I would recommend hiring a car and driving to see Torres by yourself so that you can stare at this awesomeness for hours. Better yet, stay at the hotel that is right on the lake...I know I will next time.
title: The most beautiful place in the world!!

review_text: Very practical for tourism, it travels much of the city with explanations and variety of stops. Very good choice for first visit. Valentina and Camila looked after us very well. Review of: Cable Car, Funicular and Sightseeing Bus in Santiago two days Estimado viajero, nos alegra saber que disfruto de su recorrido, muchas gracias por compartir su experiencia con nosotros. ¡Esperamos su pronta visita!
title: Good for first timers.

review_text: Amazing experience! The Guide Rocio and the van driver are super attentive and pass a lot of knowledge about the locations to us! I highly recommend!!! Worth every penny! Review of: Full Day Trip to Cajón del Maipo Yeso Reservoir + Picnic
title: A dream!

review_text: The best way to learn a city is to do is with somebody who lives there. On the tour day we had a really bad wether: it was cold, windy and raining. And I was cold. But in spite of this it was a great day and a great tour. I saw a lot and got a lot of information about Chile, people and their life. It was very interesting for me. To the end of the tour I enjoyed the Chilean hospitality with Ignacio and her great parents. I hope I see them again! Katarzina It was a pleasure to show you around the city . I am going to always remember that day because was completely different to the others tours. it was cloudy and raining, and we decided to change the schedule and go to know others places through the city and finally was an excellent day, very funny, Successful day! I liked that you have enjoyed the experience with us. thanks for having prefered us. A big hug from Santiago de Chile. Ignacio
title: A great day with Ignacio and his family

review_text: We had booked this tour almost a month prior and with no access to emails were not sure how it would turn out. Turned out great. On the plus side they do pick you up from your hotel but this takes a while if the tour is full. Casablanca is just a tourist shop stop. Limited but free wine tasting. Big liquor store with LARGE selection of Rio Tinto wines. Rest of the tour was as described (reverse order though). Both cities are worth seeing and the tour gives you a good overview. Review of: Private Tour: Viña del Mar and Valparaíso Tour with Wine Tasting in Casablanca Valley Thank you for your comment! we're really happy that your experience with us was great and that you could enjoy the tour to the fullest. Do not hesitate to contact us the next time you plan on visiting Chile, it will be a pleasure to welcome you once again. See you soon! Best regards, MTO Tour Team
title: Great outing and good value

review_text: We had an great experience with Mitampi. The office staff and guides are all knowledgable and attentive. We went on tours to Rainbow Valley, Moon Valley and on the Stargazing excursion. We had fun and learned a lot on all three. Thank you to Catalina, Juan, Diego, Franco and the rest of the team! Thank you so much for your feedback. We're so happy to know you had such a wonderful experience in San Pedro with us. You are always welcome!
title: Excellent tours

review_text: Summer tours in Chile were great. Well-organized agency, good communication and 10 rating. Always informs you before each tour of the pick-up time at the hotel.

review_text: We thoroughly enjoyed the experience up volcano Villarrica! Equipment was well provided for and we had a thorough briefing beforehand. It was a pleasure to have shared this great experience with you and thank you for trusting in us. Greetings from the staff of Antü.

review_text: Andrea was very knowledgeable and a great guide. She was fun and funny. She shared all the history and important details about what makes Vik winery unique.
title: A beautiful winery with very good intentions and details

review_text: A great park in downtown Santiago that can be accessed easily from different entrances. The main entrance and probably one of my favorites is the one at Pedro de Valdivia. From here you can climb up the road, take the cable car, or go on one of the many trails and head in numerous different directions. The roads are well marked and there are small shops selling water/drinks/ice cream etc. It really is a great way to spend a morning or afternoon exploring this great park.
title: Running up Cerro Sam Cristobal

review_text: 3 friends and I had a great trip to Viña del Mar for a full day cooking class with Boris. This was a fantastic experience and I highly recommend it. The staff where great (especially our teacher Boris) the locations was very professional and the food was so fresh and tasty. I will definitely be going back and taking more friends and family along!
title: Fantastic Experience

review_text: I visited Santiago for business. Having a free afternoon, I decided to join this walking tour. Our tour guide Sergio was super friendly and knowledgeable. His English was perfect and he took special care to make sure everyone was able to hear what he had to day. I would highly recommend this tour to my friends! Hello! Thank you so much for taking the time to leave a review about your experience with us in Santiago, we really appreciate your feedback, and we are glad you enjoyed the experience with Sergio. We hope to see you again with Strawberry Tours in the future, walking and discovering new places!
title: Great walking tour of Santiago!!

review_text: Rating 10 - great service offered by the Araya team, especially the guide José, he is very good, knows him well and seems to really enjoy what he does
title: Exceeded expectations

review_text: Hector was a great tour guide. He was very knowledgeable about Santiago and Valpa. He was able to give us great insights. He is very responsive and flexible. Thank you for a great day. Review of: Valparaiso and Viña del Mar Full-Day Private Guided Tour
title: Delightful Day

review_text: It was all very incredible! The landscape, the path, Casa Zerando (with the best barbecue and picnic), the friendliness and care of the entire team (especially Yuri and Don Mário ❤️).

I tried to enter on the backside and apparently it hadn't opened yet so when i walk by the main entrance later in the day it was open. Although there may only be one way in or out. Its a steep walk, but not to far as you wind your way up to different levels, gardens and lookouts. The best view is from a castle like out cropping at the top. Santiago was either fairly smoggy or had a lot of dust in the air the day I was up there. Nice easy hike for a great view, although the funicular on San Cristobal Hill is even easier and you are higher with grander views. Plan to spend at least an hour walking up and down and enjoying the grounds. There is a small convenience store close to the top if you need a soda or bottle of water.
title: Short hike to great views!

review_text: We've been wine tasting all over the world, and this was one of our favorite experiences. It was intimate and unique and we felt like we really got to see and taste authentic Chilean wines. Christian was an amazing, fun guide, and we felt like we left with a new friend. We would do it again if we could. =) Review of: Maipo Valley litle wine bus from Santiago Hello Melissa, thanks a lot for your feedback!! Always very rewarding to see our clients/guests have a great time. Specially when you have been wine tasting all over the world. I’ll congratulate Cristian on your behalf.

review_text: Excellent guide, very knowledgeable, designed a great personal three hour tour. Larisa and driver, Omar, were very prompt in arriving. Very personable; provided interesting anecdotes and a thorough historical and modern day perspective on Santiago. I highly recommend this very professional guide.

review_text: Visiting this park was just as breathtaking as the pictures we saw on National Geographic. We were nervous about going in winter after reading reviews warning us about visiting in this season, but we got very lucky; the weather was stable, and we had clear skies almost every day. We were warned that the park might be closed, but we went with a very knowledgeable guide, and it was never an issue.

The tour was a good pace, the visit to the vineyard and wine tasting was great, and we would definitely take this tour again. We appreciate your preference and interest in our tour of Santiago + vineyard. We are glad that you enjoyed it, as well as and through the comments that kindly come to us, we know that our guides and drivers enjoy their work. Thank you for your excellent review.
