Most of the buses leave right at 7pm, while the sun is still setting. If you go by yourself you might have a better chance at an amazing photo facing the other way (with the Andes catching the sunset).

The place has also little souvenir stores, coffee places, a beautiful church “Santuario de la Inmaculada Concepción” and some breathtaking paths around the mountain. review_text: Great hiking options in this park. Not extensive loops, but enough to keep you busy for a couple of days, even without a boat to take you across the lake. Park at the free parking area, which is right past a paid parking area and closer to the trail. There are three directions visually, and no clear sign pointing to this 12 km trail. The one to the east goes to the lake (a nice place to cool off post-hike), and the middle one goes into a fenced area that looks like a picnic site. Go through the picnic area to a trail, and 500m in there is a sign for "Sendero Paso Desolacion 12km" with a good trail map and altitude guide. 4.3 km to the first junction, through flat, sandy terrain. When you get to a pair of deep arroyo / washes, you are almost there. The junction offers little in the way of places to stop for a lunch (though we did anyhow) but instead gives you the choice of a shorter hike down to alerce tree stands and the lake, or on up to the pass. 1.9 km further, with the latter half up steep sand, is a great look-out. Be careful, as the path divides and there seem to be multiple paths. Generally keep to the lake side of any path splits, though they all go the same general place, the saddle above you is visually obvious as a destination. That saddle is about 1 km further, and for those that are time constrained is a decent end-point. You'll see a waterfall to the east, and great views. At this point the steepness levels off to a gentle climb, as well as the sand giving way to packed sand / rock. Keep going to the end if you can! Why is this marked "Hard" in guidebooks? Here's our take: - Hot, exposed terrain. If it is sunny, bring hats and sunscreen, and plenty of water. - Walking on sand. We are experienced hikers, with plenty of altitude and distance experience. Yet a 400m altitude climb up a sand dune was TOUGH. Don't underestimate this calf-burner. - No exit points. This is what you came for, right? "Desolation". Yet we crossed path with someone who had sprained their ankle who was really suffering. We gave supplies to assist, and when we checked in the next day, it took them OVER 7 hours to do the last 5 km. It's not dangerous terrain, just really slow going if you get in a pinch. (If this was helpful, please hit the "thanks" button.)
title: Description of "Sendero Paso Desolacion" hike

review_text: This company deserves more than 5 stars. We waited till the last minute to arrange transportation from Santiago, Chile to our cruise port at San Antonio, which was about 80 mi. Our cruise left Sat. afternoon and since we had already booked a hotel in San Antonio for Fri night we were looking for possibly a wine tour or something to do on Fri. along the way down. Our flight from the US didn’t arrive until 8:15 AM and all the tours we contacted said the tours would have left by the time we got thru customs. We contacted Eduardo at Transfer Chile Tours, explained what we were looking for. He replied within minutes, asked some questions, made some suggestions, and within about an hour, he put together a wonderful tour working with OUR schedule. He arranged for a personalized tour with our driver, Santiago, who drove my husband and me to 2 wineries (Undurraga & Chocolan) arranging for an hr long tour at Undurraga. He drove us to a small village (Pomaire) where we watched them make pottery and had a great lunch. We made an unexpected stop along Rt 78 at a strawberry farm where we were given some sweet, sweet strawberries to enjoy. Santiago was a perfect guide, translating for us, taking us places we normally wouldn’t have gone, sharing local history and info with us, driving so my husband didn’t have to, etc. We can’t say enough good things about Eduardo and Santiago. We would strongly recommend working with this company. Jackie & Harvey Jackie & Harvey. On behalf Santiago and myself, thanks so much for your awesome review. It was a pleasure to have you as clients and friends. Sure Santiago enjoyed as much as you did. He was talking about that magical time that you guys shared with him. We hope to see you again.

review_text: Part of our group hiked on the glacier. It is neat to see the various colors of blue associated with a glacier. It is cold hiking on ice. We also had some scenic crusing, by the glacier hoping for some calving, in a boat as we went from on end of Grey lake to the other end.

review_text: Stayed in Provedenci and used the metro several times. It is easy to use but can be very crowded during rush hour. Saturday morning was awesome. Rode several stops to the central market area.

review_text: The hike is very challenging (mentally and physically) but well worth it to see such spectacular views on the way up, plus the lava in the crater when you summit. The hike took us around 6 hours and our company provided all the equipment (crampons, outer clothing, helmet, ice axe etc). We went with Antu who were amazing - I really needed the inspiration/motivation to get me to the top. I couldn't have done it without them, highly recommended! Also seeing other groups which were quite large and left later than us made me glad we chose Antu. Most of all I felt safe with them at all times which was my priority. Take loads of snacks, water, suncream. Also pay the extra 10,000 CLP for the lift at the first part, there is nothing gained from walking it.
title: Hike Volcan Villarrica with Antu

review_text: The crew was very helpful, especially when I had problems steering our koyak. They stay close by and manage the experience very professionally. review_text: Located in the Las Condes area of Santiago, this is one of the nicest urban parks we have visited. Everything was clean and well manicured. During our visit we saw many locals taking an exercise class, joggers passing by, and people just lounging on the well-maintained lawns. Along the park there were sculptures, an event center (Centro Parque), a couple of children's entertainment venues (Kidzania and Selva Viva) a skateboard area, exercise machines, a climbing playground, a dog park area, an artistic bridge over the boulevard Av. Manquehue, and even a playground for very young children across the street from a kindergarten school. We also appreciated the many signs asking people to clean up after their dogs and to help keep the park clean. This spacious park was a relaxing end to our three-week trip to Chile.
title: Spacious park stretching along many blocks

review_text: Angelo is a solid guide and he and Rodrigo were very friendly and knowledgeable. However, the price was very high for the experience we had. We paid $400US per person (higher than their website states) for a “full day” kayak trip down the Gray River but we were done and having lunch by 12:30. We were told we would kayak around the icebergs in Lago Gray and we barely entered the lake before turning back down the river. Good guide, but make sure you are very clear with expectations and the plan before committing. Thank you for your feedback. In regards to the price- we try to be as transparent as possible with the trip itinerary and price. For this reason we post all these details on our website. The higher price you are referring to is the value added tax (VAT) because the trip was booked through your hotel, in which case this tax is applied. In all cases, the price is made clear before booking. Each trip is different depending on various factors such as weather, group dynamics and the capabilities of the passengers. The idea of this trip is the experience of kayaking shared with friends and family, not arriving at a particular location. I hope you enjoyed your kayak experience. Best wishes.
title: Kayak experience

review_text: This is a must see museum of Chilean history. Be sure to get the head phones for a nominal fee that give a self guided tour in English. And the wall with the names of the dead and missing was very moving.
title: A most interesting look into a very important part of Chilean history

review_text: I had an absolutely amazing experience with the High Mountain Expedition team during our climb to Ojos del Salado in December. From start to finish everything was professionally organized and the team’s dedication truly stood out. Kati provided incredible remote support, ensuring everything was clarified before my arrival in Chile. Cris was an invaluable guide offering expert advice on equipment, managing logistics and making sure everything ran smoothly. My hike with Marito was very comfortable - his attentiveness, kindness and professionalism was an immense support on the way to the summit 🙏 A special shoutout to Silio, who prepared a fantastic variety of delicious meals during the trip. I can be quite picky when it comes to food, but he always managed to offer something tasty. Of course, challenges come with any high-altitude expedition and we had our share including a car breakdown. But given the extreme conditions of the desert and mountains, this was completely understandable. Cris did an excellent job of quickly adjusting the plans to keep us on track with our acclimatization schedule. Overall, this was an unforgettable adventure and I can’t recommend this team enough! If you’re looking for a truly professional and supportive expedition crew, look no further 😉
title: Incredible Experience - highly recommended!

review_text: Climbed the Villarrica volcano today with Patagonia Experience and had brilliant time. The people from the offices where we bought our tickets were extremely helpful and detailed about the hike. Great staff. The guides on the day were the best I have ever experienced! Extremely skilled, insuring our safety, and fun guys. They had many years experience of climbing the volcano and made us feel reassured. We were provided with all the kit (jackets, trousers, gators, crampons, backpack, helmet, gloves, plastic sledge etc). We were grateful that it was so well prepared as some of the other tour company groups we saw didn't get crampons etc and I would have really struggled without these. Once on the hike the faster people went on ahead with 1 of the guides, and we remained with the other. whilst we were slower we never felt under pressure and with his help we made it all the way to the top. Great views, amazing experience and top notch team ! Highly recommend Estimada Eva: Como Parte del Team Patagonia Experience, agradecemos que usted se haya dado el tiempo de dejarnos tan buen comentario. Esperamos tener su visita lo mas pronto posible otra vez, para poder brindarle nuestros servicios de muy buena calidad y profesionalismo. Un cordial Saludo desde Pucon, El team de Patagonia Experience.

review_text: We booked with another agency but were grouped with others on this tour. This trip is highly recommended, however, as we didnt speak Spaish we would have struggled without one of the other members in the car who spoke both English and Spaish. The driver/guide didnt speak a word of English although we were told he would. Towards the end of the trip however we were starting to get to grips with it and actually managed to understand some of it! Bonus. The trip itself was great, so many things to see and do, various coloured lagoons, thermal spas, guisers, flamingos, llamas, and a canyon that looked like an anaconda. This is all before we got to the main attraction which was the salt flats! We were up for sunrise on the saltflats and the pictures will never do it justice. We took a walk around an island of cacti, whilst our guide made us breakfast on the saltflats and then spent 40 minutes takig stupid pictures of each other danching out of pringle cans!!! We stayed in basic accommodation with shared bathrooms but it is possible to pay more and have private rooms and bathrooms. However we met some really nice people and enjoyed sharing a room with them. The food is basic but very filling and we had 2 hungry men at our table. On the last evening we stayed in a salt hotel/hostel, had wine and llama steak, which was actually quite tasty. All in all this was a fun packed, informative (thanks to our resident interpreter) and worth while trip. We would and have recommended it to anyone that has asked.
title: San Pedro to Uyuni Salt Flats tour 2 nights

review_text: We disembarked from our cruise ship in Valparaiso and planned to stay for an additional two days in Santiago but weren't sure how to get there. I found this company on line, did some searches, and booked a one-way wine tour from Valparaiso to Santiago with stops at 4 wineries plus lunch. Natalia was our sommalier and we couldn't have asked for better. When you consider what the cruise ships charge for such a trip, you usually only get stops at two wineries for the same price and then they take you to the airport, so you'd have to pay additional for a cab to your hotel. Natalia and her driver picked us up right at the port and dropped us off at our hotel at the end of the day. In between, we had a personalized tour of the wineries in the Casablanca Valley, and Natalia was wonderful company. She took candid photos of my husband and me throughout the tour and then sent them to us afterwards. We felt like we had known her for years. We have a friend who's a teacher in Santiago and she also recommended this company; she said she has used them in the past and they are very reputable (which is nice to hear when you're booking something thousands of miles away and paying for it ahead of time). I wouldn't hesitate to book a tour with them again if we're ever in that part of the world, and I would highly recommend them for personalized service and a reasonable price. Very pleased that you enjoyed the tour with one of our best guides. Maybe see you again sometime. Thanks for choosing Wine Tours Valparaiso.

review_text: I think this business has great potential, the country is perfect for biking and the landscapes are fantastic. I picked the trip to Cajon del Maipo which is great, I had never seen such a landscape in my life and it's really breathtaking. Being a mountain biker for decades already and given the landscape I was expecting a bit more off road experience, however I understand that for Patricio it's difficult to judge the capabilities of the people who book a trip. Biking down hill was pretty exciting, and even though we were going down on the main and only road I had a fantastic time. Juan Carlos! Thank you for your review of our MTB Tour Cajon del Maipo & Embalse el Yeso! Indeed for us it is almost impossible to know the real physical condition or level of biking or mtbiking of the participants until the day of the excursion. The minimum participant amount for this tour is 2 people, we offered you to join this group (the couple) for the tour so that you did not have to pay extra for a private tour. They had lower level of fitness than you, what may have somewhat affected your experience. We do not offer routes requiring more experience, the route we biked down is the only road in this area of ​​the Andes mountains, and it is the same road we drove up by vehicle. This is a good thing in case of accident or technical malfunction, as we always have our vehicle & driver assisting us in this area without phone reception. Even so, we had a fantastic day with good weather, we enjoyed a descent at full speed from the 2,500 meters almost without holding brakes, and reaching down to + 50km, viewpoints and waterfalls, the only thing we missed was the Condor! For the next time visiting us, if you´d like, we will wait for you with a personalized MTB Tour San Cristobal Hill where we can offer you more technical routes, and at full speed. Uyuuuuuuy !!! Un Abrazo! Atte Patricio Huaso Tours & Bike Tours Santiago.

review_text: I've just done the 9-day Full Circuit trek. Fabulous. Wonderful, Amazing. Torres Del Paine is such a globally renowned destination that giving it five stars is the easy part; you know it will be stunning before you even arrive. Perhaps the best additional advice I can give is to recommend you carefully plan the season for your visit. We trekked in the first week of November; i.e. the shoulder (beginning) of the summer season, and I would thoroughly recommend that period. It's a bit colder, of course, but there were relatively few trekkers on the trail and we were extremely fortunate to have fine weather for (almost) the entire week, which is of course almost unheard of in Torres Del Paine. Having visited the refugios, I can well imagine that the big crowds that arrive in the summer season (December-February) would significantly detract from the experience, and personally couldn't think of anything worse than having to endure them both at the campsites and on the trail. Go early in the season or right at the end (March-April) - it will make for a far more enjoyable visit.

review_text: We stopped at this place after a long tour in the area, and after chasing it for a while (it was a bit difficult to find as the number was unknown!). Respect to many other places we have seen in the area the place is sort of peculiar. Not one of those run-down, decadent and careless places very common here, and neither one of those supposedly international restaurant that fill the area. This is something chilean but with some personality: typical menu, ok, but well done, well prepared, served with care. And here it is: the difference is really in the service. All the many young waiters that served us were extremely friendly, nice, attentive, and try to serve as quickly and honestly. The pork ribs were really good with the "arroz arabe". And so was the tabla montaña. The place has a pretty strange arrangment, quite typical here but with a personal twist. Not really cheap, but it is so much better than the typical other area that it's ok. Nice people, nice place, nice food. Last but not least: good music from Manuel Garcia, a chilean singer, as a background (the waiter told us that he played here and is a regular customer). As we cannot withstand Reggaeton, so common here, we would be back just for this reason! :) Bravi! Continuate così! (= keep going like that).

If you come in the afternoon, the light is pretty with the sun going down, but if you are planing to take the road down when is it dark, you can't be sure that the lampposts works, so make sure to bring a flashlight. review_text: A friend and I had a couple of days free in Santiago before a planned trip to Antarctica. We spent one day in Valparaiso and another day on the Full Day Penguin Island SUP tour. Mick was quite attentive, well supplied with wetsuits and boards, and really gave us great information about the area during the ride to Cachagua Island (Penguin Island). Once at Penguin Island we were blown away by the incredible beauty of the landscape, island and penguins. It really was a magnificent day. We had lunch at a beachside cafe which was idyllic. My only comment is that you need to be a practiced SUP paddler to handle the turbulent waters there. When we had lamented the fact that we didn't have time in our schedule to see a Chilean winery, while in Santiago, Mick said that he would take us to a special winery on the way home. He took us to Don Maximiano Vineyard which really made the trip even more special. The tasting room was inside a stunning Spanish complex built in 1880. I wholeheartedly recommend the Penguin Island SUP tour with Mick. Review of: Full-Day Penguin Island Stand-Up Paddleboard Tour from Santiago

review_text: We stumbled on this trekking agency whilst looking for somewhere to take us to see cacti. Leon greeted us and informed us of his personalised cactus trek, he told us we'd see some amazing sites, and we were hooked. We just didn't expect it to be quite as incredible as it turned out! Leon and Paula were extremely hospitable, and very kind - they really understand great service! They provided picked us up from our accommodation and supplied us with plenty of sandwiches and snacks! They drove us around 20-30 minutes out of town to the cactus canyons where we started our cactus trek. The trek is of easy difficulty, they gave us helmets and walking sticks (and we wish we wore better shoes!), and it involves a circle trek around the canyon. Leon is an experienced hiker, and the route he took us on was phenomenal!! The mix of water in the desert, with the 8m high cacti and the special caves dotted through the trek made it our best experience of the Atacama Desert (and we had jam packed days!). This trek is by far the most fun and breathtaking hike we have ever done, the scenery is beautiful, Leon's knowledge of the area and history is incredible, and the service of Leon and Paula by far surpassed all our expectations! 10000% recommended!

review_text: We were told that after 1pm only tours can enter moon valley meaning no sunset unless we joined a tour. FALSE. If you buy a ticket before 1pm this ticket also allows you to enter the viewing area at Mirador Piedra del Coyote (a few minutes drive from moon valley entrance) for the sunset viewing. This is where all the tour groups go as you can see the sun set over the entire valley. Tickets cost 2500 per person before 1pm which gets you entrance to the valley plus entrance to the viewing area for sunset - just keep hold of your ticket. So, save yourself the £20 tour price and drive or bike yourself!

review_text: A great hike - strenuous and beautiful. There is one main trail (i don't think there are options). It's basically in the shape of a P. It's 12km long and takes about 5 hours return. You start at the bottom of the P... hike to the middle of it (all under the sight of the Volcano Osorno which is gorgeous). The first part of the hike is desolate. And the hike is appropriately called desolation! Remember this is all at the base of a volcano. When you get to the P you keep going straight where you are going to make your loop (up the straight part of the P). Then you turn right and down to the lake - where eventually you make your way to a hidden lake) to rest. It's quiet and gorgeous. Lovely! Then of course you can either walk back around or if you prefer (and it's summer) walk the beach back (which is not part of the P) but would look more like an upside down U if you were hiking it. Now, two tips. And these are IMPORTANT! 1- there is free parking right behind the paid parking lot. Don't waste 5,000 pesos paying for paid parking. 2- and most most most importantly - bring a hat or a fly swatter or something that you can use to bat away the terribly large and annoying flies that exist in this park. If you hit them they actually leave you - but if you don't they will stay with you the whole hike. I got good at batting them away so wasn't overly annoyed once I figured out the secret. The secret is to stop once a fly circles you. Just wait and you'll see the pattern he flies in around and around you. Then bat him away with your hat/swatter. When you do - he leaves. I saw others who didn't know how to get rid of them and they were sooo upset. I mean one guy was screaming get them away from me! It was quite funny. But after 5 hours of them... it does get rather annoying.
title: Gorgeous!

review_text: What a delightful day we spent exploring Santiago and soaking in the history of this vibrant and artistic city founded over five hundred years ago. All of this was made possible with the good humor, quick wit and vast knowledge imparted to us by Thomas Poussard, tour guide extraordinaire. My friend and I were heading towards Valparaiso for a cruise to French Polynesia and we spent the day and night in Santiago to get a taste of Chile. We only wished we had made more time for this wonderful city. Thomas and his friend and fellow guide Claudia picked us up at our hotel and we spent the next six hours seeing the historic downtown (the entire city is historic), visiting the Bellavista area and the ecclectic house of famous poet Pablo Neruda and the cathedral. My favorite part of the day was visiting an incredible wine bar with flights of Chilean wine. The owner had ingenious markings for the bathrooms using drawings of a wine opener to indicate male, female and handicapped differences! Truly fun. If you find yourself going to Chile call Thomas first, tell him what you want to see and he will magically make your Chilean dreams come true. Well worth the price for a private tour at your pace.

review_text: We emailed in advance of our trip to see if there were possibilities of scheduling an ice hiking trip given the season hadn't exactly started yet (we ice-hiked on Sep 23), and fortunately we were able to slot it in as weather conditions were favorable. We were also the 2nd trip of the season! Pedro was our main guide, and was thankful that he spoke very good english given that we spoke very little Spanish. He was very knowledgeable and made us feel safe the entire trip, and was extremely careful and attentive given it was our first ice-hiking experience. It was definitely worth every penny, and we had some awesome photos and videos to go with this experience! I would highly recommend them. The guides also gave great advice on our W trek, and even helped us lug a small ice glacier on our boat ride back because Mark's knee was twitchy. We felt really thankful for that - we were able to hike the rest of our W trek having taken their advice seriously. We had a lot of fun skipping stones, taking GoPro videos and talking about outdoor adventures together. Also, one small note, we did this one day 2 of our W trek, hiking West to East - best decision ever since somehow hiking 1 day behind everyone else that probably flew in to Punta Arenas and rode into Puerto Natales the same day meant we hiked a lot of the remaining route in solitude! Awesome!

In addition, he is involved in and knowledgeable about many aspects of environmental conservation, outreach, and ornithology in Chile and South America, so we had some great conversations about birding, conservation, etc. Honestly, much of the day felt like being back home, birding with my semi-professional birding friends...except that Fernando was patient with my constant, "what bird is singing that song?" questions. He took lots and lots of time to try to coax out a calling Black Rail (ultimately without luck) and a Striped-back Bittern (with luck!) I appreciated the professional commitment he made to ensuring we saw as many species as possible. He also quickly understood my interest in learning more about natural history, species behavior, etc., rather than just ticking off species, so for me the day was a rich and full birding experience. The company's professionalism is really impressive. The booking process was easy; communication was timely and comprehensive, and Santiago was an awesome driver! They offer a multitude of tours around Chile and South America. My experience was so rewarding, I'm thinking of planning and booking their complete Chile birding tour.

review_text: The easiest way to get to La Sebastiana is by taxi, but you would miss all the charm of the Ascensores (funiculars) which make visiting Valpo (as Valparaíso is affectionately known) a truly unique experience. The closest of the Ascensores to La Sebastiana is the Espiritu Santo (which is under repair now in January 2018), but you can also take the Reina Victoria Ascensor (closest to the Bellavista subway station) and walk to the San Luis Church, where you will take a micro (bus) that will drop you off on the corner of Calle Ricardo de Ferrari. There are three Casas de Pablo Neruda in Chile and in La Sebastiana you will learn how Pablo Neruda was a Master in enjoying life to the fullest. After visiting his house, you may want to take a stroll around the streets of Valpo and appreciate several houses and walls that are painted in many different colours and styles. These are called "Museo a Cielo Abierto" ("Open Air Museum"). You will also find a couple of places where you can stop for a quick meal, as you walk all the way down, back to the hustle and bustle that awaits you in the city below. The amazingly beautiful streets of the upper hills of Valparaíso remind us of Montmartre (it is the same "feeling", as many artists prefer to live and work there) but the way these charming colours contrast with the port of Valpo below is unique.

review_text: A fantastic tour of the vineyard with professional explanations. The domain is located in the valley between 2 rivers. The vineyards are all flat, creating a micro climate. The mornings are +/- 2° C colder. The domain has a bio-eco system (constructed by a Belgian) for water purification with various vegetation that attracts insects from the vineyard and therefore they should not use pesticides. They also have a heat pump to generate energy for wine production and the water that is not pumped back is used for rinsing and cleaning the installations, which then flows back to the river via the bio-eco system. Here they only make red wines but they have a new investment closer to the ocean for white and rosé with elegant mineral notes. With the necessary guidance we tasted beautiful wines. Conclusion: friendly welcome, very good explanation, professional company, beautiful wines. Highly recommended. review_text: Excellent tour. Guide was extremely knowledgable and really enjoyed the walk through town. Lunch at the winery was incredible. Spectacular views and wonderful food and wine. Highly recommend.
title: Coast and winery tour

review_text: I booked this trip the day before and it was easy. Got a text from our guide, Sebastian and we were picked up from my hotel in Santiago. Sebastian was very knowledgeable and very passionate about his country. We wandered around the beautiful streets of Valparaiso, met some artists and jewelry makers and learnt some more history. In the afternoon we went for lunch at Vina - Casas Del Bosque and were spoilt with wonderful food, wines and the service was impeccable. We headed back to Santiago and dropped back at our hotel. Thank you Ecordua and Sebastian for a wonderful day. Review of: Valparaíso: Discovering the Jewel of the Pacific Thank you for your wonderful review! We’re so glad to hear that booking your trip was easy and that you had an amazing day exploring Valparaíso and enjoying lunch at Casas del Bosque. It’s great to know that Sebastian’s passion and knowledge added to the experience and that you enjoyed meeting local artists and learning about the area’s history. We truly appreciate your kind words and hope to welcome you back for more adventures in the future!
title: Amazing day trip

review_text: It was very well attended to and I scheduled the tour for the day I could fit into my schedule. I highly recommend!!! It was recommended by LikeChile.
title: It was amazing!!

review_text: We had an excellent time at this vineyard and I would recommend anyone in Santa Cruz to visit and create their own wine (a daily midday event). It may seem expensive at $30,000 but considering the amount of wine you drink there, the tour (in English also) and the bottle you take away its actually very reasonable. Learnt lots, (about the vines, the grapes and the process) and drank awesome wine in the sun all with lovely friendly staff. Also recommend taking a picnic. It's also lovely landscape to cycle in. We hired from our hostel, 10km away in Santa Cruz - Hostel Del Centro, also recommended.
title: Delicious wine, beautiful sun & friendly staff

review_text: Everything was great. Benjamin and Gabrielle did the fantastic tour for us. The only thing I would have changed was when we stopped for the llamas. They were in horrible shape and injured, and it was very unsettling for quite a few of us to see them in that condition especially on a tour. Review of: Inca Lagoon in Andes Mountain Range - Visit Local Vineyard with Tasting included
title: Great tour

review_text: The tour guide, George, made the trip a great experience. He kept the whole bus interested in Chile's history and geography. Review of: From Santiago: Viña Concha y Toro Traditional Half-Day Tour Thank you very much for sharing your experience with us!
title: Concha y Toro trip experience.

review_text: The wind made it hard to view as it should have been viewed. Waterfalls are my favorite and this one was amazing.
title: Beautiful Waterfall!

review_text: The Cemetery is a peaceful place and it is interesting to see the variety of nationalities and the size of the mausoleums--reflecting the cosmopolitan nature of the history of Punta Arenas.
title: Interesting insight into the history of Punta Arenas

review_text: Excellent tour.. Our guide Francesca & driver Rodriguez were outstanding. Francesca was knowledgeable. Professional and engaging.
title: Valparaíso a Must See

review_text: An amazing tour with Valentina Belen and Concha y Toro. Essential stop if in Santiago 😊 great tasting of different wines and cheese 🧀 Review of: From Santiago: Viña Concha y Toro Marqués Half Day Tour Great to hear you had an amazing tour with Belen and Concha y Toro! Thank you for sharing your positive experience. We hope to see you again soon for more adventures. 😊🍷🧀

review_text: Majestic mountains, turquoise lagoons and sharp winds...
title: Movie Scenery

review_text: Right in the middle of the main square of Puntas Arenas is the statue to the hero of this area who found a safe passage through the straits names after him instead of having to hazard a ship by going around the Horn. It is both impressive and imposing, very well executed.
title: See the magnificent statue of Hernando de Magallenes

review_text: Beautiful excursion to Valparaiso and Viña del Mar, I highlight the guide Rocio for her professional attention, highly recommended. The trip went as scheduled, I surely would not hesitate to contact this agency again. Review of: Tour Valparaiso Viña del Mar Reñaca Beach from Santiago.
title: Excellent excursion

review_text: If you want to sit back, relax and let you guide through the surroundings of Santiago, this is a tour for you. Our guide Pablo gave us a lot of information and was eager to chat with us. We had a lovely apero at the Embalse del Yeso. This is the most affordable tour I've seen and the organisation even goes when there's only 1 passenger. The café in the morning and house of chocolate in the afternoon were less interesting for me. Review of: Cajon del Maipo and Parque Salto El Yeso Full-Day Tour thanks for your choice
title: A lovely tour to the Embalse del Yeso and Cajon del Maipo with SkiTotal

review_text: Perhaps many people do not realize that there are icebers and glaciers in this area - well there are.... and they are spectacular. I needed one more day to take advantage of seeing more -
title: as good as you can get

review_text: Very high quality and unique goods. The pricer are higher than other places such as the Saint Lucia market - but quality is much higher. Nice place to spend an afternoon. Unfortunately it is in la Condes area which is always a challenge to get to on public transportation.
title: Good place for unique souvenirs

review_text: A recommendable visit, best in the late afternoon. You really need to bring a lot of water, you will get very dry. If you go to the salt caves first, don't bring a camera for that part, you cannot hold a camera, water and a smartphone and not damage something while climbing and crawling.
title: Great scenery

review_text: The thermal baths meet the goal of having pools with different temperatures, but only that, the enclosure completely falls far below the standard one desires of a space close to nature and relaxation, although they are economical, do not meet, the place is untidy, dirty, with many of its facilities in poor condition, broken and neglected. Open electrical boxes, exposed tubes and cables, broken bunkers, waterless pools, dirty bathrooms and dressing rooms, broken tiled hallways and detached concrete. Honestly for the same value there are much better thermals.
title: Thermal Trancura a disappointment

review_text: You can walk all over the beach,. Romantic and nice also there is a personal trainning for free. You can see people walk or making surf.
title: Very Good

review_text: Me and a friend did two trips with We Love and both went with guide Sebastian, could not have been better, communication was fine and interactive for all, not to mention the education, I say the same for the drivers who accompanied us (Isaac and another I do not remember the name). Oi We Lover! Ficamos felizes em saber que teve uma experiência tão boa com a gente. Obrigado pela confiança e esperamos te receber de novo em breve! ❤️

review_text: I tried to book the premium tour online he night before but received no response. Didn't get a response with a follow up email in the morning either, so I tried calling and they had availability for a regular tour in English. If you want the premium tour in English then book a couple of days in advance. The tour itself was great, very informative and the guide was knowledgeable. Wine tasting (2 whites and 2 reds) was also very good. To get there get the metro to Quilin, then a taxi for CLP2300. They provide a van transfer back to the metro at the end for CLP1000 per person.
title: Great tour but booking process could be better

review_text: Museo Aeronautico y del Espacio is located in part of where Aeropuerto de Los Cerrillos, Santiago de Chile main airport, was located in the sixties. It has a nice and interesting display of military and civil aircrafts.
title: A must if you like airplanes!

review_text: We had an amazing 2 full day private tours with an excellent guide Norman. Everything was very well organized. We also did the 3 days Uyuni tour with them. The bolivian drivers were very helpful and careful. Unforgettable memories.
title: 2 different tours

review_text: Wonderful experience. The cabins, pool, river and tasting with the great Don Pedro. The valley is impressive
title: Wonderful.

review_text: This was a great tour with Francisca. She was very involved, caring, personable, and loves her work. She answered all questions and was concerned that everyone throughly enjoyed the tour. The walking tour was really exceptional to see and the driver was very capable and professional. They fill up on weekends so go on a weekday if you can. Be sure to request Francisca. Thanks Review of: Valparaiso Port and Vina del Mar Full-Day Tour from Santiago
title: Guide made it a wonderful day

review_text: Very good agency, very attentive staff and easy to communicate with. Prices for the tours were good, similar or even a little lower than the other Brazilian agencies I researched. A tip, if you can, pay for the tour in slipper pesos for them. I paid on pix, and then when I went to do the calculation, I saw that the value was higher than if I had exchanged reais for pesos and paid at the agency. I took the tour to Concha y Toro, where they basically offer a transfer and buy your ticket (the driver was super nice, unfortunately I don't remember his name, but he's a Bahian). And the other tour was to Portillo, this one was super complete and was really worth the experience. The spectacular guide Maria spoke from beginning to end, giving valuable information and explanations. The "pajarito" driver was also very sweet and attentive. Delicious and well served picnic.
title: I recommend!

review_text: Excellent tour. Daniel, the guide, not only gave us his knowledge of the place, but also entertained us by telling us ad hoc stories, it was very pleasant. Together with the driver they prepared a delicious cocktail for us. We do not remember the name of the driver, but he was the one who took us to the Valley of the Moon on October 2 in the afternoon, and we want to highlight him because he drove with great caution. We recommend this tour with a 10.
title: Excursion to the Valley of the Moon

review_text: The view at the end was great, the tour guide Jorge was wonderful, but this is advertised as a “picnic” and there was no food or drink provided. You get a driver with some narration up to El Yeso, which if that’s what it was advertised as, would have exceeded my expectations. review_text: Almost 4.200 m, and those beautiful Lagoons in the nowhere, Amazing tour, starting very early in the morning and finishing after 5 in the afternoon! Highly recommended!!!

I loved their sympathy and efficiency. Unlike most agencies for astronomical tours, they only do it when the weather permits. review_text: There’s 3 caves you can visit. We visited the main one first, which was really nice and interesting, but didn’t take much time (30-40 minutes or so). The day after we came back for the hike to the other 2 caves, which we really enjoyed. It took us about 2,5 hours and there’s some very nice views and beautiful nature. We only ran into one other group on this hike, so a good way to escape the crowds that visit the main cave as well.
title: Visit all three caves!

title: Enbrace the Stars

review_text: Wonderful experience with Nature. The guide was very knowledegable about all things in Chile. We enjoyed seeing all the plants in bloom. We enjoyed our conversation along the way. The countryside was very interesting. The boat ride out to the island preserve to see the penguins was a short, very safe experience. The penguin colony was unbelievably awesome. As an extra bonus, we also saw porpoise, otter, huge jellyfish in the water. There are a lot of birds in the area as well. The seafood lunch after the tour was some of the best seafood I have ever tasted. The seafood is caught the same day you eat it! I highly recommend this tour. Review of: Zapallar and Cachagua Island Experience Thank you so much for your lovely review! We're thrilled to hear that your experience in nature was so memorable. It sounds like the penguin colony and the surrounding wildlife made for an unforgettable adventure. The boat ride, while short, really offers an up-close view of the area’s beauty, and we're so glad you got to experience the porpoise, otter, and jellyfish too! It’s also fantastic to know that the seafood lunch lived up to your expectations—freshly caught and perfectly prepared. We’re grateful for your recommendation and hope you return soon for more amazing experiences with us! 🌿🐧🍴
title: Exceptional tour seeing an incredible penquin colony! Tour guide was a wealth of knowledge.

review_text: Villarrica is an extensive and very beautiful lake, made even more interesting by the beautiful natural scenery that surrounds it. In the city of Pucon, the urbanization of the surrounding village seemed more rustic and interesting than in the neighboring city that gives its name to the lake. Both in Villarrica and Pucon there are lake beaches that are very popular in high season. We visited 5 large lakes in the Araucania region and we can say that each one has unique landscapes and views. Finally, contemplating Lake Villarrica is one of the main activities on a tour of the region.
title: Lake, mountains and volcano form a beautiful setting

review_text: I'm only giving 1 star because you can't give zero. Let’s go to the facts: you contract the tours with Welove, but most are outsourced. That is, you pay more expensive thinking you are buying quality, but are put on excursions with cheaper agencies, with lower service. The food offered is terrible — I had a bad time — and the lunch in Piedras Rojas was served cold and of poor quality. Guides are rushed, do not give enough time in the sights. I don't even have a photo in Laguna Antiplânicas for that. Before hiring, I asked if the tours were all done by Welove herself. I was assured that yes, or that the outsourcers would maintain the same standard. That's a lie. If I can give you some advice: rent a car and take the tours on your own — it's no seven-headed beast. Or close with the Araya: it's more expensive, but the experience is real. Unfortunately, we left to close there and there were no more vacancies in Araya. Welove is just marketing. And more: none of the guides speak Portuguese or is Brazilian Lamentamos profundamente que sua experiência não tenha sido como esperava. Entendemos sua frustração e valorizamos cada ponto levantado. Seu feedback é importantes para nós, pois nos ajuda a identificar pontos de melhoria e seguir evoluindo. Reforçamos que contamos com um setor de pós-venda sempre disponível para acolher qualquer relato e buscar soluções. Quanto à operação, seguimos com parceiros selecionados para manter nosso padrão e possuímos diversos guias bilingües para atender nossos clientes.
title: Only marketing

review_text: This is an amazing sight. In ways it reminded me of the Namibian Dead Vlei. Awesome views after the initial 20 min walk to the top. The altitude is high and if visiting in the afternoon it can be rather hot. Make sure you are hydrated with good sun protection and comfortable walking shoes. Have a camera handy for some terrific shots.
title: Hot very hot!

review_text: We hired HecTours to pick two couples up after our cruise ended in Valparaiso. We wanted to tour Valparaiso and then be taken to our hotel in Santiago And then have a day long tour of Santiago. Our guide, Hector, was terrific, making sure we saw as many sections and art as possible. He also took us to a wonderful seafood restaurant and helped us choose typical Chilean dishes in Valparaiso. In Santiago he showed us so many historic, civic and interesting sections as well as the produce market which was great fun. I highly recommend HecTour Service if you want the best guide. Day two of our
title: Wonderful, helpful and flexible.

review_text: You can find wine country all over Chile. A trip to Vina Underraga happens daliy with Turistik ($55) tours. You can book a morning (9am) or afternoon (2pm) tour normally lasting about 4 hours. I found the tour very educational especially having the opportunity to see the vineyard, vineyard displays (for each wine produced), distilleries, and wine cellars (both bottled and barreled in American Oak) where they store the wine for years. At the end of the tour you get to taste four-five different types of wine. They give you a complimentary wine glass and lastly you have time to buy wine to take home. I highly recommend this tour for anyone visiting the Santiago, Chile area in the future. Enjoy the Chilean experience first-hand. Happy Travels!!!
title: GREAT WINE TASTING AND TOUR WITH EDUCATION

review_text: Chileguru organised our transfers, tours and accommodation, all of which were excellent - they found the best tour guides. The whole holiday went without a hitch, and the local contact, Priscilla (queen of the desert) was friendly, reliable and conscientious. I very much had the feeling that if any problem had arisen it would have been swiftly dealt with - there's a nice feeling of being in safe hands. Douglas and Ash, It was an immense pleasure to have you in Chile and be in touch with you over the months prior to your travels. I can’t count all the laughs we had reading your travel journals before and after your travels to Atacama. I’m so happy you met with Priscilla in the desert and I know she’s happy to have met with you as well. Happy to hear you felt like your were in safe hands, had any problems arisen. I think we need to have you back in Chile soon, to see what you have to say about Patagonia or Easter Island - I’m sure there’s a lot of material yet to be discovered! All the best to both of you, Julie, Peter & Chile Guru Team

review_text: This was a great way to see the life of Santiago which otherwise would have remained hidden from us. Our guide was particularly good at passing on historical information in the context of what we were seeing. Her explanation of the Salvador Allende / Augosto Pinochet years when we were at the cemetery was very informative.
title: Excellent alternative view of Santiago

review_text: located in one of the most relevant buildings remaining from the early days it offers a unique and comprehensive collection of historical documents and pieces
title: an accurate and documented museum

review_text: Fantastic views across the salt flats. The abundance of birdlife depends on the time of year that you visit but there are normally two species of flamingo, Andean avocet and small waders to be seen. Watch out for small lizards. There are toilets and good information boards.
title: Camera and binoculars are a must

review_text: We visited the valley for the views of the Andes and the ride up the valley (60 hair pin bends). We were not disappointed - spectacular views in all directions (bar the smog above Santiago). We even managed to see about 10 condors all flying together!
title: Wonderful views of the Andes

review_text: Well designed and interesting building, good restaurant and very informative tour/tasting; for me the best out of all the main names in the valley. Impressive quality of wine too.
title: Very smart and informative visit

review_text: It was wonderful! Lorena was our guide, welcomed us and accompanied us super well! The structure, the tour, the view, the tips, the information, it was all great! I will definitely make new trips with them!

review_text: We booked the tour with San Andino, and were very happy with it. The driver/guide was very knowledgable and spoke pretty English. Group wasn't too big either and we had plenty of time to see everything. We booked other tours in and around Atacama desert with them and I can recommend them as being reliable and professional

review_text: Whipala features some of the most knowledgeable guides I've ever met in all my travels, I've done 4 tours with them with 3 different guides and they all gave us unforgettable experiences. They're professionals and really passionate about their job and the areas they're going to show you, choose them and you won't regret it!
title: What a great experience!

review_text: My husband and I were in San Pedro between the 12th and 18th of November on vacation and to celebrate my birthday. We close all tours with FláviaBia. Simply, impeccable! Every detail was thought out to please all tastes! Delicious food served on charming tables that completed the most beautiful landscapes! Like a scene from a movie! I have lactose intolerance and I was very happy with the options that were designed so that it didn't lack anything in terms of flavor and care. There are options for those who have other restrictions, such as gluten, for example. Punctuality on all tours! The guides are a real lesson in history, geography and culture. In addition to being very friendly and helpful! And whoever thinks it's not worth the cost, think again... because they're details, but they win you over. Because it made all the difference having bathrobes at the Puritama Hot Springs (freezing wind coming out of the warm waters) or being the only ones with umbrellas to protect from the sun at Lagunas Escondidas. The "FlaviaBia standard" for travel ended up becoming my parameter from now on lol
title: Couple trip to Atacama

review_text: Is the largest mall in Chile, good brands, good international prices and varied places to eat and drink. Perfect to spend a different afternoon or escape from the extreme climates of Santiago.
title: At the base of the tallest building in South America.

review_text: Our second family trip with the FláviaBia team and once again was amazing and surprising! We had contact with very qualified professionals from the assembly of the script, through in-local care in the store and guidance on the eve of each tour, by the kitchen staff making delicious meals and finally and very important were the different guides - all perfect , especially Eduardo, Luiz and Rodrigo . Very happy with the experience of meeting Atacama with this team!

review_text: My wife and I had a great sunset tour with Paul. It felt very special to drive up to the base of the volcano as the sun was starting to set, and we were amazed at how long the sunset lasted at the top. We enjoyed delicious snacks and lovely drinks while marvelling at the reds, yellows and oranges. Paul is a fab photographer and took some amazing photos of us during sunset and under the amazing array of stars. He sent all of these pictures to us the next day. Overall, a great experience with great company. Muchos gracias. Russ, Thanks a lot for you review and for choosing our company to enjoy this amazing sunset! It was a pleasure to share with you those moments and also our knowledge! Hope to see you and Nicola soon! Have a great time in Chile! Kind regards, Andreia
title: A great sunset

review_text: 12 well-marked trails, picnic area, bathrooms and parking lots. Beautiful views, a lagoon with ducks, hanging bridges, high viewpoints, a river of fresh, clean water and glasses to test the water. If you are lucky you see some wild pudú. Only approximately 40 minutes from Quellón, the route is good and signposted, you can get there in a 4x4.
title: An excellent walk in Quellón

review_text: I can think of a dozen superlatives to describe the 4-day celebration of Viu Manent's 80th Anniversary...yet the experience was so outstanding I'm almost speechless. The vineyard tours were very informative. The wines definitely show a sense of place and partnership between vineyard manager and winemaker. The family's multi-generational experience and passion for wine shows through in every glass, from Secreto to Viu1. We were welcomed to a splendid wine tasting by a solo violinist, then entered the impressive tasting room with a long table covered--I mean covered--with wine glasses. Not your basic wine glasses...different ones to match and enhance each wine that was in the glass. A spiritual experience culminating with an outdoor lunch on a warm spring day. The grand finale was their elegant and thoroughly enjoyable gala celebration. My deep appreciation to everyone at Viu Manent for an experience that will last a lifetime. A su éxito continuo. Fue un placer conocer a todo el mundo. I am so lucky I can find Viu Manent wines locally (Brennan's Market).
title: 80th Anniversary celebration as impressive and grand as the wines

review_text: I write this from the viewpoint of a couple who have taken courses at UC Davis in enology and viticulture but still consider themselves amateurs. Having said that our tour guide for this trip was Jose, the owner. He and his wife, who used to work for Ampora wine tours in Mendoza have started a great tour business. He and the driver picked us up on time then got the 5 other people with us. We went to Emiliana first, the organic arm of conco y toro. Jose was the most knowledgable wine guide we have ever had. Most likely due to his education as an engineer. He knew about the geology weather soil and history of the regions. He knew about varietals and why they were chosen. He knew about the business side of wine making. He is also starting an olive oil business. We went to a total of 4 wineries. Lunch was tasty but the 30 something's thought the quantity was insufficient. We appreciated the thought the went into the wine grape growing and production process, the wine pairings, and the esthetics of each tasting area. It was a great overview. With their previous relationship with ampora you might be able to get these two groups to cover Santiago and Mendoza tours on a single trip. When we come back in the spring we will tour with him again. Review of: Best Wine Tasting in Santiago

review_text: THE tour to book! Whether you are a wildlife fanatic, or not even so much; you will love this tour. The enthousiasm with which tourguide Zita shares her love for Whales, Guanacas, Desert Foxes, Sea Lions and a lot more beautiful creatures living in the area has a very infectuous effect on the entire group. If you didnt love animals before; you will after this tour. Plus, they give so much info on every aspect of these animals, you will feel like an expert yourself! The day starts off early, since it is a 2 hour ride to where the boat tour starts. But you can step out of bed into the car without breakfast; because everything is taken care off by Zita. During this ride Zita will tell you already so much about the environment and the animals living there, time will fly. Halfway there is a breakfast break in the middle of the desert. Be aware; it will be the most elaborate breakfast you will have on your entire holiday; so dont eat too much before!:) Once you arrive at the small town/harbour you are welcomed by the local guardians of nature (CONAF). You also meet their local partners who offer the boat and are the experts on where to spot the whales and other animals. As all chilean people appear to be, they are incredibly friendly and helpful to make your day great. The boat tour takes about 2 hours, in which your mind will get blown away. Obviously, spotting whales and dolphins is not guaranteed (apparently its difficult to make whales and dolphins appear on command;) ), so you will need to have some luck. For our tour, we did. We were shown a beautiful Whale after being on the water for only 2 minutes or so! Its an amazing sight. During this tour the love for wildlife Zita and the locals share, is very clear and the enthousiasm they educate the guests with is brilliant. Next to the whale, we saw a group of around 100 dolphins (very rare!), an isle filled with Sealions which were actually giving birth at the moment we were there, lazily chilling Seals, happily eating Marine Otter, funny looking Penguins and many other birds. All of which are so close you could almost touch them! After the boat tour, you are taken to a local restaurant for lunch. Tastes very good and you can try some local specialties. Be aware; after this moment your energy levels will be at a low due to all the spectacle. However, Zita is prepared for this; all will have a comfortable neck pillow for the ride to the next stop. Since locals in this region are either fishermen or olive farmers, you will also get a short tour at an olive farm. In summary; this will the one of the most spectacular, action packed, nature loving days you will ever have. Great value for money for a day never to forget, allowing you to take pictures that normally you will find only in National Geographic magazines and such. Big thanks to Whale Watching Chile for this unforgetable experience! Review of: La Serena Whale Watching Cruise with Atacama Desert Tour
title: Amazing tour, complete day packed with unforgetable experiences!

review_text: An outstanding experience in breathtaking scenery. We spent 4 days and 5 nights at Patagonia Camp, an all inclusive lodging arrangement that provides lodging in cozy yurts, all meals, transportation, guided hikes and treks to many of the Park attractions (park fees included); with pick up/return to Punta Arenas. Not the economy method of visiting Torres del Paine, but highly recommended for comfort, convenience, high quality food and staff, and exposure to the variety of outdoor activities available. Introduced on the first day hike in hard rain, the balance of the stay was in good to excellent weather with none of the famous winds. As seniors in reasonably good condition, the hike to the base of the towers was difficult on the return. All other hikes were easy to moderate. The staff was cheerful, very accommodating and very engaging. The guides were outstanding and knowledgeable about the natural environment. The food was carefully prepared and in generous proportions. We were fortunate in missing the crowds, enjoyed good weather, and had an exceptional experience with this organization. We would highly recommend Patagonia Camp. Information available on line at www.patagoniacamp.com.
title: Torres del Paine via Patagonia Camp

review_text: This mine tour was recommended by a couple of Chileans we met on the trip, and it certainly was worthwhile. Started in 1884, the coal mine was closed in 1976, and I don't think much has changed! The tour itself is in Spanish -- the guides are ex-miners -- so we missed out on quite a bit I know, but it was still a worthwhile experience. You are fitted with a lighted miner's helmet and battery pack, taken down in a cage-basket elevator, then walk through the mine (a little further down) and finally up and out. This is obviously not for the claustrophobic -- at times we were practically on our knees getting through some of the passages -- and it could be difficult for tall people; I'm 5'8" and I had to walk stooped over much of the time. Still a unique experience and a fascinating look into the conditions in which people had to work.
title: Unique Experience!

review_text: We traveled to Atacama in December 2024 and did all the tours with Ayllu. The differential of the company in fact are the meals offered on the tours that are very good. However, the amounts charged are quite high and the services offered should be better in order for the price to be fair. Our first days of tours went smoothly, all walking according to the schedule, which is the minimum. More to the middle of our trip we made a tour with a guide from the agency, who had already accompanied us earlier. The trip to the Altiplanas and Rojas stones lagoons leaves early and the guide in addition to driving super badly (having given light exits from the road a few times), was all the way drinking coffee and energetic, chocolate and asking for music so that it did not give him sleep at the wheel. In addition to speaking energetically at all times and being "on 220v". We followed the tour and, in addition to the strange behavior of the guide, the stove used to be part of the breakfast leaked gas, we were in a closed car and the incident was noticed by us, which left me quite tense (the worst is that this was not the only situation in which the gas from the stove leaked into the car, it occurred again beyond this). I feel that we did not enjoy this tour as much as expected with the constant tension caused by the wrong direction of the guide and their signals that you could sleep at the wheel and the gas incident. Besides other small incidents, which did not prevent the good follow-up of our journey, another complicadissima situation was the fact that on the last day we had marked an ascension to the Volcano Lascar. However, 2 days before we climbed the Cerro Toco and it was a very difficult ride for us because of the altitude (my fiancé was suffering from headaches throughout the afternoon even taking medication and I with a fast heart), with this we decided to preserve our body and health and request a change from the last day's ride. I tried to contact the agent who came to assist me and she did not receive the messages, when she received I was directed to another number to which I sent the request for a change of ticket. The same number had spoken to me earlier about the ride we would have that night. The number answered me, I asked about 2 specific tours, he informed me, said that some details would need to be confirmed, but gave me an advance of the values, duration, dynamics of the tour, schedule and also informed that we could receive a refund of the difference in values between the tour we had contracted (and already paid) and the new one. The next day we headed for the day's walk, confident that the next day, our last day of trip, was resolved. Our illusion, when we arrived at the hotel and we had access to the Internet we were informed that we had spoken with an AI of the company that passed us all the wrong information. And that was the beginning of chaos. Frustrated and disappointed, I lost an entire afternoon and night until I was able to define with the company what we would actually do. We were not granted the refund of the difference in values (which although it was not provided in the contract we were informed that there would be), we were introduced to solutions that when questioned the logistics they said that would not give and we had the owner of the company going to our hotel without warning for 2 times. One we were not and the other we were already lying in pyjamas and we did not attend. The next day we went for a tour (tour in the region's vineyard) which we considered extremely expensive because it was what I had for that day (this IA had told us that this tour would be between 70 and 100 dollars, they later told us that it was 220 dollars for about 3 hours of tour, which I consider an exorbitant value, especially for the size of the vineyard which is quite small). We still had to hear for a few times from the guide and owner of the company that we "yellowed", which sounded a disrespectful and disguised posture that left us super embarrassed, even because there was another guide in the car. He proposed another tour at the end of the day, which we went, but we had to pay for the entrance to the park. And when he left us at the hotel still tried to sell us the photos and videos he took along the way for a value between 100 and 200 dollars. We chose this agency for the proposal to offer a premium service, in the illusion that we would not have all these problems, but the values showed exorbitant before the service provided. In addition to these highlighted problems, we still had the car without battery in the middle of a road without a phone signal when we returned from Rota dos Solares, following the road by the force of gravity, since it was a descent, and the car being controlled by the brake). If I went back to Atacama I would not return with them, with all this stress at the end of the trip we could not return from the holiday happy, satisfied and relaxed as we hoped. I'm still without words and digesting everything that happened...

review_text: Lake Llanquihue is not the largest lake in Chile (Lago General Carrera in the Aysen Region of Chile is almost twice as large as Lago Llanquihue), but this is probably one of the most beautiful locations in Chile. Best time to visit is during spring or fall, so one can avoid the tourist crowds and still enjoy decent weather. The lake is pretty just about any day of the year, but it is gorgeous during a sunny, clear day when you can appreciate the whole size of the lake and the incredible view of the surrounding snow-capped volcanoes. Besides visiting P. Varas, it is worth taking a trip to neighbouring Frutillar, Llanquihue town, Puerto Octay, and if you possibly can, take a trip around the whole lake via Las Cascadas and Ensenada where you can see the beautiful Osorno Volcano at close range.

review_text: This review covers a trip to Antarctica in December of 2013. It consisted of two nights in Punta Arenas (the night before and the night after the cruise) and five nights onboard the Ocean Nova. This particular cruise includes flights between Punta Arenas and King George Island, rather than taking the ship across the Drake Passage. We wanted to avoid the rough seas typical of a trip across the Drake Passage. We booked the cruise through Polar Cruises, a travel agency located in Seattle; the land arrangements in Punta Arenas and the air travel to/from King George Island and the shore expeditions to Antarctica were handled by Antarctica XXI; the shipboard operations were handled by Ocean Nova. All three organizations handled their responsibilities very well. Polar Cruises provide good guidance in making the arrangements, preparing for the trip, and handling payment. All of the Antarctica XXI staff were excellent, with good support from the time we arrived at the airport in Punta Arenas until we departed Punta Arenas for our return home. The shipboard Antarctica XXI staff were very knowledgeable about Antarctica and very friendly and helpful. There were two shore expeditions daily, one in the morning and one in the afternoon. Each one lasted 2-3 hours, which is long enough to experience Antarctica, but not so long as to end in exhaustion. Although the weather was cold (especially when riding in the Zodiacs), as long as the pre-departure suggestions for clothing and gear were followed, it was not unpleasant. They also offer (at an additional cost) options for sea kayaking and shoe-shoeing. The Ocean Nova is a great ship for visiting Antarctica: the maximum number of passengers is 68 (we had only 49); the cabins are spacious; the onboard service is very good, the food was great (not overly fancy, but well prepared and plentiful without being overdone); and since the hull is reinforced, it can break through moderate ice. There is a spacious observation deck (fore) and a library (aft) that have panoramic windows. The views were always spectacular. There are six Zodiacs on board, so everyone can go ashore at the same time. The staff are very well trained, so it feels like it is possible to have an exciting and informative expedition, while always feeling safe in a very demanding environment.
title: Fly the Drake Passage - Cruise in Antarctica

By the way, I tried to lay down but was unable to hear what our guide was explaining. Yes, the name of the guide is Alberto. Thank you very much for your comment. We are happy that you liked. The idea is that all the tourists should enjoy the tour in this way, listening at the stories that we have to tell and observing special objects through the telescopes. review_text: This bronze equestrian statue of José Miguel Carrera Verdugo stands on a marble plinth in Citizenship Park, opposite the Moneda Palace in Santiago de Chile. José Miguel Carrera Verdugo was a Chilean patriot general and dictator who fought Spain for years for Independence and served as head of government when breaks in the fighting allowed. He was a charismatic leader but a short-sighted administrator and an average military leader. Often at odds with Chile's liberator, Bernardo O'Higgins. He was executed in 1821 for conspiring against O'Higgins and Argentine liberator José de San Martín. The conflict between followers of O’Higgins and Carrera continues to some extent to this day, but this does not prevent their equestrian statues from standing next to each other opposite the Moneda Palace in Santiago de Chile. TIP: There are many concrete benches around to sit on but little shade.

review_text: We did the cruise from Puerto Montt to Puerto Natales in march 2012. It is important to know that it is a ferry, not a luxury boat. Those days were really good, enjoying the view and the dolphins, birds or sea lions in the outdoor. We had rain for 2 days so not so funny. Prepare a book to keep you busy just in case. A good thing is that they present flora and fauna power points during the trip. Nicely done and very useful! People can get sick when the boat reaches the ocean as the waves become more important. A little pill can help you have a good night. It allowed us to meet some very nice people who became friends. Prepare to have some good times.

review_text: I GOT ROBBED IN PARQUE FORESTAL A COUPLE MONTHS AGO! This was in broad daylight and there were plenty of people around. The police and the people at the U.S. embassy weren't at all surprised when I told them about it--they had heard the same story many times. Here's how it happened: I was walking through this park taking pictures (so, yes, they were attracted to my camera, an SLR); actually I saw them checking me out and I even wanted to get a shot of them b/c they were such a clearly sinister-looking gang, kinda night-clubby/druggie types with shaved heads (not skinhead-like, rather those sorta fancy shave jobs) all sitting around a picnic table. Just after I passed them a guy who looked like one of them asks me what time it is--this is to hear my voice and establish that I'm a tourist (and it also showed them that I had an iPhone). A few seconds later something soft and wet hits me on the back of my neck--bird crap or something like it. A woman comes up to me and is helping me clean it off--she's got bottle of water and some kleenex; she gets me to take off my jacket so she can clean it off, but then to get my jacket off I have to take off my bag and camera and put them on the park bench next to me (at the embassy they told me it's always a woman doing this part). Then a guy comes up and makes a noise and stares at me (he looked like the rest of them too); this distracts me from the bag and camera; then this little old man tells me my stuff is gone and tells me that they went that-a-way (out of the park) and is running after them and getting me to follow and then telling me that they're getting on this bus that's pulling away. So that's it. Again, totally light out, plenty of people around, very nice area, and happens all the time. So if you get hit my bird crap or whatever, just get out of there. During my 3 weeks in Chile--and before I got hit--i also heard about another tourist who had all his camera gear stolen in Santiago; and in Valparaiso I saw the end of an operation like the one I got hit with: people running onto a bus I was on in a big hurry, all excited, acting like they were looking for somebody (though it wasn't very good acting), and then jumping out of the bus through the back door. So it's definitely not uncommon. I should also add that I'm 5'10", male, a New York City, and a big traveler. So not a particularly obvious target other than the camera and the fact they I was clearly a tourist. All that said, I generally liked Santiago a lot, loved Valparaiso, and loved Patagonia. And Parque Forestal was, ironically, the prettiest and most peaceful place in Santiago. Just be prepared...
title: CRIME ALERT!!
