review_text: Just completed 4 days in Putre we did a full day tour with them to the park. Also a half day walking tour. Our guide Christian on both tours was amazing. He speaks English, is knowledgeable not only about plants and animals but since his family is from the area he knows a lot of traditions and cultural information. We saw so many animals vacunyas, vizcachas, flamingos, llamas alpacas lots of birds and stunning scenery. He gave us reminders and advice to avoid altitude affects. Even with this I did suffer from altitude sickness and we had to cancel one of our tours. He was so concerned that he came to our room when he got back to see how I was. Luckily I recouped and we got to enjoy our wonderful walking tour. Hummingbirds, beautiful landscape and a great guide
title: Superb, creative and English speaking

review_text: Very good! Yuri and Mario were great guides, they knew how to explain several things about Viña del Mar and Valparaiso. Furthermore, they ensured that everything ran on schedule.
title: I recommend!

review_text: A statue and a monument on a tree-lined area. OK but not worth going out of your way to see. Stop if you pass by.
title: Statue

review_text: I can’t say enough about what an enriching experience it was to make my second trip to Patagonia Chile with Patagonia Trout Adventures. Yes it’s an incredible fly fishing experience, but traveling and experiencing Patagonia is far more. Nick and Carolina embrace the traditions of Chile and offer a truly local experience from the fishing to Carolinas wonderful traditional culinary creations. The local guides Javier and Franco were incredible and the lodge owners and hosts Benjamin and Elisa are truly wonderful. All in all, the details and logistics were very well planned, the food and lodging are first rate. Nick and the guides intimate knowledge of the local waters make for a unique fishing experience in the one of the most beautiful and pristine places on earth. I highly recommend Patagonia Trout Adventures for anyone passionate about fly fishing and seeking the adventure of a life time and a true Chilean Patagonia cultural experience. This will not be a bucket list trip because you will want to return. Jeff Rog Jeff, Thank you so much for joining us in Patagonia again this year!! We truly had such a great time hosting you and your crew. It was a memorable experience and we look forward to seeing you again soon!!

review_text: Photographs do not do justice to this alien and incredibly beautiful place. Be warned that this place is VERY high and you may get altitude sickness if you are not prepared with medication or acclimation. Numerous inactive volcanoes and salt lakes, with a few vacunas (relatives of lamas) around. It is an out of this world experience. A bucket list type of thing!
title: Out of this earthly world!!!!

review_text: While the Reservoir is lovely and worth the visit I am very disappointed with the excursion itself and the bad information provided. In all the photos and description there is talk of a picnic lunch in the reservoir itself... because that does not happen. After visiting the Reservoir, we were taken to a buffet restaurant with no additional options for paid lunch of course. Not only is this not specified, but one understands that the picnic is lunch. Then they took us to a chocolate shop. And just back, before returning to Santiago in a fome, charmless place, they serve a wine, a few cheeses and salames and some cookies. I am ashamed of how the tourist is abused, giving bad information. And the disgusting thing about directing people to the places the agency clearly has an agreement to consume there. Apart from the bad publicity, the van we went in, has no basic comfort. For a tall person, the legs do not fit between seat and seat. And in the back row there is no air so we returned to Santiago sweltering with heat, even in winter. Our Guide was very friendly but I am 100% unhappy with the experience. Commenting on it with other people on the tour also agreed on the misleading advertising. I honestly don't recommend this agency. Review of: Small-Group Cajón del Maipo Full-Day Tour and Picnic ¡Gracias por tu amable comentario! Lamentamos que te hayas sentido de esta manera pero no hubo publicidad engañosa, el servicio fue entregado, se describe como un picnic porque NO es un almuerzo, si no, diría almuerzo. Nos ayudas a ser mejor, MTO Tour Team
title: Misleading advertising. Not recommended.

review_text: The cerro is very beautiful, the flora, the rocks and the yards... 💙 It also has an amazing view of the Cordillera in clean sky days. Just be careful with the floor and stairs in rainy days!

Down the back there are tracks through the coastal Swamp with lots of ferns and Fuschias. An interesting old gardens worth visit, especially if you are interested in the old Gondwanan links.

review_text: I recommend going in January or February, these are the times with better weather in this area (it will always rain, but little). Remember to go with good equipment with waterproof and thermal protection. Do not carry more than 13 kg for men (8kg for women), the best way to do the circuit is to stay in the shelters. The landscapes are incredible throughout the tour (Carry several batteries for your camera). The trips are long, so you should make at least a break for lunch. I recommend staying 2 nights in "the french", to be able to make the walk to the camp "the British".
title: Excellent experience

review_text: I did the southern route and the tour did exactly what it said on the tin and more. Our guide was Francisco and he was excellent especially given it was his first tour with Pachamama. He was really knowledgeable about each place we stopped at and went above and beyond to help. Day two is a long driving day, but we had fair warning about this and there were plenty of stops along the way to get snacks and stretch our legs - having previously travelled through Argentina I was fairly accustomed to long bus journeys so didn't find this a problem. The accommodation in each place is fairly basic but this is to be expected as it is after all a budget tour. However, you do have the option to organise your own accommodation if you wish. I found each place we stayed in to be clean and more than fine for one or two nights. I used the bus to get to Puerto Varas and hopped off to go further south. I love the hop on, hop off concept as it allows you to spend more time in places along the way and if I'd had more time I would have definitely hopped off in a couple of places.
title: Did exactly what it said on the tin and more (Lake District route)

review_text: It was good your & well guided by Valentina castro. Connectivity of bus was good like the places which are identified. Enjoyed the city trip to Santiago. Review of: Cable Car, Funicular and Sightseeing Bus in Santiago two days We are glad you enjoyed the experience. Best regards!

There were 2 blue whales, fin whale, we saw sea otters, dolphins, penguins, soo many birds..the nature is amazing and I could easily say that was one of the best tours for me in Chile.

review_text: Our tour with Victor N. was wonderful. He was well informed and had lots of fascinating information on Chile, its people, and its history to share. And, he was very patient and happy to answer any questions. In addition, he was super accommodating. Our flight was delayed 2 hours, then upon arrival, we ended up stuck in a bit of traffic - due to a fender bender - even though it was early Saturday morning. In spite of all this making us slightly late for our initially agreed upon time, Victor was very flexible and accommodating. Plus, he gave us valuable insight into where to go and where not to go, and when. We loved the personal touch, including the casual chats we had during our 4 hour excursion. Our driver was also very good at navigating the hectic downtown travel. We would definitely recommend this tour for first-timers to Santiago!
title: Santiago City Immersion with Victor N.

review_text: all great in artkinson gallery! excellent attention and beautiful art ❤️ the shop full of color as pure valparaiso 🌈 for me the best shop/gallery of valpo

review_text: Over Christmas 2024 we hiked the W-Trek in Última Esperanzanza (great name!) staying in refugios with full board so we didn't have to carry a lot of kit. After an initial attempt at trying to remotely arrange this directly with the refugios, I surrendered the job to Experiencechile.org. Over the course of a couple of weeks they organised all transport and accommodation from our arrival at Puerto Natales central bus station to the final transfer to the airport on our way out to Santiago. It was a complex itinerary involving public buses, ferries, private transport, accommodation and food, and required everything to hang together - and it did! Everything went according to plan and we were even provided with 'contingency' tickets for an alternative route out of the Park in the event that the Largo Grey cat was not operating due to high winds. So a big shout out to Charles and the team at Experience Chile - great job, thank you very much. Review of: Epic Patagonia: Torres del Paine - 'W' Trek Hi! While we're so happy you enjoyed your time in Patagonia, it looks like you meant to leave this review for Experience Chile. This is the review page for OneSeed Expeditions. I'm sure they'd love to have it on their trip page! Cheers, OneSeed Expeditions
title: Shout out to Experience Chile

review_text: This is quite simply one of the Great Park experiences in the world. Each day you can hike, climb a mountain, kayak, horseback ride or be driven to waterfalls, and trails in the park that will blow your mind and see how healing, and spiritual a place can be. I kept thinking, how many new experiences can everyday bring and fo 5 days I was dazzled. You leave the park seeing how a dedication to purity and non- commercial commitment can save places that we can grow in and save in our hearts forever.
title: A life changing experience

review_text: This is a great park if you're staying in a hotel in the area or need a break from the mall across the street. review_text: This is truly a gem right in the middle of Santiago downtown and a good reprieve from all the noise and people. There was no entrance fee but you had to put down your name in the registration log. The main structure and water fountain at the entrance was in the traditional Spanish architecture and was beautiful. As you climb the stairs up the hilltop, the view of the city started open up and you can get a 360 degree view of the landscape below. This was short visit and you can either spend 30 minutes or 2 hours relaxing at various spot along the trail.

review_text: I did two great hikes -- Torres del Paine -- up to the base of the towers; and French Valley. First one was great even though it was cloudy. The second one started with a wonderful boat ride. Hike itself was not so bad; wide open views.

review_text: We had a great time with Martin. Very friendly and inquisitive. Also played great music on the radio and answer all our questions.

review_text: I highly recommend doing the free walking tour as soon as possible when you arrive in Santiago. They offer two tours - at 10 AM and 3 PM. Look for the guides in red t-shirts in front of the cathedral in the Plaza de Armas. One guide is for the Spanish tour and one guide is for the English tour. No reservation is needed. You’ll get a wonderful introduction to the city with many great tips on food and activities from your guide. The tour is about three hours with a break in the middle. The best part of the tour is walking from stop to stop when you can ask your guide anything you wish about the city including food recommendations. You’ll learn about the history of the city and many interesting factoids about this great city on this tour. The tour is technically free, however, you are encouraged to give your guide a tip at the end. I would recommend at least a 10,000 peso note. It’s clearly worth it.
title: Great activity to start your Santiago trip with

review_text: We did the downhill tour from Alcohuaz back to Vicuna which was well organized from Adeline and Lincoln. review_text: My sister and I did the free walking tour with Franco who was an extremely knowledgeable and fun guide. review_text: Last Sunday we visited winery Emiliana due to the recommendation of the LP and good reviews on TripAdvisor. We booked a winetour in combination with a tasting. Since we were a bit early for the tour, we could have the tasting earlier. Since we just came back from some amazing winetours in Mendoza, we might have been spoiled with too high expectations. Already at the start of the tasting it was clear that the person who was in charge hardly knew anything about the wines, or the wineyard. All the white wines were good with 'seafood and sushi ', and when we asked details about the blend he was just reading the label, or we got an answer starting with 'I think'. This is defenitely not what we like to hear from professionals at a tasting. Finally this person told us that he just started working here (third day) and he still needs to learn a lot. We can understand this, but then we expect that someone with experience will lead the tasting, and this guy will be there to learn from it.
title: Below expectations

review_text: One-day tour to the King penguin reserve in Tierra del Fuego. Ferry to Porvenir through the strait, very pleasant crossing. Wonderful reserve, the reserve guide with complete explanations and observations through a telescope to appreciate the details of the penguins, we followed the indicated route walking in silence to see and not alter the environment. The Selkman team of driver Mauricio and guide Camila are extraordinary, friendly and communicative. Camila thoroughly masters the knowledge of the area, the land and the fauna of the route, with detailed explanations. Highly recommended and exciting.

review_text: Santiago city tour/transfer from the Celebrity Pursuit to the airport On December 23, the last day of our 16 days Celebrity cruise, we arrived to Valparaiso. There were enough people to fill 8 busses for the tour of Santiago and transfer to the airport. From the very beginning our guide Ronald informed us that the microphone is not working and in about 45 min we will stop at the break/toilet place and we will move to another bus. After waiting for a while at the stop we were informed that the replacement bus will not arrive. Our very good guide Ronald made considerable effort to deliver information to people in the second half of the bus by raising his voice and shuffling back and forth. And the end of about nine hours trip he almost lost his voice but delivered most of the information to the passengers in the back of the bus. Was it worth to take this long trip when total transfer to the airport would take much less time in the car? For two of us it made sense financially with additional limited sightseeing included. For group of four or larger it will make sense to hire private car/van for a more comfortable and efficient transfer. Fortunately, we had additional two full days in Santiago. Each day we took booked half day sight-seeing and had a little time left to enjoy this beautiful city on our own. Good Travels Review of: Transfer and Santiago City Tour: Cruise Port to Vibrant Capital

review_text: Guide José Miguel lead my wife and I up Volcano Osorno (2,652m) on 25 February 2014 (the last day of the 2013-2014 climbing season on this magnificent volcano). We had a fantastic (albeit very expensive!) time. Jose is a very professional, experienced and friendly guide who provided us with the highlight of a six week trip to an extremely beautiful country full of very friendly people. The weather conditions were fantastic on the day but what also added to the adventure was two local (so called experienced) climbers getting stuck on the same morning on the steepest part of the climb as we three easily climbed and descended it thanks to José’s expertise. A five star guide whom I enthusiastically recommend to everyone considering using him to climb any of Chile's wonderful volcanoes.

review_text: I rarely bother to write reviews, but want to strongly recommend Elki Magic to anyone who is travelling to the Elqui Valley. The valley is stunning, with mountains as far as you can see after every turn, and the best way to really see it all in your own time is to go to Elki Magic and let them help you. You can rent decent mountain bikes of them and take off with their detailed maps of where to stop and visit. You can spend half or a whole day exploring and taking in all the pisco distilleries or breweries and little town squares. The dip in the river is especially needed as it can be intensely hot and you'll be cycling against the very strong winds. You will be tired at the end of the day, but its such a rewarding experience. Elki Magic is run by Adeline and Lincoln who can speak French, Spanish, English and German between them. They are the nicest and kindest couple you'll meet, and clearly love helping people to explore the valley. You’ll be given all the riding gear you need for your adventure, and they are at the end of a phone call if you need help. Thank you!
title: Best way to see the Elqui Valley

Our experience with Capital Travel was that of having a great ally that has all the necessary tools and support. However, if it’s your first challenge over 4,000 masl, we did the Province Hill and the Painter Hill in preparation, and you need to pay attention to height factors that affect physical capacity individually.

review_text: I booked multiple tours with Mario, and Nave tours, in Chile. Mario is wonderful to work with, communicates well with you. And is really looking out for your best interest. He really wants you to have a great time in his country. The first day we did a Santiago City Tour, and saw all the great sights with a wonderful guide named Marcella. We went to downtown markets the vegetable market, the meat market, and then the market where all of the workers go to eat local food. Saw many more sites throughout the city, the most memorable being a walkthrough, open air Art Museum of murals painted on numerous buildings five storeys High. Beautiful art in kind of a run-down area but Marcela made us feel at home and took care of us that day. The next day, we went to the Maipo Wine Valley tour with Mario. We saw Santa Rita Winery, and Concha y Toro Winery. Both very different and great but again the Highlight was our lunch, where we went to an equestrian center and learned about local horse culture along with chilean culture and dance. Lo and behold we had the national champion of Chilean dance in front of us along with a buffet and all you could drink wine and sangria a wonderful afternoon. The last tour was to Valparaiso and Vina Del Mar, I will say it was a lot of driving in traffic over the new year holiday. And for us not the best tour. Many crowds at that time and difficult to get into places. I would probably recommend it at a different time but for us when all of Santiago went to Valparaiso we followed them in that was not a good deal. But overall Mario does a great job with his company and his guides and I would highly recommend him

review_text: I was looking for a different kind of day out from Santiago de Chile and found it with Baño Morales. I took a local bus - a fabulously clapped-out old Mercedes - from La Florida underground station in the east of the city, which wound its way through the Cajon de Maipo before going off-road for an hour's mega-bumpy ride to the spa village. The spa is basic and surrounded by a selection of rustic eateries, a couple of hostels and a horse rental stand (I'm sure there's a better name, but it's late). The bus driver has a shack there, where he spends the day before driving back to Santiago at 6pm. I went the very last day of the season and there were not many of us. One of the pools was warm enough - it was not a warm day - but the changing rooms were a sight to be seen: bushes growing through the walls, no hot water, no loo paper etc. Supremely soviet. I went bathing, horseback riding, had innumerable cups of (Nescafé) coffee, went for walks in the hinterland and enjoyed a rather good lunch in the hostelry closest to the entrance to the spas. I was the only customer, it really was like being in a ghost town. I'd recommend it as a unique experience, one utterly devoid of comfort but full of arresting images, particularly the mountain face the locals call The Cathedral. Actually, I've just dug out an e-mail I wrote to a friend about this day out, so here it is: Well, my little adventure worked like a dream but I had to stay vigilant. The bus left from a metro station way out east and I had to be there by 7.25am. As the metro doesn't even start until 8 o'clock on Sundays I was faced with a problem. To cut a long story short, I researched bus timetables on the internet and found that the one I needed, the 210, went approx. every seven minutes from my stop, Universidad Católica. At 6am on a Sunday morning. Right. I thought OK, I'll be there at 6.30am and give it till 7am, then I'll hail a taxi. Lo and behold, at 6.50am a 210 rolls up. I couldn't pay the driver as everything runs off Tarjeta Bip cards and mine didn't have enough left on it. No problem, just duck under the turnstile, he said. Only about two other people did it the whole 30-minute journey, I was amazed. I was a bit unsettled by the fact he seemed to have no idea where Estación Bellavista de la Florida was but decided to give myself a bit of time before asking around the multitudinous fellow passengers (the bus was filled to bursting point) as I knew it was about twenty stops. With the help of reliable information I got off at the right stop and headed over to where my little bus was going to leave from. There were quite a few drivers and supervisors hanging around and all were very helpful, one even phoning the driver to see where he'd got to when he was late turning up. I got on, paid my return fare and realised that the bus which was going to take us up a dirt track to 1850m altitude was just like one of those little TAD minibuses which go round Vigoulet and the like. First of all we went round the houses for about an hour, picking up people in the far-flung neighbourhoods of Santiago before getting on a sort of decent road which then took us to the Cajón de Maipu, a national park just outside the city. Driving round the neighbourhoods was very, er, instructive: virtually all the houses, in the main 80m2 T4, are protected like Fort Knox with barbed wire along the tops of the fences, some even going as far as making cages out of the entire front and back gardens by fencing from the tops of the upright fences to the walls of the house. No cars are left parked on the street, all are driven into the front, er, gardens. And these weren't wealthy neighbourhoods. More like Mermoz, type of thing. Anyway, after much bumping and being thrown about we reached Baño Morales. I was hoping to find a facility like Bad Nauheim or Calicéo but, in truth, didn't know what to expect. You'll see from the pictures that it was a lot more soviet than that. It reminded me of an English campsite in the 1960's. I was told I didn't need to bring a towel, so I didn't. I did, though, bring bathing shorts, a spare tee-shirt, socks and underpants. To say I was underwhelmed when I got there would be an understatement. I went down and found the place just behind a group of young backpackers who also, it seemed, were expecting something else. There was no-one on the the gate so we all walked through and found the Source Brezhnev in all its glory: rusting, decrepit infrastructure, an arrow pointing to drinking water that had sweet wrappers and cardboard cups floating in it, changing rooms with greenery growing in through the windows. In short, not at all what I was hoping to find. The backpackers took some pictures of the (stunning) view and then left. I sat down and wondered what the hell I was going to do with the next seven hours. Apart from anything else, the water was cooler than I'd been led to believe and it was quite nippy, too. After having a word with the gatekeeper who'd turned up I climbed the hill back into the 'village' and took stock of my options. You could go horse riding or hiking. That's not bad for a start. I sat down, had a coffee (Nescafé à la Granny: powdered stuff in those little paper sleeves) and decided to bite the bullet and bloody well get into the water. I went for it as it was so completely unlike me I thought it needed to be addressed. So I went back down to the entrance, paid my €4 and went in. I was alone. I got changed in the Lenin Memorial Locker Room and stepped gingerly out in order to get into the first pool. It was the warmest, apparently, so it was going to be the only one I tried. What the hell, it wasn't so bad, assuming one is a masochist. I stayed in and swam for about half an hour. That's quite enough, really, if you don't have the option of going and lying on heated stone beds or getting a massage from a floozy or some such. I felt I was going to get hypothermia while getting dressed. The water also completely discoloured the white lining of my shorts (it was the water; just look at the picture). Anyhow, wrapped up in my clothes with clean hiking socks on and the gloves I brought from Toulouse (yes, I did need them!) life started to look better. I'd devoured my lunch by this time and was famished. Combination of the altitude, swimming in thermal springs and getting up at 6 am, I'd say. Anyhow, Baño Morales has something for everyone provided they're not particularly choosy so next up was a little walk (see photos of attractive bits of nature, like streams and hills). I had another lunch - very good and cheap, as it happens - in a little hostel right by the springs. The lavatory windows opened on to the inside of the restaurant, which made me howl with silent laughter, probably as I was the only customer and didn't have to deal with its inevitably more unpleasant side. They have something in Chile called Daily Gotas, which is liquid saccharin. No calories, you just drip it into your tea or coffee. Knowing this would be something I know you'd LOVE to have, I took a picture of it. I didn't try it; they bring it automatically. Yes, I went horse riding. Well, that sounds rather dramatic. I sat on a moving horse for 50 minutes. The man said 'Yeah, here you are, just take it away'. I told him I had no experience. 'Don't worry, it's easy' he reassured me. I asked him how to stop and start it, where to turn the key, where the handbrake was, type thing. 'Oh, you just do this…and this…'. 'Would you come with me? I'm not comfortable taking a horse out on my own' 'OK, fine'. So off we went. It was, of course, very enjoyable, but I know it wouldn't have been if I'd been on my own as I have no idea how to drive a horse and would have spent the whole time panicking and trying not to fall off. I took a picture, as you can see. Tell Mathilde and Emilie we were galloping really fast at that moment and I was actually standing on the horse's back when I took the picture. The side of the volcano mentioned in the picture is called The Cathedral and it's not hard to see why: it has about twenty different colours which shone in the afternoon sun. Breathtaking. I didn't bother even trying to take a picture as I knew the camera couldn't cope with subtleties, but it was absolutely awesome. It's a little gaucho village and it's about to close up for the winter. Today was one of its last days. There are lots of little cabins but no-one lives there all year round. There were faces straight out of National Geographic and infrastructures out of Brezhnev's rural Russia and it was wonderful. Still, between buses and metros, eight hours travel in one day was quite a lot.

review_text: We (3) had a one of a kind amazing sun set experience in the Valley of the Moon. The views of the many colors blazing in the sun set with a back drop of the Andes and snow capped volcanoes made for a life time memory well worth the journey. We used "AYLLU EXCURSIONS" and their driver "PIERRE" took us to the salt caves first to see the unique salt formations before driving us on to the valley itself. (Wear hiking shoes, not flip flops!!) AYLLU is located on CALLE TOCONAO #479 in San Pedro de Atacama. Owners, Michael and Flavio served us delicious fresh baked empanadas and beer while we made arrangements. We found that they offered the best rates of any of the Tour/Excursion operators in San Pedro. The next day we had Pierre pick us up at our hotel "Don Tomas" and we toured the expansive salt flats with the beautiful flamingo filled Lago Chaxa. After a delicious breakfast prepared by Pierre, we drove high up into the Andes, passing through the village of Socaire with it's adobe church, to arrive at Lagunas Miscanti and Minigues. Here we over looked these amazing high mountain lakes as Vicunas grazed in the beautiful meadows surrounding the lakes. On our return Pierre stopped at the marker of the Tropic of Capricorn for photos and the village of Toconao to pet baby Llamas. These tours were a high light of our time in the north of Chile and we recommend Ayllu and especially their driver/tour guide Pierre for a one of a kind, personal experience.

review_text: My wife and I decided to try the morning bike ride which included a visit to the market. We met Antonio and Ioanna (sp?). After a brief period of adjustment to the bicycles we were off. Santiago, at least in this area is flat, and is an easy ride. Ioanna provided an interesting commentary to local places, murals, indigenous culture, and past events in the history of the country. We visited the market area, which is huge. For that portion, the bikes were parked and we walked through the various markets and learned more about the markets, its past and indigenous culture. At the end of the market tour, we were treated with fruit drinks before continuing the bike trip back through the neighborhoods and parks to our starting point. I highly recommend this tour or possibly one of the longer tours if you have the time available. Lastly, I want to thank Antonio for his assistance with my Spanish. Mi esposa y yo decidimos probar el paseo en bicicleta por la mañana, que incluía una visita al mercado. Conocimos a Antonio y Ioanna (sp?). Después de un breve período de ajuste a las bicicletas nos fuimos. Santiago, al menos en esta zona es plana, y es un paseo fácil en bicicleta. Ioanna proporcionó un comentario interesante a lugares locales, murales, cultura indígena y eventos pasados en la historia del país. Visitamos la zona del mercado, que es enorme. Para esa parte, las bicicletas estaban aparcadas y caminamos por los diversos mercados y aprendimos más sobre los mercados, su pasado y la cultura indígena. Al final del tour del mercado, nos trataron con bebidas de fruta antes de continuar el viaje en bicicleta de regreso a través de los barrios y parques hasta nuestro punto de partida. Recomiendo encarecidamente este tour o posiblemente uno de los tours más largos si tienes el tiempo disponible. Por último, quiero agradecer a Antonio por su ayuda con mi español. review_text: I did the rafting excursion over the Petrohué River on January 24th in the morning with KoKayak. I have to say that they are professional, well organized and the guides do their job very well. The weather was beautiful, so we had incredible views of the Osorno Volcano. The whole rafting excursion was handled very well. My only disappointment (and it's a very important one) is that the guides were taking pictures of the rafting and they offered to send me by e mail (at no extra charge) within a week. That never happened. All I got was a link with some videos (even though I saw that they were taking lots of pictures.) Hopefully, at the end of the rafting, I managed to see a photographer who works for another company (Turistour) that offers the same rafting excursion. I bought the pictures from her. Of course, I do not appear on those pictures, since they were taken for people on the other group. I kept calling and emailing Ko'Kayak and they told me that there were no pictures taken during that day (though I saw the guides taking them and they offered to send me the pics within a week). Finally, I asked them if they could at least send me some pictures of another day excursion, which they did. Each person have its own priorities. For me, having a photographic memory of my experience was very important, and I did not get it with Ko' Kayak. I would have gotten them if I had chosen another company, like Turistour. It's true….the other company charges you an extra 10 dollars for the pictures, but I believe it's more professional to be charged up front for an additional service than being offered something that would never happen (even if they offer to do it for free). So if having a photographic memory of your excursion is NOT important for you, I can definitely say that Ko'Kayak conducts the excursion in a very professional and organized way. But if you want to have some pictures, I think you are better off choosing other companies like Turistour. Review of: Rafting rio Petrohue Hello Rafael Thank you for your review of our trip. I am sorry that you did not receive some pictures of rafting with us. By the way we sent a link towards 20 clips of rafting on this day taken with our gopros during your trip. Our staff has been switching from photos to videos some times and I assume 20 go pros clips is a fair amount. As the rafting trip is realized in a remote location we have to get the files back to our office to have them on dropbox. We prefer that instead of burning dvds as we assume theres is less waste and pollution then. It looks that the pictures did not make it back to our office or have been deleted from the sd cards. I apologize for that. This is the first year we offer this service of videos for free on our trips and we still have some things to improve as you pointed it. By the way our priority stays the enjoyment and safety of our guests. We make sure we have the best gear availble on international standards. Our Aire rafts made in USA are the best raafts you can find around Puerto Varas. Our USCG type V pfds are renewed every 2 years and we offer the best facilities in town with a dedicated base to our rafting and kayaking trips. The pictures taking iss still a new activity for us and we did not think that it would be so disappointing for you to receive just a bunch of video clips of your trip. We will make sure to improve the service and I want to thank you very much for your review, it will help us in this direction. Kind regards Richard Carrier

review_text: It's billed as no. 3 in Chile's top ten and a climb to the top of volcano Villarrica near Pucon certainly lives up to expectations. Make no mistake it's a full-on day, exhausting and exhilarating in equal measures. People have died up there and so they only allow qualified mountaineers and guides on the volcano. For your own safety, and to get the most out of the experience, it's also really important to go with a good 'tour' company that have good guides and good equipment - ice axes, crampons, boots, clothing etc. My partner and I are not young and this was a lifetime challenge. Our priority was to find people who could allow us to 'do' the whole thing but watch out for us at the same time. We ended with 'Patagonia Experience' located in the centre of Pucon and couldn't have been more satisfied - or better cared for. Number of people in our group was limited to 8, the equipment was complete and good quality and the guides were seriously concerned with our safety as well as ensuring the best experience possible. Couldn't fault them. We saw a lot of other tour companies, not a lot cheaper, that skimped on equipment and had groups of 30 or more! My advice - go for it, but choose who with carefully. Hola FrankHodg... Thank you for choosing us to do your Volcano Villarrica climb and thanks for your great comments. Our focus here at Patagonia Experience is the quality of the whole experience; from making the booking right through to finishing the tour in our cafe with a nice cup of hot chocolate or a pisco sour! We understand the importance of good equipment and good guides and always take the time and patience to give our guests the best possible chance of completing their adventure. Thanks again and all the best, Richard

review_text: Tickets to Torres del Paine Park are purchased online. The park is accessible by road and has a variety of accommodation (from basic cabins to hotels). We visited the park with a private guide and driver. Fortunately the weather cooperated and it was a perfect day, with very little wind and temperatures between 48 and 60. Bring layers of clothing wind protection. The day trip was an arduous 610 mile drive that took 17 hours from puck up to drop off in Punta Arenas. The drive from Punta Arenas is about 4 hours, as summer road repairs and construction can slow you down. Better to go to Puerto Natales (about 3 hours drive from Punta Arenas) as a beginning point for the park. There are several rest stations with restaurant and bar facilities, bathrooms and shopping (groceries, maps, books, handcrafts, souvenirs, etc.). Do not miss Grey Glacier!

review_text: Take this fantastic, high-quality day trip to Valparaíso with the friendly and knowledgeable Diego! As an architect who works in cultural heritage conservation, I typically do detailed planning of my own trips, because I like to see things off standard tour itineraries and also need more time to explore than most people. So, I am skeptical / picky when it comes to thinking about guided tours led by others. However, I could not figure out how to make this happen on my own in the time I had available, so I was looking at guided tour options on TripAdvisor and the Progressive Tours trip to Valparaiso stood out based upon the itinerary and reviews. I had no interest in rushing through Valparaiso to get to Viña del Mar. As Daniel from Progressive said - there are 1000s of places like Viña del Mar, but very few as special and unique as Valparaíso. So that is why they focus the tour on this beautiful and intriguing city - a World Heritage City, with a contemporary layer of street art. Diego picked me up at my hotel and we had great conversations on the drive there and back, ranging from Chilean history, the landscapes and vineyards we were looking at, soccer /football, Chile's leadership in solar energy and the innovative solar-panels / water heater combinations I kept seeing on residential rooftops, the indigenous Mapuche people of south-central Chile, and even the time he spent 4 months working in my birth state in the US! The day in Valpo was just great. We started with the boat tour of the bay, as rain was predicted later in the day. Great views of the city's hills and also of the port infrastructure, including floating drydocks and container ships being unloaded. Then on to Plaza Sotomayor, where Navy parades and events were already underway in advance of Navy Day on May 21. Then a ride up one of the funiculars to start walking the hills with their incredible views, historic architecture, and amazing street art everywhere. Diego was an enthusiastic guide, knowledgeable about the history and architecture of the city; his greatest strength, of course, was in knowing the various artists whose work we viewed. He brought me to a shop where several of the artists' whose work I admired sold small / medium sized canvases of their work. No pressure to buy anything, but I did buy two pieces to take home as mementos of a great day in a great city. Diego also gave me a few recommendations for a lunch restaurant - again I felt no pressure to choose one of them. I went with the option of no view of the bay but great food (you rarely get that combination of both a good view and good food). I really like the place - one of the best meals of my trip, great ambiance, and seemingly filled mostly locals. Diego adjusted the pace of the tour to allow for more time for me to take in the details while also trying to make sure I stayed somewhat on track so I got to see all that I wanted to see, including the interior of Neruda's house, La Sebastiana. I don't mind walking up and down hills (I lived in San Francisco, California for 15 years, which seems somewhat like a sister city to Valpo, so hills come with the territory); but I note for people that don't like hills as much as I do (or just can't physically manage them) that Diego plans the routes to minimize uphill walking, moving the vehicle as need be. I did this as a solo traveler / private tour, and I felt very safe the entire time. I look forward to a future return trip to Chile and potentially taking a full day trip to the winery trip (currently being developed) with Diego. Review of: Street Art in Valparaiso and Wines in Casablanca from Santiago

review_text: On the first of march I asscended the volcano villarrica with Politour. In my group of 18 people two died, one was severly injured and one suffered light injuries! The leadership skills of some of the Politour guides turned out to be rather week in the critical situation which occured. And in my oppinion the tour is generaly not managed in a responsible manner. The tour started normaly and beside my group about 200 to 250 other people started to the volcano on that day. However the weatherforecast predicted fine weather in the morning and some showers for the afternoon. Even though it was obvious that the weather would worsen during the day our group only proceeded very slowly taking many stops (all in all 5 stops for the 800 meters of hight which are to be ascended to the volcano). About 30 minutes before we arrived at the summit I saw different groups of other agencies turning around and going back. 15 minutes later the wind intensified and it began to rain/snow. The visibility diminished but we arrived at the summit. We started the descended shortly afterwards as the weather worsened further on. Only about 10 minutes on our way down the guide (tobias) decided to take a different way down than we ascended. This route lead through a short exposed passage with some rocks and ice. Here the accident happened an two members of our group crashed. They tumbled down the mountain about 300 meters. One of them died and the other one was severly injured. That was the turning point of the tour! All the guides except one proceded to search for the two crashed boys. The remaining guide had the duty to return with the rest of the group. The bad weather conditions and the accident put preassure on our guide and he did not seem to be able to cope with it. Instead of calming the group down and leading them down of the mountain in the safest way, he started shouting at the people and putting preassure on them and therefore rather rising the risk for further accidents (two examples: A german lady triped and fell. The guide just shouted to her "why do you jump?! Just walk normaly!" An other guy was holding his ice axe in the wrong hand, the guide just shouted: "If I see you holding that axe in the wrong hand again I will hit you so you will remember!"). Furthermore the guide was speeding down the mountain loosing visual contact to the group several times. In the end two more people of our group had an accident. One brasilian guy fell in to a crevase and was only found dead two days later and a swiss guy had light injuries. I cannot comment on these last two accidents as I didn't see or notice them. I only read of them in the local newspaper afterwards. In my oppinion this tour is sold to the people by Politur in a unresponsible manner and also managed badly: The ascend of the Villarrica vulcano can be classified as an easy mounteneering tour. But still it is mountaineering and not Trekking to some lake or waterfalls! When Politur sells you this tour they do not inform the people about the risks and requirements needed for the tour. They just tell you: No prior experince is needed, the guides will take the responsibility! This can work allright when the weatherconditions are Ok! But beware if the weather changes, the tour will be much more difficult and will require some more abilities...! Using grampons and an ice axe for the first time in your life is a different thing by sunshine than in a storm when you are wet to the bones, cold and the wind freezes the water on your skin! Furthermore the equipement which is provided, especialy the clothes are only functional for nice weather, as they are NOT water proof! The grampons and the axe are not realy sharp, which can be decisive in case you fall! People, if you want to stay alive I can only advise you: Be self-responsible and check wheater you realy have the abilities to safely make it to the mountain and back in all weather conditions. Because you can not count on the responsability of the guides! I am very sad to have to post this comment and would like to express my sincere condolences to the families of the decessed young tourists Felipe Gulmares Dos Santos and Rodolfo Zaraviz Hernández.
title: Fatal accident on the Villarrica volcano with two dead turists in the Politur group!

review_text: Amazing experience!! Araya provided a sensational experience in Atacama. I loved taking the tours with you and it was the best thing!! Excellence in service, attention, punctuality, guides who go beyond driving us and introducing us to surreal places, they take care of us!!
title: Amazing experience!

review_text: The views, once you get to the highest part, are simple breathtaking. The whole mountain range is quite sunning, and most definitely worth visiting. However, the whole experience of getting there is rather disappointing. Buying a lift ticket for the only one ski lift that was operational, took forever. There was only one attendant who had no computer skills whatsoever. It took me one hour to purchase two lift tickets. The access to the operational ski lift is dangerous and far, so I wouldn't suggest it to number of tourists, such as, kids, elder people, pregnant women...among others. It takes a lot of physical effort to take the lift, and climb up on the way back. Quite poorly managed. Someone should thought of improving the access. There was an American couple with me, who wanted so badly to see the Andes. Imagine their disappointment when they realised that they simple couldn't do. Again, has anyone thought of making this sightseeing accessible for all? I honestly doubt that. Nonetheless, the lift tickets were quite pricey. Quite a rip off, I would say. The staff was quite unfriendly, at times even rude, and genuinely not interested in assisting tourists. All in all, I expected much more. Big disappointment. Huge!
title: Amazingly beautiful, poorly managed

review_text: We've been to Pozones with public bus from Pucon. The trip takes about 1 hour in a small bus. It's really cheap and this is a good way to meet locals. The maximum you can stay in the baths is 3 hours but it's enough. Ask the bus driver but most of the time he'll pick you up 2 hours after droping you. The entry is about 5 000 pesos per person. There were about 5 baths open. 1 cold, 2 warm, 1 hot and one really hot. We advise you to go early in the afternoon or in the morning. Later it become overcrowded.
title: Good value for a relaxing afternoon

review_text: Amazing 4 trips with Atacama magic. Highlight guide was Roger for my trip to Laguna Cejar. Roger was entertaining, insightful, respectful and incredibly knowledgable. Totally unique person with interesting thoughts and really funny + his music playlist was amazing. This trip was great because I really felt like I had time to enjoy the tour vs other adventures that are super packed. Also loved the Piedras Rojas tour with Renata. Such high energy, patient answering a million questions and really dedicated to her work. Excellent tour guide for such a busy day and very good knowledge of geography. I also loved the Geysers tour (magical place) and Valle de la Luna was pretty but maybe lacked a bit in terms of knowledge sharing or storytelling. Only recommendation is to have healthier food options for the “snacks” like vegetables, hummus, avocado, etc as it was a lot of fried food which gets heavy after 4 tours. All in all I absolutely recommend this agency for an unforgettable and safe experience in San Pedro.

review_text: As a second time visit I feared to not enjoying the view and the marvelous waterfalls. Now, I can happily tell you that I did enjoy it almost as much as the first time. Very impressive amount of waters falling from many different point at the same time. Endless water just under Osorno Volcano. As tourist they charge a little bit more than for local citizens. If you are a student or senior adult it will be a little cheaper. Any way, it totally worst it. review_text: We were booked on a cruise (Norwegian Sun) and wanted a cheaper and better tour than offered by NCL. I got in contact with Denis Purtov through his web site. He already had 14 people booked for the tour we wanted of the lakes, volcano, falls, etc. He soon booked a total of 18, which was the capacity of the bus. The more people the cheaper it gets so our tour only cost us $US70 as opposed to $149 for the similar one offered by NCL. Denis sent us the names, email address and cabin numbers of our fellow travelers so we could coordinate getting early tender tickets. We met the night before the tour and two of us volunteered to stand in line early to get tender tickets for all of us. That way were able to get on the first tender and have a full day for the tour. Our guide, Patricia (Patty) met us on the pier as arranged at 8:00 am and took us to our minibus. Seating was a little cramped but on the other hand the bus was air conditioned (the day was quite warm). Patty spoke excellent English and was very knowledgeable. She took us to some places the big tour buses can't/won't go in addition to the advertised stops. We had a super day with her and returned to the ship about 4:30, well before the last tender. Much better than taking the tour offered by the ship and at less than half the price.
title: Private tour with Denis Purtov's company

review_text: When I take a city tour I expect to have some kind of commentary about where we are and where we are going, together with relevant background information about the city. On this tour we received hardly any such information but rather were regaled with stories of the guide's sex life, which whilst initially somewhat amusing was certainly not what we paid good money for. Indeed his puerile jokes caused some offence to at least one of the eleven people on the tour, to which he seemed totally oblivious. The tour of the Santa Rita winery with their guide was quite informative and interesting but in no way compatible to the several winery tours we did later in the Colchagua Valley, and only represented a small fraction of the day. It says something when you get back from a tour and you don’t really know where you’ve been and know little more about the city you have spent an entire day touring. (Post-script - we went on a tour to Valparaiso with the same company two days later and learnt more about Santiago during the hour we were stuck in traffic jams on the way out of the city than we did on our whole day on this tour). Review of: Private Half day Santiago City Tour walking and Driving

The pick up was on time, we had a small group of 4, it was warmer than usual for us so we were comfortable but there were blankets and heaters for if it got cold. The astronomy talk was interesting and after that there was a lovely range of snacks and hot drinks. The telescope viewing was amazing, Jorge is so fast at finding objects and we covered quite a bit and I loved it. He also gave us a hand with some astrophotography and It was great. Thanks Jorge, I had a really great time!

review_text: A longer trek climbing upp to 3100 meters. Our other guide Francisco provides the Good spirit that makes you feel right from the start that you are among friends. Our driver also came with us on the entire walk and provided us with those little extra details that goes outside the box to make for a Good memory. And of course having three guides with ten guests is a rare luxury! AndoAndes really was THE right choice to visit the Andes. review_text: We booked a wine tour and cooking class with Uncorked and we had really great experiences with both. Vivi was our guide to the Casablanca Valley vineyards. She was cool, knowledgeable, and gave us other solid recommendations for things to do in the area. We visited two vineyards on the tour, both of which were excellent and really different from each other. We finished the tour at a beautiful restaurant with really good food, but pretty small portions. If I had one piece of advice to give, I'd say eat something solid before this tour because there will be a lot of wine to drink and really just snacks along the way. We got pretty drunk, but that was fine with us. Everything about this tour was top notch and we sort of joked (sort of not) about taking it again. For the cooking class, we met Francisco at the Mercado Central. To our delight, we were the only people taking the class, so it ended up being private. We walked around a few different markets in the area and picked up some ingredients we'd be using, while learning about Chilean food in general. Tip: If you enjoy spice, let Francisco know and maybe you'll find some spicy peppers in the market to use for the class. We then took the metro to a really nice kitchen near Parque Bustamante. There, Cristina and Francisco gave us a real treat of a cooking class. We enjoyed that it was hands-on and engaging. We made pisco sour, ceviche, pastel de choclo, peras borrachas, pebre and we drank some good wine too. We've taken classes before, but this ranks at the top. Bottom line: don't leave Chile without taking a tour and/or class.
title: Memorable tours of the highest quality

review_text: This hill rises up just outside the main shopping area of Santiago, and provides a very interesting park area to explore. It's full of little corners that you have to 'discover', along with many pathways and sets of (fairly steep and narrow) steps. I found it a delightful place to wander and to enjoy the views across Santiago centre, and to the mountains just outside the city. You can walk up from street level at a number of entry points, or take the (free) lift part-way up. There are some refreshment booths, and toilets, as well as plenty of benches for gathering one's thoughts. And there are some useful cafe's and restaurants nearby too. This hill - and Cerro San Cristobal - are most definitely worth discovering.
title: INTERESTING VIEWPOINT IN THE MIDDLE OF SANTIAGO

review_text: Before going on the Concha y Toro winery tour I was a bit concerned about being in a too large of a group. After the tour, we've decided to have lunch at the winery's restaurant and the food was really good, with moderate prices and if the opportunity to taste many of their wines by the glass. The overall experience was really good and the winery grounds and facilities are wonderful!

A word of advice: check with the tour agency if there will be stops in lower altitudes so you can get used to it (or make sure you're prepared for it if going by yourself) but should`t be any problem.

review_text: An amazing time in Chile thanks to Connie and Francisco We had an amazing time during our trip to Colchagua Valley, thanks to Connie and Francisco. I cannot recommend Colchagua Wine tours enough. They were able to accommodate a large group, provide private transportation to each of the wineries, and an awesome private lunch! After talking to several tour companies, I'm so happy that we chose Connie and Francisco and Colchagua Wine tours. We had a group of 9 people that were all staying in Santiago. We were picked up promptly at 7:30AM in a private van (and we loved our driver). The drive was about 2 hours but was a beautiful scenic drive. We met Connie and Francisco at the first winery (Montes Winery) and they were with us for the rest of the day! We also visited Viu Manent and Montgras wineries, which were both a great experience! The private lunch that Connie and Francisco organized for us at Casa Colchagua, was fantastic and one of our best meals of the trip. It was very obvious that Connie had put a lot of thought into making this a very memorable day! Overall, we just had such a wonderful experience and it was all thanks to Connie and Francisco. We had also planned a trip for the next day to Valparaiso and Vina del Mar, which we were going to drive to. After talking to Connie and Francisco, they were able to organize a private van for us, plan an itinerary, and make lunch and dinner reservations for us in Valparaiso - all in a couple of hours! Again, I cannot recommend this company enough! Thank you Connie and Francisco for making our trip to Chile memorable and for the wonderful time. We've made new friends in Chile and looking forward to coming back some day!
title: An amazing time in Chile thanks to Connie and Francisco

review_text: KL Adventure has many different rentals available! For people who love to ski, they have randonee setups with skins, backcountry splitboards, regular snowboards, race skis, powder skis, skis for beginners, and kids! Also the do a PROMO for families! One whole adult package gets a child package for free! Which can be a lifesaver if you are renting multiple days or have a big family. For those who don't ski they have sleds, snow boots and a wide range of ski clothing, also have kids sizes. The clothes are very nice and warm, also have goggles, helmets, gloves, everything you need for rent. Also helmets and goggles for sale! We really enjoyed KL Adventure and recommend highly to those traveling to ski in Santiago!

review_text: My husband and I have booked the Active W-Trek rather spontaneous and were super satisfied with the booking process. We have received a detailed itinerary and packing list up front. Ricci and Cecilia answered all our questions and were really quick in responding at any time. We arrived the first night for our welcoming dinner and the briefing and had a great evening with amazing (vegan) food at the Garden Domes. The cabins at Garden Domes are really super nice and you can enjoy a great view. Maria, the host of the Garden Domes, was super welcoming and made us all feel home immediately. She is the nicest and most welcoming person we have met in our travel so far. Maria really made sure that nothing is missing and at the same time she filled the room with positivity. Our group consisted of 6 additional people, which was a great size. The next days in the national park were amazing and well planned. The first day we had a tour guide named Cecilia, as the first day was the hardest and most difficult day. We enjoyed being on our own the other three days and had no problems along the way. We would definitely recommend not to bring your own sleeping bag or mat as the camp sides always offer you the options to rent everything for a small price. We would definitely recommend ChileTour to any traveler who wants to enjoy Torres del Paine without having to organize the whole trip yourself. Everything was covered, from accommodation to transportation and food. We received breakfast every morning, a lunch box and once arrived dinner at the different camp sites or Refugios. Back from the hike and super exhausted, we slept again another night at Garden Domes. Maria prepared Pizza Night for us and a delicious breakfast on the next day. Maria even drove us to our next hotel after breakfast and again was just so helpful and welcoming. The experience really wouldn’t have been the same without Maria, so thank you a lot!

A perfect silence, disturbed by the catamarans low diesel throb- easily blocked out.. Then onto the Petrohue falls .. more smacking of senses ... more awe.. more raw beauty. Finally back to Varas: lovely town, lucky to sit at a bar with good beer overlooking Lake Llanquihue and the distant peaks, past the prom and the beach, with a local band playing in the square. Heaven.

review_text: I had a bad experience with Ruta Nomade on a trip to Cajon del Maipo, and would not recommend them for the following reasons. They showed up late for our pickup and were not aware of the location of the next person to be retrieved, despite the fact that I had explicitly informed them where she was staying on several occasions while planning for the trip. Traffic was bad that morning, so we were very delayed while going to get her. I would think that they would have considered the location of their clients prior to the journey, planned enough time, and certainly factored in the road conditions (especially in Santiago). These delays were especially frustrating, because I took the time to ensure that they had the information about our locations, but this did not encourage them to plan appropriately. The vehicle used for the transporting us out to Cajon del Maipo was also in bad shape and seemed dangerous. From my perspective, client safety should be the top priority for tour operators, but this does not seem to be the case with Ruta Nomade. Worst of all, the office manager that day was very rude and dismissive when I mentioned these issues to him. I understand that it is challenging to operate a tour company and deal with clients, so I approached the situation delicately, but felt it was important to give feedback. I was surprised by the harsh reaction and, to be honest, it really annoyed me and that is why I was motivated to write this poor review of the service. Dismissing honest feedback and being rude to clients in the process seem like the worst of the worst in the tourist business.
title: Not Recommended for Rude and Unprofessional Service

review_text: Three of us used Magic Chile to get to and from Santiago and Valparaiso. review_text: With just a bit more of organization and more (or better displayed) information this museum could become one of the best thematic museums (even) in the world! There are not many places that can boast such importance for history of navigation or discoveries as these parts of South America. Therefore Punta Arenas was perfect choice for a museum like Nao Victoria Museo. Exhibits are breathtaking....replicas of ships that made history! I was thrilled - I could imagine myself as a member of Magellan's crew walking the deck of his ship .. and hundreds of people visiting when I did were as enthusiastic as I was. May this review serve to improve that fascinating place and help it becoming better organized. I do hope that after my next visit to Nao Victoria Museo I'd be able to leave 5* rating.

review_text: We drove here from San Pedro and it was a very easy drive for most of the way. My wife and I hiked near and between the two lakes, maybe 3/4 mile or so each way, some along the road. It was great to drive and avoid the crowds in tour groups. It seemed like later in the afternoon there were almost no tours so that would be a good time to go (we spent a good couple hours here). Got to get close to vicunyas!

review_text: It was billed as being a 4 days cruise where we would be visiting glaciers and seeing tons of wildlife etc. We didn't even see an ice cube and very little wildlife. When we boarded they were insistent that we get up to see them traverse some narrows at 6 AM. We foolishly did. We weren't allowed to have coffee except between 8 & 9 AM. We weren't allowed to bring alcohol on board and there was none to purchase.The food was HORRIBLE. For example one nights offering was spaghetti with a thin meat sauce and an apple for desert. This at cruise ship prices! Our cabin was so small that all you could do is lie in your bunk. During the day the truck drivers watch Spanish language daytime TV in the cafeteria with the volume full blast. The washrooms were filthy and when you walked in the stench hit you like you had walked into a wall. Percy, the so called purser, gave a few talks in Spanish & English. In one of them he spouted out a pile of bunk and misinformation about fish farms killing the whales and described krill as being 3 - 4 inches long and that fish farm pellets floated freely in the ocean and were being consumed by the whales. Then he described how the ships servicing the fish farms all had echo sounders, sonar and bottom finders. Those are all the same thing! He claims they are causing the whales to beach because of this. We saw one service ship during the entire trip. This man claims to be an engineer but clearly has no knowledge of what he speaks of. We could not wait to get off of this ship. It was the worst travel experience I have ever endured!
title: This is like a prison ship

review_text: I travel frequently for work, and when time and the weather allow, I always prefer to see new places on a bike. I recently made my first visit to Santiago and Chile and went on a daylong tour of the Maipo Canyon area with Andres. It was truly fantastic. The scenery was stunning (like nothing I’ve ever seen) and the weather excellent. The workout was perfectly tiring and made the ride’s highlights, bathing mountainside in a hot spring and the delicious picnic Ines had packed for us, all the more enjoyable. That would have made the tour more than worthwhile, but it was made even better by Andres, who makes for smart company. We talked for hours on the drive out and back from Santiago (though we weren’t talking as much while riding up the “Slope of Sorrows,” of course), and I learned more about Chile that day than I could have ever imagined. I am sure I’ll remember and continue to enjoy the ride and the day for the rest of my life.

review_text: We booked at Day Trip to Cajon del Maipo Embalse El Yeso through Viator. While we did not know the provider at the time of booking, we had a great experience. I would recommend booking directly with Stamps. (We had booked a different day trip through Viator and it was awful). Ask for Vanessa Villablanca. Our tour guide was Vanessa Villablanca. She picked us up at the hotel at 8am. While we didn't book a private tour, it ended up just being our family of 4. She had a good vehicle that could handle the drive through the Cajon Del Maipo & Embalse El Yeso. Vanessa had great command of the points along the trip. She was so accommodating when we wanted to stop & get pics which we really appreciated. We went on a Saturday and unfortunately it was a long weekend for people of Santiago. As such it was PACKED. We left at 8am and the drive was perfect up to about a 1/4 mile from Embalse El Yeso. TONS of car packed a very narrow dirt road making it virtually impassable. Luckily Vanessa had parked at the bottom of the entrance area, allowing us to avoid what would have been HOURS trying to get back down the hill. You do not want to do this drive yourself nor with a car that is not an SUV. Hire a driver. We had a little lunch which was very nice. Nothing like enjoying the beauty of the area. Vanessa set up a table and chairs. She is very personable and passionate for nature. Tips: - Don't go on the weekend day if you can avoid it. - Recommend leaving Santiago before 8am, earlier if on a weekend day - Hire a driver / tour guide. You'll get so much more out of it. - When you get to Embalse El Yeso, walk the road around the corner. The mountain range opens up and it is breathtaking! - Available bathrooms along the trip will cost 300 pesos to use. Make sure you have change.
title: Day Trip to Cajon del Maipo Embalse El Yeso

review_text: My wife and I truly enjoyed the hike to San Jose Volcano with Ando Andes. It was well organized and fun day. The first half you slowly ascend from a parking area to Vale de la Engorda where you rest and spend about an hour viewing the volcano and surrounding mountains, take pictures and have healthy lunch provided by the staff. The 2nd half you hike back down to the parking area and then head back to Santiago but there is a nice stop before you leave Maipo. We highly recommend the hike. It's a very memorable experience. Francisco and his team did a great job Dear Buck! Thanks a lot for your review. We are very happy to hear you enjoyed the Andes with our guides. Best Regards!!! Constanza

review_text: I did the 'Old Santiago' tour with the wonderful Andres and two international students spending a semester studying in Chile. Everything was very easy to organise by email, and we got a very warm welcome complete with very tasty packed lunches to start, and delicious home-made tomato soup to finish! The tour lasted around 4 hours and took us through parts of Santiago that we never would have discovered on our own. It felt very safe; we were always either on bike routes, paths through the many Santiago parks, or on pavements so the traffic wasn't a concern. Andres gave us the most fantastic insight into the city that he clearly loves... I can't imagine a better way to get under Santiago's skin. My only disappointment was that I didn't have time to do more tours! Thank you so much to Andres for an amazing experience.

The trees around the lookout would need to be cleared (again) to give a full view. in the last years they grew so that part of the view is now blocked. On a Saturday, the park closed at 4:30 pm already, which we were not aware of before, so we had to hurry up, while it would have been nice to spend some more time there.

review_text: This was our first visit to the museum, located on the Cerro Alegre’s Paseo Yugoslavo. It can be reached by the El Peral funicular and is housed in a beautiful Art Nouveau(ish) mansion and its adjacent guesthouse. The buildings themselves are worth a visit, but my wife and I were especially surprised by the beauty of many of the paintings. We knew that the collection had some examples by well-known painters (for Chileans), such as the magnificent Thomas Somerscales, Juan Francisco González and Alfredo Helsby, but also paintings by some we did not know, such as the Spanish painter Eugenio Hermoso. Of course, you will not find paintings by Old Masters, but some truly beautiful paintings set in a lovely museum. I was unaware that the entrance fees differed depending on whether you are Chilean or not, and think that should stop, but even so the entrance fee for foreign visitors is only USD $6, including an audio guide, which is quite reasonable.

review_text: Six of us did this trip back in 2006. We were spending a year driving around SAM in our motor caravans and had come up to P.Natales from Ushuaia, the Christmas target for all long distance travellers. We booked cabins which were OK, we had food which was plentiful but not great, the weather was calmish and I didn't see anybody being sick. It rained a bit one day so we did play cards, but most of the time we were on deck watching beautiful mountains and glaciers slip by. We even saw three stark peaks clumped together like fingers, was that really a back view of the Torres del Paine? Our morning in Puerto Eden was the magical bit, a lost village, the Brigadoon of Chile. We met an old woman there who was one of the very few indigenous people left, she was full of stories and gave us a postcard of herself as a young girl after we had bought a few trinkets including a little handsewn bark canoe. The atmosphere in the village was just lovely and I have some great photographs of smoke drifting across through the early morning mist and low sunlight. Next it was the rusted out merchant ship perched on a rock. She just ran onto this unknown obstacle and has been there ever since. We saw dolphins and maybe a whale far off but the overall voyage was full of enjoyment and we had no troubles or complaints. The complainers seem to have been unlucky with the weather, but some of them seem to have been expecting a sort of luxury cruise which, in the circumstances is ridiculous. We were just glad to haver done the trip and to have the memories. The idea of passing up the voyage in favour of flying is so weird that the people doing it cannot have been serious travellers. They had better stay at home watching travel shows on television for the rest of their lives. Please note I had to click a wrong date before |I could submit, we went in 2006, not 2013

review_text: Unforgettable watching a calving glacier for a couple hours. This is a very expensive trip though. Had been a decade ago on a 75% off (last minute, $3,200 for two) 8-day trip to Antarctica (saw lots but no calving glaciers that I remember) on a ship that had it all: a brand new Norwegian ice breaker; great, varied buffet meals; lectures by historians and scientists all day long for all of our non-landing days in Antarctia. So we frankly expected more of the Skorpios II. First of all, the crew was fantastic and did everything to make passengers (just over 100) very comfortable. But we expected ample buffets and food instead rather indifferent "served" food. We were surprised that there were very few "foreign" travelers, almost everybody were Chilenos or Argentinians, obviously of some resources. It would really help if the Skoprios had some informed lectures about flora and fauna and history. Second, if they once had buffet meals, they should reinstate them. Obviously I would have been much happier had this journey cost $2,000 or 3,000 for two, instead of more than $4,000. There are other ways -- cheaper but perhaps more adventurous to get to see this glacier. Look at three or more guide books and study (harder than I did) before you get on the airplane for Chile.

review_text: My wife Sally and I wish to thank Jorge for providing a wonderful evening under the stars! I am an avid stargazer and have previous experience observing in the Southern Hemisphere so we planned our trip to the Atacama to coincide with the February new moon. What we didn't expect was the heavy rainfall and flooding that hit the area during our stay. While I had managed to catch two brief early morning breaks in the rain and clouds, I was beginning to think my observing might not make it beyond the hotel patio. On our last evening in San Pedro de Atacama the clouds broke and Jorge took us, along with two other couples, several miles south of town. The spot was perfect and gave me what I had been hoping for: a horizon to horizon view of the Southern Milky Way. Jorge gives an excellent and informative celestial presentation. My wife really appreciated this introduction before moving onto telescope observing. I too found it very informative. I can now get fairly close to the Southern celestial pole even if the marker (The southern Cross) is obscured or below the horizon. Once we moved onto the telescopes ( I had along my 80mm refractor), Jorge would use his laser pointer to suggests observing targets for my scope once I had exhausted my list of familiar old friends (Eta Carina, The Jewel Box, Tucanae 47, Omega Centauri) and I was able to see objects that I would not have seen had I been on my own. Everyone involved seemed to enjoy the experience as Jorge and I would train our scopes on different objects. My only regret is that I couldn't have spent more time out but I'll get that the next time I go. I highly recommend an evening with Jorge to anyone planning a trip to the Atacama! Clear Skies Dear Travellers thank you very much for your positive review It was a very difficult week every night cloudy but the last one our Pat-ta Hoy´ri (Mother Earth in Kunza) was kindly and allowed a good observation of several and beautiful stellar objets such Nebulae (Eta Car, Orion), Open Star Cluster (NGC 2516, NGC 3532, M45), Globular Star Cluster (M47, Omega Centauri) and much more, I enjoyed a lot with you because both were very enthusiastic and I thank watch me nyself. If you return again to Atacama Desert we´ll spend more time observing the wonder of southern hemisphere. My best Regards Jorge Antonio Corante Fernández

review_text: Our hotel arranged this half day wine tasting tour at our request. We were collected from our hotel on time in a clean air conditioned vehicle by our guide Felipe and driver Carlos. Both were enthusiastic, friendly and helpful. It was clear our enjoyment and welfare were their only priority. We drove out to Casablanca Valley to Emiliana vineyard. On the way Felipe talked about Chile, Valparaiso, Casablanca Valley and wine, as well as answering our questions. He was knowledgable, open and informative. At the vineyard we went on a wine tour with a member of Emiliana's staff, followed by a tasting of 5 of their wines. More about this in the review of Emiliana. Following the tasting we were consulted about their idea for our next wine tasting and thought it a great idea. We set off across the vineyard and drove up the old Santiago road until a point where we could safely stop with panoramic views across the valley. Here we were treated to a Chilean wine, as drunk by Felipe's mother. This was a blend of Resiling and Sauvignon Blanc. This was very different from any at Emiliana and very tasty. This was complemented by snacks they brought for us. Wine tasting in a lay by half way up up a Chilean mountain was very different and huge fun, an unforgettable experience unlike any wine tasting we've experienced in any other country across the globe. We were then dropped off back at our hotel. We were able to pay by credit card, without a surcharge. Add to this we were given a discount because of the connection with the hotel. If you want a magical experience we would whole heartily recommend this one.

review_text: Francesco picked us us at our hotel in Puerto Varas and we joined another couple for our tour. Right off he offered us a bottle of water for the trip which was much appreciated. His English was very good and he explained the sights as we passed them and gave a history of the area. We were with another couple and he spoke English to us and Spanish to the other couple. We started by seeing the volcanos from a distance and he explained the history of their eruptions and how the area was settled. We then entered Vincente Perez Rosales National Park and saw the beautiful water and waterfalls. The color of the water is magnificent. There were many beautiful photo opportunities. We then went to Todos Los Santos Lake and went on a lovely optional boat ride. The lake has a real pristine beauty. After the boat ride we drove to almost the top of Osorno Volcano to where the snow started. We had a nice lunch there and could have ridden the chair lift over the snow to the first stop but the 4 of us were happy to enjoy the view. We went for a hike and observed how the ash from the last volcano in the region had colored the soil. You could see the whole lake from this location. Francesco narrated as we drove and answered general questions about Chile, geography, sights, etc. He was always very courteous and we would recommend his tour to others. Review of: Full Day Tour Petrohue Falls, Todos los Santos Lake and Osorno Volcano Glad you and Howard enjoyed the tour Jane! Keep having fun in our country! =D
