review_text: We booked four tours with Layana. One of the tours was full so they "sold" us to another tour company, that tour was good so we didn't mind. We had two Layana guides, Simone for two tours and Rodrigo for one, both were very friendly and informative and spoke great English, and we never felt like they were giving more info in Spanish than in English (an issue we experienced in Brazil and Argentina). However, Layana's buses have seen better days! On two of the tours we had buses with broken air con so it got extremely hot and uncomfortable. But the worst was en route to the Cejar Laguna when the bus broke down and we had to wait the best part of an hour for another bus to pick us up. I appreciate that the roads are bad but the vehicles need to be better maintained. Also, maybe a small point, but when breakfast or snacks were being served a lot of the other tours seemed to have a much better offering. E.g. at the Tatio Geysers all the tour buses were parked side by side and the various breakfasts were laid out. We got pre-made ham and cheese sandwiches, hard boiled eggs and coffee/tea. We walked about a little over the gravel (pestered all the time by horse flies!) and then lunched at the Cafeteria Mirador - definitely our least impressive meal in Chile which would score no more than two stars. Regardless the volcano is stunning from the distance - and you do get some pretty good views from it when you visit.
title: Impressive volcano

review_text: This is a lovely cool place to stroll around. You can take the red line on the metro to the end of the line and it is a short walk to the market. The nearby church is closed though. The market itself has a wide variety of crafts and all very nice not junky looking. Prices are a little higher than in town but a lot of the artists are right there on site and they are actual made in Chile articles. There is a cafe in the small village where you can sit and enjoy a small snack or drink.

In total we stayed 3 days, the agency organizing all the details and pending us at every moment. El equipo de Howlanders.com quiere agradecerte tu amable reseña. ¡Esperamos volver a verte!

review_text: Maybe the type of tour was wrong, I expected to do trekking or hiking through some places but it was all on a wagon with stops at the viewpoints so it was just getting on and off the wagon and taking photos, also with the bad fortune that our visit ended. was interrupted by a Rally that was taking place and prevented us from visiting one of the important parts of the park, which is the Milodón cave, the agency was not aware of it and despite having paid to enter, we were not allowed to pass and we missed the visit, On the way back, the guide was not very empathetic because he did not want to stop to buy a soft drink or candy for the return trip, which was 3 and a half hours. review_text: Lake Llanquihue is in southern Chile's Lake District and is known for its vast waters (860 sq.km.) and black-sand shores. Visited on 2/04/2017. There was a light fog that limited views of the distant shores but by afternoon it had cleared and we could view the distant volcanos. The little towns and villages around the lake have a shared German heritage, but differ greatly in character. Puerto Varas is a bustling adventure tourism centre whereas Frutillar is a summer holiday resort centre. This a part of the world that I could stay in for some months. Beautiful area.

review_text: If you ask a random sampling of Chileans about the 1970's you will get a broad, conflicting set of 'facts'. Some say Allende was a democratic hero, and Pinochet was a corrupt dictator, others will say that Pinochet saved Chile from becoming Cuba. Regardless, 1973 was the start of a civil war where oppressors and victims were all harmed and scarred. From this context, the museum is a harsh reminder that this form of holocaust can and did happen in an otherwise civil society. I tried not to be swayed by political leanings of the exhibits, but rather focused on the climate of fear, distrust, and uncertainty of the time. Imagine, for example, being a soldier holding a gun on someone that you knew, simply because you were ordered to do so. The museum is very well done, and for non-Spanish speakers, you can rent radios that explain exhibits and get you through the experience in about two hours.
title: Important to remember

review_text: Let me start by saying I visited in December 2013... A LONG time ago. I STILL dream about this trip and the dream of getting back to Antarctica again one day. A little background: My mom and I had always dreamed of going to Antarctica. On a whim, she said "When I find a company that flies, we'll go". So she took to Google and found Antarctica 21 (back then Antarctica XXI). We headed to the airport in Los Angeles, super excited and ready, only to find out that our LATAM plane had a mechanical issue. The flight kept getting delayed and delayed and delayed again, so we said "it's not meant to be" and left the airport. We had already almost unpacked the suitcases when our travel agent called and said "A car is coming to pick you up in an hour to take you back to the airport" to which we ALMOST said it's not worth it. But, she convinced us that this was a trip of a lifetime and since the plane was flying, insurance wouldn't cover it if we didn't go. We got on the plane, landed in Chile where we sat on the tarmac due to air traffic control strikes, and FINALLY made it to the hotel. What a journey just to get there... Then we were kept on edge weather wise as you never know what time the plane to Antarctica is taking off. We had read horror stories about people never getting to go, and hoped that wouldn't happen to us. Once we found out the plane was going, we were so excited. We landed on the airstrip, walked down to the Ocean Nova, and set sail. We even saw a lone emperor penguin right as we were walking to the boat! The trip itself was incredible, with experienced guides, majestic wildlife (minke whales, all sorts of penguins, other birds, seals, you name it) and jaw dropping landscapes. I'd love to go back here for photography one day... Thanks to Mike (whale guy!!!) who predicted minke whale behavior leading to the best sighting ever (my photograph actually won a contest!). We photographed from zodiacs and on land, providing plenty of eye level opportunities. 10/10 would recommend. See attached for some photos I took there... It's my dream to go back to photograph! Hi Elissa, Thank you very much for your message and for sharing your Antarctica21 experience with us! We're very happy to provide the opportunity of visiting Antarctica by reaching the continent by plane, therefore avoiding the turbulent waters of the Drake Passage. At Antarctica21 we always want to deliver an unforgettable experience, and our expedition guides are very passionate about the region which makes the experience even more exciting for our guests, what an incredible sighting it must have been to see minke whales! Thank you again for sharing your experience, and your photos which are stunning! We hope to welcome you on board again one day!
title: Trip of a Lifetime

review_text: Since we missed our 11:00am guided tour of La Moneda (thank you American Airlines!), we decided to visit this very popular and comprehensive museum. Upon entering the museum, you will notice a small gift shop, a cafe and the admissions desk. Explore the second floor first. Gaze at the map of the Americas located on your way up to the second floor. Notice how far south you really are! There are many unique and fascinating artifacts and sculpture to browse. Don't miss that exhibit examining colorful fabrics from that time period. You enter through the revolving doors and make sure you pull out the drawers (and then close them back!) to see the hidden contents. Keep in mind that you will view the exhibits in a counterclockwise fashion. You will then proceed down many flights of stairs to more amazing artifacts from the time period. My favorite part was the exhibition about Easter Island, especially since we were headed there in 5 days. Don't forget your student ID card (ISIC) for a small discount off the adult ticket price. They DO NOT accept credit cards and only accept pesos (not US dollars or euros).
title: Nice Intro to Santiago

Before our ride we got to pick and bond with our horses by collecting them from the pasture, grooming and saddling them. This made the experience so much more authentic. Great experience for beginner and experienced riders. Monika!! Thank you for trusting me and my horses, you were great! I'm so happy you got to have an amazing experience. review_text: My great disappointment was Cerro Tocó, whose Guide lacks skill and patience with beginners. He pulled me out of the group at the 100m walk because I got super stupid, saying I couldn't continue. As I don't believe everything they tell me, after 15 minutes in the car, I improved and climbed 500m alone without problems (just did not climb any more pq I found my group coming back) and two days later I climbed the volcano Lascar (much harder than the Cerro) in 3 hours with a fabulous Guide who knows how to drive beginners. Even proving that I was not badly tall and that the Guide was wrong in driving, Zoom did not return my money. The tours are generally well organized, with adequate time in places, good transportation and meals are tasty. The meals at the foot of the volcanoes are amazing: wonderful landscapes and delicious local food. I was lucky to make 3 tours with the Guide Alexis, who is very fun and is always willing to explain the biology, anthropology and geology of the place. It also makes great photos and videos. My score 3 is for Zoom not assuming the bad Guide error on Cerro.

The next day I rented a bike of Elki Magic and did a 18km circuit around Vicuna. With a well designed map and the explanation of Adeleine it was easy to find the pisco distilleries and a restaurant. The circuit 1 is very nice and mostly flat. The mountain bikes a quite new and therefore absolutely worth the money. You can rent the bikes for half day or full day! I can definitely recommend Elki Magic for their tours and bikes.
